text:
Fresh spring water... check!
Hugely portioned (although on the menu it said regular sized) cobb salad... check!
Cheap prices... check!

During my short stay at Reno, one of my friends checked this place out, came back to the hotel, and urged all of us to come eat here. The food was great. 

If I ever end up back in Reno, I will definitely come back here. I really want to try their "nookie" for breakfast.

I tried their decaf latte which was tasty, foamy, so good and light that I didn't need to add sugar.
The store is cute and the baristas very friendly. It has a private parking lot but it's always packed.
I definitely come back on my next visit to Santa Barbara.
Amazing Bagels!! My favorite place ever! Super fast cook and donuts are fresh and they taste so good!

Well, I visited UAL for the first time today because I wanted to see what the big deal was about.  Man, was I glad that I did!  What a place, full of great items at incredibly low prices.  Yes, some of the high end designer clothes are still pricy anyway you look at it, but still a super deal.  I tend to go into "overload" in discount places such as this with large inventories, but the critical difference between UAL and other places is the service that is received.  I was amazed when I walked in to have someone come immediately up to me, tell me about the place , where things are located and offer any assistance.  Melody, the owner was there today and she worked with me to assure that I found just what I was looking for, brought clothes to the dressing room and suggested that I try on things that I never would have chosen if I was on my own.  I walked out with a great summer dress for 39.00, some Velvet camisoles and great jewelry.  This place is a find!  I will be going back regularly to feed my new UAL addiction.

Eight of us came here for brunch for my birthday. We made a reservation and were seated quickly. We did the all-inclusive bottomless drinks which came with the order of any entree. The Bloody Mary's were excellent but the mimosas were more OJ than champagne. I had the steak and eggs which were amazing! The rest of the table enjoyed their food as well. 

Our server, Cesar, was excellent. 5 stars for him but 4 stars for the overall experience. We will be back for lunch or dinner another time to try it out!

This place is OVERRATED. Been twice now and I felt a review was necessary. 

Pros: Birra Morretti on tap, sexy menu, chic decor, good service, octopus appetizer, squid ink pasta

Cons: Carpaccio is one of my favorite foods and this was not very good at all (no crostini, horseradish or arugula for one thing...and I don't know where the "Italian kimchi" was but of that is a play on words regarding the roasted capers then I'm not sure I follow their line of thinking -- kimchi is fermented cabbage after all), sticks on sticks on sticks of butter is used in preparation of the Carbonara which totally drowned out the taste of the guanciale and I didn't see the value at all in adding corn to the dish, Brussels sprouts are just okay but what's worse is that you smell like them for 2 days (I didn't even eat them the second time around and I still smell them today!), mushroom/fontina/truffle pizza and the Quattro formaggi/pancetta were too rich for my blood. This seemed to be the theme: too much burro. 

If I go back, I will be getting Chicken Piccata because it's a great dish and very difficult to mess up. Something tells me though that it will be a little buttery...

Healthy food is a rarity in Nola, and HK does healthy food fast. I live in the campus area and I love the convenience of this place. The menu covers it all really, so whatever I'm in the mood for they usually have it.
Try the bouquet tea tonics-  they're delicious! The mochas are also very yummy and the artwork on top of the mocha is cool! The lavender latte was awesome too! If you're in Reno, don't miss it!

I went there on a Saturday night with a reservation.  Was seated right away.  I really love this place!  The menu is very diversified and the service is exceptional.  I had the filet with mashed potatoes and vegetables-the topping on the filet was so good, the vegetables were very tasty and the mashed potatoes were the best tasting I have ever had.  Love the decor and the atmosphere.   Plan on going back , luckily I work right across the street!!!  Can't wait to try more of the menu.  Had the toasted pound cake for dessert-yum! - very different from the usual.

Decided to try this out for a late morning Sunday brunch option.  Tried the classic breakfast, a nest egg and a hand squeezed OJ.  Firstly - super excited about housemade biscuits.  Its really shocking to me that very few places bother to do this.  Gravy was tasty, but could have used a little more.  Now, in all fairness, I treat gravy like an entree as opposed to an accompaniment, so for "normal" folk, you may find the gravy quantity acceptable.  I went with bacon, which was really good - thick slices, nice and crispy.  And my eggs were cooked perfectly to order.  I really liked the crispy potatoes, as well.  Two, small whole potatoes, well seasoned and seared on the outside.  The OJ was fresh and tasty - not too tart. 

My friend had the nest egg.  She thought it was really tasty, but since I didn't try it, I don't have much to say about that. 

I think the food is excellent.  I will agree with other reviews - not a fan of the community seating.  We didn't have an issue finding a seat and people did move along quickly, but since folks tend to want to catch up over a meal, you don't really have the privacy or the space to do that here.  I am hoping the excellent food results in more seating!!

Cute location, there is a line, but pretty good food. Great location, but I was disappointed that when we arrived about 3:15, after being in line for about 15-20 minutes, we were informed that the ribs are only available at dinner time. Yes I rolled my eyes! But the cashier was very friendly and asked about how our trip was going so we decided to try out the pulled pork sandwich and several of their sides. Great food! Just disappointed I didn't get to try their ribs.

We went here for lunch not long ago and were not at all impressed with the food. The environment and service was fine, and the location is good, but the food itself was (1) very small portioned for the price and (2) not great quality. We got ravioli for our kids and it was so dry that it was barely edible. We will not be going back.
Tastes like most froyo, but the staff is extremely nice, and do not give you the stink eye after your 6th sampling of the froyo. I still prefer Phileo Yogurt on south street, which has more flavors.

Ahhhhhh this place is so good! Yes, it's small and there's usually a wait. But it is so worth it. 

The noodles are never soggy or over cooked. The broth is flavorful. The ingredients are fresh. You get generous portions of meat. The menu is varied. The service is friendly. The food comes out quickly. I have no complaints except that I wish I lived closer!

food was good. coffee was just ok.  Service was slow.... we did have a large party but it was like they were doing each cup of coffee and getting each dessert one at a time, and serving us so slowly half the crowd was done before some got their first cup of coffee or anything to eat.  not well organized at all.

My wife & I had a very enjoyable first visit to Bici this evening (Saturday). Very friendly and knowledgeable staff, casual but stylish decor, no kids present but there were kids items on the menu (so I guess we were in the right place at the right time!). Food was very good overall and we especially liked the Tuna Nicoise and Mushroom Ragu over Polenta. Chicken Picata was ok but too oily or buttery. The 3-huumus selection was also very good. 

I'm sure we'll be back and would recommend it highly. On this night the friendly staff made the experience extra nice.

Healthiest lunch option in the Cool Springs area by far. Sure there are other places that offer a good salad, but Grabbagreen really makes sure you can't get distracted by the add ons (like that extra brownie for dessert). I ordered the Gulf of Mexico bowl with chicken instead of shrimp. Everything was fresh and great quality, but overall kind of bland. The avocado dressing just tasted like a pureed avocado, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but if you're looking for a flavor punch that dressing will not suffice. If you get chicken, it's ground meat instead of chopped--just FYI in case you don't realize it when you order. I think the ground chicken definitely makes the bowl look more like that classic clean "meal prep" lunch. I'm sure there are other bowls with dressings that are far more tasty. I mean, they even have a healthy mac and cheese. But when I come here it's either the intention to go all the way and eat as many greens as possible. 

As others have said, Grabbagreen is a great option if you're really trying to stick to a healthy eating habit. Or if you're like me, you eat here when you feel really guilty for eating a bunch of junk days before. There are quick grab-and-go items available and fresh made juices and smoothies, so it's a great option to add to your Cool Springs lunch rotation.

Nice and friendly staff, decent food and a fun environment. 

Most everyone has tried hibachi before and this one is a nice option and top 3 choice in the game.

I can never wear the same outfit again before washing due to the lingering smell of hibachi and there are usually leftovers with rice and noodles. 

Stop by and give it a shot if you never have and make sure to sign up for the birthday club free meal.
Amazing food. Ridiculously high quality ingredients. Definitely will come back whenever I get a chance.

I had high tea with a friend here and while the tea was outstanding, the sandwiches were nothing special. They were things that I could make better at home and not what I would typically expect from a $16.95 High Tea service. The service was not very good either, as one of the ladies was pretty rude to us most of the time. My friend spilled her tea a bit because it got stuck on the saucer and she just threw her a napkin and kept talking to the table next to us telling them "sorry about that" like we were an inconvenience.  It took my friend 15 minutes to even get her back over to get her a new saucer. There were not that many people there so it's not like it was a busy day. Overall, I probably wouldn't go back here, but if I did, it would be just to get tea and nothing else.

Any hotel near the Opryland Hotel automatically loses a star.  Why else would anyone stay in this part of Nashville unless you need access to Opryland or Opry Mills Mall?  This Radisson is directly next door to the Opryland Hotel.  So there is your access.  They use a bus to shuttle every half hour.  That's convenient.  The hotel can be found online far cheaper than Opryland Hotel.  It's clean and the renovations are done.  That said-the place is spiffy with what I consider small basic rooms and small small shower area. There is a cool restaurant with live music over dinner.  Not Vegas but nice anyway.   Some of the rooms face the inner atrium.  My room faced the opposite way towards the street.  So I heard cars and trucks go by in the morning.  I can say the staff was nice and the room was clean.  Lots of restaurants in the area if you don't want hotel food.  Normally I'd say 3 stars but it's basically the freckled face stepchild of the beauty next door.  If you are just there to shop at the mall for a couple of days.  It's the way to go.

Typical McDonald's.

Open late - and thats a win when you need a burger at 1 am.

I came here with a bachelor party group on a Saturday evening.  We sat in the back, and first ordered our drinks and some oysters.  Not a very impressive beer selection...and pretty hefty on the pricing.  The oysters came out and were excellent.  This was my first time doing raw oysters and I was impressed...but then again, it's pretty hard to screw up raw oysters....guess I'll give more credit to the Gulf of Mexico on that one.  Next, for my meal, I ordered the duck confit and white bean cassoulet with bacon and sausage.  The meal came out and I first went for the duck wing.  It was simply roasted with some seasonings.  Very tender and very good tasting.  Of course, it seems pretty hard to screw this up too.  I'll give more credit to the duck.  Next came the garlic sausage.  This was not good.  It was a giant six inch long sausage, about 1.5 inches in diameter....just a giant chunk of meat that didn't have much taste.  It was overall pretty bland.  I don't know where the garlic they were talking about is in it.  Next was the smoked bacon.  It was more of a bacon cube.  Just a fatty piece of pork belly....which was almost all fat.  Not impressive.  Last came the white bean cassoulet.  This was also very unimpressive.  I'm not sure what seasonings they added to this or if they added any at all.  It was just white beans with cheesy/mooshy tasteless stuff in between topped with breadcrumbs.  Very, very unimpressive.  Overall, I was very unimpressed with this place, especially considering the reviews and prices.  You're better off getting a few Krystal burgers on Bourbon...yes, I am serious.

Yuck!! This place was horrible. Bland cafeteria style food thats luke warm with no flavor. I received ""kraft"" mac n cheese from a BOX..... lmao... wow!!! & green beans from a can. Didn't even doctor them up, just directly from.. the.. can... Never again. Even the hot chocolate was gross n made with WATER

this place is amazing. don't let the exterior fool you. 

i had lost all hope for any decent ethnic food in tucson after trying almost a couple dozen, but praise the lord, thanks to  sher-e-punjab, all faith is restored. 

my bf and i had a great dinner last night. so many flavors wrapped up in each dish, even the rice had clove in it!!! the chicken tikka masala was fantastic, creaming flavorful goodness, unlike the tomato paste over at Saffron. the chicken in the korma pretty much fell apart - so amazing. and my favorite dish that i always order at an Indian restaurant, the navraton koorma; it was bursting with flavor and tons of amazing veggies and paneer!!!

we ordered everything 'spicy' and it was absolutely perfect. they aren't scared to put heat in the food, which most places in tucson seem to go the opposite route to appease all of the old retirees i assume. 

thank you for one of the very few great dinners i've had in tucson!!!

Ever since the new ownership the food quality tanked. Their old homemade Caesar salad dressing got replaced with store bought dressing and their famous chilli nachos changed for the worse. Everything seems like it is canned or store bought and it seemed like there was no fresh ingredients. After several disappointing meals I stopped eating there. Recently I returned just to have a drink and the bar smelled so bad we turned around and walked out without ever getting a drink. Used to be my spot every weekend to eat and i miss what it used to be. Our server I recognized as being there before the ownership change and she was always very friendly and an outstanding server. That is all the place has going for it now

Met Jennifer E and her hubby here for dinner.  The place is small.  There were five us is and we sat at a table for four.  The restaurant has a bar, stage for the band, and different size tables and chairs.  The food was tapas style servings.  

I ordered the beef, kimchi, rice bowl and small order of tempura shrimp.  Others at the table had : lamb sliders, pork belly, scallops, and fish tacos.  We also had an assorted cheese & meat plate to start.  For desert we had a brownie with ice cream and a marshmallow pie.  Everything I tasted was really, really good.  The band we saw was great.

Tucked away as it is on Cumberland Street, I never would've found Eatalia if it weren't for Yelp and the positive ratings it had for the place.  All of them are completely deserved, as my fiancee and I couldn'tve been more happy with every part of the dining experience.  

One of the managers and owners of the place, John, could not have been more helpful and friendly.  He even warned us that one of the specials we were ordering (the crabcakes) were a few dollars more expensive than other things on the menu, after we'd briefly complained about the misery of paying for our own wedding.  We got them anyway, and don't regret a thing, by the way -- all crabmeat, baked and served over some spicy fra diavlo sauce with garlic mashed potatoes.  I loved everything about my meal.

My fiancee got the branzino in a semi-sweet triple sec reduction sauce, and it was as good as my own dish.  Honestly, we just ended up splitting the two dishes, as it was too hard to resist either of them.

I don't Yelp much, but felt that I had to after that meal.  We're both so happy this restaurant is in our neighborhood and can't wait to go back.  (Also: Moving here from Brooklyn -- How great is BYOB???)

Last minute choice before the March for Science. Great service and really delicious service.  Daughters BFF loved the super buttery salty bread, but we did not.

Every scrap of the cinnamon French toast was eaten. The eggs were delicious. 

Excellent mimosa bucket option.  The Bloody Mary was nice and peppery, too.
By far the best Italian market I've been to! It quite busy when you get inside and the sweets are amazing!

Here is another review on a great Barber shop. I travel the country every week and ever 2 or 3 weeks I try and find a barber shop to go a clean up and shave. I drove 20 miles to this shop and I wasn't disappointed at all! 

My barber was very dedicated and focused on giving me what I wanted and making it look good. Fresh fade, lined up, and straight razor shave. All for $20 bucks. You can't beat it. I'm not sure what the normal rate is but for what I got $20 was a great deal. I just had the same thing done 3 weeks ago at a shop in Dallas and it was $80. 

Very well done I'll be back next time I'm in town. Thanks.

I drove past the Barn Attic yesterday and turned immediately around to go in and poke around:  I am SO glad that I did.  I spent 3+ hours exploring all 4 floors which are absolutely PACKED: mad props to the clothing selection, and a special shout out to  vintage greeting cards (Secretary Day FTW!), beautiful antique lamps, and stacks upon stacks of complete vintage dining sets.

I came away with 12 items for $95 (just clothing and jewelry, I wasn't furniture shopping).  As the owner told me, this is NOT a thrift store, and she is right: it is way better.  

I found the owner quirky, entirely pleasant, and exceedingly helpful and patient.  Other reviewers are correct, she will greet you and give you the rundown on what's available in her barn and try to give you an idea of the scope and volume of what she has (which is a lot ... I can think of only a few places that might rival the clothing options here, and I have never in all my days seen so much jewelry in one place, ever).  She came upon me in the lower level of the barn, where a huge selection of amazingly organized vintage clothes live.  

She let me know they measure and organize all dresses and skirts by the waist size and showed me where I could find the wall-mounted tape to get my measurements.  Being a bigger girl as far as vintage shopping goes (modern size 12, top to bottom) this way of organizing the pieces meant everything I picked to try on fit me.  Literally EVERYTHING.  All 18 pieces I tried on.  This was an unprecedented first for me.  

The items I came away with were reasonably priced (between $4 and $10 an item).  The more unique or on-trend the item, the more you'll pay.  I scored a tortoise statement necklace for $30, something we sell at the pricey retail store at which I  work at part-time in the city for a whopping $88.  Whoever says the clothing is overpriced simply has not yet taken the time to go through the considerable inventory carefully, I found a TON of reasonably priced and thoroughly unique items.  Perhaps this is because I'm used to shopping in Philadelphia where I pay more for items that are hand-picked, transported, and marked up from places like Barn Attic.  Not only are the clothes a total steal for how one-of-a-kind they are, they were not at all picked over like they are in the shops of Philadelphia or NYC.  

Some things you can find yourself, but the owner knows where absolutely everything is and will point you in the right direction with unfailing accuracy.  She assisted me with 10+ cases of jewelry, helped me shuffle and explore through trays upon trays of vintage and vintage-looking jewelry (organized by color, the perfect way to shop for costume jewelry in my opinion).  

I asked, and the owner isn't interested in selling her inventory online and shipping to customers and clearly enjoys interacting with anyone who wanders in.  If you can't handle this kind of old school personal service, shop vintage finds on eBay, which I have done many a time.  With online vintage shopping be prepared for things not to look like you thought they would or fit the way you'd hoped (or even fit at all).  

I defy you to find a vintage shop as organized, fairly priced, with a staff that's willing to actually assist you ANYWHERE in a metropolitan area.  

This is a one-of-a-kind, wondrous place to explore.  I will absolutely be back, and  soon, with as many city girls as will fit in my car.
Excellent customer service. One of the few places in the airport outside of the gates that serves alcohol. I didn't try the food. Drinks highly over-priced, but you really have no other choice
Awesome sliders!!!!! Had the shrimp special, it wss to die for.  Must have in the rotation of favorite spots!

Wish I could give it zero stars. We were there for two hours. The first one and a half were spent patiently waiting for food and a second round of drinks. During our wait, two other tables of diners left after not receiving their food. The general manager, Joe, has no idea what his staff is doing and doesnt seem to care. There were a total of three tables occupied in the entire restaurant...no one was being served. The food came out cold and dry. Terrible food and terrible service. General manager "sorry for the bad experience but please come back." TURN AROUND AND GO TO RUBY'S DINER!! It is worth the wait...there's a reason "Plate" has no line. I did not enjoy paying $60 for a lunch with terrible food and terrible service...will not do it again at Plate

A solid establishment. Q pizza was yummy, loaded with bacon. They have roasted garlic on their condiment table.
Mac and cheese was great. It's good for your soul.

Good food, good location and usually kept pretty clean.

Service is not very good at all, in fact it is the main reason for the 3 stars.

For dine-in the servers really have no experience in serving.. you may get one meal before your friends do. I ordered a slice and some garlic knots while the rest of my party ordered 2 sandwiches. The waitress brought my slice and garlic knots together, then brought the other orders about 10 minutes later... She also asked if we wanted refills on our EMPTY glasses when she brought the slice, we didn't get our drinks until we were done eating our food. The place had a total of 5 patrons ( 3 at our table ). At the time they had 2 waitresses working, 1 lady working the cash register and 3 or 4 cooks.

My other complaint is when ordering over the phone for pickup. I have ordered at all times, late/early, lunch/dinner and have given them plenty of time to finish the order 20-30 mins before I show up and still end up waiting 20 minutes for my order. I have even tried paying by CC with hopes they would make the order before I showed up... Someone needs to teach them some urgency and they would get 4-5 stars.

Food is pretty good, pizza always consistent. Stromboli's are HUGE and tasty. Garlic knots are pretty good, cheese steaks are pretty good. Wings are average.

Something happened in the time that I wrote my initial review. Broadway changed their food menu, which is now pretty limited and not nearly as tasty, and they must have had a change in staff. The wait staff is now not nearly as attentive and almost seem disinterested in providing good service. Overall, very disappointing and strange.

Love this salon.  My hair is fine and thin and Dona French always pulls out all the stops to make it look wonderful.  If you're looking for a stylist who can really cut and color hair, your search is over.  She's the best!
Family favorite of the places we ate during their visit to NOLA.  Cute atmosphere, unique (and huge!) donuts.  This is also a favorite of mine and my friends, who live here in New Orleans.

Great night again at Burger Up.  

Marshall was our awesome server with a great personality and very efficient.  We appreciated how he took care of us but also gave us space.  We were very lucky with him as a server!  

I got the mushroom and Swiss burger with truffle fries.  There were no truffle fries left on my plate.  I could have licked the sauce I just love it!  It was actually quite impressive how quickly I ate them.  My burger was just okay. I would not get it again.  Not enough mushrooms and no cooked onions.  The burger was too small for the bun and the cheese did not adhere to the toppings which made it quite a mess!  

The problems I had were:  we were sat in a seat with out backs to the bar and a few servers ran into me without apologizing .   I was as close as I could get to the table without sliding off my seat.  Also, the hostess let people hold the door open (since there was a line out the door) which created a cold jet of air directly towards my spot.  Lastly,  the hostess did not look up from her book when we were leaving to say good bye. I just really appreciate southern hospitality and Marshal has it, but the other servers lack it!

Website was wrong all week, came to see the same movie twice, was wrong both times. Had to break my 4yr old's heart TWICE trying to see Isle of Dogs. Customer service unwilling to do anything to make it right. 
Also, theatre covered in trash.

Can't beat their steakburgers.  Even though you don't have a choice of how done you want them, they are always good, even well done.  I always get the frisco burger, toxic to the coronary arteries, but delicious.

This place ROCKS!  Since my teen years (Doesnt matter how long ago that was!!) It's a MUST STOP for me & my family! 

Peanut Butter Cup PLEASE!!!  mmmmmmmmmmmMMMMM

The summer months are the most fun, but any time they are open - it's a great time!  
When the sun is beating down & you just cant stand the HEAT?  Just pull into the Frosty Boy & have a special TREAT!  haha 

Now that I'm living in California I still crave it.  I get text messages and photos from family whenever they are there - MEAN!!  haha 

You can bet I stop in EVERY single time I'm home in Indy! 

 I HEART YOU, Frosty Boy!  I HEART YOU!

Upscale and fancy are the two words that you'll never see in the same sentence with this restaurant's name. What you will hear consistently is how good the food is.... I stop in here 2-3 times per month. The ladies that work here are very nice, welcoming, and helpful. The food is always hot and tasty. I've never had a  disappointing meal here. The  lunch specials are reasonably priced, and the meal size is usually more than you can eat at the time. When I'm passing through, I always search for more Chinese restaurants, but always wind up pulling into this lot. Its really meal good enough to tell someone about.

So I usually don't complain about anything business related because I'm a pretty mellow customer, but the service here actually prompted me to make a yelp account. I walked in and everyone was just sitting around doing nothing, they were on their phones and not even asking if we needed help. I literally had to bother one of the representatives to even look at me and when she finally did, she just gave me this look like, "what the fuck does this little girl want?" I'm a college student and my phone was stolen two nights ago so I went in to get a new phone. When I explained what happened and that my mom had already spoken to a verizon customer service rep who told us it would only cost 100, she laughed in my face and told me about all these extra charges that would make it closer to 200. Then when I had her explain the extra charges and information to my mom over the phone, she was completely rude and soooo disrespectful. Granted, my mom can be a bit abrasive at times but I was listening to the entire conversation and it did not warrant the response that Brenda (the sales rep) had. My mom was talking about how she had received different information than what Brenda had told her, this bitch actually held the phone away from her face IN FRONT OF ME. How dumb could you be?! My friend and I also overheard her talking about how irritating my mom was being when she went into the back room and even 30 feet away from us. She made several remarks and comments about my mom and the information she was "trying to make her understand," and I was literally infuriated. Then once I had paid for my phone I was on my friends phone telling my mom the total and explaining the process etc and Brenda didnt even say have a nice day or goodbye once the sale was finished, she simply walked into the back room without anther word. I told one of the other very nice sales women that I was very disappointed and she seemed more sincere than the lady who had worked with me. I really wish I'd spoken to her instead. So basically, DO NOT GET BRENDA. Unless you feel like getting irritated and pissed off!

I am shocked at what happened when trying to redeem a groupon.  The "owner" as she titled herself, said the$55 valued groupon wasn't valid for grooming services... only spa services and there would be additional charges to get our dog groomed.  It seems like she is upset she used groupon for marketing and trying to scam customers for an additional charge.  I would NEVER support this business and recommend if pets are treated like people....BUYER BEWARE!!! My advice is go somewhere else!

Love this place!!! Always something adventurous and delicious on tap, only gripe is that it's not closer to me lol.  The main tasting room is small but cozy, during warmer weather the outdoor bar and seating is available.  If you are in the area, it's well worth it to check out for a brew.

Love their fried okra and smoked chicken wings. The pork sandwich was good, but wish they would put a scoop of coleslaw on it. Next time I'm going to try the smoked turkey sandwich.

No beer for sale. :(
I'm not a big bar-hop, but if I lived in NOLA, I would frequent this place. I rally liked the look and the drinks.

Benefitting from the limited options available in Bala, La Collina is the epitome of a traditional Italian restaurant.  Uninspired menu of things like chicken Parmesan, and tortellini soup.  The waiters, while pleasant, were all very old and slow,  I'll be back, but only because its the only real option for a business lunch in the neighborhood.

Happy fish, take some notes. The ceviche at Cuenelli's is amazing! The fish is cut into small pieces, little to no membrane on the fish, and the ceviche is flavorful and it is refreshing. Every bite allowed my tastebuds to go on a new adventure, from spicy to zesty to tangy. The onions and the accompaniments to the ceviche were also amazing and fresh. The fried yuca was crispy and although lacking in flavor, it was delicious when it was dunked into the juice of the ceviche. The service was attentive and the ceviche came out in ten minutes. Unlike a lot of Latin American restaurants, the exterior and the interior had a clean and modern look. Overall, the best Peruvian restaurant in Tampa!

Drinks we had were great, our server was outgoing and friendly. This would be a great place to stop by for some drinks or desert, but the food was seriously disappointing. I ordered the Friday special, enchiladas la bamba, which turned out to be just a really plain taco casserole on top of tortilla chips. Really nothing special about it at all. My date ordered the chicken pesto, which turned out to be the type of frozen chicken with the grill lines painted on it. As I said, the food was a major disappointment and I would not recommend it, but the drinks were good and the atmosphere was nice and appealing.

This shop was one of the worst I've ever been to. I called in advance to make an appointment for a simple oil change. When I brought the vehicle at 10:45 for an 11:00 appointment it took over an hour just to get it into the garage. It was not completed until 1:00 and at that time the cashier told me she doesn't know how to process a fleet vehicle and would have to wait for a manager. She then said the manager is on a conference call which usually takes about 30 minutes. Poor service and concept of time. I will never be back to this shop and if you cherish the time in your day I suggest you don't either. I would have given them negative stars if it was possible. Oh yea they also charged $98 for the oil change and new wiper blades.

What are these people talking about, they must work for the restaurant. My girlfriend and I ate here today and the food was bland, microwaved, and horrible presentation. Not to mention it was pricey for how horrible it was, $65 for 2 of us. If you want real italian food Arugula is right down the road. Don't waste your time or money. Very disappointing.

They're not getting even one star from me!  First, we were told we'd be charged a fee for paying cash.  Then, after using our card, they charged us 3 times.  When we called and complained they were completely uncooperative.  We called later to speak with the manager and weren't connected to one.  This place also needs new carpet! DO NOT STAY HERE.

I know how hard it is to leave your pet.  But, if you have to leave them - this is a really nice place.  I have boarded my dog here several times in the past year.  He is well taken care of.  The staff is very friendly and helpful.  Cannot say enough about The Lodge at New Tampa...... Excellent!!

I initially heard about The Beauty Parlour from friends. Every time they went to this salon they'd come back with gorgeous haircuts & colours. After one particularly bad haircut, I decided to try out the Parlour.
According to their website, The BP believes in beauty with a conscience. They offer ammonia-free colour services with little or no scent properties or chemical emanation. They also stock Kevin Murphy products, of which I am a fan. 
Anyways, after walking up the stairs  to their 2nd floor location (note:no elevators) I immediately feel comfortable in their spacious, tranquil salon. I feel relaxed here, and I enjoy the vintage-y ambiance created by their reclaimed furnishings and wood flooring. It's also got high windows with views of Whyte Ave.
The friendly receptionist usually offers wine (!), coffee, green tea, or juice.While waiting for my stylist Alysha, I check out their mini-boutique. Clothing from local designer Cinder+Smoke and jewelry from local artist Plum Tipsy are among the fun products they stock.
I always get my hair done by Alysha. She listens as I attempt to describe what i want, and my hair turns out gorgeous every time. She cuts with precision and doesn't use the razor much to texture my coarse,thick hair.
I highly recommend Alysha!
Because I have short hair, I am charged for a men's cut ($60), so it's very reasonable, in my opinion, for an exceptional salon.  Also, you get 5% off if you pay with cash!
I love this place, it's a high quality salon experience without pretention.

Warning! This review is based strictly on ambiance. My friend Erin S. wanted some pub food and a good beer to go along with it so Brew Brothers it was. Whoops...at first I thought we were in Rum Bullions.  

I actually thought I had been transported back to Gorak Shep for a brief oxygen deprived moment as a noxious cloud of billowing cigar smoke descended upon us like a shroud. Erin asked if we could sit 'outside' for the fresher air. Unfortunately, this was the type of cigar that not even my grandfather would have smoked as the cloying smell permeated every corner of this restaurant. 

We ended up leaving and not having any food or drinks so this review is simply for the mere existence of the place and the optimism that the smell will have dissipated prior to our next visit.

I live just down the road from this place so I was excited to find a good pie shop near me. I went with my family and felt disappointed. The pizza was average at best. My wife and I both felt that it wasn't worth the money. The wait was LONG, we are patient people so we usually don't mind but eventually we wondered if we had been forgotten sitting out on the patio. Maybe our expectations were too high from the reviews but we won't be going back.
Kevin does an amazing job on acrylics. Clean new salon. Very friendly staff and open sundays!!

You wouldn't expect such a nice dining area in a shopping center pizza shop.. I really enjoy a sit down dinner here.  Quiet, pleasant atmosphere, generous portions and delicious food ! 

Couldn't give a 5 star review though because I have found pizza shop staff and hostesses to be consistently "snotty" and often uninterested to serve. Sorry ladies!

This place is seriously good! Priced reasonably at $7.95 for a signature or build your own. We love the Art Lover!

Quick & friendly service, very clean and high quality ingredients.
Always quick and efficient. I don't have a regular person I go to, but can always rely on a great Brazilian wax. Not super pricey and always have times available.

Carrot cake slice was yummy -- full of good stuff and moist.

Eclair -- didn't stand a chance once my husband got it.

Hazelnut cake -- got it for my for her 70th birthday and she and the family were thrilled.  Their mom had gotten the same cake for years (under previous owners).  The pressure was on, and Swiss Haus delivered.

Went into Petit Piquant to get something to eat and needed to use the restroom first and they said we don't have one you can try the library, which was closed. Needless to say scary part of town walking next door to the library! I went back and said anywhere else? They said gas station down the street. No thanks! Homeless people and sketchy outside everywhere! Now was going to go to the bathroom after breakfast. Ordered the short rib Benedict that was on their menu and they said they didn't have it! They didn't have a restroom for customers or food that was on their menu!  I won't be back!
The service from Elsie was excellent. The food as always was great. Very busy on a Saturday morning but the staff handles that great.
Got the Tennessee burger and was not disappointed. It was cooked just right and the flavor was great. Ordered a side of tots and they were fresh and flavorful. would definitely recommend.

NO "NEW TRACK RECORD" HERE... YET

Barbecue and Bourbon has a good Speedway, Ind., location and concept.... It's just that their service, portions and prices were somewhat disappointing. 

Small (read that McD's hamburger sized) BBQ sandwich, out-of-the-bag chips and a soft drink totaled $10-15 with tip. OUCH!

They may have been pricey, because they had a lot of employees on the clock (talking to one another and not the customers, which they out-numbered). 

Give them some time.... Hopefully, they'll adjust and improve.
Good food. Nice atmosphere with great outdoor and indoor seating. Came here twice in a span of 1 week. Staff were friendly.
Probably the best squid salad we've had! The sushi was fresh and delicious.  The outside seating was nice and dog friendly!

I'll make it quick.

1. Received a recall on my car in January. Got it fixed end of April. Why? Because the first time I had an appointment in February, they scheduled me, then cancelled me 1 hr before my app. (Mind you I was in town from the bay for the weekend and didn't have much time to spend at a car dealer but planned it into my plans anyway) why canceled? Because they didn't realize they don't have the parts. Told me in February and in March they would have them within a week. Nothing. Every time I called. Airbags deploying with  shrapnel flying out...their fault. Who is driving around all these years with this hazard me? Who should be fixing it ASAP? Toyota!!!

2. Mid April I received two more recalls....haven't heard from them yet on parts. Apparently will receive a second letter in the mail...however did not happen with first recall.

3. The guy who took care of my paper work asked me to give him 5 stars if I receive a survey on service, stating that anything below will look bad for him. Nice guy, odd request, but I thought hey okay no problem! Soon as I got into my car I noticed they didn't been place the airbag lid on correctly wth! 


4. Oil change went fine here. 

5. Estimates are crazy. Do some minor research and do the repairs yourself. 
Lights toyota est. $50, I did it for $10. Air filter (glove compartment) toyota $80, me $5. Air filter engine toyota $40, me $10.

5. Also bought my Toyota here...they asked me if I've been here before. Really? Brush up on customer service!
Service was quick and prompt.  Had a nice selection of remnants which is all I needed this trip.  I will be back!

Fresh authentic Mexican food! Their avocado and salsa is to die for! I love their steak tacos also.. also have a tasty tamarind drink. I've tried almost everything on the menu and nothing is disappointing.

First, we LOVE the wings here and visit this place pretty regularly HOWEVER, the service seems to have declined to a level that has made us seek out another wing place to give our business to.   A couple of months ago I called to place a call in order and was told to hold.  The person who answered put the phone down and I waited for 10 minutes before giving up.   Last Friday, I went in to pick my order up and the person who rang me up couldn't be bothered to interrupt his conversation with another employee so he had to run my card twice because the first time it was done incorrectly. Finally, last night  I called to place an order and AGAIN was left on hold for over 11 minutes.  I ended up ordering from a place that is 5 minutes out of my way but seemed to be worth the drive since that establishment picked up on the second ring and took my order immediately.   Again, great food but not good enough to deal with the inconsistent service.
Nice staff. Very pleasant. Pizza was very good. Spicy sauce was excellent. Quick and cheap.

They will only sell bottles of water.  Owner too cheap to give glass of tap water to take a pill! Now the rest of my review:  My mom just moved to the area and I drove up from Tampa to take her to lunch.  I love dive bars like Rick's on the River and Skippers in Tampa, so I thought I'd really like Sams.  Upon arrival the waitress came and sat us.  I wanted to order a margarita and a glass of water, but she refused to serve me a glass of water and advised that I'd have to buy a bottle of water for $1.69 instead.  I used to tend bar back in my college days and I'm pretty sure it's required by the health department and probably some other agency that water is available for customers.  Plus, what if I wanted a scotch and water?  Hmm.  Anyway, I ordered a wedge salad and it was huge.  With the huge salad came one small side of dressing.  When I requested more dressing to use on my entire salad the waitress said she'd order more for me.  I asked her what that meant "order," and she said it forty cents.  Now, I know that is not a lot of money, but really???  She stated that the owner has determined how much dressing is adequate for a salad--as if customers don't have various preferences when it comes to salads.  NOT customer-oriented at all.  They are lucky they have such a good location because that place would sink with that kind of ownership were it not not for the Gulf.   One star for selection of food and view.
Great Besh restaurant Mardi Gras day morning. Service was good. Food outstanding. But no caffeinated latte only decaf and grounds in the regular coffee made for a less than stellar morning

Came for dinner Sunday night. The food and bar program were outstanding, as was the decor but I have to say one of my favorite parts was your staff.  They are beyond compare.  Thank you for the wonderful dining experience, especially enjoyed the tuna tartare and the goat. xxoo.

The best breakfast, lunch, brunch spot in Tucson hands down. The food is great. The staff are the best, even new hires prep and pastry knows how to pick who is right for the job. Chefs at both locations are spot on. I love the food there. I've nearly tried the entire menu, and always up for what chef Hannah has to offer with the French toast. I love both locations central and east

Interesting decor - Old Hollywood - meets Art deco?  There's something kinda old, but also something kinda modern about the place.  While the menu is somewhat limited, the food is very good. The roast beef is tasty, though I had a hard time tasting the horseradish that was supposed to be on it.   The home cooked crunchy potato chip are Yum. This place has very good service -  a good place to have lunch with friends.

Great location for dinner and music if you want to avoid the crowds on Bourbon Street. We had the bulgogi with fried egg, steak and crab cake, mac and cheese -- all amazing! Their signature cocktail "The Muse" was delicious, we would definitely go back on our next trip to NOLA. Tip, reservations are a must. You still might wait 5-10 minutes but it's worth it!

Don Day! How did I not know about this place till I used the Yelp app on my phone to locate a restaurant near by. I am glad I stumbled upon this joint as there aren't that many Korean places to in Edmonton.

I came around 2pm during the week and there some diners finishing up but the place was not packed. I was greeted by a very polite Korean lady who guided us to our table. She came with menus and corn tea quickly. We noticed many lunch specials for $10 like bulgogi, and teriyaki beef/chicken. My friend opted the bulgogi which came with noodles and miso soup. I ordered the pork bone soup with rice which hit the spot. The soup was flavorful with a good amount of spice and hotness. The kim chi was savoury and delicious. Wasn't a big fan of the pickled onions but that didn't ruined the meal by any means.

The K-pop music videos playing on their mounted big screen tv brought good vibes. The Korean posters/ads on the wall brought a bit of nostalgia to the place as well. Their decor is not what will bring you in here but their food makes up for it. My friend was also happy with his bulgogi by the way!

Me and my girlfriend had the Tequila Patron Pairing for two and was great. The service was excellent and the food was very well prepared and tasty. It was a complete experience. The Guacamole is to die for and the Huarache de Hongos is really really good. I definitely recommend this restaurant.

I attended an event there. You would think an event which draws in strangers to your business would be an opportunity to show your best?  I'll just say the service was not bad. IT SIMPLY DID NOT EXIST. SIXTEY OR SO PEOPLE STUCK IN THE SAME ROOM FOR OVER FIVE HOURS.  TWO SERVERS.  WHO.WERE NEVER EVER TRAINED AT THEIR JOBS.    What do I know.  I only eat out ten meals a week or more.  Shoot yourself in the foot?   The sad part is the food is good when it arrives within the hour.

Let me first mention that Penca is one of our favorite restaurants in Tucson. We eat there often and take out of town visitors there, too. So yesterday (5/4/2017) my husband and I took a visitor, whom we had told before in glowing terms about the outstanding food and the great cocktails to Penca for dinner. Imagine our utter disappointment and embarrassment when we experienced a complete breakdown of the kitchen - and the bar. First, they were out of three items we tried to order, and that was just us. But okay, can happen, no big deal. However every single dish we were actually able to order, was tasteless and just not up to their usual level. As a starter we ordered the guacamole y salsa. The guacamole was bland and gooey, no lime juice, cilantro etc. There was also a little bowl of cubed tasteless tomatoes - don't know what that was supposed to be, pico de gallo? No onions, cilantro, peppers, lime juice anywhere to be found. The third little bowl contained some green tasteless sauce - tomatillo salsa?  The menu states "topped with queso fresco" - nowhere to be seen. 
The tacos which are usually outstanding were a huge disappointment. The tortillas were soggy and fell apart, instead of rolling them up and eating them with your fingers you had to eat them with knife and fork, because they broke down into pieces. Maybe there were one or two nopalitos in the nopales taco, but mostly red cabbage. The guajolote contained hard dried pieces of turkey. Chipotle cream?, green onions? Nothing. The Mancha Manteles was more or less okay, except the pork chop was a bit on the dry side and so were the masa cakes, not much mole there, too. Maybe they ran out of the moles, cilantro and limes, too. 
We finished with the usually great churros, which were - you guessed it - not fluffy with a crunchy crust, but one was overcooked, the other undercooked. 
We had told our visitor, that Penca is one of the best places for good cocktails. But not only was the kitchen in disarray, but there seems to have been no professional bartender around either, even though plenty of people were standing behind the bar - perhaps to many? Maybe they ran out of tequilas and mezcals, too, because our cocktails (all five of them) contained so little alcohol they were completely unbalanced -  basically sugar water. Very embarrassing to have described those as some of the best cocktails in Tucson. These days, where one can find fantastic cocktails in great restaurants and bars it is surprising to be confronted which such unambitious (or inexperienced) bartenders who honestly should be ashamed to push an unbalanced ten dollar glass of sugar water on the customer. Two stars, because the ambience and the server were still great, but the kitchen and bar deserve zero.

I took the time to write this review, because I don't want Penca to go downhill like so many other restaurants in Tucson which started out great and for some reason became mediocre and eventually had to close. I certainly hope this was a one time incident. Please get your act together, don't cut corners and hire experienced, intelligent chefs, and bartenders.

I was really disappointed today. I guess like any place that caters to walk-ins it matters much who you get for your service, even though I scheduled my appointment 2 days in advance. I would say for this type of Salon (walk ins welcome) it was my first $35 pedicure that took less than 30 minutes, not quite the relaxing experience I had hoped for on my Sunday afternoon treat. 

 It was get em in and get em out mentality. My manicure was below average too, I was not asked to wash my hands between filing and applying polish, and I did not receive lotion or hand rub like the people around me. I can see the polish from my previous manicure on the sides of my nails even after my new manicure was finished.
 Overall average to below-average service with a slightly above average price. I will not be going back.

This business never ceases to amaze me. They place the customer first and they understand the concerns of the customer, especially when they are faced with the uncertainty of an unknown repair and the costs associated with. I came in with a troubled idle problem on my 2004 Jeep Grand Cherokee and the mechanic there diagnosed it within minutes and the part arrived a few minutes later. I was on my way in less than an hour. Their prices were very reasonable. I am very glad I found this place.

Shoutout to the barista with the awesome dinosaur shirt. Just as a mark of authenticity, my three drink order came out to $10 even. I didn't get your name, but you were great!
To the rest of the staff- thanks!

This place is legit! The portions are good for the price, the service is friendly, and the food comes out pretty quickly. The space is small, so there is often a waiting list, but it's worth the wait. I do wish there were more vegetable dishes on the menu. Vegetarians will have a hard time here.

Love their food! If you are looking for a great steak, pork chops, fish or an assortment of cheeses, this is the place for you! They have choice and prime cuts of meat. Not only can you get the best high quality meats, but they also have a deli case you can get all different types of sides (twice baked potatoes, broccoli salad, baked beans, grape and feta pasta, orzo salad or a wide selection of dessert bars). They have a huge selection of wine to pair with your food. Lunch time they make sandwiches to go or sit there and eat. Always great food! I am never 
disappointed. If you haven't been there yet, you must give it a try!

We went on a Saturday around 11:30, they didn't have too many vegan options and no plant based protein option which is always disappointing and why I'm giving 3 instead of 4. The ambiance was excellent - decor and design was clean, modern and beautiful. They food was pretty good, I didn't like how they brought everything out when it was ready so each person's meal came out separately so we were all sitting there til the last one arrived.

Look no further, the best photographer in Chicago! As brides you know once you get engaged, your on the hunt for your perfect wedding vendors. In my case, the first stop was Redwall Photography. We knew that photography was one of our biggest "wants" in our wedding because photos can show so much emotion in a still shot! Well it was a December evening and it was a few weeks after we got engaged and once we met Tasha that night, we knew that this was the company we were going to go with. Like I said..look no further. She walked us through some examples of her work and talked through all the options - that alone sold us how dedicated she was to her work. Once we booked, everything else was made so easy by Tasha, with constant communication & understanding of what we wanted. Our engagement session was so much fun and she made us feel so comfortable! Her husband Aaron is so awesome too!! They make a great team. Fast forward to our wedding day, logistics were quite difficult for our wedding causing a lot of movement and craziness but Tasha & Aaron were able to manage it quite well and seemed to be everywhere at one time! She captured so many great memories that we will cherish ALWAYS! People constantly contact me to ask who our photographer was and that they LOVED our photos! Makes me feel so good that we knew we made the right choice. Tasha at Redwall Photography is someone that makes you feel like you've known her forever and makes your wedding experience that much better!

We will be using Tasha for our other memories we'd like to capture!

Thanks again, Tasha

Let me start out by saying Edward Josimov Director of operations with Lex is Awesome. I celebrated my 36th birthday here in VIP and it was a memorable night. Everything was Perfect. The staff is very attentive and nice. The ladies are on top of Everything. If you have a special occasion Definitely consider Lex VIP. I Promise you won't be sorry. We are regular patrons here and we are looking forward to continuing enjoy this beautiful adult club. Thanks for Everything.
The Davis's

Omg grrr. Two visits. Not one. So I'm not just hitting them on a bad shift, or picking the single slow cashier. Omg. I'm standing in check out, both times checkout took longer than I spent shopping. SLOW is not the term. Reading a sign in front of me:"Threes a Crowd" stating they will open another register if they see three people in line. Hah. Now my intelligence is being insulted. Like I can't count over three??  (What's four and five...nine)....  Not even close. I think I counted five or six each, in the two lanes that were open at nine pm on a Saturday nite. The following day, several lanes open but None moving. Two folks had bags of ice, I wanted tell them it would be melted by the time they escaped the store.  ALSO Be aware if you are visiting Carpinteria, they've gone bagless...bring your own bag. But they were cool about that. Which is why they get two stars. Prices high, but what's new at Albertsons.

Half price sushi EVERY DAY!!  I am in heaven! This was our first time. We were there tonight (Friday night) the place was full...that's a good sign. The service was slow but we were not in a rush as we were dining with friends. The food was worth the wait. We just moved to this area and it will become our go-to place for sushi.  The staff is friendly too! Check it out.  The Osaka salad is wonderful!!!

I really love Angela - the owner of the new Wings to Go on the Corner of Vine & 15th.

So, I ordered a bunch of party platters (boneless wings & buffalo shrimp) for a party I had.  Everything was piping hot, fresh and perfect.

I really want people to support this much needed busines on an otherwise "dead" block.  Need wings?  Catfish?  Shrimp?  Corndogs?  Come here to get them.

I opened up my email today to find out The Body Shop reduced their clearance product down another twenty percent so I stopped by here on my way home today to pick up a couple more spiced apple shower gels before they retired the scent,

From the outside this store looks smaller but once you step inside it does go quite a ways back and I think they carry everything the other locations do just in smaller quantities out on the sales floor. Visually I find it very appealing as everything looks so neat and organized which makes it easy to find what your looking for.

In terms of the customer service here I personally found it flawless. The lady working stopped what she was doing to greet me and offer assistance then when I told her I was just looking she went back to her task. I generally enjoy browsing on my own so this was just the right level of engagement for me.

Overall as a franchise I think The Body Shop suffered a little bit when Bath and Body Works made their way to Edmonton due to how much more expensive they are as compared to B&BW. I think they are worth it though due to how many more "real" ingredients they use in their products as well as the amount of fundraising they do for women's charities. I also really like their loyalty program because even though the card is ten dollars they essentially give you your money back on your birthday by offering a ten dollar discount to you during your birthday month.

It's a great company and this location does well at maintaining that standard of excellence that The Body Shop has created and maintained since the first day they opened their doors.

Fresh food and BYOB is an ultimate plus!!! We had so much fun at this restaurant and our waiter was awesome. The weather was gorgeous outside, so to be able to sit-n-eat with the great sun, made the experience event better.

I had the breakfast bomb and my honey had the honey cristo. Both great choices for brunch, and we had a side of chorizo which was packed with flavor and the right amount of spice. The orange juice even tasted fresh with our sparkling wine-spumante. 

This place is definitely for foodies!

Had a breakfast here (as Kimpton guests), which was the worst hotel breakfast we've experienced ever. 
As we walked in no any kind of greetings or smile, just a  sit where you want gesture.

Had: a) BEET ME (a small glass of supposedly beet, carrot, ginger and cilantro raw juice, which in reality was filled with 2 huge cylinders of ice taking the 2/3 of the space in a glass and the rest of the space was filled with UNDRINKABLE mess of awfully tasted beet and ginger juice with nowhere found carrot or cilantro flavor). And this is coming from the person who LOVES raw juices and familiar with many flavors of them. Otherwise why would I ordered this mess for the price of the $9 ?!?! for THIS??? 
         b) Supermarket quality bagel and Croissant with the slice of Philadelphia Cream Cheese bought in some of those Warehouses (like BJ'S or Sam's, no condiments like jams or jellies coming with them) for $4 each?!
         c) 2 cups of not good tasting coffee (no milk until asked, no refills offered) for $4 each?!

And then comes the question from the waitress "How did you like it?"
Well, she received our honest opinion about how we liked it, and after hearing it, said with of course an attitude: "If you didn't like it you don't have to pay for it", which actually was the only positive (and I would say fare) part of our experience in this place. Paying about $30 for a minimal breakfast for 2 should include much more hospitality, taste and satisfaction than was offered to us here.

My husband stayed in this hotel twice in October. Once for a period of one week and second time for three days. he left his expensive tie,, shampoo and conditioners in the room. He left the hotel went to court and directly to airport. There was no other stop. He tried to contact the hotel and ask about the tie. He was very unsuccessful the get any results. He could not get connected to the housekeeping and the front desk people would not return the calls. Eventually after calling twice and numerous emails, they denied the there was any tie turned in to their lost and found! It seems to me that they have a  MAJOR trustworthiness housekeeping issues on top oft badly managed guest relation services.. We will never stay at any Doubletree hotel again..
Tampa dive bar.  Fabulous. Friendly staff makes all the difference.  The sandwiches are huge.

I come here when visiting family in the area. Not every week but often enough. Service is average, but they accommodate a lot of people quickly. Once walked in with a group of six and they didn't bat an eye. Handled the group quickly and efficiently. Sometimes they are too quick and nail color is not applied too well. I wish they could speak English to be able to communicate more easily.

I expected this place to be quiet on a Monday night, but it was almost completely empty when we went around 8:45pm. I don't like dining at places that are not busy...it makes me uncomfortable. 

Anyway, I had the pomegranate martini which was tasty as most of their martini's are. I don't know what it is about their house salads, but they are the best!!! They have avocado in them and this very yummy cheese and it was my favorite part of the meal. Their fries still get me every time as they have this special spice mix on them that makes them unique to any other fries I have tasted! 

I hope this place still gets good business on other nights as I would hate to see it go!

P.S. Their kitchen is open til midnight everynight! I like it!
The main reason I love this place is because they have sugar free froyo. They always have great tasting flavors.
have now tried the traditional pizza, and it's quite good. the crust is my style. not too greasy. delivery was quick.

I had read reviews and they sounded good so I got my husband to agree to go there. It was dinner so that is the menu we ate from. What a disappointment. 
There is a selection from chicken to fish to steak and shrimp.  But nothing was interesting or even that appetizing.  Weird combos like steak and grits, on a dinner menu? I love duck but is just sounded bad. We looked at each other and said this place will not last in New Orleans. And that was before we ate anything. 
I asked him if he wanted to go somewhere else and he said no, let's give it a try. Being so unimpressed I opted for a fried catfish plate. Should be predictable and easy, right?  Undercooked fries, cheap hush puppies and catfish worthy of a gas station. Husband also went for something that should be easy to get right, shrimp Alfredo. Well, frozen shrimp, over-reheated pasta and an odd pink sauce later, we learned it is possibly to make a completely mediocre version.  
Wait staff was fine. We were the only ones in there (should have been our first clue) and we got reasonable attention, I thought--till we left. I hadn't noticed it when we walked in, but just outside the door was a board with daily specials. Our waitress never said a peep about it. Perhaps it was because she was busy with all the empty tables.   
Don't bother. For the prices, there are so many better places to go.  FYI--My husband said I need to do a better job of research before he will do that again! LOL!

Came hungry and left satisfied. Tuna melt with a tomato soup fit the bill on a windy and cold florida day.  When most other restaurants have a wait at international mall, you can order your food and enjoy and continue on your merry way.  Maybe I just lucked out but only waited about 5 minutes for my pager to blink and my tummy satisfied.

Yep, the service still sucks, but who cares when you're planted in a hot steaming bowl of kimchi stew.  I could wax poetic about their kimchi...they must put crack in it, it's ADDICITIVE.

I wish they would sell their kimchi by the jar.

I just drove into town. Wanted to eat before checking into my hotel. Passed a string of the typical fast food joints. Then nothing. Was about to turn around-to settle when I spotted Joey B's. I had been there once before and I turned right in.
Sat in the bar. Got a menu right away. Was struggling with what to get-burger-wrap-Philly style... Then the waitress came up and announced the special and took away any doubt-any uncertainty. Just two words, Sloppy Joes. A great Joe is great food. I've had great Joes- I make awesome Joes. I ordered without hesitation.

Didn't have to wait long at all- it arrived along with my fries. I've only ever seen Joes with the goods in excess-promising to drip out should I dare to lift and eat. I did not need to worry the goods didn't even make it to the edges. It was also covered with a white melted cheese. Odd but I try new things.

Thank God for the cheese- it provided about the only taste. The tasted like three ingredients, ground beef, ketchup and the cheese. So bland, so disappointing. As to the fries, not house cut, likely frozen and equally bland. Pretty much the total experience-bland nothing special at all. Seems like they need a Joe throw down so as to experience a tasty Joe.

Cured is just what the East side has been waiting for! I finally found my new go-to salon :) I got a gel manicure and regular ped (they call these "Quickies." Don't let that name fool you though, my technician did meticulous and precise work on both my feet & hands. I was there for about an hour. Definitely make an appointment, they'll honor your time even if a walk-in is waiting. Total was $85 with tip. 

PARKING- Park in lot to the left of Cured (next to electric tattoo) or on the street Petway. Don't park in lot behind salon.

Living in the great southwest, we have just recently began to enjoy the benefits known to most mid-westerners as Custard.  Culver's and Freddie's have opened franchises in our area, and I have enjoyed their products. I went to Ted's last night on a lark, because it was written up in a "What to do in St.Louis" type article to find out if what we have now compares.....NOT even close!  Whenever I try a new food or item, I have standard orders I use to compare.  Hot Fudge Sundae is mine for Ice Cream and Ted's is the best I've had.  Period.  Luckily I ordered the Super-sized and enjoyed spoon after spoon.  It's the closest to home made hot fudge I've had.  The simplicity of vanilla and hot fudge allowed me to savor every bite.  Now I have to find a way to return to St. Louis to enjoy this great treat!

Like many others I'm still confused as to why there is an umlaut in Lüke. I almost laughed out loud when the couple next to me thought that there would be German food served. Silly nolans. 

I came here due to the fact this place was walking distance to my hotel - well at least my original hotel reservation at Intercontinental. 

It was "We Live to Eat" week in NOLA which was an equivalent of restaurant week. So I made reservations to try their prefix menu.

I started off with the oysters (not part of the prefix menu). They were really good and fresh. I was disappointed I missed out on the happy hour special as I would totally come back for the oysters. 

For the prefix menu I had: 

Lobster and ricotta stuffed squash blossoms
This had an interesting lime-y taste - yet savory. The thing I can compare it to is the lime, salt, pepper sauce you dip french cube beef in. The squash blossoms were good and the lobster was a bit negligible. 

Slow cooked swordfish with heirloom tomato, olive, caper, garganelli
If I learned anything on this trip, it is that I don't care much for green olives. I don't know what I was expecting with this dish -  and I think this is my fault for perhaps not reading  the menu carefully or asking questions. I suppose this is a good dish if you like swordfish, tomato sauce and green olives - however because I don't like those things that much I really shouldn't have gotten dish dish. 

Fig tart, brown butter ice cream
This is really good if you like fig newtons. It was basically a giant fig tart with ice cream. It was pretty good - but I don't care for figs that much. The ice cream was delicious though. 

In all I couldn't really understand the flavors that were presented at Lüke for restaurant week. I think the ambiance is great for an after work kinda deal as it's very french brasserie. The happy hour specials I understand for the oysters are also very good. I would come back for happy hour if I lived in the area.

I am one of the few reviewers to have gone when it wasn't Restaurant Week.   I'm pleased to say that the service here is what you should expect from a fine dining restaurant including the ever so fancy amuse bouche.

The entree pairings were  unique and the servers were excited to educate you about them.  For instance, as a complement to my tuna I had purple rice , which was new to me.  The server was happy to tell me it came from Japan and brought me out a plate of what it looks like dried, even suggested where to purchase some.  

There is a lot of space in the restaurant and the servers keep their distance so it is a great place for a business dinner.  For those of you who are not so fortunate to expense this dinner, with entrees costing about $30 ea, you may find pleasure in knowing two tidbits:
1) Tuesdays are BYOB nights 
2)  Fridays have $35 three course menus

If you are going with someone who is handicapped, I'd suggest calling ahead because the restrooms are on the second floor and I did not see an elevator.

Manny was so nice helped me with my cabin air filter and then went the awesome extra step and installed it for me!  I really appreciated it. He saved me money and time.   Thanks for the wonderful customer service!!!

My partner and I were overall fans of the Jamaican Jerk Hut. Small, quaint place with a long wait - but definitely worth it if you're into some spicy, unique food. Definitely beware that when they say spicy - it means SPICY! I usually like hot wings, but they were over the top a bit for me. My partner loved the heat, though (even though he was sweating from it).

The coconut shrimp is delicious - well battered, tasty, crisp, with sweet coconut milk.
Also loved their chicken soup.
The wings were SUPER spicy, couldn't get through them, but my boyfriend loved it. The flavor beneath the heat was divine. 
The quarter jerk chicken was also good - but we definitely should have gotten the sauce on the side. The wings were hot enough, so we couldn't get through the chicken.


We loved it here, but I actually don't think we'll be going back. It seemed like after you tried a few things, the flavors meshed together, and weren't quite as unique as they first seemed. A good find in the city, especially if you like to try different food - but not necessarily my go-to place. I was expecting a bit more, but was still pleased!

Outstanding! I've eaten here for years and it's always consistently great. The only negative is that they don't have air conditioning, so we can get a little uncomfortable for me temperature wise.
Their cranberry barley salad is one of my favorites. Got the quinoa and kale salad as well as chicken salad. All three were excellent. And it's cheap!

Food and Service is excellent.  I take every guest who visits me here!!!  The best part of this location is the people who work here.  I have been known to dabble in one person dinner parties at the bar.  Every time i am greeted with a smile and great conversation.  Will continue to come back!

We went on a Sunday at lunch time. We stood in line to order for about 1hour. Food was good, but a bit cold once when we got it. It took about 30min to get our food. We are from Texas, so we have high expections for BBQ. I would have rated it a 3/4, but unfortunately there was a tiny baby roach crawling across our table after we finished our food. I wish I could say we'd  be back, but most likely not.

People were way too harsh on this place when they were first opening. We need to up their rating. Taco Tuesday is the best here (shout out to the Barbacoa). Wait staff is super friendly. This place is great. Come check it out!

prepare to break up with your current dentist! as the reviews speak for themselves - fast, friendly and very affordable, not to mention a fantastic job done. cannot suggest them enough, especially for those of us who prefer to private pay. high marks all around.
Good food, great value, friendly service. You get a lot of food for the money if you order the combo!

Thai food is one of my favorite types of ethnic food and of course, Pad Thai is a tried and true favorite dish at any restaurant I'm at. I'm am serious when I say that the Smiling Elephant truly does have the BEST Pad Thai ever!
There are no words to describe how fresh, flavorful and melt-in-your-mouth delicious it is. I could taste and savor all of the herbs and spices and sauces individually, but at the same time, they all combined beautifully.
I also go the lemongrass hot tea which was relaxing and refreshing at the same time. As an appetizer, we ordered lightly steamed vegetables with an incredible peanut sauce - this was just as good as the Pad Thai!
The staff is genuinely sweet and you can see all of the cooks doing their thing - I caught the eye of a cute little old Thai lady in the kitchen and she waved and smiled enthusiastically at me. The only downside is that the place is *tiny* and gets really crowded fast - so get there early! I can't recommend this place enough. :)

Danny Boy Beer Work's tasting room just opened (the grand opening is this coming weekend from what one of the employees mentioned) but it looks like it's going to be an amazing spot. I met a client here for drinks and once I navigated the confusing roundabouts and found the place (in the middle of a "planned development") I was impressed.

The interior is great - industrial, for sure but very thoughtfully designed. I like the reused beer bottle light fixtures and the fact that the brewing equipment is featured prominently in the space - not behind glass or hidden away. They've got big roll-up garage doors which will make this place absolutely delightful on a warm day. On the ground floor, there's space for about 90 and then there's a smaller second floor with space for about 45. The upper level is intended to be more "family friendly" and would make a great place for a private event.

In terms of beer, they've got 4-6 of their beers on tap at any time and more than 20 "guest taps" which range from Coors Light to Belgian Trippels. Craft beer lovers will be very happy here as the offerings are varied but high quality (except for the Coors Light which I assume is offered for people without taste buds). I went with their house Ginger Witte which was light, refreshing and very easy to drink. House beers are $5 for a pint and guest taps range from $7-8 depending on alcohol content.

Wine is also available but for the moment, only by the bottle. I think that will change once they open up their full service kitchen. All of the employees we interacted with were really friendly, excited about their new space and happy to tell us what they've got planned for the future.

It's kind of an odd location (middle of a residential super-suburban area) but definitely a place worth checking out!

My friend and I hatched a plan to go on a poboy tour of Southern Louisiana during my last visit to New Orleans.  Our first stop was supposed to be Mahoney's, but it turned out they don't open until 11 AM. At this point, we were both starving and anxious to get our adventure started and were not in a mood to wait for an hour for Mahoney's to open. My friend remembered Magazine Po-Boy Shop as being a pretty good place to grab poboys so there we went.  

I read in one of the review that this is a Cash Only place.  Actually, they accept credit card but their card reader wasn't working properly so my friend tried to get money from the ATM but it wasn't working either! Thank goodness we had enough cash between the two of us to pay for our order.  The staff were all nice and very patient while we were struggling with the cash situation.

The food?  My friend ordered the muffuletta and I assume it was very good because I swear he demolished it in less than five minutes! I ordered the oyster poboy and it was good but it's not something I would gush over.  Overall, it was an alright experience.  If I were hungry and I was in the neighborhood, I wouldn't hesitate to go back, but I will not go out of my way to go back to the place.  There are plenty of restaurants in New Orleans to check out!

My second time visiting for breakfast and I cannot gush enough over the delicious food! They have a Laid back, welcoming, and amazingly helpful atmosphere and staff! I also adore the new owl coffee mugs!! Portions are perfect and taste sooo good!! And again... Super friendly staff!!

Look out, Denny's, this place is starting to become my husband's and my special goto for breakfast for dinner. So very good. The portions are large, but yummy. I like the blueberry syrup and the staff is very friendly.
I've had the Pa-Nang Chicken from the lunch menu many times, it's sooooo good I can't bring myself to order anything else when I eat there.

Gulf Coast Van Lines was utterly fantastic. Right from the time I got
the quote they were super professional and super responsive. The
moving crew were the best movers I've ever had, they were super
careful and they wrapped everything very well. They were quick, they
were fast & they took about half the time they estimated so they saved
us a bunch of money vs. their estimate. I couldn't be more happy and I
would gladly recommend them again.
Loved the Jamaican chicken curry. And the little doughnuts! Great place for a tasty meal where you can come as you are.

Was here for work and wanted Italian. Came in and looked at yelp on iPhone just to see what is recommended, since got bored from the SLOW service from the servers. 

Then saw the 1 - 2 stars reviews. Oops.

Well since I ordered my beer already, I was too lazy to get up and go. I mean the food was alright afterward, but definitely service needs more attention to customer.
This place was great! Had the egg sandwich, the egg was cooked just right, runny but not so runny that it dropped out of the sandwich. Potatoes were tasty and coffee was strong. Highly recommended.
