Poor attempt at a real seafood dive. I had high hopes for this place. Kaz's Seafood Dive occupies the former Mama Iguanas and Cherry's before that. It's not a bad location, rather bad concepts that have filled the walls of the restaurant. 

The decor is decent, but the bathrooms are a bit rundown and the toilets leak everywhere. Weird since they just opened. You would figure they would make sure everything was fixed prior to the grand opening. 

The waitstaff was friendly enough but not knowledgable about the menu or what side items come with certain entrees. Perhaps this was due to opening day issues. 

The food was poor. Frozen seafood and fries everywhere. Fried food galore. I ordered coconut shrimp for $9 and it didn't even come with a dipping sauce. The side dishes are bland and not very enticing. Cole slaw, red beans and rice. The usual sides are underwhelming. The most disappointing part of the food was the "bread rolls" that their sandwiches consist of. I ordered a fish sandwich and expected a nice meal for $11. When the sandwich came out I found that the roll was made out of Howie Breadsticks. You heard right. Pizza breadsticks. Apparently the owner Kaz also owns a Hungry Howies franchise or two and is using Howie Bread for rolls for his sandwiches. This is hugely disappointing. The fish was ok, but the rolls were crap. My buddy's crab cake sandwich was mostly filler and bland. Mom's seafood pasta was gummy and came out warm. 

All in all. Four of us for dinner had a jalapeño appetizer, coconut shrimp, a fish sandwich, crab cake sandwich, and scallop pasta Alfredo. 4 beers and a sweet tea. Grand total $70 for lunch. Wow. I can't believe I spent that much on such disappointing food.

A very busy restaurant. Arrived at 1 pm and our order was taken immediately and we had our food in 15 minutes. The restaurant is easy to get to and right across from a Starbucks for a coffee on the drive home.
We had the grilled chicken sandwich on a toasted bun; it has bacon and Swiss Cheese- it was delicious! Our side was mac -n- cheese- it was just right!
Drinks are self help with large plastic cups. It's great because you can get a drink to go.
The restaurant is clean and the parking is good!

It's a little bit of a challenge to find the place, thanks to a tiny sign outside, but it's a nice find after all.  This bistro is a fairly quiet and small place that has a laid-back atmosphere and calm service.  It does seem like they are going through some minor adjustments to find their niche.  For instance, each customer is told to sit themselves, select their order, place it at the cash register, and a server will deliver the goods.  There is, again, a tiny sign that explains all of this, but it's hard to see, since every customer that walked in while we were there asked the same questions about 'what do we do'?  There also is an outside seating area, but it's not clear of its availability and if service extends in that area.

The selection is pretty good, and the food is also fresh and well prepared.  I ordered a French Club, and my wife had the Americano Salad, and we both liked our choices.  I had a standard cup of coffee, my wife had iced tea, but I could have used a shot of tequila when I received the bill:  with tip, $34 bucks.

Nice place, but the nearby competitors may be too much of a challenge for this place.

(Also, it's probably time to invest in actual menus, since your copier is cutting off the top of the paper stock menus, and even our Server couldn't help with some of the missing text.)

I went to visit Indianapolis and found this bar. Since it was my first time here, the bartender recommended something based on my preference. It tasted good, not overly sweet. Btw, I like margarita . So he made this for me. The appetizer , however, is not that good.

Probably, no, definitely the Nicest motel have ever stayed in. Clean, beautifully appointed, great location, and a good deal. The management is friendly, and the free muffins in the morning are delicious. 

I would recommend it, but they regularly sell out. So you go somewhere else, Ill stay at the Castillo!

I really wanted to rate this place much better. My girlfriend and I went on a Friday before a concert, so it was rather busy. We found a table just in time, about 5 minutes after we arrived there was a line out the door of people waiting to sit. Given it was a busy Friday night (during March Madness no less), one would think the bar would anticipate extra crowds and staff accordingly? Ehh, I guess not. It took about 10 minutes to get a drink order, and then another 10 minutes to get a food order. My friend ordered a local draft and when it arrived it came with a free insect. Luckily it was ONLY a fly and not a roach, but still... Ick! The waitress didn't seem too surprised (as if this happens regularly), and brought a replacement. My drink was protein free so no complaints on my end. The food came out in decent time, but we kept having about 3-4 of those little flies swooping around our food. It's March and cold, where are the bugs coming from? I have serious concerns about the cleanliness of this place. The food was good, I got the Englishman in Italy and was happy with it. They have some great looking food on the menu. My fries were those "Rally's" type seasoned fries, and I didn't care for them. My friend had a grilled fish sandwhich that she said was very good.
In the end, due to the lack of staffing and extra insects with our beverages, I could only give Chathan Tap two stars. I will try again, as it was an interesting bar, with a nice atmosphere.
Wonderful. Clean, peaceful facility; Keri is an amazing host / business owner / angel from heaven.

Fabulous service and great food! 

Every time I go to Moto, the wait staff is remarkable -- friendly, efficient, knowledgeable and polite. Our waiter even took our valet stub out for us while we paid the check so our car would be ready without us having to wait. The food is great too - love it! Great atmosphere, good music. I recommend their black pepper tagliatelle bolognese and their meatball appetizer.

After seeing the Knicks get swept in the first round to the Celtics. I was able to catch the Hornets play the Lakers that night in New Orleans.

Before I left for New Orleans I looked to see how much tickets were going for at MSG. The cheapest was $450. The cheapest here, another first round playoff game against another mega marque team, $40. AMAZING! 

We got to see Chris Paul drop a triple double and sent the series back to LA tied up at two a piece. Ric Flair was on the big scream, going crazy. It was a blast. 

With tickets so inexpensive down here, you should definitely stop by if you are visiting.

I had to have my screen repaired to trade it in. My son in law found Phone Repair Philly on line to have the best price. We got there and what a high tech, customer friendly place. Quick, while I waited service with refreshments. What's not to like?

Let me begin by saying I was introduced to this sushi restaurant by my old roommate who works there, who ranted and raved about the sushi at Sakana. I figured it would be okay, BUT WHO KNEW?!!!?

I consider myself a sushi connoisseur and honestly have never encountered such innovative and delicious sushi combinations!
The menu is filled with vast amounts of different types of fish combined with their unique twist on traditional sushi. The custom sauces (which were created by the restaurant owner and chef) add to each amazing bite you take.

Definitely recommend any of the press box rolls, the Merry-go-round, the Red Dragon, Half & Half, and I'm not sure what its called but its spicy and has mango and is absolutely superb.

The staff is super friendly, always attentive, and i LOVE marcos.

Theres usually a wait so try and beat the dinner rush and get there pretty early. The bar seats are the best. The chefs are a kick.

This is one place you won't be disappointed by.

Food and service is always great! The pizza and the seafood stuff mushrooms were full of flavor. There is often a wait but luckily they have an upstairs seating area so the wait usually moves quickly.

I stopped in for lunch and as soon as I walked in, I was right in front of the salad bar cooler.  After I walked around it, I was treated to a friendly and unique atmosphere.  They have a number of cool classic items decorating the walls with only a handful of more modern touches (a couple flat panel TVs with advertising.)  The wait staff was very friendly and I ended up ordering the lunch special bacon cheese burger and jambalaya soup.  The menu has a large number of specials and includes more of what would be considered home cooked.

The soup was very spicy and had a good amount of flavor, so it was pretty enjoyable.  The burger was ok, though they asked for a temp, you really aren't going to cook a food service round stamped type patty to anything other than well done.  My guess is that it started life as a frozen patty, so I was a little underwhelmed, as the other dishes of food had more of a "cooked in a kitchen" look.

Overall, the wait staff is the reason I rated the restaurant as a three star.  The food was ok, though it was a little bit pricey.  (Though, they will send you out with a giant to go cup of your drink.  Seriously, this thing is at least a liter.)

I would come back again, but I'm not sure I would have it on the top of my list in the downtown area of Plant City.

I'm really surprised at the low reviews for this place.  In my opinion, it offers the best valued Ethiopian food in the Philly area, a place where competition is steep.  The food here is a good $2 or so per item cheaper than in most restaurants, and the service I have found is consistently better than average.  The quality of the food does not at all suffer from the lower price--instead, you just give up the fancy atmosphere, and that's cool with me.

This place is a little divey, in a 70's cafeteria sort of way.  There's an eating area on one side, seat yourself, and a bar on the other.  The bar is dark and the seating area is brighter, but not exactly the most brightly lit place.

But I like it.  There's a positive vibe in here.  They're often playing energetic hip-hop music.  It's the sort of place that I feel very comfortable, and I'm not quite sure why.

But I always like the food, especially the vegetarian food.  I especially like the Foul and Vegetarian platter here.  Food is cheap, portions are good, quality is consistently good, service is consistently good.

Seriously, what is there to not like about this place?  The only thing I can imagine is if you're looking for something fancy...which I almost never am.

Epic win!

I bookmarked this place when my family and I were staying in SB for a day. I expected that lines would be super long for a weekday so we went to the pier (where the restaurant's located) and put our name down at 4:45pm (you can choose to sit inside, outside, or whatever's available). The waiting time took around 30-40 minutes, which I expected as the restaurant as pretty small and couldn't fit a large crowd. So we sat down close to 6pm and enjoyed the experience. 

Parking: there is parking on the pier, but you'd have to get there early before rush hour to snag a spot. Free parking for the first 90 minutes I believe and then $1.50 for each hour after that (I think).

Food: Food was good, not exceptionally as amazing as I had imagined it to be (which is why I took off a star there).

Waiting time: Waiting for our food took a while, but there was also only one waiter serving everybody sitting outside. Service from the waiter was really good - he took care of us even though he was busy managing the other tables as well. 

Would I come back? Maybe not. This was more of a "I'm glad I tried it experience but would rather explore other restaurants the next time I'm in SB."

Read the good reviews and decided to give it a shot. Ordered the Pei Mei spicy chicken dish with white rice which I was told was pretty spicy and was their version of General Tso. Couldn't wait as I was starving. Dish was served pretty quickly and piping hot. Not only was it NOT spicy contrary to the name, but it was lathered in a sweet goop that didn't taste good at all. Ended up leaving half the entree untouched. Pretty bummed as I had high expectations. Perhaps I chose the wrong dish but just wasn't impressed.

First Watch is amazing!  The first time I saw the name I was up north and thought it was a eye glasses store.  My loss!  I saw it again at the downtown location and realized it was a breakfast/brunch/lunch spot.  The hubby and I went here for weekend brunch and were blown away.  Service was so good; our waitress was friendly, knowledgeable about the menu, prompt, and almost a mind reader.  The food was awesome.  They make a clear effort to purchase local (if possible), fresh ingredients.  Our order came out quick and was well made.  They also have really great coffee AND our server made us to-go cups on our way out.  Definitely worth a stop!
Good place to chill with friends for a drink. Food is so-so, not the best or worst. Very cody inside.
Really easy to sum up, great food, great service! All around a very good experience on the first visit!

This was so good! I'm a picky eater when it comes to meat and there was a great balance of lean meats in with the normal meats that my family love. We tried all the beef items and most of the seafood. My favorite sauce was the house barbeque and if you love hot food, take a chance on the hot peppers. They're fantastic with lots of heat, but a great flavor. This is our new spot for family nights out.

This Starbucks is typically pretty packed at most times of the day. There is usually nowhere to sit inside. The set-up is sort of L-shaped. You walk in and to the left are couches and tables. Along the path to the counter are more tables. The bathrooms are in front of you all the way in the back.

The staff has always been efficient and sufficiently friendly in my visits here. The parking lot can be a little tricky since it's two rows of parking spots, and you have to back up toward each other to maneuver out. This location is in Short Hills plaza, connected to Hollywood Tans, Classic Cake Company, a Vietnamese restaurant, and a dog toy store. 

They usually have bagels when I get there, which I enjoy. At the end of the night, the pastries like mallorka sweet bread are pretty stale, so I don't recommend getting anything like that late.

What I love about this location is the patio style seating to the side of it that they provide. This is great for warm weather when meeting up with a friend.

Unfortunately, the crowd that this location brings is ritzy, snobby Cherry Hill/Voorhees people. I sometimes wish I'd brought ear plugs when I come because overhearing their conversations is nearly painful. 

Overall, I'd say come here and get your drinks and snacks to go, unless it is a nice day - then enjoy the patio with a friend.

We went to India Sizzling II on Saturday night and had the buffet.  My husband and I are both vegan and appreciated the time our waiter took to explain the dishes to us.  There was a wide variety of options and the dosa were amazing!  We tried the masala dosa and the onion dosa and they were both great.  The flavor was great and the food wasn't too oily or salty (have had that problem at other local Indian places). 

In summary, great food, attentive service and a clean, pleasant dining room.  We will definitely be returning!
Yum! Love the happy hour menu and prices. Fun atmosphere. Great appetizer options. Will definitely be back!

I am giving them 3-stars only because I know they can do better.  We loved Maynard's, but I am sad to say it has lost its standing for me.   

First, if they ever suggest eating upstairs, don't!  It reminds me of a cheesy Holiday in restaurant.  There are too many other wonderful restaurants in Tucson to have dinner instead of eating in their "second" dining room.  

Second, The food came out so fast we felt like we were being shoved out the door before we even sat down.  Bad form.  I don't care how busy the restaurant is, every customer that comes to Maynard's is expecting a nice long 3-4 course leisurely dinner, not a rush job.  

We will go back and try again, but we will never be seated for dinner in the "second" dinning room.

My husband and I visited the restaurant today after reading the Yelp reviews and decided to try it as we had a craving for curry on such a cold day. The restaurant is small and quaint but do not be deceived as the food is amazing and does not disappoint. I ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala and my husband had the Chicken Curry and we both had Garlic Naan. All of it was phenomenal. The owner greeted us and was very kind and checked on us while we ate. We will definitely be coming back to this little gem and I would recommend it to anyone. Please check it out.

Group of friends and I, foodies from another city, came to this restaurant based on the views alone despite the mixed reviews. Got lucky and had a great window seat with no deposit. 

The zebra seats... LOL. 

The menu had a nice selection. We all got the lobster bisque as an appetizer. It had nice spices although there wasn't actually any lobster in it and the "croutons" were egg based and the texture was a lot like tofu. I thought it was tofu. 

Moving on to the main course, I had the chicken. Rice was undercooked but the chicken and WAFFLES (pleasant surprise) was cooked perfectly and had a great flavor. 

Had lobster Mac and cheese and cheese grits as sides. They were good as well. The table agreed the food was just okay and next time we would come would be for drinks only at the bar. 

Our server was very friendly and the presentations were great.

When I was shown to my seat of was still wet so I had to use the napkin to finish the job. Place was full and service was poor. I ordered the Atlantic Tuna melt - not convinced that the tuna was fresh and it was cold. I ate half only - no one asked why - not the place if you are in a hurry 

Tried them again on Jan 13th - had an Eggs Benedict - one of the eggs was under done which I hate - taste was good but again make sure you have plenty of time for lunch - no quick lunches here

I went here based on the Yelp reviews, and Nei was my stylist. She was a lovely person, and I had a really pleasant experience with her and at the salon, but this is a very bad haircut. 

I've been getting my hair cut the same way for 5-10 years and have never had a really bad haircut until now. I'm not entirely sure what went wrong. I think that we had a hard time communicating about what I wanted (it was clear from the beginning that my words weren't having their intended effect)-- but also some of her techniques seemed like they just weren't doing good things to my hair-- and the techniques were much different than those of other hairstylists I've been to. Near the end of the haircut, I realized that things were headed in a very bad direction... but I think my attempts at intervention ("could you maybe make that more even? Focus on this section?" etc) actually ended up making things worse. 

It's really so bad that it's become a joke with my friends. The two different sides of my hair are uneven in maaaany different places, and the layers are cut in way that makes them still out at odd angles. It's a mess, but it's so short that I'm waiting a few months before going somewhere to get it fixed. 

Maybe this was just an off-day. It looks from the reviews like my experience was unique, and I thought everyone I met at the salon was friendly and made me feel at home. So: 2 stars for great people, 0 stars for the cut.
Great food for a reasonable price.  I really enjoy the vegetarian plate and the med. salad.
Love this place donuts. It's soft inside and not too sweet. Perfect with coffee. They have so many kind of donuts chose. It's cool place have a great breakfast or afternoon tea time.

I made an appointment here, for my mother in law and myself. I was going to go to sally nails but they were booked. I am so happy I came here! I am verrerrrry particular about my nails, they all have to be the same shape and length, to a t... I spent 40 for a fill on my set. I got shellac for the color changing, so that was extra and I was charged $5 for the special shape but it was so worth it. Finding somewhere that does good specialty nails is hard, and this place nailed it (pun intended). She -didn't get her name- was quick and professional and my nails look amazing! Not only that, they have a very clean and sterile environment. I am not from this area, but when I come back, if I need a fill I will 100% come back here.

Yes. Go here.

I went here with my boyfriend on a Saturday night and they sat us outside...it was November and about in the mid-40s. They had a heater so it was ok but they were nice enough to let us move inside when a table opened up!
We had $3 pumpkin beers (can't remember the brewery) and I had the egg-bread thing (also can't remember what that was called). Get that - it's a huge piece of puffy focaccia with a thin melted layer of cheese on top, a runny egg yolk and shaved black truffles on top. WOW I think that was the best thing I ever ate. I also got butternut squash which was good but compared to the egg thing wasn't that spectacular. My boyfriend got some sort of panini that he liked a lot. Very cozy, good for a date or a group.

Decent pizza but not great. I guess I'm just used to a different style. I had the "veggie bianco" which is a thin crust with roasted peppers and olives and cheese but not tomato sauce. Tasty but greasy.

Service was good, but the noise in the restaurant from the kids and the television was offputting.

Solid Chinese food. Recommendations: kung pao chicken, dan dan noodles, beef noodle soup, pork fried rice 


I've ordered take out from here and dined in several times. The wait staff is always very accommodating and seats me without a very long wait at my favorite window table. Take out is quick as well and you can order via Yelp or just call in. 

My one tiny qualm is the prices.
The appetizers are a bit pricey ($6-7 for 4 dumplings is a bit unreasonable). I would recommend this place for a nice seat down meal but probably not an everyday routine take out.

Pretty decent barbeque -- nice to have on the south side.

The decor was a little rough, as was the counter setup -- seemed to have been a rapidly launched restaurant, using existing building components.

My Grandchildren and I were there on 4th of July explore the gardens and watch the fireworks and we enjoyed ourselves. The Grandkids had fun on the inflatable giant slide, carousel, playground and exploring the various gardens. They also enjoyed making bracelets with beads.  Every staff member was friendly and patient with the children. I was most impressed by a coworker there by the name of Andrew. He was so delightful and kept his pleasant personality while multitasking. I would be overwhelmed with the work load he had that day but he remained delightful and attentive....that alone would have me and my family go back to the Camden Children's Garden again!

High class no
Good service no
Ambiance no
Action 4 stars
Friday high hand promotion every 30 minutes for 500
The players are loose on 1/2
Plenty of variety 1/2 2/5 10/20 Hold'em. 
Omaha 
Enjoy and good luck!

Wonderful, intimate atmosphere and elegant minimalist decor. The food is prepared with a fresh, new side item and soup each and every day, so the menu never gets stale. They even have a breakfast menu on Saturday mornings IIRC. My only complaint would be that the food is perhaps a bit overpriced for what it is, although everything is very delicious. I will be back to try something from their gelato bar!

The help can also be a touch slow, but I was by myself and buried in a book so I'll just chalk it up to that. :P

Being new to Indianapolis this was my first and last visit to Bagger Dave's.  My husband and I figured since it said Tavern it would be more geared to the adult crowd, boy were we wrong.  We were the only table with out multiple children.   Our waitress came over asked if it was our first visit to which we replied "yes".  She proceeded to what I assume was explain the menu, but talked so fast I was not able to follow along.  I placed my drink order (unsweet iced tea) and she looked blankly at me.  She seemed confused when my husband ordered water.  When she returned with our drinks I had my build your own burger for filled out.  She stood at our table until I finally spoke up and said I had my order ready.  She then questioned me on everything on the form as though I was not capable of reading and filling it out.  My husband ordered a chicken ceasar salad.  We waited quite a while for our food.  When it arrived my husband commented that there wasn't even enough chicken for a chicken tender on his salad.   I noticed there wasn't enough energy a teaspoon of mayonnaise on my burger.  Then I picked up a sautéed mushroom that had fallen off the burger but it was ICE COLD.  I felt the rest of the burger and toppings ... patty was warm not hot and the bacon felt like it had been warmed by the heat of the patty. The fries were so greasy they dripped when you squeezed them I was I need of food and there was no server in sight so I began eating.   I was about a quarter of the way through and our server appeared.  She asked how everything was and I told her.  She stared at me blankly then said "I can bring you a side of mayo."  I told her no thank you and she left.  At this point I stopped eating and noticed my my "medium" burger was rather pink/rare.  A couple minutes passed an the manager came by our table and asked about our food.  We proceeded to tell her the issues and she looked astonished.  She asked if she could remake it and I declined.  She did say she would take it off the check and would check to make sure everything was OK in the kitchen.   She seemed particularly surprised at how our server handled it.  We waited for our server to come back so we could ask for our check.  When she did she very rudely asked if her manager had offer to remake "it" to which we said we had declined and asked for our check which she brought, took our payment then returned the receipt without another word.  It has been almost 5 hours since we left and I am looking for anti nausea/anti diarrhea medication to counter whatever the food has done to my digestive system.

We got 4 tempura rolls of different flavors and waited 45 minutes for our order.  I have never waited so long for my food at a restaurant where you are the only customer.  All tempura rolls tasted exactly the same, maybe it was for the amount of batter they had.

Of course the Children's Museum is great for kids, but also consider it for a first date. It's low pressure and there's plenty of stuff to talk about, look at and touch. First dates make you giddy like a kid anyway.

For all ages, here are my favorite parts. First, ScienceWorks. Try to dam up the running water and send your boat around the loop. Then, play with the Rube Goldberg machine that sends pool balls for a spin.

The trains. There's a real train, miniature trains, running trains, train villages. All cool.

Currently, there is a superhero exhibit running with one of the Batmobiles in it. There's also a spot for kids to draw their own superhero, which is creative.

Keeping it simple... these guys are awesome. 

Super friendly, both on the phone and in person.
Very reasonable rates for very decent equipment (the life vests have seen better days, but that's probably because they spend most of their time in the bottom of the boat, right?) 
 
90 canoes and 45 kayaks (which have been sold out in advance almost every weekend this summer - plan wisely) - shuttle service (bring your phone to call at the end)

When we got back into town last night, we met some friends for a beer - talking about our ride down the Harpeth, not one, not two, but THREE different people said, "Did you use Foggy Bottom?  Good." 

(well, they didn't all say it exactly like that, but you get the point - when you want to float the Harpeth, call Foggy Bottom)

This place is a gem ! Absolutely love just getting a tray and filling it up with goodies. They have lots and lots of baked goods. Don't really know what everything is called but it's delicious. Some of them are filled with pastry cream and it's not overly sweet so just hits the spot. The prices are also unbelievable. You won't spend more than $10 for a tray full of yummy treats.
This spot is pretty nice. The food in this park is pretty trash. Beer selection is also terrible. But sometimes there's great music. Music makes up for the wack food.

I have been to HipCityVeg four or five times now, each time accompanied by my partner who is vegetarian. Both of us have enjoyed our dining experience every time. The ingredients are fresh and consistently delicious. There is some oil sprinkled on some of the dishes which takes away from the fresh and crispy feeling I sometimes associate with healthy eating. That said, the food is very flavorful. I'm yet to have anything that's less than great. The prices are also very reasonable. There's a good variety of drinks that are available but that's one part of the menu I have not really explored yet.

If you can find the place - I searched for thirty minutes, hence the missing star- you will undoubtedly love every moment.

The product: (disclaimer, as with all great products, the experience is more than "the product, i.e., the haircut, and Moosehead is no exception, as the ambiance was what made this place great): regardless, the hair stylists are meticulous, striving to pay heed to the small things that Fantastic Sam's can't or doesn't.  The entire process lasted nearly an hour, and I left feeling that (a) I received a great value and (b) refreshed and groomed impeccably.   

Ambiance: this place has a lot of it.  It features leather, overstuffed chairs, dark wood flooring, a humidor stocked with cigars, several televisions tuned into ESPN and a moose with a clever necktie.  An Abercrombie-catalogue-like, masculine spa. 

Most salient, the haircut is amazing. Two shampoos, a scalp massage with mint tree-oil, and a straight edge razor for pesky neck hair.  Pampered experience.  If there was a 4.5 stars, this place would merit it.  As I said prior, however, it's very hard to find.  It's located in a converted apartment-complex, with several other hairstylists; several signs adorn the building, but the Moosehead is the least-likely to be noticed; the door -which was closed - had but a single number (5), with no sign or "Moosehead lettering."  For how much $$ they have manifestly put into the interior, I don't understand the lack of external advertising.  Nonetheless, and as set forth above, the place is great.  I will surely go back.

Great for men's hair dyeing, even though I wasn't sure what I wanted. I worked with tiffany who expertly bleached and toned my hair. 

When the color turned out to be not quite what I had in mind, she and the other staff were glad to help me switch to a lighter color. 

The owner offered me a free follow up to get the color just right after I had gotten on the right track after the second round of toner.

Not yet a 5 star, but close. The breakfast food is their go to and is as good as the others locations. I took a chance on a burger and I was a bit disappointed. The burger wasn't cooked right and the portion of fries on the side was rather small. Granted this was the first week they were open so I'm not going to jump to conclusions. 

Other than that the place is great. Beautiful (loud) room with plenty of space for families and groups too. 

The service was excellent and the parking was easy in the back.
Chava has the best service!!! One of the kindest people I've ever met. With no clue with what I wanted to do with my letters, he gladly assisted me. They're extremely patient and helpful.

I haven't been here in about 6 months and its definitely gone downhill. Went for lunch today and I should have made the connection that since it was slow there was a reason for it. First of all, I was NOT there for beer...so I can't comment all that...but I use to enjoy their food. However, my fries were cold, onion rings were heavily breaded. When I say breaded I mean thick very thick mushy bread. These were terrible. Burger was okay...my guest with me said we should have just gone to Punch Burger...much better tasting and 1/3 of the price. Service was extremely slow, as well. With so many burger options...this is one that is no longer on my you should go try this place out. So disappointing.

If you are visiting New Orleans and don't go to this cafe, then you are missing one of the most traditional things to do there.  We went late at night because during the day we saw a long line outside the cafe, I was not sure of trying the beignets and after one small bite I ended up getting an order just for me. Not sure of coming back, coffee and beignets are delicious, I'm just afraid of having sugar problems!!

Skip online & shop local first! Esther was amazing! I showed her a photo for my husband's costume idea & she put it all together for me & out the door I went & for a very fair price! Can't thank you enough!

I had my wedding here the end of August.  It was perfect.  Everyone at the club was helpful, and very nice.  The food was great, and freshly preparded on site. The staff on the day of was the best, everything ran smooth and I could not have asked for a better place to have my wedding.

Fantastic experience! From the service to the food, the evening was very special and memorable.

We definitely recommend the Red Pony Martini, BLT Ravioli & beef tenderloin; finish your dinner with a Good Night Rebecca martini and you'll have a big smile on your face when you leave!
After early morning breakfast at BK's tacos in Tucson. Wait staff was incredible and very nice
Knowledgeable, friendly, helpful, and a great location.  Seeing how Lowes and Home Depot employee's are about as helpful as a soup fork, an old school hardware store like this is a sigh of relief.

Tonight was our first visit to Bar Louie and it was great! We sat at the bar, our bar tender/server was Alyson. She was VERY nice and knew the drink menu well despite only being one a few weeks. I ordered boneless wings and my husband ordered a burger cooked medium with fries. They were both delicious and came out as ordered.

Table Top Cafe is an awesome idea and a great place to meet up with friends if you want a place to hang out and play board games. Sure, other cities in Canada already have this but this is the first one in Edmonton! 

We went there for the first time on a Friday evening and all the tables were full. The owner, Brian, was nice enough to ask and we were able to squeeze onto a table that wasn't full. The place is bright, warm and inviting - perfect to get your game on and man, there is a BIG selection to choose from. Not only that, you can purchase the games brand new right there and then.

All you need to know is:

1) It's $5/person to play
2) You can play and try unlimited amount of games. Hours are great too! Open till 2am Friday and Saturday, 12am for the rest.
3) Brian is a super nice guy. He was nice enough to show us how to play/start a new game that we had grabbed (Terra Mystica)

Will definitely be back to try more games and to bring new people!  Oh and apparently you can reserve a table if you call ahead.

We rented a suite to stay for five nights for our son's wedding in New Orleans. Prince Conti is a small, intimate and tastefully decorated hotel, conveniently located in the French Quarter. The tasteful decor in our suite was erring on the side of 'shabby chic' and overdue for refurbishment. We had some maintenance issues, which, when brought to the attention of the manager, were quickly resolved. The hotel staff is wonderful, very attentive and knowledgeable about the French Quarter. Food in the breakfast cafe is ok, not great. There seems to be some strife in the kitchen, with quite a bit of hollering that carried out to the cafe area. Service was not great. We thought that being off of Bourbon Street, the hotel would be quieter, but the  music from nearby night clubs and boom-box equipped vehicles driving by vibrated our windows until well after 2 am. Reasonably priced, if you can get a quiet room.

generic Starbucks.

In Tampa across from hotel & office location.

Coffee was excellent.

Very good selection of non-coffee goods and foods.  Wifi - noted a large number of persons having coffee & plugged in to their notebooks/laptops.

Comfortable seating although i, as is my want, ordered take out. 

The coffee here was very good.  I'm not usually a huge fan of Starbucks coffee but the coffee i got here was excellent.  

Service was professional, prompt, kind, good humored and most courteous.

Recommended.

Fantastic!

I know it is really petty, but the only thing that knocked off the fifth star is the absurdly loud clubby music blaring from the speakers (complete with whistles...just too much).  

On to the good--the atmosphere is lovely.  There are multiple rooms.  We enjoyed a drink in the bar before being seated downstairs in the dimly lit wine cellar.

We started with the antipasti and some salads.  The Caesar is for two and is prepared table side.  It was one of the best Caesar salads I have tasted.  I enjoyed the Gnocchi with Speck for my entree.  It was insanely rich, but delicious...hey, it made two additional meals in the days following.  I guess you could call that a bargain??  We were too full for dessert, but noticed they offered Bananas Foster.  Not what I would expect, but always a great option!

I'm not sure when we will be back, but I look forward to my next visit!

fo-shizzle-my-nizzle---after being downtown Nash and heading back to the hood.  This place is freakin' awesome.  I can get down with my hot juicy friend cajun chicken  and biscuit.  I enjoy me some popeye's chicken and this location was always friendly helpful and clean so not sure what the other yelper was ranting about.  But then again this was close to my house so I was able to grab and go...Been here several times and it was always fresh and hot and good tasting.  I would go here over KFC anytime....the rice side dish is really good too...depends on how hungry you are...Prices are great,,,,
If you want seafood on Indian Rocks Beach, this is as good as it gets. Fast service.  Reasonable prices.  I've tried them all and I always come back to PJ's.

The winter of 2011 I learned the hard way: Crowne Plaza SUCKS. I never stayed at one and wanted to check them out, and regretted it almost immediately. 

Wallpaper was peeling, furniture was crap, rooms were cramped, bathrooms were a joke (and to call them puny is being generous), only one accessible electrical outlet, the thermostat was there only for looks but completely nonfunctional (which sucked when the temp hit 74*F in the middle of winter - heat was on and being on an upper floor of a tower windows don't open), the television was and old CRT television with no aux inputs (so no reviewing photos with your camera, and no hooking your iPhone, laptop, or tablet to the screen), and - get this - the knob for the shower came off in my hand. Oh, and the rooms are not soundproofed, and the doors are about 1.5" off the floor which makes the sound issue even worse (so roll a towel up and shove it against the bottom of the door), PLUS admits a lot of light from the hallway. Needless to say, I was not happy. 

Oh, and internet access is ethernet only; no WiFi unless you're on the bottom floor, and being in a steel-and-concrete building (essentially a faraday cage) cellphone reception stinks, so if all you bring for checking email is your iphone or ipad or android tablet, you're going to be SOL.

Decor was outdated - they're stuck in the '80s, but you could have guessed that by the television mentioned earlier.



Valet parking is slow. Do yourself a favor and call ahead when you need your car if you're in a hurry.

On the bright side, the staff at the front desk was friendly. I ran into the same key issue that others have; the key didn't work and needed replacement. They didn't try to blame me like other folks have complained though.

 I have stayed at many hotels, and this was by far the worst I have stayed in. I have stayed in total dives in tourist traps where every accommodation is a dive (think: cottages at Old Orchard Beach, Maine) that were far better than Crowne Plaza. This hotel is definitely not worthy of four stars. If I could rate it a negative number of stars, I would.

I could have paid less for a room at the Hilton or Ritz-Carlton, but I made the mistake of wanting to try Crowne Plaza. Never again!

Went in today for an Oil Change. I was a little nervous follow a bad experience at another location, Well I am really a Fan of this place. I was greeted warmly by Chris who listened to my request and took my car in immediately, Spoke to a gentleman in the waiting room who said he loves these guy and has come here for many years, A young couple from AK was also there. After less tan 45 min. my car was done..WOW and the young couple's car who came in after me was also ready. I am really impressed & when I mentioned I was doing a review, the couple from AK said to add their excellent review of the service they received. I will definitely be back & will also recommend them to my friends & family. They clearly know how to provide excellent service in a professional & friendly way.

Never again!  We ordered a delivery meal today for 6 people around 11 am.  It is nearly 1 PM and it isn't here yet despite 3 follow up calls.  They said the food was ready 45 minutes ago; the latest call indicated that was not true.  I don't care if the food is the best on earth, will never do business with them again!

Completely understaffed. Waited over an hour today just for someone to acknowledge me. Employees were great but for a Saturday afternoon you need more than 2 people working. So many people were waiting around to be helped and many ended up just walking out.
the best banana pudding!!! The service is second to none! I absolutely love this place! I make it a point to visit every single time I am in Philly.

I love thin crust pizza and Boulevard has some of the best!  Service is always friendly and quick.  Their sauce is very flavorful.  The salad and mini pizza combo is very reasonably priced...you can get pizza, salad, and a drink for a little over $6.00.  That's a pretty good value.

This is  a very good market. It has most of the stuff that you used to be able to get in China town, and it is slightly easier to park.  The parking lot sucks, but it is better than the one at T&T.  Meat prices tend to be pretty good, but quality of the meat seems to be hit and miss.

I tried to love this place but their vegetarian dishes are TERRIBLE. I've tried the ital stew and the spinach and groundnut stew so far. They are both incredibly bland. The veggies in the ital stew were mushy and overdone.  When I told the waitress that the ital stew was bland, she said that it was because it's vegetarian. *pause* what? I've had plenty of vegetarian Jamaican food that was flavorful. Avoid this place if you're looking for vegetarian dishes and walk down to Caribbean Delight. They do a much better job.

Outstanding in every way possible! We got lost and were 30 minutes late to our reservation! They were super accommodating. When one girl got up from the table to use the ladies room, our server came over and spent a full minute refolding her napkin for her and placed it on the table. I've never been to a place with that detail of service. The food was out of this world! We got the olive oil flight and the Black Pepper Tagliatelle! I was speechless that's how good it was! Would recommend this place to anyone in a heart beat!
So delicious. You will leave so full. The owners are very nice and always come and chat when our work group shows up.

Maybe one of the best taste Japanese Ramen in Tucson. I ate the white Tonkotsu and my buddy ate black roasted garlic Tonkotsu, both of them are very delicious.

I love everything but the fact that the noodles is a little bit less than I expected.

So I ate at Burger Up over a week ago and I'm still waiting for my food ... and waiting ... and waiting ...

You can't fault the entire restaurant as a whole because of one waitress, can you? She was horrible. Weird personality, excruciatingly slow and nowhere to be found for 99% of our meal. And the place wasn't even packed...It's hard to fault Burger Up for this one person, but they did hire her, yes?

The food was good. Not great, but good. I like to order the most simple thing on a menu at a new restaurant because if a place called "Burger Up" can't get a normal burger right, then why try anything else? 

The burger had good taste, but was quite dry. It wasn't a "juicy" burger. The fries are fantastic, but a lot of places have great fries. I will also note that their homemade ketchup is surprisingly very tasty.

This place is cool and has a good atmosphere, but you'll get a better burger at Five Guys or Rotier's.

I probably won't go back unless invited by a friend...and I really wanted to like this place.

I go to Bryn Mawr College and I frequently order take away from Ekta. They used to have the most horrible delivery man, but they fired him and his replacement is very friendly.  The butter chicken is my go to, and it's quite flavorful and creamy. You can really taste the butter and the other spices they use.  The vegetable samosas are nothing to brag about, they're merely okay.  There's no pop of flavor and the pastry is occasionally soggy, but generally they're fine. The chicken korma is also delicious. The sauce is a good mixture of being nice and thick and flavorful. I am partial to the peshwari naan, which is much better than their regular naan which is dry, flavorless, and not worth the calories. The peshwari naan, however, is softer in texture, and sweet, but not too sweet.  

Like most restaurants on the Main Line, it's BYOB, but luckily there is a liquor store across the street. The butter chicken tastes even better with a Kingfisher. Service in the restaurant is mediocre. It's family run, so the servers aren't trained and or particularly friendly. I'd recommend take away or delivery rather than eating in the restaurant. It's reasonably priced as well. Take away takes usually 45 minutes, but I've had cases where it's arrived in 30 minutes.

Overall, this Indian restaurant is pretty good. The town where I'm from has one of the top-rated Indian restaurants on the East Coast, so I'm used to a very high level of quality Indian food, but this restaurant on Lancaster Ave delivers (no pun intended).

Above average food but honestly a bit overpriced. I don't mind paying a premium for a good meal but I don't get why their burger is worth $20+. Four stars if it was priced a bit more on par with the food.

I don't really think this (or probably any) AYCE sushi place is really a five star restaurant, but I do think it's the best AYCE place in town, so it's getting five stars anyway.  I've never had a bad thing here, and it seems like their rolls have a little more imagination put into them than some places. 

Staff is insanely nice also.

Best. Dumplings. Ever!!

I have probably had well over 2000 dumplings since I last began to appreciate them back in college. After months of searching for a good dumpling near Philadelphia, these dumplings finally hit the spot. The steamed pork are obviously the best, but the fried veggie are good too.

When you pull up, it doesn't look like much aside from your typical stripmall Chinese food restaurant. However, it's super cute on the inside. Very clean, sweet service, and little fried crispies with duck dipping sauce and hot tea waiting for you at your table. My boyfriend and I went on a rainy Monday night, so we were literally the only people there. But, in the half hour we were there, they probably had 10-12 people picking up their orders. It's definitely a local gem and the go-to for Chinese food in the area!

Definitely recommend coming here on a random night or ordering takeout. You will not be disappointed!

30th Street Station is Philadelphia's version of "Grand Central"... here's where the buses meet the regional rails, meet the El, which meets the taxi's... you can get anywhere you need to go on the East Coast from here, including the train to PHL. 

There are plenty of food options such as Auntie Anne's pretzels, smoothies, a pub, quick sandwiches, etc. There is a GNC vitamin shop and quick mart, too! Did I mention Ben & Jerry's or Philly Soft Pretzels? 

This place can be crazy though, and the regional rail often only runs once per hour at night and on the weekends, so be sure you check your schedule and routes ahead of time!!
GREAT location.  A few blocks from Royal and Bourbon Streets but quiet.  Try to get a first floor courtyard room.

I had what was basically a pancake burrito filled with eggs and vegetarian sausage for breakfast. That's all that really matters in this review because that's just insanity. Delicious insanity.

Other things that I GUESS are worth mentioning is that it can get QUITE crowded, so be expected to wait a while before you can get seated. The menu is fairly extensive and the portions are on the large size, while the prices are also extremely fair. I think it's well worth the visit here.

Our department from work recently held a team building event at escape challenge.   We had a hour to figure out how to get out.  We did the hardest room challenge, the mansion library. 

We were able to get to the last challenge until one of our team members cut the wrong order of wires to defuse the bomb - we were so close. 

After the challenge we spent the next hour in the virtual reality room.   That was fun!   Overall a good experience.  The staff was friendly.  We had our event catered with food from Fuzzy tacos.

The only negative was it was hot in the virtual reality room.  They had no air ducts in there and the room was about 10-15 degrees warmer than the rest of the building.  

If you are looking for a fun time to spend with friends/and family you should check this place out. 

It was worth it.

I wish every maintenance company was like this one.

It's probably a sad comment  that the thing that blows me way about Family Air is that they schedule appointments quickly, phone if they're running late, and nearly always show up on time. Oh yes, they also fixed a furnace problem another company had created. It did take two visits, and I paid for two service calls, but it was a complicated problem and at the time of the second visit I thought I'd be looking at a costly repair, so I'm very happy with how things turned out. Highly recommended.

I stumbled onto Nippon Tei thanks to Yelp! when I was looking for some Japanese food (not sushi, sadly) that was close for lunch. Since my first visit, I've been there a couple more times.  The first time, I got takeout and it took 15 minutes and was served hot and with a smile. It wasn't too busy at lunch time, but it seemed like everyone knew each other in there. The servers/chefs greeted almost every person by name. To me, that's an indicator of great service.  Both times I got the same thing, so I'll get to that in one moment. 

The second visit, I met a friend here, also for a weekday lunch, and we dined inside. I didn't really get a chance to appreciate the atmosphere the first time, but it's quite nice.  It's elegant without being pretentious and also feels warm.  That's a hard combination to accomplish in my opinion.  I had the vegetarian spring rolls which were delicious and filled with veggies rather than a lot of fillers.  Because I don't like sushi, I'm always looking for places that I can go and have a successful meal with my friends who salivate over the fish rolls. I had the yakisoba which was terrific. I got it with chicken and it was a perfect ratio of chicken & veggies to noodles.  It was satisfying, not at all greasy (as I've found some other places are) and they were able to spice it up for me.  When asked for it spicy, they ask for a number from 1-5. I always get 3 and am satisfied with the spice level.  The sauce is delectable, both sweet and savory.  

I will definitely be back!

Came in for lunch. Waited several minutes to be seated. The bar tender stared at us. The wait staff saw us. No one made a move to come seat us. Meanwhile a group of 15-20 baseball players/families got up and left because after 15 minutes no one even took drink orders. 

It's not just that they seem to have opening problems, it's that the staff are individually lazy and uncaring.

Haven't been here since I lived here 14 yrs ago so it was past time. I wanted a quick overdose on fried seafood and boy did I get it! quality and service was great. Lunch was much easier to get in than I remember the dinner. I was also wonderfully surprised to have found out they participate in Advantage Dining Miles program... great seafood and miles, felt like I was at Harrah's and hit the jackpot.

We visited Monkey Joes on a Thursday at 11 am. It wasn't busy at all. There lots of large inflatables to play on. There is a small arcade and lots of party rooms. There are tables scattered throughout the building. Tvs and computers for the adults to use. My only issue is the lights to and in the bathroom are very dim. The bathrooms could have been cleaner especially with the fact that everyone is wearing only their socks. Parents can NOT get on the inflatables unless you are helping a child ages 4 and under but no bouncing.

I love everything about this place, except for the rude and incompetent bartender who always seems to be working when I go in.  All other service is always excellent.  Food wise, I have never had anything besides the wing platter with mac and slaw (which more BBQ restaurants need to serve, some people like wings as a meal!), and the Tuck Special because both are so good I can't stray.  I like that I can either come with friends to drink and watch a game, or by myself on a weekday and get some work done on the free wifi.
The food is great, frustrating to wait 20+ minutes. They need to have more help preparing. Honestly don't think if it is worth the wait.

We headed here for a weekend breakfast. It's off SR  54 in a mixed used building (apartments on top). We found parking in a lot across the street. Luckily for us, they weren't too busy and we were able to order right away and grabbed a table outside to wait for our food. They had a great menu, lots of coffee options. We both ordered their pressed Cuban breakfast sandwiches and were pleased. 
I'd say my only 'complaint' was what appeared to be American cheese. I would have preferred a Monterey, Provolone or Cheddar but I get that American melts better. But that's it.  
We'd definitely come back next time we find ourselves hungry and in the area.

Great staff! Everyone was helpful and friendly.

The beds have an adjustable firmness control and were really, really comfortable. The room service is above average; good food, accurate and quick delivery.

OTOH the rooms were noisy and in my room, the toilet ran and the tub drain was slow and backed up a little. The exercise room is smelly and needs a reno.

Went here for lunch/early dinner 
Around 4:30
Place was quiet, perfect little spot

I got the power bowl with chicken
Loved that it was made to order 

Food came out pretty quickly 
Great portions
Healthy, fresh, satisfying 

Well worth the try. Great if you're trying to eat clean

13$ for food and drink

Sriracha on the table 

I'm comin back

We went for brunch on Saturday and it was super busy. And not like organized Patachou busy, it appeared to be pure chaos. I get that the workers were probably all over the place and busy, but we sat for 20 minutes before we got water, another 10 minutes to order, and then another 40 minutes for the food, and when they brought it out, there was no silverware, so we had to wait another 5 minutes to eat, and by the time I could finally eat, my food was cold and just honestly didn't taste the greatest. Maybe I'll give it another shot when it's less busy, but honestly, just not a great value proposition. The homemade chipotle sauce was good, but honestly that was about the only redeeming quality of my first visit to Biscuits. Spicy gravy wasn't spicy. Biscuit wasn't fluffy. Food wasn't the greatest. Pretty average spot all-in-all. Oh and they overcharged us. Not a fun experience. At all.

Lobster pasta was dry and did not have great flavor.  Clam chowder was decent.  Steamed clams were ok.  Overpriced and nothing really wowed me. Customer service was lacking in both friendliness and timeliness.

Rumor has it, Southern Candymakers is the best place to get pralines.  I would believe it - they are delicious.  Get 'em while they are hot.  They give you a free sample to get you addicted.  The employee's are always very friendly too.

Good atmosphere and great martini's!!! This place has charm and is perfect for a night cap. If you are not a fan of smoking in bars, then St. Louis in general is not the place for you - and this place is no exception. I will say that you might want to try the martini that has "Pig" and "Leather" in the name. It is trouble... and the chocolate rim... YUM!!!

This is a classic "main drag" tourist restaurants. We were starved and in a rush, and the reviews on yelp made it seem safe. Food was OK, restaurant was clean, and so were the bathrooms. Good Bloody Mary. The only complaint is that we had Crusty the Clown as our waiter. Seriously thought the guy was loaded. .
What can you say a Saint Louis icon.  A must visit place, wonderful dessert experience.  Try the apple pie concrete

I absolutely love the Carne Seca burrito. This burrito is loaded with the very best Carne Seca in town.. in a very fresh tortilla. I always have them add some shredded lettuce.   It's so good that this is always my first and last stop when I visit Tucson. Don't get it to go. Enjoy it there. The meat is so juicy you really need to eat it ASAP.

My wife and I moved here a year ago from Nashville. We have been hunting for authentic Mexican food for when my wife doesn't feel like cooking (originally from Mex). Well needless to say we found that place in Real Del Monte. Great drinks, great food! Ok prices. This place isn't super noticeable as it's a hole in the wall type of place but very good food! Will be going back many times.

Really impressed with this place. I had to change my appointment multiple times, and they were accomodating and friendly- I was even able to change it via text. 

The doctor was very knowledgeable; she explained why I should get my eyes dilated and photographed to keep a record of the shape, etc. Although I did not plan to have that done at that particular visit, she said I could come in at a later time and would not be charged an additional office visit. 

I also spoke to someone about glasses and they gave my an additional 20% off of my already discounted price from my insurance. 

They are open late and on the weekends- I will definitely be back!
Came here for brunch, loved the atmosphere and food was great. My husband got the French toast and I had the chicken and waffles. He also had a good IPA, great beer selection!

I have begged and pleaded with my company's HR department to drop these turkeys. Somehow no one was responsible for contracting with them, so there's no way to get some other kind of prescription coverage.  I pay for half my medication out of pocket so that I have the peace of mind knowing that I'll have my medicine when I need it. Terrible customer service.  Terrible company. If you ever have the choice, choose differently.

This place was great.  There's no too much else to say.  Their cheese was phenomenal and everything we ate was wonderful.  Service was friendly and fast and when we got the bill, I was amazed at how reasonable it was for 3 people to eat lunch.  They even pleased a very picky 11 year old and I can tell you that's no easy feat.  Good food, good prices... I'll be back.
I was told about this place from a friend. After ordering my first concrete, I ate it in the car and got back out for another.

The order came in 16 minutes late.  I did not mention this to the manager when I called him.  I had called him to complain that my order of Shrimp Ceviche had only one shrimp but that the Beef Kabab was good.  He did not offer a refund or an offer to give me a new order of Shrimp Ceviche.  I think he was also the cook, because, he didn't give a damn.

Wanted a sandwich and beer. His tenderloin had cheese in it which he did not order. Also had a hair on his plate he didn't order. Bathroom out of order and needs upgrade. Won't be back.

You reply 8 months later? That's a problem.

I don't understand all the 3 star reviews on here. 

This is a solid new spot with great apps and homemade noodles for their soups. 
They make a perfect soft boiled egg that goes in some of the soup dishes, that I guess scared a few people? Also their kimchi is the best I've had so far in philly.

Friendly service, fair prices, BYOB, fresh juices everyday and unique food combinations.  We had the crispy rice cakes, kimchi, fish ribs, ramen noodles and hand torn noodles with lamb.

I would definitely go back, remembering to bring a 6-pack and I need to try the wings, I hear they are awesome.
Had 2 separate small jobs done by Zimco. I'd highly recommend them. Professional, friendly and got the job done quickly with no messes. Very good work.

These guys were fast, efficient and super friendly. I always went to Jiffy lube and the corporate places. This changes now. I even got free windshield wipers for cheaper than what I was paying from other places. Great coupon! Not to mention they use an automated system that shows me my exact report and I could also directly text back with questions. Great place.

This is my go-to grocery store. There's not too much special about it other than its location. Their deli is ok, but I find the bakery lacking. It's more expensive than Superstore, and I assume also more expensive than other Save Ons that are not located downtown. 

The only thing I really love about this location is its amazing bulk aisle. I haven't seen one quite as good in a regular grocery store (not including, saying, those stores that do exclusively bulk). Cheap spices and baking supplies!

Redhound is a warm and inviting place. And, the food is darned good too. My wife and I reside in Paoli and bumped into the Redhound a couple years ago. Having driven past one too many times, we made plans one night to head over for their burger special. 

All the food is above average pub fare. Great burgers, grilled sandwiches, salads and of course, a good choice of cocktails if this is what you desire as well. Since our first visit to the Redhound, we have been there several more times within the last year. Family friends, fun, personable and tasty. Definately worth a visit.

5 Star service from our amazing waitress! The place was packed after the wine walk downtown, drunken girls in the bathroom vomiting and crying... That was a side note... I took Mike T's advice and stuck with the Brewer's burger (medium rare, of course!) It was awesome! And the usual XXX Blonde and tried a seasonal Pumpkin Ale, you have to try before it's gone, easy to drink and great! The hubby was a little disappointed with his Vietnamese BBQ beef but only because it was lacking on the amount of beef although he loved his IPA as usual (Anchor Steam lover that he is!)
Food and service was excellent. Had the sautéed crab claws, on the half shell and chargrilled oysters. Save room for the bread pudding it was amazing.

Couldn't have better things to say about this place. We pulled in figuring it might be a tourist trap but it was a rainy day and it looked pretty cool so why not check it out. Our bartender Kevin was awesome. His service was excellent, his recommendations for food were spot on (down to where he thought we would / would not enjoy based on our home state), and every drink he made was great. We tried the bbq shrimp, the tuna poke, and the crab bisque... all were delicious. The prices might be considered slightly above average, but I wouldn't hesitate to pay them for the service, quality cleanliness, and atmosphere. The fish tanks and artwork were a great plus. Definitely would recommend and return!!!

Used to really like this place.  Went there two weeks or so ago and got the dinner for four.  For about $76 (after tax and tip), we got about $20 worth of food.  We all left still hungry.   And the food, especially the shrimp, was not good.

I'd love to give the Element 0 stars but that's not an option.  First, maybe years ago this was a  modern, up to the date hotel, but not any more.  First, the problems with the room.  There is no water pressure in the rain shower head, which results in not better than a weak urine stream.  They have shampoo/conditioner and body wash dispensers mounted on the wall which reminds me of showering at the YMCA.  One of which didn't work causing me to do my hair with body wash. Nice.  The TV on both nights showed "No Signal" on all the network channels as well as ESPN channels and their one premium channel Showtime.  That left me with the weather channel ad some other random junk.  Their "breakfast" included consisted of  out of the box donuts, muffins, some stale cereal in a tube and juice.  When I called Johnny at the front desk about the reported issues with the TV and Shampoo dispenser, his response was welll I'm not in maintenance" response was less that what I expected.  After I hung up on him he insisted in calling me back to vent his opinion on me regarding my concerns about the hotel.  If you a business traveler or even a casual traveler go to the Courtyard Mariott, and not this weak franchised version of a Westin hotel. 

btw... Chair is room is broken, desk light in room is broken, TV swirl stand in room is broken, No pen, desk pad, etc.. Just thing you expect from Hotels not named "Motel 6"

Tiny and rustic spot. No real way to explain the brilliance of this place. If you want to see a show get there AT LEAST an hour ahead. I got to sit on the floor on cushions   The trombone slide literally had to pass my head for his low notes. I could read the serial number on his spit valve. Intimate and amazing. Incredible house band. You cannot ask for a better experience. If you don't want to stand or sit on the floor look into reserving bench seats. This is a must in New Orleans!!

Pros: the food was delicious. The server was cool.

Cons: our server was inattentive. Specifically: we were not checked for water once during the meal, I fact he didn't check on us at all. He also ran off right after we ordered our entrees so we didn't have a chance to put in an appetizer. Waiting for like 10 minutes after we were done eating for the check was awesome, too.

Had our server not been such a phantom, the restaurant could have easily scored an appetizer and another beer from us.

Verdict: not terrible, but don't go out of your way to come here, either.
It was average pizza, under cooked for me and kinda doughy. Huge slices.

What a wonderful and chic restaurant. Great place to have a sit down dinner or a drink and snack at the bar. Kale chop salad and the pork belly with horchata foam was the best meal I've had in a very long time.
Amazingly prepared vegetarian food. I am huge fan of the asparagus blue corn tacos and also the veggie nachos. BYOB.

I'm not strictly a fan of Arby's as say compared to a sit-down restaurant. But as far as fast-food joints go, this was pretty good. I went at peak lunch rush. The place was busy, but the lines progressed quickly. I placed my order, it came out quickly, but not so quickly that I wondered how long it had been sitting on the counter waiting for someone to order it. I went to the self-serve area to fill my soda. Their Pepsi was out, so I let one of the clerks know about the problem. She refilled the Pepsi immediately, then went so far as to ask me if she could get me a napkin (those were almost out too) or anything else. Service was tip top!

This location has a drive-thru, and really good access from the highway. You can enter the restaurant from two different locations which is great, since it's right off a divided high-way, and if there weren't two entrances, a u-turn would be necessary for half the patrons.
Just went in for appetizers. We got the Buffalo chicken dip and deviled eggs which were great.  They were out of chips for the dip and substituted french bread.  Probably better than the chips.
I had the duck and it was incredible. The rice and vegetables are fresh and flavorful. The atmosphere in the restaurant is very pleasant as well. I love this place for dinner.

Well, I had friends over one day, and we decided to take a stroll down Magazine because we were starving.  Everywhere we wanted to go was extremely busy, and we passed this place. Nobody was in there, but they were open. A little hesitant at first.. we decided to try it....     The menu at the time had so many things to choose... We ordered lima beans and shrimp, grilled catfish with shrimp creole sauce, and we decided to try the charbroiled oysters.
Oh, my goodness....let me tell you, it was all good. I was really surprised. The service was good, too. They were training a new server that day...I can't say much about her since she didn't know what all to do yet, but the guy who was training her, and also taking care of us, was nice.  The prices are reasonable. 
I will recommend this place. 
Since I liked the food so much, I have been back numerous times... for to go orders, though.

This review is for Alex customer service representative when u dial *611. I was giving a review through text however I believe My response was too long and didn't get sent so I am yelping! I chose 5 (10) stars Because Alex has proved to me today that the customer service has much improved over the last 10 years I have been with Verizon! It went from " I see you owe a balance are you calling to take care of that today" to " how can I help you" huge difference! She helped resolve the issue and reassured us that our bill will not be over $ 1000 ! What a relief! I do have to add that I was yelled at by a Verizon customer service (rated a 0 in the past) representative years ago for owing over $300 and I was being judged for not paying my bill when I was truly going through a struggling crisis, I will never forget how much I cried that day! I called today owing way more than $300 and never once did Alex mention my balance or bill. Prime example that she was looking out for my needs as the customer! I cannot thank Alex and everyone involved in this resolution enough! However, I do need to add that... the Verizon Goleta office is very sneaky and are responsible for the whole mess. I would look into these "salesmen" only out for a commission and not the customers best interest at heart! Compassion goes a long way!

A kitschy surfer themed bar with nice decor. Went there late night when it was a young, drunk, just-out-of-college type hookup bar. Fun but a little young for my taste.

We also had a daytime function in their second floor meeting space, which was also nicely decorated, had a nice breeze from the floor-to-ceiling open windows (with wrought iron railings). The food and service were pretty good, and it was inexpensive. Would definitely recommend for groups.

This place is AWFUL. Never again will I go to this location or ANY clarkson eyecare for that matter. They wrote the wrong perscription and want to charge ME to make up for their mistake!! I was given bad attitude by the receptionist and they are VERY UNPROFESSIONAL!!! Do not go here!!

There were some pro's and con's to my dinner at the Red Owl Tavern. Pro: We were seated quickly. Con: It took FOREVER to get our food after we ordered. Pro: The Mussles in the curry au jus were phenomenal. Con: The fried Calamari was bland and unspired.  Pro: The specialty cocktail slushy was out of this world delicious. Con: There is NO bathroom in the restaurant. It's located like a mile away in the hotel. Pro: I have to say, the management took care of us that night. Since the food took so long to come, they took all of our drinks off the bill and 50% off the check. I probably wouldn't make a point of returning, but at least they tried to rectify the situation.

What a great hidden gem....has been a local "dive" bar under several names, but things have changed....everything is cooked on the spot. The ribs are out of this world, and at that price for an "appetizer" they're a whole meal. They've recently added fried cheese curds, and if you're from anywhere near Wisconsin, you'll know at first taste, that they're the real thing. Hospitality is definitely 5 star. They make you feel like family the minute you walk in the door. Don't know about the other music, but there's a group on Tuesday nights called The Boomers, who know all those oldies and goodies that we and our parents have loved through the year. New dance floor doesn't hurt, and it does get a work out! It will definitely become one of our "go to" places, and will bring our winter visitors there.....
Rita's is always a summer tradition, the options for water ice are plentiful.

Squeegee Express is the best window washing company in town! Great price, sparkling clean windows, polite, wore booties in the house to protect my floors, showed up on time, and stuck to the price quoted. I've been washing my own windows for several years which simply means they weren't washed very often. They went above and beyond the call of duty by removing and reinstalling the cat seats I have attached to the windowsills in two rooms. That needed to be done to remove the screens and clean the tracks. When they say they "vacuum" the tracks, it is far more than that! They scraped all the built up dirt out of them, and now my windows open and close more smoothly than ever! I would recommend them to my best friend and will certainly be calling them to keep my view of sunny Arizona clean and clear! Thanks, AJ!

Carrolton Market offers delicious and creative plates. The atmosphere is quiet and intimate. The staff really aims to please and take care of their diners. I appreciated the warm hospitality, the prompt and attentive service, and delicious food and cocktails.

This place is AMAZING. The cardio equipment is fantastic. The pool is really great considering we are in Philadelphia .



In terms of swimming coaches- Roger is fantastic. He is patient, brilliant at swimming technique and he  breaks down all of the swimming strokes to really ensure proper form.

A+!!
Love this place!!  Great Sunday brunch food and fabulous soundtrack too!  We had a super server, Amy!!

HORRIBLE SERVICE!  This is now the third restaurant (unless I've lost count) to occupy the space since Harrah's opened.  The food is descent and the beer is very good, but, alas, the service is HORRIBLE!  It seems to be a problem that has plagued this venue space since it opened; it takes way too long to get served and food ordered.  What should've taken 45 minutes took over an hour.  I only eat here if I have to when I'm at Harrah's.

We visited the Kenner location September 10 for a friends birthday dinner. We had a party of 11 adults and we all arrived for 7 PM and they sat us at the table with in a few minutes.  Quite impressed and our server was excellent on spot w everything.  Price is reasonable for the food quality and portion size. I had the Lasagna and my fiancé ordered chicken parm. Both were good and everyone said theirs was as well except a shrimp dish.  There was not enough shrimp and I agree. Again service was excellent.

This place is awesome. Perfect when you want a break from the heavy greasy food and actually want to eat healthy. Don't get it twisted their healthy food still has flavor.

I had an amazingly fresh green blast with kale, carrot, Apple, lemon and ginger; no pre-made mix I watched her juice it!

For brunch I ate the hatchery sandwich with turkey which included egg whites,  tomatoes, garlic, goat cheese, mushrooms and spinach on a croissant, it was awesome! Very light and full of flavor. 

It's a small place but big enough for the crowd. It's inside a building facing diamond street where people load up for cruises so it can be hard to miss. But don't miss out!

OK . . . this would be a 4 but it seems over the years the prices have creeped up but the food has definitely stayed the same. In a good way of course. I swear they have the same dinner ware since the day they opened. This place (except for the prices) hasn't changed in decades. CASH only! Closed on Tuesdays -- found that shit out the hard way ;( -- some of the t=THE BEST fish spread around. Take it to go is the best unless you're just coming from the beach.

Had a Solo lunch at the bar and really enjoyed the food and great service. Had the Black tie Chicken Pasta and Caesar salad with some fresh garlic cheese bread.   GOOD FOOD and GREAT SERVICE... large portion from lunch menu ... I travel weekly for work and hope I make it back here soon, Thanks to  April the Bartender

Ohhhhh where to start!!!! I ordered a falafel pita with no hummus, no black olives, no cucumber, and no green pepper!!! Well I got exactly what I did not want!!! I am not being a picky person but unfortunately I'm not a hummus fan (yeah I know I like falafel but not hummus) and I am allergic to cucumbers ( not my fault but makes me puke and gives me a rash) so what happened when I opened up my pita.... Went straight to the trash!!! I am never calling in an order to this place again!
Great selection and well informed proprietor.  Eric will answer all your inquiries.  And the prices are very cool.  Quality and expertise.

I like Chuck E. Cheese. The staff is very helpful and friendly and the atomosphere is very vibrant and colorful. I greatly enjoy coming here. The pizza is delicious and they always have full soft drink machines. However, it can be a bit expensive so look for coupons online. Otherwise, it is very safe and clean:)

I was nervous about where to go get my nails done. I had to find a good place because it was my wedding day. I found Clayton nail and it was meant to be!! Love the e service!! I believe the girl who helped me was Tracey. I was clueless on what I should do and she helped me!! My new favorite spot!
Great Vape Shop! The guy in the shop knew his stuff and they make their juices right there! He will even let you try before you purchase. Such a breath of fresh air from snooty or ignorant shops.

We had our daughters High School Graduation party on the newly renovated patio area. Dion and Candice really went out of there way to make the party special for our daughter. From the oversized balloons to the fantastic food the party was a complete hit. My wife and I have been going to Chic a Boom Room for 20 years, but the new owner (Dion) have really made a great Dunedin landmark even better. Thank you all for a great time and making our daughters special day even better! We cant say enough good things about this place!

The atmosphere and dessert were amazing. The service was quite poor. The hostess stand was turned around and pushed against a wall. After waiting in line for 20 mins to order, we were told we needed to wait another 20 mins for a table to order there.
