Our names were written on a piece of paper and were never called, although several tables were sitting empty. We finally just seated ourselves at the bar and were finally served. No one knew who ordered what and customers had to keep repeating their orders to ensure they received the correct ones. Would go again for the food, but will definitely be getting it to go until the service is addressed.

This is my favorite spot for an in-and-out lunch! The Turnip Truck has such a wide selection of foods, including a salad bar, a soup station with 4-5 choices, and several other food options. I usually load my to go box up with a bunch of different foods, and I've never been disappointed. 

There's also groceries, which I don't have experience with, but I'm sure everything in there is great because it's known for its healthy options!

There's an inside and outdoor area to sit when you want to eat, which is awesome! 

There's also a juice bar here. I've loved every juice I've had here, as well!

In Philly for the day haandling sone business and asked by the Misses to stop by this restaurant and pick up a platter. Cant say I am familiar with this particular establishment. This was found off a search of african restaurants in Philly. The platter I went to pick up was a red snapper fish platter, which was one of the largest platters I had ever seen. The container had to be close to 10 inches long. White rice, sauteed onions, fish looked great and seasoned. Was alsi able to get somne pics of the place both inside and outside and could see it being worth coming back for other full platters. Great find on Yelp!!

Portion sizes were lacking and I wasn't impressed with the dish I ordered either (The Sweet Potato Hash). I mean a hash isn't a fancy dish or anything so I didn't expect much but at least give me enough to feel satisfied. I wouldn't say I have a huge appetite either :/ I guess I'm also comparing this place to Hash House A Go Go so i'm bias. On another note, the servers were very nice. However, I had to ask a couple of times to get a refill of water/coffee, this is probably just because the place is new. Lastly I was disappointed that they sold out of "dossants" so early in the day, 11 am which is prime brunch time! I ended up ordering the white chocolate croissant thing and it was alright. I was expecting it to be more flaky, not stale. I'll have to give it another try, order something else and hopefully go early enough  to try the dossant/cronut that everyone appears to be raving about in NY.

PLEASE PLEASE make sure you read in its entire form the 4 page contract for the tool rental at any home depot. The reason im giving this store a 1 is because Troy and Matt (the assistant manager) were patronizing me when i was not understanding their policy to charge for a FULL day if you keep the rental for over 4 hours on the second day. Troy asked me if i had ever rented before at any home depot and i said yes 1 time and he said well its the same policy at any home depot you go to. Well Troy, im sorry i do not know your policies but you dont have to treat me like im crap. He agreed to reverse the charge but would need manager approval and the manager MATT came and asked me what the issue was and i explained, well i wasnt aware of your policy to charge a full days rental for being 6 hours late. He said, well it in your contract. I said, SHOW me where it says that. He fumbled around for 5 minutes and could not find it. The money was not the issue for me. It was the way i was treated, like an idiot that should have known. After waiting forever for Matt to show me in the contract their policy i ATE the $150 extra they charged me for 6 hours overage because i could not take it anymore their stupidity and lack of customer service. Again, right off the back when i questioned the extra $150 charge Troy got defensive so i assume he gets the same complaint from other customers about their policy. I must say, i do not disagree with their policy, only that they treated me with the utmost disrespect and patronizing customer service. I must add that MATT the assistant manager did try to refund $63 but with an attitude as if he was doing me this huge favor. I didnt want the $63 at this point. All i wanted was an explanation of their policy and to show me in writing where it was. They could not do that. My daily $$$$$ spent on flips just went out their front door. Kudos to Matt and Troy

I met my friend Hannah for a friendly breakfast and coffee session at Cairdeas today and I must say that I was impressed with the small local cafe. 

I ordered the Dogtown Breakfast Sandwich - egg, bacon, sausage, and american cheese with an orange slice on the side, along with an iced vanilla coffee. It was, dare I say, the best breakfast sandwich I have ever had. Highly recommended. I also have a tough time being critical with anything involving bacon. 

My small coffee was upgraded free of charge for some reason. I didn't complain. 

The staff was incredibly helpful and friendly. One of the employees wanted us to try (for free) a fresh pumpkin breakfast bar that was one part pumpkin pie (soft, rich, and flavorful center) and one part coffee cake (with a crunchy, strudel-like topping). 

For whatever reason, the front door and a front window were open. It was a tad chilly inside, so maybe close them during those brisk fall mornings? Just a thought.

After we were finished with our chat, the barista boxed up our leftovers (since the sandwich was quite large) for us. I love Dogtown and now I have another reason to come back.

David (Porter) saw me sitting in the car in the heat and immediately asked me if I was ok and being helped, even though I said yes, he still went to see to whom I was assigned to and got someone out right away to move me along.  The person I made my appt with was out and because of David's pro active, problem solving, critical thinking, I did not fall in the crack. Kudos to David.  Also, I would like to thank Dimitri Coton, the mechanic who worked on my car, for taking pride in his work and giving me his best.  An invisible person to me but I would like to say Thank You, what Dimitri didn't know is that I'm driving that car ALONE to Vermont and he made it and me safe to do that.  100% of the time I get my car serviced I receive 125% service.  Anyone with a blue shirt will spend all the time I need explaining to me how to use my navigator, radio, steering wheel....AWESOME people every one of them....FERMAN does it with class, skills, and patience.

Wow, I just read all the reviews and I'm shocked!  Let me start by saying that I met the new owners a few weeks ago when picking up an order.  This evening I picked up a meatball and onion small pizza and it is delicious.  Crust not too thick, sauce good and plenty of toppings.
I'm from just outside Manhattan and am really picky about my pizza.  There is very little good pizza in Pasco County and I'm sick of all these places who advertise as being from NY or have NY in their name.  I'm not sure what part of NY they (may) be from, but it's bad pizza.  
Slice of Life is quite close to the "real deal".  Give them a try-I think you'll be glad you did!          On another note, I often picked up from the previous owner and saw maybe 2 to 4 people having a dinner in.  Tonight every table was full at 6:30.  So I'm guessing the dinners are good too.                                                                                                                                                    I've been getting delivery or picking up at Slice of Life for about 4 years and was never disappointed but I think these new owners have really got something here!

The price was great and the food is tasty. The first two times the service was impeccable and the staff was attentive. The third time the tables which have beautiful decorative mosaic tile were covered in tacky plastic and the service was not very good. I had to ask multiple times for silverware and napkins. The food is definitely worth checking out. I'll definitely give it another try. I love Peruvian food.
Stopped in for lunch while in NOLA for a trade show.  Great Cuban sandwich!  Would highly recommend it.  Bread was incredible.

My first time in the Indy airport and at this establishment. Not impressed with the service or food. Ordered a margarita pizza which came with canned peeled tomato pieces and very little basil. Since these are the only two ingredients I wouldn't expect it to be hard to make well. Should be fresh tomatoes slices and ample basil--very easy. Then, my husband ordered a sirloin bacon burger and watched the cook wait until he received enough orders to fill his grill before starting to cook anything. I was completely finished with my pizza before his burger was done. The sad thing is that the restaurant (and airport) wasn't busy at all. No excuse for bad service! Will not come here again. I'm sure other restaurants are worth the walk down the concourse.
This place has been my neighborhood staple for many years. the food has always been good and very consistent.  Prices have always been reasonable ... I would recommend !

Actually shocked Mena's gets some bad reviews. Went there for an early lunch and they were already hopping. LOTS of phone-in orders from locals...that tells me plenty. I had the chicken gyro platter - nice salad, warm pita, chicken breast that wasn't dry, tzatziki sauce(extra! thank you very much!) and fries.  Only meh part were the fries...kinda mealy and not crispy, but no biggie. I concentrated on  the totally delish chicken and pita.

Waitress was a doll and kept my coke filled (was working a hangover, dontcha know!). 

Place is only breakfast and lunch, so plan accordingly. And I would go a little before the rush...like I said...place was busy! Oh, the prices are very reasonable, esp for the FQ.

No signs of food poisoning yet. Will update if need be. So far this is a positive experience. Came on a Sunday just before midnight, very convenient they are open till midnight every night. Gotta say though, key lime pie was no bueno. Dark night is definitely got the win on this one. This place is much better than Dough Cone next to Carrabbas. Very negative experience there. The little chocolate bear is a nice touch, we were very satisfied with that one.
I love Cafe Du Monde, but this cafe's employees at Lakeside Mall have AWFUL manners. Horrible service! ..enjoyed my food and coffee though.

They have decent pub food.  The beer is probably the crappiest micro I have ever had.  I actually went as far as to try them all just to make sure I wasn't missing something special.  On the weekends usually have live music but it can turn into a meat market real quick.

Fantabulous!!! Andre was amazing. Osso Bucco was amazing.  Bananas Foster was amazing.  Tiramisu had a little too much Creme and not enough "cake" espresso for me. Other than that nitpick.....absolutely worth the price I paid. Will go again for sure.

Stay because the staff is awesome. All the ladies we encountered were so helpful and nice. We were told our part is haunted but that was ok to us. Our view was of a brick wall and a building (room 25) and finding an outlet that worked was difficult. The next morning the shower wouldn't work and our waste basket looked as if it had been crushed & brought back to life. Street parking only here by the way. Breakfast is plain and simple!! Our AC stopped cooling and I thought I would have a heat stroke but I endured because these kind ladies gave us this room very last minute on an event weekend for only 1 night and that's unheard of! I suggest the Tavern next door for break fast, lunch & dinner if you need affordable good food. The staff was awesome there as well. Either way the location is so convenient, the staff is fabulous and I would stay again. We stayed during a marathon therefor the streets were blocked with Peppe first biking then running and a pretty jammin band playing in the street. Did I mention there is also tons of food nearby like tacos, sushi, and BBQ! Oh and a cool pizza place next door.
Crappy little building but the best cake donut I've ever had! So much better than any grocery store donut you could get.

A cute and eclectic shop that I could spend a lot of time in. Definitely a more out there mix of items - bright,  colorful, statement pieces are going to be found here - which I consider a huge plus. They also have a substantial jewelry section in addition to the other knick knacks - think journals, t-shirts, mugs, socks, unique kids books, etc.

This is my first review that I ever left but felt like I had to.  We ordered the general tso, sesame chicken, bourbon chicken, pork chow mien, shrimp chow mien, and all with pork fried rice. We eat a lot of Chinese and this was the worst ever. The flavor of everything was terrible. The bourbon chicken taste like liquid smoke was poured over it and was dry and rubbery. The general and sesame was the same sauce with sesame seeds added.  The chow mien did not taste bad as it was mostly flavorless. Finally the fried rice did not taste like any fried rice I have ever had.  Not being funny, a can of la choy would have been better and much cheaper.

From out of town and came upon this place that was near where we were staying. Everything was good. Had orange chicken, chicken egg foo young, and beef broccoli. Egg roll and cream cheese wonton. Nothing that would say spectacular but very good. Pricing was normal for not being fast food.

I'm visiting my Daughter at Dillard University. She spoke highly of Li'l Dizzyy's Cafe.  We had the buffet . The food was amazing.  I enjoyed everything I had the fried chicken , green beans , Mac and cheese and of course the Gumbo. The atmosphere is cozy everyone is really friendly. Its like eating at a relatives house that can really cook. On my next trip I'll be coming back.

It's cool that Haddonfield finally has a brewery in town! I recall that one of my final articles as a hyper-local reporter in the borough more than five years ago was on a special beer event being hosted by Indian King Tavern; otherwise it was a dry town. I'm glad they've moved past that ordinance, as the brewery brings a nice breath of less-stuffy air into the main business district.

Kings Road is a local brewery to the core. They offer a host of quality suds in a variety of styles. I appreciate the experimentation. I tried lighter beers during my visit, including a saison and a coffee saison. While the coffee was not my thing personally, I did like the complexity that went into formulating the brew.

While they don't serve food, they have a whole booklet of menus from eateries nearby. You can call or walk to any of them, or just have a meal after your visit. The brewery is so central that there's plenty of places to choose from in the direct vicinity.

I no longer live in New Jersey, so I won't be a regular, but I'm hopeful I'll be able to return at some point in the future to check out their evolution. I'd recommend it to locals!

I can confirm what everyone else has said - these guys are the best!  They are reliable, talented and above all, honest.  They have helped me keep old junker cars safe and inexpensively on the road, doing only what needs to be done.  They have also taken care of my "better" car with the same eye to economy.  I trust them completely and recommend them to everyone looking for a place to take their car.

This is my 2nd restaurant for We Live To Eat Restaurant Week and my fourth Besh Restaurant (I still haven't tried Besh Steakhouse).  Besh has another winner of a restaurant.  I just loveee how all of his restaurants are so completely different from one another!  Off the set menu, I got the crab and corn bisque as a starter, which was tasty.  I just wish there was more crab in it.  My entree was the Veal cutlet.  I could not finish it since the portion was too big.  I liked it, but I didn't love it.  I really wished their infamous shrimp and grits were on the set menu for me to try!  My boyfriend had the Luke Burger which was HUGE and so tender.  I highly recommend the burger!  He also got the Abita Turbodog which he said was "really good."  Those words rarely come out of his mouth, because he's already tried a big variety of food and drinks so he's usually very nonchalant about anything he intakes, so that beer must be something!  He's a big fan of dark beers if anyone wants to know his taste.  For dessert, we got the Bread Pudding. OMG!  AMAZINGGGGGG!!!  It had to be one of the best Bread Puddings I've had!  it came with a rum praline sauce and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.  I would come back just for this dessert!

I definitely plan on coming back, since I want to try so many things on the menu including the pate and the shrimp and grits.  I'm also going to try to come during happy hour for those quarter oysters!

Watch out for the 'extra' charges these people add to your boarding fees!  We have an older dog that requires several medications twice a day.  Most of those meds are chewable and only need to be added to his kibble.  When we left our dog for a 14 day stay, we were advised there was a fee for dispensing meds - so far nothing out of the ordinary.  Imagine our surprise when we picked up our dog to discover we were charged $1.75 PER PILL!  Over $200.00 to distribute meds which only needed to be added to kibble.  All the other kennels we have used charged a flat medication dispensing fee - per pill charge, really!  While they have posted 'best of' reviews/notices all around the property, it seems to us what they are really 'best of,' is separating customers from their money. This was doubly dissapointing as when we used Holiday House in the late 90's and early 00's their fees were much more transparent and reasonable.  While the care seemed to be great, the upsold charges exceeded everything in our prior experience!  BE WARNED!

Food was fantastic!  Service was great!  We were treated like we were so important.  The only reason holding it back from 5 stars is the restaurant was very warm and I felt the tables were to close together.  Everyone was on top of each other.
Soooooo slow, over priced, undermanned, and chaotic environment inside.  Poor parking, minimal seating, and odd location.

I originally gave this place 2 stars but quickly realized it was only to do with the stylist I had that day. The customer service and quick responses are exceptional. Glad to have had a chance to chat with Tatiana as she referred me to a stylist working there and was able to change my mind about this place! Will be returning.
Our server was Kelly, outstanding server and suggest you ask for her! Food was great and restaurant was clean.

Good food! Awesome neighborhood with lots to do and a clean and comfortable restaurant. The decor is cute and the drinks and food were tasty. My cons are around cost. $3 for a small bowl of mushy collard greens was a ripoff, and the food was good but very overpriced. We paid $42 for two po boys, a beer, and a sweet tea. I would recommend for sure, but only if price isn't an issue or you're there for the neighborhood.

So when Brandon ceased to work at Wizards at the end of 2014 I was sad because I knew that it would be a while before I had a regular comic book shop to frequent. When Variant Edition finally opened its doors to the public with a grand opening on Free Comic Book Day I was sad because I couldn't be there. Well, this store certainly doesn't disappoint. Not only does it have a TARDIS (what other comic book shop has a TARDIS, I might ask?) but it has three of the most  wonderful staff members/owners: Brandon, Danica and Brendan. And I definitely have a comic book shop to call my own again, which is splendid!

They do a brisk sales in graphic novels, comics, and Magic The Gathering cards. There is a nice children's section (yes I shop there too). I like the personal attention I get from Danica and Brandon when looking for comics to purchase because they'll likely know immediately if they have it in stock (whether out on the shelves or in the back). I love the graphic novels section and tend to spend a pretty penny (yes, I actually did use some pennies on my last visit, strangely enough). But really, since the store has only been open for just over a month, I would expect it to only get better and better as time goes on. Quite honestly it's already impressed me! It's clean, bright and filled with wonderful wares to purchase! 

Accessible (only a block or two away) from transit, this location is just off of some major roadways and has ample street parking available. I highly recommend checking this place out as it is most excellent!

Got recommended this place by the cabbie on the way to the hotel. Came in the wrong door but got seated right away. Dave my waiter should get credit. With a beer in my hand (nice draft selection), I set to see what yelp at to offer. Thin crust pizza was heavily recommended, even by my cabbie, but just wasn't in the mood. Saw one review for a soggy crust and no New Yorker needs to read further. Same reviewer mentioned the steak pasta. I took the plunge. I ordered a salad as a starter and the steak pasta. 

Salad came out ok. Nothing spectacular. And then IT happened. I can't stand when they stack the entree right on top of the salad. Had the salad for like three minutes and the pasta came out! Party foul! 

Ok so regained composure and started the pasta after I took my time with the salad. Steak was cooked well. Sauce, sour cream base, was nice. Bread was an after thought. Had more steak than the steak dinner the two happy blondes next to me were eating. 

Overall not bad. Waiter very attentive, borderline too attentive. Atmosphere was nice for a Thursday evening. Struggled between three or four stars. Opted for four since in a post-prandial coma. Tomorrow Charlie Gito's...

This building is pretty cool and in an industrial area of Tucson; a lot off of the beaten path but easy to get to and not too far from I-10.  After working at a brewpub in Michigan, I have grown to prefer micro-brew beer.  Our waitress let us sample a few beers to get an idea what we wanted which was nice because their beer sampler is kind of pricey ($12 for 3oz. samples).  My boyfriend ended up with the Hefe and I opted for the nicely balanced yet somewhat malty Amber.

We met up with my family who all enjoyed their dinner; wings, reuben, philly, and burgers.  Service was great, knowledgeable, attentive, and responsive though the Saturday evening was not busy at the brewery.   Overall I recommend anyone to check it out, oh, and bring your shuffleboard game!!

This review is specifically to boast about their alcoholic milk shakes- WOW.  My husband got the bananas foster and I seriously have to try to copy cat it once we get home so all my friends can compliment me on the concoction. The burgers were great, not sure I can claim them as being the "world's best", but they were definitely great. I'm not a big French fry eater but these fries were perfect. Long, crisp, perfect dash of salt... so good we ended up ordering a side order of sweet potato tater tots and those were great as well.  We left stuffed and happy. Would recommend.

one of the employees at this location was wearing a cross during lent. i could tell they were not at all religious, so i asked them kindly to please tuck it into their shirt, at least while i was there. that felt simple enough, it was a sign of respect for me, the customer. WELL the employee decided that they couldn't do that to show me a modicum of respect. instead they motioned as if they were tucking it in their shirt and as soon as i turned my back it was sitting there, emblazoned on their chest. i was truly offended and upset. i didn't even want their food anyway at that point. i just couldn't believe an employee could be so inconsiderate.
Love going to this place, they do a great job and and so kind. Their prices are low as well and you still get quality service.
I went to this place for the first time last night. It was amazing. I like that the menu describes what is in each piece of sushi. I will definately go back
Came here for breakfast and was extremely satisfied! The staff is friendly and the food was delicious. Orders classic Eggs Benedict and the Basic Skillet. Both were seasoned perfectly and filling.

Very impressive location of "Whole Foods Market" !!!

I was a bit skeptical of going here, after visiting many locations of WFM around the country - yet, I have to admit that I pre-judged this location by a lot.

Hmm... Variety of foods, prepared goodies and everyday things is blown my mind away - they even better, then many SF locations of WFM - yeah, hard to imagine at first thought.

Just for fun - I have randomly scanned for items, I always buy on weekly basis in SF - yeah, they have them all - or even more (like a fresh "Opah" fish from Hawaii - we don't have it in SF)

I guess if you are fan of WFM like myself and living in the area - you don't need to dream about visiting WFM in SF or LA - you already have better option in the area ;-)

Great job team WFM @Reno!!!

Wish I lived closer to Santa Barbara so whenever I crave for a good greasy late night snack I can easily visit Mad Dogs, there were so many things I wanted on that menu too, definitely cheap good eats!

The texture is refreshing and tasty. My favorites are the classic cherry and lemon. The flavors do not taste super artificial and it's the right amount of sweetness. Also the people who work here are pretty nice!

Best in the city.

If I could put no stars I would I was looking forward to coming here for months ...... customer service is absolute terrible (Jennifer) is the worst should not work in any establishment where u have to serve people my drink was disgusting and they refused to make a new one even tho I paid for the souvenir mason jar and only had two scoops ......it's fine if I had to pay for another one but dnt be nasty and rude about it tho I will never come bkk me and my party 8 won't be bkk

I found Midcity Wax + Spa on yelp and highly recommend! My last Brazilian wax (before Suzie) I was on the table for over an hour (and I'm not even THAT hairy) with Suzie I had my Brazilian and underarms done in about 25 mins. She's professional, clean, and knowledgeable, and no hairs left behind! She uses hard and soft wax depending on the area and your hair. We talked about skin care and she even gave me some samples of the skin care line she carries, Arcona?and they're great! I want to book a facial and massage next! Also, gps led me to Cortez St and it was easy to park off Canal and walk two buildings to the left.
Just moved here and needed a nail spot, they are amazing. The spa is clean, everyone is so nice and do amazing work

We finally made it here with the intent of checking out this place for a possible UYE. Even though the executive chef was apparently sacked soon after opening, we had heard his recipes had endured. Also, four weeks from opening should have provided an opportunity for the restaurant to resolve their service challenges.

We were warmly greeted upon entering about 6pm on a Thursday. While there were many people there, the fact that we didn't have reservations was a non-issue! Our server, Alexa, also greeted us and did a fine job the entire evening!

Chips and three kinds of very tasty, fresh salsa were provided gratis. Green, red, and black bean! All were delicious but none had the slightest heat. I was surprised as salsa is a great opportunity to get your spice on!

We ordered a margarita and a watermelon/strawberry alcohol concoction. Both were very fresh tasting and went down easily! Who doesn't love a perfect margarita? I don't know and I don't care to find out!

We next ordered the octopus appetizer but were informed it wasn't available. For a high-end restaurant with numerous unique choices, this wasn't a wonderful start. But, we adjusted and got some bacon guacamole (really, this is on the menu!) and vegetable empanadas instead! 

The guacamole was fresh, covered in bacon and tasty but devoid of spiciness. I was expecting at least some slivers of jalapenos or something with some kick. Hrmmm. 

The veggie empanadas were huge, hot, and chock full of cheese and veggies. They were so large they could have been a meal. Again, they didn't have any spice at all. See a pattern here?

For dinner, we ordered two entrees, duck tacos, and fish tacos along with a side of Mexican corn. Each plate comes with two tacos so for you math aficionados, that's $8 a taco. They better be good! They were perfectly made, flavorful, with perhaps the slightest amount of spice. At this point, I suggested to my wonderful wife that we ask for hot sauce figuring perhaps they had a house made variety that would be amazing? They don't. The offered a standard off-the-shelf boring brand in a bottle and we declined.

The Mexican corn was the culinary highlight of the evening, off the cob for ease of eating, and full of flavor and spice!

In summary, the service was on point, the spotless restaurant was well decorated, and the food was very well presented although not everyone on the menu was available. If you want hot or spicy Mexican food, this isn't it. Ultimately, we enjoyed our meal and will probably return, perhaps.

I first visited this chain restaurant in Florida and loved it! Finally tried it back home and the experience was the same. 

The food was great, service was pretty good. The only problem I had was the 1hr long wait, but that's what I get for going at 5pm on a Saturday afternoon!! My boyfriend n daughter both enjoyed everything. Both of them are picky, but they loved the food. 
Oh and the loaded sweet potato is EVERYTHING! 
Will definitely go back!
Great service! Huevos Rancheros is where it's at! Definitely coming back. Good for a little breakfast variety in Franklin.

The dip, as people keep saying, was awesome.  

But I didn't go there for the dip.  I went there to eat dinner. And did we ever pick a bad night.  They kept apologizing for the food being so late, and then when they finally managed to bring it out, it was lukewarm.

90 minutes for lukewarm food.

My fajitas came out on a regular plate, b/c they had somehow managed to run out of clean fajita plates.

And my food, after waiting for it for 90 minutes, was LUKEWARM.

For me, this is their 3rd strike.  I really enjoyed the restaurant in e past, but after having other bad experiences (the busboy had to wait on us once) I'm finished.
As we walked in the employee kindly greeted us. Very good customer service! & the food was very delicious(:

I'd like to start by saying I don't frequently review apartments and I'm not usually critical. However, my experience here was by far the worst I've had as a renter. Here's a few things you can expect living at the Rosemont Plaza: 

* The busiest, loudest intersection on the Main Line. The traffic outside the apartment is extremely heavy during rush hour, making it impossible to turn into the building. Prepare to wake up each day to the sounds of honking horns and good luck trying to turn in/out of the apartment at peak times.

* Very poor insulation - the walls and windows are so poorly insulated you can hear a conversation going on in the parking lot even from the higher floors and all your neighbors. There's no privacy. 

* No central air or heating. Each apartment in Rosemont Plaza has a wall unit that only has heat in the winter months and cool air in the summer. There's no temperature controls, and if it's an unseasonably warm day from November-April, there's no way to cool down the apartment and the air becomes very dry. 

* Construction. During my time here, the construction was frequent on my floor to retrofit existing units. This was very loud and disruptive. Water was turned off often. There's no getting around the building's structural frame is very old and the renovations don't mask more fundamental problems with the AC, plumbing, insulation, and air quality. 

* Inflexible lease terms - I had to switch to a month-to-month lease because I wasn't sure when I would need to move. This came with both a rate hike, which is pretty typical, and the stipulation that I had to give 90 days notice to move. Why are you paying a premium for a month-to-month lease if it doesn't give you the flexibility to move? I've never encountered this before in any apartment contract.

The whole process of terminating the lease was also about as pleasant as pulling teeth. I suggested a date well in advance of the 90-day notice that I'd like to vacate and was only later informed my proposal would require management company approval. They did not let me know how long this approval process might take. It took months of back and forth to finalize a date and this process seemed cumbersome at best and really time-consuming for everyone. I think this could have been avoided by being transparent with tenants from the outset of those pre-approved dates to vacate and have them select one. 

By the end I was just counting the days until I could leave. The icing on the cake was the security deposit was also returned a month late - Pennsylvania law requires that deposits be returned in 30 days. It was not. I honestly have no idea how this apartment complex received so many good reviews.

At $100 for 2 people including salad, filet mignon, 3 seafood choices (shrimp, scallop, crab cake), two side dishes and 2 dessert, you cant go wrong!!!! it is so filling! The waiter was great service, straight forward and friendly..  This was the second time around for me at Morton's and I still remember how great the ginormous bread was ( nice and fluffy )  I had the mojito tonight but not strong, very sugary.  The steak was cooked just the right way for me ( medium rare ).  It was so much food for 2, we had the 2nd dessert made to go beforehand.  I recommend getting the $99 deal meal.. just let them know and they will let you know about the choices you get to choose from, or go on morton's steakhouse website to get the coupon and promotional code.. it is so worth it i believe for not having red meat for 1.5 months! living on the island and lack of meat, soo WORTH IT!

Very good Italian pastries....not superlative. A few things cross over into excellent, but again, most are very good. Quality or not, prices are pretty high for what you get. Pine-nut cookies at $23 a pound? Traditional Italian cookies at close to the same? Really? Only Termini's is higher. The people who consider anything made there "the best ever" have obviously never been to many Italian bakeries. Good basic place and convenient, but not in the same league as most South Philly places.

It's sometimes hard to do a transaction sight unseen on the internet, but Robert (sales) Monica (sales manager) and Randall (financing) worked diligently with me and gave me a great deal. I would highly recommend them!

I've got a shoe problem.  It's DSW's fault.

This place is a fancified warehouse, housing every kind of shoe imaginable. Thousands of options can be overwhelming, but they've got it organized by gender then style, so you can hone in on what you're looking for. Or maybe you're looking to look.

If so, grab a big black tote to hold your findings and don't miss the back room. It's sale central. And while some stuff is tacky and understandably marked down, some of it makes you do a double take and wonder if it's been misplaced.

I haven't walked away once without finding something I wanted. This is my first stop when shoe-shopping. Joining their rewards program was a no-brainer for me; every dollar I spend earns me a point and before I know it, I've got a certificate worth at least $10 off my next purchase. It's the problem and the solution.

Came here for valentine's day for the first time! The food was really good and the service was quick. I ordered the snapper fish with vegetables and fries. The vegetables and fries were good. The fish was okay. My server didn't ask if I wanted it seasoned so it was plain. We also tried the roasted fish of the day which was delicious! I will be getting that next time. Highly recommend the roasted fish!
Overrated. Everything was expensive and the food was decent, but just that decent.  This place is far to expensive for what you get.

This is my vet, I have forsaken all others. 

Very nice clean reasonable prices.

its well worth the drive across town for me.

I had an awesome experience with Mathew at this mall! He was so patient nice and helpful, he helped with sizing and picking different styles I really enjoyed our experience and love everything I wound up getting :)  it was truly a great shoe shopping experience! Thank you Mathew!

It was my first time at armature works and after looking around I decided on Hemingway's. The ultimo Cuban had amazing reviews so I went ahead and ordered it with rice, beans, and plantains. I was disappointed because the meat was seasoned with too much salt. I even had my brother try it and he agreed it was salty. Overall the experience was just average. It was a busy Sunday afternoon and the wait time was about 20 mins to get my food. I would try it again because i know it has the potential to be 5 stars.

We stopped by this place to get a quick bite and get out of the rain. We split a Hemingway Cuban sandwich and an order of beignets. Great little side place away from bourbon street and good selection of beers. Highly recommended!

I almost never sign up for store savings program cards as they never seem to amount to anything but I have to admit that the Rite Aid Wellness card (no fee) has been worth the effort. Each time I come in and use it (even if I don't have it on me, they can still look up your account info by using your phone number), I save cold hard cash. On my last visit alone, I saved $2.50 off of two items! For someone who doesn't clip coupons... this is a winning situation.

The check-out area staff are always super friendly but the pharmacy employees leave a bit to be desired. I asked a simple question about what aisle a product was in and the lady acted like I was asking her for money?!

Not my favorite of bridges. Navigating around it can be very difficult. If you miss the wrong turn you'll get stuck going over the bridge when you don't have to. There's not much signs to display where you're headed.  
The bridge is clean and well maintained. Besides the signage problem it's ok. Don't walk over IT!

Enjoy your ride!

*please vote below if you enjoyed reading*

Fusion and small/large plate trends combine to produce a mediocre result.  There were a few highlights including a delicious calamari salad, but there were more misses than hits including a Korean fried chicken sandwich in which the overly breaded and generous chicken pieces were completely dried out.  The shrimp dumplings were also a disaster, offering four small dumplings with so little filling they tasted like plain dough swimming in a sauce.  The short-rib filled steamed buns were a reasonable take on the original though they were, like the originals, too doughy.  (That was OUR mistake).  In sum, there were some interesting flavors ruined by some poor preparations.

Let's hope the entire small plate shtick runs its course soon.  It won't, of course, because it is so profitable, but it isn't generally a satisfying way to order...or eat!!!

Customer service at this location is VERY different from the Seminole Heights location. My husband and I ordered some beers and when we asked for some chilled glasses (which were sitting visible in the fridge) we were asked to drink out of the can because they were closing in an hour and didn't want to give out any more glasses! So because you're lazy (girl with dark hair in braids) we have to drink sub par beer? No thanks, we won't be back to this or any other location. Go to King State y'all...you can get better beer and better service there any day of the week!

I noticed that this restaurant opened up fairly recently near my jobsite. After several coworkers recommend the place I decided to check the place out.

First off the customer service, the lady behind the counter was extremely friendly. She was very helpful and attentive.Also the speed of the service was fairly quick.

The food itself was pretty good. It's your typical comfort food. The first time I went I had stewed chicken and it was fantastic! The sides I had were dirty rice and mustard greens,Those were also good. The next time I went I had hamburger steak with mash potatoes and gravy. Also I had a stuffed bell pepper. I ate every last morsel of that plate.

Now down to the nitty gritty details. This place is more geared for take out instead of dine in. They do have a few picnic tables just in case you want to eat there. This place has a few video poker machines in case you've been bitten by the gambling bug. Still I think the best aspect of this new business besides the food is the price! I was going to a place called "Charlie's Restaurant" just a few blocks from where I work. But after I tried the food here and paid less I decided that I want food from Stackers instead.

In short if you are on Belle Chasse hwy and you want to get some cheap, tasty food then check this place out!

Great stay!! Couples trip to party New Orleans style. We booked three rooms (I booked all three rooms at the same time, reserving under one credit card), I was baffled as to why we were spread out all over the hotel. Anyway, that wasn't a biggie. Check in was smooth with a very direct young woman. She had a check in and move along type attitude, but that's better than being flat out rude I suppose. Room was great, clean, and spacious. Decent breakfast, better than most places that offer free breakfast. Parking was expensive at $30.00 per night. Walking distance to French Quarter, casino just across the street. We never took the car out, walked everywhere we wanted to go. I have stayed at Royal Sonesta and Hotel Monteleone, I would chose this hotel over both of them due to room size and comfort. Check out was a breeze with no unexpected expenses added. I will certainly stay here again!

This place is outstanding! The building is clean, well decorated, and top notch amenities. I spent 5 nights here for a business conference and thoroughly enjoyed my experience. The staff are very nice, friendly, and helpful.

I agree with the review below! If you are plant based and refrain from the meat + cheese, you still get charged extra for guacamole and charged the same price as if you have all of the animal products in your meal. I feel if I don't get cheese or sour cream or meat, guac should be at least included for free-I am eating less. The black beans and especially the Sofritas are always old and crusty looking, or they are out completely and I have to wait for them to cook. Customer service was blah. Workers were bickering about "where they put the tofu."
Def a bigger Flame Broiler fan after this visit.

Best dog day care near Carmel.

Been taking our Newfoundland here for about a couple of years now. They love him, he loves it there, he is able to play and he doesn't get sick. We drop him off there almost every workday. They are always very flexible for us and easily the best value for the service.

Food was good tasting, portions felt small -especially side dishes. I guess they are trying to do gourmet comfort food, but something didn't mesh. It was sorta family style served, but we felt bad taking more than a tablespoon of any dish because there wouldn't be enough to share. Not sure what audience they are going for.
Very professional service technicians and customer service reps. I have been a member of their HVAC service club for many years. I know my furnace and a/c will be properly maintained twice a year.

2.5 stars.  Only went there once, but I don't feel compelled to go back.  Sushi was ok, but lacked in presentation and the frestness was hit or miss.  More expensive than better places around Nashville.

Tried to negotiate with these folks and was told

 "If you want to pay 'x' an hour for a 3 man crew im sure there are some guys you can find on craigslist." ...'There is no negotiations we are not a used car dealership. Please feel free to spend your money where you choose.
"

He could have politely said "sorry that is our rate and we would love to show you the value you will get in a perfect move"  But apparently that's their business model, take it or leave it.. guess they don't need the business, nor do they understand the basics of customer service.

Just completed my scuba certification with Rock Bottom Divers, had a great experience. I was a novice walking into the shop and felt very comfortable and informed every step of the way, from buying and fitting gear to completing my last dive. Sean the instructor for my class was great to work with, always aware of what was going on and acted calmly and accordingly in every situation. Scott the owner was very accommodating as well. He let my friend who was visiting from out of town borrow his own personal face-mask to join one of our dives. I felt a love for diving from everyone in the store. I would suggest anybody interested in diving visit this shop.

Charbroiled oysters!!! Best I had in town. Crawfish spring rolls were amazing as well, bartender (dont remember her name) was super cool. We had an allergy and she was great about helping us out with that. This place is a must when I go back.
My go to Chinese place when at home.  Favorites are the steamed dumplings, Chinese pizza, and curry chicken.  All the regulars such as general Taos are good as well

This place is a total joke they are not in the business of helping people they told me that I should come in with five her dollars down and then there were going to be able to get me into a car then a couple days later they quit talking to me and I kept texting and trying to call them to find out what was going on with my application then we finally got a hold of me after someone else trying to run my application instead of the person who initially started my application come to find out the finance department wants me to put $5000 down for a car that they're going to put me in debt an extra $15,000. Who in their right mind it's been $5000 and give it to a car dealership to get into a car and still be in that almost 20 grand that's to have to make payments for the next for five years instead of just using the $5000 to buy yourself a car I have the title to go along with it I don't think the stupid car dealerships know how to get business especially from people who really need a car why would you asked to put $5000 for a car that's idiotic and I would not recommend this car dealer ship to the devil himself.
Best buffet. Lots of yummy dishes. I was impressed immediately because not only did it looks great it tasted great too. I love the gelato.
This place is the bomb! Excellent food. We had Mike as our waiter and he was great. Tempted us enough to want to come back for some sweets!
Knowledgeable staff and lots of variety of drinks and bakery items. Almond croissant and salted caramel latte was delicious.

Waited an hour for a 12", $16 pepperoni pizza and the restaurant was less than half full, didn't seem like a backed up kitchen, just a slow establishment. 

The pizza crust was so hard and rough that it tore up the top of my mouth. 

Not great pizza, not great service, not great prices. Wouldn't recommend this place.

Very happy with my meal. The dogs were good and fresh, the fries were very good, the place was clean, the staff was super friendly. I had a lot of questions, because that's my nature, and the staff was very informative and good natured.
Vinny is the best bartender ever! Love him. Really great food too! Great place to visit when you come to nola!

We had the best time at Top Notch. My family had been dealing with some difficult times and really needed to do something physical . Top Notch was the perfect way to accomplish this . We all had a blast and it felt very cathartic for all of us . None of us had any experience and the staff was very helpful. By the end of the evening we had all hit bullseyes and all of us felt better! Thank you for a great evening!

I struggled between 1-2 stars. First mistake for me was ordering buffalo cauliflower not wings. This is a dish I typically love. This was not good at all. Barely tossed in sauce and not even hot on the inside. 

The rest of the fam ordered wings and gave 3 stars. 

We struggled with service the entire meal. No drink refills, never received carrots & celery ordered, and then waited for our bill. 

We've visited several times and this was just not good. My husband loves their wings so we will be back for another try.

I hate to do this but I have to downgrade this restaurant quite significantly after my last two visits in the hope they will take notice and improve again. This used to be one of my favorite Mexican Restaurants but the last two visits have not been good at all. Yesterday my wife and I went for lunch. She ordered Fajitas and I ordered a Chicken Taco Salad. Her fajitas were not sizzling at all when they arrived and in fact were only lukewarm. On top of that the onions were barely cooked and hard to digest. My Taco Salad was not much better, there was pork mixed with the chicken which is not a problem for me but you simply don't do that. Overall it was quite tasteless and dull. The visit before that was slightly better as the food was at least hot but not the standard we had come to expect.

On both visits we had to wait quite a long time for someone to take our orders and they were not that busy on either occasion.
Wait line never takes long. I've dealt with all staff and everyone is always quick and helpful.

Luke was a pleasant enough place, but not nearly as nice as it believes itself to be.

We visited for lunch on a Saturday, and the food was fine. My steak was a perfect medium, which was odd because I ordered it medium rare. The music was so loud that the waiter misheard us several times. A restaurant pretentious enough to have half of its menu in French should probably have more  discernment than to blast 80s pop at a volume that barely allows for conversation.

The tables were small and crowded, the food overpriced, and the wait staff unskilled. In a city filled with excellent food choices, I definitely will be looking elsewhere for a pleasant meal.

I had an excellent experience tonight. The vegan tacos are very tasty, albeit spicy. However if you remove some of the red sauce they are just right (warning the dipping sauce is habanero, and taste like fire).  The French fries were again phenomenal. The portion of marinated mushrooms was larger this time and just as yummy as the first time. They have a rich garlic flavor that I love. My friend got the Fondu with pretzel bites and raved about it. The Smokey cheese was excellent.  I also got the cauliflower trio and enjoyed the various textures. She tried two of their dessert tarts and said they were delicious.  I had the vegan cake, which was the perfect way to end the night.

Edited to add: three months later I came back here just for cake. I had been at dinner somewhere "vegan friendly" that didn't offer dessert. I spent the night watching my besty enjoy her dessert, while I sat across the table drinking water. I'm so tired of going out to eat, and leaving with no dessert. Vegans like cake too!!!  I'm grateful that Zeppelin had a vegan cake on the menu. I drove all the way here from down town just to order a slice of cake. It made me so happy.

The restaurant has upstairs seating and downstairs seating. We made the mistake of asking to sit upstairs and there were only huge groups who were SO SO loud. It kind of killed the experience. The acoustics up there are not good, so it was so loud you couldn't hear the person next to you. I had the Fleur De Lis omelette and it was good! The grits and the hash browns were yummy, crawfish was good! Next time I'd get the seafood Benedict but this was filling without being too heavy, and I shared it with another person in our party. I'd recommend but also highly suggest you sit downstairs - you can people watch and the sound won't be so oppressive.

Perfect buttercream on perfect cupcakes with delicious rotating flavors. Best brownie -- chewy without need to underbake. Excellent mini pineapple upside down cake.  Hard not to buy too much.  South Street was aching for a great dessert spot.

Great job transferring both audio and video. Everything was meticulously tracked via bar code. Items were ready when promised.   Your VHS tapes and audio reels are disintegrating so even though it is a financial investment, it is worth it. My project  was small enough for a USB drive but for a larger project, you can provide your own external hard drive (or they will sell you one).  And when there was something he couldn't do, he referred me to a place downtown that took care of me.

Absolutely terrible take out ! Not worth it. Food is terrible. 
Nachos mostly had corn. Barely any cheese or pico de gallo. Never sent spoons for soup. At a hotel with no room service so couldn't have the soup- nothing to stir the soup.  Worst Mexican ever.

Fantastic! You can sit down in the spot w/food and a beer, but I'm a wine woman, so I ordered takeout via Yelp. The Garlic Gobi was divine. It's cauliflower wrapped in corn flour with garlic, ginger, and some other herbs. Freaking fantastic. I ordered it mild, and it still burned, but I'm a spicy whimp anyway. This is one of my go to spots now anytime I'm in town.

More like bad fortune  chinese restaurant.
Dumplings were mushy and straight out of the freezer of the asian grocery on washington ave. 35 dollar order and only one fortune cookie. They botched my order..  The low men and beef with broccoli tasted likethey were stale. Never again!

The staff is so friendly and recommended incredible dishes. I had the breakfast sandwich with fruit. The croissant was so flakey and delicious. The fruit was fresh and the potatoes were amazing. The pecan coffee is incredible and bottomless. A friend had the salmon cakes and those were great too. Everything I tried, I loved! 

The wait was long, but worth it!!
Great food! Terrible service. This is a place you have to know when going in your food will be amazing but expect to be treated like dirt. It's been that way for years. No hope for it now.

I went for lunch today. Not very busy the waitress was slow and not attentive. Once our order was taken we never saw the waitress again. She never checked on us during the meal and only came by once we were done to give us our check. 

Food was cold my filet slider we're very small had zero bbq sauce on it, the onion ring wasn't an onion ring it was a green bean. My slider bun was soggy, and my fries were ice cold when my food came out. I would have asked for new fries, but never saw my waitress, to let her know. 

Very disappointed to spend $40.00 for lunch and having subpar food.

Great happy hour and staff is very accommodating for a party of 6 during that time without a reservation. 
Happy hour specials were great to get a few and share with the table. 
For entree I got a medium rare steak and it was okay, honestly a little bland. The sides were great though!
Very authentic tasty. Food is very fresh. 3 different burrito sizes to choose from. Will def be back

I wanted to write and tell you all that this wine tour was the highlight of our trip to Santa Barbara. We enjoyed Shawn's (the owner/guide) humor, local knowledge and professionalism throughout the tour. I would highly recommend this tour. well worth the price!!

We stopped in for an early Sunday breakfast and had a delicious meal.  My kids enjoyed the chocolate chip pancake and the French toast.  My husband had the Boudin omelette and a bloody mary; I had the seafood Benedict and a bloody mary as well.  Everything was tasty and well prepared.  Our waiter was a generous soul and brought me an extra cup of Hollandaise (it's like he knew it was my favorite!)  They forgot my husband's biscuit, and our table was a bit wet when we sat down, but otherwise it was a wonderful meal and I would highly recommend it!

I bought both my church dress and party dress at Truly Forever. The service and prices were outstanding. Their wide selection helped me find my 2 dream dresses. I cannot wait to wear them on my big day. Thank you for being a part of the memories!

Super cute, local wine bar in Ferguson. There are definitely 'regulars' there but everyone who comes in feels welcomed. It is a small plates place. Everything I have tried on the menu has been good. Obviously the wine selection is huge. Definitely a cute 1st date night or 2nd or 8th. But also still works to just meet friends for a drink.

I thought I'd try McAlister's. I had never been there before and was driving by. Yikes! First, I waited 10 minutes to order. Then I waited 40, yes, 40 minutes to get my order. And I wasn't the only one. Several of us had to wait that long, and we expressed our displeasure to the deli staff. The extraordinary wait certainly doesn't encourage me to return. I should note that I liked my sandwich, but my daughter's wrap didn't come with the promised Caesars dressing. I don't think I've received such poor service at a fast casual restaurant since I lived in Hugo Chavez's Venezuela!

I decided to update my review after an unpleasant experience at this gym.  Here's the gist of what happened. I purchased 10 personal training sessions before they had this new "Thrive" program. I liked my trainer and was seeing results from our 1-on-1 sessions. Out of the blue, my trainer either quit or was fired. (There seems to be a lot of turnover here, not sure why). But back to the story...when I tried to schedule sessions with a new trainer because I hadn't used all of my sessions, I was told that ALL of my sessions were used, which is a total lie. I was owed for 4 sessions, and the gym only made up for 2 of them. They should have refunded my money, but they didn't. They basically said that it was what it was and that was how it was going to be. I really don't like this gym, but I continue to go because I enjoy the WeFit classes, and because it's close to my office. I'm currently searching around for a new gym to call home because this one just isn't cutting it.
Great breakfast and lunch. Use door dash and everything so far has been fantastic. Both breakfast and lunch Bach made as requested. No issues with the food

I've been coming here for like 10 years...it used to be a small salon and now it's extended 5x as big. 

I have had Beth do my hair for several years now. She is very good, quick. She knows what she's doing and does it and I'm in and out fast. 

The salon is gorgeous!  It is always fancy nancied up in beautiful decor. 

The staff is polite and very professional.  

I feel like I'm in Beverly Hills here...I see Dolly Parton every time I go in! :)

They are a full service Salon and I highly recommend it to everyone, men and women!

The prices are very compatible with any other salon.

Go get your hair done here and feel like a million bucks! It's sooo worth it! You deserve it!

As far as sushi and sashimi go, Izumi is tops. The staff is always super friendly and accommodating. And it's a BYOB, which makes it even better. They almost always have a rock shrimp tempura as a special. The first time I tried this dish, it was graciously comped by the chef because the waitstaff asked us to move tables. Now it the dish a staple, ordered every time I go. It is melt-in-your-mouth good. The tuna sashimi is always incredibly fresh.

The atmosphere is relaxed and casual. I like dining there in the summer when the windows are open and Passyunk Avenue is bustling. Izumi is consistently very good.

Lately, consistently one of the worst Starbucks in the area. Never enough staff and when they are staffed, few baristas seem to have a clue as to what to do. You'll wait 10-12 min minimum for a drink and I've waited as much as 20 minutes.

I lived close by to this place for a month, and visited a few times. As far as sports bars are concerned, this place is a nice and clean enough place to catch a game and beer. The Diablo burger will satisfy your burger craving. However I wish it were spicier. Supposedly turns into some sort of club at night on the weekends, but I never visited during those times.

I am surprise by how much I loved this workout! I've tried boxing/kickboxing before but the other places just weren't doing it right (or so it seems after trying this place out). I bought the amazing groupon deal for 6 classes and a pair of gloves and I'm so glad I did. Although, I could have fallen in love with this place after just one class! I was very happy to find that the instructor took the time to show me all of the moves/punches before the class started (even though we ran into the class start time). Honestly, I needed that refresher and if you're a first timer this will put you at ease!

I loved the intervals, they were perfectly spaced so I wasn't doing the same thing for minutes on end. I also really liked how the intervals built on each other - definitely made it a challenging but fun memory game so your focus is not on how tired your might be, but rather what's next in the combination. I also like how they do body weight exercise intervals but it's not overkill. It's definitely the challenging stuff I avoid, like plank jacks, pushups, etc but they more than welcome modifications because at the end of the day it's your fitness journey.

Only qualm is that the space is pretty tiny - that said, I went to a class with 30+ people in and it didn't feel cramped! It's just weird when they tell you to run two laps and it's the size of a large living room, you know? Definitely a great workout either way and I could see myself buying class packs after my groupon runs out (here's to hoping there's a student deal though)!

This place COULD be amazing. At present, it is not. 

What's good:
* The menu CONCEPT. Great ideas, nice flavor palettes. Farm-to-table: yay.
* The decor CONCEPT. Cool, contemporary.
* The service. Our Robert Downey Jr. look-alike waiter was a doll. :-)
* The wine list. Very nice, albeit small, selection, with some Frenchies in there.

What's not:
* The menu EXECUTION. Grossly overcooked bison burger, grossly undercooked truffle fries. Dry and mealy 4-5 oz. burger, soggy, soft fries. Ugh.
* The decor execution. I have never sat on such uncomfortable chairs. I am not one to suffer for fashion.
* Cleanliness level. The floor under our table was disgusting. There are large area rugs in the restaurant that people drop French fries and food all over, and all the staff does is sweep it up. I cannot imagine how filthy those rugs are. A real turn-off. Also, the housemade ketchup (also meh) bottle was sticky and gross. Menus had stains all over them. Ugh again.
* The name. "Burger Up" conjures red formica tables with molded plastic scoop chairs. Couldn't be a worse or more misrepresentative name.
* The prices. Two burgers and fries, with 4 drinks: $70. Come on.
* The location. This restaurant does not belong in a strip mall. It belongs in E. Nashville or downtown Franklin.

I might give it another try, but they need to get their act together.

This was the most horrible food I have ever eaten at a restaurant.  It had no taste except disgusting.  Paid $25 for a roasted chicken plate and could not even finish it because it was that bad. If they do not change their menu, I'm afraid they will not be in business for much longer. Awful!
CJ's is amazing, great environment and friendly workers. my family just LOVED this place. the food was excellent and everything was just nice. i will definitly be comming back very soon. (:

My experience was interesting, if not particularly good. I'm unsure if it was because we lost a waiter for 20+ minutes (and then several times after that he would get one person's order and run leaving others hanging,) drink orders were forgotten, we had to flag a waiter down at several points, and we got transferred from one waiter to another who said she wasn't our waiter. 

Perhaps my table was just downright confusing, but the experience wasn't great.

The place was busy, seemed understaffed, I had half of my table wanting a waiter throttled and in a grumpy mood, and I was just ok with the pizza I had.

For me, nothing was particularly horrible, but for the friends it seemed I was hearing nonstop complaints including a story of waiting over an hour for a deep dish to have it dropped and destroyed at the table by the waiter. Whether this happened that visit or prior I didn't get, I was at my car for a couple of minutes so might have happened that visit.

I stopped asking for clarification of people's complaints at some point because I was just not having fun...

The pizza was surprisingly better the next day, but that could just have been from getting out of a situation where I felt the table might be flipped if a food order wasn't taken or delivered soon.

So pizza ~ok, service I personally had was ok, service friends had between meh and eek.

This location doesn't seem to have that ONE aisle where all the sale items are. This is something I'm used to from the 19th & Chestnut CVS and it was really helpful. Like all the other CVS stores, the sale items are located at the end of the aisles and are also marked within the aisles for easy spotting. As far as service, there are more young teenagers here than any of the other CVS I've been to. Don't be surprised when you're at the register, there are about 4 of them behind the counter carrying on, as kids tend to do. That doesn't mean these kids are total jerks, they're just young and the ones that have rung me up have been polite and friendly. 

This store is part of a mini strip mall. It is 24 hours, has an ATM inside, as well as pharmacy and 1-hr photo. It has a big parking lot and is next to a 24 hour Dunkin' Donuts. There is also an Acme and Rita's in the area.

The food here is so yummy. Honestly, I've been there about 15 times, and I always order the same exact thing. I usually get rice noodles with the coconut curry sauce, tofu and veggies. There is always so much food with your order, and it is at a good price too. Can't wait to head back soon.

I was only in Philly for a couple days, but was recommended by many to come to this particular restaurant for brunch.
Probably the best restaurant experience I had during my stay in this city! I ordered the Creole Shrimp and Grits while my boyfriend had the Kitchen Sink. HUGE portions and definitely worth the price. Born and raised in the South, I was quite impressed by the grits! They were cooked perfectly! Same with the shrimp as I had a bad experience at another Philly restaurant with their shrimp. I also ordered a salted caramel latte, also very delicious. 
We currently live in NYC, and we felt unimpressed with the rest of the restaurants we went to, but Green Eggs certainly steps up their game. 
Will definitely come back and will recommend it to my friends if they visit Philadelphia.

My husband and I had a reservation at this restaurant at 6 pm on Saturday night. LaScala's came highly recommended by my Sister because of the food and location to local theaters. We were seated promptly and that is when our troubles began. We asked to be moved because the air vent was blowing cold air right on my head. Our waiter didn't seem to take kindly to that, so the manager came over and moved us to another table. After that we watched 4 other tables of customers move because of the same reason. There are air vents around the whole dining room right above where everyone sits, blowing cold air on them. That being said, the situation was quickly resolved. We were at our table for 25 minutes before the waiter came back to take our drink and meal order. No bread, no water, no service. We placed our drink order at 6:30 along with a salad and entree order. A few minutes later we got our drinks and bread was brought to the table. At 7:25 we still did not have our salad or meal and our waiter informed us that our "dinner ticket" had been lost by the kitchen and our meal was never made. I was so furious that I got up and walked out the door. We had tickets to see a show at 8 pm and I was not missing that. That being said, we stopped at a local eatery and got a delicious bowl of soup and continued on our way. I have read several other posts stating concerns about the service. I don't know what's going on here, but it seem's that they do not have enough help. Our waiter seemed flustered from the very beginning and his night was getting worse by the minute. A women who was seated in the dining room  just before us was screaming at the top of her lungs about sitting there, being totally ignored the entire time we were there. She pointed out four tables that were sitting there as long as we were with no service also. Where was the management? It looked like a bunch of young kids running the place. This should have never happened. The manager should have handled this and we should have been compensated. We are going to go back. When we do, I'm going to speak to the manager and let them know what happened. This won't happen again. I won't stand for it a second time. We cannot comment on the food, because we never ate anything in the hour and a half we were there.

If you want a cold cafeteria style breakfast come here. Garbage customer service places like this should shut down and allow better food on bourbon. Very disappointed in every way skip this place for sure. 

If you do eat here wait to tip.

Came back last to have some dinner and of curse the coconut curry was great! But what hit the spot for me last night are those PIZZA dumplings! My friend and I where pretty blown away on how we thought we where actually eating pizza at one point. I love the creative idea. Thank you for a good meal once again.

Very good indian food.  Service was very good. The appetizer sampler was a great start for our party of three.  Had the extra spicy lamb vindaloo and it was delicious. Definitely spicy but i like super spicy food. Wife had the chefs special biryani.  This had savory flavors and was moderately spicy. Daughter had karahi chicken it was not spicy at all.  It was more sweet and still very tasty. There was enough for two people to eat from any one dish plus jasmine rice.  They offer to go boxes which you will need if everyone orders a meal. Had the garlic and the cheese naan.  Prices were reasonable for dinner and service was quick and friendly. I will be back for the lunch buffet.

CID Entertainment is a complete garbage company. They buy up all these tickets and then sell them on Ticketmaster, disguised as ticket master tickets. There is nothing on my tickets that says I bought tickets through this company. They are scam artist. Kelly Clarkston should be ashamed to work with this company. They want MORE money for tickets THEY BOUGHT UP, when the tickets directly on the website are LESS THAN the tickets we bought. It's a TOTAL SCAM JOB COMPANY!!!!! Do not use them for tickets or ANYTHING! It's a joke! All we wanted were BETTER SEATS!!! THEY ARE LISTED ON TICKETMASTER FOR LESS BUT WE ARE STUCK WITH THIS SCAM OF A COMPANY because we UNKNOWINGLY BOUGHT "3rd PARTY TICKETS." NO WHERE, and I mean NO WHERE DOES IT SAY these Tickets are CID tickets.

This place is so popular but it's not the best. The custard is totally fine. I like it well enough. But for a native from the STL I can't for the life of me figure out why this place is the holy Grail of all custard to so many people.

As people who are new to the plant-based diet (and have never felt better), this place gives us back the restaurant experience. When we started this diet we missed going to all kinds of different restaurants and trying new foods because places typically only have limited options for plant based folks. Everything is 100% plant-based here and there are A TON of options, I think you could easily bring non-plant based friends here without complaints. Not to mention, it is owned by extremely kind people who stopped to chat with us and gave us a sample of their homemade "Gouda". We will be back soon!

Great location attached to the Palomar. The service was exceptional for our large group of 16, and the food was delicious. I also appreciate that they have Albariño on the wine menu, which you rarely see. 

My only complaint is with the grilled octopus. What you actually get are pasta noodles with a small bit of octopus on top. Tasty but disappointing since that's not what we were expecting.

Word of advice...if you need to use the restroom, it's on the second floor. Take the stairs. This place may very well have the slowest elevators in the city.

I'm in Nashville for a few days. After a few days of not being home, there is no fridge to grab a little snack. The guys I'm with are into going to all these different clubs. I had to put the breaks on the party when I saw Mike's Ice Cream.

Walking in, it's not giving off an ice cream vibe. It's a dark space and in the back is where the ice cream and coffee (?) is happening. 

A few years back, I was in a Chicago suburb and I found an ice cream shop that used a local dairy to make their ice cream. I was looking for something similar for Mikes Ice Cream. Their website has an apartment rental?? Ok, so Mike is a little quirky. Does he make good ice cream?

Walking up, I see "Blackberry Cornbread". Sold! One scoop cone please.
I grab my ice cream and sit up front. Wow! Mike, you did good. The ice cream is creamy, and the blackberry is dreamy. The corn bread is nice but it didn't allow the ice cream to stay together. A big hunk of ice cream fell (I caught it in my hand) at a piece of corn bread. 

I appreciate the fact that Mr. Mike made an interesting flavor. Total fan of Mike's Ice Cream, if your in town and want to cool off then come to Mike's Ice Cream. They're also serving coffee!

Fake Italian. Inside was very nice, unfortunately the food was not very good. I had linguine with white calm sauce. Pasta was over cooked and very few fresh clams, it was loaded with can hard and dry clams. The meatballs were not homemade but low quality frozen meatballs. Sauce was loaded with sugar. My nephew had sub par Chicken Parm dinner. All atmosphere sub par food. Bill for two was 70.00 with tip. I will not be back

"I was driving home this evening around 7:45, when I heard a nail in my tire. I wasn't sure if Pep Boys was still open, but I swung by really quick to see if they could help me out. Although they had been closed for nearly an hour, Steve was still inside working hard. When I knocked on the door and explained my situation, Steve immediately grabbed some tools and came right out and got the nail out for me!"

Great tacos, quick service - just what you want in a little cantina. It's great that someone decided to run with the idea of splitting this building into half cantina, half sit-down restaurant.

My only issue here is the parking - the lot is small, and given all the other places around this restaurant, street parking can be difficult to find during peak hours.
The Beer Pairing dinners are a great price for all the beer and the very nice 4 course meal you get! We had a great time and will definitely be back.
Racist against silent majority. Tourist trap. Deliberately overcharges for mediocre ice cream. Staff silently hateful. Avoid.

When I want to be magically transported back to Asia for a meal.... this is the place I go to get my fix.

Let me first start off with the location. It's on 38th Street in what appears to have once been an American style diner. The kitchen is visible as you walk in the front door behind a bar with chairs that I've never actually seen anyone sitting at. I'm always escorted to the left of kitchen to sit in a booth. Ambiance is lacking, but you will enjoy looking at the dragon statues and giant jolly buddha at the front door. Honestly, I like the unintentional mish mash of east meets west. 

The menu has great variety. Maybe a little too much variety as it is always hard to decide. In addition to Vietnamese food they also serve traditional Thai dishes such as papaya salad. I will share a few of my menu favorites: 

1. The Vietnamese pancake. It's #36 on the menu... I think. Don't hold me to it, but it's between 32 and 39.  The pancake is more like a crepe but made out of just egg and filled with seafood, meat and veggies. It is served with lettuce, sprouts, shredded carrot and basil. I recommend ordering some rice wraps to stuff with this pancake goodness and drizzle on some of the sauce that comes with it. 

2. The bahn mi thit. Basically this is pork sandwich, Asian style. It comes on a French baguette (Vietnamese food is very influenced by the French. For more on this check out :
http://theculturetrip.com/asia/vietnam/articles/b-nh-to-baguettes-french-influences-on-vietnamese-cuisine/). Don't let the veggies that come loaded on this sandwich fool you: It's delicious.

3. The Pho. I don't care which one you pick, it's delish. For me I stick to the Pho Thai because I really like rare beef. I have yet to finish the entire bowl. If you do want to finish it don't plan on ordering anything else. (P.S. Some of the dishes they use to serve the food with  are very miss matched. I keep getting my pho in a 'Let it Snow' bowl. It's a  fun little game to see which bowl I end up with.)

4. The taro bubble tea. Yes, it's made with a root vegetable, but it's quite tasty in desserts. Plus it has a fun purple color. 

In the year I've been a patron of Saigon I have not had a single unfavorable service experience. Food is served quickly, and the staff is friendly. 

No complaints from this Yelper! Saigon is the real deal on the West side.

As another reviewer noted, this business has changed hands several times, as well as locations.  The original owners opened it under the name "Taj Mahal" in the industrial area on Glendale.  They moved it to the space on S. Virginia now occupied by Thai Chili (next to the XXX theater). 

Some time later, new owners took over, changed the name to S.S. Super, and the quality of the food took a decided downturn.  This short-lived period ended when the longest-running owners bought the place, kept the name, and dramatically changed the food quality for the better, as well as installing an excellent lunch buffet.

A few years later, that third set of owners moved to the current location on Moana, changed the name to "Taste of India", and continued to provide excellent food & service.  The ambiance consisted of gaudy-yet-fun Indian wall hangings and Indian pop music on the house stereo.  The owner/hostess always greeted you as though you were a long lost relative, i.e., "How are you my dear? So good to see you again."  My wife and I LOVED that restaurant, and although we tested out the other Indian offerings in town, we always came back to Taste of India.

Recently we went for lunch at our old favorite, only to find that it has changed hands yet again, along with a name change to "Taste of Kabob & Curry".  I'm not sure, but perhaps the owners are the same that operate "India Kabob & Curry" near downtown on S. Virginia.  Regardless, things have changed at our old favorite spot.  Gone are the decorations (there is nothing on the walls, and certainly nothing that distinguishes the place from any other strip-mall business), gone is the exceptionally good service, and gone is the outstanding food.

To be fair, the food wasn't bad.
