Service is the "here, catch" variety. And as is common in Vietnamese joints, we were only halfway done with the appetizer when the main arrived

I'm an avid Chinese go-er - this place is pretty good, the staff is very friendly, place is clean, and the food is fresh!  I had the General Tso's which was VERY (big emphasis on very) spicy, my boyfriend had the Empress Chicken which was doused in the sweet n' sour sauce it looked like.  Not his favorite.. but overall it was good and I only gave it a 4 because I love spicy food but I can't tell you how much my tongue still hurts because it was so spicy lol

FYI This is not your hole in the wall Chinese food.. I'd compare it to Panda Express

We loved the entire experience here and yes it really was wonderful. The Mediterranean breakfast was enough for us to share and the Bloody Mary was perfection in a glass. A nice get away (even for a local) to one of the best beach towns in the world.
Came here with the fam for lunch. Kids loved the decor and how speedy the waitresses went around on roller skates. The food and service were great - a very fun place to eat!!

I went here on Sunday 1/25 with my wife prior to heading back to new york.   It was a great stop and a place I've heard mixed reviews about.   One friend said it was great, better then outback and another said it was terrible.   I found it somewhere in between and on par with outback.

We walked in and on the left is a barrel of peanuts.   Feel free to eat some and throw them on the floor!   Next they seat you but on the way to be seated they show you steaks in the case and you can pick yours for dinner!   I was happy i love steak.

Next we sit down and order a sirloin and a rib eye, both with salads and sweet potatoes loaded.   We received our steaks and they were both done to our liking!  It was perfect.   The potatoes had marshmallows and caramel sauce on it and they were also amazing.   Another plus to add on the meal where the freshly backed bread with the cinnamon sugar.   Amazing rolls :)

Overall the service was outstanding, I didn't have to ask for or wait for anything.   It was fast as soon as we were finished our salads dinner was here.   Steaks were very good, mine (the rib eye) was particularly flavorful and well done.   

On the way out the manager asked us how everything was and I said I had a great time and it was our first time here.   They gave us a present!   They gave me a bottle of their sauce to take home!  It was a great treat.   I'll definitely go back here.

I love this place.  The salon itself - it's full of interesting and amazing art pieces.  Nothing in here is purely functional, it's all decorative in some way or another.  Get a lollipop on the way in and totally go to get your hair done by Mae.  I have only ever gone to her, so I can't comment on any of the other stylists there, but I can definitely say that Mae is great.  She was recommended to me by a friend who always has the best hairstyles and I"m so glad that I started going to AMMO.  Not only is Mae a great stylist, she also is a cool and relaxed person and is easy to talk to.  My hair always looks perfect when I get out but then it also looks good when I style it myself at home. The cuts grow out really stlyishly too.  The prices seem in line with other similar salons in Philadelphia, maybe even slightly cheaper.  If I were to choose one negative about the salon, it's that sometimes it's difficult to get an appointment and I have to book well in advance, but that's probably because she is so popular and in demand.
Wow, delicious food.  Sophisticated presentations and plates, yet still very accessible and low key setting.  The trout is amazing as well as the prime rib.  Service was excellent.

My aunt selected this place and she's from the area, but, otherwise, I probably would not have ever tried this restaurant. Honestly, that wouldn't have been a tremendous loss because the food was okay at best for Cuban food, the interior was dirty (especially the bathrooms--so gross), and the service was awful. We ordered a variety of different things: the plantain chips were pretty good, the chicken chicharones were also good, the fried rice and sweet plantains were also good. None of which could be labelled as the best I've ever had though. The steak was really dry and cold by the time I received it. My brother got his sandwich well before (like 20 minutes before) any of us got our food. By the time we got out food, he was already finished--and my food was still cold when I got it. Also, the server was really rude. She kept forgetting about us (a table of 11) and she seemed annoyed whenever we asked for little things an extra plate or another set of utensils. On top of everything, they dropped a plate of food on my cousin, completely forgot our reservation, and took forever to have us seated. I honestly would not recommend this restaurant by any means. The only reason why it got two stars instead of one is because it's still tolerable Cuban food.

This place was fantastic.  The water play area alone kept my toddler occupied for a good long while, and frankly he probably would have been content there for the rest of the day if not for his two parents wanting to check out other exhibits.

I'm not sure what some of the other reviewers expected out of a children's museum, but yeah, it leans more heavily towards play exhibits. That said, there are plenty of educational opportunities if you're paying attention; you can see how a lock on a canal works, play with morse code, experience optical illusions, and they have the staple "air blowing into a beach ball and the beach ball stays on top of the air" demo.

The downstairs area has a lot of fun play exhibits, like a hospital and a grocery store. There is a train area but honestly, it's kind of boring. There is a pretty cool diorama of historic Philly, but it's probably more fun for the adults than it is for the kids.

Some of the exhibits are a little worn. The big piano (the one the kids step on) is pretty busted - lots of notes don't work, and some keys can't actuate individually; two fire at once. The music rainforest area has a couple broken instruments, and some buttons around the museum just don't work.

I thought the staff was pretty good, and at least they day we went there were staff members supervising the "3 and under" play areas. I actually saw one staff member turn away a 6 year old and his mom. They do allow older children if they have 3 yr old siblings wanting to play there, though.

My only gripe with the place is the price. Same price for adults and kids ($15 as of Sunday), and the charge 1 year olds, which I found a little odd, since most places I go to only start charging at 2 or 3. Throw in the $8 parking and two parents and their 1 year old is over $50. Yes, you can probably find a cheaper way, but at list price, it's just a little bit pricey. Also, tickets for the carousel are separate.

It's a bit far from Pat's or Gino's (which is fine, since real afficianado's will go to Tony Luke's anyway =) but we did end up going to a place called Abner's when we went to visit a friend near Drexel university, which was pretty decent.

Anyway, great rainy day or cold winter's day activity, with lots to do for the little ones (it does seem a little boring for the kids over 7 or so; lots of "pretend" play type stuff). But remember that 1 year olds need a ticket, and parking isn't free.
Ordered the crispy avocado club sandwich and the signature smash fries with rosemary. Delicious. First my fries were cold but they bought me a new batch. Everything was fresh hot and delicious.

Really good, fresh food that arrived fast!  The bruschetta looked amazing and would've been probably one of the best I have ever tasted if it was dressed with the balsamic vinaigrette as promised-- imagine it was still good, though!  Lots of prosciutto and tasty bread with fresh spring mix// can't wait to order again (with a side of balsamic!)

Also had lasagna, which was traditional with a sweet sauce and lots of cheese!  Served with spring mix salad and some tummy garlic cheese bread - definitely a keeper!

Just upped to five stars... Tried the chicken Alfredo and it was delicious...creamy, seasoned well and the chicken was amazing!  So impressed and blessed to have yet another incredible delivery option!

After reading reviews on yelp I had been wanting to try this place.  However, when I realized they were the ones that replaced Riddles, it was VERY hard for me to walk in the door.  Oh Riddles, how I miss you so! (and your veggie plate!).  

We walked in and the place was packed.  It was during one of the world series games, so not only was it packed but it was crazy!  They immediately got us seated though.  I was shocked and pleasantly surprised!  The service was great, I really enjoyed the dark & cozy atmosphere, and the food was great too! 

There were so many interesting items on the menu I'd love to try but for some reason it just felt like a burger night.  I ordered the All American with regular fries and a house salad.  I enjoyed it all!  

I can't wait to take my husband back and try a wide variety of the menu!

Friendly Staff and good vet care but absurdly high prices for standard procedures, not to mention inconsistent price quotes. I called two weeks prior to ask what the cost of a microchip would be for my cat that they have the records for but was never seen. I was told $51 for the initial visit because she was never seen before. While the initial visit fee I understand, the price for micro-chipping is outrageous and honestly downright insulting especially considering the SPCA microchips for $35 and a discounted rate of $25 on certain days. You would think as a local vet, they would make microchipping affordable or at least reasonable as to encourage it with pet owners. 

I had an unrelated appt for my cat this past week and I was happy with the service but when I called back a few days later to make an appt for microchipping, figuring I'll just suck it up and pay the $67 out of convenience, despite my principles.

I was inititally told $51 + $67 but when I explained she was just recently seen, the receptionist (who was polite) told me oh ok, no problem, we can make that a vet tech appt then and it will be $87. $87?! For a micro-chip?! That's insanity and I do not appreciate the price gouging. I would like to stay here because the facility is nice and the staff seems knowledgeable and it is local but if this is what they overcharge for minor procedures, then I don't want to even know what they gouge people for on more serious procedures. Unfortunate but probably time to find a more affordable vet option.

I have been to Soak twice. After my initial visit, I decided to give them a second chance. I am sorry to say that both experiences were horrible. I received the same service that others have described - hurried, unappreciative of my business, rude, novice, etc. I think the worst part is that both times my pedicures were just bad. How hard is it to paint toes? Each time I ended up with polish all over the tops and sides of my toes. When I asked for a "clean up" my technician dipped a paint brush in remover and wiped it around my toes. The result was skin stained red. Really, it was laughable, except that it cost so much. I really think they hire girls right out of beauty school. I got a better pedicure at Walmart! I also had a wonderful pedicure at Atlantis for nearly the same price. Just read the reviews before you visit this establishment. They have multiple 1-star ratings for a reason.
They left their Yorkie tied to a tree in 30 degree weather then laughed when I told her that wasn't ok. Never use this place.

I love the folks at Sleepy Hollow.  I feel 100% comfortable leaving the dogs there when I'm out of town.

They noticed that my boy dog was very stressed and was taking it out on the female, so they separated the two.

I love that they keep detailed log of how much they eat, if they are drinking, going to the bathroom, etc.  It makes me more secure that someone is really looking after them.

The prices are really reasonable too.  $16 a day per dog plus $4 if you want an optional play time/walk.

I will definitely use Sleepy Hollow again.

Only having been here after work I will say I enjoyed myself. $2 Tecate really hit the spot after a long day. I like how small the bar is and the great wall art. I hear they have live music on the weekends but watch out.... it gets crowded. My vote is....... I will go back for cheap beer and to complain about work!

Great care,  nice staff. Our second year to leave Sophia for Hot August Nights 
We will return next year

Pig. Heaven. 

We decided to have a BBQ for my friends 30th birthday, but we didn't want it to be just any old BBQ, which is why we decided to get a magnificent 60lb boneless roasted pig from Esposito's! 

The piggy completely surpassed expectations. It was perfectly cooked - the skin was golden and crispy, the meat was juicy and tender and the pig was filled with herbs and flavorful roasted garlic. But the BEST part was the huge jug (must have been 3-4 gallons) of PIG JUS. I honestly just dunked my entire sandwich in the jus - it was delightful. 

This was my first experience Esposito's, but it definitely won't be my last!

Came here during spring break trip after a day of traveling and it was wonderful!  Quiet, relaxing atmosphere. Staff is professional and discreet.  I had 2 teen girls with me and we walked in taking a chance we could be seen. They were very accommodating and we were able to be side by side while getting our massages.  

The massage started with the scalp/neck and moved to the feet. The massage was moderate to deep pressure and was just the right amount of pressure.  I elected for a chair massage and it was perfect to end our visit.  Would definitely come for another visit!

If you are looking for good quality meat, cheese, deli, veggies, fruit and bakery items...THIS is the place.  Prices are good.  The store is clean and the employees are friendly.  I LOVE shopping here.  Also the organic ice cream is delish.

Went with my cousin and her two kids and we ordered the chicken banh mi, chicken pho, and 2 rice platters. The banh mi tasted fresh, the pho had a rich flavorful broth, and the kids devoured the rice platters (and they are extremely picky eaters). All in all, we had a great meal and finished it off with their vietnamese iced coffee which was nicely balanced, neither too sweet or too bitter. I will definitely come again the next time I'm in Philly!
Friendly, welcoming, and of course great food!!!

I've always been very pleased with this location.  The workers are friendly and it's close to where I live.  It's pretty small, and sometimes there can be a really long line, but in my experience it usually goes pretty quickly.   On the bright side, one entire wall is filled with headshots for musicians who made it (and probably some who didn't quite get there) that are signed, so at least there's something fun to look at.  They've also got an automated package center where you can send your mail using the machine if you are in a hurry and don't want to wait for the counter service. 

Also take care of passports at this location.

We went to Branzinos as part of Center City restaurant week. It was fantastic. There are three different dining rooms that I could see, though we sat at the table in the front right by the window. This place is BYOB and they have wine holders available to keep your wine chilled. 

I had the crab ravioli as an appetizer, which had a lemon zest kick to it. It was a cold ravioli which was new to me but not bad. The sirloin however, this is where I was won over. It was a lean and healthy cut of meat, cooked to medium rare perfection. The fingerling potatoes were just as fantastic. 

Overall, if you're looking for a nice dinner in the Rittenhouse area, definitely give this place a look!

Terrible. Pho beef broth has no flavor. Very little beef and 3-4 VERY thin slices of tendon. Condiment, bean sprout is not fresh. The old lady server, may be the owner has an attitude. A hot tea pot for 3 is $4.50. Worst Vietnamese dining experience ever.

I tried this place out because I had heard they had 'authentic' Fish & Chips, which is a dish I had fallen in love with in Portsmouth, England while in the Navy, so that's what I had.  Was it good?  Yeah, it was decent.  Was it authentic?  No, not even close!  I'm not sure what fish they used, but it didn't taste like Haddock or North Atlantic Cod (which is what traditional Fish & Chips is made with).  The batter was too heavy and the "chips" (fries) were seasoned fries, which I found a bit odd, as that is not too "authentic".  Since this place touts itself as a traditional "pub" I thought they would have a side dish of mushy peas, but no, they had cole slaw.

The decor is okay, with an "Irish Flair" that seems to be a bit overdone in some cases, particularly the uniform the waitress wore, making her look more like a schoolgirl, not "Irish".  The place was very clean though, so that was nice.  

The service was pretty fast but then again, the place was roughly 99% empty, and the server (Angie) was very polite and seemed a lovely young lady, no complaints there.  There were several people at the bar, and only one other table, but she handled everything nicely and seemed fairly knowledgeable on the menu.  

Decor:  Okay

Cleanliness:  Seemed VERY clean

Service:  Excellent

Food:  Decent

Went for the brunch and food just Ok not worth the 44 dollars. I also expected more I guess. I hear it was better when you got to select your main course and the salads and sides were the buffet part. Oh well.

It's everything you want a last minute craving stop to be. Delicious sandwiches - I had a special and he had this delicious coconut marinated chicken? Tons of outdoor seating and hipster beards, but you get good food and reasonable prices out of the deal as well. Which was pretty unexpected for something hyped with 1000 yelp reviews.
Excellent service. Sales guy was very patient and kind. Lovin' my new bag! Can't wait to go back.

Great gastropub experience!  Make sure to get the Kennet Square Mussels. They're out of this world. 

Really reasonable prices for the quality you get. And hats off to our server, Zamika. She's the best!!
I have been here multiple times and love it.

I'm giving this 2 stars because my massage was great. I made an appointment for a deep tissue massage but when I paid apparently I got an aromatherapy massage. Regardless of how weird that was, it was a good message. My facial on the other hand was awful. I specifically asked the aesthetician if she did extractions for milias and she said yes- after an hour of just what get like getting my face washed and what I figured were extractions she told me she got some on my right cheek- the rest weren't ready and it's illegal in Pa to remove milia? So basically she picked at my skin and got nothing and left marks? Also the legal thing That's not true at all, my normal place does it and if it were illegal I'm positive they wouldn't advertise it. I told her I get welts, who doesn't know not to try and pop a welt? It stung and I said something but I she was nice enough so I just left. Waiting for someone to call me, I can't believe I paid for that but I also wasn't going to say something in a room w 3 people.

This is a great place for breakfast.  Generous portions, delightfully friendly service and excellent food.  We had a special dietary need in our group and they worked with her to figure out an option that worked.  We'll definitely be back.

Went here for the first time a couple weeks ago after being at the farmers market. Ordered the fish sandwich and it was rubbery, dry and overcooked. The fries were really good however. My partner got the breakfast poutine and wasn't really impressed.The waitress was a doll! very friendly , knowledgeable about the menu and the specials and was very attentive. I have experienced better food. Sadly, won't be back.

We have visited this store every night but one during our family vacation. Each time we walk through the doors the staff are extra friendly and let us sample various flavors before making a decision. Even if they're super busy! Their ice cream is all made in store and simply has cream, milk and sugar. No nasty syrups or artificial flavors! If you're in the area I would highly recommend stopping by for a waffle cone (or two, or three...)

I went to see Merissa and this is the best haircut I have received in a LONG time! She was very professional, friendly, and starts off the haircut with a shampoo and warm towel around the face. They offer water, soda or beer when you first get there. The barber shop itself is large, bright and upscale. 

Highly recommended and I will definitely be going back!

Being a food monster, I have to rate this place more heavily for food than for drinks. I will say, so as to start with something positive, that these guys know how to make a decent drink. I've had a great manhattan here and my wife typically loves their champagne cocktail. However, with even a decent mixing guide, it's hard to screw up a cocktail if you use quality (not top shelf, but qualtity) ingredients. I also think it's cool that they have bourbon and scotch tasting phlights. Unfortunately, cocktails are fairly expensive (think Fork, Chandler's).

But... their food freaking stinks! At least the last (and only) time we ate there. I don't remember my wife's meal (probably a salad and probably forgettable), but I had fish tacos and we split some french fries. The fries were totally medicore and reminiscent of some kind of bag o' freezer fries. When they arrived, they were mushy and undercooked and cold. My fish tacos were totally sub-par and, according to my wife, that's a bad sign (because I gobble up anything that someone calls a fish taco). Service was not stellar, even on a slow weekend afternoon.

We won't be returning. There are much better places for fish tacos (10 barrel, Cloud 9) and, if you're going to spend a bit on drinks, there are much nicer places to eat and get an expensive cocktail (Fork).

Koch's is the best, they gave me a cookie in my birthday. It's not a "fast food" place, this is a real deal deli. If you've got the time and want a really great sandwich with top notch ingredients, Koch's is the best place in Philly. Maybe... The world!

This place is the worst Starbucks I have ever been To. The manager Scott work behind the counter like a he knows what he is doing but for all the moving around. The coffee maker has no drinks on it and he is not getting anything done. I have waited several time for up to twenty to twenty five minutes for a single drink. At least once a week my ices coffee is hot. It just not a good place .

Like other reviews said, the exterior of the restaurant looks like a mom and pop Mexican joint, but the inside is much more renovated. There are about 4 tables and some bar stools. The owner was very nice and helpful, and very eager to make our orders vegetarian and make them exactly how we wanted them.

We ordered the nachos which were very good, but could have used some tomatoes/lettuce/fixings. The enchiladas verdes were very tasty as was the vegetable burrito. 

I am very judgmental when it comes to Mexican food as I absolutely love it; and this place delivered a great product AND for cheap. For three people plus non alcoholic drinks we paid $40 including tip.
Would highly recommend this place!
Been coming here since I was a kid. It doesn't change and that's a good thing. Still the most reasonable place in town for a good meal. Cook your own or have them cook you lobster or crab.

Very good inexpensive Cuban food

There are many Cuban places in Tampa but this has been my go to place for years. The food is consistently good as well as the service. 

My favorite dish here is the fried pork chunks (masas de puerco fritas). Try them you'll like them. 

The sandwiches here are good as well. They are a meal all by themselves.

I stayed at this hotel overnight during the end of summer. It was in good condition for the price. There were many guests so it was a bit noisy and social (some were hanging out in the balcony and chatting), but nothing excessive.
The space is very cozy and Sharone made me feel comfortable right away, she is both warm and professional. I would definitely recommend her and return for other services.

Yikes - I will NEVER come back.  A simple carwash took almost an hour and a half.  Not how I wanted to spend my Saturday afternoon.  I was told about 45 minutes...which would have been bearable.  True it's 1pm on a Saturday - but come'on.  They literally have just 1 crew working....and trying to get through seemingly 50 cars here.  Really - 1 freakin crew?  In the bay area I was out in 30 minutes TOPS on the busiest of Saturdays.  Why?  Because there were at least three crews working on a Saturday to accommodate the rush.  Its as if a restaurant had 1 waiter for 100 tables on a Friday night.  I saw cars wait in line - and then turn around and leave because of how long everything was taking.  They had more sense than me. 

And looking around - the employees walked and worked as SLOW as can be.  There was absolutely no hustle at all.  The employees seemed lethargic, sad, and just totally bored and miserable.  I absolutely don't blame the employees here, its just that this place seems TERRIBLY  mismanaged.  

At my old carwash (before I moved), the employees hustled, they had fun, they smiled, they did a great job and they got tipped very well.  

As for the "quality" - it was fine but 100% NOT worth the wait.

When is Local not a good idea?

1. Their beer selection is fantastic. Last night I had the Green Flash Grand Cru and the 90 minute. They were all bangin, MmMMMmMM. 

2. The service is fabulous. Everyone is super friendly and always up for a chat. Even when I first started going there, everyone was very friendly and I didn't need to become a regular to get the same level of service. Everyone knows their beers and recommendations are right on point. 

3. Snow storms are a great time to go and people watch.

This golden corral is like any other I have went to.  They have a variety of foods and switch stuff up on different days.  Nothing special or bad.  It's not 4 or 5 star food so no one should be expecting that.  Not sure why the rating is 2.  The staff was polite and helpful as well.  There was also alot of seating.  It was a Friday evening it was busy so sometimes you had to wait for things to be refilled.  That was understandable.  I'd go back if I was in the mood for GC.
Good food Great prices would have loved if they had a kid's menu but other than that Burger was amazing  Bar area was Great lots of Tv's an pool tables

My wife and I went her for Valentine's day.  Started off with oysters and moved on to the skate for me and cod for her, since the suzuki had run out.  Both were excellently done, with subtle flavors as opposed to an explosion of salt and sugar that you get at some places doing these types of broth dishes.

Even at the end of the night (~10) the service was helpful.  Definitely recommended.

So I decided to take the plunge and treat myself to a Breitling watch. After looking for weeks online at all the gray market sellers of new watches and reading about some of the horror stories about defective watches and other issues I decided to look into a pre owned watch. I came across Govberg and saw the Breitling I have been dreaming about but thought I would never be able to afford. I sent them an email after their regular hours but heard back from them first thing the next morning. Alaina was the sales consultant and she went over all the history of the watch with me, went over pricing, gave me some discount, but I was still very skeptical about buying something like this online.  After lots of pondering I  made the decision, placed the order on Friday afternoon, Alaina sent the watch out fed ex Saturday delivery, received it by noon today and it's beautiful. I want to thank Alaina for all her work and I would recommend Govberg online to anyone looking for a pre owned time piece.

Dined here for restaurant week jan 2015.

Loved everything and booked another dinner that same week.

This restaurant has some of the best bread and butter.  The baguette slices are served warm with amazing french butter.  I can't stand when restaurants give you cold bread!

My meal was great but what made me want to come back immediately was my girlfriends beef bourguignon.  They used short rib and it was melt in your mouth delicious!

Definitely give this place a try!
Always delighted to find vegan food, Charlie ... is a truly delightful find. Funky, hip, BRILLIANT food, and adventurous cocktails make this place simply divine. My current Philly favorite!

I always get great food and drinks here. My server tonight was Gabby and she is now my favorite. As I was dining alone, she didn't feel it necessary to rush me out. I know she makes her mobey by table turnover,  but I was ready to enjoy a nice, leisurely dinner and read. I took only a small table. Gabby made sure to pace my food and drinks perfectly. Kudos!!

Great place to unwind after a busy day. Quickly found seats at the bar. Vibe was interesting.. does not compare to the cigar bar in Manhattan. Waitress was really friendly and helped us pick out cigars. The bartender on the other hand was not so friendly. Not sure what her deal was since we were at the bar ordering a bunch of whiskeys.

Terrific theater with super comfortable seats. Looks deceptively small until you go into the screening rooms. Nice size size but not too big. Sound was perfect. We were there for a private screening recently and the two guys in suits checking tickets looked very Secret Service. I expected to see surveillance mics in their ears. Right before the screening, one of them came in and pretty much threatened the room about turning off electronic devices - going so far as to say if he sees a glow, you will be escorted out. Yikes! But I was glad - last thing I want is to listen to some dickwad talking or texting. 
(Now if they could just eliminate popcorn and noisy candy bags. Heaven.)
Great customer service, professional team, competitive prices. I'd highly recommend 6th Man for your next move.
Amazing sushi! Great portions and delicious!!! Definitely would recommend it to anyone!!!

The experience of the all you can eat meat is a great concept. The service however was awful. I went there to celebrate 2 years with my boyfriend and we were treated like criminals. My boyfriend heard the bussers talking about us and making rude comments in Spanish. They even followed me to the women's room which felt extremely invasive. At the end of the meal they stood above us until I handed them my credit card. There are better places for the same meal up in the Northeast. Never again.

I usually love this place... for drinks  (not food) but tonight I stumbled in my new shoes (they were heals.. I thought I was being cute..) but the chick bartender said to me...order wisely...and so I ordered  nothing... not even there shit  food... later she apologized to my husband saying she shouldn't have been so judgemental... as she couldn't tell if I was drunk or not... 
Go some where else yelpers!!!
The best food I've had in years!!!  Cocktail shrimp, fillet, and seared Tuna.  Perfection!!!!!

For a ramen shop in the middle of Chinatown in Philly? Okay- I'll take it!

I was skeptical at first (coming from NYC with its fair share of popular ramen shops such as Ippudo, Ivan, Momofuku, Totto, etc.) but it's actually decent ramen.. is it comparable to those places I listed? No. But if you're in philly and you want ramen - go here.

I had the pork buns and the tan tan ramen. Pork buns are good, but wasn't outstanding.. maybe the meat was a bit drier. But the tan tan ramen, which is I guess the "spicy miso ramen" version of what I usually eat at ramen shops, was good. Good portion and price point ($10). The topping amount is a bit lacking, didn't have that much toppings as I'm used to with other places in NY. Overall - I'm a fan.

They take credit cards but not AMEX.

Have had this pizza three times, and it keeps getting worse. Chewy, heavy, flavorless, and often undercooked dough, cheap cheese, flavorless sauce, decent toppings, and in spite of all this, nice employees.

Have you ever had a moment when you almost didn't want to write up a yelp review for one reason or another, but then you reflect back on the whole point of yelp - and decide you have to write it.

Hubby and I visited NYC earlier this month for a terrific anniversary trip, and flew Southwest.  There were delays because of fog (not their fault), cancelled flights because of weather delays (not their fault), and we had to sometimes wing it and fly stand by as a result.  All in all, terrific experience, however.

If you've ever met me, you know that I'm a big girl.  Always have been, and I've come to grips with being a large woman.  When hubby and I were in the Nashville airport waiting for news of our yet-again-delayed flight, the desk agent came over and asked me to come talk to her.  She knew that our flight was connecting in Baltimore for LaGuardia, and I thought it was just about those delays and that since ours was the only flight originating in Baltimore.

She very politely explained that Southwest's policy for larger passengers is that if you appear to be likely to encroach at all on the adjacent seat (which, let's face it, a lot of people do with the tiny airline seats), they offer a "Reserve Seat" voucher that you put in the seat next to you so that noone will have an issue sitting next to you.  They factor the reserve seats into the capacity of the plane, and they charge nothing for that.  And then she asked if I would be OK with a reserve seat voucher.
Well, of course I would... 

I realize that some people might read this review and complain saying they pay more for their airline ticket to allow for reserve seats.  To clarify, it was always my intention that I ride next to my husband, and we would thus only encroach on each other.  I paid the $10 Early Bird Check In fee on our tickets so I didn't have to worry about checking in however many hours early (I always forget) and get our boarding passes to allow for such.  I did everything in my power to not inconvenience anyone, so I'm thrilled that Southwest takes it a step beyond.  I don't know what their requirements are to qualify for such, but for once - I'm glad I was "big enough."

When our flights were ending in the cities where we were landing, hubby and I selected seats in the back so that if the flights were full and folks were coming in scoping for seats - they wouldn't have to think less of the big girl with the reserved seat next to her.  About half our flights this trip were full, possibly because of all the fog delays.

I will admit that prior to this trip and my being made aware of this policy, I had anxiety traveling with Southwest because of encroaching and basic uncomfortable-ness on the planes.  We would drive to destinations when that was at all reasonable, but now that I know Southwest goes to this much trouble, we will absolutely fly with them any opportunity that arises.

I did also note that a few other people had special seating needs on some of our flights, a medical issue where the lady needed an aisle seat and a father and young son where Dad had not checked in early and really needed to sit together.  When that arose, it was awesome to see that the flight attendants simply ask for volunteers, and when you give up your initial seat to accommodate a need, they offer you free adult beverages on your flight.  That, folks, is my kind of airline.

One of the best meals I've had in a long time! The staff was so nice and my friend and I had a great time! We didn't even have to wait very long for a table. The waiter overheard my friend say I was only in town for a day and a half (should have stayed longer!) and he ended up bringing us extra fried oysters with our starter salad. The pan fried fish I had with pecan sauce was amazing and I ate way too much of the already large portion. We were too stuffed for dessert so they brought us small pieces of cakes to try anyway. I now understand why this is such a favorite. This is a must, especially for visitors to the big easy.

LOVE THIS PLACE!!! Great neighborhood bar. Wonderful and helpful staff - everyone is informed and knowledgeable about the beers and food offered. The menu is always changing and offers a wonderful selection of delicious food (the chef is a genius!). I highly recommend their Scotch egg and their raw bar. Stop in an see what they have to offer you, you won't be disappointed.

I usually go here if I've had a junky day at work... which means I hadn't been by since the holiday season.

Anyway, I went last night and the phone ahead carryout service is definitely not as good as it used to be...

 I called ahead to place a carryout order and was told there would be a brief hold... Brief hold? I was literally on hold the entire 15ish minute drive to get there and I left my house about 5 - 10 minutes after I dialed the number. 

So I just went to the carryout station and placed my order there and went to the bar (telling the carryout person I'd be over there). It was around 8:30pm at this point

The bar was crowded, I'll give them that, but it still took awhile longer than I would've thought to get a drink -- most people already had drinks. Once I got one in my hand though (my standard cosmo), it was perfectly made and nice and smooth. 

I only had half of my second drink (vodka and cranberry) as I hadn't had anything but 5 Dove Chocolates to eat that day, but they both were made wonderfully.

This worked out for the best as it was right after I got my second drink that my carryout was finished (which should tell you how long it took to get a drink...)

Got home and everything was nicely packaged as always.

---

Note that I have also been here sit-down and so my stars are based on a combination of all experiences.
Great food! Great coffee! I just wish they were open in the morning for coffee.

Great bar. The owners are the nicest people. Went there for lunch and grabbed an amazon veggie burger. Came back the next night and checked out some band that was rocking out. Everyone I talked to in there was super friendly. Great environment
This Target is in a congested location off City Avenue. Essential items are there when needed. Shopping carts seen dumped onto Presidential Boulevard. Clean it up!

I eat a lot of Indian food, which in no way makes me an expert, but it has made me very picky. I love Tiffin in Philadelphia and Coriander in Voorhees, and this place just doesn't measure up to either of them.

And the main reason for it is this: the food is not spicy. The first time we ordered from IndieBlue, we didn't specify a spice level because, in our experience, curries are usually a little spicy even if you don't tell the waiter you want spicy food. Because they're curries. And that's what curries do. They are spicy and warm and delicious.

 But the stuff we got was so unspicy as to actually detract from the appeal of the dish. I don't like my food to cause me physical pain, to turn me beet red, or cause my entire body to sweat -- so don't read this as a review from a disgruntled masochist who was denied some bizarre, food-based pleasure. But in Indian food, I do find that the complexity of the spices and herbs is boosted by a healthy dose of chilies and heat. And this food just didn't have it. It was flat. Edible and decent, but flat.

So we ordered from them again, this time specifying "spicy" dishes. And they still didn't cut it. Spicier, yes, but still pretty mediocre. Part of the problem is that I don't like incredibly rich, creamy/milky sauces, and my mataar paneer was exactly that. And not spicy enough. 

So, if you like Indian food that isn't spicy, go here! I can assure you that you will not encounter anything unpleasant. I'm going elsewhere, where the balance of flavors is more to my liking.

Smile points:
+ flatbreads are spectacularly drool-worthy
+ fantastic sangria
+ excellent service and decor
+ frequent complementary small samples (at least when i've been there)
+ imaginative and innovative flavor combinations
+ great for groups

Frownie face:
- my wallet got real thin afterward
- many of the dishes are overly salted
- I liked the food but wasn't falling out of my seat over it (which I would expect for the price)
- I think (slash know) Jose can do better
We had pizza there tonight. It was very tasty. The place is small but extremely clean. Service was fast. We would visit again.

I found this hotel to be well below what I would expect from any Marriott, especially an AC Hotel. The service was mediocre, but the hotel has obvious signs of not being well maintained. The art in our room had made divots in the wall that were left unrepaired, there was an extremely obvious and nasty stain on the chair in our room, the mattress was like a rock, WiFi router on the ceiling in the hallway was exposed, and doors throughout the hotel were dinged up. This hotel's saving grace is that the lighting throughout is low and it hides much of the poor condition. If that wasn't enough, the video in the elevator was frozen and when we joked with an employee riding the elevator, he mentioned that it had worked for a year or so. On checkout day, there was an employee behind the desk in plain clothes. Certainly not what you would expect when paying $200/night!

I visited this location once a week ago. The experience was OK. The server was pleasant and the food was OK. I visited a second time with some people from work who wanted to try it and this visit decided i would not be eating here again. 
The service was poor and inattentive. The food was very basic. The quality of the food is really no better than some frozen food dishes you could make and in some cases the frozen TV dinner option would be better.
This is unfortunately one of those places that sets the appearance of quality food but lacks the food to back up the image they are selling. 

there are plenty of better places to eat for similar style cuisine near this location.

We came for a quick lunch and had a great time! The lunch deals are were fantastic (an appetizer and a tofu curry with rice for ~$8), and the portions were just enough to fill us up. I ordered a Massaman curry with fried tofu, and my friends ordered the Red Curry with Tofu and the Coconut Soup with chicken. All three dishes were delicious, and rank among the best Thai food I've had! Additionally, the servers were very accommodating of our need to get back to work, and were very prompt with taking orders and giving us our bill.

All in all, a great spot for an affordable, delicious lunch! I will DEFINITELY be back!

Had lunch today. We started off with pork belly (special) Best we ever had.   I had the Salmon bubble box. Daughter had one of the daily specials, it was some kind of oyster seafood roll with an extremely light tempura. My Salmon was just a little dry but from I understand, that is what most customers want. Next time if I get Salmon, I will tell them to "under cook" it 

Great Quality, good prices, excellent service, slightly slow kitchen; and it had people but by no means crowded.

Hawk, our waiter was on top of his game. 

Oh yeah, nice decor; trendy but not crazy back ground music. 

I normally don't struggle with giving a rating, but in this case I'm going with five stars.
Amazing place with great coffee and excellent customer service! The owner kirk has amazing customer service and knows some asl. So they also cater to the deaf community.

Ok yes it's a "chain restaurant" and your over it I get it.... it's also in a Truck Stop if truckers come here it's gotta be pretty good. The staff is friendly and they don't hover. The coffee is good and fresh and sure some of the food is weighed part of corporate whatever. But you know what your gonna get and the food is gonna taste like any other Denny's. They are bringing other seasonal things in the menu and lighter options like Chicken Sausage and Egg Whites and etc. Its a large space and it seems they get regulars and they are as nice to you as they are to them. It's simple, solid diner food no it's not like some old school place owned by a family but the menus are solid and the coffee is fresh and yes parking is plenty. I had the moon over my hammy (a breakfast sandwich) on sourdough bread, cheese, scrambled egg and ham with a side of red potatoes. The husband had a few eggs and chicken sausage and we had coffee and water. It was good, not anything that would weigh us down on the road. So there you go.. Four Stars for the service, food is solid and simple 3 stars give or take

I wish I could give negative stars. This place used to be the best local pub until Travis got fired! He now works at 312 pizza in Germantown. Travis is the greatest of all time and we will no longer be patronizing Hillwood. You lost a lot of loyal customers when you fired Travis's

I found this spot the night I got to Reno while I was walking around the city.  I'd already had dinner but I put it on my list to try when I came back to Reno at the end of my trip. After dinner at Bowl, I went over to The Chocolate Bar and had the truffle plate for dessert.  There are seven of them in different varieties, and they were smaller than I'd pictured, which is good.  I didn't have lots of room!  I savored them all.  SO delicious!  My favorite one was the raspberry.

We have been to Nashville several times and each time like to try a new restaurant.  This place did not disappoint.  I would, like everyone else, recommend the Hot Chicken Mac n Cheese as well as the Brussel Sprout Pizza or Pie as they call it.

Note - We went during a busy night.  It is my understanding the second floor is for "walk ins."  We waited maybe 15 minutes on a Friday night at 7:30pm.

Yes, the tofu hoagie is good but in the little time I was located in West Philly, they had increased their prices. That means that the pomegranate aloe vera drink for 2.99 became 3.29. Bummer. Overall, the prices can be a little better for a West Philly corner store.

However, the staff is really very nice and that in itself makes me return every time. They also have an ATM machine since it's cash only.

This place was great! Waited in line for less than 15min (there were 3 lines of probably 7 cars each)... The guy was friendly, professional and competent. I didn't even have to get out of my car. By the time I was done paying the $9 I was done! I was expecting this to be a real inconvenience but this place made it quick and painless!

Read a lot of review and thought this place would be good.  First clue should have been it was a Friday and at lunch there was nobody there.  The server and the hostess were both very cordial and prompt.  My wife ordered a turkey sandwich.  The turkey looked like it came out of an oscar meyer deli pack,  Flavorless and bland.  Our friend ordered soup.  It came in a large bowl but again was rather tastless.  We did not try any deserts.  To bad had high hopes for this place.

Oh, Bru, I could kiss you - especially if your lips were made of your delicious burgers. This place knows how to do burgers plain and simple - juicy, flavorful and a myriad of different burgers to choose from. My personal fave is the 3 cheese garlic burger. Always cooked a perfect medium, juicy, cheesy goodness on a toasted bun. They also have great fries and a house ketchup that will ruin all other ketchups for you. On to apps - their chili is ON POINT. Perfectly seasoned. There is also a shrimp/sausage spicy Mac n cheese. Yeah. Give it a try. Now after stuffing your face with all the afore mentioned goodness, don't leave without trying their white chocolate and peach bread-pudding with homemade whipped cream and candied pecans. Lastly, if you're the thirsty type (like myself) they have a full bar and local beers on tap. The only downside is how popular and therefore packed this place is. Be selective about when you go, start with a beer then eat like a maniac.

My family and I had an amazing time in Apartment 13! This was my 4th escape room, but it was the first for my three family members I had with me. Everyone really enjoyed watching the story unfold of this room, and we were challenged but still had a great sense of accomplishment when we were able to escape with just a few minutes left. Hunter and Christian were our Game Masters when we were here, and they were both amazing! You can tell that they are very knowledgeable about the rooms, and truly enjoy their work. We can't wait to come back for more rooms!

First class service, bar none. I arrived at 7;30 a.m. with no appointment and was immediately greeted in a friendly and professional manner. I explained my siutation and was told that they would assess my situation and get back with me. Within 90 minutes I received a phone call with the assessment along with the estimated cost and time of completion. By 11:00 a.m. my truck was fixed and ready to go. Everything about the process was up front, first class, and professional.

I really want to give a better rating but I can't. The food was absolutely amazing but the service was THE WORST I have ever had anywhere. They need to find some new servers and the place would be great.

I have been here a couple of times.  First time, a friend came into town and we had lunch together.  We were amazed with the seafood selection.  No wait at all which was nice.  I just love their NE clam chowder with large generous proportions of clam.  Second time, I picked up the Maryland crab chowder at the take-out counter which was just as good.

I went to Butcher and Singer last night with Kristine and Jeff G. for Restaurant Week. The restaurant is beautiful, even with the classic "gambling dogs" painting on the wall. 

While everyone else had a Cesar salad for the first course, I chose the Beef and Barley soup. I was glad I did. Everyone said the salad was very salty. The soup was yummy and exactly what I needed to warm up. 

We all ordered the Filet Mignon and garlic mashed potatoes for the second course. The steaks were cooked perfectly and were very flavorful. We also had a side of Brussels sprouts with bacon and a bottle of wine. 

Most of us chose the Chocolate Fudge cake for dessert. It was the kind of cake you know you shouldn't finish but can't leave alone. It was very rich so I was thankful for the scoop of vanilla ice cream that came with it. It helped to mellow it out. Beware of the brandied cherries. 

Kristine G. chose the Baked Alaska. It was the complete opposite of the Chocolate cake in taste but still very good. 

Service was great and the food was good. I'd definitely go back outside of Restaurant Week to try a few other things that caught my eye.
Awesome ice cream shop. Locally owned! Please check them out if you have a chance. Great area in the city. Try a new flavor. All of them are really good.
Really good food. First visit got off to a slow start but once I figured out their process we sailed on through.

Sadly, I need to update on my most recent experience negatively. I decide last night to order carry out because I just didn't want to go back in due to the previous experience. I was going to use the gift card I received due to the bad experience last time sent to me. I called the line and the phone just rang, rang, rang. I called three times and eventually hit a different option in order to get someone to pick up. I am not sure of the hostess' name but she was so rude. I told her the other phone just rang and she rudely replied that they were busy so there's nothing she can do. I asked her to take my order and she huffed and puffed and asked me what I want. As I started ordering she kept interrupting me to ask what else I wanted. I was trying to tell her specifics about my order. Then, she told me it'll be about an hour. I asked for my total and she said she's just a hostess so she don't know. I then said ok I'll wait. She, again, rudely responded well, you will have to call back then because she's busy. I said ma'am I need to know how much money to send with my husband. She didn't tell me to hold on or anything just put me on hold. After about 20 minutes on hold I gave up. I do believe she would have kept me on hold on purpose. I tried calling back an hour later. A nice young lady named Tonya answered and I asked to speak to a manager. She put me on hold and the same mean rude hostess got back on the line and asked me who I was and why I needed a manager. I said I was a customer and had an issue I'd like to speak to a manager about. She would not let me talk to a manager. She just kept saying they were busy. Now, I understand the restaurant business because I was a server for 7 years and then a service manager for 3 years. Even though it may get busy you must never lose that customer service. It's a part of the job, always treat customers with hospitality. Period. If a customer asked for a manager, they should be able to speak to a manager. I just can't fathom the ridiculous service at this location. She is entirely too rude to be in the front of the house.

Elevation Burger is an attempt at an east coast In-N-Out Burger.  Doesn't come close.  

The food isnt bad, and they even have an iphone app to place your order, which I tried and my order was ready upon arrival.  

3 stars because their food isn't bad, its actually good.  But they come nowhere near as good as In-N-Out Burger.  Not even close.

You can order something up to like 10 patties on a burger.  Next time I'm going to order a 10 patty bohemoth burger and a diet coke.
Very helpful visit today. They scheduled me same day, explained the issue, fixed it and got me out the door as quickly as possible. Will definitely be back.

Let me start off by saying that this place is awesome! Whenever I get my nails done now it's here. I've been coming here off and on for a few years. Really, only coming when I have fake nails that need to be fixed up. But about a month ago this awesome place saved my butt. I had gone to a nail salon closer to my place and they destroyed my beautiful fake nails with their crappy job. A few days later, I came here to get them fixed. The people were so nice and able to fix my nail problem. Flash forward a few weeks later, my nails were still holding up nicely. I was getting tired of the color and the nails were getting too long for me. Thus, I got them filed down, filled, and got a new color. I love it. These guys are my life savers.

All there people are really nice. Most are neat to talk to as well. I would have to say that they are all really good people. None of them do a bad job and they are all fast about their work. They don't want you waiting for too long and have a system going. Having the system is nice because you are able to get in and out in a timely matter. 

Parking is a little bit of a nightmare right now, but there is construction going on and they will get back the other lot soon from what they were telling me. Since this is a temporary problem, I can't give them trouble for it on the overall rating.

For future nail jobs and when friends ask, I will definitely tell them to come here.

If you want a cheap department store that has a little bit of everything, I am a pretty big fan of the Target chain of stores as it is. In my opinion they are better than all of their competitors.

This store is one of the biggest target stores I've ever been to. For that reason it has a little bit more of everything you might want. I think the placement of goodswas a little awkward, and I had a little bit of trouble finding what I wanted. But otherwise it was your typical target store, and a pretty good one to boot.

We really enjoyed our dinner at Five last night. The wine by the glass options were excellent. The amuse bouche was a charcuterie/cheese/crouton that set the tone. I had the tagliatelle and my husband had the salad -- both fresh and Home grown. Delicious!  We each had a special entree -- I had the chicken leg which was fall off the bone and my husband had the beef short ribs -- equally fall off the bone.  So glad we shared. Topped it off with the apple crisp.  This place is so natural and delicious. Highly reco.

Seems like the new chef has asked for a lot more money.
Their prices are creeping up to that of some higher end Philly restaurants.
$30 for a chicken dish?
Getting a little ridiculous Domain.  You need to re-think this.
You're loosing a star in my book.

Amazing prices. You can get milk and eggs for dirt cheap. I wish this place was just closer to where I live so I could go all the time. Ice cream is amazing too. Try the cookies and cream best flavor.

I really wanted to give this place 5 stars. When I walked in I was intimidated because I was completely underdressed, but I was greeted with a smile and super friendly bartenders. I ordered a shot of whisky and began smoking a cigar. Midway into a spirited conversation with my friends( one shot in) I opened my left hand onto an oncoming waitress. She grabbed my wrist, twisted her face up and began to tell te other staff how she almost got a SCAR on her face. As I sat behind her she kept digging into the situation making me feel very uncomfortable as a customer.  In all honesty I was done... UNTIL......

I had to PEE. The bathroom changed my perspective. The attendants were awesomely  amazing. They treated me like a princess and sprayed after I peed and gave me hand towels and called me beautiful.  Ugh, I'll be back. Even if to only sit in the bathroom and drink expensive shots with the attendants.

Walden's is a great spot to grab breakfast or lunch, and the staff are so nice! They have kid toys and booster/hig chairs if you want a conversation with another parent yet also nice enough to catch up on a little reading. Easy access for free refills instead of getting inline all over again.

yayayayayay!  Loved it here!!  Just what I needed, good apps, awesome atmosphere, and super close to where my hotel was located.  I wasn't sure what to make of the name of the place... like was I walking into a bar where people bring their pets or what?!  Nope. A bi-level bar with wall 2 wall black and white dog pics.

Scratched my head for a bit on the decor and then kept it moving.  Asked for a Yuengling and the waiter suggested I have a drunken fox lager... Glad he did!

Staff was a bit stiff and didn't smile much but it was packed for Saint Pats festivities and I'll chalk it up to that!  Can't wait for me and the hubby to travel to Philly land again and stop in for another fox!

I heard about this place when I was watching the best thing I ever ate on the food network and all I can say is try their Shrimp and Alligator cheesecake! It is amazingly delicious. Too bad this dish is only comes in appetizer serving. The garlic cornbread is so good too. I wish I was able to sample everything on the menu. I will def be back when I come back. Service was excellent as well.

One of my favorite things to do to relax is go to a Barnes and Noble and read. I love that this is encouraged here and that the cafe is pretty great unless it is crowded. I usually come early on Sundays and spend an afternoon. They have such a good location!

Wonderful authentic Vietnamese food. My wife ordered a chicken dish, but I was adventurous and ordered the Pho Deluxe, which included every type of meat, including meatballs, flank steak, and tendon. For non-aficionados of Vietnamese cooking, the flank steak is served raw. The proper method for eating it is to put the meat in the very hot broth and let it simmer until it's ready to eat. Yum! The owner was very helpful and made sure that I understood how to mix all of the ingredients for my Pho.

We will definitely be coming back for more!

First off, I've read all the other reviews and I can only say "wow...am I lucky!"

Took a party of 5 in yesterday including two children for supper.  Got there just around 5 p.m. and it wasn't busy so we quickly ordered, sat in the back and waited.

Drinks came out quickly, free soda refills.  

Then my Greek Salad, which was pretty damn good without having to go to Michael's.  In fact, I'll say that for me it was perfect because it had plenty of olive and feta and peppers and just the right amount of dressing.

4 Slices of pizza...the kids loved the cheese, the adults loved the margherita.

Next I had the meatball sub/slider which was basically a meatball sub cut in thirds.  It was delicious.  I had pretty much sworn off meatball subs after one too many disasters at Subway, but this was tasty and perfectly sized.

Garlic knots...check!  Parmesan Fries...check!

The food flew out of the kitchen, was piping hot, drinks refilled without flagging down the server.

Best thing was we fed 5 for under $40 and everybody was stuffed.

I know people have been frustrated with waiting and delays, etc but last night couldn't have gone more smoothly.

My only complaint is that I took my iPad in case there was a long wait but they don't have wi-fi, which would probably go a long way to soothe the purported long wait times....please...
made the purchase easy had most of the add ons in stock and went out of there way to get are new rzr ready for the weekend

When I moved to SF two years ago, I went through several trial and error experiences trying to find a hairdresser that could give me the perfect blonde I was looking for.

That is, until a friend referred me to Erica at eSalon. She is AMAZING! She does the perfect highlights that look so natural and she listens to what you want to do. She is also the sweetest and makes getting your hair done enjoyable! I have now been to her for over a year and every time, I am so happy with the color. She is simply the best!

Probably the best coffee shop we went to in NOLA. They have just about anything you'd want, the staff is friendly and knowledgeable, and the place is super clean and modern. Loved their iced coffee. Bathrooms were nice too!
I live 4 blocks from dominos. I track my orders online and tonight's order took over 30 minutes from the time it left the store to get to my door. Arrived cold

My friend and I thought this would be a great place to stop by for brunch on a weekend morning.  I'm not sure why, but this place wasn't as crowded as I was expecting for a Saturday afternoon.  My friend ordered the salmon crepe and I go the strawberries one.  She absolutely loved hers and wanted to drag the rest of our posse here next time.

I loved my strawberries one too!  The creme fraiche really added a smooth creamy dimension without being overpowering.  I'm always worried when I order a fruit crepe that it'll be too sweet - but this wasn't the case here. The crepe had just a little bit of sweetness but didn't feel exceptionally desserty to me.  I can't wait to come back and hopefully try some of the other amazing looking dishes!
The sushi was good but the service was terrible had me waiting on a server for about 20 min before i spoke up and then didnt get drinks for another 10 min steer clear if your lookin for good service

Not bad pizza, but management is poor. They didn't deliver all the order, and the delivery driver didn't receive my phone number from the ordering person to call me on the phone once they arrived. Not great, but not bad.
The family meal is so good! It costs the same to feed a family of 4 from Sparta with healthy grilled chicken and rice and gyro meat and veggies as it does one trip to MCDs. HIGHLY recommended.

This was our third visit. Can't complain about the food since we loved what we got.

Starting with the 2nd visit the service was horrible and slow.

This last time we sat for almost 20 minutes without anyone acknowledging us, bringing us water or even a drink order.

Needless to say we won't be going back. Texas Roadhouse is right down the street, the service is fast and the prices are lower.
Great food! The racist jokes by the toothless cook were a little surprising but the food did rock.

Local joint hidden at the end of a strip mall behind Kroger. We were on our way to a different place when I recalled a recommendation from Four Square and decided to try it out. Once we actually found the place (not their fault) we walked in to find the place pretty empty for a Saturday night at 6:30pm. We promptly were seated and our waitress came right over and took our drink order. Being that we had never been here before she gave us plenty of time to look over the menu and make our selections. We decided to start with fried pickles. For the main course I chose the 10" "Load Up The Wagon". As I looked around while waiting for the pickles my eyes were greeted with a basic decor and color scheme. What was nice is instead of using the standard florescent lighting they have installed chandeliers which give off a better glow than the alternative. They have tables, booths, and what appears to be a bar section for anyone 21 and up. There is a jukebox in the corner to purchase music you may want to listen to while you dine in. The wall sconces above the bathroom doors make it easier to locate them. The fried pickles were different as they were actual spears vs the typical "chips" that you get at other places. When our food came out I was happy to see that a 10" was going to be enough food for me. It was delicious. Good amount of toppings and and just delicious. Its worth another visit for sure. For the price you get a good amount of food...we didn't leave hungry at all. :)

Really liked this place! Nice environment and really delicious food. Definitely a more upscale option for Chinatown, but the cleanliness and service is worth it the few extra dollars per plate, in my opinion. I got the Pork with Vermicelli and added on a spring roll (which was seriously one of the more delicious spring rolls I've ever had). 

The rice in the rice dishes was a bit on the soggier side than I would have liked, but overall this didn't take away from a nice and satisfying night out!
Place was really good! Our server seemed busy and wasn't really a talker. Overall great atmosphere really good food and not bad price wise!

Stopped by here because we read reviews that they had decent dim sum and didn't feel like driving into Tampa. We only ordered about seven dim sum dishes, but for the most part they were pretty good. We also ordered and beef and garlic combination for lunch which was excellent. The fried rice was tasty and the beef with garlic sauce was flavored and had plenty of beef in it. When you walk in it looks just like any other typical Chinese take out restaurant, except there are more seats. Service was friendly and attentive. Would definitely recommend.

If you are a bandwagon fan, don't come here.  Only seriously hardcore Pacers and Colts fans are allowed here.  How serious is this place? They will give you a two hour wait if you are NOT wearing home town gear.  Why?  Because you might get a beatdown.  Try to root for Miami or New England here.  The last thing you will remember is the fact that everyone next to you got up all of a sudden.  I swear one my "friends" almost got his tail kicked.  Luckily for him, he is a pretty good size.  If only they knew he was a pussycat.

The Pacers regularly hold events here, like viewing parties and draft parties, because the crowd is so loyal and boisterous.  It's good that we have hometown support so strong in my little neck of the woods.

I can say that the German beer selection is pretty impressive, even for a big city. I can say that I've never seen so many options before for Ritter Sport chocolate bars. I can say that the spicy landjäger was pretty good and I wish I had purchased more. I can say that Jamie the owner is gregarious and displays a lot of pride and passion behind his business to offer the amount of German food options that he does, whether it be made there or imported.  

But I honestly know jack squat about German meals other than the times a German friend of mine in Boise made a rare dish for me. So I'm taking a pass on this rating and will let the palate of a demanding native rate them. Factoring in the grocery options, the prepared food (including the rotated meal of the day), and the service, I was told that this is much better (and cheaper) than Schnitzel Garten and light years better than Prost. So there ya go. Straight from a German's mouth: five stars.

I was thoroughly enjoying myself at this restaurant until my waitress greeted our table and then went missing for practically the rest of the night.  When I commented to my friend who had dined at this location twice before, she had the same issue.  My major wtfs were:  it took forever to take our cocktail order, after she took our appetizer order and finally brought it out..she brought out a pizza stand..we hadn't ordered our pizzas yet because she had forgotten to take that order, we had to hunt her down for 2nd beer, ordered desserts and couldn't finish them and of course had to hunt her down again to get a box.  1 word that describes the experience was annoying.  The food was really good but service sucked.  I would recommend going to the Callowhill location..it seems like they run a tighter ship and the view of the parking garage is kind of a buzz kill.

Cool, fun, and happening place to get some quality eats in the Seminole heights area. I've been here a couple of times, and have tried a variety of things off their menu. The decor is very "hipster" with that retro americana feel. 

Their pizzas and unique drinks are what keep me coming back to this place! (My favorites are the purple drank and the hog pizza)They serve elevated american fare that wont leave you going home hungry with the portion sizes. 

For the vegetarians and vegans out there, they have a variety of really good options for you. I really like their Good Burger. You can tell it's not meat, but it still satisfies your hunger without the red meat guilt (if you suffer from that). I also find their curry dish fairly appetizing, but beware it is spicy. 

The few downsides to this place is the parking and the wait times. This place can get really packed on the weekends so try to come at an off time or early to beat the wait. They do take reservations, so if you are planning to come with a big party call ahead!

Oh I got suckered in with the aroma of the crawfish/shrimp boil wafting out from their front window where they cook their shellfish. However, the troughs of shrimp and crawfish were beyond spicy! And I love spicy... This was the lingering, growing spiciness that makes it hard to enjoy subsequent bites. The shrimps were jumbo but their crawfish was barely there with a couple of decent sized ones thrown in just for appearance. I would recommend the barbeque shrimps as it was cooked just right with the right amount of seasoning. The fried platter wasn't seasoned at all... but of course my taste buds were burnt by the overpowering shrimp/crawfish boil.  In a town full of great restaurants, don't bother with this one.

I don't know why anyone eats here, other than the chargrilled oysters people swear by. The service is poor, and today my table was served a plate of cold, old tasting French fries. The "redo" plate was just as bad. Waitress first told us there was no drink menu, then sullenly slapped down a menu with the wine list. We asked for French bread and it was ancient. Spinach dip was like green slime. No New Orleans restaurant which prides itself on being the best at something should serve anything this bad on its menu, or do it with a sour face.
Nachos and pizza are great! Nice place to hang out in Midtown, often have life music.  A little expensive but not too bad, mushroom pizza is fantastic.!
Best restaurant and cocktail bar in St Louis by far! Ambiance, quality, service all in check. Must haves-bacon wrapped dates, a Lions Tooth cocktail, & pot pie.

In the summertime, this is where I am every single Tues/Thurs!  Kim Massie brings the house down with her phenomenal voice on the back patio.  The stage is built to look like the front porch of an old house.  A totally diverse crowd - from Cardinal fans to 80 year old  regulars - dances until the microphone goes silent.  If you're there after the kitchen closes and you're still hungry - don't worry! There's a pizza co that delivers right to your table - just give them a call on your cell.  Phenomenal!
Solid spot with great veggie and vegan options and a more adventurous beer menu than other neighborhood wannabes.

Updating based on the number of times I have been back to eat the Dan dan noodles and the other dishes I chose have been quite delicious so I'm rebranding this ratings. 

Dan Dan noodles. Nuff said. Actually everything else was ok, nothing bad but not amazing or anything. the service was great. I would return for the dan dan noodles anytime. So good.

Sen Thai -Asian Bistro is an extremely lovely establishment on Locust in Downtown St. Louis.  We came for lunch, and got one of the last open tables.  The staff were very friendly and seemed genuinely happy, even though the place was crowded.  Immediately I took that as a good sign.  I was starved, as I usually eat most of my food midday.  We ordered the Thai spring rolls, an order of crab rangoon and the satay.  The spring rolls were different in that they were vegetarian and had some crispy fried veggies in them.  That said, they were delicious and still had that clean fresh that those who love spring rolls desire.  The crab rangoon were large, and were packed to the brim  with the cream cheese mixture.  They were fried just right, and were perfect.  The satay came with a terrific peanut sauce, and I think that I could have eaten three more orders of them.  Seriously, while everything here was beyond fabulous, you must get the satay.  

For my entree I ordered the ebi curry, which has shrimp.  I ordered this because I wanted a curry, but most of them have bell peppers [I'm allergic].  Any thoughts that I was settling were blown away when the dish arrived.  Not only was it beautiful, but it was delicious!  There were shrimp, stew and rice along with starchy veggies.  The heat was strong, but not overpowering, and the earthy taste of the food played nicely with the sweeter taste of the rice.  This is the sort of dish that I think of when I think of the perfect dish.  The shrimp were large and cooked just right, at the peak of freshness.  

One friend got the Pho beef, and as usual we all tried bites of everyone else's.  I just had a bite of the beef, and it was succulent and delicious.  My other friend ordered the chicken Bangkok spicy noodles.  They were indeed spicy, but were delicious.  I had the Thai iced coffee, which in my opinion was a perfect compliment to my food.  The prices are within reason, and the service is good.

I had a good experience with Dr. Stunkard. I have trouble eyes: my vision was horrible, I had Lasik and saw perfect for about a year and now 5 years later I'm back in contacts full time. I also have an astigmatism, severely dry eyes and have struggled to wear contacts. Most of these things were undiagnosed issues that I thought I had to just deal with until I saw Dr. Stunkard. He spent a good amount of time discussing my issues with me and doing a thorough exam. He really helped me clear up things that had been bothering me and provided me with solutions for them. I have a much easier time wearing contacts and my eyes are generally more comfortable. I took a star off because the office could be run a little better.

Nothing going on here.  Ask for assistance, DO not expect anything.  I was told to wait 2 minutes, I waited 15. When explaining in the way out, the young guys thought it was funny.  I don't.  My time is something and I expect to be treated with respect.  You can't avoid Home Depot.  You can avoid this store.

Okay, let's take this review up another notch!

In my short life, boxing has been one of the hardest workouts I've had to endure.  I am a young professional and I have experience (high school, collegiate, amatuer where applicable) in football, basketball, boxing, track & field, and wrestling - oh and combat training (I was in the military for a while); the only training harder was wrestling.  I've worked out at many gyms & with many different workout philosophies - heavy weightlifting, endurance weightlifting, aerobics, crossfit, p90x, boxing gyms, kickboxing gyms and yoga.

About the gym, this place is a true school of hard knocks.  It's located in the large basement of the Banana Republic for Women on Main St, so it gets humid (perfect).  There's jump ropes, pull up bar, 5-6 speed bags, 5-6 heavy bags, mats, free weights up to 65lbs(would enjoy some 70s and 75s), tires, sledgehammer, ab balls, medicine balls, gloves, wraps, weighted vests, changing rooms, bathrooms, fight music, and a high energy trainer - Joltin.

Joltin Joe (owner, trainer, and CEO) is the man of the hour.  He's rough, rugged, yet pays attention to detail and knows what it takes to get your body to top peak physical shape.  I've been working out at Joltin Jabs since December.  He's helped me lose about 5 lbs and cut about 2-3% body fat and it doesn't stop there.  He's helped me out in many other ways too, he's a MYK native and knows the area very well, and has a big heart - PICK HIS BRAIN!

So to put it all in perspective, Joltin Jabs is like having a personal trainer except you'll be working out with 2-6 other ppl at the same time depending on when you come in or the day.  I go 3-5 times a week and on average workout with 2-3 other ppl.  At the end of the day, he'll give you the tools, guidance, and motivation to take it to the other level, the choice is yours.

Visit www.joltinjabs.com or www.joltinjabs.net and do your research!  This place is stamped, certified, official!

I've been converted. Yes it's overpriced, $4 for a cupcake, and even for a non-cupcake fan like myself... I have to give my allegiance to them now. 

Their cupcakes are by the far the best I've had (better than Georgetown cupcakes!) 
Why? 
- Perfection in the level of sweetness a human being ought to be having (none of that diabetic frosting) 
- Rich and moist cake texture a cupcake ought to have 
- Natural creamy smooth frosting that compliments the flavor it is representing

Must try: 
- red velvet 
- pumpkin spice
- green tea matcha (not always sold- check their Instagram) 
- CHOCOLATE CHIP COOKIES! $5 for a bag

We stopped off here on our way home from DC, and had a decent lunch that would have been a heck of a lot better had the server there not gone out of her way to make a couple of her customers (us) feel like jerks. 

The restaurant was not busy at 1:30 on a weekday afternoon, and we were seated right away.  Harry's is a beautiful room, with a large lounge area off to the left of the main dining room, which has a huge high ceiling, an open-floor design, and a fireplace at one end.  Combined with the muted earthtones of the place, the fireplace gives Harry's a warm and inviting atmosphere. 

Our server was in no hurry to take care of us, however, and we sat for quite a while, waiting to give a drink order.  When we did finally do so, we sat for even longer waiting for it to arrive.  In a room that's only 1/4 full, between 12 and 2, there's really no excuse for slow, surly service.
