The chicken was well done, and I really liked the yogurt sauce. Speaking of which, while ordering, one of the employees (manager?) asked if I had tried it before and suggested I have a little sample of the yogurt sauce before ordering. I did and enjoyed it, so stuck with my order. Despite liking my sandwich, I acknowledge that I may have liked it even more had I gone for one of the other, not - so - light options. Another time.

Based on the reviews I read, I was really expecting more from Kabob's Merion Station location.

Located just down the street from Saffron, Kabob is a bit smaller and in my opinion not as good.

The Tikka Masala seemed a bland; it lacked some of the traditional spices. Went on a Saturday and staff was not very friendly. It was fairly early (6pm maybe) and fairly empty so not sure why

The seating environment was okay but the noise level was a bit high for the small space. 

If you're dining in, Saffron maybe a better option. The food is bit better and the environment is a bit more intimate

Way more upscale then we were expecting based on the menu prices. I can only assume they're growing a client base and reputation before bringing prices up. Clean and modern, the atmosphere was very enjoyable. The chicken tableau was magic, and I don't say that lightly. It was probably the best chicken dish I've ever had and i highly recommend it to anyone.

The food at Lucky 13 really was tasty. I wasn't sure what to expect - it's dark, they were playing Guns 'n' Roses which morphed into some speed metal eventually...I don't equate any of that necessarily with good eats. 

The beer choices were standard and tasty. They were better than standard but we're gettin spoiled now in this city! Had some great familiar local brews that hit the spot.

I got the smoked trout sandwich and it was huge and fresh tasting. Reminded me of whitefish a lot and I was a big fan of the potato salad which wasn't that gross mayonnaisey nonsense but full of pep and flavor and ...yum. My friend got something involving catfish which looked really impressive - it even had little crafish on top. Who knew?

I guess my only real complaint was the music. Luckly it changed when some kind dudes took over the jukebox. I didn't expect them to be playing the soundtrack to Les Mis or Celine Dion or anything but, loud thrashing hardcore speed metal whatever the hell it was isn't conducive to eating this lovely food and enjoying brews. It makes you want to throw your barstool at someone's head. I sensed the staff dug it but you gotta  think of your clientele too, friends. 

Service was nice, not awesome, but friendly and fine. I'll be back but I'll make sure to take control of the jukebox immediately.

My favorite bar in Reno.  Excellent martini selection, great atmosphere and those to die for Blue Diamond almonds.  After living in an over-priced, um, city, like Las Vegas it is a relief to go back to Reno and find a fantastic place like the Roxy Bistro.  You get the amazing selection, great service, cool atmosphere and excellent location all at reasonable prices.  If Heaven has a lounge, it is the Roxy Bistro.

This was an amazing tour! Eight of us were in town for a 4-day weekend in New Orleans during Carnival season (pre-Mardi Gras) and wanted to learn a little more about the city. I hate bus tours so we decided on a bike tour and Kristine definitely delivered. 

The bikes were new - with their own New Orleans street names - and had soft cushy seats. No gears or hand brakes- just reverse your feet to brake like your old Western Flyer. Eight people is the largest tour they will do and I must say we were a spectacle. We had matching purple tie dye shirts with our own insignia - Crewe of CalMoKan (we are from those 3 states) - and we got lots of stares, questioning looks and even some applause and cheers as we were riding through town. Maybe they thought we were a parade.

Additionally, with so many of us, there was lots of chaos and ADD and Kristine dealt very well with us. She was very knowledgeable about New Orleans and was definitely not giving us a script. We asked tons of questions - both on and off task - and she answered them all. She was laid back and adaptable and just made the tour very enjoyable.

We hit Louis Armstrong park, Treme, the Riverfront and took the Ferry across the river to Algiers Point. We stopped at a bar there for a drink and quick snack of chips (we were starving with all the exercise!) and then headed back. She even gave us mini moon pies once we got back that they were going to hand out at a parade.

Go here! You won't regret it! She and her partner Richie (?) also rent bikes for a period of time if you don't want to take a tour.

This Wawa needs a major facelift. This was my local Wawa growing up the area and I never had many complaints about it... until I branched out and met other Wawas. I recently moved back to the area and was shocked when I first went back in. Very small, not too clean, and definitely NOT the nicest people working there. I miss my old Wawa :::sigh:::
wow! Great Pho and outstanding service! the new owners are doing a great job look no further for a great bowl of Pho!

Usually just do the drive thru but today went in to eat. I can't believe how dirty it was. Wow! Disgusting.... then on top of that, our server brought our food and check and then left the restaurant. Literally had her purse and walked out and never came back. I don't think I will be able to ever come back, even the drive thru, after seeing how gross the inside of the restaurant looked.

The sandwich was good, not bad not great.  My main problem here is the price, with tax I paid $9+ for a very small sandwich.  I like to support new independent places, unfortunately with the location and prices this place is going to be a hard sell for people.

In all the hotel is not bad. But we stayed here around the same time last year. The heat in our room was set at 60 the room must have been well over 85. I complained to the front desk. They sent someone to "fix it". He came to the room and just turned on the AC. Even as it was snowing outside. This year we came back again, now in a different room. We were shocked to have the same problem again. Again, I called the front desk and again they sent someone to turn on the AC. So it appears that you have only two choices here, cook or freeze. Last night we just shut the whole thing off and opened the window, only to hear the trains all night. They must get some very big electric bills here. No wonder the rates are so high here. This will be our last stay here. You would think after a year they would have fixed the problem.

When you search "Harvest" on Yelp, the "free flatbread" offer pops up. This might entice you, but I implore you to ignore the part of you that wants free food, for you will not find this dining experience to be a liberating one. My friends and I went to Harvest this past Saturday night in the hopes of having a delicious late night dinner/snack. Once seated, we waited at least 8 minutes before a waitress came to our table. We were quite parched and eager for water, and we also were very hungry! When she finally arrived, we placed our orders for water and three pizzas. When the pizzas arrived (after quite a long wait) they tasted like glorified cardboard. I'm not exaggerating, there was NO flavor. But we were famished so we ate it (which I regret). I even asked for red pepper flakes and after covering my slice in spice, it was still barely edible. I have a pretty low threshold when it comes to pizza satisfaction, and this is the first time it was not met. The combo of poor service and poor food made this evening both forgettable and memorable. Harvest has very good drink specials (such as $3 long islands) so I gave them two stars for that. If you want a cheap drink, by all means go! But don't expect any fresh harvested (pun intended) ingredients or flavors- you won't find them here.

Great food. Friendly staff. I had Gumbo and a Poboy; both were delicious. The portions were generous and the prices were very reasonable. The service was fast; the wait staff was very attentive. My party included a vegetarian and they were able to accommodate her diet. I am looking forward to going back and trying new things here.

I love this place.  Food comes out so fast and it's made with quality ingredients. My only complaint is the price.  It's pretty expensive for what you get.  For a beef pho with meatballs and flank it's around $9 but to add any other kinds of meat it's like $2+. So if you want a deluxe pho it'll come out to around $12-$13.  Highly recommend the banh mi and iced coffee.  The spring rolls are also good and are pretty big.

Finally had brunch at Noble Crust and I must say I was Pleasantly Surprised!!!
The food was very well prepared and very interesting combinations I must say.
I had the Short Rib Benny and my husband had the Bronzed Salmon Benny and we thoroughly enjoyed both, the portions are more than enough, I couldn't finish mine.
We also enjoyed some interesting cocktails!!
Great twist on a Bloody Mary.
Our waiter Jimel had some very good suggestions 
And he's service was top notch. Quite a charming young man.
We will definitely return, this time for dinner.
We'll see what suggestions Jimel has this time.

Ambience good, tried several techs and so far liking the experience.  Had one bad experience, but now I know to schedule with someone ahead of time and to be specific about the type of service I want otherwise it creates problems with the scheduling for others.  

Techs to ask for are Tee and Emily.  Friendly and provide great customer service.

It's funny that when you to go fast food places people that work there are not usually the most pleasant, I live near this one and on occasion drive thru for the Mc Muffin deal and they are nice and quick, for the money they make and the fact it is a really fast paced work environment it's nice to see.
I've just started using this cleaners, but they are kind, professional and items are ready when promised.

Sun King on draft! Holla!

If you need any more reasons to sit outside on the canal bank... here's another one: avoid the cursing & arguing staff that doesn't get along. They were trying to invade my lovely early evening work session. They couldn't stop me though! 

But yeah, what a gem -- on the canal, huge patio that serves Sun King & Wine. 

A French influenced menu of crepes and paninis... I didn't eat here out of fear that the slobber from the argumentative chef would drool down onto my arugula; so, I stuck with Sun King. A Wee Mac in fact.

Closest intersection is Michigan & Indiana. Street Parking around the corner on Indiana is the easiest. 

A beautiful space of a mixed use development. One giant upside of new developments going in on the canal.

I visited this location yesterday to pick up my order.  I was greeted with smiles and lots of positivity by the staff.  Miss Keisha was great.  She took my order over the phone.  The guys were funny and great too.  They waited until I arrived before my fries were cooked.  They said, that's what they do, because they wanted the fries to be FRESHHH! In addition, the environment was very welcoming & happy! Thanks for the great food, fast service & excellent Customer Service Five Guys! I highly recommend you check out this place! You'll leave out feeling GOOD!!!
Excellent environment, service and good.  They have a nice wine list as well.
Delicious! I'm a cannoli snob and gotta say the half chocolate half vanilla cannoli is amazing.  Great old time feeling atmosphere. Be willing to pay a little more for high quality.

We came in for the Chai, which we'd heard is thee best in town.     We each ordered a Chai (which was a standard size coffee mug)
It was spicy and good, but almost half of the cup was foam.  For 5.00 I expected a larger size.    It could have been hotter as well. 
If you want more than a few sips , order without foam & ask for extra hot.  We were disappointed , because of driving 30 min & parking 3 blocks away on a Sun evening - only to spend 18$ for 2 small Chais & an order of kale chips.  The chips were extremely salty to our taste.    
It's an ok place but very pricy for what you get.     I wish there were a place to get a great spicy chai , in a pot with a couple of decent servings.     Years ago, there was a place in Tucson called Casbah, which had wonderful chai made from scratch to order.  Since then, we've never found anything that comes close to the wonderful chai we always had  there.....

I checked in and my reservation was wrong...and so to find me a room they raised my rate for the mistake they made to another $100/nite.  When I got to my room the toilet was dirty...I called the front desk and was told they would clean it tomorrow!   The hotel manager called me after my trip to say "we are sorry" and offered me a letter of apology as her way of "fixing" it.  
All hotels make mistakes...it is what they do after that separates the boys from the men...I wont be going back here and neither should you.
This place deserves all the high ratings it gets.  The only problem is you want to order one of everything and i think we did.  Everything taste as good as it looks so don't go if you are on a diet.

A must-do for locals and visitors alike. Locally owned and easy to find, The Hook is officially on my short list for easy, delicious fare. Order at the counter and then find yourself a seat... and definitely try one of the many specialty cocktails on the well-planned menu. 

The curry seafood chowder was absolutely delicious and loaded up with meat, the tartar sauce appeared to be fresh and homemade, and they have large seafood platters to share with friends. Also... yay... curly fries! Pleasantly surprised to have those delivered to the table instead of the traditional French fry. 

This is a great seafood house whether you want something a little more complex or whether you prefer a simple fish and chips. You won't be disappointed. Check this place even if just for a drink. Next time, I'm eating the fish tacos because they looked awesome.

Staff was very friendly and went out of their way to work with my insurance company. Dr Hurd was great! very personable, knowledgeable, and easy to work with. He explained exactly what my issues were and what to do.
one small issue is with Google Maps not knowing exactly where Dr Hurd is now located - it wanted to send me to his former office, then it wanted to send me to the former Innovision site that was in the same area (it's closed). an update is needed.

I've only ever grabbed take out from here, and it's no-frills pasta that hits the spot when I'm craving it. I like that you can mix and match pastas and sauce. 

Last time I came, I got a small to-go box with half beef tortellini with the meat sauce, half plain pasta with the spicy mushroom sauce and 1 meatball. Came to just under $11 and was enough pasta to last me two meals. Also, a bun is included if you're so inclined. 

Simple, fast and inexpensive. I'll take it!

This is for the take out service only.
Let's just say, it's hit or miss. I did it once before and it was ok. Short wait, food was good and price was reasonable.

 Did it again today and it was a disaster. I had to repeat my order multiple times to the individual at the counter, who still didn't seem to understand. After standing around more than 20 minutes, watching others who came in after get their orders before me, I questioned where mine was. It seemed they had no real idea where it was. Also, i still didn't have the coffee I ordered. At this point, I decided to just walk out and go make my own breakfast. I'm sure I was done before they figured out where my stuff was.

It might be an ok place to sit inside and eat, but if you're looking for something to go, relatively quickly, try somewhere else.

I'll give this place 4 stars because the service was excellent. The food was good. I heard a lot of hype about it and went in with high expectations... It was a one-time deal for us. Online reservation was great and they called to confirm the reservation.

Great food, great beer, great service.  Out waiter near the bar tonight was awesome offered great advice and was just a pleasure to be served by.  Everyone there is super friendly and clearly love working there.  If you are going to visit Indy and going to B Ripple, HopCat is a must go.  Crack fries, ice cold local beer, awesome service--what more can you ask for.

Fast and friendly....but..... I had my hair cut by the owner and he seemed distracted and did not take any instruction. It was as if he was on another planet and was trimming someone else' s hair. When I left, I had to drive to a friends for a touch-up. Disappointed and will not be returning.
Absolutely love this place!!!! Delicious falafel with sides!!! Yummy pita!!! Delicious hummus and fries!!! Must try!!! Got the whole family hooked!!!

It's 84 degrees and this place is hot as hell and never enough lines open only come here cause it's close to my house plus got redbox but this place never has anything in stock like seriously and the cashiers 99% got attitude problems

Still perfection to me... I recently got my copy of KDHX Live: Volume 8 (If you donated $88 during this Fall's membership drive or are a Frequency member you get this wonderful gift!) and it has revived my love for this station... And plus cooler weather always gives me this mood for anything indie. Go KDHX!

Nice warm pies, but the could be a bit bigger
Nice decor that's modern with a hipster vibe in downtown Reno

It was late in the evening after the St. Patty's Day parade in Irish Channel. This truck was parked in front of Rendezvous bar on Magazine Street, where it is often parked. After a long day of all day libations, we realized we had only eaten a small bit of chips and a cupcake during the entire day. So my gal pal and I went outside in search of food, when a friendly gentleman offered us some of his tacos. I heard my mother's voice in the back of my head saying, "Never take anything from a stranger." But I swiftly shrugged that off (when have I ever listened to that voice? Sorry, mom!). We thanked this generous man, and ate his taco, exclaiming "Great! Now we don't need to buy any!" But, we were wrong, we HAD to by more. We ran to the truck, "We need two orders of those tacos that guy had...Wait! We need three orders of those tacos!" We had to buy three orders. They were delicious! And we ate them like lions feasting on an antelope--it was not pretty; we literally growled at our friends when they asked for a bite. 

After a long day of drinking and being completely famished, one could say that anything would have tasted good at that point...But these tacos were different. They were legitimately so so so good! And I will eat them again and again, instead of passing this food truck by.

Call Gordon Ramsay for help. Quick. Because the only thing that would improve this place is throwing everything and everybody out and starting again from scratch. 

We were in a hurry to leave (no surprise there) so I brought my credit card and bill up to the front to pay rather than wait for our waiter (he was MIA most of the meal). As the manager processed the card, I watched our waiter prepare two desserts as follows: (1) Use ungloved fingers to "help" position cannoli on plates (2) use same fingers to put dollop of whipped cream on each plate (from spray can), accidentally getting some cream on his fingers (3) put can away, lick fingers (4) wipe fingers on apron (5) pick up plated desserts to take them to unsuspecting victims. Absolutely disgusting.

I liked it, they have great TVs all over the place with every game and speakers for your table. Food was decent. Service was good. I would just not say the place is exactly very clean. PRO TIP: order the brownie bites with vanilla ice cream.

I appreciate the thought behind the restaurant: healthy, well portioned meals made with ingredients from local producers.  However, this increases the cost and decreases the serving size.  I came out feeling like I paid a lot for very little - while the food was good, it wasn't anything mind blowing.

I like the updated menu
I had the.beef crunchy tacos
Everything was fresh.and tasty
I had the ground sirloin burrito
Huge serving one of the biggest and tastiest burritos I have had in a while

Well we were a bit disappointed when we arrived because we thought the entire building belonged to Antique Archeology. Well that's the impression given on the show. It is a small shop that has some interesting pieces but for the most part it appeared to be a showroom for items NOT FOR SALE! It was neat to see some of the pieces we saw on the show other than that expect to see majority Antique Archeology  souvenir items: t-shirts, hats, etc.

Same as all Planet Fitness locations... clean, affordable, great equipment and good instruction.  I just joined after moving here and I'm impressed.  The staff is friendly and the facility is brand new.  Not crowded and a very positive atmosphere. Best deal in town.  Get on their website to see what plan works best for you.  You can't go wrong any way you go.  Good luck and happy health!

Fun place.  Western themed complete with gun fights and saloon.   Food was plentiful and good tasting, not gourmet but definitely good... it's a cowboy steak house, not some east coast fancy restaurant.   
I almost order the vegetarian burger for kicks, but thought better of it and ordered the Brisket Dinner

Brisket was excellent!   My friends ordered the cowboy steak, a very good deal for a lot of plain-old good food

Bowl of cowboy beans for the table... awesome 

Rootbeer was great too!
This Starbucks is a gem. Inside the Bellevue. Beautiful decorative arts carved into the high ceilings. At a great location. If you happen to be in the theater area, recommend to stop in.
Great Chinese food!  Cooked it fresh and the lady helping us was very friendly and nice!  Thank you!

Great cheese steaks.  Get one every time I'm in Roxborough.

Bob D.

This place is like my local diner. Love coming here on weekday mornings for the breakfast special. My usual is eggs over easy w/the potato latke and buttered grilled corn muffin. I see way too many people eating toast. Do they not know about the grilled corn muffin and biscuit option????

I always come here after a night shift. I sit at the counter and have my food within 5min. Speedy, friendly service. Delicious eats. They keep me coming back.

Oh, and that rotating jam!
The veggie wrap (sans avocado & cheese for me) is really tasty. The staff is very friendly. This is definitely on the list for whenever I'm in the area.

I live a mile away so Ive been here dozens of times. I know what is good and what isn't. So cheap in price and food is okay enough. I think its an excellent deal really. You just cant have high expectations. I probably wouldn't come here if I lived too far though - its just really convenient for me. Beers are only 1 or 2 dollars which is amazing!

I am so excited about this new resale store. Such a great location for South City folks. They are in a small space but do a lot with it. Prices are competitive and all the clothes I have seen are in great condition. Super friendly service too. I hope more South City moms of girls start selling there so I can buy it up!!!

I had visited as a kid and based on the memory of the arch swaying I couldn't get myself to go up. There was a wind storm so I do have a little bit of an excuse. About half my group decided to not go up so we enjoyed the museum  downstairs.
These girls working here are very nice and talented!!! The shop is very clean and new with pretty decors :) . Pedicures come with the liners . Price is reasonable. Check it out !!!

I love finding wonderful dessert places when I visit a city! Sucré fulfilled my wish! I got 8 macarons and they were HEAVENLY! It was a little pricey but I mean I did expect this from the "look" of sucré. I also tried their peppermint marshmallows during the holiday season and they were delicious! I would definitely stop by here again if I find myself in New Orleans!
Worst ever. Slow and incompetent servers. Been here forever and every time she brings drinks or food the order is wrong.

Great spot for just about any meal. I went there for a late brunch and had a hard time making up my mind there were so many delicious options to chose from. I didn't try any of their coffee drinks but I hear they are really well known for their lattes and the foam doodles that too them. Will definitely have to go back and try one. Also really loved how they used names and pictures of dogs for table numbers.
The last few times, I knew something was off.  The food is still good, but not to the level I was familiar with.  It is quieter and the service is very fast.

the customer service of the staff in the car audio department was fantastic they were very helpful and patient and did not try to shove extras down out throats, the place was clean and felt nice being in there, of course this is in a nicer neighborhood so one would expect it not to be ghetto as some others places nearer downtown.

Feathers in my cap:
1. Four-course turista menu costing $35 per person
2. Freshly baked bread made in-house, with goat cheese in olive oil for spreading / dipping purposes
3. Non-spicy mussels in white wine sauce, with extra of the freshly baked bread offered for soaking up the broth
4. Lasagna (mildly spicy) with fried egg on top, yummy runny yolk soaking into fresh sheets of pasta
5. Short rib ragu so juicy and tender
6. Cheesecake with berry sauce on top ... mmmm cheesecake
7. Friendly service and never empty water glasses
8. BYOB with wine store across the street
9. Warm/inviting/small/cozy atmosphere
10. Coat rack in the back, no need for awkward placement of puffy down coats over small chairs

Blackeyes:
-Immediately adding junk to the trunk that almost knocked over a neighboring table's wine glasses when I tried to exit the restaurant.

FYI:
-Cash only

I've had a lot of barbecue in my life given that I lived in Austin and this place is pretty good. The brisket had a nice flavorful smoky taste and the ribs had a unique flavor to them and good rub on them. Four stars only because I like the fall off the bone wet kinda of ribs and brisket which is a different kind of style.

I love the desserts at this place! We got the fruit crepe cake and matcha mousse cake which were both so good! I  it 4 stars because of how crowded it can get and people randomly sat at our table while they waited, so the server took their order as well. It was just a little strange. But, still love this place!

Never eat a salad here. Even though it's a bar, you should still expect not to get sick from a simple salad. I ordered a Caesar with chicken, and the chicken was spongy, like it had freezer burn. It was definitely not fresh. I've been sick to my stomach for 2 days since. Not a flu-like bug, a bug you get when you eat something bad... Food poisoning.
Two types of oysters. Both amazing. Raw and Rockafella. Can't decide which I liked more. The balcony seating is exactly what we wanted. Just what we needed to finish up the trip.

Love their donuts! I've tried these before but it's my first time going to the actual bakery. We went after lunch and there isn't any line. We found out they only accept cash (thankfully we got some cash with us). There are no tables here, you can't dine in. So you better eat as you go  or just order a dozen to go. The people there are nice and smiles a lot :) We had to decide the ones we want and the older lady helping us was very patient with us. The donuts are freshly baked (that's how it tasted) and I especially loved the one with cream filling. The look of this bakery is not so modern but I kinda like it that they are preserving the look. Not sure if they're trying to keep it that way in that area because there's a Dairy Queen branch pretty close and it is one of those old branches with the original Dairy Queen logo outside. You will kinda feel you traveled back in time in that area. Back to Long's, I can say that I have tasted other better donuts but I kinda love their donuts for some reason. I will recommend  their donuts and I will keep coming back.

You know when you go to the doctor, because you have to go, but you're like thinking to yourself, this is going to suck so hard and I'm going to hate it. That's EXACTLY how I feel about trotting down to this Party City. While I'm driving down there I'm weeping to myself, "Okay you're throwing a party. You need their eco friendly paper plates and cups and you need to inflate those two huge mylar balloons you bought off of Amazon. You literally can't go anywhere else! You can do this!! Go to Party City,Di!!!"

It's partially how this place looks like on the outside... Oh and the inside. They have all this construction going on so every time I pull up, I'm like squinting at the hours on the door trying to determine if the joint is actually open because it's looks SUPER closed not just a little closed. By the time I tentatively go in, and wander through the place I'm like, "Oh yeah. Look at all this crap! This rocks!"

I love how big this place is. They have a ton of Halloween stuff. They have napkins and table cloth in every rainbow color (and clear, silver, and black). So you're having a luau party in December? Yeah, they got your back. Need all those little toys for goodie bags for your kid's birthday? Yup, they got that too-- with candy. And Bachelorette and Bridal stuff, I can't type anymore my fingers are cramping... this place has GOT it. If they don't, my bad.

So appearances aside, go for it. Rip off the bandaid fast and make the trek to Party City because Target may be prettier, but this place has got what you really need, baby.

I have been to around a dozen BW's around the country.  This one is one of the better ones.
Steve at the bar does a great job of taking care of the customers.  Jeff the manager does an all around excellent job with both staff and the tv's.
The food has always been quick, hot, and high standard.

Took my daughter there for lunch, we have been customers for years.. Ordered clam chowder, my daughter removed, hard, fur like object from her mouth.  The waitress said the distributor was at the register and he explained it was crabmeat. REALLY??  We went to front and manager and distributor were there. I asked who puts crabmeat in clam chowder. Neither could answer.  Bothersome, that manager did not even come to the table.  We would really like to know what she put in her mouth!!!
OMFG!!  I love this place.

Goodness where should I begin.  Between the drinks, oysters, fish and overall presentation of food this place is definitely a ten.  The fried seafood is seasoned to Cajun perfection.  The must have is the chargrilled oysters.  If you've never tried oysters, this is the way to have them.  You will be forever hooked! Be careful, you might not order anything else.

I cannot say too much about The Bride Room and the lovely ladies who work there. I purchased my wedding dress, rehearsal dinner dress, and bridal luncheon dress from them as well as all my bridesmaid's dresses and the experience was spectacular. They were excellent about communicating, incredibly helpful in making decisions, and over all understood the style of my wedding and knew what would work well. They have a beautiful selection and went out of their way to bring other dresses into the store that I wanted to see. They are meticulous about their care of the dresses and accessories. I felt like they cared about my wedding and I wasn't just being pushed through the process. If you are looking for a wedding gown in Nashville I wouldn't go anywhere else!
The customer service is above and beyond. I ordered the filet mignon (medium), hands down one of the best steaks I've ever had. Served exactly as I asked and more flavorful than words can describe.
Great Mexican food very friendly staff great prices on menu large menu to choose from

Recently moved to Marana. I was referred to Kevin for gel polish. He does a exceptional job. My polish last for atleast 3 weeks with our peeling and I don't take special care. He is a hoot. I have such a fun time going there. I've had two other people do pedicures snd have been extremely happy with their service as well. Prices are very reasonable and it's worth driving across town for.

I think this place serves more than decent Thai food. Tom Kha was good enough, though I think it could be a little more sour. I was expecting more from the volcano chicken-- it should have been crispier. However, the duck curry hit the right flavors and the duck was cooked very well. Despite being picky when it comes to Thai food, I enjoyed the dinner overall. To have Asian food in this part of town is a major plus as well (I seem to seek out Asian food in New Orleans.)

The ambience is good, dimly lit, and peaceful. Yes, take your date here. The service is great. The food came out pretty fast compared to other places. 

Their menu is what would keep me coming back-- it seems to be pretty authentic and has a variety, rather than your typical pad thai and curry. I was surely eyeing down the pompano for next time. The only qualm is that it is pricy. The major dishes are around $15 each.

Slow service, waited 25 minutes for a Perrier. Got the jambalaya and it was severely under cooked. Onions and peppers were raw and the rice was hard. Fajitas were fair at best. Manager took the jambalaya off the bill but didn't offer much of an explanation. Second time there recently and both were sub par. Probably will not return. I don't recommend it.

I live a block from South Philly Taproom but more than half the time, I come here instead. The food is more vegetarian-friendly and the folks are more fun. Not nicer, but more fun. Both places have their merits and SPTR has the better beer list for sure. If you're reading this you probably spend some time in South Philly, so check both out. Lucky is maybe oriented toward a younger crowd, if that matters.

The food was wonderful. We enjoyed the complimentary ceviche limeno offered on yelp. Would definitely order it next time. The guacamole and chips were wonderful too. My husband loved his red snapper tacos. Two of us had the combo of steak, calamari, shrimp and octopus. Very tasty but the octopus was chewy. The Chile relleno  was also enjoyed 
The only negative was that it was very warm in the restaurant. Our server was very attentive and knowledgeable about the food. 
Would definitely return. Outside seating is lovely but only on a cooler night.

Saw this cute shop in my Fodors book, was really looking forward to going in. We found it today and were so excited to see so many cute dresses and accessories!! However, our excitement soon turned to annoyance as we noticed the obvious hovering of the sales lady!! Every move we made she was on our tail as if she suspected we were going to steal! Saw some nice things that we wanted to purchase, but after less than 3 minutes we decided to leave. So uncomfortable! So we went to Razzle Dazzle around the corner where they were very friendly and happily accepted our money.

My girlfriend and I stayed here June 29 and 30th. Nice place. We choose this place because our friend who was getting married over the weekend, had this hotel as one of the 3 choices to choose from for anyone wanting to stay the weekend. 

After reading the reviews, we felt we picked the right one. So the the pros and cons of the hotel. Starting with the pro's: we like the pillows. One was firm and the other is soft. The bed was is very comfy. Not to soft or firm. Just right. Nice 40 inch flat screen tv. I don't know if all the rooms come with a microwave, but ours did and we had fridge as well. 

Con's: the room is small but does serve it's purpose. The AC blows directly on you. I tried adjusting the vent, but it still blow directly down on you. There is 12 dollar a day parking fee.

Overall, I have more positive feelings of this hotel. The location is great. Close walk to state street. Right across the Santa Barbra Brewing Company. You get free breakfast every day from 7am to 10am. The staff was very friendly to us. The valet guy was nice and told me how to get to the beaches and which ones was good for surfing. 

I would stay here again. But next visit I like to try the other hotels. I'm not saying this is our go to hotel just yet, but it's close to being that.

My husband, daughter and I went on Sunday, January 14, 2018.  We arrived at 4pm to a place that had maybe 3 tables filled.  Most of the tables were empty.  The host was somewhere in the back.  Took a bit of time before we were even acknowledged.  One of the waiters that saw us come in came to greet us after he took an order from one of his tables. It was at that time that the host appeared.  He never greeted us, just looked at us and waited for us to speak. My husband asked for a booth, the host walked over to it, again not saying the least, follow me.  We proceeded to walk over, and that is when I noticed the reserved sign on the table and asked about it.  Which he responded it was reserved for 5:30pm.  At which time I said we will take a table that wasn't reserved when he responded that most of the tables were.   At this point, I'm boiling inside thinking, why didn't he tell us this at the host desk.  I told him nevermind a table and we left.    

The host is the first person in which you come in contact with, they set the mood for the restaurant. He was very rude and unfriendly. 

We have frequented Stephens many times and realized this isn't the place for us anymore. If I could not give a star, this review would be starless.

What happened to this place? Did getting a visit from Guy of DD&D go to their heads?  

I had a pastrami sandwich from Norton's about four years ago and it was good but our most recent experience here was very disappointing.  I had the classic pastrami; it's supposed to be on rye but this one was on wheat bread which imparted a weird taste; moreover, the pastrami was over-grilled.  My wife had the roast beef melt and, in her words, "Was wa-ay too salty."  

  Anyway, Three Pickles remains our favorite deli and we won't be back to Norton's.

We arrived late after attending a concert. The staff was very friendly. We've been here several times before , each time the experience was perfect. The entire crew is involved in your visit. The cooks, bartenders and manager make it a point to make contact with you. They make you feel like celebrities. The chef does an incredible job. Now we are regulars here.

Awful. Giuseppe has gotten too big for its britches. Even though they "take reservations" it's a joke on the weekends. And it's BYOB, so if you come empty-handed, expect to wait without the benefit of a barstool. food and owner's attitude have deteriorated. Should have stayed the big fish in the small pond down the street.

this place has theee best porterhouse steak ever. best steak in SB.  also ordered scallops but not all that great.  tomato basil soup very delicious.   and service was very very good. it was on high end on price but well worth it for couple on a great night out.  definitely coming back on a romantic getaway weekend vacation

Good chicken and fixins here at Willie Mae's uptown location. I didn't experience any wait or poor service, as other reviewers mentioned. I had the baked chicken and red beans. The chicken was very tasty. No lack of flavor here. The beans were good, just fine. Lunch came to around $16 with a sparkling water and tip.

Went during happy hour and had a great experience. Tried 5 or 6 different dishes, which are served as small plates for less than half their price on the dinner menu. All were excellent, but highlights were the crab bisque and chargrilled oysters. Beer and wine selections were fantastic, as was the service! One of our orders was slightly delayed, we noticed but said nothing - and unsolicited, our server brought us another dish we were discussing earlier - on the house! To sum up, a quintessential New Orleans experience: Great food, drinks, and service the way it ought to be, but rarely is these days. A great meal!

I'm a fan although I do think this place caters more to tourists. Overall the food was tasty and the wait staff were on top of it. The turtle soup wasn't as great as I had hoped, especially since its one of their specialties; a little too salty.

The biggest selling point for me was the $0.25 martini. Yes, you heard it right. $0.25 martini at the fanciest place in NOLA. We had to uber to get here because it's not at the French Quarter, and it's right across from a cemetery that I really wanted to visit but it rained that whole day. This place is super fancy so RSVP a head of time. They also enforced a dress code-no sandals, shorts or T-shirt for guys. The martini special is only for lunch on the weekday with a purchase of an entree. Luckily, they still have the special on Memorial Day and we were able to make it. 

For starter we had pork belly with foie gras. I thought it was kindna dry and nothing to ride home about. I also tried their soup1-1-1 which was a sampler of gumbo, crawfish bisque and their famous turtle soup. The turtle soup was so good but the other 2 soups weren't. I had the quail and that was delicious. The beef tenderloin my boyfriend got was a little dry and very chalky/grainy in texture. I tried my friend seafood platter and it was pretty fishy, so glad I didn't get it. The bread pudding was a little too sweet and it was just decent at most. The brownie and peanut butter cobbler was way too sweet for me and I didn't like it at all. I asked for the girliest martini they had and it was so so so strong. I could feel it after just 2 sips and gave the rest to my bf. 

Overall, this fancy place was decent. Not the best food we had in New Orleans but it was fun to experience. The service was great and the place is beautiful.

5 stars for the BEST FRIES ON THE PLANET. 
Shamefully, I haven't really eaten anything else from this spot. But I would walk out of my way, take 2 buses, and fight snow and rain to get an order of these fries. Just. Perfect.

I've heard so many good things about this place.
I had my birthday dinner there this past weekend. The service was truly terrible. Our server was arrogant and super slow. 
Onto the food. The bread was honestly some of the best Italian bread I've ever had. It would've been more enjoyable if our table had olive oil on it like the other tables did. The artichoke app was mediocre. My branzino was delicious. It was a really small portion but the taste was great. My girlfriend ordered the pasta and crab dish. There was much minimal crab and it was bland.
I won't be going back here.

Snazzy... I went here for my birthday and its sure fancy, with flavor overload... the food was very pungent, and they only give you a little food, but it is so flavorful you can't eat too much anyway. They start you with strange crackers and olives with feta, you can't really put the olives on the crackers, so its a weird combination. 
Expect to pay more for this upscale place.
The atmosphere was cool and chic.

Dear Paul,

I called to make a reservation to try out their Tuesday night deal but was transferred to an answering machine with no instructions, so I didn't know whether the reservation went through. While $30 on a Tuesday sounds like an amazing deal, cutting the portion of everything in half (or less) is not enough to satisfy a grown man. Since there were no description of the deal anywhere and no warning from the single waitperson, I fully expect bigger plates. Having only one sad little baguette as bread doesn't help either. My friend who ordered the crepe while delicious, was the size of my index finger and I have small hands. The creme brulee was good but it was thinner than an eraser. 

One waitstaff for the entire restaurant doesn't seem to be enough. There were long wait for food and service, which I suspect there's only one staff in the kitchen as well. Though the taste of the food is excellent other than the bitter greens that comes with the short rib. But still, given the portion and the slow service, I don't think I can recommend the restaurant to my friends. Jean Georges, a Michelin 3-star restaurant in NY, offers a $20+ prix fixe meal with bigger portions.

I'm sorry but I wish it was better and I wished I didn't have to go next door to buy hoagies afterwards.
Regular pizza is usually very good for some reason Sicilian pizza not as good lots of homeless people across the street be aware of your surroundings

Stopped by as we were in the area on First Friday. The location is easy to get to with street  parking, no meters. The building is nice and has a great ambience. It is dark and 'lodge' feeling. Fishing theme inside, check out a couple of the tappers. I had the IPA which was decent. I gave it 3 stars on Untapped. 

The place was busy meaning the bar was full and the tables in the back were also full. 

Nice place. Stop in for a pint or a glass of wine if you prefer. Decent prices. Barkeep was friendly.
Great hookah and its byob! Not my choice of music but I can live with it! The mango mint was amazing.. Didnt try the food though.

One word: overrated. This place has good wings. Tried the hermanaki wings and they were fine. But the service put such a bad taste in my mouth I wanted to walk out. 
We came here on a Sunday ready for a Purdue/IU rivalry game. We got here 45 minutes before the game and for us a four top for our part of 9. Luckily the table next to ours opened up and we were able to snag it. We asked the bidder if we could turn the tables and he said we could, do we did. It really did not make any difference to the aisles but a male, who I assume was a a manager, came out and very condescendingly told us we could not sit like this and we had to move the tables back. He said we were blocking the staff trying to move around. The way we were seated in no way impeded traffic compared to the way the tables were originally set up. The whole situation was annoying because there were other tables that could be moved together but because it's open seating there were 2 and 4 tops sitting there, you couldn't move them. 
The food was fine. We got buffalo dip (too much cheese, barely any chicken), wings and beer. The beer was cold and the wings were warm but when you kick off the meal with a rude manager, it dampens the rest of the experience. 
Anyways, to sum it up, GET A HOSTESS, this role is very important in a busy, full service restaurant. This will prevent groups of 2 sitting at 4 tops. And considering this is the first impression your guests see, it's really important. Maybe the managers should fix this restaurant before delving into opening a second location. No matter the location, I won't be visiting again. Best of luck, Ale Emporium with your rude staff and OVERRATED wings.

Horrible customer service, lady was rude i wouldnt even rate this a 1 star. Paid 6 dollars for a burrito that is small and not even near being good or what a actual California burrito is supposed to have in it! Im pissed. Nicos is better tasting, bigger an cheaper.

Very helpful  staff.
i am on a gluten free (wheat) diet.
I need help finding food that i can eat.
The food here is delicious..i have been here multiple times with my colleagues as it is near to my office. A must visit for good food lovers

I wouldn't say that this commissary is better or worse than the majority I've seen.  They have better prices than going off base but for very specific ingredients you won't find them here.  

On certain items you are better off hitting up a Walmart (soda/pop), or a local grocery (sometimes Tom's has some great sales on fruit and veggies that are much better than the prices the commissary offers.  You also need to watch dates on the meat, when it's out, because we've seen it where it goes bad the same day we would purchase it.

Usually we still support the commissary regardless of slightly better prices on a couple things at other places.  (Unless we need things we just can't get there such as certain spices). Generally it's a good way to get a lot of food for your money - particularly without tax.  I'd certainly recommend supporting it if you are nearby and have the option to do so.

Let's start off by saying it's easy to pass or feel lost with the construction going on. Complimentary valet parking yes!! Went inside and seated right away. Not a large crowd at all. Our table was very unique with a tree built in the center where you can write on it. It was a little cold due to it being a garage door seating?? Server was great. The alcoholic mixed drink options were poor. Appetizers were amazing and food was hot!! Entrees were also great however I felt like I had more oysters in my steam pot then any other fish. The only way you could get a crab pot is if you ordered for two. No single portion and it was $48. Overall nice atmosphere and great food!

for lunch today my job ordered adams great place !!

#tdubstl

I really enjoyed The Foodery but my one complaint was lack of a really inspired bottle selection. The Foodery seems to have the standard craft beer offerings, and a lot of them at that, but finding something unique and obscure proves to be a bit more challenging. That being said, I did end up finding a can of Mass Rising IPA and bottle of Flower Power IPA, so that was a score.

Here is my main complaint, the service here is really lacking. I tried to ask the bartender for help on finding some local IPAs and he just shrugged me off. I don't know if its lack of training on the bartenders part or if he just didn't care, but a little bit of help would have gone a long way.

Food wise, the wife and I shared a Roasted Turkey sandwich. At $11, I actually thought the sandwich was reasonably priced.

Overall, I give my experience here  a C+/B-. The lack of service was a big drawback, sadly.
Pork was ok, the chicken and the beef were great. Love the tempura shrimp asd on as well.

Just started working in Manayunk.

Goodbye, $12 fancy Center City Salads.

Hello, cheap cheesesteaks.

Did a compare/contrast between Dalessandro's and Chubby's. This place wins by a landslide. 

I much prefer the finely chopped meat and deliciously salty, melty provolone. 

Jimmy Fallon was right.

National Mechanics is by far my favorite bar in Philadelphia. I live in the Art Museum area and I would prefer to trek all the way to Old City than hang out in my own neck of the woods. Paul, Lauren, Drew and the gang ROCK, HARDCORE. Ignore that one review about Drew. I appreciate the fact that "NAT MECS" does not feel the need to have PBR to generate a crowd. Come to Mechanics if you are a beer person. Mechanics celebrates the local brews with Yards and PBC on tap. It's also a place that barely advertises and is always full at night. You can plan your whole week here! Well, I do.

Monday, when open, lunch with my old city buddies. Tuesday, if you feel up to it, karaoke night! Wednesday, hang out with John and get a team together for PUB QUIZ. Thursday, just hang the !@#$ out! Friday, sometimes SIDESHOW, most of the time, a great place to meet and hang! It's a favorite for all of the historical organizations like the National Park Service and Once Upon A Nation staff. Saturday, another hangout night if you get there a little early. The place fills up fast! Sunday, start your day with an amazing brunch menu. I am a hung fan of the french toast! Go somewhere else for the rest of the day, then come back around 9 and play Wii on the big screen! if National Mechanics opened a WAWA and a little Coffee Bar, I would not need to go anywhere else! Oh, and a little bookstore with a small selection of high-end adult magazines...hehe. In 2008, Once Upon A Nation made National Mechanics the first stop on the Tippler's Tour which runs every Thursday from April through October! Oh! I forgot to mention, the place has WI-FI!!! And it's Free!!! All you haters need to stop hatin on Nat Mecs! Some girl got her feelings hurt because Drew didn't think she was sexier than his hot, hot, hot girlfriend, so service was bad...haha! Makes "Mecs, YOURS!"

I came here for the light dinner. I ordered grilled chicken salad and it was great!!!!   Highly recommended for that light dinner.  And I saw great oysters at the bar and would like to try that sometimes.

Hooray for real spicy food! With flavor that's integrated! 

This place has the best Thai food I've had in St. Louis (at a good price for the quality, to boot). Turns out the temple is just down the street. No wonder! 

There's a pretty decent beer selection, considering that it was completely unexpected. 

The smoked ribs were so yummy. My curry was tasty, too. I had it at level 5 (the top of their typical spice chart, not the spice challenge), and it was perfect. A true five. Real spiciness. 

And I love Thai desserts! 

It's definitely worth the mini-trek from the Central West End. It puts all those Loop Thai places to shame.

Check out their pepper/herb garden in the back. They grow their own ghost peppers!

I was a regular here when I lived in New Orleans.  I frequented this location and the one on Veterans Blvd.  The food was always good.  My favorite appetizer is the crawfish egg rolls and the crab and crawfish bake. The shrimp bordelaise pasta is a tasty entree to try.  As a side dish, I usually have the macaroni and cheese wedge. For me, the desserts always steal the show. I've had the carrot cake and praline cheesecake a few times.  The service is average.  No complaints here.

I called at 9 o'clock on a Friday night and asked for carry out and it only took 10 minutes, they were very friendly when I walked in, and they both greeted me by my name and made me feel welcome. best experience I have ever had at a Pizza Hut in Castleton area. Pizza was very hot and fresh.

This review is not about accommodations at the Ramada, but about their (lack of) customer service as part of their relationship with Greenbee Parking. Greenbee markets off-airport long-term parking. My wife and I were returning around  10 p.m. Pacific from the East Coast after having traveled all day. The hotel is supposed to send a shuttle to pick up clients at the airport. We were informed by the desk clerk who answered the phone that the shuttle was busy elsewhere and that we would have to wait an hour. The hotel is about a five minute drive from the airport. I told him that was not acceptable and asked if there was anyone else available to pick us up sooner, or could we take a cab and be reimbursed. He said no. We took a cab anyway because it was already 1 a.m. on our body clocks. When we got to the hotel, I presented the cab receipt of $15 to the clerk, who said he wasn't authorized to make reimbursements. He took a copy of the receipt and my contact information and said the front office manager would call me back the next day. That never happened. I followed up twice and left the manager voice mails with no response whatsoever. The lack of followup is evidence of an extremely poor customer service attitude, which probably also extends to their hotel operation. For what it's worth, Greenbee was no better with their customer service.  No return phone calls. Very disappointing all the way around.

Really? You expected them to paint a whole room for $179 INCLUDING trim and ceiling?  

Let me know how that works out for you!  Better yet, post pictures!  I would love to see them.  

We called Just Paint to paint our kitchen and living room. 

Final cost was about $600 plus the cost of paint - which we were able to buy ourselves  - a real money saver!

And we could not be happier.  

At the same time, friends in Marlton paid over $1500 to have about the same area painted and I honestly cannot see a difference (ours might even be a little better but I don't want to tell THEM that). It's bad enough that Just Paints will see this and see how underpriced they truly are! 

This is a real paint job, with rollers and brushes and real painters that know what they are doing!   And they did well. 

Despite taking longer than expected, the owner not only honored the original quote, but then went over EVERYTHING with a fine-tooth comb!   They guys could not leave until not only WE were satisfied but until Vince - the owner - was satisfied!  (And he had them retouching things that  that I would never have noticed!!)

All Living Social deals have some fine print.  If that's your only beef, get over it.  

If however, you are looking for an excellent interior paint job at a better than fair price, with guys that arrive when they say and stay until the job is done.  AND you want to work with an owner who cares obviously and desperately that the job is done right? 

Just Paint did great for us!   We will definitely be having them back!

Food was good, authentic Mexican tacos. I would give them the 2 stars just because of the service. I get to the spot someone ask me to sit on a table.and them this guy approach to take my order no signs of being a waiter. Ok after bringing my order I ask for more pieces of lemon, he looks at me as if I was bothering or disrupting him of cleaning another table. He brings the food and no forks or nothing was bring to me, even though I was eating tacos I still needed them.
Then another guy that really looked as a waiter begin taking care of me and he was really good. The funny part is that when I stand up ready to leave this guy was eye balling me as if he was going to punch me in the face and then says good bye. Only for his service I won't go back to that place or refer any of the construction people on my project.

Always good experience here, family friendly and great service. 

The food is always fresh and if your in the mood for Italian it's not a bad choice. 

We often visit if friends or family are visiting and then like Italian. 

It's not "gourmet," but good basic Italian. 

They keep things well kept even though they've been around for a while now. 

My only complaint is that it gets too crowded sometimes!

We came on a Monday afternoon with very little traffic so our service was quick, efficient and polite. The food was good but the BBQ pulled pork was overpowered by the potato roll it was on - definitely get it on the Italian roll! Baked mac and cheese was our absolute favorite. Would definitely recommend.

Ate here for the first and last time.  Chicken dish I had was supposed to contain sundried tomatoes and artichokes, found a couple of small pieces of artichoke, tons of onions and peppers, not a sundried tomato to be found.   Every item on the menu had a complete description of what was supposed to be on it; no reason for me to expect onions and peppers.  Also, the dish wasn't very good, and waiter was nowhere to be found.  Not again!!!

Called in an order and was asked exactly how I like my Burrito,  with refined beans or black beans, rice, etc...I asked is this extra?  She said its. how it comes I also said I liked the red sauce that goes on burritos and she said, yes the chipotle sauce. We can make it Wet for you. I thanked her, but knowing that was extra. Why wouldn't you just say what requests have a secret upcharge to them. I arrived to pay for my order and it was more than I anticipated and asked why. $1.00 more for some sauce over the top. I said I didn't want to pay what I was not told about and she said she would take the charge off. Meanwhile they made me wait for them to make me another...twice I was asked to pay for their mistake...literally and figuratively. Tip to Management: Train employees to be upfront in pricing with NO secret hidden upcharges!!

Awesome service, very cool atmosphere and tons of desserts and drinks to choose from. Bailey's can easily host your  romantic evening or casual group outing. It's a lounge so don't expect pub pricing but you will not be disappointed.
Ordered some chocolate cake for dessert via takeout. My order was ready in 5 minutes and damn that is some good stuff. Yum

We stopped in to Tapped on a Saturday afternoon with relatives, and we are so thrilled to discover this little place! When you walk in, you are carded at the front and provided with a wristband that is linked to your name and credit card. There are more than 40 (local craft) beers to choose from as well as a smaller selection of wines, and everything is self pour. 

You are charged by the ounces that you pour, rather than the number of beers that you sample, so you can taste everything for a pretty affordable price. 

If you exceed 40 ounces, you will have to go back to the front and get a "refill" on your wristband. There is a selection of appetizers and wood fired pizzas, and you order everything at the counter to have delivered to your table. It was too early for dinner, but we did try the pretzels and wings. Both were good, but the wings could have done with a little less sauce. 

All in, this was a great place to take out-of-town company, and we will definitely be back for future afternoon and evening dates.

Me and my family ate here last night for Dinner and it was amazing.  We were planning on eating at a competitor restaurant but no one ever answered the phone so the young lady at the hotel front desk highly recommend this restaurant and boy did she get it right.  The atmosphere in the restaurant was bright and inviting, the staff kind and accommodating and our waitress was attentive and very knowledgeable about the menu.  I had a taste for several Jamaican classic and she recommend Jamaican me crazy which comes with Ox Tails, curry goat, (I opt for curry chicken) and jerk chicken every thing was tender flavorful and filling.  Huge portions.  We will be back.  Maybe this week

As the only place outside of CA and NY you can get Blue Bottle coffee you expect Sparkroot to deliver a really good shot of espresso. The good news is they do: I'm told every barista there received specialized training from the Blue Bottle people, and so far ever shot has been smooth, chocolate-y and awesome.

As a traditional meat eater myself I was concerned I wouldn't like any of the sandwiches either; but the Brie, walnut and apple panini concoction was really, really good.

Where do you go when your starving, hung over and need something yummy to eat while in Nashville???  The correct answer is this place!!  Don't be fearful of the odd location and weird set up. Find a parking spot and walk right in, you will not be upset. I had the BBQ sandwich with a side of Mac and cheese and French fries.  The BBQ sauce was soooo good (I asked for a spicer sauce and was given buffalo sauce and I didn't use it bc I loooooove BBQ). The Mac and cheese was 100000 times better than what I can make at home!  My husband ordered the same with a side of smoked green beans...don't pass these up. I wish I ordered them...they were by far the best green beans I have ever had. So after eating mediocre food all weekend (aside from that fried bologna sandwich I had), you need to hit this place up while in Nashville.  Nashville is known for their music not food!!!

Dong A 2 is a typical Vietnamese grocery store. The prices and cleanliness are average for this type of place, but the selection is a little lackluster. Kind of like this review. Boring, I know, but there's not much else I can say about it, really. 

If you happen to be in the area and need to hit a Vietnamese grocery store, Dong A 2 will probably suffice, unless you're looking for a specific name brand or special item. If that's the case, you will probably end up making another trip.

Really, really good food.  I've dined here 3 times and enjoyed the experience.  Out of the 3 visits one was not as exceptional as the other two visits.  However, to be fair, it was crazy busy and right before Christmas.  I've loved the food and the drinks are very, very good.  Great service at the bar from Dave!

Great place to go for dinner! The pimento beignets are delicious...and the fried green tomatoes. The hot chicken was pretty hot but our waitress Lindsey was so awesome and brought us a glass of milk. The peanut bombe was out of this world. Great service and food!

Amazing selection of beer and music every time I've been to Publiq House. It is one of the best places for live music in New Orleans outside of Frenchmen Street.

Love that they serve their beer in mason jars!

Would definitely come back a million times over.

Big V at the bar is the best. I think he has a fetish for Californians.

Anyways, I've been to the Acme on Iberville, right downtown, as well- and this place off Veteran's is a lot better, hands down. First of all, you can actually hear the people you dine with. The one downtown is too dark, and too loud, and too busy. We didn't wait long on a Sunday afternoon lunch (I came here twice, and the first time there was no wait at all).

The atmosphere is friendlier, less rushed. I enjoyed the people siting near by, very entertaining stuff goes down here. Both times I was hear, we talked with nearby table neighbors, who were nice and open and willing to share some tips on getting around and enjoying NOLA. On my second time, Big V invited me to his part of town, I think I fell in love.

It was a good way to be welcomed in NOLA, delicious oysters. If you've never had em, try the charbroiled one. They're quite heavy on cheese and fatty deliciousness, BUT you should try anyway.

We ordered a starter of the crawdaddy tails- yum.
I got a dozen oysters, and Big V gave me five extra ones. 
I also tried the spinach/oyster soup- which was too salty for my taste.
The fried oyster poboy was excellent, but I wouldn't get it again, just because the taste of the oysters really dies out once theyre fried.

Now that I've ran through all the ways you can double your cholesteral levels- enjoy.

You are very limited on good Asian markets in Reno! My Mom and I set out to find a very particular kind of cookie that only Asian markets carry. We were delighted by the size and choices this little gem had. The employees there were very welcoming and continued to ask us if we needed help finding anything. 

Great find!!!

We lived in China for a period of time, so we have developed a taste for good Chinese.  I believe that Mandarin Palace is the best Chinese in SB.  They make a variety of dishes that Americans just love and they do have an authentic Chinese menu as well.  Their dry green beans with pork are one of my favorites not to mention their basil chicken.  Hubby loves their beef noodles and Walnut Shrimp.   Their lunch special has a lot of food and main choices.  They have a chef from North China, so their authenticity & taste has improved since new ownership.

The service here is terrible . Waiting 45 minutes for chicken skewers is totally unacceptable.  It appears the kitchen staff does not know how to complete an order. Half our table got food in 10 mins and the other half waited 45 minutes.  Guess this is my first and last time!!!
Was told it would be 15 minutes for my carry out order. Took an HOUR! Never coming back!

AKA as The Grill. Locals called it Camelia's. Restaurant is a diner & very casual and inviting.  Staff are very friendly and make you feel welcomed. Food was delicious! We actually ate at this restaurant two times this weekend because we loved it so much. Things we tried:
Gumbo- best I've ever had!!!!! I went back a second time for the gumbo but unfortunately they were all out. 
Fried catfish sandwich with fries-Delicious!
Bacon burger- described as the most delicious burger EVER  (even better than Buffa's).
Mexican Omelet- Yummmmmm
Chef's special omelet - was good but a HUGE serving so make sure you split this one.
Pecan pancakes - we devoured. 
We're definitely going back!

Inventive menu of mostly small plates, but menu has changed since moving to The Gulch from former POP space in East Nashville. Sadly the menu no longer seems to have as many great vegetarian options.  Especially missed the tofu dish and salad of three gem lettuces.  New location is more LA-like upscale and tables are much closer together than before.  Noise levels are high so it's difficult to have a conversation.  Staff was not as attentive as one would expect.  Our waiter was overly dramatic and he didn't seem knowledgeable about ingredients and preparation of many of the dishes.  We still like Little Octopus, but miss the originality of the POP location.  Sadly, It seems like just another typical restaurant in The Gulch.  Too bad.
Splendid little place with a tasty selection of frozen yogurt, crepes, and there's beer! Good beer! They're very friendly as well, which is always quite nice.

I've ordered take out from here 4 times and every time something goes wrong. Food is just okay but it's close to my house so it's easy. Today I ordered, drove there, and then they called and told me I accidentally ordered from the dinner menu and they couldn't make any of the food.

My new favorite chinese take out! The owners are friendly. The restaurant is clean. The food is delicious. There isn't much more to say. If you live in South Tampa and are looking for a good NY style Chinese takeout restaurant this is it.

**I consider myself an expert. I have tried them all in South Tampa. This one easily stands out from the crowd.

Enjoy!

Good beer  but now that I can buy it elsewhere, I'll never go back to the Brugge.  The service is unbelievably horrible, probably the worst I've ever experienced.  I don't know if they didn't consider me upscale enough to be there or what but it's just not worth being snubbed to get an above average beer.

We had dinner at Brophy brother and ordered Oysters on a half shell,Oysters Rockefeller, Baked Garlic Clams and Blackened Sea Bass with coleslaw and vlam chowder. The views were beautiful,we sat at the deck which had heaters. The baked clams are to die for, the coleslaw nice and refreshing and they put poppy seed which worked well for taste. The only thing is their oysters had a metallic and strong aftertaste,we order oysters all the time so this was definitely a little off putting. Service was superb however.

Do NOT go here unless you want to spend lots of money for services, only to get it back in a state WORSE than when you put it in. I spent over 2500 to have various repairs done. They gave me my minivan back with a rattling sound. I took it back and had them check it out, to which they said it's NOT anything they did but something else that must have coincided with their repairs. They would need anther 280 to fix it. I told them the sound appeared RIGHT after I got my vehicle back from them and after spending over $2500, I expected minor issues to be addressed. They said I couldn't prove it was their repair, but they'd be willing to fix it for another 280. I told them I would not be coming back to them since this is the second such time and experience with them. Worst experience ever; but I'm new to the area so it was all I knew at the time.

I LOVE this salon- great friendly atmosphere and stylists who know what they are doing.  I have had cut, color, waxing, nails and makeup done here. Fabulous EVERY time! My daughters also had long lasting colorful streaks put in their hair that was trendy and  professional. It also didn't leave their hair damaged or faded looking afterwards. I highly recommend this salon for kids and adults - Ashley is my favorite stylist but they are all Awesome! If you are sick of overpaying and want a friendly professional place and great hair this is the place for you!

We ate at the Worker Bee Café this morning during a stop on our way from Huntington Beach to Pismo Beach.  I had searched Yelp for a breakfast place and found this gem.

What did we really appreciate about TWBC?  Not only was the food fresh and of good quality - it was made with love.  Just that little bit extra that makes you feel really satisfied.

My over-medium egg was cooked to perfection and my home fry potatoes were soooo tasty.  Hubby had the Worker's Benedict and loved it.  The hashed browns  were the best either of us has ever had.  Oh, and the coffee is EXCELLENT.

We were lucky enough to get a booth and it was large size - not a dinky squeezeintoitbutyoucan'tbreath kind of thing.

They are very busy and at least today the service was not fast.  But it was not unacceptably slow either.  

The owner is a very sweet man and his son is the chef.  We congratulate them on a job well done.  We own our own business and know it is not easy.     They have obviously found their calling.

Will make this a regular when visiting Santa Barbara. My husband and I have enjoyed this restaurant both times we've had dinner there. Great quality food, perfect portions & 
awesome service. I recommend to make a reservation though because the wait could be long.

Oh my gosh. Perfect little find tucked away and more than I ever expected!! Their sausage gravy is amazing! They dice up their jalapeños to add a little spice to your plate and it's just the magic touch!! You can sit outside and enjoy the water as the dolphins play near by, this place is a hidden gem!!

I was visiting from out of town and stopped by this place for breakfast.  The breakfast tamale was delicious and the portions here are huge.  Maybe too much food for a small bulldog like myself but I noticed they like to eat more in the Midwest.

They also had this coffee called "Big titty Blend" of which proceeds go to breast cancer research.  Being the breast connoisseur that I am, I couldn't stop looking at the coffee bag and giggling.  The kind staff finally gave me the bag for free because of my enthusiasm.  I don't live in Boise but if and when I return, I plan to pay another visit.

I'm a local. I come here as much as I could since I don't like driving. The staff are the lowest and poor customer service associates of servers and bartenders I have EVER encountered. I have been here over a dozen of times and the staff just aren't friendly. So I have resorted to take out from now on. 

When you order take out, their lines will ring and ring. When they answer they are extremely rude. So now, I resort to an outside application like Yelp or order up. 

When you go in to pick up, you need to flag down an employee. Good luck. They won't even talk to you. I give the food a 4. The staff a 0. Burgers are small. On the light side.

I have been in love with Spicey Pickle since I discovered them in their closed Sparks location. They have changed their menu a little bit over the years but overall they have remained true to their origins. Their Bandido panini is my personal favorite and their pasta salad isn't too wet, which is perfect as I've found their are some that think too much mayonnaise is just barely enough sometimes. Just popped in again after awhile and I discovered their now selling gelato and slurpees. Unsure if that's just for the summer season but I hope not. Gelato is freaking amazing. The only sad thing I can think of is that when they're busy, this particular location doesn't always have enough space. That's okay when it's warm, but in the winter I'm more likely to take my food an go instead (maybe that's part of the plan? Wouldn't blame them, it does get crazy busy during lunch hour!). Also their slurpee stand has taken a lot of room, so a few less tables now more than ever--just something to keep in mind for all of you. Overall I love the sandwiches this place has, and yes, they do sometimes have odd hours, but the food is worth it in my opinion. Will be back again!
Came for a fancy bachelorette party dinner. This place is delicious! Everything has so much flavor! Staff was great, informative and fun!

We were on the Saint Charles trolley and happen to go by seaworthy. It looked charming from the outside and so we hopped off and decided to give it a try. A very eclectic menu with a very attentive wait staff. We enjoy the ambience of the inside of the restaurant. A very unique menu that did not disappoint. Our server suggested that we begin with the pork belly. It was melt in your mouth with some nice apples and ricotta cheese. A very nice way to begin our meal. My daughter enjoyed the crayfish roll with delicious with Very light french fries. I enjoyed a new redfish dish that had just been put on the menu. Cooked to perfection it was on a bed of lentils with some collard greens. We also enjoyed some delicious roasted vegetables with our meal.  Absolutely delicious. the bar looked very charming and had many lovely looking cocktails. Settled for a glass of rose that went nicely with my meal. Would highly recommend this little gem of a restaurant!

The Good:  The food is delicious!  I ordered the Yellow Curry Lunch Special and every part of it was amazing.  I hate tofu but somehow, even though I asked for no tofu and was given it, it actually didn't taste awful, which is my usual experience.  The spring roll was perfectly crisp, and fresh tasting.  Also, the delivery person was prompt and very courteous.  I really enjoyed this experience.  

The Bad: I asked for no tofu and received some.  Admittedly, my order is often difficult for restaurants to process because I do not want meat or tofu and this seems to confuse even the best places.

UPDATE!!

They are open until 7:00 on Friday nights and from 11:00 am til 2:00pm on Saturday!!!

Yee haw!!

We bought two Groupons for a total of a three-night stay here.  When we booked, I initially had some trouble getting in contact with the manager (Barbara), but we finally connected.  I was able to book on the dates I wanted and everything - no hassle.

The day before our stay, Barbara called me and the boy toy to confirm what time we were coming in, answer our questions, etc.  She gave us some great advice (like not renting a car, based on the sites we wanted to visit).  She also told us that our first night we'd be staying in a different hotel (Hotel Olivier) since we had two different Groupons.  It was the first I'd heard of it, but we're pretty easy going and travel light so it wasn't a big deal at all.  In fact, looking back I'm actually really happy that we got to stay there because the Hotel Olivier was a super cool old hotel!

Anyway...after staying at Hotel Olivier, Barbara picked us up from the hotel, drove us to Hotel Storyville, let us put our bags in an anteroom (our room wasn't ready at the time), and told us when our room would be ready.  She had given us her cell number earlier and told us to call with any questions / problems.

During the day we called her to set up the tours we got through our Groupon and she took care of everything for us.  When we rolled in late that night, toasted from our cocktail tour (yes, I highly recommend it...through Historic Tours New Orleans, Inc.), we had to call her to let us in because we didn't know the code to the front door.  She rushed downstairs and helped us.

Our room was pretty nice.  I didn't have any problems with linens or towels or anything.  But it wasn't like 4-star quality hotel.  It was more like staying at someone else's lake house.  It was super quiet (since it's on Esplanade, north-east-ish of the French Quarter) and the neighborhood was beautiful!

Overall, I was very happy with our stay.  Barbara was AWESOME!  Seriously, so helpful and that more than made up for the hotel's lack of amenities and front door issues :)

Brenna's lived up to the hype was one of the best breakfasts you will have, while delivering old school southern charm.

The space is huge and beautiful, it feels like a museum.  Take some time to walk around, check out the courtyard. The murals on the walls were all unique and worth checking out.
