................

Meh. Mostly filled with stuff I am not going to buy. Sometimes I'll get the meat on a stick from the Asian dudes, but thats about it. I think its nice that the park offers these kinds of things though. While I may not be buying any of the things at the market I like moseying on down on a sunny Saturday.

I have been coming here for years and am shocked to see one let alone two bad reviews. The Garden consistently provides me (and legions of friends) with the look and results I want. The place is busy for a reason! People are so negative these days. I am on a mission to show praise where it is deserved.

Definitely not my favorite LA Fitness location, but it's the closest location to my office and on my way home. I don't feel super great about my vehicle being left in the parking lot and like to be aware of my surroundings when I'm walking in & out. I've also had some issues with male gym-goers wanting to be a little chattier than I'd like, which I haven't experienced at other locations around Indy.

In regards to the facility itself, the equipment is in decent shape and there's plenty to choose from. I like that there's plenty of room around the machines so you don't feel crammed in next to your neighbor (ahem, I'm looking at YOU, Glendale). I can't speak to the classes, as I haven't taken any at this location yet.

I prefer the Fishers LA Fitness, but this location is convenient. It's not horrible, just...meh.

My husband has been going to Eagle Dry Cleaners for about a year and half and as a matter of routine gets his shirts washed with starch, not dry cleaned.  Today when he went to Eagle Cleaners to pick up his order, he noticed that his bill was significantly higher than usual.  When he questioned the amount , the woman who happens to also be the owner seemed  annoyed that my husband didn't just pay the bill. She was reluctant to check it over to see if their was a mistake. As it turns out my husband was charged for the dry cleaning service, not the service he received.  Rather than apologize to him for the error, both she and her husband behaved with blatant resentment that my husband just did not pay and go? Not at all happy with the way he was treated. my husband said that he was not going to come back , to which their response was  "Good"  We would like to tell Eagle Cleaners that they are far from the only Cleaners in town and any one of the other establishments would be happy for the business that they threw away because of their totally unnecessary rudeness.
Lou the Shoe is an institution. My family has been going to him for 3 generations and his work is always reasonably priced, prompt and exceptional. I won't go to anyone else.

Awkward is the best way I can describe how the bearded bar tender made us feel. The cosmo he made was not a cosmo at all. It was some other weird concoction. My wife wanted to leave before we ordered and yet we ordered even though we had an odd feeling. 

My burger came out still bleeding (literally) red blood 
Spewing out. My wife's tuna was served so raw that when we showed it to them they apologized and commented immediately that it was like sushi. 

Apparently they have been open for a week and yet I was told they are changing names from Kingsford to Kings. Odd and awkward with bad drinks and undercooked food. Very doubtful they will be around long at all even with a prime location.

What's not to love about an airport that features live musicians? There are a ton of cute souvenir shops with local favorites like Moon Pies, moonshine and musical albums. 

Pro Tips:
- Grab an iced tea at the Orchid House and enjoy live music from a performer or two. Bring cash for tips!
- There aren't any Priority Pass lounges, so plan to hang out at one of the restaurants before your flight
Come here! The food was really good, well executed, service was great, chef/owner came out to ask how everything was.  We will be back, solid restaurant!

Finally after months of pondering and planning, we made it to Zahav for my birthday dinner, without a reservation!!!
The wait wasn't too bad. 20-25 minutes while we sipped our cocktails. 

Service was top notch. From our server to waitress and hostess, seems like everyone was a model professional. Interiors were fancy. I loved the open glass kitchen and being able to look at the chefs and other kitchen personnel in action was nice. 

The food was sumptuous. Everything we ordered was culinary gold. The Turkish hummus was like nothing I have had before. Came with bread the size of a regular naan bread. And the combination was just great. 
Duck kebab and chicken kebab were top notch. The meat was juicy and very flavorful. The fried cauliflower was also very well done. 

Can not recommend enough. Reservations go months ahead. So plan ahead. 
I would definitely be back.

This place is awesome!! I am not really an Italian food seeker or a pizza or heavy bread place seeker but this place is definitely worth eating at! The patio outside is so beautiful with lots of greenery, they had a live band, fans blowing to keep a nice breeze and the bugs off you. We went on Monday and they have early bird specials, happy hour, $4 margs and Mojitos on Mondays. We really enjoyed our time here. We did notice their mojitos were watered back which was a little disappointing. We each had 5 mojitos and it was as pretty clear they contained half the alcohol of a normal drink.

I was invited to Momiji Sushi by my good friend Frank and along with a pretty companion named Joyce,  we met there for lunch.
Momiji is a small place just off South St. We were greeted by the owner,  Ada, a petite pretty lady who welcomed us with a respectful bow at the waist and a beautiful smile. 
 While we were pondering our selections from the menu,  our server bought us out a bowl of warm and lightly salty edamame to munch on. The menu was creative and the sushi rolls had names like the Hulk roll and the Volcano roll. Of course you know I ordered the Volcano roll. For an appetizer, I ordered the vegetable tempura and for a community dish, we ordered a healthy plate of udon noodles with prime rib.
 The vegetable tempura came out first and it was cooked perfectly, with a lite, crisp batter with a nice variations of vegetables, in addition the dipping sauce was very tasty.  My volcano sushi roll came out next and it was a sight to see. It had fresh tuna wrapped in rice with crab eggs on top symbolizing the fire and a orange sauce drizzling down the sushi rolls onto the play like hot lava!  It was delicious, tender and the fish was very very fresh.
 Next came the udon noodles with the prime rib beef, and the noodles were firm and tasty, the tender beef and the accompanying sauce made this a really special dish.
Ada suggested we should try her specialty desert which was fried ice cream with bananas and whipped cream. Looking at the plate, it reminded me of all the cleavage on a Mexican cable show, I couldn't take my eyes off of it. I had a wonderful meal and a great time at Momiji.

ORDER THE BREAD STICKS! I am obsessed with them now. I wasn't planning to get some but the folks at the table next to me had a plate of them and I couldn't resist after seeing them. Super good!

Down to business - the interior is essentially the same as when the venue was under Scotty's ownership in terms of layout and decor. I'm curious to try some more of their food to compare the food to the food at Chatham's Mass Ave location. On the day I went it seemed as though not too many students were working there, I'll be interested to see if they have more students employed once they have been open more than a few weeks.

I am obsessed with the breadsticks now, but I was disappointed with my fish sandwich- I should have gotten it spicy so I will go back and give the main dishes another try - especially since I love the Mass Ave spot so much and try to get this up to five stars once they get their groove in from routine at their new location.
Great food and service! Their tiramisu is DELICIOUS. If you just go there for the desert, it's already worth it

We met JoAnna for our first time but left her class as good friends. We had so much fun learning specific techniques. I can't stress how much I appreciate her accommodating me being gluten free and vegan. She even had separate equipment. We learned so much and laughed the entire time. We didn't know what to expect but we're blown away with the entire experience. It's very personal, interactive, fun, and delicious. She is an tenacious women and it's inspiring to hear all about her career as a chef. We will be back!

We really love coming here, whether that's for dinner or brunch. We really enjoy the atmosphere with plenty of covered, outdoor, dog friendly seating, and the food is always amazing. The jerk octopus is one of my favorite starters in all of Tampa Bay, and the Gem Lettuce Salad is a must when we visit. We usually split the Spanish Tortilla and the Steak and Egg Quesadilla when we come, but they often have great specials, which can sway us. And although I eat meat, they have some great vegan options as well. I really enjoyed the Mushroom and Kale Paella they're currently offering too and the Grilled Impossible Burger is really good too!

This place is pretty damn amazing and probably one of the best burger joints in the Mission Viejo area.
The positives of this place are numerous but my favorites are the fact that this place is so unique with that pretty cool ambience. The menu is pretty diverse with good variety. The bread is made fresh and goes really well with the sauces and toppings. Our food was all good, no complaints.
The things that I think can improve is little things like adding the fries to the dish. I didn't realize that fries or chips were extra so our burgers look pretty empty on the plate. And for a handful of fries it would've been $3 extra. The burgers were in the 7-8$ range so adding fries would be a nice touch and make the presentation more complete. The place is fairly small so if you come Churing busy hours don't be surprised if there are no seats inside, and maybe even outside.
Also, for 5 dishes, we waited more than 30min. Not acceptable... 
Overall it is a good place if you're Looking to have a casual burger outing...

Have been missing Houlihan's so much !!  I saw one in the area I was driving thru and stopped for a to go order.  Everyone was very nice & friendly.  Place seemed  clean. However I got home and looked at the food I just paid $48.00 for.  Very disappointed to say the least.  I ordered the Asian chicken wraps, and received a small portion of chicken with a half a head of lettuce.  The baked potato soup was the consistency of thinned out mashed potatoes.  For the chicken fajitas half the container was full.  Also ordered the spinach artichoke dip and the container half full again. I can understand now why so many have closed.  Sad to say this will probably be my last trip to Houlihan's.  Please see pictures posted...

Amazing decor, I love what they have done with the place. This is definitely the place to be on Tuesdays. They have amazing specials, $2 tacos and $5 margs. 

I think the food is very average but worth it for the specials. Regular priced food definitely not worth the price. Their guacamole is really good and has a little spice to it, which I really like.  I would definitely go here on a Friday night instead of Kilroys, simply because I love Margs, but again nothing to rave about, drinks are definitely made with a mix, but still tastes good. Service is a little slow for drinks when we went, but it was still new so I will cut them some slack since they had opened the week before. 

I have heard great things about the frozen and specialty drinks.

one of my favorite spots in Santa Barbara.  came here years ago for dinner and I remember the tasty cioppino.  Came here to day for take out.  they have outdoor seating and was extremely busy.  didnt see cioppino on the take out menu, but got fish and chips on the go.
the fries were super crispy and warm and delicious.  the fish was crispy and the batter was not thick at all. lots of fish, so tasty! the sauces were amazing.  came with Cole slaw with poppy seeds in them, adding to a different kind of crunch.
great views, good food.

I would say a very solid start for such a new brewery! All of the beer if very "drinkable", but they haven't quite nailed any of their beers...yet! Remember this is a very new brewery, so I would say give them a year and they could have some really good beers. The lightest beer "burn the villiage down" is smooth and would be great on a hot day. The scottish ale is probably the best beer they have and it is yummy. They still need work on the IPAs and Stouts however.
Service is always very quick, staff is extremely friendly, and restaurant is clean. My daughter absolutely loves the cupcake pancakes. Thank you IHOP! Keep doing a great job!

It's wine tasting inside of the mall!!!! 
- that's it. That's the review. I choose all of the sweet flavor offered. Our server said that the flavors do change. I recommend taking advantage of the winery and madam Tussaud's combo ticket for a cut and fun date night.

Omg. this place is a nightmare. I placed a To Go Order. The girl I spoke to literally had no idea what she was doing and had to place me on hold multiple times. Maybe train your staff? Of course, when I got home I realized the order was completely wrong. I didn't feel like calling to complain because I noticed the receipt was not right either which means the girl I spoke to put the order in wrong. Shocking. The people who work the front desk are ruder then the day is long and its just.... no.

Very trustworthy, honest shop. The check engine light in my 1999 Jeep was on, and I thought I was looking at major repairs. Also requested they service my transmission and check my brakes. At a dealer that is a green light for them to charge big $$$. These guys told me neither my brakes nor transmission needed service. They found the problem with the check engine light and fixed it for $225. What I thought would be a major bill was actually minor. Give these guys a try - they won't take advantage of you.

This place is a nightmare. They literally put me on hold for 22 minutes, and then closed down while I was on hold, cutting my call off. This was 48 hours after they were supposed to call in the refill of my meds, and didn't. They didn't call them in the next day. I've been waiting up all night to get the nonscheduled, non-narcotic medication that allows me to function for the third day in a row. They told me if the medication they gave me didn't work, I was out of luck, because they weren't trying anything else. There is not a single Doctor in this building. The Nurse Practitioners will present themselves as Doctors, and will not bother to correct you.  The staff is rude, they do not care about the patients. Every place around will refer you to them. I would sooner go to the vet.
Horrible, first of all the bartenders don't know the difference between a real and fake ID. The price doesn't equal quality. Go somewhere else it's honestly bad.

When I arrived, the waiting room was empty, and no one was at the sign in window. I waited for quite some time for someone to show up. The woman who came to the window was a bit rude and seemed generally irritated that I was there. The phlebotomist was pleasant enough, which almost made me rate it two stars. The most upsetting part is that LabCorp performed (and charged me for) tests that were NOT ordered and then failed to send those results to my physician. I had to go to LabCorp because my schedule would not permit me to have my blood drawn at my physician's office. From now on, I will have to call off work if I need blood work done. I will absolutely never be going back to LabCorp.

I'm always down to explore new places in indy and this coffee shop has all the industrial vibes that I love. It's pretty spacious with lots of seating but I would highly suggest getting here early because it gets packed fast. It's a good place to hang with friends or even study. I see lot of college students which is probably because of IUPUI and it's part of an apartment complex.

Good ole Grotto's. Born and raised in Wilm but live down in Texas now, Grotto's is always a go-to when I'm back home. Especially during NFL season, usually always place my bets here! And as any true Delawarean will tell you, Grotto's is as DE as it gets. Always love the crowds up there, great place to watch a game.

Located off a not very busy road is this absolute gem. My girlfriend and I stumbled across this place on complete accident and without doing any research. We came completely underdressed but were still greeted cordially and seated right away. Hummus and bread were brought out right away and was just perfect in whetting our appetites. Our waiter was knowledgable of the menu and answered all of our questions. I ended up ordering the special which was a lobster asparagus pasta. It was unbelievably decadent and flavorful. My girlfriend had the mussels and we were blown away by the balance of flavors between the white wine, prosciutto, fennel, and mussels. She couldn't help but soak up all the delicious sauce with the bread we had left. This place is perfect for a date night or just a casual night out!
Great people and service!  They not only helped me with my current issue but took on finding out why my second car still did not have plates.  amazing service that goes beyond measure.
It's a great place if you're in a rush and don't want to spend a crazy amount of money. I love it here!

Order ahead for Thanksgiving.  Then you go and they say we don't have yours.  The racks have bread, but we don't have yours.  Just put rolls from the racks in the bag and substitute the large loaf with a different one.  Say our mistake Andy all is fine.  Nope.  Not that easy.  They were ready to turn me away with nothing.  Even the best falls from the top. Never to rise again.  Like that ?  Bread is good service well, I will go to a different location from now on.

I have Celiac and finding gluten free products is not always easy, these guys have a great assortment of GF products and their wine selection is surprisingly awesome. There are always some great deals. They also have great deals on plants.

Great food, service is spectacular. Great wide open layout in a great part of Reno. I would say though, don't show up on a Friday night if you are looking to eat and talk during dinner. On Friday they usually have a band that plays and it gets too loud to talk in the restaurant. It's one thing to go if you know the band and are expecting that but it's really frustrating to show up to a spot to spend money and you can't hear anything aside from music.

Why didn't I take heed of the Yelp reviews I read before renting a property through Coastal Hideaways? I hope you do! First home was inhabitable, major roof leak that had gone on for months and was rented to us despite this fact. Second home was given in a location we did not want: Pool and spa inoperable. Fence falling down. Thick layer of dog fur on bed covers. Such filth, it goes beyond description. Rats ate through our food on kitchen counters. Rat feces under, on and even within the bed sheets. Dirtiest home I've ever encountered. Family of ten had to leave for a day for the pest control company and one maid. House still below third word country motel standards after the second cleaning.

And even after all of this, it took a month to get back our security deposit, after we were told a certain check number was sent, and only after threatening to report our experience to the Better Business Bureau. Funny thing is: the check we finally did receive was of a lesser number than the one that was "lost".

I really like this restaurant! It had been a while since I've been to Fuji, but the redecorated restaurant is beautiful. They have great deals on sushi on Mondays and Tuesdays where you can get 1/2 priced rolls. I have also gotten various teriyaki and tempura meals here and they were all delicious. There service is quick and the atmosphere is pleasant. I definitely recommend it!

I absolutely love this place! So many options to choose from depending on your dietary needs. 

I love the seasonal bowl, really tasty! They also have a great selection of smoothies and juices. Healthy healthy!!!! 

The atmosphere is fun and engaging, very clean "green" feeling.

A very nice outdoor atmosphere in Ybor. Went there for dinner early on a Friday evening, and on recommendation from our server, I had the Rum Runner Mahi Mahi, which was delicious. The sauce is light and creamy and the sliced bananas were a surprisingly tasty addition. The dish was served with black beans and (a lot of) rice.

I also had the black bean soup, which was good (but I think mine is actually a lot better).  On a prior visit, I had the Cuban Roast Pork, which was pretty good as well.

Its a great mall. Although Pandora is not all that great. Their product is overpriced for the poor quality of jewelery they sell. I have had my bracelet for less than a year and have been back twice for a broken charm and a broken and lost clip. They replaced the first one after 2 months of waiting for the okay to do so. and when I went to see about replacing the clip they said they do not cover the clip which is one of the most important parts of the bracelet so it does not stretch. The manager Michelle was very unprofessional and the girl who was with her accused me of being a lier I had the reception to prove we had bought the charm and and had the bracelet with Me with me missing clip. They would only replace it when it was a defect on Pandora. And when the guy who took the receipt. Gave me the wrong clip. Apparently they are all idiots there. They will not go above and beyond to make the customer happy and they don't know the difference between flowers and sand dollars. Needless to say I will not be returning there and Pandora all together has lost my business. Corporate office will be hearing from me.
Best lunch in downtown. Great sandwiches and even better soups. You must try Thursday's beer cheese soup and BBQ sandwich. Simply amazing.

I love me some Becks. Very friendly, funny and fast service. Good vibe from the regulars. Good juke box, or just good old rando Pandora. Sports on the TV, trivia night on Wednesday, open Mic comedy on Thursday. It is great unless someone like 'Matt B" (bogus name) comes in and is exceedingly rude and disrespectful and thinks they own the place.
Pretty simple: clean, comfortable & great staff. Very close to my place of work when in Philly and my preferred hotel to stay at.

Absolutely delicious! Had the pulled pork platter with Mac and cheese and the blues corn. My boyfriend had the brisket sandwich with pork and beans. 

Excellent food and service. Great ambiance. Just a heads up, it gets busy during peak hours. Will definitely be back.
Great service, great burgers with a simple menu. Small order of fries can easily feed two. Pricey for a burger, but worth the treat every once in a while, definitely not something to have every day.

I have not been to this particular store in quite awhile. They have a lot of new stuff, really cool things I need, want , must have. Cool novelty item stocking stuffers for the kids too.
I will be back after Christmas when its not so busy to get more , more , more STUFF.

Inside and out the place is fantastic.  I love love love these guys.

I find what I want and they are always eager to find what I am looking for.

You guys are awesome and I am glad you are here!

The food and drinks were good for the most part (breadsticks were kind of hard and cold). My sangria was delish! I ordered the garlic rosemary chicken for my entree and it was garlicky goodness. Chicken was cooked well and was not dry. My husband had the stuffed chicken marsala, which he liked very much also.

Service and food were a little slow, but our server was very friendly and it was not her fault (hopefully) that the food took so long to come out. So overall, not a bad experience and we were not in a rush that night.

I don't like ice cream but this place is delicious. I had a scoop of Ferrero Rocher. The Caramel is amazing as well. I could stare at their display cases for a while so pretty! 
Staff is very nice so we'll be back soon.
I've been going to this salon for a year now. I won't go anywhere else! Christopher is awesome, and everyone is so nice there. I highly recommend this salon!!! Love this place:)

Renting at the piazza - Their slogan is that it's not about living, it's about lifestyle. If you like fire alarms going off several times a week in the middle of the night, rent here. If you like piss poor communications and response from the management staff and maintenance staff, rent here. If you like walking past trash scattered all over the parking lot from the dumpster they put right in front, rent here.

I know this amazing business through my Dad who has taken his vehicles here for a while. Richard and his crew should be known for their great and honest work. My check engine light came on in my car last week and it took one phone call to get the car in, diagnosed and fixed within 2 hours. He also quoted the price and final price fell within the number quoted. I cannot tell you what peace of mind I have now that my only car is running much better and it didn't break the bank. Thanks guys so much!!!!

The is one of the top Dive Bars in the city...Good bartenders, cheap drinks, red heat lamps beaming rays of warmth on what has to be the lowest ceiling of any bar in the city. Its great! Dont eat the food, its terrible. little peices of hotdogs cut up in the jambalaya, or kraft singles with a slice of ham on white bread. I havent seen food out in the last 10 times Ive gone.

The have two jukeboxes that primarily play country music, so if your looking for your Johnny Cash fixture this is it. Its open 24 hours a day, and gets a ride range of characters. 



Theres a pool table in the back as well.

The product made me fall in love all over again.  It's was simple, but nearly perfect.  I added my little touch by punching four holes to loop through a tulle-like ribbon.  
The card stock came in this pearl color and it looked amazing and feels great.  The sample on line did not do it justice.  I'm just glad the invitations were just as I pictured, but even better.  

The only downfall are the envelopes.  They are pretty cheap and flimsy, but it'll do the job.  I didn't pay extra to upgrade any inner linings.  I was able to live without it...
Excellent customer service.

Wine tasting in 90 degree weather while listening to Jazz is how I spent most of my day on July 3rd.

This is a really nice winery with a great product and knowledgeable staff.  They made me and my family feel not only welcome, but right at home.

$2 dollars to sample seven of their wines from a list of about 20.  A bargain, especially in these hard economic times.

When in Indianapolis, do as the Romans do...  Wine taste at Easley.

SO DELICIOUS.

I was visiting my fiance in philly and he wanted to take me to Dim Sum Garden. I am so glad he did!The pork soup dumplings is a must!! We also had the pork noodles and the mapo tofu. I don't like food that is too salty or sweet and I thought these two dishes were full of flavor but not too much. I enjoyed my meal so much that we came back two days later!
AMAZING SUSHI! The fish is so fresh but even better they use very little rice! They nailed it from great service to the freshest fish!!

I get that this place has a whole history to it, so I felt compelled to ty it as a tourist (also had to try Pat's). I liked the fries here but preferred the cheesesteak from Pat's.  The fries were thinner and crispier at Geno's which I preferred. I went at an off hour so there wasn't a line, but I definitely wouldn't wait in a long line for this food. It doesn't taste any different than other cheesesteaks I've tried before.

Great experience! We just had a birthday party for our 3 year old two weeks ago.  They exceeded our expectations in how they handle our little ones event. Our party host Julian was very tentative in made sure everything ran smooth. Large variety of food to choose from for the party and plenty of features to keep all the little ones busy. Everyone had a great time and will certainly be back in the future. Thanks!

Le Cafe Creperie was a nice place to find in the Cherry Hill area.  My dude and I stopped in there for dinner after some shopping last weekend and had a decent experience there. 

Although we enjoyed our crepes, I wasn't convinced of how the meal was going to be after having a cup of the french onion soup to start: the flavor was missing. My definition of a great bowl of french onion has a thicker broth, bountiful croutons and a great application of cheese, so, I was not super excited about something that tasted more like a packet of Lipton's. It was really weak, but I ate it because I hadn't eaten since my earlier lunchtime at work. This could use some work. It was at this time that my dude was presented a fountain Coke consisting of 75% ice. 

But then things got kind of great! Our crepes showed up and they were quite good. I ordered the spinach and mushroom and was glad that I did. The crepe was a great texture, the veggies were fresh, and I love the drizzle of cheese on top! My boyfriend ordered the veggie. His dish tasted completely different than mine, but it was still really good; these two crepes alone qualifies this as a great spot for vegetarians, in my opinion. 

My dude ordered a deal from the menu that included one sweet and one savory crepe. When his sweet crepe arrived, between the two of us, it lasted on our table for under five minutes: that was fantastic! We ordered something with bananas in it...that's how little memory I have of this thing, but it was one of the best desert crepes I've ever had. I'd definitely return to have this again.

The bill: we were super happy to discover a 25% off yelp coupon upon check in. Thanks, Le Cafe Creperie! It took way too long for the server to collect our payment, but that was the only time the service was a little off -- I swear that I'm not a huge service snob, but it took 25 minutes for us to pay our bill.  Prior to this, our orders were taken very quickly and our waitress was pretty on top of things. 

Overall, everything was swell and I will most likely return again to form a more solid opinion of everything.
The food is excellent, and the service is even better! As others have stated it is a higher end restaurant and the price reflects that, but it's absolutely worth it.

This Kaldi's location sometimes makes me question whether I've stepped inside a day care center that's run amuck. Coffee houses are there to unwind study, relax, and concentrate....on BS, but not there to be barraged by a score of screaming kids running around the place aimlessly out of control. Unfortunately, being in Kirkwood comes with the territory, and this downtown location caters more to the family demographic which is perfectly fine; just that it kind of interferes with the vibe of enjoying a coffeehouse. Ordering was a challenge amidst the constant whine of kids in the background. (ok by now, you can tell that I am not a fan of kids lol). The tea selection here is great though, I love how they prepare it. The inside is stellar. I just was pretty annoyed of having the tea in middle of a Kindergarten setting....can you say HEADACHE! I had to double check my laptop chord was not going to trip up these kids who were running around the store for no reason. Lesson learned..NEVER leave the city limits again.

This is a great new place downtown to check out. Tons of beers of draft (since they make them there) and some killer food. Make sure to try the breadsticks with beer cheese, huge wings and I heard the burger is good as well. Very industrial decor makes for a cool atmosphere and they have a large private room in the back for small events or birthdays (it had its own bar!)

This place has wonderful food. Teriyaki chicken and beef served with steamed veggies and steamed rice: a classic combo that they do well. They even have a spicy variety. Service was great and the cashier/server was very enthusiastic and friendly. Prices are acceptable and the restaurant itself was clean and pleasant. If you want a quick and quality teriyaki bowl and you are in the area don't shy away from this place.
I said I would come down after I returned from Puerto Rico and try the food that my friend Shana recommended, all I can say is I will be back.

Following my initial review of Ezra's, I've gone back twice to check out other popular dishes (can't stop, won't stop). The classic buddha bowl and the nacho mama bean bowl (how fun is that name?) are 5 star worthy!

The buddha bowl features falafels (never had them before) and the BEST kale I have EVER eaten. Local honey spice kale. I could eat it every day. A heaping bowl of greens and healthy veggies for $12.

The nacho mama bean bowl is served with warm quinoa and pinto beans atop local greens. Again, addicting. I ate it rather quickly because I couldn't get over how delicious it was.

Service both times has been quick and friendly!

Other notes:
*nice sized, clean bathroom
*free filtered water
*grab 'n go options available in the fridge (Mondays are grab 'n go only)
*delicious assortment of raw/vegan "baked" goods and treats
*don't forget to tip if you pay with cash!

Maybe it's me or maybe it's not But I just didn't find this place very memorable. The food was fine and the service was good. Big servings for those who care. But all in all probably would've driven out of my way to find better Greek food.
The service was good and atmosphere was laid back. The fried pickles were a nice starter. Standard diner fare for options and quality.

This is a must for vegetarians and vegans.

Great food, desserts, and juices.

Staff is very friendly, and service is fast

I have been to this place many times, in fact I use to come here regularly. Sadly over the last few years the quality of food has decreased. The food they currently serve looks meager (while more pricier as well) compared to other Sang Kee places.

My windows and screens look like new!

Very friendly, quick response, email reminders, conciseness staff....I highly recommend this company.

I would have loved to eat outside but it's just too darn hot right now! We came for brunch. Service was great and so was the food. It was a little warm inside, even in the basement, where we were seated. Maybe just due to the extreme temperatures. We will be back though for happy hour and other menu items.

neat place. Not much on "ambience". But the food.....

My brother and I stopped in for a drink and some apps. The Louisiana popcorn (breaded crawfish) and the breaded pickles were fantastic.  It was wings night - both the voodoo and the honey habanero were outstanding. Can only give three stars because i haven't had the main courses yet - but I'll definitely be back to give it a shot. So far so good. Really nice beer selection as well.

Maybe if I wish hard enough, PizzaRev will open a location in Dallas. I came here while visiting Nashville and I am in love with this place. The level of care that the employees took to not contaminate my food with gluten was literally the best I've ever seen at any place where people prepare the food in front of you. I was super impressed. Besides that, my pizza was delicious and I got to have vegan cheese without being charged extra! Places that can cater to the people with super specific diets are the best. This place is the best. Come here to eat. The beer taps were really cool too because you can pour your own and there are so many options! I don't drink beer so I didn't try it myself, but my dad had a great time pretending to be a bartender.

Martins is a great southern style bbq restaurant. It's the best bbq joint I've been to in Nashville. I came here with 4 people and ordered the big daddy sampler which was more than enough for us all. The ribs fall off the bone and the chicken is amazing. The atmosphere of the place was very good and had a very country feel to it. Ive been defeated two times by the end of the meal  Definitely suggest this place to anyone in  Nashville especially if you are on holiday from up north and want to try out an authentic southern restaurant this is the place for you.

The best place for food in North Wales or Montgomeryville. Excellent food. Try the Bahn Mi pork sliders and wings. They are amazing. I've never had such fancy Vietnamese food preparation. A great place for a business lunch or date

It was such a lovely night last Thursday so we decided to go back to the Blue Moon.  MUCH better experience than last time!!  Our server, Tracy, was awesome.  She smiled, was engaging and accommodating, and she introduced herself as soon as she came to our table.

We started with cocktails.  My boyfriend really liked the Port O' Call because it wasn't overly sweet.  We had the coconut shrimp app.  Tasty, but overpriced at $9 for 4 butterfly cut shrimp.  Next we tried the wings.  Another customer highly recommended them stating that they are the best in Nashville.  We completely disagree.  We ordered them extra crispy but still came out with slimy skin.  The ginger sauce is terrible too. Then my boyfriend got one under-cooked.  Sent them back, but Tracy returned with excuses from the kitchen.  We could care less what the kitchen had to say about it.  We didn't like them end of the story.   The wings should have been promptly removed from our check.  I shouldn't have had to ask to have them taken off the bill at the end of the night.

Next we ordered the catfish basket with extra hush puppies, subbed mac n cheese for fries, and added broccoli.  Catfish filets were cooked very well...crispy outside and moist inside.  Mac n cheese was pretty good, but the broccoli was fantastic.  Cooked perfectly and nice and garlicy.  The extra hush puppies came out about 8 minutes earlier than our dinner though.

Lastly, we ordered 2 desserts to go.  Some chocolate cake thingy and key lime pie.  The chocolate cake was huge and tasty.  The key lime pie was a tiny slice that Blue Moon should be embarrassed to serve for $6.  We both laughed when we opened the container at home.

Overall a good experience.  Hang on to Tracy.  Now we know what not to order next time.

Peche is definitely the best new seafood restaurant in New Orleans. I went a few weeks ago and sat at the oyster bar, which was a fantastic experience. For an appetizer we had a mix of Louisiana and Apalachicola oysters served on the half shell and shucked before our very eyes. The guys at the bar were entertaining and friendly. For an entrée I had Pompano, and it was certainly the best Pompano I have ever had. It was one of the best fish dishes I've ever had growing up in New Orleans. I can't wait to return to this restaurant, and I recommend it to both tourists and locals to experience excellent seafood expertly prepared!

AMAZEBALLS!!!!!  Yummy pizza place near the beach!  It has a nice bar area and there seems to be live music outside frequently when we go.  I love it bc they offer gluten free pizza crust and it tastes great.  So my boyfriend can get what he likes and I can get what I need!  My boyfriend said they have great garlic knots.... sadly those were not GF :(
we enjoyed our food, the server was professional, the atmosphere delightful.

I don't know what is more disappointing, the sub-par food at Geno's or the fact that the Food Network and Travel Channel keep airing the "rivalry" between Geno's and Pat's. 
Too bad I noticed the signage after ordering my food, otherwise I would have walked away.  Call me fussy, but I really don't like to be yelled at while ordering my food, and having food shoved in my hand.  Sorry, I didn't brush up on my Geno's "lingo" and I said my order all wrong...I should be publicly flogged for that transgression.
Keep your politics to yourself, and just be polite to your customers.  Funny, how something so fundamental is missing at this tourist trap!
If you are really looking for a good sandwich try SOS (Subs on South), plus they will "happily take your order in any language."

Where do I start with this location? 

I'm visiting my parents from out of town and our Red Robin is good.

I will start with it took our waiter, Mike, 10-15 min to come over to even greet us to get waters, by the time he did come over we had already made up our minds on what to order as well. We ordered our food and I got a spicy sombrero salad no tomatoes dressing on the side and a grilled chicken kids meal with a salad. We waited for our food for 25-30 min and I saw 2 other parties receive their orders before us and we ordered salads with chicken... Come on! I honestly blame the server he was horrible. Not personable, when we asked about our food he blamed the kitchen and chicken not being cooked all the way through. Just horrible service. Disappointed!

WHAT A WONDERFUL STORE!

i can't express how amazing this store is. located near the french market in the french quarter is this very lovely boutique. when i walked in, i was immediately greeted by two young gentlemen. i have to say, i was immediately drawn by their accessory collection. i was so impressed by all the unique, one of a kind pieces! all at a very affordable price. i was able to chat with the employees and learned that they hand pick their selection at trade shows and local artists which allows them to sell their accessories at such low prices. 

seriously, i wanted everything. i even told him i wanted everything! i ended up purchasing two necklaces, one ring and some john lennon inspired sunglasses for just $20! how can you not say no to this deal? 

i highly recommend this boutique! if only i lived in the area, it would definitely be one of my top favorite spots. thanks gnome! if i'm ever in the area again, i will definitely stop by again and raid the place of your accessories!

This is a solid 3 star mall. If KOP is the gold standard 5 then this is 3.

Some decent stores, some decent looking woman and not to mention a Nordstrom Rack that just opened. You'll appreciate this mall if you're used to places like Neshaminy or Exton Mall. But this mall can get boring pretty quick. Not too much window shopping.

Honey has great flavor combinations, service, and plate presentations. The entire menu is set up as "small plates" that are meant to be shared. The portion sizes are large appetizer size. Depending on how hungry you are - each person at the table should order 1 - 3 plates. The servers will pair the food choices in an order that brings out the best in the flavors - the result is like getting a 7 course meal. The menus change with the seasons although the ribs are a mainstay and are the only item that has been on the menu since Honey opened 6 years ago.

Ryan and crew put on an awesome brew-vent, called "The Cellar Thief" The team was welcoming and had great beer and food for the event. Great place to hang out with friends and enjoy great beer and food.
Have just been for drinks. Very enjoyable. Food looks greeat, as customers were very happy too
Super tasty smoothie for a long drive - a little whey, lots of juice and veggie options. Fast, friendly service, and a very clean place. Love!

This place is pretty cool. Staff was helpful and courteous.  You have to have a sense of humor and patience.  TIP: get the clues and use them wisely!  I would do this again and would recommend this to anyone who to flex your brain and have a great time with friends.  I would definitely not do this with family!
This place is legendary. Fantastic hamburger. Great atmosphere. Be ready to wait however.

I went to this chili's yesterday for dinner and Marcus was our server. One of the worst servers I have ever had. Very unknowledgable and completely unprofessional. We sat at our table for a good 15 minutes before he even came over and took our drink order. Marcus couldn't tell us the drink specials and when he asked for our ids he looked at my friends id and said "oh okay you're 22" her birth year is 1992 I don't see how you get 22 out of that and when he asked my boyfriend for his id he looked at the date and said "I don't know that date" and proceeded to serve him alcohol anyways. After 25 minutes of sitting there with no drinks or anything he finally brings out my boyfriends drinks. We sat at the table waiting for a good 40 minutes and my friend and I still had no drinks so I got up and asked the manager to seat us somewhere else. We then sat with a server with dreads who was slightly better but we still had no drinks for a good hour. We were at the restaurant for a total of 2 hours when every other time I've been to this location or any chili's for that matter we're done and out the door within 30-45 minutes. The manager came to talk to us at the end of our meal and asked what all happened and then told us they were having trouble with this server. We received no apology and he didn't offer us any kind of compensation or anything. I've worked at a restaurant so I know at what point you are supposed to greet your table and have drinks at the table and when a server screws up we always offered to comp something off the bill or offered a free dessert. Absolutely horrible customer service.

I love getting waxed here, the staff is very professional. The staff and management are very accommodating and understanding. I find it very easy to get in and plenty of appointments available. I find the pricing to be reasonable and the payment plans are very helpful when selecting a package. Keely & Teja are a joy to talk to while you're waiting. They are very professional they are great ladies and make the atmosphere very friendly and comfortable. Lora does my waxing and she is amazing. Always checking in to make sure the wax is the right temperature and to make sure that you're comfortable. They have a great team there and I recommend anyone to try it out you will have a great experience.
We always enjoy Bonefish. The food is very good for a chain-type of restaurant. The drinks are good and the waitstaff always seems to know what they are doing.

We stopped in here on a Monday evening.  In know I'm in the minority, but I liked the Korean food here when it was Sushi Boat - it wasn't fancy, but it was authentic, and similar to stuff I had growing up; think more like at home cooking than restaurant food.

Changes seem pretty limited - looks like they're not using the old sushi counter, which had one of those conveyor belt boat systems, though it's still just sitting there on one side of the restaurant, taking up probably 20 to 25% of the floor space of the front of the house.  Sushi Boat had a small bar on the left when you came in, though it looked like it was more storage than a bar.  Rolls and Spicy have renovated this area slightly, and turned it into the sushi bar, with a half-dozen bar stools or so.  The rest of the space is the same as before, with maybe ten booths, and a few free standing tables.  

I ordered the seafood soft tofu stew (soondubu chigae), which is one of my favorite Korean dishes, and an order of hamachi since I wanted to try out the sushi.  The GF ordered some rolls.  The a la carte prices seemed dirt cheap for the sushi - nigiri was $2 or $3 for two pieces, and rolls started at $3 for things like a California roll or spicy crab, on up to around $8 for a caterpillar roll.

They had one waitress working the front of the house, and we saw a guy running around, helping out a bit here and there.  We started wondering if they were the only staff working, but we eventually did notice someone wandering around in the back - not sure if they may have had more staff hidden in the kitchen, but I doubt it.  The tables that were cluttered when we came in remained cluttered, as they didn't have the time (or perhaps the organization) to bus the tables.

My tofu stew came out, and I waited for a bit, thinking the sushi would be coming soon.  After a few minutes, the GF told me to go ahead and eat before my food went cold.  During the wait, I had been looking at my food (which came out in a standard little stone bowl), wondering if they had heard that I'd ordered the seafood version of the soondubu chigae, as I was only seeing a few scraps in it - at most Korean restaurants, you'll have some clams, a shrimp or two, and other random seafood, that you might have to pick through a bit - think like a cioppino.  While I found a few pieces of clam meat, it seemed to have come from one of those bags of mixed frozen seafood, and there might have been one, maybe two, tablespoons worth of seafood in the whole thing.  Then I tasted  the broth, which had a promising bright red color to it.  I was surprised that it had almost no flavor whatsoever, and almost no kick what-so-ever.  Bizarre.  Overall, the chigae basically seemed like it had been thrown together in five minutes, with no simmering, no making a good stock/broth ahead of time, etc.

Even more surprising was that while I was eating, the sushi was nowhere to be seen - another group or two came in (in addition to those that had come in previously), and it became obvious that tables were becoming restless - we overhead comments from other tables such as "I think they're having to kill the pig . . . " and muttered complaints as one table that came in later got banchan (Korean "appetizers") before the other table had even ordered.  I heard/saw the waitress comp the Sapporo the table that came in right after us ordered as they were having to wait so long (they didn't have any food, and they'd probably been waiting 20 or 30 minutes).  That seemed like a good gesture, except they didn't comp any other tables as far as I could tell.  As I'm finishing, the waitress comes over and says "Sorry - we've started your sushi now", with an awkward smile on her face and no explanation for the disjointed service.  At this point, it was obvious she had no experience as a waitress, and her limited English skills were such that we didn't press for an explanation.  The fact that the guy we had seen helping out front earlier left the kitchen and was now working behind the sushi bar seems to suggest he may have been trying to run the back of the house all alone.

We ended up getting the rolls and the nigiri to go, and basically got what we paid for - sushi was like what you might get at a grocery store.  GF mentioned that if she didn't have to wait, it could be okay togo, as it's so cheap.

I still want to give this place another shot, as I've heard decent things from people who've gone when no one else is there; not that that's a glowing endorsement, but I definitely crave Korean food occasionally.

As an aside, I have no idea who did their web page, but obviously not someone who's culturally sensitive.  The link to the Japanese menu at http://rollsandspicy.com/reno-nv-japanese-food-and-sushi.htm, reads "Click here to view our Rolls & Spicy Jap Menu".  In additional to the racial slur, the link is broken.

Overall, inexperienced restaurant owners/staff, uber-slow service, mediocre food, but cheap, serviceable sushi

What's not to like?  Nothing like this in Chestnut Hill; a great addition.  Very cosy with an adventurous bistro menu.  Could maybe use a few more wine glass pours, but what they had was solid.  Wonderful, small bar and attentive staff.  Me like.

My newest lil hangout and breakfast joint on the weekends. It gets wildly crowded and there is often a line out the door, but I totally get why. They serve La Colombe coffee and a plethora of super delicious baked goods, as well as sammies, soups, salad and a daily homemade quiche!  It's hipster, cozy and everyone who I've encountered here is super nice. Looking forward to becoming a regular.

I recently moved to Philly and was looking for an awesome lady tattooer to supplement the work I get done at Cirque du Rouge in DC. I looked through a bazillion portfolios and decided to give this shop a try. They set me up with Tina, based on the fact that I really like American Traditional style stuff. Man, was I happy they did. I have to say that I almost never get this lucky out of the gate, but Tina is a keeper. She is super amazing and talented and a perfectionist, which I appreciate since this stuff is going on my body forever. 

I've had several pieces done by her and am planning on a leg sleeve in the near future. The shop is clean, everyone is super friendly, and I highly recommend giving them a shot. Ask for Tina de Carlo!

We had heard and read so much about this place, and had seen the most recent Zagat ratings for food and service, and so were prepared to be wowed.  But no, that did not happen.  

Instead, we left shaking our heads in wonderment about how many better meals we had had during our nine days in Louisiana and how much we had just paid for a very so-so meal at Brigstens.

The service is wonderful. But the food was not. It was not bad, mind you, but my Gulf fish special was very dry. My mother-in-law's paneed rabbit was dry and was encrusted in a rather thick crust that didn't do much for any of us.  My wife enjoyed the rabbit appetizer in creole mustard sauce.  

All in all, a disappointing experience.

We're getting nice weather, so the itch to get some cigars was overwhelming.  So, the beautiful wife and I finally ventured to Hill Cigar Co.  And I'm ecstatic that we did!

As others have stated, Hill Cigar Co. is a very friendly and welcoming place.  You very much get the sense that you're more than a sale -- you're instantly a valued customer.  Great vibe.

They have an excellent selection of cigars at expected prices.  And best of all was them having my favorite "casual" stick (Zino Classic No. 8).

It's been about 30 minutes since I was there and I'm already looking forward to going back.

(extra bonus: their business card is a faux matchbook)

Terrible service. My wife, daughter and I went their for brunch time meal. We were first seated in a corner table next to the kitchen and the restroom even though there were other same size tables that were free. When we asked to switch, the waiter said we can't do that. When we offered to wait for a better located table, he tells us that we'll get the same table! Frustrated we asked to talk to the manager, but she wouldn't come to meet us. We decided to leave for another cafe where we had a great friendly service and a savory meal. We ate at many restaurants in New Orleans and eat out a lot across the US. Stanley was the worst customer service in our experience.

Coffee taste so gross here . They got my Order wrong and it was so bad I had to throw it out. Save yourself from going to this location they have workers that are not all there and do not care about the customer . Do not go here.

Excellent food! The owner Chris is so welcoming and funny. We went at an unusual time so we had the place to ourselves. This gave us an opportunity to talk with Chris and find out more about the food. She makes the pirogues herself and they are wonderful and authentic tasting. Not the pastry like pirogues that other places serve. Oh and bring your pooch if you want to sit outside. Chris loves them all!

The food gets 5 stars. I enjoyed the food. The temperature of the restaurant gets 0 stars. I swear it was about 85+ degrees in there tonight, no joke. The kitchen/grill is open to the bar and restaurant, but I have been to other restaurants with the same concept and they were still able to maintain the restaurant at room temperature. It was really disappointing because the food itself was delicious, but it was so hot inside and everyone at my table and around us was sweating/trying to fan themselves with napkins...it was very hard to enjoy. It was my birthday dinner, I picked this restaurant because I heard it was good, but I will probably only return in the fall or winter because of this issue. :(

Filling the void of the reviled (or beloved, depending on your perspective) "Breezer" on 96th street, we now have a small chain winery / restaurant concept out of neighboring Illinois. Remodeling (and expanding) the old space, Cooper's Hawk is a modern twist of dark wood, mood lighting and darkly dressed, knowledgeable servers.

We tried CH the night before Thanksgiving and were really pleased. The bar was full, with new patrons grabbing up the self seat high tops and booths and chatting up a storm in their slick surroundings. We opted for the dining room for a litle more quiet and were not disapointed. Our server was amazing. Incredibly knowledgable about the menu, the history of the restaurant / winery, the wine and the beer. He gave suggestions, came and went on a cadence that was neither intrusive nor too fleeting and promptly brought the bill when my jet lag began to set in.

The menu is steaks, burgers, salads and some fish. They run a scratch kitchen - everything is made fresh, down to the dressings. We tried the burgers and they were great. They do those yummy little fried onion curls as one of your toppings which both dresses up your little friend and tastes delish. Nearby I saw steaks and fish being consumed post haste and everyone looked happy.

CH produces their own wines and interestingly has a barrel wine that is never bottled. You can see the barrel when you walk past the kitchen where they will happily pour you a sample if you want to try before you buy. In the entry area is an actual wine bar for tastings and a storefront where you can puchase bottles and assorted wine trinkets if you have stockings to fill. It fits in and doesn't feel too commercial or cheesy. They did it right.

The apple tart dessert is made fresh so you'll wait for it, but its good. Overall, great experience for a restaurant that's only been open for about 3 weeks now. If they are working out any bugs, you sure can't tell.

I went here for lunch around 10:30 this morning and ordered a breakfast plate. A coworker who went with me comes here all the time, first time I've been. He ordered a baked potato with chicken on it, looked delicious, and got it in 10 minutes. I waited 30 minutes and then got up to request a refund because our lunch break was over and I could definitely tell they forgot to make my order. I suppose I should have given them 1 star but they processed my refund without any resistance in understanding, and they tried to make it right but I simply could not wait around any longer especially since I didn't even smell anything cooking from the nearby kitchen. What I can't understand is it was not busy at all when I was there, there was a couple moments it was just me in the dining area, waiting for waffles and eggs to be cooked should not be long of a wait at all. 

I'll come back, someday, but not anytime soon. Their menu did have some delicious offerings I want to try.

What can be better than to have a pint while playing w/ lil' plastic toys that came from those bubble cup dispensers? 

This family tied "rebel rebel yell" dive flavor is what not only makes South St. "SOUTH STREET!" but it's a well known establishment to most of the Philly residents etc. 

You won't find a group of servers more scurvy and unique, much like the illustrations of oddities that deck the exterior of this hodgepodge collage paradise. (That goes for the patrons too)

Many walks of life take shape here daily and it's good to have a mix up from the norm. Even if you just stumble in alone your bound not to be bored and can write down some "Bohemian Dreams" of sorts in your poetry journal. Heck, ya might make a friend who'll ask, 

"So whatcha writing? I'm an artist too!" 
Aren't we all Hemingway? Skip that guy, you can do better. The one over there... He has that "Hunter S. Thompson" sophisticato mystique that you need in your bed tonight lady. Errr... I mean to write poetry of course, of course. 

*RECORD SCRATCH* 

Oh, oh... Ya he's wearing a pink fedora hat. Ya... sorry.

A.D.D. BUTTON!

Tuesday tacos is the best! Try a medley of all their different beefs and yes there's veggie too Vegan Girl...

Oh that makes so much sense! Of course! How stupid of me? Right? Right? Goodnight folks.

I have tried this place on three occasions, the first was on valentines day 2013 a few years back they were running a good special at the time. We had a BBQ Pizza, and also tried their dessert which was a heath bar slice of pie. 

The interior of the place is really fancy, from the outside you would never think it would look the way it does on on inside. 

The BBQ Pizza was delicious it comes out on a fancy tray and is decorated nicely. It had a lot of flavor and after a slice I was already full. The Heath slice of pie was surprisingly really good as well, it had drizzle on the plate they brought it out on.

Since that visit we have been there once more and got take-out recently. both of those times were very good as well.

The only downside to this place is that they are a bit more expensive than other places. 

If you are looking for a new pizza place go ahead and give this a try for yourself.

I was already nervous about a tanning salon from all the horror stories online. I did my research and went to this place since it had the highest ratings. I sincerely wish I hadn't. Today was my second visit, and it will be my last. They currently have a 3 free services going on right now that was never offered to me. I was under the impression the only way to try their services was to sign up for a membership (which I will be immediately canceling tomorrow once they open). The time I went in I tried the hydration station, and the massage bed, and I went on one tanning session on level one for 8 minutes (since I'm fairly pale). While the massage bed was interesting, after I got out of the hydration station I had to sit down for a good 5-10 minutes because I felt like I was going to pass out. I was in that room for a good 50 minutes and no one bothered to check on me. The tanning session was weird, the bed was greasy and smelled really bad. However I went a second time, today, thinking okay maybe it was just a bad day for them. I did all of the same services and a spray tan, and again I felt like I was going to pass out after the hydration station. However I did level 1 for 11 minutes today after the woman at the front desk insisted I wouldn't burn. I told her I burned easily, and that the woman before her just wanted me to stay at eight or nine minutes so I wouldn't burn. But nevertheless she continued to insist 11 minutes. No surprise I'm red as a lobster, and in so much pain I can barely move. The spray tan? I don't know if its because I'm already burned, but it's orange and looks bad, fake bad, and it's extremely streaky and patchy. I even added the extra PH she suggested! My boyfriend noticed it as soon as I got home and I hadn't even said a word about going to him. I can't believe I let them talk me into to this! I wish my money could be refunded to me, and I hope to god they let me cancel this outrageous membership.

I am going to preface this review by saying that I have been there once. I am not a local, it could have been an off day, it could have just been me. I'm just saying... I've definitely experienced better.

   I ordered the shrimp poboy. The bread was stellar! The tomatoes were lower quality than I expected, but I can get over that. What I can not get over, however, is the shrimp. Underneath the breading, I discovered that not only were my shrimp not cleaned (i.e. intestinal tract removed), they weren't even peeled. Someone just dunked them in breading and fried them up... gross. I made it a few bites into the sandwich before I realized it, and after I did, I made a meal of my bread while my husband ate his roast beef poboy without complaint. 
   I wish I had ordered anything other than the shrimp... this place definitely has some fans and I feel like I missed out. Hubby said his wasn't anything to write home about and so we won't be returning on our next visit. Too many other places to give this one a second try...

I had a great experience at Philly Bridal. In fact, I plan on returning and buying my dress there later this week. 

I had first been to this store about 2 years ago with a girlfriend. I remember how beautiful the dresses were then, and it was one of the first places that came to my mind when I started thinking about dresses when I got engaged this year. 

There was a good selection of choices, but not to the point where it was overwhelming. My consultant, Michele, was wonderful. She was candid, friendly, and gave helpful suggestion throughout the session.

While there were a selection of higher cost dresses, like beaded Lazaro dresses, I was most surprised by that they also offered other quality dresses at more affordable prices. I do not think that you can top this value.

By the end of my appointment, I knew this would be the last wedding dress store that I would be going to. I cannot wait to go back there and finalize the dress of my dreams.

Ever since I moved from California to Philly, I've been searching for a place like this! My "go-to"  salad place was Pluto's in Cali. Although Sweet Green isn't identical Pluto's, the greens available and signature salads are incredible and by far have more variety than Pluto's. I walked for the first time a bit overwhelmed and the guy making the salads was incredibly helpful. He suggested his favorites and answered some of my questions. I ended up choosing the Guacamole Greens Salad. He was super helfpful and the salad was delicious. I also like that they ask whether you want "light," "medium," or "heavy" dressing. Medium was just perfect for me. He told me to take a menu home so that I can plan ahead for my next visit--I definitely did and will come back! Glad they opened this up near the Jefferson University area..it was a great addition!

This is a great place to start a night. It's HUGE, filled with people and yes, is basically a lump of tourists... but get a hurricane, sit by the flaming fountain, enjoy the company of your friends and get ready to have a great night.

Yuck!
Sorry I hardly ever give one star reviews but this place is not worth going to.

Food was disgusting salsa was like marinara, the chilaquiles were the most disgusting thing I had ever had.  The green sauce was so not okay.
Our server commented on how old I look(btw I am 27) and how my friend looked immature.  Great job server
The alcohol was no bueno
Shrimp was overly peppered and gross.

Everything was bad so no this is just not the place.  We will not visit again.

My suggestion to the owner one have servers who actually know the dishes and can recommend.  Also make sure your servers don't tell you about what they dislike and how they don't eat there.
2. Make a cocktail that doesn't just taste like syrup
3. It's Tucson and Oro Valley so make sure if you are going to do Mexican to do it well.

If you guys want good Mexican this is not the place.

Male Bartenders were super rude and arrogant, terrible service. I waited at the bar and tried to signal the bartender for a drink and he put his hand up to wait and kept chatting with his co-worker. 

Then after 5 mins I signaled the other bartender, he approached he seemed annoyed that I was there asking for a soda while i waited............. he said I couldn't get a free refill because I wasn't ordering food or alcohol with it.  Maybe he was concerned about his tip percentage. 

I came in to meet a female friend (date) and I left with her as soon as she showed up Only thing good is the Decor...

I will never return...

Just sat down at this restaurant and saw a mouse run across the dining area. This place is one of the worse restaurants I've been to. 1. They do not accommodate parties larger than six. 2. They do not substitute sides, so if you don't want fries you're stuck with them. 3. I stood in line OUTSIDE for 45 minutes (one of the shortest waits I've had at this place). I am so done with this restaurant!

First time here. The ambience was dated and very un-Carmel. Well worn linoleum and basic tables and chairs with upholstered seats (must be hard to clean.) 

So I am here a little late in lunch hour and there are still a few people waiting. The owner and one team member getting everything together and they are a little backed up so I have to wait about 5 minutes to put in my order which is no problem.

Everything looks fresh and I got the gyro meal (fries and drink). Decided against the Greek salad since I saw it was mostly iceberg lettuce. 

The gyro and fry with drink special was about $10 and change. Served in styrofoam containers which is fine since there was so much meat that I would take it to go anyway. The gyro itself I thought was a little salty as if there was some seasoning added to the meat. The tatziki sauce (the highlight) was nice and tasty with fresh cucumber (like an Indian raita) and not super heavy like in some places. I could have used more considering the amount of meat. The fries-pretty American- and not too salty which was refreshing as the soda. Good thing the soda had free refills since The meal was making me especially thirsty. 

Service was friendly and food above average. I might come back and try something different next time like spanakopita or falafel.

I've never been thrilled with the place, but it offers a good fall back if the place you wanted to go to was closed/packed, you cant figure out where to go on a date, you need to entertain a friend in town, etc...

But I'll never go out of my way to get here.  In by opinion, your better off going to Monks/Devils Alley/Belgian Cafe/that beer place in old city for beer, a friends house for wine, and mercato or de brunos for cheese...

My friend and I stayed here three nights with our daughters: my six month old and her 16 year old. On one morning I requested that the sheets be changed on one of the beds; I stripped the sheets and left them for housekeeping. To our surprise: the sheets were taken but not replaced, we were left no clean towels, trash wasn't collected, and the room wasn't turned over upon our return. When I called and asked for bed linens, I was referred to a manager who offered a free night adjustment to our bill. Because we paid through a third party, this wasn't possible. So, in lieu of a free night, she offered us free snacks. We thought this might be fair as it added convenience to grab a drink on our way out for the day. However, the following day my friend went to get 2 waters and was asked to pay. When she told the lady at the front desk about the offer of free snacks, she was made to wait as the front desk attempted to reach the manager. When the manager was unavailable, the front desk told her to go ahead and take the waters. Later, I called to find out what the deal was and the front desk informed me that the manager called back and said the free snacks were only for one evening. Now, I am surprised to learn that they charged my credit card for the so called "free snacks" that they offered us. Poor communication, poor management, poor housekeeping, mediocre and small rooms: I would not recommend this particular Holiday Inn Express as It doesn't live up to the brand's reputation. There are so many better options in Nashville.

For our FIRST time here the 6 of us on Mother's Day,our dinner came out COLD. 40 minutes after ordering our food. When it was sent back from the second floor there was a wait of 18 Minutes. Then the 2 lobster tails (my wife) have received came out as 1 . Again down stairs 2nd time. I was disappointed here. Our hostess was so apologetic to the 6 of us. With that being said about Christine our hostess, she tried so hard to please us all. The manager has made a management  decision, and complimented our entire dinner. Now that decision has made me and our family willing to give Maggie's Waterfront another try. We will see?? G.Opperman
Or was amazing! Super helpful. My iPad is just like new. The button didn't work, the screen was shot. He sent it in to sodder it back together. I'm so stoked! Thanks Or!!!

The entrance is a bit odd.  You enter the building on the far right but once inside you must walk to the far left cutting directly through the dance/floor and dining room area passing a dividing wall and again to the right to get to the bar area. There is no podium or host area and at first glance it feels a bit stark and screams average south side bar.  Let me assure you that this lack of feng shui aside, it's the food that brings me back each time.  
    The wings are meaty and large and each flavor is unique. Try the Irish whiskey glaze or spicy honey mustard. The blue cheese is homemade and delicious.  The fries can be ordered "loaded" with bacon and cheese or regular.  The reuben, fish and chips and cheese curds are all very good. In fact, there hasn't been one item I have not thoroughly enjoyed. My suggestion is to not expect to feel cozy here, but the food and staff will certainly make up for the lack of decor or atmosphere.
Great local coffee shop with fast service.  Super clean and reasonable prices with good hours...open at 6am.

Fat Dans was quite tasty. I had the wings with teriyaki sauce and my gf had the pulled pork sandwich with the hot BBQ sauce. The toys are delicious and the waters were ice cold. The decor reminds me of an old, yet modern, pub in Chicago with the place decked out in Cubs memorabilia. Definitely will be back again to try some of the other delicious options.

Mama Lu and Madam Lu (on State St) are owned by the same lady.  The former, however, has a bigger authentic menu selection as it also serves Taiwanese snack.  I was a little disappointed after browsing through the menu.  Everything was entree size and quite pricey.  It would have been better to half the price and the serving size, afterall, this is snack food.  

This is far from the best Chinese food I have ever had, but for Santa Barbara, this was adequately satisfying.  

Complementary peanuts and broccoli stem salad.  The peanuts were simply fried and served with a generous pinch of salt.  The marinated broccoli stem salad embodied the Chinese spirit of not wasting any food.  The outer tough layer of the broccoli stem was removed and the remaining tender heart was thinly sliced and marinated in salt, vinegar, garlic, and chili oil.  The result was a refreshing health treat from something that most people simply throw in the trash.    

Taiwanese fried chicken came out really hot and lightly dusted with 5 spice salt.  It could use more basil and a crispier coating.

Xiang La fish was crispy fried fish sauteed with dried chili pepper, scallions, and garlic.  The little flavored crunchy bits were even better than the fish.    

Zha Jiang Mian.  Mama Lu's version consisted of small cubes pork and shrimp in a fermented bean sauce, a greasy and homey concoction.  

The Chinese restaurants here are not doing themselves any favors by not translate their authentic menu.  This limits their food to only people who can read Chinese and excludes people with adventurous palate (more accurately, collectors of dining experience) or Chinese American kids who can't read Chinese, but still crave some nice home cooking.  I have included pictures of their authentic menu and I would be happy to help anyone with questions.  Lastly, don't get crappy buffet and complain that Mama Lu sucks because buffet is not representative of what they do.

I agree with every review. I wish one star was an option.  We rented a 1 br at 13th and Walnut for a year and from the start there were problems. Moving in is horrendous 
(there is nowhere to park).  There were several issues with the bathroom and the heat. We moved out after a year (would have left sooner if there wasn't a fee) AND HAVE NOT RECEIVED OUR SECURITY DEPOSIT!!! They lied saying they mailed it twice. Unbelievable! DO NOT RENT FROM THIS COMPANY! THEY WILL STEAL YOUR MONEY!!!
Amazing!!!!!! Our group had a blast!!! Everyone needs to experience an escape room at least once and the great escape room in Tampa is the best!!! Andrew made our night unforgettable!!! Loved it!

For a DIVE BAR.... this place RULES in many way!   You wanna have fun in a clean, funky place with PUNK playing and children running around.   This is is.   It's better than I'm making it sound!     Killer dive bar with many extra details that set this place apart!  Trust me.  it's worth a visit!

I'm not a regular at this or any McDonald's but my experience at this particular one was great when I stopped by to get a famous Shamrock shake. The drive through line was short, the service was prompt and the shake was delicious so no complaints from this guy about the experience!

Great drunk food and they are open late.  It's not the best but it is filling.  The owner was very nice.  They were able to make the food very quickly so there was little or no wait.  The place seems like college hangout.

My husband and I were really craving some Mexican cuisine. We haven't had any since moving to New Orleans and we had our favorite restaurant in the last city we lived in so its always hard trying to find a place as good as your last favorite. 
This is only about 13 minutes from our house so we decided to try it and we were not disappointed. It was so good.
I ordered the burrito loco and so did my husband, it was a little spicy but I enjoy spicy food. They also had a special 2 for 7$ margs, they were small but I'm not complaining.
Overall, it's just really messy, cheesy, warm Mexican food that is so tasty and sinful. Next time I have a craving I will come back here. 
The prices were also fair, most dinner entrees are under 10$ and I had lunch the next day as well! Service was a little slow but they were somewhat busy and I'm not in a hurry.

If you're in the area give it a try!

Interesting that they have a drive-thru.

Good, decent-priced sushi. Edamame was a little dry and oversalted but other than that, no complaints. Service was quick. They have your typical sushi rolls as well as some creative ones. It took a while to go through the menu though.

Well, we tried to eat dinner here tonight but despite the posted hours online AND on the door they aren't open until 7.  

Not impressed at all and will probably not even try the place despite it being around the corner from our house.

This is a great airport, easy in easy out, ample parking. There are several electrical plug outlets all over the place (very important for us business travelers).

Getting through TSA is easy and the terminal is very clean.

RUN AWAY AS FAST AS YOU CAN!!
 If I could I would give 0 stars as well. This is a very dishonest owner and so are his employees. From the lease agent to the manager to the maintenance guy. We have had nothing but problems since we have lived here. And yes...cock roaches is one!

I come here all the time and really try my best to like it, and usually chose to come here because they accept credit cards, and have a wider menu than just pho and summer rolls.  Usually other people on my party are not all into pho like I am and could seriously eat it five nights a week! 
Alas, the bris métis always too fatty and I end up getting. Rid of most of it on a separate plate away from my broth and the summer rolls have the scallion too thick in it...I still prefer pho ha and am finally expanding my horizons and moving up Washington avenue to try some other locations.
