I went to Rinse on a whim and got an appointment with Michelle. She was so nice and gave me the best haircut I have ever gotten! I have never written a review but had to for her and this salon.  I get so many compliments on my bangs and haircut.  I'm moving but will have to come back to Philadelphia just to see Michelle.

I want to like this place, after all it's across the street from my friend's market. But where do I start? No literally, where do I start? As soon as you walk in, it's the dining room. You have to track past all the diners to get to the ordering station (on the right) and cashier (on the left). After gazing around and seeing a few people just standing around, I had ask if anyone is in line. Luckily they all ordered already and so I ordered and then did a 180 to the cashier to pay. Sounds confusing? Sure is. Good news is the tacos are bomb! Bad news is, goddamn it's pricey for this neighborhood. South Reno, I'd expect to pay $2 for a original style taco but in this end of town, a lot of other joints got tacos for $1 to $1.75 at most. Would I come here again? Yeah when I'm visiting my friend but I won't go out of my way or I'll hit up the drive through so I don't have to deal with the cluster fish in the dining room.

This place is a dump.  Last visit ever.  Took 26 minutes to get my order and 5 more to get sauce!  Disgusting garbage all over the floor behind the counter.  No one in the restaurant because they were smarter than me and ditched the line.
Been coming here for years. Close and easy! Try not to go on weekend or evenings though cause it gets crazy busy.

Can't say enough good things about this place.   Some of the best Pad Thai in town.   The beef melts in your mouth.   Hint: skip the lunch portion and order off the regular menu.   You can thank me later.

This is the bar of which Yogi Berra said, it's so popular that nobody goes there. Fun but long waits. Better to go north across the parking lot to Palm Pavilion or to the original Frenchy's or Frenchy's Saltwater Cafe.

The Blue Willow is a pleasant and bustling little establishment with an original take on traditional meals. My family went for breakfast because we've heard wonderful things and read great reviews. We waited for about 30 minutes then were sat inside. I ordered the Eggs Benedict, a staple in my breakfast repertoire, my husband ordered the Blue Willow Special and we ordered our son the fruit crepes. I was disappointed with my eggs Benedict because the wheat muffin was an overpowering flavor against the eggs and ham, and instead of a traditional Hollandaise sauce, the Blue Willow's sauce is a combination cheese sauce sprinkled with what I think was cayenne as it was spicy, although not that spicy so maybe paprika. I loved the potatoes though except for the sampling of burnt ones. My husbands meal was very good though. I loved the combination of eggs, shredded chicken, green chilis and cheese. The green chilis were plentiful and gave the dish a burst of southwest flavor. The kids crepes were great. It was one crepe filled and covered with fresh diced fruit, with a dollop of whipped cream and a sprinkle of cinnamon. I was really impressed. 

The staff was very friendly and our waitress was cheerful, helpful and attentive. The staff wasn't made up of young kids, so the level of courtesy and eptitude was wonderful and refreshing. 

We will go back, although I will not be ordering the Eggs Benedict again.

Not a good experience at all. My daughter were sitting at the table for over 25 min before I got tired of it and ask to bring us coffee. Poor service. 
Also, we were sitting next to the bathroom and it smelled. I asked hostess to resit us. I told her where we were sitting and she said no. There were some empty tables, restaurant was not fully sitter. Bad service

If you have travelled the world and stayed at other Hyatts you will find this is the worst one. Having been spoiled and had learned to trust the Hyatt name I was utterly disappointed by this experience. You can probably do better at the Holiday Inn
While the history and atmosphere of this Tucson landmark is fascinating, the service and food are mediocre.

I've been counting down to the opening of this 13th street addition for months. I easily made OpenTable reservations for last Thursday - just over a week after the grand opening. We were promptly seated on the first floor. I love the decor - the open air, the tin roof and unique wall paintings. 

Our waitress introduced herself and asked about drinks. We had questions about a couple cocktail ingredients and she had to go back to the bartender to answer what they were. IMO, at a minimum, the waitstaff should know all of the ingredients listed on the menu. My friend and I both got the dirty margarita - yum. 

We were ready to order and wanted to start with one of the cheese plates. The waitress told us when we ordered that they didn't have cheese that night. "No cheese" is my biggest nightmare. I understand but wish she said that up front before I was salivating over said cheese. 

Okay, now for the good part - we both ordered the pork shank and a couple sides to share (haricot verts and the fancy fries). The pork is out of this world. So tender, falling off the bone, perfectly salty and seasoned. I've been dreaming about it since. We had the beignets for dessert which were also lovely. 

I will definitely be back to Maison, but hope the waitstaff is a bit more prepared next time.

My wife and I stumbled on Clementines by accident a few years ago.  Since then if we're anywhere within a few hours we'll detour just to eat here!  Food is great, portions are big enough to share. It's a trip down memory lane, just like grandmas cooking,  Did I mention the pie?

I came here because we were told this place is good....yeah well don't waste your time it is overrated.  The crew was super nice and friendly the ambiance is very nice but yeah the Philly cheesesteak with provolone was nothing to write home about.  That meat needs to be seasoned and maybe, just maybe, it will be raised a couple stars with me.  

Maybe there is another Philly cheesesteak spot that is more bomb.  But I will say that Paesano's is the bomb! Try that place!!

Meh. We've had better meals at different Carrabbas. 

The service was fine, and I must say that they have some very attractive servers here--male and female. 

Our soups were as usual, but our salads were bland. It just felt like it was missing something compared to our usual location is St. Pete. 

The entrees were usually good. The standouts were the steak marsala, chicken parmesan, and chicken Bryan. They were all as good as usual. The menu items that were not so good were the lasagna (kept falling apart, no cheese), the cavatappi dish (can't remember the name, was tossed in oil and has very little flavor), and the tag pic pac (not flavorful, but was less salty than usual. We've had all of these at our usual location (minus the cavatappi dish), and they were all better there than here. 

Our post meal coffee and dessert were good, but it was slightly unprofessional (in my opinion) how they had three Nespresso machines on the server island. When we ordered espresso, we watched them pop a Nespresso pod into the machine and let it brew. It tasted good, but I was picturing something more...classy. They could have at least kept the machines in the kitchen. 

With the food being either average or sub par, and this place being further than our usual location (a guest was staying at the Holiday Inn nearby), we won't be back.

The experience exceeded our expectations even after reading the positive reviews! A friendly staff awaits from the front door to behind the bar. We had late reservations due to limited availability so we decided to roll the dice and arrive early to enjoy the bar with the hopes that maybe a table would open up early. The bar experience was awesome thanks to a blood orange margarita for me and a spicy cucumber 'rita for my wife. Both were incredible! We were enjoying our time at the bar, picking the bartenders brain and inquiring about how he creates such a delicious cocktail that we were sad when a table did open up for us 45 minutes prior to our reso! We sat regardless...the food and atmosphere were incredible. From Pork Cheek Tacos, to Bacon Guac (OMG) to some duck fat tamale, a brisket nacho-like platter and a pork carnitas we certainly sampled the clever menu! Not to worry, my son was on hand to help plow through all of this. Best part...the bill was at/about $100! A bargain! Can't wait to return! Gracias to the Lolita staff! A great night for my family!

I was extremely hesitant to visit Premium Steap after reading such mixed reviews. However, after being released from work early on Friday and suffering from a sore throat all week, I decided to venture in in search of a tea based relief. Unlike many of the reviewers on Yelp I was quickly assisted by a very friendly young salesperson. I told her my favorite flavors and she guided me through a multitude of selections. I emerged with gratitude and a bag full of delicious, organic, reasonably priced tea. 

I can attest that the Spicy Chai steeped in coconut water then mixed with coconut milk and cacao was not only heavenly, but has eased my throat pain.

Double win!

I can't wait to sip on more of these marvelous infusions throughout the summer!

I have to admit every flavor of this gelatunious gelato of sorts is packing some serious punch of YUM! I also love their selections ranging from the normal you'd expect from vanilla to chocolate and cherry etc. but then we move into some more exotic flavors like "pineapple-mango- hazelnut" (actually I don't think they have that but you get the idea) and last but not least "Russian-barfight-rasberry" (which I know they don't have) but again you can combine and create some interesting flavor combinations with some seasonal treats as well...

This time of year being PUMPKIN! which is out of this world and doesn't have that spicy kick which most pumpkin stuff like lattes etc. have. 

Always great service, interesting novelty Euro-brand items to look but if you can afford thirty dollar biscottis and a jar of six dollar peanut butter (which I hear is amazing) well by all means stock up...

...and that brings me to my only issue with this place. Price. A little over four dollars gets you a small cup of two fair scoops of their mouth-watering ambrosia cream. Mind you, it is partly worth it and I'm glad you get a toothpick for a spoon b/c if I had a regular cereal-sized one I'd be finished in two bites. 

Though if you want medium or a larger one go for it because the pricing is much like the movie theatre scheme of ".50 more gets you a jumbo size". Though the large cup sizes aren't that big but if you are a Parisian... you're used to a kid's cup being large. 

Sadly, us Americans have been poisoned by the "Bigger is Better!" lifestyle from our food, drink to cars and accessories of useless junk. So Capogiro is a reminder of the "small things" in life. It's a relaxing treat, yes it might be a bit pricy but it sure beats out Mr. Frostee or a Crappachino from a certain mutated double-tailed Mermaid.

I had a taste for pizza, my friend wanted fish; I wanted simple & casual, my friend wanted something a little nicer. With Napolese, both of our needs were met, and bellies were full! 

It's a nice dimly lit intimate setting, almost too intimate. The tables are pretty close, but it worked. There are plenty of options to choose from for all appetites. We enjoyed our wine & cocktails and complimentary olives, then we opted for the fire roasted shrimp appetizer served with cheese covered focaccia bread, and the Roasted Salmon Pizza. Everything was absolutely delicious, and the service was terrific.
We loved our bbq pork and smoked turkey. Place was crowded, but we got a table quickly and the food was out fast. Definitely plan to go back.

There is a covered outdoor theatre in Hawrelak park that hosts this summer festival of plays, that seems to run for 5 weeks.  This year it was Caesar and the Tempest.  We saw the Tempest.  Professional acting and costumes.  Decent set.  Good humour.  Runs for about an hour and a half, but there is an intermission.  They have a concession that serves drinks including alcohol.  A good night out on a summers eve.  Prices are reasonable at around $25 but less on Tuesdays and Saturday matinee.  Word is out however, so parking was full on Tues and the covered seating overflowed into the grass.  Evening plays start at 8pm so you may need a jacket or umbrella to get back to your car.

Southern Thrift is an overwhelmingly large thrift store - too much for me to look through everything in one trip.  All of the furniture is at the front of the store, and included some tables, chairs and sofas ($30-$130) of varying attractiveness.  Some of these items were missing knobs or wearing through (and were priced accordingly), while others actually looked presentable.  

They also have the usual thrift store hodgepodge of framed prints, plates, cups, toys, books, and random junk.  But to the right of the register you can find some kitchen appliances, phones, keyboards, and mouses, that might be useful.   Of all the thrift stores on Charlotte Pike, Southern Thrift came closest to meeting my expectations: a big no-frills store lit by fluorescent lights ,with few treasures and a bunch of stuff that nobody wants, all at very low prices.  

Tip: The "vintage" rack to the front left of the women's clothing section has a much better treasure to trash ratio than the rest of the clothing racks.

The order for pick up took one and a half hours. I get it - they were swamped and understaffed and we chose to wait. But nothing was done to make up for the wait - no free egg roll or soda. And to top it off, I ordered Moo Shoo but was given something else - no plum sauce, no pancakes just chicken and vegetables in a nondescript sauce with white rice. No mustard or soy sauce in the bag for egg rolls. No apology. On the plus side, my husband enjoyed his shrimp lo mein. I have been going here since I was a kid but it will be years before I go again.

Jim's didnt live up to the hype I recieved about it by any stretch of the imagination. Perhaps it is the regional food/flavor seperation or what have you, but I was far from impressed with what was said to be the best cheesesteak in Philly.

Went there with 2 colleagues because the sign said they had pumpkin beer and I love pumpkin!  Apparently, the sign lists all the beers they have year round, it's not a menu.  what?!  Anyway, no pumpkin beer for me.  The food was pretty uneventful.  I had a salad with grilled chicken.  It was fine, nothing to write home about.  I would not return to this restaurant and I wouldn't recommend it to you either.  There has to be something more delicious waiting for you in Indy?  Let's hope.
Very accommodating and great food and drinks! Healthy options and all seems fresh. The Harmony latte is my favorite and they even have macadamia milk!

This place has amazing wraps, pizza, salads, YUM. Make your own or pick from the menu, can't lose. Chips are home made and to die for and I would drink the balsamic vinaigrette if I could. My only qualm is that it's SO expensive. $25 for two wraps and chips! Yeesh. But worth it..

bought my bike from here and couldn't be happier with my purchase and the service from this store! they were even willing to look online for some accessories we inquired about since they didn't carry it in their store. 

my husband asked about tuning/maintenance on bikes and it seems like they're a lot more affordable than other bike stores in the stl area.

I really like this location and their staff. I've been coming here for two years now and the staff all know and love my dog. She gets excited to see the vets and the techs every time we visit and will immediately hop on the scale to get a treat from from them. I would definitely recommend their friendly service. Cassie on staff is particularly wonderful.

Nobody liked their desserts and when I got the bill I was a little surprised, $60 for 4 desserts and a few drinks.  IT all tasted like it had been in the fridge for a week.  They told us there is a dessert chef.  I find that very, very hard to believe.  None of the cake products were moist at all.  Will not be back.

Wow............how is this place still in business. I came in at 6:15 am to get a coffee and get some work done on my laptop. I order a coffee and ask for honey. The girl immediately says they're out of honey. OK. So I take some agave. I couldn't help but notice the tall guy with the beard wrestling with a coffee machine appearing quite frustrated saying F this and F that and "this job sucks I have to get up at 4:30 in the morning" etc. after sitting down for a few minutes it becomes clear that all of the four employees are disenchanted with their jobs and do nothing but complain and talk about working elsewhere. Of course I go to sit down and the wireless internet doesn't work. I almost think they might do this on purpose so they don't have to serve anyone. There wasn't on other person in the place. 
In my opinion, these are young immature kids of the entitlement age and someone needs to call corporate to come and clean this place up. 
Worst Starbucks experience ever.

Always important to confirm: CASH ONLY!

We went to Dim Sum Garden on a Friday night, and it was PACKED!! We were seated pretty quickly though, which was really nice. We ordered a few dishes to share and the food was prepared pretty quickly!

The 3 of us ordered: Scallion pancakes, steamed shrimp dumplings, fried vegetable dumplings, and the stir fried Udon noodles with seafood and vegetables. The menu in general is really big with lots of different options, some plates smaller and others larger (entrée-sized). We enjoyed our meal here, and the service was great!

I absolutely love this place! I've only been for eyebrow threading, Ms.B does an amazing job. My eyebrows always look great. The salon is quiet and clean. I usually just walk in without an appointment. I've never had an issue with waiting.

The interior is very very cool and gives that western tavern sort of vibe which I liked. The little muffins they serve are insanely good so be careful not to fill up on them before! The ribeye that I had was excellent but the shrimp pasta that my girlfriend had seemed bland and simple for the price... still good though. Service was excellent!

Yum!  And yes!  Or...si!  My mom and I came here for the Yelp Elite event a few weeks ago, and we could not wait to be back!

We brought my dad and husband to join us, and we got their delicious Paloma drink and the beef cheek appetizer to start.  These beef cheeks are the most tender, delicious, fall apart at the touch of a fork pieces of meat I have ever had.  

My dad, husband and I decided to each get a three taco plate with different tacos so we could all swap and have one of each.  We got the duck, the fish and beef cheek.  The duck was mine, and I don't normally order duck, though I love it, because it's almost never done well so it's a waste of money.  I decided to be brave and get the duck here and I'm so glad that I did!

It was cooked perfectly, the toppings were paired amazingly...this really was some of the best duck I have ever had.  I would totally recommend it to anyone who even sort of likes duck.  

The fish tacos were also delicious, and my husbands beef cheeks were delightful.  

This can easily be the place we go to for all occasions, now!  Our wedding anniversary is coming up, and we are planning to do our anniversary dinner here, as well as my birthday dinner, never mind that my birthday isn't until May.  I've already made my decision.  Everything here, from the service to the food, is done outstandingly.

Perfect food. Great scene. The service was great and the food was amazing. Unreal beef tartare, oysters, Brussel sprouts and broccoli sides, fried bread and best dessert ever (apple toffee cake).
Really was an unbelievable food experience in a laid back cool atmosphere

For a shop right in the heart of Bourbon, this place is actually very quiet & unusual. Yes, they have the standard VooDoo dolls, etc., but most of their merchandise has much more charm & thought behind it. Tiny shop. If you can't climbs steps, the entrance may pose a problem because of a steep stoop.

I had been feenin for oxtails for months, I Google this restaurant while visiting in tampa. The place did not disappoint. The oxtail was delicious had me sucking on the bone.  The seasonings just right cooked to perfection.  I will be back ;)

I had a great first time experience there today for my noon appointment with Christina for a Ouidad cut. 
I was greeted and taken to get my hair shampooed as soon as I stepped through the door and had a great shampoo with deep conditioner which was included in my charge. 

The environment was clean, warm, comfortable, and inviting. All of the women who worked there were friendly

My stylist Christina was skilled at cutting, warm and kind mannered and did an excellent job on my hair. The service was on the expensive side, but you get what you pay for. In all, I would definitely be returning to Christina in a couple months for a trim.
.
We wanted to change our 1-car concrete driveway into a 2-car driveway.  We called J&J.  Good price, good people and good workmanship.  What more can you ask.

Very popping place on a Saturday night.  The rooftop was crowded with people hence we were unable to stay up there but for 3 minutes. I gave the goat cheese balls in panko bread crumbs a try since yelp had so much to say about it, I was pleasantly surprised on how good they were! The nachos were a bit spicy but enough for the four of us to munch on. Overall, I'd go back but probably on a less busy night. I live in Miami and don't want to be elbow to elbow with people like we are normally are back home.

It's better than the other two Flowing Tides I have been too!  I had the Chicken Wings and they were over cooked, the Buffalo sauce was really good, the Cheese burger was juicy and cooked perfect!   I asked for real well done fries and they cook them the way I love crispy....  I will going back!

I like to take my 4 young kids here to bowl and I really wish I could give it 5 stars but I can't because of the staff alone! I went there one day and the 2 older ladies working at the counter were so rude and miserable even my children noticed it. All my kids are under the age of 10 and I asked for one of the lighter weight balls and they gave us one. ONE! I asked for a second one because I had 4 kids using it and they said NO! I even offered to pay extra or let them hold a deposit and they still said no! Can you imagine having to share 1 ball for 4 kids? It wasn't fun at all.
Then all my kids wanted the bumper down. My oldest was 10 and he really didn't care but the other 3 did. So when I asked to put them down they said they couldn't because anyone ever 8 (I think was the age they said) can't play with bumpers down. I said I have a 3 and 7 year old that need them down so if the rest of us don't care why do you guys care. And they just wouldn't put them down!
Any other questions I had they were just so rude and so miserable. I couldn't believe it! It was a horrible experience and will never go there again. I do have to say the food is great and we'll priced and the game room is really nice. But it's not worth going because of the horrible service!

I went to The Paris Room for a quick lunch with a colleague today, and it was a bad decision. The service took forever and the crepes we got (pepperoni, mozerella, and cheddar) were awful. The cheese was not melted and the pepperoni was over cooked. How they managed that is beyond me. The cook was really sweet and apologized for it, but I certainly won't try it again. Then, even though we "made our own" and the cost should have been the base $2.75+ $1.75 for pepperoni and $1.00 for the cheese,somehow the cost per crepe was over $7. Not impressed.
I have literally been coming here forty years. All of the pastries are hand made fresh every morning. I highly recommend the ha, egg and cheese biscuit!

One word: Achieke. The best. I don't mess with anything else. No I'm lying....when I'm in the mood for pop which is like a rice pudding cook with tamarind that you heat up.. Like sati I think.  The wait time is the worse. Expect 1 hour wait time.

Love this place so much!!!  It's so great!  They are always changing up their flavors, and you can get sample cups to try before you buy!  They charge by weight so you can get as much or as little as you like!  Plus you get to be the master of your own creations with their self serve yogurt machines and toppings you can add! I love that they also always have soy and sorbet flavors as well!  TF can't be beat!

I can't get enough. Hand's down my favorite pizza in STL. I love the inventive menu, friendly folks and prompt service. The toasted T-Ravs (in meat and non-meat) are AWESOME! I will always make my way to Joanie's when I'm in town.
Great, friendly staff. Helped me with a special drink request without a second thought!

Another  fabulous  dining experience.  The shrimp is suck your and delicious in this beautiful women butter sauce with the grilled corn absolutely the best appetizer I've ever had ever paired with delicious wine
Everything was great. I'm glad I have them another try. I had family in from out of town and they wanted to eat here. Everything from the service to the food was outstanding.

As someone who originated from the NY area, I am a big fan of NY delis.  This one falls short.  It should be named Gyro Deli since the focus leans towards Mediterranean food once you're inside.  Sandwich choices are basic, though meat ingredients are high-quality Boar's Head variety.  I'm sure the gyros are good, though I didn't go for a Greek sandwich.

Cost is a little high for what you get.  I think Jersey Mike's offers an equally good sub sandwich.  There just isn't anything stand-outish about this place.  Maybe the Greek offerings are better.
Nice little shop, very friendly employees. Food lacked flavor. Wouldn't go again. It was plain and blah.
Wonderful food, good service. Great spiced ice tea.

I was in this wawa the other day when i overheard the older coffee lady, Robyn I think her name was (about 50 long dirty blond hair, tattoo on left arm),  loudly conversing with a male customer saying that "back in her day a women wouldn't be aloud to leave the house wearing that!" (something another customer was wearing)then in a tone that is usually reserved for making fun of someone she threw up her hands and went on to say "oh no, I was raped!!"  and laughed loudly enough for everyone to hear. It was disgusting and completely inappropriate. If I wasn't in a state of shock I would have immediately talked to a manager. I never wright these things but I was just so disgusted.

Not planing on coming back.  Outrageous cost for such poor quality food.  Service was good but if we wanted to eat canned food we would have went to the damn food bank.   Spend $70 and had to go get something to eat elsewhere. After stomach settled down.  Food court at mall was better

Love love love this place! Prices are great tacos are the BEST I've had and I've been going to CT for about 6 months now and taking anyone I can so they can experience this place. We also love the root beer that is out of this world!! Thanks Capital Tacos for always going above and beyond to make the customer happy ;)

Excellent service and attention! Everybody was extremely helpful, knowledgeable and super nice! This is going to be my go to location now. I've been going to the one on 82nd St. for like 20 years. But this one is not as crowded yet because I don't think people know about it

I feel obliged to disclose that I own a small white dog, and my love of him may have influenced this review.

I dined here with a small group of people in their oak room. The service was slow and forgetful (put dishes down in front of the wrong person, mistake on someone's order, etc), but they were incredibly friendly and apologetic, which made up for it. 

I got the spice honey walnut shrimp to start. I was worried it would be too spicey ( I'm a wimp), but I must say it wasn't spicey. I loved the shrimp, highlight of my meal. The shrimp tasted incredibly fresh, and the portion was pretty sizeable for a starter at a place of this caliber. 

On the flip side, the entree was my biggest regret. I got a trout entree amd was really put off by the plating (just did not look appetizing) and the skin was still on my trout, which struck me. I'm normally a salmon eater, so maybe this is normal for trout, but it was not stated on the menu. I felt misled.

I really enjoyed the decor of the place. The dog theme really runs through the restaurant and as a dog lover I really loved that. 

Ultimately the shrimp was so good I would give them another try, but if you go in the near future please avoid the trout.

Great spot near Bourbon street.  I went here on a friend's recommendation, great location, and good menu.  The friend chicken was great and the Purée was amazing.  You get Jalapeño cornbread and has a strong kick to it.  

The only thing lacking was the dessert, I had the banana layered cake and the waiter said it was what NOLA was known for, but honestly it didn't taste that good.  There were so many other items that I think would have been better. 

Overall a good spot if you want to go somewhere good on Bourbon street.  My friend also recommend Emeril's restaurant, but it was book for the weekend and we couldn't get reservations.

All the food tastes very premium. Love the beer taster platter. Disappointed they got rid of the pool table. There was also a time where they told us they would only split our large group's bill into four smaller ones. It felt like we had to scramble to pay appropriately which added unneeded stress. I would've liked to know about that policy well before the end of the meal.
Great Pizza and atmosphere.  Love the craft beer self serve taps.  It was walking distance from my hotel on West End. Convenient, will stop by again next time I am in town.

The brown butter and sage ravioli are amazing! The rib eye, free range chicken, and lamb are also delicious. It's a bit small, crowded, and loud, but that's how Italian places tend to be, I guess.  Either way, that's the only major downside (well, including that there always busy too!).

So amazing! My fiancé and I got the steak for 2, which of course was pricey but totally worth it. You get so much for your money. We were able to take so much food home for the next day. We will definitely be going back to celebrate future special occasions.
I highly recommend any class. It's such a loving environment here. Truly one of the most welcoming yoga studios in the city.

We lived here from May 2015 til March 2016.

Pro's:
Centrally located to beaches, downtown, whole foods, malls, airport, etc....
Amenities are Fantastic! (I saw several other places that were also very nice, but we have a heated pool year round and it feels very exclusive here.)
They have the Nicest people working here!!!! Jessica, Nick, Steven, Erika, Horatio, Ernesto, and Roberto are so helpful. They went out of their way to be gracious and thoughtful.
Privacy (Staff and just the overall feel is that I am able to be as anonymous as I want.)
I really liked living here. If you want to feel like you are enjoying a resort style living, this is the place. Definitely meant more for professionals, singles, or temporary basis living. Also, we have two small children, so we should have asked for a lower floor unit. 
Huge closets, great bathrooms, and beautiful granite counter tops.
Con's:
Noise (there is little to cushion the sound between top and bottom floors) The noise between floors is really loud. (I had to listen to a woman being hurt upstairs on multiple occasions-i called the police more than once)
The fire alarms are extremely loud and went off 3x while we were there. Only once it was because of actual smoke/fire. But my son was traumatized by the experience (they went off twice at night or nap time unnecessarily.
Would give a 0 but it's not possible. Website says open 12AM - 12AM. Just called at 3pm & dude says "Shit, I'm done at 5:00". Never mind then.

It's great! It's big! Great for groups, and has a huge menu. You will find something you like. It is tucked away with a few other businesses, and is very bright inside. It isn't great for any ambiance, but that's okay for the food, and for the price. I wouldn't have known about it if it weren't for my friends, but we plan on going back and getting takeout for sure.

If you are willing to spend $$$, this place is fantastic. We started with a dozen oysters- east and west coasts.  Served on ice with fresh horseradish- clean and cold.  Excellent.  We moved to the blue crab dip and grilled octopus- both of which were ideally prepared and tasty. The girls shared the Dover Sole and guys had the cowboy ribeye.  Both were exquisitely prepared and our meals were as good as any found in St. Louis.  If there was any issue with the evening, it would have been with the family that thought this high end establishment would be good for a family dinner.  This place is NOT for families.  Keep the kids at home.

Neat atmosphere for a microbrewery/restaurant. The menu was varied and quite reasonable. The salads were excellent and the beer was good. This isn't supposed to be a 5 star restaurant but if you are looking for a great hangout in Indy to have some good food, drink some good beer and have plenty of room, this is it. The service was very good and we had a great time!

Wow! We ate here because of the positive reviews and were not disappointed!  The steak was amazing. The mashed potatoes were the best I've ever eaten. The fish tacos were very tasty. And the spinach salad was perfect. The employees went above and beyond to answer our questions and were very friendly. It was obvious that they not only enjoy working here but are also very proud of the food they serve. I would not have noticed this restaurant just by driving past, but SO glad to have found it. Will definitely return and tell friends!

Love this place! Just went for the first time about 2 weeks ago and it was Classic Italian comfort food. We started with a "small Cesar" salad and entrees were meat lasagna and beef stroganof- all excellent. 

What I loved about this place was the ambiance and service. Our waiter, ugh, I think it was Tim, was hilarious! He also let us know about the large portions and specialty items. Great service!

Meals were huge and yummy garlic bread on the side....I  we filled up on bread cuz we both had late night second dinner.  :-)

I recommend this place to anyone looking for classic kind of Americanized Italian. It took me back to my childhood. Not too gourmet, but delish in its own way!
Best pho in town. In fact, everything is great! Most friendly Vietnamese restaurant I've ever been to as well.

Love the healthy selection. Staff is friendly. The garden bar is great. So many selection of drinks and desserts. Servers are  prompt and respectful. Even the restaurant manager was out and about talking to everyone.

Came here for our Anniversary dinner in May and had a wonderful experience.  Both the Hostess and Server (Katie) went over the top!  They made our night very special and went way above and beyond what they needed to do.  We couldn't have been any happier with the service, it was excellent!!
This was a very good place.  I'd certainly go back again.  I had a Gyro salad and with added condiments, it was very good.

We have been to the cat cafe three times and have loved each experience. (We drive 25 min to pet cats...) I appreciate the funky grandma/cat lover vibe. Service has been great and the cause is even better. Although my farmer parents think it's outrageous we pay money to pet cats, I think it is one of the best bargains in the city. For $10 I am able to entertain my poor, deprived, pet-less child for a half hour, get a hot beverage and leave a tip for the barista.

Harrah's Reno is a decent place to stay.  I would only stay here because I do get free comp'd rooms to play and gamble here, but beyond that if I was going to pay for a room, I'd splurge a little bit more than on what they have to offer.

I am new to Philly, but I know good pizza. If you like wide soft crusts and a lot of provolone, this is a place to try in the area. Customer service is great and the two large slice/20 oz deal is reasonable for $5.99. The chicken gyro is worth a try too. Parking in front is small, I usually park in the empty side parking lot. The posted signs on who/when parking is permitted are contradictory though. Just that word of caution.

This staff is wonderful and extremely helpful, and also very HONEST, which I have found to be the most helpful. Some associates at other Sally's locations claim to know what they're talking about even if they don't, and at this location I have found that they are the most realistic about their knowledge of products and outcomes. This is very important when dealing with hair. Particularly, their employee Deja was a huge help during my last visit and also went above and beyond in making efforts to help with specific hair dye color questions and opinions. Out of the three Sally's locations, this is the only location with a fully friendly staff. I also suggest investing in their beauty club card, which is $5 per year if you do not have a cosmo number. It's definitely worth the discounts.

Cindy, my coworker lives there part time  and here part time, meaning every 3 months or so he visits home. He recommended you to us and he says that me makes sure that he takes all of his out of town guests there. It was a great recommendation. Still craving those crab fingers.

The old Parthenon was a grand favorite with my family for many years, in Broad Ripple, where the parking is difficult but we always thought it was worth it.  I was happy to discover that the restaurant is still around, altho I have to agree that the new location is lacking...not the warm, dark, urn-adorned ambience of old.  But, the food is still the great Greek stuff of memories.  Altho my fav, pastitio, is no longer on the menu the spanikopita is as always, spectacular, and no one will ever make a better Greek salad!!! Many main dishes there are great!  The Parthenon will always be my favorite Greek restaurant, just for the food.
Ask for chef Johnny and you won't be disappointed. They customize, are creative and friendly. I have never left this place hungry or dissatisfied. Love the scallops! Coconut shrimp. Surf and turf!

I do not like commercialized historic tours.  I just don't.  Maybe I am too cynical, but they seem so contrived and like they are trying too hard to make it all an experience.  THIS IS A NOT FOR PROFIT and WONDERFUL.  I felt like I came out knowing more about Nashville history and the history of horse racing.

The grounds are beautiful.  They gave quite a tour of the house, our guide did an excellent job and there was even a wine tasting at the end.  They gave 3 samples and there was literally no pressure to buy, although we did buy, because after all, we were basically giving to charity.  How can a person go wrong when they drink wine and make the world a better place?!

Now read this part carefully:  We were on an anniversary trip SANS KIDS (that means without).  We have a 12 and 10 year old.  I think they would have been miserably bored.  The tour is pretty long and you need to stand in one place so as to avoid knocking over the priceless heirlooms.  It is Nashville.  The house has a/c but still hot.  The wine tasting is in a very small area.  You can physically bring the kids but even well behaved ones that are interested in history and horses will probably be anxious to move on.

It was OK.  Had the bandeja paisa.  The area was dry.  The meat was a little over cooked.  The tostones and chicharrón were really good.  Not the best columbian I've had but not bad.  The waiter was a bit slow and forgetful.  I had to keep reminding him to bring me stuff.

There's a reason why Port of Call is always busy....it's because it embodies what is awesome about NOLA.  Strong drinks, good food, reasonable prices, and cool staff - what more can you want? A shorter wait? Well that ain't happening so here's what you need to know to have a good experience here.

1. Do not come here when you are hungry. You should expect to wait for a table so come about an hour before you think you'll be hungry and the timing should shake out.

2. If you're coming with a big group (more than 6), don't expect that you'll all be seated at the same table. The staff tries their best to have you close together, but with the limited space, you just don't know.

3. When you have put your name in for a table, go to the bar and get a cocktail. A monsoon will treat you right. Also, their go cups are the best ever - make sure you get a lid!

4. Order a mushroom burger - medium rare. Add cheese and bacon bits to your potato. (Warning, they use the fake kind but I like those, so no harm, no foul.)

5. If you need to head to the loo, don't try to cut through the bar, head to the left dining area - much easier to get through!

Following these tips will totally make for a great experience - ENJOY!

Great time with a fun crew. 50 beers on tap...and so many crafts....including Fat Heads Spooky Tooth (rock on Cleveland). Plus thanks to Jason for holding my Green Lantern tile for pick up. #iwillbeback

Tonight I tried to get a late night meal, and since the posted hours said this location was open until 10pm I decided to go here. Lo and behold they were closed. This is not the first time this has happened. At least three other times they are listed as "open" and they close early. Bad for business if you don't post an updated schedule in today's internet world.

Visiting with friends and found this gem- away from the tourist traps of the French quarter. We grilled our own meat at the table (chicken, short ribs, pork and bulgolgi) and garnished it with kimchi and other small pickled dishes. So fresh and absolutely delicious! Great service and well managed restaurant. Made best buds with our table mates.

This is such a nice park, great for kids! they have a little farm where there are about 10 different kind of animals that you can look at and walk through. they have two ponds where you can fish and walk around. they have ducks you can feed. huge play ground. lots of areas to have picnics. My kids always enjoy going here, not to big not to small. Highly recommend it.

So we wait 20 minutes to be seated and then they seat 2 parties who "signed in" AFTER us. It was extremely rude so we left. It was also very hot and very cramped. I suggest Kenny's Korner right down the street.

This restaurant is excellent! Would have never thought to stop here... I came with my parents per their recommendation. Everything we ordered was delicious & the bartender was so nice & welcoming. I'm very picky & I give this place an A+. Will definitely be a return customer.

We were 5 adults/family in Tampa for one night and wanted a Brazilian steakhouse without it being overpriced. We searched on Yelp and came across this great restaurant! Couldn't have asked for friendlier service and such a wide selection on the salad bar as well as the mouth watering meats. The grill master was there serving us delicious cuts. The establishment was in a peculiar part of town and sign out front looks dated but don't let that full you because inside is a nice and comfortable atmosphere. I wish I was in Tampa again tonight so we could go again!

For the food alone, I'd give 4.5 stars.  I stopped in on a Tue at 5:30pm.  Wasn't busy, the host was nice, the waitress was pleasant, the food runner too.  All three seemed a bit detached, were professional, not aloof, but didn't do anything that made me feel particularly comfortable.  I was a single diner, I think I was low-stakes for them and because the place was nearly empty, they weren't into any kind of groove.  Some staff are skilled to the point that they are more adaptable and able to connect with a customer in most any phase of their day. They could have asked if I'd been there before, just something to make a connection. I put out good energy, am polite, clear on what I want.  Will tip quite well (25-30%) if someone makes an effort.  

Overall vibe of Varga is urban professional (Yuppie), definitely hetero, but gay friendly. 

I liked the waitress but was a bit uncomfortable overall.  She helped me pick a beer, I said I liked dark beer, but not too bitter, she recommended and brought me the most bitter beer I think I''ve ever tasted--a mocha beer.  I was fine with it, it wasn't bad and I can enjoy most anything.  

Food was quite good--there's real skill in the kitchen.  Chili took a few minutes to warm to--wasn't particularly spicy, but there was a lot of subtle flavor.  Crab cheese fries are off the charts.  Plenty of crab, tasty cheese sauce, crisp fries, home-made ketchup on the side.  Relied more on flavors than on lots of oil, or butter, I'm always impressed when something is rich, but you don't come away feeling trashed or immobile.  

They have an ice cream dessert with three flavors in a serving, each based on a breakfast cereal--I'll make another trip there to try this.

Poor service. I wanted to eat there and took my chances if they would accept walk ins. I stood in front of the reception for about 15mins and the receptionist on the phone didn't even bother to say something to me. Another lady came and I asked her if they accept walk in. She said sorry we are busy. I felt like they didn't even checked if some diners are almost done and didn't even ask if I want to wait. So I just walked away and decided I'll never eat at that place.

Great tour, friendly staff, smartly designed trolleys (buses).

I'm familiar with this tour company from Key West, I've taken a couple on various visits. The new Nashville branch lives up to the solid Key West version.

We did a two day option of this hop on hop off tour. Day one is our usual - take the whole tour at once to get a lay of the city. Great overview, fun stories. Day two we started at the Parthenon, and got off at a few stops along the way of things we wanted to see more of. All four of the drivers we met were charming, fun, and helpful when you ask questions. 

The trolleys are open on the sides which is great for a breeze and photos, but they are also covered, a huge plus in the hot Nashville sun. Some of the other tour buses have an open top, and I'd have baked without a cover. 

I definitely recommend these tours. Great value!

I had Stanley Steamer out to clean my kids rooms and a couple of traffic areas today. When I called to schedule the cleaning I was told a little over $100 for 3 rooms and an entry cleaning and that they would show between the hours if 9:00am and 1:00pm. They arrived at exactly 12:30pm, which is in the time frame, but I was already upset for having to sit around and wait all morning. They did not cover their shoes with booties at any point during their time here. I had several stains in my children's rooms that did not all come out, but I know they state that its a possibility they won't. Then as they were doing the stairs they knocked down an expensive photo of me and my kids but did not tell me the frame was damaged, they just hung it back up like nothing happened! They did however work very quickly and was out in not time, but when I received the bill it was $213 and all I added to the previous total that I was told was $30 for the stairs...feel like it wasn't worth $200!

Love-Love-Love this small town shop with big charm.  Customer service is the best around.  The girls in the shop take time with you and are so helpful.  Their selection of Brighton and Trollbeads is fantastic as well as Alex and Ani and others.  Located in historic Allentown, their selection is always changing to keep up with the times.  Favorite place to shop hands down- their care in wrapping each item in their signature black bags is a treat in itself.  It is gift-giving at it's finest!  Cute gift cards available if you just can't decide. My go to place for gift giving for the special ladies in my life.

Really good spot off the beaten path.  Legit wings and 4-star super friendly service!  

Been here a few times for lunch and I'll keep going back.  Always clean and always busy.  Great for burgers, wings, and daily specials!

Oh, beer too!

Wow talk about a hidden gem. I really wish I knew about this place earlier with all the times have flown out to Chicago. The experience is so much less stressful then dealing with major airports. Got to airport earlier and enjoyed nice weather and sat outside on a bench before checking in. Security took literally two minutes. Coming home I walked off plane and was in car within 5 minutes of landing (carried on). No traffic going to or from airport. As has been pointed out parking only 8 bucks a day (Newark by comparison is 27-33 a day (and have to take air train- when its running- to get there). They really need to do a publcity campaign and get the word out- want to make sure this place survives. Know Frontier Airlines gets alot of bad press but I found their service very good and will definitely look to fly out of here as much as possible going forward.

The croissant sandwich with egg, cheese, and bacon was amazing. Super fresh, buttery, and steamy. I still dream about it but unfortunately no longer live in the area. Donuts are also amazing and super fresh.

I tried a boba drink several years ago and the pearls were kind of tough and powdery, so I never ordered one again. They may have improved this part over the years.

The food here was excellent, the drink selection was varied, and the staff and atmosphere were perfect. If you have any special requests, email and let them know--they were very helpful in planning my date night for my girlfriend. This is by far my favorite restaurant in St. Louis, and if you can only choose one while in town, eat here!

We had cocktails fused with lavender and it was the best drink I've ever had in my life. Another highlight.. the apple pie stuffed CHURROS! Everything about this place is BOMB.. Even down to our waitress, Brooke. 5 stars.
Fun fun fun. Ride the carousel bar and act like you are one of the rich and famous. Great entertain,net and the bartenders really know how to mix a drink
Soup dumplings are the best ever.   Great service.

A little bit ago, my boss and I took a client here for dinner and man it was the best meal I ever had in the city. I had the patte ravioli and the pizza as an appetizer and it was incredible.

The service was amazing even when my boss and our client got a little drunk and started making a scene. They had a guy lubricating the inside of the wine glasses so that the wine would turn better when poured. 

Now listen, I love Machismo burritos and a non-lubricated fountain drink but every now and again it's nice to go somewhere and share some roast rabbit. 

I recommend this to anyone who wants to showcase the city to out of towners, and anyone who appreciates food and atmosphere.

This was our first time at this restaurant and it was fabulous!! Two of us got grilled chicken tacos, and one of us got shrimp tacos and we were all more than satisfied!! The nachos, salsa, and guacamole were also so delicious! We had a picky eater with us and they were more than accommodating! The server was also incredible! Would recommend this place to anyone!! Happy to support a local place! (:

While some days I wish I could pick up everything I need for my Waldo kitty at some fancy pet boutique, because, y'know, he's totally worth it (and as particular in general as I am), Petsmart gets the job done. One of the biggest cat sections in town. Carriers, a wall of toys (even fancy Martha Stewart toys, meeeeow), bowls, fountains, scratching posts, litter, litter boxes, food, treats, you got it.

Not a ton of staff around to help, but when I find someone, they're great. When I had trouble finding the right carrier for him an employee really went above and beyond to help me find the right one. I also joined the Petsmart loyalty club, too, so I get discounts!

A happy kitty is a happy kitty mommy, and this place keeps Waldo happy.

The structure of this DD is pretty cool looking. It's modern and this DD promotes it's green awareness. I've had service issues several times here though. The staff seems pretty stressed and makes mistakes pretty frequently. The drive-thru line can be a mess also, with two different entrances converging to a single speaker. During peak hours, the drive-thru line will loop around the parking lot, blocking parking spots, so good luck if you happened to park and go inside. It's not the best DD I've visited, and it's far from the worst. The donuts (when I get the right one), are always pretty good. That matters most, right?

Great drinks and even better food. My girlfriend and I arrived with no reservation to a packed house on a Friday night. We were told we could eat outside but opted to grab drinks and wait for a table inside. After waiting for a long time, the manager/owner came by and thought we had already been seated. He took care of us immediately and got us our next round on the house. Service was friendly, professional and top notch even with the seating mix up.

Highly recommended -
     Food: Steak Mac and Cheese
     Drink: Goat's Beard

I have been coming to Kon Tiki since 2007 when we first moved to Tucson.  Being a fan of all thinks Tiki I couldn't wait to come here.  The decor is amazing.  One of the best Tiki bars that I have been too and I've been to a lot.  The drinks, some of them are good and they are very strong.  

The down side to Kon Tiki is the strange rules, the food, and the bartenders
.  
1. There are certain drinks you can only have 2 of.  But then they will let you drink what ever else you want.  Weird!!!
2. They have a dinning room area where you have to sit if you want to eat off the main menu.  But you can't sit back there just to have drinks.  Even if it's standing room only.  Strange!!!!
3.  The food is terrible, so get something to eat before you get there.  Ate dinner there the first time. Never again.  I can't even begin to explain the horror.  The apps you can order in the lounge are all frozen right out of the box.  Needs some work for sure.  Lots of revenue lost there.
4. The bartenders are the rudest people I have ever encountered.  They all have a complex that they are the second coming of Christ.  WTF get over yourself, you are just pouring drinks.  

I will still continue to go because of the atmosphere.  The cocktail waitress are quick and friendly.  I am never surprised when a new rule pops up or the bartenders are yelling at customer like they are second class citizens.  It's Kon Tiki and thats just how they roll.  Aloha

There was a line, so I tried to place an order on the touch-screen and had some problems, asked the employee to close out my account information, she said she could not, they don't "have a key." I asked for a manager, a woman named Emma who seemed not at all into it from the moment she came out (look-of-death type expression), and who said customers can't place orders on these kiosks, they're for pickup only. I said, "Well, okay, it might be helpful if the sign said so because at other locations these touch-screens are for placing orders." Her reply was, "I've never had a problem with it before." I said, "Okay, I realize that maybe I'm the stupid one, but there could be a sign that says NOT FOR PLACING ORDERS. Because if some locations offer touch-screen ordering and some locations don't, that's confusing." She seemed displeased. Anyway, why do so many Panera/STL Bread Co locations have such terrible customer service? Are employees encouraged to be rude to customers? I'm beginning to think so.

The only reason why anyone would go to Sweet Endings is because South St. is too far of a walk to go to Phileo. They have half of the toppings as Phileo and while afar the decor looks neat... inside the counter where the toppings are served are already cracked and construction at the time was not complete on the outside of the store. To each his own on the flavor. If you like it tart or like someone was too cheap to add the rest of the ingredients... per haps this is your thing but its not mine. My husband and I ended up spending 10 bucks on our yogurts and threw them away immediately... We couldnt fake the funk. Move on save your money honey.

This branch is just like the rest of the tree - rotten to the core, misguided, and only gets 1 star because Yelp hasn't invented the turkey YET!

TRUE STORY
   The week my twins were born (several years ago), I accidentally over drafted my account.  My first ever overdraft after banking with them for years.  It was long hours in hospital for 3 days straight and I forgot to make a deposit.  My branch decided to charge me NOT 1, NOT 2, no no no - 5 OVERDRAFT FEES!!!  Because, in "real time", which is bull shit, they just used the BIGGEST charge to overdraft 4 smaller charges (which would have cleared just fine if not for the biggest charge).
   They were so kind to refund me 2 of these charges, huh?  Especially at this time in my life when I could have used the money more than ever...

JUSTICE DELIVERED
   Years later, after moving into a nice place and situating my family well, I needed to re-order checks.  I updated my address with them at the time of the move.  Yet, weeks later, when I ordered the checks, they were sent to my old address!   I guess I'm not the only one who makes mistakes!?
   The woman at the bank said they cancelled the order, but no, they didn't.  Checks were delivered to wrong address, and I was billed for those checks.
   The manager of the branch offered to remove that charge and re-issue me new checks at no additional charge.  I told her that, by my calculation, the bank owed me $105 compensation.  The $105 is what I was charged for my first mistake, so I felt that $105 is what they should pay for this mistake.  They didn't feel that way.  So we drove to the bank, leaving the car running right in front and not even parking, and withdrew our money.  My wife went in while I waited in the car.

THE PUNCHLINE
   The assistant manager came out to ask me to move my car.  I asked her who she thought she was - she said proudly "The assistant branch manager!"  I told her "In a company as big as BOFA, that is the equivalent of Shift Leader at Taco Bell, so KISS MY ASS!"  She just tucked her assistant manager tail between her assistant manager legs and walked back inside while I waited there.

BANK OF AMERICA SUCKS - PURE AND SIMPLE - AMEN.

Jada is absolutely fabulous! I've seen her regularly for 2 years now, and it has made a profound impact on both my body and my life. She has helped me to process and move through emotions stuck in my body, and to more deeply understand what is going on within me. Her hands intuitively go to wherever my body needs healing, and it feels so good. Her longer sessions are so worth it, and I love that I can get in on Tune Up Tuesdays for $20. I leave sessions with her feeling relaxed, peaceful, lighter and at ease.

Katrina is the best massage therapist I've had. She caters to your pressure so wonderfully and genuinely listens to what your needs are. I'm a regular so she remembers what my style is but always make it a point to ask if I have a specific need for that day. I highly recommend her at this location!

I went to Feast with some friends to celebrate a bridal shower. I was really looking forward to trying this new restaurant in the Midtown District. The restaurant is well located and easy to access. I would imagine on a busy morning/afternoon parking might get tricky, but I had no problem with this. The interior design/theme of the restaurant is clean, well thought out, and inviting. The servers and wait staff were all dressed nicely and our server had a very hip bow tie. My first impressions were overall great. 

I ordered a lemonade basil vodka drink and enjoyed every last drop. It was refreshing and tasty, yet had plenty of libations! To eat, I ordered the Jube salad off the brunch menu. I was craving a hearty salad and this choice delivered. Unfortunately, the salad dressing was a little zingy/spicy for me, so if you are sensitive to that I'd recommend ordering it on the side. Lastly, I ordered french fries because I can't live without those at any meal, haha. They were definitely tasty. 

Overall, I had a great experience and look forward to going back sometime with my husband. The outdoor seating area looked really nice and I'd love to give that a try some weekend morning. If you haven't been already, give it a try for yourself!

This was the first Which Wich experience for me, and I was instantly a fan. Love the ordering system, marking your own bag and just handing it to the cashier. The sandwich I got was a good size for the price, and the taste was great. A location just opened in my hometown so I'll be visiting soon.

We have had up and down experiences at Outbacks across the country. Back in Kinnelon, NJ, that Outback was the pits. Never had a good experience there, though it was brand new when we lived there. They even gave us $75 in free meals/appetizers to compensate for the one really bad night, and still, it never got better. However, the one in Boardman, Ohio was pretty good when we lived there. 

That said, we have passed this one for months here in Bay Pines, since we live down the road, and never stopped in because it's always been packed. But a couple weeks ago, we stopped in on a Wednesday for their 2-for meal deal. We weren't expecting much. Maybe that's why we had a good time.

I usually get the filet, but that's not on the 2-for deal, so I got the prime rib and my husband did the ribs. 

First out, our Bloomin' Onion. Not as salty as usual. Yay!!!! It was actually edible.

Next, our salads. Normal, fresh. Good. I save some of my onion for the top of my salad. Nice little topping there. 

Then our meals came out. 

My husband thoroughly enjoyed his ribs. They were fall off the bone, and he ate right through them. 

My prime rib was delicious! It was a good sized serving, minimal fat, but done rare, as asked, with a wonderful au jus and creamy horseradish on the side. I poured the au jus on the plate, so the meat was surrounded by it, and then dipped my fork in the horseradish before each bite just for the spark on my tongue. It was truly a good cut of meat. I was so impressed! 

We are going to switch from Cody's to Outback, being that Cody's screwed up our steak order royally. I am so happy this Outback is good, because I really do love most of their food.
Stopped for dessert... the doughnut was amazing with ice cream!! Can't wait to try another flavor... it was yummy!!

This was such a nice surprise
Food is outstanding
Restaurant is clean and good looking
I ate the shrimp fajita ( with several huge  jumbo shrimp) husband had beef burrito
We ended with a fantastic pastel de chocolate for dessert
Neighborhood is not quaint or anything like that but worth the trip

I have been hearing all the praises about this place (the Center City location ) for a while, but I rarely trek down to the city for a meal. I was surprised to see that there was a HD location in the burbs so we tried it out and it DOES live up to the hype! They have a traditional Chinese menu and an Americanized one, but if you are going to eat here then do it authentic. 

Appearance: This location is in a strip mall so I wasn't expecting much in terms of decor, but it was actually contemporary and inviting. Single bathrooms, but not an issue since it wasn't super crowded. 

Service: OK service and the place is BYOB. 

Menu: Since I was a newbie to the HD menu, I took the suggestions of  other Yelpers. Before ordering, you have to know that these dishes are spicy! I am Asian and can really take some heat, but some of the dishes were mouth numbing (in a good way). If you can't handle the heat, tell them to tone it down before ordering. The portions were decent sized and definitely can be shared by 3 adults. 

Apps: The one appetizer that stood out was the Dan Dan noodles! It looks pretty bland when it comes out, but when you mix it up and take that first bite...yum! 

Entree: The deep fried shredded beef , chicken with hot dry pepper were good choices! We also ordered the cumin lamb, but I thought the cumin was a bit overpowering in the dish. The pork lo mein was average, but we ordered that more for the kids. I prefer just having the dishes with a bit of white rice instead. 

Overall, if you are willing to pay for PF Changs garbage...try HD instead and get a way better meal! Plus, rarely have leftovers tasted so good. I would definitely go back and sample more of Mr. Han's menu!
It wasn't the best Cafe con leche I've ever had but I enjoyed the environment and location. I'm gonna try something else next time

Once a month or so, usually on a Friday, a group of us at work will decide to forego the wonders of the food courts and get lunch at a place that serves. Fiona MacCool's is regularly chosen, since it is convenient for us, always seems to have free tables without the need for reservations, and is big enough to handle quite a few groups greater than four people. 

Definitely find it an upgrade on the old Elephant and Castle, whose space it occupies. And prefer the "patio" since it is brighter. 

Likely visited 10 or so times since it opened and the food has ranged from decent to good, usually some type of sandwich accompanied by the Irish chips (like those). In my last most recent visit I tried the Ma's Crispy Chicken and would put it at the good end.

Service has been consistently good, the food arrives quickly and they have no problem breaking out the bill for each person. Can't really say anything about the bar or what is on tap, since I don't work for a 1960s ad agency, but expect to continue visiting the restaurant on a regular basis for lunch.

If your car breaks in Indianapolis, this is a solid place to go. Honest, reasonable, with good customer service and clear communication.

My wife took the car in for a sound the brakes were making. They got the car off the ground, took off the wheels, and found a few more problems than we thought. However, they were kind enough to actually take my wife in and show her on the car where each problem was so she could see it for herself. turned out there were some brake problems and a couple of tire issues. 

Note-on the new tires, for $6, they gave us a "roadside hazard" thing where they will fix or replace the tire for free as long as there's a certain amount of tread left on them. This seemed like an amazing deal to me.

The employees were friendly, knowledgeable, and willing to take the time to explain things to people who don't know a lot about cars. It may not be the best mechanic in the world, but I'm certainly not looking for a new one anytime soon.
Had a good time having cajun fries! The employee by the name of Mahnoor, and the rest of the crew is full of energy! Best S&S spot in STL!

Located in the Warehouse District, Peche serves excellent coastal seafood with a modern approach to old world cooking methods. It serves delicious oysters, fish, and crab plates.  My favorites were crab + jalapeño capellini, spicy ground shrimp and noodles, and seafood gumbo.  The ambience is casual, but neat and enjoyable.  Strongly recommended.

Naan & Kabab has pleased us each of the four times we visited the fine restaurant.
But this time, I want to talk about the extra reasons we are pleased. The flowers all around the exterior are well tended and attractive. The lighting is perfect. And the interior of the restaurant is welcoming and pretty.

Our most recent time, our waiter was Tom, and he performed above and beyond the call of duty. My favorite is the Mediterranean Stew but this time, Tom mentioned that I could have any of several meats in the stew. I chose chicken, Lori and I love their raspberry iced tea, and Tom brought us a carafe of it so we could top it up on our own.

One more thing that means a lot to oldsters like us whose income is Social Security, you'll be delighted to know that make another meal at home should you want. I had the leftover the next day and it was very good.

But most especially, I want the owners to know that Tom was personable, kept us aware of things we should know and was an exemplary server.

I don't get the attraction to this spot.

I have dined at City House on 4 occasions.  

I was there 3 weeks ago and that will be my last visit.

We ordered a pizza as an appetizer and requested garlic on the pizza.  The waitress told us that the chef takes exception to customers who request any deviation from the standard recipe.  Are you kidding me???  Our tab was in excess of $300.  I take exception to overly pretentious cooks.

I had the short ribs. It was nothing more than a plate of overcooked meat.  No garnish or anything else...

City House is just not that good...

One word: flavor!  Everything had so much flavor. Meatballs should be called amazeballs!  I would have taken a photo but I made a pig of myself and ate them all. Also ordered the veggie pizza and it was equally delicious. Owners are super friendly. Atmosphere is low key pizza place. Loved it and we will be back!  Mangia!

I will never go to this nail salon ever again - I had a terrible experience.  I went here because it was convenient but the nail tech cut my heel during the pedicure and now I have cuts on my heel, making it very difficult to walk.  I called the salon to complain and to request my money back.  I was told to come back to the salon so they could see for themselves.  I did, and they ended up refunding my money for both the pedicure and the manicure (the manicure was terrible, too).  As I indicated, I won't be back.  I should have read the reviews here first.  It looks like I'm not the only person this has happened to.  By the way, I wouldn't even give it one star, but I had to give it something so I could post this review.

About two weeks ago an owner got in touch with me about my review. Good for him. More business owners should take the time to deal directly with their customers...especially on yelp. Yelp has become the mecca of "go" or "don't go" so owners...keep that in mind or you might be hanging a sign that says "Lease Available".  

My biggest complaint was the delivery time and "the owner" (don't you love quotes) asked for another chance. He sent me a coupon for a free pizza. He told me the things they were doing to remedy the delivery times so why wouldn't I try CT again since I got a bribe....coupon. Sorry. No harm no foul. 

So...I made my order and I was told 30-45min. It took an hour. An hour on the dot. It was 6pm on a week day and I realize its dinner time. I'm not a monster. I did it on purpose. I wanted to see what kind of phone to door time they would do when everyone is doing the same thing. Ordering food via delivery. I'm sure the delivery times at 3pm are much better but I'm a scientist of delivery and a superhero of yelp. 

The food is still very good and the owner seemed like a nice guy. The delivery time was better then in the past...so were baby steppin. Thumbs up to the owner for the willingness to give out free food and put his business on a stop watch, under a microscope.

We feel that this is the best Mexican place in the area, hands down. The chips and salsa are wonderful, and brought out quickly. The service is fast and friendly. The menu is extensive. And the food is wonderful. 

What's more, the owner looks just like El Macho from Despicable Me 2! Especially when he is wearing his usual red shirt. It's astonishing. You must see it for yourself. It's like they based the look of the character right from this guy! 

We don't even call the place Cancun. We call it "El Macho's." And we go there at least once a week. Never disappoints.

We made a reservation for a late lunch so that we could walk right in after touring the Museum of the American Revolution. This restaurant is a great idea. Great menu and well appointed Colonial home. However, the service is super slow and unimpressive. The waitress was nice, but we were literally left wondering if being super slow was part of the ambience. Our lunch took two hours, after we were seated. After we ordered, the food came out relatively quickly, it was just a long time between the waitress seating us, taking our order, coming to see if we wanted dessert, bringing a check, etc. They didn't even seem to be understaffed. Everybody just was moving at a snail's pace. And one of the bus boys was clearly high. Even my teenagers (of course) noticed. Overall, none of the waitstaff really seemed to have bought into the concept of a period restaurant. Definitely seemed like they were reluctantly going through the motions. Food was fine, but at $200 for a lunch for the five of us (including one ordering on the kids' menu) something needs to be fairly impressive.

Super friendly service that makes you feel like a local even if you're not.  Charming to watch the local give and take here... Plus really fine selection of fresh donuts to boot!  A real uplift from the oversell of trendy to be seen places.  Just honest to good donuts and coffee.  Simple.

Great spot for a quick massage. Went with the 45 minute table massage (for $45), and it didn't disappoint. The last few minutes, the masseuse used hot stones while massaging my back, which felt amazing. I'll definitely be back!

Before performance came to town I always went to BGI. Since then,  I have only been backl to BGI once.... That should tell you enough in and of itself. Very friendly staff, excellent prices, fantastic bikes. I've been riding my 30 speed Fuji road bike for almost 4 years now. The best purchase I have ever made in my entire life! Definitely have to give them a look if you haven't!!
First time here July 19th. Love the decor. I had the Love Triangle cocktail and it was very strong :-) and good. Love the bar area. Service was empeccable. I will go back.

The food , the art, the atmosphere. All excellent. An eclectic mix of high end cuisine and and a chill vibe. Roy has created a casual New York/LA scene that feels like home.  It's impossible to chose a menu favorite but don't miss the bread, house salad or tomato soup. This guy is no amateur. You will not be disappointed.

I will keep this review small and sweet,  I would have given them 4 stars but the chips were not good at all, hard and bland maybe even a little stale but hey they are FREE right!?!?  I told my friend I sure hope the rest of the food is not like this.  I will say that the salsa that comes with the chips is VERY GOOD; they give you the basic red one and the green tomatillo one, which is the one I prefer.  Now let's get to the food... I ordered the sampler and my friend ordered the fajitas which I found a bit pricey for a lunch item.  For my sampler, I chose a tostada, tamale and a fried jalapeño pepper stuffed with beef, this plate also comes with white rice and black beans.  All I can say is thank God that the food did not taste like the chips.  The tamale cornmeal on the tamale was perfect and the tostada was delicious and the fried stuffed pepper well let's just say that I was wanted to order another one.  I was very happy with the food.  My friend enjoyed her fajitas, very tasty but just a lil pricey for a lunch portion and just let you know they charge $2.00 for refills which I thought was a bit too much.   If I could suggest something to the PANCHITA crew it would be to get fresh made chips!!!
We came here kind of randomly for brunch, got great food and friendly service for a very good price--not to mention complimentary mimosas. They don't have drinks to order they do invite you to BYOB

Great date night with my wonderful husband.  Great fast service.  Used a groupon but still got the happy hour prices on the wine and appetizer. Food was delicious and service was fast and efficient.  Will definitely go back.
Went for opening day and got a great deal on a few pizzas. Good for the price when it was $2.99 for a large cheese and it's great fresher. I'll come back if there are some deals for sure!
Very fast extremely cheap compared to vet bills. It's a public service what they do. Thanks for taking care of the stray puppy I found.

Breakfast is very affordable and tasty. The staff are always so friendly.  
Lots of food for the price . .a great stop on a weekend morning before the flea market.
Great little place to become a regular!

Love this place. I know several people who use Winner parking in Philly several times a year and everyone is very pleased with their service. I've used them numerous times over the last 5 years and the service is always great. Prices are very reasonable. I would highly recommend using Winner parking. It's a no brainier.

Amazing AMAZING so very excited they opened in our neighborhood .    The place is totally cool and hip.   Great staff. OMG the flavor explosions in the sandwiches are spectacular.       Kimchi and hot pepper jelly.   Simply delicious.   LOVE

Place used to be great when Kathy ran it. Then she sold it and it's turned into a tourist trap filled with hipsters, overpriced drinks and way overpriced food. Ten dollars for a cheese steak when I can go a couple blocks down South Street to Jim's and get a real one? fugetaboutit! 

Basically, what used to be a punk bar is now a shithole

( I wrote this months ago but it just posted. As of May 1st, 2012 I saw Marcellas's was CLOSED and For Sale. I nearly cried.)

This is my favorite restaurant in New Hope. I have never had a bad experience. I do admit that the wait is long, but that's actually why I prefer it. I host my birthday party here every year because it means my friends and I can sit back for a wonderful three hour meal (we drag it on that long, it's not THAT slow) in a beautiful, unique restaurant. If you know the wait is long -- and you go and have a long wait -- don't leave a review based on that. You knew.

So first of all let me say I'm a bit of a cheapskate.  

That said, I have no problem paying 9.00+ for a salad if it's worth the money.  

Here is what the menu said I ordered: 
Spring mix, diced tomato, bleu cheese crumbles and onions tossed in ranch dressing and topped with breaded chicken with your favorite wing sauce.

I ordered mine without tomato and grilled chicken (I know, so picky... but I want what I want.) 

Here's what I actually got: 
Lettuce, some egg, grilled chicken, and dressing.  And not much of any of it.. (Again, nothing worth 9.00) 

The whole reason I went to this cleavage factory was to get a BUFFALO chicken salad.  Instead I got a lame dinky salad with some grilled chicken.  They also show you the salad before you pick it up.  So I got a glance from 5 ft away across the bar, looked like a salad to me, a skimpy one, but didn't realize everything else was missing - so I guess it's all my fault.  

In summary: 
- My order was late, not terribly late but late. 
- No blue cheese, no onion, no hot sauce.. so it's a salad..  not a buffalo chicken salad
- Skimpy on the size for an entree salad.
