On a plus side, the staff members here are very pleasant and polite, and I may go back since it's around the corner from my office and what I got didn't taste bad...  but I'll bring my magnifying glass with me to make sure each ingredient is actually present before I accept the meal.

In general, I really like this Costco. This review, however, is about the Tire Center where an attendant there SAVED ME about $700-$500 on tires. On a previous visit, he had also saved me money. 
Yes, they are super busy and there can be a line and a long wait. Just be prepared to uber or have a ride so you can go about your day but it is totally worth it. 
Also, if you call them on the phone they are so busy it may be hard to get prices in a minute's time but they are busy for a reason and if you are persistent you can get answers but much easier in person. 
My dealership told me I needed two new tires because they were dry rotting and needed a patch on a tire (at least) at the tune of $690 (plus tax)or $36(plus tax) for patch.
So instead, I took my car to Costco, their tire guy(I think his name is Joe) who is very straight forward took me outside and explained to me why I didn't need two new tires, that they weren't dry rotting, just dirty and unless I wanted to spend the $490(cost of two tires there) I would be fine to drive. They charged me $12 to look at the nail and about an hour or so I picked up my car. 
What am I trying to say with this long review? That they are worth the trip and may save you a load of money.
Great pizza and fast delivery!  I usually use the grub hub app to order which is really convenient.

Trust that this is a well-informed praline review. I have tasted more than 6 brands of pralines in the French Quarter. See the lengths I go to for you Yelpers?!  I found Loretta's about 5 years ago and thought it was one the best sweet treats ever. But this go round in the Big Easy, I made a concerted effort to try EVERY praline place I saw to verify that Loretta's was indeed the best. Look no further, these are the best with a melt in your mouth texture and smooth finish. They are also well packaged and presentable souvenirs. Don't bother with the others. Come to Loretta's for the best tasting/best looking/best packaged pralines.

LOVE the skirt steak with chimi churrey sauce here. I've also tried the arroz con pollo and whole fish and empanadas.

I would never venture out of here if it wasn't for my puerto rican friend. Now I come whenever I'm craving hispanic food. It's the same owner as Mixto, but Tierra is much cheaper with bigger proportions. Also, you know it's a good restaurant when latin people come here!!!!

Where to begin? Well, I will start with the fact that I am an infrequent but rabid fan of Indian cuisine! I absolutely enjoy the mix of flavors and spices in any Indian food. 

The basic premise of Bawarchi seems to be good quality and flavorful dishes with the desire of solid service and friendly staff. I met my wife and a friend here after a long day of work, excited to try the new restaurant on our end of town. Our food took a little bit to arrive and we were asked if we would like a drink on the house. We took them up on the offer and enjoyed our unique appetizer (#7) while we waited. Upon arrival of our meals, which were served family style we promptly dug into chicken tikka masala, lamb pepper masala, and egg biryanis. One bite, 2 bites, 3 bites and more. I wish I had a shovel to get the food down my gullet faster! It was like an party in my mouth! The flavors were fresh and was cooked to perfection. Then all of a sudden, it was almost like an orgasm as we finished fully satisfied and ready to go to sleep. What else can I say, the food and experience was great! We will be back to try some of the other dishes. Thanks to the staff for a great experience.

It's a good tourist spot to bring people to to have the "I'm in a shiny Nashville bar!" experience. Then you take them to Robert's to have the "I'm in a real Nashville bar" experience. 

This is sort of the cars-hanging from the ceiling, big-hair big-boobs girls, cover-band, big lighted stage, three floors, bad drinks, kind of place. Service is iffy. It goes back and forth. Bathrooms have attendants, but aren't clean. 

It can be kind of fun if you go with it, and just let your soul flow with the tacky. Wear your inner Bump-it for the night. This is sort of a "Take my pic for Facebook, omg, Kelsy/Trevor/Jacob!" kinda bar. 

I have played here, and all I can say is, they don't pay the bands, so please, tip the crap out of them. On the plus side, places like this are the reason Nashville musicians  wise up, leave town, and start touring. Also why bands are so brutal about getting deals.
Terrible restaurant! They cut corners with everything. Very disappointing, especially since so many other things at the Peppermill high end.

Could Jeni's be better? I don't know how. There's always a huge line, but they've worked it out so you never feel rushed at the counter. You can discuss combinations and get samples to your heart's content, but somehow they keep everything steadily moving. The flavors are so fresh and interesting, not factory-chemist flavoring but real ingredients. I visited Nashville and went to Jeni's twice in two days. You should too!

Practically perfect in every way. This quaint, pint-sized airport looks more like a day spa than an airport and is nearly as relaxing: 21 daily departures means that there's never a queue and that shop owners are fresh and excited to see you. Match those things with close and convenient rental cars, free wifi, and ample seating and plugs, and you've essentially designed my dream airport. 

And that's where the practicality shoe drops: it's perfect... if you can afford to fly direct in and out. Luckily Alaska saves the day with non-stops to PDX and SEA that are similar in cost to major airports nearby, but only if you book well in advance. Outside of those markets, the prices will make you sicker to your stomach than the little puddle jumper you hopped on to get here. But in this case, you absolutely get what you pay for!

Good pizza - it's not Sally's in New Haven, but it's my favorite place in Nashville (and is definitely leagues ahead of the Domino's and Papa John's of the world).  The signature pie (the Perfect) has a nice mix of classic toppings and isn't too overloaded, and the Sicilian pizzas are good if you're into thick crusts.

Everything's not perfect, though (despite the name).  A number of the vegetable toppings (the broccoli and spinach come to mind) are frozen and lack texture, and the prices are higher than some other places in town - though you definitely get what you pay for.  Other than calzones, the rest of the menu is very limited, and the pastas leave a lot to be desired.  That's not really a criticism, since this place obviously focuses almost exclusively on pizza; it's just a reminder to have reasonable expectations.

A little-known treasure here is the pizza dough - they'll sell you a huge ball for $3.  If you're having friends over for a pizza dinner or want to bake focaccia, buying dough is an easy way to skip all the prep and mess.  It also lets you make pizza at the last minute, since you don't have to wait for the dough to rise.  A highly recommended shortcut.

This restaurant is in a row with a few other chain restaurants with a shared parking area off US-202 on the southbound side. There is traffic light access from US-202 northbound at Rocky Run Parkway. There didn't appear to be any shortage of parking spaces, although I would note that I visited the restaurant when it wasn't terribly busy. 

The restaurant and restroom seemed clean enough. The decor is intended to be a bit rustic/rural with pipes used as door handles and such. Service was good. The meal begins with a complimentary serving of chips. I thought the serving of chips was on the small side, but it's free so I can't complain. It's also an opportunity to try the five sauces on the table. I have to say though that their hottest sauce, the "Devil's Spit", isn't really that hot. I had to use a lot of it before it even began to burn.

For the actual meal, I had a Georgia chopped pork and catfish combo platter. In addition to one side order, this dish comes with a corn muffin and corn on the cob. I thought the portion size was pretty good, maybe enough to have leftovers to take home if you're not a big eater. The pork and fish seemed well-prepared.

We recently celebrated our Anniversary at Fleming's. My husband LOVES steak and these steaks were by far the best. Also, the Fleming's Potatos are a must try. 

Service was excellent! Worth the extra cost especially for special occasions. Will be returning soon.

Friendly staff and really fast service. The fried chicken is delicious just like it is at any Popeye's. This beats KFC every day of the week. Give it a try. 3 piece dinner is just the right amount for 1 hungry guy.

Tonight was a fabulous party in Carmels newest grocery store. You can hardly call it a grocery, there's so much to look at. If you crave it you will find it here. It's a huge store with a restaurant, sushi bar,olive bar, pharmacy, blow out and makeup salon...I could go on forever! This place is just what Carmel needed. They put on a good show tonight with music, food and a great staff. I can't wait to come back for brunch and a facial!

This stuff is by far the best stuff you can get on this side of the pond. Period.  I just recently tried the much-hyped Grom gelato(which is an Italian-based company) in Manhattan and while it was very good -- it still didn't compare to Capogiro.
Its so difficult to decide which flavor to choose since you know that everyone sounds better than the next one.  My fave is the honey-rosemary goat milk.  Who would think that combo would be so delicious?

This is my go-to spot in olde Kensington/fishtown for solid, authentic tasting Mexican food I.e not Tex Mex. 

Ingredients always seem fresh and their portions are hearty so you're always left full and satisfied. And their sauces are awesome, the green one especially. 

If you dine in, they give you free chips with fried beans and cheese - chips are perfectly deep fried and crunchy!

Their take-out is pretty solid too - no crazy long waits yet, although they did forget my sauces one time (so remind them on the phone).

Best dishes in my opinion that I've tried:
- steak burrito
- enchilada verde 
- chicken tamale with green sauce 
- guacamole and chips 

They also have an awesome range of Mexican sodas and Coca Cola which always tastes better than the American version. 

I'd skip the tres leche cake though (tastes fruitier than I prefer) and just eat more chips and guac.
Not very good. Chicken tasted like salt, salad was full of not well cut or chosen leaves of lettuce or kale. Had to ask twice to get a water.

It is always nice to go into a retail store that has few customers and many worker bees; and having a difficult time finding someone to assist. Fortunately, one man stepped up and walked away from his buddies, who were busy entertaining themselves with one of their smart phones. Lots of laughter with that group, but very little customer facing energies necessary for competency in a good retail operation. The one fellow that tried to help me save my review from becoming a one star review. Lots of competition out there and I am now heading to a competing operation. Too bad for this company. Another unhappy customer.

During our last night stay at the intrrcontinental, husband and me decided to try Shula. We sat at the bar area. At first, we were only going for two appetizers and two drinks, but we ended up ordering like 5 appetizers. 

2 orders of jumbo shrimp and 3 orders of calamari fries. It was super good! Husband was a bit disappointed of himself for not going here earlier during our stay. Oh well, we will just have to come back here again.

They have some interesting desserts. I had the macarons, which were delicious and the perfect texture. My husband liked his gigantic brownie. The rainbow confetti cupcake is adorable and would probably delight anybody.

I ordered online and picked up the food. I ordered a combination of rolls for my sister, brother and I to share. The Alfredo Roll was the best...definitely lived up to its reputation on yelp. The Mother of All Rolls was delicious. Philadelphia Roll was just okay...a little too thick for me. Spicy tuna roll was delicious. We also ordered spring rolls, which tasted frozen to me, but it's okay because I know their specialty is sushi rolls. So, I would definitely go back to this place and dine-in next time.
Juicy burgers.  Quality meat. Variety of sides. Great beer selection. Shakes looked amazing!  Service was slow but friendly.

This place is amazing. The atmosphere alone is worth the trip. Their cocktail list is seasonal & refreshing. The burger is the best I've ever had & I can't go without ordering the roasted & fried oysters. Cheese curds & blue crab gratin is also a top choice. Don't leave without trying the butterscotch dresser! Their entrees change almost daily, which keeps the menu fresh but can also catch you on a day where you're not feeling the choices - on those days, go BURGER. We absolutely love this place & are so glad it's in our neighborhood.

One of the best experiences I've had. This humble restaurant is a bit hidden behind spring garden, near the Community College of Philadelphia. I didn't pay no mind to this place for the longest time until I see so many good reviews on it.

We came here for lunch and it was pretty chill. The ambiance was quiet and homey, nothing too fancy but really welcoming.  The staff is exceptional, they are friendly and extremely professional. The language barrier could be a small problem but don't let that deter you because they are very patient.

I ordered Taiwanese braised pork belly with boiled eggs and mustard greens over rice, dan dan peanut noodles and a lunch combo that consisted of five different dim sum items and an appetizer and fried rice. Let me start with the combo. For 9 dollars you get; shrimp ha gao (steamed dumplings), shiu mai,  a veggies dumpling, pork and shrimp dumpling, pork in a soft bun. On top of this I got the chicken dumpling appetizer and one egg fried rice. All that for 8.95! All of the items were delicious, on par with china town dim sum.

The dan dan noodles was also decent, it lacked a bit of saltiness and meat. Not all places make this dish with meat but I prefer mine with a little minced pork. It was good and fresh anyhow and it came out super quick. The pork belly is the highlight here, it was soft and tender and melted over the rice like butter. It's been slow braised in this flavorful sauce that coats the entire bowl rice when poured over. 

On top of this we had two lemon honey green tea. Our total bill came up to be 34 dollars. You can't beat something like this. We had over 10 items that fed two people with a drink to go. Our waitress was very polite and offered a relaxing lunch. I highly recommend this place for those who wants Chinatown food without the hassle.

This is literally one of my favorite places in Indianapolis. What can I say? The wine is amazing! My coworkers and I have gone there for the wine flights. What a cool concept and a delicious one! The food has always been good! It's a great place for a date or a girls night out. I have yet to do a wine tasting as they have a room for that as well!

My wife had the shrimp and lobster tacos and I had the macaroni and cheese with shredded chicken.  Both were very good.  The were served warm and promptly.  I must say the mac and cheese was prepared just about as good as it can get.  We both had one of the house brewed Kolsch style beers and it was great.  I had a discount coupon which they gladly accepted.  The service was good.

Found this place nearby and decided to check it out. What a cute place! We stopped by around 6 on a Saturday night and had no problem getting in for two people. We wanted to sit outside since the weather was nice and they had a beautiful lounge style setup with couches, fire pit, lights and curtains. All to ourselves! 

The menu, man. It was one of those menus where you're trying to decide between ten different items. Lots of vegetarian and seafood options for moi! Ended up ordering shrimp skewers and a cup of tomato basil soup. Both were great, the soup was dairy free and tasted like roasted marinara sauce. If I was in the area more often, I'd come back and try some of their salads and appetizers. The desserts sounded good but the one we were interested in was out. Nice shopping center, especially at night with the lights.

RESTROOM ACCESS REFUSED.  LOL.  THEY WOULD NOT LET US PEE!  I wish I could say I was kidding.  The show was over, we walked to the hallway where the restrooms are located immediately after the sound stopped and the lights went up.  Two people ahead of us made it into the corridor and then a bouncer completely blocked the hallway saying that the bathrooms were closed.  Several normal, rational and calm people asked kindly to use the facilities and we were all told we would need to leave.  "The bathroom lights are off."  It was a LIE.  We can see people in there and it wasn't even crowded.  It's only 10:30pm on a Saturday. WTF?!?!
Food was good but the cleanliness could be improved. Sandwhiches are big enough to share!!

Where to begin? It took 20 minutes to have our order taken...at 2:00 in the afternoon with only two other families there and they already had their food. At the 50 minute point they start bringing out the wrong dishes. They left the dish and went to the back. After a few more minutes they proceed to bring out more dishes we did not order. They ask us if we would like to get what we ordered but we didn't have another hour to waste so we took what they brought because they were going to comp it. Great! All's well that ends well. After a while they brought us the bill. What happened to the comp? They didn't even bring us the bill for what we ordered but for what they mistakenly brought us, which was way more than we planned on spending. That's why we ordered what we did. After talking to them we finally reached a price but what happened to the comp? That was a very long and expensive afternoon. The only reason it's not one star is the food was excellent. Even if it was not what we ordered.

So after the "what do you want to eat"..."I don't care" conversation for the 10th million time...we picked this place...we love so many of the place in the area thought we'd give it a shot....it will be a go to place for us from now on!
We called to see how busy they where and how long the wait would be...the guy was super nice and made us a last minute reservation...but when we ended up sitting at the bar.  The bartender was sweet and very informative, she made great suggestions for dinner and all of them were delish!
We had the meatballs, the grilled spring onions( our favorite), the potato gratin and the chicken confit. Look forward to going back and trying the rest of the menu!

I love this place so much. The severs know me by name, and are always sweet and helpful. You can also tell the food is fresh, and the chefs know what they doing.  They have a huge menu, and you can even make any regular roll onto a hand roll! I only wish they delivered, but other than that I am so impressed every time I go.

So we were headed to The Grand Ole Opry and got pulled off the highway by the Jack's BBQ billboard.  We found it, just as they were closing.  The staff was very nice to let us in and made us feel welcome, even though I'm sure they wanted to wrap up and go celebrate their own New Years.  They fed us well, and made sure we were happy.  They even gave a us a Happy New Year helping of delicious apple cobbler. YUM!

The plate we had consisted of moist turkey and succulent sausage (and that's at the end of the day!)  The brisket "ends" were tender and delicious, too.  Loved the green beans, too.

It's not an easy find for tourists, but I bet the locals love having Jacks nearby.  I know I would!

Enjoyed a lovely meal here.  The owner was fantastic and so excited to share her love of her restaurant with you.  The menu has a diverse selection of entrees and I enjoyed my meatloaf very much.  

Olive is a cute new addition to the BYOB scene in Society Hill and you should check it out!

I had the wings and fries for lunch.  Pricing was a little high, but the food was just - ok.  I would go back one more time to try another meal but I wouldn't say this is a must stop location for lunch on a regular basis.

5 stars all around.  Had the asparagus to start with followed by the salmon.  Everything done to perfection. The staff here make you feel like part of the Cà Dario family which really makes everything so enjoyable all around.

Where to start.....we didn't make it to the hotel until 6am and got charged a full night. Asked for non smoking the room smelt horrible and couldn't be moved. Go to check out and the manager asks why we are leaving early and we weren't and goes oh never mind u get charged for Friday night even though the room was only for 4 hours. After check out we get a notification from the back that the hotel charged us 4 times. Go back to the hotel manager assured us it will fall off the account and only be the one charge and now a couple days later there is a other $400 charge from them for god knows what!! Never would I recommend this place to anyone unless you want to be ripped off

I was visiting in Nashville and looked up a few restaurants to check out while on vacation. Barcelona was one of those stops. My first impression of the place was that it's airy and stylish. Seemed like a popular spot for the locals. The waiter was knowledgeable about the menu. He even crossed off the items off the menu that I couldn't eat because of my dairy allergy. I thought that was a great gesture to do despite the place being packed. There wasn't much to select from after he crossed off the dairy food items. What was left on the menu was many dishes that tasted the same. There wasn't much of a tapas variety to select from. Everything was overly spicy. I ordered the beef empanadas, ceviche, broccolini, and hanger steak. What I thought was odd about the place was that the water cup were the same exact cups for the alcoholic drinks that came from the bar. My waiter accidentally filled my vodka & tonic cup with water. I had to wait like 30 minutes to get a new vodka & tonic beverage. Sort of annoying. The bathroom was a bit cramped for this large venue space. I had to wait about 8-10 minutes to use one of the stalls.

What happens when Circuit city closes and Best Buy has no competition.

A year ago, we bought a Sony TV and got a play station as a package deal. The play station was free. We bought the extended Geek Squad warranty. It's deceptively branded as "black tie service."
I asked the salesman point blank, so if this TV fails in the next two years and is a lemon, geek squad will come out and take the old one off the wall and replace it? Service is included? He said, "Oh Yes" and proceeded to tell me what has turned out to be one long string of lies. In my opinion and based on my experience thus far and assuming that Best buy trains their staff, they are training their staff to lie to us.

Here's the short version. Within a few weeks the TV fries, we call GEEK squad, first call takes 1 hour and 20 minutes. By the way, I already had a heavy duty mount on the wall, and since they were running 5 days behind, I hired a truck and two guys to bring it out. They used this to their advantage.

I was informed on the first call that since geek squad didn't hang it, they would need me to take the TV on and off the wall for them. "It's a liability issue" Wow, so let me get this straight, not only do your TV repair men not handle TV's, you are going to need me to do it for you! So I hired my employee for a couple of hours to run out and help me(three times).

A third party repair person showed up and verified the TV was messed up and then left and ordered the part. Then they came back a couple weeks later and installed a new module. the issue with the TV is that every time the SOny Play Station updates, it freaks out the Sony TV. That's right, Best Buy was selling incompatible units as a promotion to us suckers.

Flash forward, it's a year later the TV is a lemon, they agree, they give me a code for another sony TV and tell me to go into the worst managed store on the earth. I stood for 45 minutes in the TV section trying to be polite to the people who where before me. The experience went down hill from there. They won;t deliver the TV because I refuse to pay someone else to take their lemon off the wall again.
I've contacted corporate and been escalated and apologized too and assured by and now lied too, by their top people.
Go to New Egg or some other outlet. I stopped buying anything from them years ago, but tried this one last time, lured in by what turned out to be a faulty TV and a salesman full of false statements and warranties that are only partially true., This is what is wrong with American A total lack of integrity and accountability.
My Name is Paul Edwards and geek squad should be called poop squad, and best  buy needs to go..
PS The Sony play station and the Sony TV are not compatible therefore every time the play station updates, it fries the TV. Isn't that special.

Hated this place. The property manager forced me make an appointment for the day I was to move in to fill out paperwork. I did and on my way there, she called and said she was going to be 30 more minutes because she was at another location. The hours state they are open until 5, why isn't someone there during business hours? Especially when you force someone to tell you what time they will be at the office. 
I found a better, less expensive storage down the road (and locally owned- Allisonville Self Storage) so I set a date to move out online bc nobody would answer during business hours nor would they return my calls. 
I don't recommend this place at all.

Some of my coworkers had this company deliver their lunch. I noticed the Baggin's Club and thought I would try them. It was very good and the bacon was perfect. 

I was disappointed with the tomatoes on the sandwich. It is not only this place that does this but like 99% of sandwich shops do even from the area I live in. Sandwich shops new to learn to cut the center of the tomatoes out. See photo. Getting the part of the tomatoes made my experience less than perfect. The other issue was with the potato salad. They make it way to much mustard. 

Over all not bad but little things to make it better. I will come back but will stay away from the extras.

Jared was the bomb! Very informative and full of information. He kept everything interesting. So much history, he keeps the tone upbeat and entertaining without making light of any of New Orleans history. Well done.

Looking for the best cheesesteak in Philly? Look elsewhere. If you're looking for one of two proud Philadelphia establishments deadlocked in a tense battle for the glory of originality, look no further. Pat's is an experience, and I would recommend trying it...once. After that, look elsewhere for the tastiest cheesesteak.

Came here for the first time with my best friend to get our nails done. We sat right away which was great. I believe I was with the owner because he was the one giving charge and answering the phone. Instantly I noticed his station was filthy and almost wanted to ask if anything was sanitized. I got acrylics with the white tips. At first I thought he was doing an ok job but then I really started to question. After I left my nails felt extremely flimsy like they were going to break off and one of my nails were burning!!!! It's been 2 weeks and you can see ALL of my nails underneath. He clearly did not place them on right because this has never happened to me.. also one of them sure enough broke on me. NEVER EVEEEEERRRRRR again.

I am rather jaded towards the VIP theatre, as there really isn't anything that makes you feel Very Important as a customer. I date a movie fanatic and we go to a movie almost once a week, always at VIP. The service in the lounge is usually very slow, doesn't matter what time of day or how busy it is, the service is always slow. Long waits for drinks and food. On Saturday we waited 30 minutes for two poutines and when they arrived, they were cold. This is par for the course. I don't think I've ever actually been served hot food. Why do I keep going back you ask? The comfort of the seats. They are over sized, you can stretch your legs and lean back. If it wasn't for these seats I wouldn't spend the extra money going to VIP. 
So in review- eat before you go and you'll be fine!

Big patio seems really appealing, as does the thought of having Mexican food in Southern California. That's where the appeal of this place ended for me, though. Bland food, greasy chips, watery salsa, unnecessarily large portions. Nothing spectacular, nothing to write about. Blech. Seems like it would be a good meeting spot for a drink as it is large and has a large patio. After which the group should get up and walk down to many other finer establishments down the road. Service was fine.

I don't write many reviews, so please forgive the poor grade. 

This is the poorest run restaurant I've ever visited.  I live near by, and I come if only to support the local businesses. But, this place is a wreck.  Unprofessional, empty, and the cook sucks!

Please reconsider any visit here. Try any other restaurant nearby, including McDonalds.  I have tried 5 times, and it was never a good experience.

I generally dont like wine, but this place had some amazing choices! And the food was spectacular. I tried the italian meat dish, the spiced almonds, the marinated olives, and bruschetta. Delicious! I plan to go back and try some more of their cheeses. Also the service was excellent. 

Nonetheless, the prices are a little high. So be willing to drop some money.

I was intimidated by the soy sauce so I stayed away from the Bob burger and instead got the Connie burger.  It was good.  Really, really good.  I asked for onions and side of bbq sauce and it was brought out with the burger (at no addl charge).  This was better than the wildcat burger at Trident.

The bar itself is small.  It's a ring in the middle of the restaurant, which would make for a friendly experience with all the other drunken bar-goers.  The waitress was friendly, as was the cook who brought out our food.  Towards the end of the meal the waitress got sluggish and left me without anything to drink for a few minutes.  But I was so involved with downing my burger that it didn't bother me.

I will go back again.

My husband and I decided to check this place out after reading all the rave reviews. We chose to eat inside, as opposed to the Drive-In. HUGE mistake! Our waitress (don't know her name, but she was sporting the classic mullet quaff if that helps), comes over after a good 15 min. of us just sitting there waiting. (Mind you, she's just up at the counter holding the wall up.) We think she's ready to at least take our drink order. Nope. She walks all the way over to our table just to rudely bark, "I'll be back over here when I get the chance!" Ummm...ok?!? Twenty min. after that, she comes back over and asks for our order. My husband said he'd like the cheeseburger. Her response? "You want the burger with the cheese?" We got our food a few min later, and it was absolutely disgusting. It tasted like school cafeteria food; the buns were stale, patty was super dry and thin, etc. Best part of the whole experience? We go up to pay, and my husband hands her a $20 bill. As he's placing it in her hand she asks, "Are you paying with cash?" hahahaha We will NEVER go back to this hell hole.

I recently got a coat of mine dry cleaned here. I also asked to get the zipper on the coat fixed. The guy said it would be ready on saturday, which was 5 days away. 5 days to dry clean and fix a zipper? okay. Anyway, I go get my coat on Sunday. 
They charged me $25 for the cleaning and the fix. I get home and the zipper is still broken. 
Guess who's never getting my business again?
Horrible customer service... print job not ready when promised...you have to call multiple times to speak to a human being and staff who answered was incredibly rude.

I give this a five star because great food , service and clean place the staff are always very friendly and you don't have to wait long for your food. I recommend getting the taco bowl. I would definitely recommend this Taco Bell.

We usually go to the office in Warrington, but had an issue and wanted to see a doctor in the evening, so went to Trevose, even though we've had multiple unpleasant visits there in the past. We saw Theresa McGowan, the nurse practitioner. Our visit was rushed and she was rude. She acted as if my concerns were not valid. I would never take my children to see her again.

I should have looked at the reviews before ordering, maybe then I wouldn't have been surprised. I ordered the chicken Madeira to take to work, and by the time I was able to sit and eat my dinner I found the chicken completely raw. When I called to inform, they didn't offer a replacement or anything just said "sorry about that you need to call the app through which you ordered for the refund" and hung up.

Always good food and drinks at a fair price. Good happy hour with plenty of beers on tap. The place is always busy which speaks to the consistent quality. 

Better find a ride home if you plan on getting a ship wreck!

I've just tried their authentic Indian dishes and they were all great. Their chilli paneer(cottage cheese) had the perfect amount of heat and paneer was soft which I usually don't get in other Indian restaurants. Vegetarian Main dishes, dal makhani and palak paneer were incredible too. We went for lunch and it was busy. They just have two big dining tables, and other tables are tiny with 4 chairs around them which can be tricky with Indian dishes; we asked to change our table after appetizers which the staff happily accommodated for us.

Dined here for lunch yesterday and they messed up my order, brought me part of my order and never brought me my rice. I ordered sautéed eggplant in a spicy garlic sauce which was ok.  I pointed out to the server that he messed up my order and thought he was going to bring me the correct order however that never happened. They billed me for an entire meal though. *dead face stare* I may go back for one more try.

I received my first full set of lashes by  Meghan. I love them! The facility is clean Meghan was great and I appreciated the time and explanation of the process. I signed up for the membership and I am looking for forward to my next visit. Very pleased with the results.

Pleasantly surprised! Great service. Nice host. Food was great and it's priced right. Nice local spot if you are in the Milmont area, don't pass by thinking it's anything like dirty Nelly's ! Much improved

I love this place. Have been several times and never been disapointed.  Roasted naan and dip is fantastic. Entrees are always great, "awesome dude" is deeelish!  One thing, if you don't care for the flavor of lamb, order the chicken or the steak.

I've been eating here for years. Food has always been good, some of the best "bar food" in is.  I was a little worried when they changed the name and got rid of some of my favorite menu items, but they replaced them with other good grub. Good cold beer and good service.

It's and OK place. Cheesesteak sandwichs are good but a bit on the oil side. More a Tourist Trap and Kitsch type of a joint but still a fun place to visit. (the place is lit up with neon like a Las Vegas Casino) Here's what I suggest. Buy a classic Cheesesteak sandwich or two from BOTH Geno's and Pats just down the block behind you and take both of them home to the wife and kids. Cut them into 3" bite-size pieces and have them on a Friday or Saturday night for dinner while watching the Phillies, the Flyers or the Eagles. I've found in my wife and son like Pat's while I and my daughter preffer Geno's. This way everyone is happy. Enjoy!
Cute and cozy place!! The food was delicious. Went in on Friday night and it was pretty slow. Such a shame that people are not aware of this place. They have great service and the food is great.

Liked the atmosphere in this cozy vino/Mexican place. Food was very tasty and staff was friendly. Just looks like great neighborhood hangout. They have outside seating too. I would recommend it if you are close by for lunch, dinner, or just a glass of vine.

Best Sazerac anywhere. Love this hotel. The hotel is amazingly beautiful at Christmas time, but this bar is a bar. No frills just a great drink and your on your way. Your well made drink will be accompanied by some chips and nuts and most importantly, it will put a smile on your face. Probably because the drinks are strong. :)

Well, since my previous review I have been back to Osteria for an excellent meal, and even more importantly, I spent some time in Italy eating at Italian restaurant. Chalk it up to ignorance, but I judged Osteria harshly for serving its delicious pork with no accompaniment. I had no idea that this is how secondi is routinely done in Italy, and while it still bugs me, it's tough to fault Osteria for true authenticity.

So congratulations Osteria, you get another star from a semi-anonymous internet food critic who obviously has more to learn.

I went there for the first time today for lunch. Really don't waste your money.  I had the chicken burrito bowl with chicken and it tasted like a frozen heat up meal. The woman working the counter was very nice.

Surrounded by bookshelves and low chairs, I felt like all we needed to complete the library feel were some carrels - but I'm glad that we had some tasty food instead. We started with a round of raw oysters, which came out quickly and were delicious. We also sampled from the appetizer menu with the Scallops (good-sized) and Wagyu Slider Duo (so delicious - don't miss these!). We ordered the Miso Black Cod (tasty, but a little too sweet - I prefer the Buddakan version) and the 8oz Filet and concluded that the steak is the way to go here. Throw in some Jumbo Green Asparagus (soft without being mushy) and some decadent Truffled Mashed Potatoes and you have 2 people who could not manage to eat dessert, even on a birthday outing.

Was in Reno for the Tailhook Reunion . . . such a blast.  ANYway, stopped here on the way home and had their slider combination.  The meat was a bit small in proportion to the bun, which tasted like Hawaiian bread.  I think they take a regular patty and slice it in quarters, hence the strange shaped patties.  The meat was very lean and tasty.  I also liked the fries; very skinny, so they were crunchy.  A nice change from chain fast food.

Seated right away in a perfect table in the back corner.   Quickly offered drinks and apps that arrived immediately. The thousand layer bread was delicious liked the potato one the best -3 orders for 6 of us plus some Fire Cracker Fritters.  All good. Loved the Jungle Chicken, Kung pau Shrimp- not anything like chinese.
Attentive service throughout, without rushing us. Overall an excellent meal

I made it to a show here before it closes as a venue! I am grateful for this as this place was definitely an experience in itself. As everyone else has mentioned the church is hot as b***s, its all high schoolers, and its smelly, but its definitely one of a kind. 

My boyfriend and I got here pretty early for Com Truise last week, stupidly thought we could buy beers at the venue and realized we went to a show in literally a church basement. We then walked around the corner grabbed a six pack and walked back into the church. I did not know you aren't supposed to bring beer in? Oh well. 

Once the show started, we were right in the front, the crowd was mostly 15 year olds, but everyone was really polite and not pushy. We gradually got sweatier and sweatier and then luckily the show was over, I thought the sound was decent no complaints and the bathrooms were definitely better than some other Philly venues (Kung Fu Necktie I'm looking @ you). 

All in all the opportunity to see a show here reminded me of the time I was 13 and went into CBGB to get a t-shirt before it closed. This place is a Philly legend and its amazing to think that Arcade Fire played in this very church basement many years before they closed out Coachella.
Our go to Chinese takeout! Great quality and taste for the price. Love their wonton soup.
Children's Garden is awesome.....the special events are all awesome......great for family or alone.....

Amazing! I was very spoiled by a Thai restaurant where I used to live. Since moving here to the Avon/Plainfield area we have tried I believe every Thai restaurant and have been extremely disappointed until now. I have got tried the yellow curry and it was very good. I had the spicy basil fried rice during lunch and it was delicious and very filling. I highly recommend Bangkok Kitchen and I am looking forward to returning again soon. It is 'tis the season for pumpkin curry which is the bomb!
Enjoyed the workout on the 32nd floor to the view of the Superdome and smoothie King center
Had a great, healthy dining experience here. Good energy, nutritious food selection, and friendly staff--made for an enjoyable and low-key byob dinner. Good times!

I stayed at the Franklin Marrioitt Cool Springs for the first as part of a company meeting. Because I know the area well, I was expected a very nice hotel and I wasn't disappointed. 

Checking in was a breeze; however, I had requested a feather-free room and once I got to the room, I saw that it was not. I went back to the front desk and they apologize profusely and immediately sought to fix the problem. 

While I waited I sat in the bar area (not at the bar, just in the area) and was introduced to Iggy. He came up fairly quickly to ask what I wanted to drink and when I told him that I just wanted a glass of water, he did not seem happy. He brought my water and placed it on the table. I said thank you and he turned around without acknowledgement. Sufficed to say although I finished my water I didn't see him again until much later in the evening (more about that later). 

After a brief amount of time, I went back to my room and everything was changed to feather-free. The room was extremely nice and wonderfully decorated. 

Later that evening I met my colleagues for a drink in the bar and we were served by Iggy, who seemed to be having the worst day ever as he did not smile one time. Essentially all he did was point to people so they could give him their drink order. A "thank you" for making the drink did not bring a smile, head nod or anything from him. I have to say that in all my years, he is one of the worst bartenders I've dealt with. The other bartenders were much friendlier so it was not a "Marriott" way. Anyway, enough about him.

As we were there for a company meeting we had a couple of different rooms and they were both nicely designed. The employees attending to us attended to our every need and were extremely friendly on both days. I would certainly recommend this property for its meeting spaces.

The rest of the visit was great from the other employees, hotel appearance, room, restaurant (Stave, which is a separate review), shuttle, etc. It is a shame that one employee can cause a 5 star experience to be 4 star.

We ate here during Covid, and felt quite safe with the tents that they put up to separate diners. The food is also as good as ever. Had some amazing mussels and fries the other day! Service was very prompt and efficient as well.

This place is amazing! Great customer service and the food is out of this world. I had the bison burger it was prefect. It was great finding a healthy option. The manager was amazing hands down this was service at its best.

Visited 2 different times. First time was for my daughter, celebrating 21st birthday, to have a hurricane on Bourbon Street at this institution. The second time we decided to try the food. I must say we were not disappointed. Salmon,rice and veggies were great. Chicken Caesar salad was delicious. OH! Did I mention the Iced Tea? It was the alcohol variety iced tea. That is my favorite!!!
GREAT sandwiches and really cool place for lunch.

Chicken and arugula salad. 3 colleagues and I went over lunch. 

The chicken had a heavy smoked flavor but it was very tender and not dried out. The goat cheese was minimal. The dressing, herbs in olive oil was unpleasant. It was not infused oil; it was oil with herbs that all sunk to the bottom no matter how much I stirred. The oil tasted like cheap olive oil. 
I asked for another dressing, after waiting for 8 min and finally waving my arm around in the air to get the waitress's attention. The only other dressing they had was a tomato dressing that was better but still not good. The waitress said, "we don't have any cream based dressings." It's not like I asked for ranch. I'd have been happy with a simple balsamic. 

In the end I ate 1/5 of the salad and wished I'd never gone there. It wasn't just "not good." It was unpleasant.  That said, my colleagues said the brisket and burger were decent. 

Never Again.
I love their smoothies and get them frequently, but today I ordered a sandwich and there was a METAL WIRE in it. Like how does that even happen? Ew.
we stop here every time we make a trip to Reno, everyone is always helpful.  the only thing is they were out of a lot of ammo this past weekend.

I had never been in Laurie's before but on a friend's recommendation I went looking for a comfotable walking/hiking shoe. The woman who waited on me informed me I had wide feet! My Dad was a shoe man with International Shoe company. I always had properly fitting good shoes. He taught me how to fit a shoe properly. The woman informed me she was an "expert" in fitting. So I found a shoe that I liked & of course it had to be ordered. Two weeks later, I was fitted in a shoe a size larger & wider based on the "expert". I told the woman they were rubbing my heels & felt very large on my feet. She tightened them up. I left & two hours later I had blisters on my heels! Needless to say I took them back & ordered the proper size off Amazon for half the price. I will not be going back to Laurie's!

We have given this location three chances to be better but are always disappointed. Tonight's burrito was so burnt when we got it home it was unedible . The soft tacos and filling were cold as if we had placed them in the fridge for later. We really want to enjoy going here, as we do other mucho locations, but the food is just not making the cut here. If you guys change something let us know! It's nice having options in the area but this is currently not one of them.

Best Mac and Cheese in Philly. Best Fried Chicken and Candied Yams. Service is good. Love the tables/lamps. 

Only bad thing is the music is waaaaaaaaaaaayyyy too loud when you are just trying to eat something at 5pm

If I owned a retail business in Tucson I would load up the staff and take them for lunch to here. This is an operation to see in action. They are effective efficient and present. Oh and they say Thank You and make eye contact. Best part is his was established on day one and is the same every visit. Wow so refreshing.

I have had a bunch of massages before, but this one was something else. They made me feel amazing, like a new person. I was so relaxed when I left it was crazy. I highly recommend this place; I'm most definitely coming back.

Freaking awesome customer service! I had to write one for them. I ordered headphones that were at a killer price but they ran out of stock, I guess mix up in inventory but they called me right away and offered me a better headphone for the same price. Shipped quick and offered me a free t-shirt! WOW, I wish everyone had this kind of stellar service.

Dr. Liu was my dentist for a couple of years, until recently, and he's an excellent dentist.  He's not covered in my new insurance plan, sadly, and I sure wish he was.  His office staff is lovely, too.  All are very good at their jobs, gentle in their treatment of patients, and very nice to deal with.  I highly recommend him, and will return to him in a heartbeat if my insurance plan includes him again.
Mozzarella boats are great. Chicken wings are soggy. Customer service is TERRIBLE. It wasn't even busy and it took 45 min for chicken wings and mozzarella boat  Will never come here again.
It is feel like a warm fuzzy family breakfast place. They are fast and everyone take care of the customers. Price is very good and food is delicious. We like to visit it again.

Come for the beer--it's great! Always something new and interesting on tap. The food's fine, nothing too exciting. And pretty disappointing for vegetarians, especially--just one blah portabello mushroom sandwich. C'mon, Jessop's, give us vegetarians some options! (Until that happens, I'll stop in for a pint and then head elsewhere to eat.)

What a gem! My boyfriend and I ate dinner here this evening and we're thrilled with how fresh the food was. 

I ordered steamed dumplings for my appetizer and he ordered crab rangoon. Both delicious but the steamed dumplings were amazing! 

We tried the hot sake and it wasn't very good in my opinion and it could have been hotter but I will admit not to be a sake connoisseur. 

The drunken noodles were very flavorful as was the volcano chicken. 

The staff played no games when it came to leaving at 9:00. They wouldn't even let anyone that arrived after 8:30 eat in the restaurant, to go only. And they didn't mind mopping beside us in order to get out on time but they did encourage us to take our time lol 

I enjoyed the array of drinks they offered but I expected an extensive martini menu being that they advertise themselves as a martini bar... they only had 3 on the menu and they were pretty standard and not very strong .. but tasty all the same. 

I will absolutely be dining here again but I'll be sure to come early in the evening.
Love the space! Love the drink menus, fries, service! Go! Stay! Great lighting, acoustics, and overall ambience!

I have been here a couple of times and every time it's just gross or bad service. Last time I went we were served rotten chocolate milk, the time before that a hair in my pancakes. Once we asked the waitress when we done eating if we could do separate checks and she looked at us as if we had 10 heads and gave us extreme attitude  for asking. Safe to say I won't ever eat here again.

Great food but a bit pricey.  I always get the Cafe St. Charles and it's always the perfect coffee to alcohol ratio, great for a girl born and raised in NOLA.  I've lost count of how many times I've been here.  I always get something different and I've never disliked my food or had to send anything back.

I have been using this post office for just over a year. I typically use the self-service kiosks outside of business hours. Until recently, these kiosks have been temperamental at best. When they would print my postage stickers, there was a 90% chance of the stickers getting stuck in the machine. Once in a while, a swift kick would free the sticker. Sometimes the sticker would fall once I purchased my next one. Frequently, however, I was out whatever amount I paid for postage. What an unnecessary hassle. 

Recently, the machines were upgraded, and I haven't had the same problem since. 

On the rare occasion that I have gone inside to mail something, the line is typically very long, and there aren't enough employees working. The employees are friendly, however, and are quick to help me with whatever I need.

Second re-review for Shiao Lan Kung. Keeping it at 4 stars, as I think I have a good handle on what I like from the menu now.

Recently had an order with the following items for family: Steamed Dumplings, Hong Kong Wonton Soup, Chicken in Hot Bean Sauce (no bone), Salt Baked Jumbo Shrimp, and Orange Chicken.

Steamed Dumplings: FIlled with shredded pork; among my favorites places for steamed dumplings in Philly (I also recommend Lee How Fook and Sang Kee). Size is quite good and sauce is as I expected.

Hong Kong Wonton Soup: Merely good; wontons are quite small and filled with shrimp primarily; don't think there is any pork, which would add depth to the broth. Inclusion of Chinese broccoli is nice, and overall, isn't a bad option (prefer hot and sour soup, or regular wonton soup.)

Chicken in Hot Bean Sauce: Sauce is quite good and fairly spicy. Chicken taste is good but pieces are quite thin making texture a bit funny at first, but this dish grew on me. Ordered without bones, but might be better with them.

Salt Baked Jumbo Shrimp: Among the most iconic dishes here. Always tastes very good, but size is a tad bit small. Don't order it by itself. Flavor is among the best of any food in Chinatown though

Orange Chicken: Didn't try myself but relatives liked it
Fantastic Tucson "landmark". Excellent food. The drinks? Heaven in a clam shell. If you don't "like it" here, you don't belong here. It's just that simple.

I have been going to this place for a few years now. I love the customer service from these two little ladies that have worked there as servers for years. 
     One of them goes by the nickname of Shorty, and the other one, well, I can't remember her name. They're definitely senior citizens I would say they're close to around 80-years-old.  They have a real "Nana" endearing demeanor. 
     A friend and I went there for lunch yesterday and I noticed I didn't see either one of the two older ladies. I asked a male server where they were and he responded that Shorty had died. I gasped. I loved this old lady, she reminded me of my grandmother. Every time I hugged her it felt like I was hugging my grandmother. Sometimes I would just go there so I can get a hug from her before I left.
      The owner chimed in and said, "She had it coming, she was a big smoker, we told her not to smoke, she got what she deserved.  She was a huge pain in my ass anyway, I'm glad she's dead."   He said that with a creepy smile. 
     My lunch buddy and I looked at each other like, he must be joking, nobody can say something like this and be serious. Then he went on to say,
      "And the other one just had a stroke" he says referring to the other older server.      
     "Believe it or not," he continues, "I was going to shut this place down. Those two old ladies were a pain in my ass. I was sick and tired of this. But if the other one drops dead from complications from her stroke, I'll consider keeping this place open, Ha, Ha, Ha."
     My buddy and I looked at each other and realized, this guy was serious.
     Then he and the server started talking about Shorty again, her smoking and how she deserved it because she was such an avid smoker. And the way they went on about the other little old lady as they went from table to table.  It kind of made everybody in the restaurant uncomfortable. 
     Is something wrong with this guy I'm wondering? Is he a little off? Normal people don't say things like that. 
      I always love their food, and I always loved the really cool atmosphere of that restaurant. But then I realized that I missed the customer service of those two little ladies. Without them, it's not even close to what it used to be. And even so, after hearing that man talk about those two little ladies, I will never go back there.  I hope that guy rots in Hell. 
     The only reason he had my business was because of the customer service of those two little old ladies. They were sweet and nice and they made you feel welcome. 
     I will never again give them my business and I would strongly advise others not to patronize this monster weirdo with his greasy comb-over.
This place is amazing! Great food and helpful staff! I have never been disappointed eating here. Tons of vegetarian options too!

The Sylvan park area is an awesome area with food options that I think is a huge win for those that live in the area. Great walking distance and side walks with all places being family/kid friendly. 

But this isn't a review about the neighborhood. We want answers right? Ok dry pun. 

Walking in I thought Answers was a hole in the wall bar, but was surprised about how nice the set up is and the fact that it's a great option for locals. They had a wide range of drink options and patio seating that is great for most/all occasions. The food was "just" ok. We went as a group of 15 for a after work "happy hour" and nearly ordered everything off the menu. It wasn't bad, but wasn't "wow" I need to come back. The service was prompt, but our waiter seemed uninterested.. I thought it was me, but my colleagues voiced the same opinion from their interaction.  Nonetheless we ordered too many dishes to name. All decent, fairly price and portioned. Glad i checked it out, wouldn't rush back.

my husband and i regularly order from there we ordered online a combination platter and a 2 liter of soda for some guest who were stopping by when china king came they forgot the soda  and when i called back the lady on the phone was very rude to me and said the next time we order from them they will put in a free soda because they can't come back because they are totally busy and don't have time ! ok really well i oorded it and then i called e back she then said i was crazy .. okay well we got out money back and never again

Martinez Custom Painting just finished painting my house. They did a GREAT job! First off, the crew is very professional. They wear white uniforms and are nice looking! (The last painting crew we had looked like a bunch of parolees.) Then they proceeded to power wash the entire house! So nice to know that 5 years of grime weren't trapped under the fresh layer of paint. Then they carefully masked everything off. No spatter, no mess at all! The next step was to pour all of the cans of paint into big plastic trash cans so that the paint is uniform in color all over the house. They stirred and mixed so that there is no line where one can stops and the next one starts. Now get this -- never seen this before -- they sprayed and then rolled!! And to top everything off, they cleaned the windows when they left!!!! I would give Martinez Custom Painting the highest  possible recommendation.
Great food, great service! Eager to please, helpful, and casual. Sushi was good quality and we didn't feel rushed to order or finish.  The presentation was also great.  Can't wait to go again!

Dominicks continues to be on of the best pizza shops overall that I've ever been to. What impresses me most is that every time I come here everything is good. Its consistently excellent. It's clean and well run. The staff is friendly and sharp. I don't think there's anything on the menu that pops out as world class or best I've had, but everything is very very good; including of course the pizza. As a business owner it's very easy for me to spot an owner who neglects the details or has inconsistencies in their end product. I don't know this for sure but whoever owns this place is probably there very often or has some excellent staff to ensure a consistently great product. Always go out of my way to stop at this place!

Yes, please. Simply put, yes, yes, pretty please. 
Anthony's is well worth the title "high end chophouse". We started our rainy Thursday night with the beautiful entryway, where we checked my coat, gazed at the decor, and walked the way to the booth. Caleb, our server, came over fairly quickly, took our cocktail orders, and went over the menu with us. 
While our drinks were made, we were given water (much appreciated) and then quietly looked over the appetizers, soups, salads, and entrees.
First, the appetizer- crab cakes. Now, I love a good crab cake, I even have my own special recipe, but these blew us away. The special ingredients were the pickled red cabbage and carrots! The vinegar balanced amazingly with the buttery flavor of the crab, and the sauce was perfectly balanced. 
Then, we got a bread plate as an in between. The pretzel bread was wonderful, not too chewy, soft in the inside, salted nicely. The butter seemed a little strange with it, however, the French bread was paired perfectly with said butter. 
We moved on to the entrees. Now, this is a steakhouse, essentially. However, you couldn't tell from the entrees. Mister got their signature ribeye, with a side of mushrooms and spinach. The sides were very good, but that ribeye. Oh that ribeye. They recommended it medium, and we took them up on it. Beatifully seasoned, evenly cooked, but the mind blowing part was the egg. And I know that sounds odd, an egg with a steak. But this egg was incredible. Cooked so that it's almost poached, but with a soft egg white, almost as if it's been done sous vide. That egg changed the steak to be even better than it already was. 
Now my entree was the jumbo scallops, with a side of garlic frites. The frites were tasty, yes, but the scallops stole the show for me. Scallops seen fairly standard for a steakhouse, but the extras made this a wonderful exception. They have some kind of mashed vegetable (plantain maybe? I'm not sure), but they have a bean, corn, and chorizo topping that just nails the flavor. I would go back just for those scallops. 
And finally, the dessert. Bread pudding. Now, before you judge me for ordering something that usually means "soggy bread", let me describe this to you. Spiced bread, soaked in a delicious liquid (not to soggy, still a slight chew) topped with house made whipped cream. And to finish it off- salted caramel bourbon sauce. I'm not even a fan of salted caramel, but, pardon my French, oh damn. That was amazing. That is a dessert I will order again and again and again. 
Only one other restaurant has made me so content that I want to go home, put on sweats, and let my food baby relax, but I am pleased to say that Anthony's has joined those hallowed halls. Welcome to the Sweatpants Club, Anthony's. I'll return as soon as I can.

Urbanfront is a decent sized Pilates studio CRAMMED with state-of the art equipment (4 reformers, 2 or 3 Towers, a few chairs and a Cadillac).  There is also a large room for mat classes that about 12 people can be in for a class.

The owner, Karen, is a Certified Power Pilates partner - which is good news for me, as I study this method of Pilates.

There are 2 changing rooms and 2 restrooms in the hall near the studio.

Fees are competitive.  Private, Duo, Semi Private and Group classes are all offered.

I came here for a mat class and returned for a private session with Theresa which was excellent.

I plan to return again as I purchased a small introductory package of Private sessions and mat classes which was a good value.

Dozen Bakery doesn't have a homey bakery feel like some places, it's definitely more spacious than other places. I ordered a peanut butter cookie and the bacon and cheddar scone. The cookie was pretty solid, generally what I was expecting although their cookies fall more on the crispy side than the soft side. The cheddar and bacon scone is totally worth trying at least once. It was very moist, more like a biscuit than a scone, and had a nice black pepper flavor that really brought the whole scone together.

We love Carlitos restaurant. Dinner on the patio in the evening is a nice way to end the day. Good food, good music, good service.  Prices are not cheap, but hey, it's an evening event: atmosphere, music, outdoors in SB on a summer evening....

The salsas and the guacamole have excellent "sazon" - a good taste that is frequently lacking in other Mexican restaurants.  We couldn't get enough of  it!    The Carne Tampiquena  plate is very authentic and tasty.

The music on our last visit was memorable.  We had the pleasure of listening to a flamenco guitar player accompanied by a violinist. Fun improvisation going on between the two of them. It made my evening.

My only critique would be the chile relleno - not the best.  It was more like a deep fried omelette with a cheese-stuffed chile in the middle drowned in a bowl of caldillo.  Don't get me wrong, the caldillo was very tasty, and the chile and cheese were too. It was just the half inch thick dense deep fried egg that could use some improvement.  It was too heavy, thick, oily for my taste.  .

It is a focused one hour workout that makes me feel accomplished. I don't have to think about formulating a workout plan, because OTF does that for me and makes sure I get a mix of exercises that work a variety of muscle groups. I like that the heart rate monitor ensures I am accountable to myself and allows me to workout at a pace that is best for me. It feels very personalized even in a class of 20 or more! And the coaches at Green Hills are all friendly, motivating, and full of energy. It's great!

Really good food. I will never come back here, though. The service  was ATROCIOUS. We were here for half an hour and were not offered anything to drink. Eventually we got up to get our own food because it was apparent the waitress was never going to come back for our order. The counter service was no better. Our food was plated and then sat under a heat lamp while we waited to pay for it. People who walked in after us were served before we paid for our food. Finally, 40 minutes later, we got to eat something.

This is a super friendly family owned sandwich shop in Hyde Park. It's basically like a little friendly neighborhood shop that you normally find in small towns, except it's in a big city. Right when you walk in, you're greeted by the son, who takes your order, and is very helpful and knowledgeable about their food options. The food itself is good too, and many dishes have a St. Louis twist to them, like the St. Louis steak sandwich which is like a Philly cheesesteak but with provel and mozzarella instead of the normal cheese. They also have really good quality bread, and everything is very reasonably priced. If you're ever in the neighborhood, I definitely recommend checking this place out.

This place is steadily becoming my favorite way to spend my mornings! The breakfast menu is diverse enough to keep me coming back morning after morning. Be sure to try their... I never use this word but... HEAVENLY pancakes! 
The staff is friendly and efficient and the atmosphere is nice and relaxing.  So glad I found this place!
My favorite sushi spot in St. Louis. Great selection and great casual atmosphere. Sushi has been great every time I go. Spicy girl is my recommendation if decide to stop in.

Came here via recommendation from Sterling care just down the street. Absolutely love the web check-in feature, especially when you're not feeling good it's always better to not feel good at home where you're comfy rather than waiting long hours at urgent care. Filled out the online form in less than five minutes, rested at home, got a phone call just before 9 AM saying they could see me at 9:30, showed up at 9:25, sign a couple papers, waited a whole two minutes before being called back to see the doctor. Medical assistant was very professional, and I really appreciated that for an urgent care doctor the doctor was very thorough, asked me lots of questions and thoroughly explained any symptoms and medications. In about 15 minutes we found out I didn't have strep throat, just tonsillitis, prescription sent off to CVS and I was on my way. Fantastic office and staff!

We went back on our second trip to Broad Ripple, because my man loved the Jalapeno Poppers so much.

They really do have amazing bar food and good mixed drinks!  We also got a pitcher of blue moon.  Their prices were really good also and it's fun to just chill there, eat and drink, and be merry.  We have yet to try the pool tables but it looks fun.  Next time!

One of my usual go-tos.   Tonight we went for a friend's birthday and I brought a cake.  I put 3 candles in the top and just asked them to bring it out later.   Can you believe that they charged us $10.50 just to cut the cake and serve it?  They didn't even bring out the cake whole with the candle.  How can you mess up a birthday cake? Who doesn't just bring out the cake with the the writing on it?  They also didn't give us the leftover cake and kept it.  I really wanted to complain, but didn't because it was my friend's birthday.  Just a little too much nickel and diming when they are already overpriced.  Won't be running back there too soon.

Simply amazing. Yes it is a hole in the wall feel but there is not a bad word that can be said for the food. We had gator bites, slaw, fish and chips and a pound of snow crab. The Gator bites were cocked and season perfect. The fish was the same. Both of these has spot on batter to meat ratio. The slaw was a no frills down home slaw. Now the crab was the biggest surprise. I have had snow crab at many many places and it is usually anemic in size and a pound usually includes the frozen water and shells. This was a heaping plate of girthy crab goodness. There were several claws and the amount of meat in each leg rivaled King Crab. So why not 5 stars? The bickering between the staff as it was closing time and they seemed to want to get home. This is understandable but it was very annoying to listen too. They also did not have the dungeones crab I initially wanted which seemed odd for a place called crab shack to run out of. Final eh part was the price.  The food was worth it but the atmosphere was more of a locals only place which took away from the value a bit. The crab shack is a hidden gem and I recommend anyone visiting the area to stop in!
I am confused. Am not sure why this place got four stars. Went here when Bakersfield couldn't seat us. Service bad. Food gross. Convenience but would not come back. Ever.

I visited this place with my Dad after googling many of the BBQ joints in Philly to see which one we should go to. It's a good thing I did my homework beforehand, because it paid off big time. 

Just by looking at the menu I can tell that this place knows what it is doing, specifically because they offer brisket either lean, moist, or burnt ends. My Dad and I each got a 1/2lb mix of burnt ends and moist brisket, as well as 1/2lb of pork belly to share. The moist brisket was the best brisket that we have ever had! We love fattier cuts of brisket, and this brisket was so tender and juicy it was insane. I highly doubt I will find a better brisket, unless of course I go to Texas. The pork belly was also very good, not as good as the pork belly at Jimmy's BBQ but I (and my Dad) still liked it alot. The burnt ends were the only semi let down. Half of them were really good, with a char on the outside and fatty goodness on the inside. But the other half were lean and a tad dry. 

As for the sides, my Dad got the beans which, he said, were very good. I had the coleslaw and it was good as well, nothing extraordinary, but good nonetheless. 

A great thing about this place was that they gave you a jug of water. I like to drink alot of water when I eat, so it was refreshing to not have to wait for the waiter/waitress to refill my drink a couple of times. Also, the food is served on butcher paper, similar to how it is done in Texas (except for using utensils), which is cool. 

When we were finishing up our meal, one of the owners came over to us and she talked about how they (the owners) had gone to Texas to taste authentic BBQ, which taught them alot and gave them their inspiration for how they would cook and serve meat. This was cool to hear, since anyone who gets inspiration from what Texas BBQ joints do is definitely doing something right. 

Overall, both the service and the meal were great. I will definitely be coming back here again, and hopefully very soon.

This place is awesome.

I was afraid this was going to be like a dog factory - quick and dirty, impersonal, you leave feeling a sense of shame and guilt...wait that was my last night in Vegas...nevermind.

This place wasn't like that at all. They are what they are - a subsidized low cost spay/neuter clinic - but they do it so well.

They were booked out for their neutering service so I'm going to drop my boy off a couple weeks from now for that, but I went for his shots and microchipping today, and I was quite pleased.

Get there EARLY. They only do their wellness clinics (pretty much anything a pet needs besides getting fixed) Tuesdays and Saturdays from 12-2 only. I got there at 12 on the dot today (Tuesday) and there were already 7 people in front of me. I waited a good 45 minutes to be brought back. I don't blame them for it, though. More accurately, I think it's great that people are utilizing this awesome low-cost service and getting their pets taken care of.

The med tech was super friendly and explained everything to me and made sure I was comfortable with them taking my new puppy back. He got three shots and a microchip in, like, two minutes. The vet then came and explained everything to me, including all about the heartworm preventative they were giving me. They were quick and efficient like a clinic like this should be without making me feel rushed.

This is seriously the place to go if your dog or cat needs vaccinations, deworming, heartworm meds, microchipping, and of course, to get their manhood/womanhood taken away. ;) I am getting my puppy neutered for TWENTY DOLLARS next month, on a special. $20! That is $105 less than what the vet was going to do it for.

Run, don't walk, with your pup or kitty to Carol House Quick Fix Pet Clinic.

The people here have always been friendly, even on the several occasions I came in bleeding and in need of supplies. The store itself is fairly dirty on the outside, but the inside's clean.

I have a Rite Aid card, but I never have it on me and I really wish that they'd just drop the program.

The parking lot is massive!

This was the worst experience ever. Server did not communicate well. Did not know answers to our questions. I had to ask for my own refills even though he walked by several times.  I went to the bar to get my own drinks and place settings.  Food took almost an hour.  And when I got my bill they had overcharged me double the drinks. They ran my cards twice ask so I paid 240 bucks for a bill that should have been 84. Such an awful experience.

Dinner menu was reasonable for a bar menu and whilst I forgot what I ordered it was nice. Beer options are good but not extensive. Wines are nice too. Typical Sheraton pricing. Bar was very busy all week due to a large corporate group which created quite a lot of noise & buzz but pleasantly so.

Couldn't love Pucci Manuli more! Incredible toys, stuffed animals, lovies...great place for gifts. Which is why I went. The salesperson was so kind and pleasant and wrapped my gift beautifully. I will be back!

Oh how I love real European-style thin crust pizza. What Americans call "pizza" is typically too doughy to me - two slices and I'm done and and the predominant taste is the crust itself. Pizza Rev is new to Nashville and is worth giving a try. 

We opted for the "design it yourself" pizzas, the toppings are all free so you can have as many or as few as you like. I ordered a thin crust with marinara, mozzarella, Italian sausage, ham, red onions and capers.While I was helping my father with his order my order was called, his came out two minutes later. So ticket times were fast and the food was prepared in front of our own eyes. 

The concept is "serve yourself" and that included beverages. For the beer they give you a wristband and you pay for your beers when you leave, we were a little confused because we thought that we'd payed for the beer up front. Insofar as ambiance is concerned we owned the joint, there was no one there at 6:15. It made me wonder if the restaurant will survive, there was one employee there named Ladarius and he seemed to be training a couple of the others. There was no management staff there so the restaurant had sort of a high school feel, lots of employee talk and it kind of felt like a Sbarro's.

That having been said, I'll be going back because of the quality of the product and fast service. Check it out, y'all; it's right off 21st on West End, perfect for trips to the Vanderbilt area.
Phone Staff is rude. There is not voicemail greeting. Simply unprofessional.

Love this place reminds you of your grandma's home cooking! Everything is made from scratch and is absolutely delicious they make their own fresh horseradish and have amazing pies! My favorite part is the relish tray I don't know why I just like it!

I only stopped in for some beer after lunch and the selection was right on.    
The Phils were on and ahead by 5 so the awesome bartender tuned between the Tour de France and the game.  They had some craft beers from California which I tried and was impressed by.  I hope I can return to get some food some time soon, but for now the staff was super friendly, the atmosphere relaxed and it seemed to be a good, chill spot.
I love lucky wishbone for a fast food place there chicken is soon good I like it alot and they have been around Tucson since the 50's

Anthonino's is an unsuspecting looking restaurant from the exterior nestled away on The Hill. The menu collides Italian and Greek classics into a diverse group of offerings. We started with the toasted ravioli (as recommended on the menu by Guy Fieri) the ravioli were large and crisp with the meat based filling looking a little funky since it was a grey mush, but the taste was spot on. For entrees I had the Tutti Mare a seafood post with crab claws, squid, clams, and shrimp. The seafood was succulent and properly cooked not too chewy, and at the recommendation of the waitress it was served in a pink sauce which went very well with the fresh pasta and sweetness of the seafood. Dessert was the largest piece of baklava I've seen and Cannoli's. Both very traditional but done well.

Great sports bar!  Every seat in the house had a view of at least one TV and two of them are big enough to be movie screens!  They've got eating areas, drinking areas and even a playing area with pool tables, dart board and an air hockey table.  This looks like it would be a fun place to be on game day.

On top of the great ambiance, it has very good food.  It's bar fare with a few extra twists (the mahi mahi sandwich was very good!).  The portions were good for the price and the food was well cooked.  The desserts were pretty good too but over priced.

There are 4 Frenchy's in Clearwater Beach, but this one is right on the beach with beautiful views and live music. We were there for sunset on a Friday night and there was about a 25-minute wait to be seated outside. It was a little chilly out, and they had heaters which made it very comfortable. The sunset was perfect and the food was excellent. my son had the kids fried shrimp, my husband had the fried grouper nuggets and I had mahi Florentine, with onions tomatoes and spinach cooked in a delicious coconut sauce.  We also had an ahi tuna appetizer. Highly recommend for the view and the amazing, affordable food!

This place is terribly unorganized and the staff is very sloppy. I was excited to try it because I love the Lucky Dill, but this place is sure to tarnish their reputation. Then again, their reputation has rapidly declined since they were bought out. They were also out of pickles...(this is affiliated with the Lucky DILL).
