They also use the previous buildings restaurants menu (Sports Legends), very lazy.

I read a review about these people being stuck up. I would say this is far from the truth. I ate at Cochon restaurant last month and then the butcher twice this weekend. The people are friendly and patient. I will say that I had a young person who said I had to wait for something but then the butcher overheard me and stepped in tale care of me. I think that girl must have been new. All of the older  workers act like they actually have a stake in the company. They take pride. They are fabulous. Food is a winner, too.

Service was horrible and food was mediocre.  The waiter was extremely rude and not at all helpful.  The seats were very uncomfortable and when we asked to change seats, we were denied.  The atmosphere seemed o.k., but with the rude waitstaff and so-so food, it's not worth my time or money to try again.

I absolutely love getting my hair done by Alex Sanchez. I naturally have very dark brown hair, which is pretty harsh against my pale skin, and Alex always dyes it a really flattering shade of blonde. She is really willing to take the time to make sure it looks good. Just last time, I went from long hair to shoulder length hair. I was a little nervous beforehand, but after seeing her work her magic, my hair looks phenomenal and I have received countless compliments on how bouncy and voluminous it looks, which is amazing when your hair is naturally kind of thin. The color looks deep, but not artificial and fake. Love Alex Sanchez, she is better than any hair stylist I have ever had.

I have used WWW for several years with great confidence. When ownership changed I hoped for the same great service and that's what you'll have with Wynter and her team. Very thoughtful and caring people all. They supported me and my dog during a surgical recovery (turning "walks" into "sits" on a moments notice, with many changes in schedule along the way) as my pooch had to take it very easy. What a relief to know people who knew her were keeping a close eye and concerned about the human, too!

My friends and I visited Front Street Cafe for dinner. We were in town visiting Philly and had read about this restaurant. The cauliflower appetizer was outstanding. But my kale salad was dry and the leaves weren't cut--they were the size of my hands. It was clear the salad hadn't been mixed or properly prepared. I asked for extra dressing (which was tasty) so I could add it to my salad and it arrived twenty minutes later. To top it off, they charged us 50 cents for the extra dressing. It's a shame because we really enjoyed the rest of our experience.

I don't even know where to begin....well, yes I do.  My trip to Vango began by getting a full pat-down at the front door.  Seriously, four polite, well dressed people getting patted down and having bags searched on 18th St at 10:00PM on a Friday night was absurdly comical.

Even before the TSA style entrance, I had problems with Vango.  We came down with a TravelZoo voucher that was unfortunately expired, so only the price paid was still valid as a gift certificate.  We were going to get four drinks and head up to the roof, but that plan was derailed when an obnoxious bartender started screaming (literally) for her manager to come and take care of "these people with a voucher."  

The even more obnoxious manager comes over and says, you can't use that after 9:00.  I told her that there's nothing on the voucher that says that, and it's not even a promotion since we're just using what we paid for it like a gift certificate.  Her response:  "We decided to put a policy in place and there's nothing I can do for you, have a good evening," and she just walked away.  

I will forfeit the cost of the voucher, and hop on the bandwagon of Vango bashers out there to see to it that this place doesn't survive another six months.  Do Not Go Here!

The Indianapolis Airport looks nice and modern.  It seems to be going through a construction period where there are lots of empty storefronts with "coming soon" signs on them.  This is in Feb 2020.

TSA Pre Check was only at Concourse A so if you have a flight in Concourse B, you may find yourself walking further than you planned.  After walking to the B side, I found that many of the people movers weren't operating, no "directory" so I couldn't tell what dining options there were, and a lack of seating when you did find a dining option.

As someone not eating meat, I didn't find a lot of vegan/vegetarian options at the various places.  So plan on having your own snacks or searching through the pre-made Farmers vending machines or sandwiches that may or may not be friendly for your diet.

The appearance is nice, but it still needs some work to cater to the variety of travelers.  The bars are packed and if you wanted to wind down with a drink before your flight, good luck.  It's not overly busy on this travel day, but I can see lots of frustrated travelers if there was an event going on.

Fantastic food and cocktails.  I got the large shrimp dish with a cabbage-grapefruit side that was amazing.  The seafood gumbo was also delicious and had very intense seafood flavor.  Cocktails were also very good.  My husband got the cobia and we split some chocolate-coffee ice cream for dessert.  Service started out great, but then a different server ended the evening and was rude.  Definitely would have been a 5-star experience except for the male waiter at the end who acted like he wanted us to skip dessert and hit the road.  It was near closing, but 20min before 11 and we were hardly the last people in there.

Got the tilapia and it was cooked just right! There was stuffed crab meat and other things in the dish but it was all so good! I picked off some of my friends food and all of their food was just as delicious as mine!

This was one weird hotel.

We checked in on a Thursday night and the hotel was quiet and serene. There was no one in the pool area, so we decided to check it out. The pool water looked green and cloudy, so we opted against jumping in. The hot tub looked welcoming, so we spent a nice relaxing 15 minutes in there and went back to our room. 

The rooms are BIG, no doubt about that. You get a living room area with a couch and TV and table. There was a small kitchen area - sink, microwave, and fridge. That was a plus! 

A door separates that area from the bedroom, which had a large bed, TV, table and closet. We were pleased so far.

Then the weekend hit and the place went from quiet to crazy.

We attended a managers reception the next evening - we were told it was from 5:30-7:30pm. We weren't able to even have any snacks because there were no plates. So we had to wait for a while - and were then able to indulge in chips, salsa and peanuts. Big whoop, but hey, it was something.

We had a beer and a mixed drink and went up for one last drink before 7:30pm. That's when a security guard at the bar told us it was now a regular bar, no open bar. We were confused, as we had been told by the receptionist that it was until 7:30pm. We had also gotten our last drink after 7pm. We didn't want to cause a fuss, and we went back to our room.

The pool was incredibly crowded once the weekend hit. I'm not sure what happened, but there were a million people in there at all times. Where did they all come from? There were also people hanging out and leaning on the balconies at all times. Not a big deal, but it didn't seem very private. I had the curtains on our room closed at all times, because there were lots of people at all times.

The next morning, I was awoken to the sound of loud music next door. It wasn't our room neighbor - it was the cleaning woman! She must have been blasting the radio next door. Not cool! There were some people trying to sleep (like myself).

When she cleaned our room that day, she also forgot to stock the room with bathroom towels. Lovely. We had to get those from the front desk.

The rooms that were on our same floor, but further away, smelled of cigarettes and pot. They were smoking rooms. There must have been a bachelorette party going on, but that's no excuse to have part of the hotel smell like a smokestack. Gross.

The breakfast in the morning wasn't so bad. We got French Toast custom ordered and had some eggs and whatnot. It was good, and the hours on weekends extend for breakfast. That was a plus.

The area itself doesn't seem too safe, but we always found parking and had no safety issues while there.

Overall, I don't think I'd return to this hotel. There were lots of people - so much so that I couldn't enjoy the pool - and the open air atrium in the middle of the hotel seemed strange and made it a long walk to our room, which was no where near staircases and elevators.
Fast service. Honest pricing with plenty of notice and chat about options. Great people to work with. Will be where I take our family's cars from here on out.

Spectacular food. A little out of my usual lunch but definitely  a terrific place to go. The tea was like a milkshake and the soup definitely  hit the spot. If you care to experiment with out of the ordinary flavors. This is the spot.

They were going to charge me $1017 for the lenses alone!  Frames additional of course. They said it won't cost me that much because my insurance pays some. You better have really good insurance. By the time your insurance is done paying your balance is still going to be what you might pay elsewhere with no insurance. Nice people, immoral company.

Just wanted to add an update: The service and food at Dubu remains top notch during Covid. The added safety precautions and increased cleaning makes us feel safe when enjoying some of our favorite food. I'm so grateful I can enjoy my comfort food during this time.

This is my go-to spot when I'm in the mood for hibachi grill.  Service is excellent, the food is excellent, the chefs are personable and the owners work hard to please their customers.  I have never had a sub-par meal here and always leave with a full belly and a smile on my face!
My roommate and I both got severe food poisoning within two hours causing us to miss work and that day's pay.

Comrade brought it! Maybe I was raised too close to the foothills of the Cascades, but a moody Slavic themed bar filled with comfort food makes a lot of sense to me. I think my favorite thing about Siberia is that get the illusion that when I step outside again I'll be met with a dusting of snow and it won't be 125 degrees out.

I stumbled upon Priscilla's class when I wanted to try something new and find a fun, interesting way to exercise. A little more than a year and a half later and I still love walking into the gym knowing that I will sweat, sing, and dance to a great, ever-changing playlist that mixes fun and calorie-burning moves to create an inviting Zumba class. To borrow from Pitbull, whether you wanna feel sexy or simply get moving, join Priscilla Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays. OH YEAH!
Great experience with my basic manicure and pedicure Groupon. Very kind and my nails look amazing. Melissa is great. She took her time and did a perfect job

Amazing farmers market. Behind the factory at Franklin, so after the market you can go inside for more craft stores, awesome food and an amazing antique store. The market had all the normal fresh produce, tons of food and drink vendors, and many flower vendors. M wife always gets Amish bread and milk, and this time we even got grass Fred free range meats. Neat thing about this farmers market is that theirs so many different vendors offering stuff that you can mix or match! 

Grocery list: grass fed pork, fresh goat milk, sourdough bread, cookies, brownies, fresh carrots stalks and all, fresh clover bee honey, home made soap and eucalyptus bathing salts, and we got lunch from the crape food truck and tea from a local stand! Even better was many stands used ingredients from other stands their to make their food, like the crape food truck using fresh produce from the market that day!

Highly recommend!

I can't say enough about this cigar lounge in the french quarter. Best selection of cigars downtown,
Best selection of spirits in the city!! Great atmosphere amazing bartenders and customer service second to none. This is the place to hang out if you want to relax and enjoy the best cigar lounge in Neworleans. I will be back every time I come to this incredible city!!

This company is a bunch of criminals. Credit card was stolen that was used for auto payments. Trugreen never contacted us to say that they were not getting payments and continued to do our lawn service the entire summer then stopped in the fall. When we called to ask why they stopped is when we discovered that he credit card was the older number of the stolen one. We made a lump payment to catch up. Few months later we are getting calls from collection agencies asking for money. We are completely paid up to date at this point. We did exactly what the true green reps said to do and not once did they mention anything about it going to collections. 
On top of it all they have done OUR service on the neighbors yards and charged us! We never would have known if the neighbors didnt tell us. Bunch of incompetent workers at Trugreen. 
I would never recommend them to anyone. Stay as far away as possible.

I keep going back here because it's convenient to my house, and it's open on Sundays.  I always regret it.  After a visit here, my polish always seems to look dull after about a day, and it never seems to last.

Good dim sum with a side of bad customer service.

I really like the dim sum here. Unfortunately, I've been here a handful of times to know that customer service is a nightmare. Don't get me wrong, I absolutely understand the busy-ness and COVID restrictions, but that shouldn't excuse lying to your customers or being stingy over sauces that come with your orders.

Every time I've come here, the staff seemed rude and irritated. I ignored that at first. But upon leaving with the food, I noticed that they would never give enough sauces. This happened every time I got takeout, which is significant enough for me to notice. But again, I ignored it. Until my mom came to town to visit.

I took her here. We ordered two XLB and pan fried soup dumplings, and paid in cash and tipped them right then. We also asked for vinegar and chili oil for the sauces. After waiting 20 minutes or so, we grabbed our bag and my mom asked if the sauces are in there, the waiter nodded. Me, being untrusting of their business and attitude, opened the bag there to check, and lo and behold, they only gave one tiny cup of sauce... for THREE things... and had the audacity to lie to our faces, despite us tipping them. I went back and requested more, and the waiter unwillingly left and came back with some sauces. When we got home, I tried to cup of sauce they gave us initially, and it was dumpling sauce, the one that we didn't request at all. I found that to be absurd.

Needless to say, my experiences here have put a bad taste in my mouth. The dim sum isn't good enough for me to justify dealing with bad customer service every time.
So delicious! Food was amazing and our server Kurrie was so nice. Manager made sure we were enjoying ourselves as well. Definitely coming back soon !

Came in for lunch with two co-workers was seated pretty quick. Got appetizer pretty quick waited for 20 minutes to get main dishes. One of the dishes was wrong and was not the correct hamburger. They offered to take it back and get the right one best we could not wait because we had to go back to work he accepted the burger anyway. The waiter was well aware of this. After eating I figured there would be some kind of discount forgetting the wrong item nothing. Paid for the bill and realized that they also added two cheesecakes on to the order that we never ordered. Still no kind of corrective actions were taken very poor customer service at this location highly upset will not eat there again as we work around the corner.

The people who work there are nice for the most part but occasionally you encounter the employee who doesn't seem happy to be there.
My mother is a patient as well as me and we don't have any complaints..
Just know that it's the same as any doctor's office - you'll be waiting a LONG time. Even after your appointment time. Bring a book.
The doctor seemed to know what he was doing but came across as condescending at times.

This is located right across the street from Hyde Park Cafe and I always remembered it was a vacant space back in the days of my college days. 

I came in to have a little dinner with some friends. I made reservations but was surprised that it was not too busy for a Saturday night. I decided to get the Steak Frite. It's a shame I don't remember our server's name but she was wonderful. My steak came out salty due to the seasoning on top and I'm usually not the type to send anything back to the kitchen unless it's really not edible. The server came by to ask how the food was and I just mentioned the steak was salty but the fries were great. She apologized and said she'd get a new one started for me. I felt terrible because like I mentioned, I never send food back! The manager also came by to apologize and gave me complimentary chips and guac which was very nice of him because we all know, guac ain't cheap!

I also ordered the Borough-Vardier which is similar to an Old fashioned and it was very light but strong (if that makes any sense haha). I has two of them and the server actually took the second one off due to the steak mishap so I can tell customer service here is great!

My friend ordered the salmon entree which was very yummy. The fries with garlic aioli with my steak were so good too! All in all, I had a great experience here and will definitely be back a!

Pretty cool spot. Great location of course, on State Street in Media. The bartenders have always been nice over the past few years I've visited. I especially like the "Orange Crush" cocktail. I hope that always stays on the menu!

Don't move here. Listen to me folks, management will lie to you, promise to fix air conditioning and electrical outlets, and never do it. Trash everywhere (not just management) with people throwing their garbage into an overflowed container. Watch your WiFi security, this complex cares  nothing if criminals steal your personal information or damage both your cell phones and computers. Squeaky floors, outrageous air conditioning bills, and a general manager who does not care about her tenants. Don't be mislead by the superficial facelifts they put on the buildings, out unit was termite infested and the manager did nothing about it. She also did not abuse by federal law which stipulates children of the opposite sex, above the age of six, can not share a bedroom. They are homophobic, if you are gay, stay away!

My husband and I made a visit to Philly on Thursday not knowing about this restaurant as we were walking to the market area, we passed by  and they were just opening for the day.. 
Lucky lucky us...
Walking in we were taken by the atmosphere, gorgeous decor, reminded me of the  El San Juan Hotel in Puerto Rico. We felt immediately welcomed by Nina the hostess who was very friendly and  attentive.. she was very happy to introduce us to the restaurant. 
We were immediately seated even though they had just opened around 11:30 or so and handed the menu by the very very nice waiter..  you  could tell he really liked working there and was 
We ordered the grilled octopus... decadent, tender,  perfectly grilled with arugula and wonderful slices of red potatoes yummy.... the lobster ceviche.... exquisite, perfectly balanced flavors....
I had a recommended peach mojito... delishhh!  Just the right amount of mint, peach and lime. 
My husband had the suckling pig sandwich which was tender, lean and full of flavor.. 

As we were taking care of the check, the chef sent a complimentary dish of bread pudding....  amazing just right, not too sweet as typical bread pudding dishes. He came out to say hello, we could tell he was passionate about the food and the restaurant, invited us back.  

Can't wait to go back and enjoy the outside area, so beautiful and tranquil...
We have been to many Latin restaurants and are very familiar with the cuisine, 
The Havana room is on the top of our list... we will definitely return with our friends real soon.

I enjoyed my experience here and food.. Comfort food on my lunch break. Mike was very accommodating and had very great customer service, something you don't find often anymore.. will be back again. My food order has no issues..

This was probably the worst experience I've ever had with a local restaurant. I tried to reserve a table for 13 people, only to be told that they will only take reservations for a minimum of 10 people, and there has to be a minimum of $30 spent per person. (They actually said $30 in revenue per person - that's how they phrased it to me - the inquiring customer) Needless to say, I'm not wanting to guarantee that I'll spend $390 for a 10 year olds birthday party, so instead I decided I'd just go to the restaurant an hour before I was meeting my party. This should be plenty of time for a table to open up. I show up, tell them how many people are coming and what time is expecting them. They say no problem, give us 45 minutes to an hour. Sounds perfect. Exactly 2 hours later, they tell us a table just paid and will be open soon. I would have left by now, but I'd already spent $60 in games to keep bored kids at bay, so I gathered everyone up, we went to our table and waited another half hour for our order to be taken. Another 30 minutes pass, we eat the sub-par food, and I tell the hostess it's my son's birthday, she said they'll bring out a brownie Sunday for him as a surprise. At least there's that I suppose. Another 20 minutes go by, our waiter comes out and walks right by our table blurting out "his birthday brownie is on its way"....  Thanks for ruining that surprise pal. More time passes, the kids get tired of waiting again, we dismiss them to go play while we clean up, and finally they bring out the brownie to an empty table. At this point, we pay the bill (well under $300 mind you), and ask for a to go box for the remaining food and brownie. I box everything up, and start to carry it out to the car with the presents, and I dropped one of my to go boxes right at the hostess desk (nothing spilled, just dropped it), and no less than 4 employees stood there watching me attempt to gather everything back together. In fact, another customer held the door for me to help, since none of the employees could be bothered to even ask if I needed help. 

All in all, I'm glad my extended family was there with me during this visit, because it saves me the trouble of having to explain how terrible it was, and why none of them should ever bother going. 

I'd like to say the  only semi-redeeming part of the whole experience, was a $3 jack and coke, but it was served with a lime, which was weird as it was, but it made sense once I tasted how watered down the drink actually was. So the lime was just to give some sort of flavor I assume. 

Definitely never going back again.

Edit - worth mentioning I literally created a yelp account just so I could rate these guys.

They were so friendly and helpful! My little pupper loved these ladies. I had just gotten my dog from Indy humane and she was super skinny and hadn't really eaten. I went here and they gave her some treats that she loved and got her eating. She warmed up to them and I doubt she will be afraid to go back like dogs usually are with the vet.

So much potential! Cheddar biscuits were great. Maine lobster was tasty but $50 for 2lb seemed a little pricey.  Salad was over dressed.  Draft beer selection was good but could expand number of tap handles.  Lemonade was great and so was the chocolate lava sundae.  

Service needs help.  Need to be trained and pushed to have sense of urgency.  Tables were not being bussed despite line out the door.  We had a 5:30 reservation but we're not seated until 5:50.  Server did not clear plates so we ate dessert with our plates from appetizers and dinner still on table.  Both server and manager, however, were nice and generous.  

Lobster pot needs a makeover.
Stopped in for a late lunch and was pleasantly surprised by this little gem. Good prices and tasty food. Had a veggie wrap and it was great. We will definitely be back!

We ordered delivery last night to celebrate our anniversary, and we were so impressed with everything! Arrived promptly, well-packed, and hot. The brisket was absolutely perfect; we tried appetizers and a kids meal and they were delicious too.
We dine out so rarely these days - thanks for a great meal!

It's a shame this place loses a star for something as simple as security and parking, but allow me to highlight the positives of this venue! 

The Fieldhouse has great acoustics. No matter the event, your view is almost certainly worth every penny. "Nosebleeds" hardly exist with its layout. (They are there, but even these seats surpass many other venues I've been to.) The Fieldhouse itself is not difficult to navigate through; signs are posted everywhere. Ushers are there to help, but you're better off navigating your own way. (I'll get to that in a minute.)

Prices are reasonable for concessions. You can spend $12 for a drink and a hot dog or nachos and be full. Beer, of course, is more pricy, but that's standard. I don't justify spending $8 for 16 oz. of liquor anywhere, and that includes here. But, it sells. The Lightbound Courtside Club is a neat little place. Expect to spend $50+, however. The food is plentiful but average. The servers were nice enough. I'd go once for the experience, and maybe save it for special occasions from then on. 

Restrooms are plentiful, and clean (a major plus for someone who has a slight phobia of public restrooms). 

The overall feel of the Fieldhouse is welcoming. There is plenty of memorabilia of Hoosier traditions to be seen. 

Now, to the negatives, which may be not even a big deal:

Security is subpar. The ushers are around, and smiley, but not necessarily helpful. One took me in the complete opposite direction of where I was supposed to be. No biggie, I needed the exercise I guess? We attended a concert here and showed early. Times to be let in kept being extended. Security didn't have an answer, and was nonsensically changing lines around. A small annoyance, as we had been waiting for some time only to be cut by people who showed up long after we did. They weren't particularly helpful, but not nasty or rude. Could have been addressed better, and this is a problem even outside of concerts. Maybe something to consider changing.

My daughter and I had the opportunity to attend the Yelp Elite Event at Color Me Mine! Walking into the building, we felt very welcome and excited to get started. SO MANY OPTIONS to paint, from plates and cups, to figurines and everything in between. We had several colors available to chose from and they were very encouraging with different resources to help decide what you want to paint (Pinterest, stamps, tape, employees, etc). At one point, my daughter dripped some paint where it didn't belong. It was easier than we thought! They even came by later to check in with her to make sure she was happy with the fix and see how it turned out. They offer a VIP deal that gives you a discount on the pieces that you paint, in addition to NO painter fee for the year. This is an amazing deal! I can see myself visiting Color Me Mine many times in the future! Amazing experience! Can't wait to see our final products when they're done being cooked. ;) Thanks again for another amazing event, Yelp! And thank you Color Me Mine for hosting a beautiful event that introduced us to a cool new business!

We have a large property and were installing our fence in phases. We used a different contractor than Heritage to install the first portion of our fence - cedar, dog-eared - very standard. To finish the remaining portion, I decided to shop around since I wasn't thrilled with our first guys. The fence was good, but some boards had to be replaced soon after install and I was wary of their quality. So when we had to complete the fence I read the glowing reviews on google and gave Heritage a call. Todd came out, was pleasant, gave us our estimate/contract, and we signed. The fence was installed and looked great for about 18 months. About 6 months ago we noticed a few wobbly spots, but nothing major. Then about a month ago we noticed that the entire length of fence, installed by Heritage, had come loose from the posts, upon closer inspection some nails never even connected the post to the panel, and the fence now leans about 2-3 feet forward and is potentially pulling down the first section we installed 2 years before that one AND our fence that it is connected to, installed 15 years ago and still standing upright. 
We called them and expressed our very real concern and there was little care or sense of urgency. They sent Todd out one week later. Todd agreed that it was not installed well and they would need to reinstall the posts and he would get back to us. Of course, we assumed he meant, he would get back to us with a time when they would come to fix it. Nope. They sent us a proposal where WE were expected to now pay them to fix their shoddy work. It was about $400 on top of the $2600+ we had already paid. We called the office and spoke with Chris, the owner. He agreed to come to see the workmanship for himself - though only after laughably citing wind as being a likely factor in the fence falling down - and came out on June 3.
During our June 3, 2020 conversation Chris mentioned numerous times that the soil was the issue causing all of the posts to become loose and compromise the fence. This runs counter to the opinion of the company's estimator, Todd, who inspected the fence two days earlier and said the reason for the failure was that the posts were not set deep enough. Both also mentioned that pine needles could also have caused the posts to list 30 degrees after just two years, so at least there was some consistency. Apparently the wind and pine needles and clay deviously conspired to only topple the fence Heritage installed and not the adjoining sections installed by other companies.
Chris's primary argument was that if Heritage or its installers knew about the clay on the 2018 install date, they would have used concrete, so the faulty workmanship of Heritage was ultimately the responsibility of the homeowner (me). In the proposal/contract there is no mention of clay, any homeowner responsibility to detect clay and notify Heritage, or alternative post-setting instructions should clay soil be found, as Chris erroneously noted numerous times. In addition, clay was never noted by the estimator (either in 2018 or 2020) nor the installation crew. Only when the owner comes out and refuses to stand behind his product is clay cited.
In all fairness, I did chuckle when Chris dug his hand into the soil, pulled up some clay, and said "See? This is clay" like he had uncovered some secret substance heretofore unknown to mere mortals. 
Most egregiously is that when asked if Chris stood behind the workmanship, he responded that he had nothing to do with the company two years ago when the job was complete, yet the 2018 proposal we received was sent from his email address, with a signature for good measure. How this desperate and easily-debunked lie aligns with Hertiage's "family-owned" mantra is something for them to wrestle with. You can see the screen grabs in this post. 
You'll also note that there is no time limit to the warranty indicated in this proposal/contract, so I am still wondering how he can hold customers to an undocumented, one-year warranty while trumpeting a five-year warranty on his office phone and advertising. 
We have contracted with a reputable company to fix Heritage's mistakes.
Finally, we welcome the inevitable response from Chris where he acts like the measured, rational party. Really looking forward to him explaining away the lie about him not being with the company when the fence was installed. Perhaps we doctored the email address and proposal/contract. In Heritage's world where clay is a mysterious substance only homeowners can detect and pine needles can push over fence posts, I guess anything is possible.

We unintentionally adopted a stray cat that wasn't spayed. She was an outdoor cat, but we fed her. Then we decided we wanted to keep this cat & be responsible for her, especially after I recognized her semi-tolerance of Gilligan, so of course we wanted to have her fixed. Yeah, Kitto had an attitude toward my own cat, who had sorta tolerated our other *dominant* cats over the years, including her own recently-deceased sister, and she obviously disliked both of our dogs. But Crayola (a mostly outdoor cat) can look out for herself after 12 years with us, so she was less of a factor in taking in a new cat. She isn't missing meals. 

Anyway, I've digressed... I chose to take Kitto to Harmony for spaying after I'd read several complimentary recommendations in our neighborhood's Facebook group. Literally 7 minutes from my house on back roads, I loved their convenience. We were also very happy with their prices, AND excellent service, plus Kitto had no complications. Another bonus, I'd called on the Tuesday before Christmas, and they had an open spot that Saturday. Super easy.

Plus, his rabies shot was expiring & I needed to get more heartworm pills for him. Again, Harmony was able to accommodate my schedule with a morning appointment later the same week. The vet that saw him was friendly & clearly LOVED animals. She seemed to really like Gilligan, which I definitely appreciated.

I love that Harmony is super close to my house. But even more than that, I really love that everyone working there genuinely seems to love their job AND all the animals. That means a lot to me. I'll continue to bring my pets here since I've discovered this gem in Town & Country.

We made the mistake of allowing Sloane Moving and Storage to move us and to pack about 10% of our belongings that we had not packed. Sloane totally defies the principle of conservation of matter! What had been 10% of our belongings was so padded by Sloane's movers that it became 80% of our boxes!  

Sloane's slogan "We baby your furniture" actually means that they place one of two small items into a 4 ft by 4 ft loosely taped, flimsy carton, and then shove dozens and dozens and dozens of sheets of wrapping paper in order to fill their huge, unwieldy and badly-smelling carton. Needless to say, because of Sloane's packing, it was very difficult to find our belongings!  Since we have to pay for trash removal in our new home, it took nearly 3 months to dole out all of their unnecessary, voluminous wads of wrapping paper into our weekly trash without incurring charges for bulk pick-ups. 

For some bizarre reason, Sloane packed us by combining dirty items such as toilet plungers or trash cans full of garbage (obviously not meant to be packed)  with clean clothing. We had to wash or dry-clean every single article of clothing. 

In their defense, we thought they were friendly, and we didn't blame them for their truck breaking down on the turnpike with a flat tire. There was very little damage to the furniture and our belongings.

What did annoy us was that the morning after our move, we got a call from the man in charge of the move telling us that the owner wanted an additional $350 from us since he made a mistake in his calculations.  We found this demand for more money the day after the move completely unprofessional.  Sloane made everything more difficult, and we would advise people to avoid using them. At the very least, if you do use them, then make sure you pack all of your belongings yourself, and don't pay them to pack your stuff for you.

as a native of Philly people are always asking me where to go to get a good cheesesteak.

before i can answer that...a little lesson:

1. it's a "cheesesteak" or "steak"  not a cheese steak, Philly steak and cheese, steak and cheese sandwich etc.  get it straight!  wikipedia will account for these other names for outsiders, but their really just catering to the simpletons.  http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheesesteak

2. if you're outside a 50 mile or so radius of Philadelphia, it's not really a cheesesteak.  it's a fact.  it's just the way it is.  cope.  of course certain exceptions do exist but YOU are not qualified to make that assessment.

3. cheez whiz is a very appropriate way to account for the "cheese" part of the steak.  when ordering one's steak with cheez whiz, simply asking for "whiz" will suffice.

4.  it's not a steak if it doesn't have onions.  to order your steak with onions, one need only ask for a steak "with."  "with' is the universally understood request for onions on your steak in Philly.  

5. a steak with marinara sauce on it is referred to as a 'pizza steak."  that's the way i lime em!

6. the secret to a great cheesesteak, which often goes unnoticed by those enjoying them is the bread.  most self-respecting establishments will use Amoroso's rolls.  they are the unsung heroes of the cheesesteak and a long-time Philly favorite.  http://www.amorosobaking.com/

let's review.  if i were to order a steak while back home in Philly, i'd say "gimme a pizza steak - whiz - with!"  

as for Jim's, they make the best steak in downtown Philadelphia.  forget Pat's and Geno's.  they make good steaks as well, but i truly believe their reputation isn't fully deserved.  they're the places that tourists flock too.  if you're going to stand in line (and you most certainly will!) for my money, you can't beat Jim's.  and don't be afraid of that line!  it may snake it's way out the door and around the corner but the very most you'll ever wait will be an hour and you'll find out at the end of it that it was well worth it.

You have probably driven by Trattoria Pasquale's a hundred times, without realizing that you're missing out on one of Tampa's hidden gems. This place has probably 10 tables and doesn't look like much from the outside, but your life will be changed for the better at this restaurant. The intimate nature of the restaurant makes it great for a date or a small family gathering. 

To make a reservation, you need to call their number or visit their website online. When you're putting them in your maps, don't forget "trattoria" or it will not pop up. They are also BYOB, so don't forget to bring your favorite wine to pair with your delicious food. 

And, speaking of the food...I highly suggest you arrive on an empty stomach. You will get classic Italian bread to your table with oil and roasted garlic in it (see pic - yum). I highly suggest the burrata appetizer, it's full of flavor and absolutely delicious. You cannot go wrong with anything on the menu, so choose whatever sounds good to you. 

They also have a "Big Night" where they host special evenings featuring cuisine from various regions of Italy. Check out their website for more info on this.

I also had a side of sweet potato fries and a vegan shake (made with soy and almond milk, I believe). Fries were hearty and filling. It was honestly SO much food; I was too ambitious with my order. But I managed to finish my plate--mostly because it was too good to stop eating. I'll definitely be back soon.

The Cathedral-Basilica of Saint Louis, King of France, also called St. Louis Cathedral is among the oldest Cathedral in the states. The St. Louis Cathedral is one of New Orleans' most notable landmarks. This beautiful cathedral is the heart of old New Orleans. This building looks down on the green of the Square and General Andrew Jackson on his bronze horse. In September 1987 Pope John Paul II visited the cathedral. The Cathedral is said to be haunted by Père Antoine. He was a priest at the Cathedral and his body is buried within the church. This was my first visit to the south, so I was beyond excited to learn about Nashville history and plantations. However, I was sad and disappointed when our tour ended without a visit to the slave cabin in the back yard or a substantive story about the 136 slaves who worked and lived on the Belle Meade plantation.

What a missed opportunity to educate the public and future generations about our country's tragic involvement with slavery. The majority of the tour took place inside the mansion and centered around the lives of the plantation owners, their families, and their famous presidential visitors. 5 minutes of the 45 minute tour was spent describing the life one slave who bred horses that won races and made a lot of money for the plantation owner. 

There was an appalling silence around the very people who powered the economic engine of the plantation -- the 136 slaves who lived in the back yard. 

I've had the immense privilege of visiting Berlin, Germany where their tour guides mince no words when it comes to describing the Holocaust, the facts about how Germans treated Jewish people, how wrong these actions were, and the ways they're remedying this through educating the next generation. 

I wish the Belle Meade Plantation's owners had researched what life was like for the slaves who lived there, and had incorporated those stories into our 45 minute tour. I wish we had spent half of the 45 minutes in the back yard slave cabin understanding how the slaves lived, why half of them chose to stay after the Civil War, and the stories of the ones who ended up leaving and living as freed men and women. And I wish that after these stories were told, the tour guide could acknowledge that American slavery was morally wrong. 

I realize it's probably not easy to get information about the lives of the individuals slaves who lived at the plantation. But with modern archaeological techniques and our unprecedented access to historical information, I have faith that the owners of the Belle Meade Plantation can piece together enough about what happened in that back yard to paint a more accurate picture and lesson about our country's painful past.

I'll admit it - I'm a downtown-dweller that wanted to dislike Five Star. The idea of trucking out to Clayton for a burger when Range is by my doorstep seemed less than appealing. However, given the recent tendencies for Range to have inconsistent burger temps, wacky service, etc, I opened up my eyes and gave Five Star a try. 
I left complete satisfied, and eager to come back. 

Five Star does the simple things well. I had the beef burger with green chiles. The heat was light, but lingering, and the few friend hatch chiles atop the patty were a nice touch. The green chile mayo had a bit of heat, but mostly good flavor - indicating they made it in house. The burger was ordered medium well - a temp I find hard to perfect. Yet, it arrived at my table a perfect light pink inside, with a great crust outside. The meat was flavorful and juicy, which can be challenging with grass fed at times. I did find the patty needed a touch of salt - but that was it. 

The best part of the meal - and I find myself laughing as I write this - was the bun. Yes, the bun. I went to a burger place and fell in love with the bun. This is where they beat Range hands. down. The bun was perfectly fluffy - but also had a light crust to it. It was just perfection overall. 

My companion had the beef burger with bacon, bbq, and an onion ring. Again - his comments echoed my sentiments.  We split an order of the mixed sweet potato/russet fries, and they were also flavorful and cooked well. 

Overall - I would say that while Range has the sexier burger options, Five Star is hands-down a great bet for a darn good burger made with sustainable ingredients and happy meat. Carnivores rejoice!

Listen up, friends, the literary gods have smiled upon Elysian Fields. The name, one I.J. Reilly, our iconoclastic hero from A Confederacy of Dunces (one of the best books ever written). Not homage nor mirage, but a shop, and don't expect tomes devoted to the study of Boethius here. They peddle gifts, souvenirs and sundry NOLA-inspired items. 

This store kind of blows my mind, not unlike the man, the myth, the legend himself (but much less gaseous and pompous). It's got *exactly* the perfectly cool NOLA-inspired treasures made by, oh yes, *local* artists and crafters. Shadow boxes with birds? Put one on my mantle. Statement piece jewelry? Put that around my neck, baby. And it's all affordable as hell (I haven't seen art this affordable anywhere, really). You may even find yourself buying your own gifts. There's literature, coffee table books, music, soap, sculpture, paintings, folk art, and, and... more that I'm forgetting and/or haven't yet seen because they are constantly adding stuff to make this tiny store packed with goodies at every peep and turn. This is a review after one mere visit, and I barely feel like I took it all in.

So, visitors to our fine city I advise you to skip the jenky crap on Decatur or in the French Market and get thee here for gorgeous gifts and swell souvenirs (unless you want an alligator head. Oh and they don't yet carry *my* carefully crafted bedazzled alligator heads, but I hope they soon will).

Further literary nod, this is also Stella and Stanley's address in Streetcar Named Desire.

It's always so much more fresh and high quality than what you would find at other grocery stores. They also have a huge selection of veggies and fruits, sometimes I see things I've never seen before! 

In addition to their produce, they have a lot of high quality grocery items, including a large seed/granola/grain self-yourself area. A lot of it can be pricey, however, they often have great sales going on. I recommend planning ahead by snagging a newspaper ad with their on sale items! 

The staff at Sunflower is also something worth 5 stars. They are always helpful and friendly.

There was a big Irish guy named Shamus who always let me in thru the musicians entrance so I wouldn't have to pay a cover charge and then the fun began! 
I went to the new JC Dobbs the other night to see an old friend, Mike Tyler perform there and the spot looked great, and they even sell food upstairs and I'm told it's good and I had a great time. It made me remember the groups like Johnny O and the Classic Dogs of Love, Strawberry Affair, PM & the New Breed, Mike Tyler & Montana, Doug Grisby & Candi, Chuck Treese, Starr Cullars & Lindsay. 
And if I just had my man Shamus there to let me slide, I would be back in the life!

I've wanted to leave a great review for Tom Wood Toyota, but unfortunately I can't. I purchased my Camry a few years ago from another Toyota dealership, though living in Indianapolis, I chose Tom Wood for my service needs. Changing my oil and rotating my tires for over 40,000 miles now, at first it was just okay, but recently it's turned terrible. Suggesting I need an alignment that costs $120 (after I've put new tires on the car and had it aligned somewhere else), they've insisted I need this the last three times I've been in for service, approximately 15K miles of services. 

In yesterday's service visit, Nick, the young man who was assisting me with my appointment, opted to mock rather than assist when it came to me declining my alignment, as it wasn't needed and I knew this. I was in for an oil change and tire rotation only, as it was time for those services. Upon stating I do not need an alignment, as I have someone that can take care of that, he quickly replied "Well, why can't they change your oil then?" I confirmed I would be getting an oil change yesterday, along with the tire rotation and asked for the complimentary car wash, then left. I would return to pick up my car later.

After service was complete and I paid, I picked up my car and noticed immediately my maintenance required light was still on. This should have been cleared with the service. Additionally, upon reviewing my receipt and recap of services performed, I was only charged $60 for a tire rotation - no oil change was complete.

Ultimately, I want to like Tom Wood Toyota and recommend them but that just isn't possible nor the case, as increasingly my service experiences have been rather frustrating and painful. I will likely be contacting the service manager Monday to ensure another customer doesn't experience this and I get my service rundown clarified as to why my oil wasn't changed, but I'm ultimately going to choose going somewhere else from now on.

One of our new favorites!  Their pizza reminds me of the great pizza from Tag's Pizza in Croydon that we ate as children.  It was the best and this is close to being as good.  We've tried several entrees and they're equally as good.  Even the reduced COVID menu is fantastic.  Try it, you'll like it.

Family owned market. Went in to grab some dish soap and was politely greeted by who I think was the owner's son. Each person I interacted with was very responsive and kind. 
Will definitely make it a point to stop in more often for my quick trips. 
I recommend going here and supporting a local family owned business. 
Quality of service was really outstanding.

Went last week for my first time in nearly 50 years, and I enjoyed 5 of the 7 items I bought to sample.  I would go back more often, but Covid has created LONG lines. I truly hope their other items are as good. 
They really should go back to their original extended hours :D
Went there as it was next door to our motel. Was pleasantly surprised. Fast service, very friendly. The food was outstanding.

I've been going to BJ's for about 4 years now, ever since I came to Reno for college. All of the people there are very friendly and actually care about you. They offer you free soda or beer while you wait which is always great. They accept walk-ins but I always make an appointment because they are usually pretty busy. I've always been pleased with my haircut over the years and have never had any problems. I've been getting my haircut done by Mari for the past few years and I have to say she has given me the best haircuts that I've ever gotten, I highly recommend asking for her.
Horrible service. Food is average. $43 bill and they want to charge more for using a credit card. Don't accept credit cards if you don't want to pay the fee. Rip off!

Had lunch at Chili's today outside their back patio.  It was great because we were the only ones sitting outside - I'm really into social distancing these days.  Ordered their $5 margarita (always delicious) and a Caesars salad and their shrimp tacos which came with chips and salsa. Portions were perfect and price was right ($8 lunch combo).  My companion ordered the 3 for $10.99 which included a coke, potato soup and bacon burger with fries.  Burger was huge so he had to take half of it home.  Service was excellent with Oscar taking good care of us.  We will definitely be back for more of their lunch specials.

Went to the student show last night. So fun! The sketchers (actors? comedians?) were great - really funny. I especially liked the intro video about a cat getting fitted for a wedding dress a la "Say Yes to the Dress". Hilarious. The theater is cute, convenient and cheap - only $5 for the show we saw. And you can bring your own booze. Need I say more?
Just moved to town. Veryyy good Mexican.  We both ordered the beef fajitas and a pineapple margarita.  Very large portions so you won't leave hungry.  Def will be back

Mmmk.....that's some nice coffee........great.

Gimme one more cup, please.....and you can make that double..........

Eh, it's not like I'll be avoiding this place since I won't be able to divert my itinerary if I have to. The airport is small, but I'm not put off by that. The terminal for my connecting flight was somehow not attached to the rest of the airport and there was a shuttle area taking people to and fro. The shuttles run fairly quickly but with just a few minutes between flights it felt like forever, especially since the 'line' is really a huge crowd that stretches further than the space available-and if there's someone who's in a wheelchair it's hard for them. 

You always could walk out and in but that would require you to go through security again-again, if you're pressed for time is also not a viable option. The concourse I was on, hardly had any food options-no place for even the signature Philly cheesesteak which would have really made my opinion of this place higher but, it did not. I may just pick another place to fly out of if I can, if not I'll just suck it up and join the crowd.
NYPD is a great slice, but the prices are too high.  Thin crust, great cheese, and awesome toppings served piping hot.  Goes great straight down the gullet, even if it's painful to my wallet.

Not a good experience. Twice. Didn't review the first one. Not sure why I went back, and absolutely won't go back again. First, the young man working had long hair all over, wearing no gloves, and wearing no mask (anyone who owns a restaurant today should have kitchen staff in gloves and a mask!). Expect more wing for $.87 per wing. Boneless should be called "Popcorn Nuggets", and Traditional Bone-in we're smaller than BWW...which is bad. Cajun sauce was ok...traditional sauce with some dry rub mixed into it. Just ok. Louisiana dry rub was not. I have no idea what it was. Maybe I got the wrong sauce?  It was peppery, and greasy wet. Far from a dry rub. I have a stomach ache now.
Not a good experience.

I have never had such appalling service from a bar tender.... two bartenders in fact. 

Completely ignored me at the bar. No eye contact. No smiling, no urgency. Truly unreal. I have never stiffed a bartender but today I did. 


They also really need to fix their air conditioner...

Overpriced for what you get. The food wasn't bad and the place was bigger than I expected but they are charging top prices for ok food. You can do better for the price. We are outside which was nice for the weather but the tables were cramped and all leaned outward because of how the sidewalk was tilted that way. Would be nice if they at least adjusted the tables so they say level. I can't say it was actually bad but I won't be going back.

We used PPA for our wedding and it was perfect! We couldn't have asked for a better turnout. 
Dan, who also runs the outfit was our DJ. He had us give him a list before hand and then he threw in his own flare during the reception. He was amazing at judging the crowd and playing just the right stuff to get everyone off their feet. Only wedding I've seen where the dance floor was full beginning to end! Afterward people kept coming up to me to tell me he was the best wedding DJ they'd heard!
All the gear was there on time and he was extremely responsive even though he normally does equipment rentals and not DJing. 
I've seen the warehouse. He's got a little bit of everything if you are just renting equipment. 
In any case this is the only sound company I will recommend from here on our regardless of the event.
Called for delivery at 7:04pm. Delivered at 8:00pm with my sweet tea looking like someone spit chewing tobacco in the cup.

The girls and I went to Overtime downtown last night to catch up and have a few drinks... we wanted a place to sit down as opposed to a nightclub so we chose Overtime.

Not impressed that we were forced to pay $10 cover each at the door.  It was around 10pm and not even busy at all... plus other pubs in the area (Hudsons, etc) do NOT charge cover.  As soon as we paid $40, the doorman tried to lead us to coat check so we could dish out even MORE money just to get into their establishment.  We just ignored him... seeing as it wasn't busy at all (probably due to the fact that most people don't want to pay to get in an empty pub), we had a selection of places to sit and chose a huge table which had plenty of room for our coats too.

Our server was really nice (she even gave us a free shot saying we were her only table) and she made the experience much more enjoyable.  She was the only good thing about that place!  However, the music was so loud (in a nearly empty pub... kind of awkward) that we couldn't even hear one another so we left after only one drink.

Had we not been charged cover though, and the music wasn't deafening, we would have stayed for a few more rounds of drinks.  But instead after only one, we left and went down the street to Brewsters.

The entrance is a little confusing.  You enter and then stand on the walkway until a staff member notices you.  There is really no place "to wait". We were them seated in a little room around the back.  There was a giant window to watch people walking by.  The entire restaurant is dark. It is designed to look like the interior of a ship (I assume). Very dark wood and ship decorations, even the ceiling.  The atmosphere was very interesting.
They only serve steaks or burgers with a baked potato side.  
The burger patties are large proportions and comes with all the "fixins".   The potato was delicious and can get fully loaded.  The only thing that we didn't like was the mushrooms. They were canned and had a weird sauce
On them.

Wish I had read the reviews before booking but this was a last minute Memorial Day weekend activity. Not sure what I can add to what's already been said. We took our 1 and 3 year old here. They loved it but we were grossed out. The food was terrible. The grilled chicken sandwich was rubber and the bread had a chemically taste. The pizza was raw dough even though cheese was burnt on top...The only decent thing was the chicken tender basket.

The only redeeming quality is the number of life guards at every water feature which was great. Aside from that what a dump. Rooms in serious need of renovations. Carpets worn down. We stayed on the water park level and heard nothing but screaming every 15 seconds while kids were down for afternoon nap. Cautiously gave the boys a bath in the tub...

Water was a lovely gray hue. Crap in the water. Over chlorinated pools. Went outside with our boys to the adult spa area since we were getting a headache and were told to go back in bc kids were not allowed by the adult area (even though my husband and I each had a stronghold on our babies given the 110 degree spa in front of us) and this was the only source of fresh air!

My 3 year old loves Busch Gardens where he can go everywhere but wasn't able to go on the 2 slides here because he did not meet the 40" height requirement. Had to stick to the kiddie slides which were a bit small for him but he still enjoyed it. 

Will not be coming back.

I returned here with my husband for his nose piercing.
Belle is AWESOME! She is very thorough and does not rush into any type of procedure. She explains everything and is very professional.
Her shop is clean and very nice! The jewelry selection is very good as well!
I'd highly recommend here if you are looking to get pierced and I would advise making an appointment with Belle prior to so that you will be given her undivided attention.
I will definitely return for my next piercing and for any of my my jewelry needs.
Thank you so much Belle for being kind and courteous! And....for treating your patrons the way that they should be treated!
You rock!

My sister's order on a regular ,this pizza store can be very busy so calling for delivery can be time  consuming one time I called they had me on hold and me and my sister heard there whole conversation about another customer being rude on the other line about the wait time for delivery and not being able to get his order. I end up hanging up and next time I visited I place my order and picked up my own food.  
I always get a chicken and broccoli cheesesteak it sound weird but it's delicious . The pizza is ok hit or miss to my opinion , I haven't tried anything else I just stick to what I know !

One of the best chai lattes I've ever had, great service and they still take reusable cups which is fantastic, you even get a discount for bringing your own. Will always go back when in Santa Barbara.

A damaged bumper and taillight were replaced by Schaefer Autobody in Creve Coeur in a minimum amount of time.  Matt,  as the estimator, contacted me daily with updates of parts availability and meeting the estimated completion date, which they met. The repair was excellent; the paint color matched the 15 year old body color perfectly, the car was washed and the interior was spotless. AAA has selected Schaefer as a repair facility and they deserve the confidence of AAA.

Such a fun time! My friend and I booked the airboat tour and are so happy we did.  They were able to, easily, pick us up from our hotel in the French Quarter and drive us to the tour location.  Check in was quick and easy.  Every employee we met were extremely kind and helpful.  The air boat was a great time!  We were out on the water for about an hour and a half and were able to see a handful of alligators.
 Our boat Capitan definitely knew what he was doing and had a lot of facts and tid bits to share about the area and the wildlife.  
  Overall it was an awesome adventure and can't wait to book again when we are back in town!

I took my dog here Saturday afternoon because I thought he'd broken his leg in a fall. Turned out to be multi medical and neurological issues related to a pre existing disease. I feel they did everything possible to save my Stewie but things were just too overwhelming for his little body.  They kept me updated and brought me in to tell him goodbye. I will miss him every day but feel that Dr Lee, Holly, and the others were wonderful. Thank you all for trying to save my sweet baby.
Terrible beef veg I, almost un edible. Really was super disappointed, and it was wayyy too expensive

I popped in for lunch and had some Blantons and Totchos at the bar.  The weather was nice, so most folks were seated outside, so Stacey kept me company at the inside bar.

The Totchos consisted of BBQ pulled pork, beer cheese and salsa over a massive bed of tater tots.  They are definitely meant to be shared.  I got my belly full, and felt like I barely put a dent in them.  What stood out was the pulled pork.  Very tender, and delicious, so as I got full, I just ate all the pork from the basket.

I think next time I will just get the pulled pork sandwich and keep it simple.

Love driving 20 minutes craving a burger only to be met with rude staff who can't give my an answer as to why all associated pages and websites say open, but they aren't open to the "public".  Won't be coming back when I'm deemed lucky enough to order food.
I love Nina!  She is personable and does a great job on my nails every time. I would recommend this place over and over again.

I bought a "like new" treadmill that had been "tested".  It came with 5 years in home service, so i figured there was no way it could be a problem.  Didn't work.  at all.  It has been over a month, and it still doesn't work.  First, they would only set up a maintenence appointmemt.  so, after 2 weeks that guy comes out to the house, and sure enough, it's not just maintenence.  so they order some parts, and set up a technician appointment for 2 more weeks out.  parts come to the house, broken.  I let them know, they send more.... broken.  Ok, whatever- today comes.  technician doesn't show up. i had my dad take the day off work and wait at my house all day, no show, no call, nothing.  So, he calls them, they want to re schedule the appointment....2 weeks out.  I'm calling back.  they hang up on me after waiting on hold for 20 minutes for a manager.  I call back, and i've now been on hold for another 30 minutes, and nothing.  what do i do if i can't even talk to somebody?  I am furious, and getting more furious by the minute waiting on hold.  this is obsurd that i don't have a working machine after spending $1000, and waiting over a month, and i can't even get a hold of you guys!  WORST COSTUMER SERVICE EVER. EVER!

Excellent. 

1) This place is SUPER cheap. 
2) Got the noodles, which was good. 
3) However, the soy milk is fantastic!!

I was always so curious about the place. The atmosphere and the pictures of their food on instagram looked amazing. We tried it this weekend and me and my husband did not like it. The best thing about this place was their horchata. It's amazing. Anyway. We had their pato which was a mole dish. It tasted too much like anis. Or some weird spice.  And we also ordered the breakfast enchiladas. On the way home I threw up. :(  
If we ever go back. It will be solely for the horchata.

I have been coming to this practice for 2 years now and I really like Dr. Downie and her practice! I have always dreaded going to the dentist until I started coming here, which says a lot. 

The location is great and parking is easy right out front. Front desk receptionist is friendly and polite and it's easy to schedule appointments. They have a convenient system to send reminders via email and text and also to let you know if there's a cancellation and you would like to come earlier which I thought was nice.

The practice is a clean and modern space. Comfortable chairs with television screens to entertain you while you have your exam or cleaning performed. Kelly the hygienist  performed my cleaning today, and Dr Downie did my exam efficiently and thoroughly and seemed to know exactly what was going on. Last time I was there Dr. Downie herself did my cleaning which I thought was cool. They are both super friendly and professional. I particularly appreciate their straight forward nature and that they didn't try to sell me a bunch of services I didn't need (that has happened to me in the past and I really hate when dentists and their staff pull that kind of stuff - pretty unethical!) so I really appreciated an honest and friendly visit!!! I look forward to my next visit!

This locally owned business has me so impressed with the level of customer service and genuine willingness to help. You know how if you want really good food, you have to find a place where the people who actually own the restaurant are still working in it? It's because they take pride in their work and it's the same in the service industry, but in this case instead of the difference in having an ok versus a really good taco, you can trust that varmint won't take over your house. All that to say, it's a big deal and it's hard to find someone honest and dependable when you need a bug problem fixed ASAP. Allison's pest control goes out of their way (talks to you after hours!) and provides a wealth of knowledge on top of service. I'm so happy to have a go-to pest control business doing honest work, and friendly & reliable at that, that I can use and recommend.

We've been meaning to come here forever! Not a long drive from Mid-City, but we were just never able to get out to Lakeview. Well, that finally changed on a Thursday afternoon and we sat at the bar for drinks and a snack. 

First - the drinks. They're AWESOME here. We tried a Starry Eyes and a Balcony Breeze, and both were just delicious. 

For food, we got the Junior Burger and it was perfect. Definitely one of the best burgers in Nola, and a top 10 probably anywhere. We also got the Korean Ribeye Sandwich, which was delicious but nothing too special. We upgraded our sides to the brussel sprouts and truffle fries, and these were excellent decisions, to say the least. 

Killer spot - great drinks, and that burger alone is worth visiting for.

Michael Murphy Gallery is the most professional fine art gallery I have seen in the Tampa Bay area.  Even though parking can be difficult at times, the location is in a fabulous part of town with many popular shops and restaurants in the area. 
 
The collection is on rotation and features Florida artists as well as national.  
The artwork on display in the windows and the front of the shop are more spread out.  However, if you around more around the back of the shop it tends to get more crowded.  There is more to look through, so take a peek.  

Michael's staff is extremely friendly, knowledgeable, mature, fair, and humble.  Definitely strike up a conversation to get more information on the gallery and new works coming in.

There is also a large business in framing that takes up about a quarter of the space.

Came for the view, but got so much more! The sangria is freshly made; I definitely recommend it. Got the burger (not pictured), was pretty decent. Brownie also tasty. Overall, great service; the waitress was very kind and attentive. Highlight of my experience would be the drinks with a view.

Wonderful sushi!! Raw fish was super fresh & it all tasted amazing. The rolls were not small which is always a plus. I am stickler for spicy mayo and the sauce was perfect! I will be coming back whenever I can!

First off, I loved that it's a brunch place and coffee shop! I only came for the coffee but I definitely want to come back to taste the food, their waffles looked veryyyy tasty! 

I had the white chocolate Tiramisu and it was so good! I don't like my drinks too sweet and this one had the perfect balance and you could still taste the coffee

My husband had the toffee coffee and so tasty as well, he likes drinks sweeter so he wished it was milk chocolate instead of dark chocolate in it but still enjoyed it

My sister in law has the chai latte, it was great as well!! Same thing, no super sweet! I like that consistency a lot!! You get to enjoy the drink without any one thing overpowering it!

Brett Hulbert and Sandra Morris are the nicest chef and restauranteurs who have realized the perfect balance  of excellent menu and attentive and friendly service.  From the moment you walk in to your dramatic exit waddle, the drinks, menu, and fare are a true delight.  Highly recommend the ravioli, stuffed with the right balance of cheese and mushroom, and served slightly dry with just the right amount of sauce, to the flavorful seasonal salad, balanced delicately with greens, and an assortment of appropriate textures and taste, to the entree (duck breast seared the right way), and a decadent, rich flourless chocolate cake.  Even the bread is thoughtful, fresh from the oven, accompanied by a housemade mushroom cheese spread.  We will return, again, and again!  Thank you!

This was once a reason for us to drive to Northern Liberties, but the food is going downhill and the staff is the WORST.
The absolute WORST.
I get that you rely on seitan and can't guarantee a gluten free option but it wouldn't kill you to offer a gf roll or slice of bread. Even if you can't do that there is no excuse to laugh in my face when I asked.
Putting that aside, would it kill anyone to greet customers?? We stood at the register for a good 3 minutes while the clerk typed away at something. She couldn't look up or bother to acknowledge us. The young man who finally took our order was much nicer but she still stood in his way and aggressively aggressively ignored us.
We had been trying to call for 20 min before we got there and the phone wasn't answered.
I don't know what you did with the cheese sauce for the fries but now it's sweet and gross. 
I hope the two sandwiches we ordered are better but I promise you, I see no reason to ever return.
You lost 3 loyal customers.
Very good burgers!!!! I really suggest the diablo burger, will be returning next time

5 course chef designed meal was excellent....every stage.
Wine pairings well done and complementary to each course.
Nice ambiance....not too noisy or quiet.

Only criticism....at a place of this level, the waiter shouldn't have to read the wine description off a card.....very minor.
Maybe the experienced waiters were off on a Wednesday night?

Let me start with this.. It's great to see so many kids having good time and stay fit and healthy.. Love it.. Now comes the spoiler alert............. Ignorant teenager employees who roll their eyes and make unprofessional gestures and faces towards you.. So this all began when I and my husband went to have some work out and fun at same place.. It was our first time and never realized it's take so much energy to jump for 30 mins. Hats off to young kids who were energetic and had a such great time..so after 7 mins of jump and afraid to get any body strain. So I just relaxed on little blue side for one min and ignorant stupid teenager who was in charge of that area.. She rolled her eyes to another young guy standing across him as if they were making fun of us. I felt little depressed and irritated as if I am too old for this place or she was really stupid employee. Moreover the shoes she apply was pretty tight and uncomfortable so I didnot knew that you need to have shoes on all the time so I removed it and again comes this monster and tell me in most aggressive way to put on the shoes .. I felt bad very bad,. As soon as she saw me walking out of the trampoline area with intention to complaining about her and to keep in mind my husband was still in there doing his jump.. She quickly disappeared by making a quick exit. I complained to manager who was a teenager or probably first of college or so.. She reimbursed me money and said she will take care of it. And now comes the best part ........... She never ask the name of he girl who was working there.... 


Well they lost a customer and will never visit again..

The food was great, the service indifferent and rushed. I went just before dinner hour and the restaurant was about half full. After being seated it took five minutes for my server to come by. He came by several time during my meal and asked how I was doing, but I think if I had said I was having a heart attack he'd have said great and rushed on by.

The food itself was wonderful. I had the obligatory boiled red potatoes which were a unique item and very good. I also ordered the crawfish etoufee, it came with bread and a fairly boring mixed greens salad. The crawfish dish itself was fantastic and worth the visit.

I like king house Chinese restaurant for Chinese American food. I haven't try everything on the menu but so far, everything I've got were good. 

I usually get the chicken and broccoli, egg drop soup, Singapore mei fun, and sesame chicken. Everything tasted delicious and fresh. The Singapore mei fun  wasn't too spicy which I like. The portion amount was good. The only thing I would say is the chicken and broccoli was a little too dry. There was not enough sauce so I would suggested asking for extra sauce.

The service was decent. I called ahead and every time when I picked up the order, the food was ready. I would like to try other items on the menu next time.

I love this Big Lots!  Everyone who works here is really friendly and helpful.  There are tons of bargains and staples you can find every time you come.  Their furniture selection is good with rock bottom prices.  My mom found a fantastic recliner here.

This is the best place for holiday decor.  

The food is hit or miss, but you can find some great deals.

One caution - their restroom is one of the most disgusting I've ever seen.  Avoid it.  Seriously, you'd be better off pooping in the alley behind the building.

Super glad I went; the meal was good; the service was spectacular; and having said that, I'll probably not go back. Weird, huh? 

It's a casual, brick wall, open air place. It was hard to hear in there. Service was stellar. They placed our plates down in perfect unison for every course without making it look and feel stuffy. Water was topped off continuously. I watched our team work. When the head waiter was busy, the 2nd waiter would notice everything and make sure there were no gaps in our service. It was impressive.

The food? It was quite good. Not superb, just good. And the reason I'd probably not go back is because the menu wasn't appealing enough to entice me to want to try more. Great places make me almost feel panicked that I can't possibly try all the dishes that I'd like to sample. Here, I tried what I wanted to try and it was good, but it wasn't so good that I now crave it. And this was our last night. I wanted to finally have dessert and I was so looking forward to a great bread pudding. But the bread pudding on the menu was key lime bread pudding and that just sounded atrocious. None of the desserts sounded very appealing. I did end up with the trio of creme brulees and the presentation was adorable, but the brulees themselves weren't the best.

At our table, we sampled:
-BBQ shrimp appetizer (good, but nothing to rave about)
-Chicken wings appetizer (served as my daughter's entree; she thought they were excellent)
-Beet salad (reportedly good)
-Soup of the day was bacon cauliflower. I was very unimpressed and wish I had picked the beet salad instead.
-Two of us had the shrimp and grits. Good, but I had better grits at Stanley's. It was nothing special.
-Bloody Mary was my least favorite of all that I had that week

So overall, I'm not sad I tried it. I've now been to one of Emeril's restaurants. Unfortunately for Emeril, I can now say "been there, done that" and feel no need to visit the place again. There is nothing calling me back.
Best BBQ shrimp in this town. Cooked in butter with spices. Just great!  Highly recommended.

I have been going to Rapunzel for a few years now for massages, facials and started going last year for hair. This salon is mediocre at best. They called me and asked me to put 50% down on my hair appointment because I was a no show and cancelled and rescheduled my hair in the past. I laughed and hung up. First off the only time I was a no show I was so sick I was in the hospital and I even called that morning! also they like I said a mediocre at best and they act like they are so superior. They lost a huge client because of the cocky attitude and I will post some way better salons in the area.

Easily not only the worst Starbucks around, but the worst coffee house ever. Seriously, this is the place people go when they want their wet dreams ruined. Over half my orders are messed up, but I stop here because it's the only Sbux in this area. Pretty sure the only reason this place stays busy is because they have a captive audience. 
The staff is consistently surly and confused, undertrained and uninvested in anything they do. This place is so bad I'm almost ready to quit my coffee.

Almost.
Our second favorite place to gets sandwiches. Sliced to order meats and cheese not just sitting in a tray for hours. Bread is good as is the mikes way. Great customer service

This was my boyfriend and I first time at this location because we always went to the one on Watson Rd. I was very impress with layout because it was bigger and spacious with a lot of tables. When you first walk in, the cashiers great you saying "Welcome to Kean Kings", I thought that was a nice touch. We put our order in and found a table to sit at, and the owner came up to us and introduced himself. The owner was very nice and we told him that we been to the other location on Watson Rd and how we loved the food. He told us to give him our feedback on the food and if there were anything that we might suggest to let him. By the owner doing that, I thought it was very nice and professional of him to do that. We got our food and it was excellent, it taste the same as if I was at the location on Watson Rd. The only thing that I might suggest would probably add some type of pasta to the menu( that's because I love pasta lol) and maybe some French fries/tator tots with cheese and some type of seafood topping, that would be so good

Mmm Godiva! This might just be my favorite part of the fashion mall.
