This was hands-down one of the best Brunch locations I have ever been too. The food was AMAZING!! And the sangria was to die for!!! Very affordable!! Absolutely beautiful atmosphere!!! I love this place so much I am going to book It out for my graduation brunch party!!
This is a great Jamaican restaurant!  All the dishes were full of flavor!  The staff was super friendly!

BEST PIZZA IN PHILADELPHIA! I go to the place at least twice a month and I live on the other side of the city. Anytime I have friends out of time we make a trip to pizza brain and enjoy the pizza and the Museum!

This place has a cool vibe with some regular tables and chairs and other larger tables with benches. Food is very healthy with many raw/ vegan options. Their cauliflower pizza (which comes as just a slice) is very good but not to be confused with cauliflower crust made with cheese and served hot. It is served cold with cold veggies on top. Still very tasty and filling it's just good to know what to expect. 
We also got the shiitake mushroom soup which had a nice flavor and I appreciated it did not have a potato base so it was low carb. The plating of these were very beautiful and the actual serving dishes are mismatched China which was interesting. 
The last thing we got were rice paper spring rolls which you can't really go wrong with. Everything was fresh, tasty and came pretty fast. Prices are on the medium to high side.
What a little piece of heaven, super easy to order great atmosphere and it's a great TACO !

Great, laid-back, cash-only neighborhood bar. Friendly bartenders, plenty of televisions for gameday, and really inexpensive drinks. It's the closest bar to my brother's new apartment, so we hung out for a while on a Sunday afternoon. It's very easy to see why it's popular with all its neighbors. Definitely appreciate that it's non-smoking, too.

Nothing served is really that good, but the variety and general quality leaves you satisfied, especially at an exceedingly reasonable price.  I like to stop there on the drive to Delaware.  It's not far off 95.  Service is friendly.

A solid choice for a quick working lunch downtown, service is order at the counter. You'll find a variety of salads, sandwiches, rotating quiche, soup and a lovely pie display. I haven't tried their breakfast items, but lunch is certainly a-ok. Fresh, health, simple and fairly priced. Ample indoor seating and lovely patio for those gorgeous sunny Arizona days.

11th floor cafeteria in the Pan American Life Center. Another place I don't want to release the secret awesomeness of but I will because I care. Too many places around CBD charge you too much for a basic salad. But If all of you come here don't ruin it for me please. It's a good thing. They have a weekly menu and you can sign up for it to be emailed to your inbox. You can also see the menu on their website.

This a quaint little spot. It is perfect for a quiet romantic meal with a loved one. 
I suggest that you make reservations, as the seating is limited.
They do not rush you eating, so you will spend a couple hours for the meal. 
Food is excellent and an ecclectic mix of flavors based in french cooking. They blend in flavors from other cultures and styles of cooking. 
I would go here again for a great French meal in a romantic spot.

I love this place.  No matter which one I go to.  I do miss the creole pasta they had.  It was a fettucine pasta with chicken and shrimp.  Now they have the rattlesnake pasta which is just too hot.  Everytime we do go...I have to have the chipotle ranch dip!  It's to die for.

Not a sushi connoisseur, I will confess, but I know and love good food.  Second time here for take out .  Their nigiri combo is now one of my most favorite things to eat on Earth!!!!  The food tastes fresh to me and the service is quick and freindly.  Added to my go to place list in the city.
French Quarter tourist trap, but pleasant, relatively inexpensive, and a great atmosphere (at least when not packed with drunks).

I love crepes - and had walked by this place many times.
So I finally went in (even though I had not before due to the high-ish prices).
It was $4.95 for a plain crepe with butter and sugar (drizzled with chocolate or grand marnier had I desired.  I did not.  I wanted fresh lemon).

They had none. Do basically I had a plain butter/sugar crepe for $5.

Whipped cream is also a free option.

For $4.95 this was too miuch for a plain crepe.
That said, it was tasty - and the service was friendly.

I will go back once more for the $6.95 crepe bearnaise.

I hope its more substantial.

Tip:  Eat there - or only take out if you are right nearby.  I work 5 blocks away and it was too far to take it out and have it still be hot and fresh.

I wish Passero's was still here.

Took my son to lunch today. We were there pretty early a few minutes after they opened, host was very to the point, not rude but not nice. Server was very nice and attentive. Food was below standard. Bread sticks were cold and hard like they were saved from the night before, salad was the typical Olive Garden salad. Thought I would try something out of my norm. Tried the chicken marsala and this was a big mistake. It was chicken and mashed potatoes sitting in soup. The chicken was very tough mashed potatoes tasted like instant and the dish was very bland. One mushroom and not sun dried tomatoes. The plus side was my son's spaghetti and meat balls were at least good. Will never order that dish again. But other than that restaurant was clean and server was amazing.

Love this place but moved out of state over 10 years ago. I used to buy the picnic salad which was their version of potato salad at Cartledge meats.  The last time I was there to visit a couple years ago the young guy behind the counter act like I had three heads. Does anyone know if they still carry picnic salad? AndLove TFM I hope Styers Orchard has a nice pumpkin pie awaiting me I know it's not the season but I wanted anyway

If you know and frequent this pub, you like it and you'll return.   If you don't know this place, and are not a member of the ultra cool club of folk who go in there, the best recommendation I can give this pub is it's within walking distance of the Algiers Ferry.    
 It is, as Andrew noted in his review that was dissed, filthy, dark and staffed by rude people.  
 Stopped in one evening with friends.  We were about to order a pint when a gentleman at the bar insisted we order their bloody mary.  He sold it so thoroughly we agreed, despite it being late in the evening and not the usual bloody mary drinking time.  Bar tender finally finished waiting on everyone else at the bar and had no one else to use to ignore us, so came to take our order.   "Bloody Mary!" she said, aghast, " It'll be AT LEAST 15 minutes!" and walked away, in search of someone else to wait on to prove her point of not wanting to make bloody marys we didn't want to begin with.  
 Now, I get it.  I used to be a bartender until I realized my hating customers wasn't their fault so got outta the biz.  But I also remember the easy lie: oh sorry, we're out of tomato juice.

This place is absolutely amazing! I very rarely give 5 stars to a restaurant, but Babe Matteris deserved all of them! I had the bacon bruschetta, and the sausage penne. EXCELLENT! Jen was our server. She gave just the right amount of service, not always asking how we were or the food was, and not disappearing till the check was due. She was perfect! Even the Chef, Zak, came out and greeted us! We complimented him on his excellent cooking. He was very humble and extremely nice. Love this place , can't wait to go back! Thank you Babe, Jen, and Chef Zak for making our night!
The staff are always amazing and the atmosphere is perfect for a casual night out with good food. When in doubt-order the staff meal.

Jackson Square  was declared a National Historic Landmark in 1960. In 2012 the American Planning Association designated Jackson Square as a one of America's Great Public Spaces. 
It has a similar vibe and size  to Washington Square Park in NYC. But it is much prettier in Jackson Square Park!
Here is a video from GoNola.com  from Jackson  Square. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OYSV3Bf5VkE
 It was in the movie The Curious case of Benjamen Button. http://blog.nola.com/mikescott/2008/12/the_curious_case_of_benjamin_button.html
CBS turned it into a broadcast center for the Super Bowl. http://www.nola.com/tv/index.ssf/2013/01/for_super_bowl_2013_cbs_has_tu.html
Here is a Jackson  Square Web cam. http://www.nola.com/jacksonsquarecam/
It is a must see mainly because the French Quarter is small and you will see it no matter what! It is a great energy about it! It is great for people watching, picture taking weddings and  anything  else you want to do in a park!!

I went to Azie for the first time with my grandson last Saturday with family friends. 

The restaurant was packed and very noisy. I would recommend putting in sound tiles to absorb the noise, as it was Loud. 

I ordered the octopus salad, but the octopus itself was tough. However, my entree, the salmon teriyaki was delicious.
For the most part, the portions skimpy and I left a bit hungry. 

Also, during dinner the smoke detector went off, adding to the loudness of the place. I'm not sure why the smoke detector went off, but I suppose it was from a mistake in the kitchen. That has never happened to me at a restaurant. 

The prices are fairly reasonable, but don't expect a cheap night out, especially if you are having drinks and desert.

Finally, the wait for the food took forever, but the waitress was long and apologized for the delay. Dinner took around 3 hours, which was longer than we expected.

Overall, but for the noise, the tough octopus, the long weight and smoke detector, Azie was pretty good. 

As I said, it was my first time there and I would definitely give it another chance.

Guacamole is NOT fresh or flavorful, it tastes like something you would find in a supermarket or at Taco Bell.  Tortilla chips were stale.

Saving grace: 3 chile margarita - delicious and perfect. Mushroom tacos were REALLY good, interesting flavor with the lemon vinagrette.

We recently had our company's Thanksgiving luncheon at the Sheraton Riverwalk.  The hotel itself is beautiful with a gorgeous view of the river.  Since I didn't stay at the hotel I can only comment on the food and service we had at our banquet.  And I was not impressed.  The food was average, at best. It was standard fare, a slice of ham, a slice of turkey, veggies and mashed potatoes.  The ham was dry.  The turkey was fine, but there was nothing outstanding.  The service wasn't great either.  One member of our party asked for tea and it took about 30 minutes to get it.  Our food wasn't served all at the same time, and our servers were not friendly at all.  The food and service did not inspire me to want to come back and try it again.  But the pool and the view might tempt me....

Extremely disappointing...worth one and a half stars, really, because 2 is being generous.

Came here with a group of five for a birthday dinner on a Friday night. Had been once before, for drinks and charcuterie, and was impressed with the ambiance and the quality of the meats and cheeses; the place is known for its charcuterie and small plates. Based on the quality of that experience and the rave reviews I'd read, I expected the rest of their interesting menu to live up to the same standard. Sadly, that was not the case.

Our night got off to a bit of a slow start, as it took about 10 minutes after being seated for our waiter to appear and take our drink order. While we waited, we noticed how relatively quiet the place seemed - our first warning sign - and how easy a Friday night reservation was to book. After receiving our drinks, my wife - who is not usually picky - asked if she could order another drink, as the one she received was incredibly stiff: a concoction made of gin, vodka, and some flowery liquor. I took one sip of it and was about knocked off my chair...the waiter graciously returned it, though, and replaced it with a glass of wine. The rest of the drinks were fine.

The dining portion of the night started off smoothly enough - we ordered a mix of charcuterie - Iberian ham and Prosciutto, both really good - and cheeses, which included a mild blue, something with horseradish, and a smooth sheep's milk cheese, and all were excellent. The only snag was that we had asked for four cheeses, which the waiter offered to curate for us, but he only returned with three. Now that I think of it, I forgot to check whether we were charged for four in the end, but the cheese we did get was very tasty.

Then things started to take a turn. We each got two raw oysters, which were decent, but very small, and the mignonette slathered on them by default masked any semblance of flavor from the oysters themselves (maybe that was the point). At $3 a pop, I'd skip them, or ask for the mignonette on the side. My wife and I started with the Israeli Salad (couscous, tomatoes, feta), which would turn out to be the only truly tasty dish of the evening. We followed up with the Tuna Crudo, which is an immediate pass - grape tomatoes and a thick, flavorless raw tuna steak cut into cubes and slapped together on a plate. The tuna didn't taste like sushi grade at all, which you would expect at this price, and had no flavor whatsoever. It could have been a thawed tuna steak from Publix for all we knew. Same went for the tomatoes; nothing above and beyond, and the exact same quality that you get for $3 in a box at the grocery store. Next up was the Bison Carpaccio, which was decent, but had none of the flavor "pop" that I've gotten from beef Carpaccio dishes at other restaurants. I'm not that familiar with bison, but perhaps beef would have been a better choice here, or maybe it came down to the preparation, but the dish was bland and nothing to write home about. Presentation was decent, though.

Our friends fared worse than we did. They were adventurous and ordered the Octopus, Shrimp-stuffed Squid, and the 20 oz. Delmonico steak w/ fresh green curry, and none of the dishes delivered on the promise set by the restaurant's ambiance and prices. The Octopus had a strong fishy taste, and the texture wasn't as supple as that of similar dishes I've had elsewhere. It went unfinished. Similarly, the Shrimp-stuffed Squid lacked creativity; the ground-shrimp "stuffing" tasted far better than the squid itself, which was rubbery. And the 20 oz. Delmonico was especially disappointing. For a restaurant with ties to Bern's, we expected them to nail the red meat portion of the meal. Rather, the green curry powder dusted on top of the aged beef as an afterthought ruined the flavor, and the temperature was a very, very cold "medium rare" that wasn't at all suited to the curry powder. It was nearly inedible, and felt like an incredible waste of what was probably a great cut of meat. We're not the type of diners that return things, but we did on two occasions at Haven - my wife's drink, and this $47 steak. Graciously, they accepted it back and did not charge us. But I'd warn against anybody else ordering this abomination. 

In the end, after paying our $300 check and feeling absolutely ripped off at that place, we decided to have our birthday dessert elsewhere. There are many other New American and Tapas options in Tampa now that are executing better dishes at about half the price; at this rate, I don't expect Haven to stick around very long, sadly.

Food is good.  Think of a beach restaurant and you get Frenchys    Dogs are allowed on the patio.  The crab cakes are so good.  Everything is good.  They have a beer of the week special.  Some obscure beef they put on sale each week.  We had a beer from Argentina.  It was good.

What can I say that other reviewers have not already said?  Dr Volinsky and his staff are experienced, friendly, and professional. They stand by their work and do not recommend unnecessary procedures. I have been a patient of Dr. Volinsky's for several years now and have recommended him to friends. Recently I called the office with a severe toothache and was seen immediately. After prescribing a medication he felt would help, the doctor asked me to call on a specific day and let him know either way whether I was feeling better or not. You know that he really cares. Going to the dentist here is a pleasure, not a pain!

We got good pleasant service even though we walked in just before closing time! The sushi was fresh, delicious and we managed to order enough to be satisfied @under $25 for 2...now im NOT the expert on sushi but from what I've heard that's a good deal!
What a dump no pool, no fan operational,sub par breakfast and dumbass bitch at the front...Not recommended ...Reserved a month in advance and still not the room I reserved...Very dissatisfied....

Philly has so many great spots for Breakfast/Brunch. We decided to try something new/different and came up with High on Market.
The food was very flavorful...possibly too spicy for some. Good fresh baked bread/toast. Coffee was good but not "best in Philly". 
I only give it 4 stars because of the stiff competition in Philly that are just slightly better.
Went here for birthday on Taco Tuesday! Great tacos! Best I have ever had! Great drink specials too!

Great food! Wonderful attention to dietary restrictions (gf). Staff was friendly and food was prompt. Saturday lunch special included a drink entree soup and spring roll for just $8. Interior very nice and clean.

New and upcoming business that is under new management so currently the offering are minimal.  I did have a chicken sandwich and fries...really good.  Give them a few months to be fully operational but it you just want a quiet off the beaten path place to grab a drink and play pool or watch the game, here it is.  Brunch is coming soon...cant wait to try.

Wow. This place is AMAZING!

I came here with my boyfriend because we wanted to do something thrilling for our anniversary and we both have never shot a gun before, so this was the perfect place to go. 

The facility is VERY clean and organized and the staff is very knowledgeable and welcoming. There are a bunch of guns mounted on the wall behind the register with a big sign that says, "TRY ONE." Pretty tempting huh? I sure thought so. I noticed they even had chairs in the lobby so you could sit and watch people shooting guns through the giant glass window. 

I can't say much about their pricing since this was the first time I've ever been to an indoor range AND I had a voucher which allowed me to use a Handgun or Rifle Rental with Ammo, Protective Gear, and Two Targets for  two people for the very low price of $37 bucks! That's only $18.50 person. Don't expect to get that deal all the time though, I just happened to be browsing online at the right time.

After we presented our voucher to the owner, he hooked us up with a revolver, 50 bullets, protective gear, and targets of our choice. Then he gave us a very simple tutorial on how to load and shoot the gun. After we got the basic idea, he took us into the shooting range, mounted our targets, and had us both load and shoot the gun on our own. When he felt like we were ready to be on our own, he left us alone and told us to signal him through the glass window when we were done.

We only had one gun, so we rotated after ever round. It was so exhilarating! I shot Osama in the head about 10 times and maybe 5 times in the chest . My boyfriend wasn't as awesome as I was, but he still managed to shoot his terrorist in the chest a decent number of times.

When we were done, the owner rolled up our targets and gave them to us to keep. Now I have proof of how badass I am.

Overall, I really love this place. I hope more and more people find out about it because it's an activity you definitely have to try at least once in your life, even if you might get addicted ;)

Came here for dinner  with my husband this past weekend and our experience was terrible. First, our waiter didn't pay us much attention, we had to flag down another waiter to get water, our drink order taken and french bread bought to our table. Second, the first entree they brought out to us was cold and didn't taste good. They took those entrees away and let us order something different. Unfortunately when those dishes were brought out they sat on a table near the kitchen for almost 5 minutes before a different waiter brought them to our table. He didn't even say anything to us, just put the plates down and walked off. These entrees didn't taste any better. Third, a rowdy group of people were seated at the table next to us, which was in a smaller room of the restaurant. While I understand we're on Bourbon St and everyone is there to have a good time, cursing, talking loud, and banging silverware on the table is unacceptable INSIDE! Especially when there are small children at another table nearby. All these things made for a terrible dining experience, even the waiters were frustrated with the loud group. We decided to call for the manager (who didn't make us pay) and he did apologize for the bad service, food, and the rowdy people. While we appreciated that, we will not return to the Bourbon House again.

I regularly shop at Joe's to find fruits and veggies at a reasonable price. I can never find good pineapples anywhere else. They always have a great selection. It's more than just a produce market. They have all kinds of stuff: cheese, pasta, wine, a deli counter, etc. Much of their non-produce items are imported goods, i.e. not the kind of things you find in your local Publix. I especially like their section of local baked goods. They've also just added an organic section. 
This little market has a very small-town feel (they still haven't begun using bar codes) and their employees are always friendly. It's clean and organized well, although it's getting a little cramped. I hope they expand soon.

By far the best bridal salon out of the 3 that I visited in Delaware! Excellent customer service and very knowledgable. Katelynn was so great at helping me figure out what I like, and I found my dream dress! They know what they're doing, I highly highly recommend.

Here on business, went to Mitchell's for dinner with a few other colleagues.  Our server did a good job overall, the food (appetizer and entrees) was delivered promptly, and tasted good.  Atmosphere was as expected for a restaurant near a mall.  The menu had plenty of options and the wine list was pretty decent.  Overall, a good experience for the price and I would visit again when in the area.

First time here and what a pleasant experience. The roasted beet salad was amazing and the artisan pizzas are over the top. Definitely try the Van Gogh! Wonderful people too! Our salads took a while - because the make them completely fresh and they are a work of art - so they brought us some of their home made mozzarella. There was no need for apology. We were very pleased with our meal and the service here!
It was a smooth transaction with Jenn she was so customer friendly it was like dealing with a friend. You have a real asset to your company.

Staff is great Denist cares, atmosphere in office is one of everyone caring about each other. Dr Jolly always listens and when she feels you need a referral to a specialist she makes sure the referral is competent. Family has been going there for about 20 years. I recently had two caps on my front teeth replaced and the time and effort they put in to make sure my color and shapes were perfect was amazing. All the staff are professional and the equipment is tops. It is a small waiting room, but I've never waited over 10 minutes for an appointment.

Robin, our server was incredible! Beer(Aruba red) was decent for being a macro, coconut shrimp were on point, but a bit smaller than I have seen. Carnitas were solid, menu was very large- almost too large. Wife got green beans that were a bit undercooked but she loved everything else!

THIS LITTLE PIGGY WEARS DIAMONDS.

This store is the most overpriced kids store I have ever seen....I am sure there is a large clientele of people in SB who go to this store simply because it is expensive, but I'll stick with Gymboree and Carters....No need to break the bank on a kid who doesn't really care what brand he is wearing.

Save the money for when he is a teenager and really does care what brand of clothes he has....Santa Barbara haughty taughty overpriced kids store for overpriced people.

I spend my weekends in coffee shops and  1/2 the time I find myself end up at Kladi's.
So far I've tried their iced coffee, iced and hot latte, cold brew, pour over, etc. in the past 2 weeks and the quality is consistent. I even picked up some beans so I can brew myself a cup at home. You also get free brewed coffee with any bean purchase! 
I definitely recommend Kladi's; it is like the Blue Bottle equivalent in St. Louis!

If I could give this place negative stars I would. I have NEVER been treated so badly by a business. Like others I bought the Groupon for this place. I went in and they had me make an appointment. It was 3 weeks out so I waited. The guy was super rude but since it was a good deal I thought it would be worth it. So I come back in for my 11:00 appointment and the same guy tells me that it will take 4 hours. They had no bays open... my question is- Why do you even work in customer service if you hate people so much? Not a single nice thing was said. I hope they go out of business soon. Obviously no one is having a good experience there. Anyway, I told Groupon about what happened and they refunded my money. They sincerely apologized for what happened so at least someone cared.

The best Vegan restaurant my friends or I have ever been to and between us that is a lot- me it was my 2nd to ever be to- so I was the noob.  We came for later lunch around 2, was open but not packed. Service was great- helpful and kind.

We had the spring rolls for an app and they were amazing.I never would have thought I'd say that about spring rolls but .... I just did. 

I had the Pad Thai and the sauce that come with it was super good - (it was the dipping sauce for egg rolls) I also tasted the lasagna and it was delicious.

I had dessert- it was Stevia sweetened and perfect with French press coffee.

Portions were big enough for me to feel full. I have to say its not cheap but to me it is worth it- as my friend said about healthy food "its cheaper than diabetes!". I'll be back again.... And again..... 

Cool building too area is a shipping container architectural design.
Food is always good here, and the 2 lovely hosts are so sweet. Love coming to this family run restaurant.

My wife and I used to eat here a lot. Service seemed to be declining so we stopped. I tried to give it another chance and get a quick lunch there today Only to be told they close at 3. That wasn't a problem except it was 2:35. The food is good but I will not be going there again.

I called this morning on the off chance they'd have availability because I'd heard such great things. By the afternoon I was getting one of the most amazing massages ever. The prenatal massage is so perfect! The decor, aroma, lighting, everything about the environment at this spa is amazing and relaxing, I didn't want to leave! And they don't rush you out either. They let you put your items in a locker, change into a plush robe and slippers, and get comfortable in the tea room. I will recommend this place over and over and can't wait to go back!

The Best sushi in Philly!
The fish is always melt in your mouth fresh
I love the princess roll
White fish roll on their specials
And the tuna dumplings
The food and service is always better when the head sushi chef is working 
Definitely go here!

Definitely a great place to stop for a lazy day Pizza Dinner.  So laid back and perfect for an inexpensive family night out.   The location is perfect to snag up a pizza on the way home from work!  Pizza is oh so yum!

Used to be one of my favorite brunch spots despite the long weekend wait. However, I had one of the worst experiences today. Put my name down for a table and had three other groups of two seated before my party of two. All of which I saw coming in after me. Then, when we were finally seated, I ordered coffee and was given a creamer full of MOLDY MILK. EWW! the waitress didn't seem phased at all when we asked for a new one, maybe she's used to this happening. The food tasted delicious as always when it came but skip ahead a few hours and I feel like I really did eat the kitchen sink!!

Green eggs, what did you do to me??

A cute and cozy cafe with great coffee! Came in here for a quick afternoon pick-me-up.  Their caramel iced coffee is the perfect amount of sweetness.  Plus they offer both almond milk & soy milk which I always appreciate.  BF ordered their cold brew which he said was stronger than the typical DD but was still nice and smooth.  Overall a really nice spot. It's small, maybe only a few tables inside and some outdoor seating.  But they do offer a "charging station" with their selection of chargers hanging by the front door.
Not a "traditional" taco -whatever that means- but as Tacos get these are likely the best I've ever had. Not cheap but that is life: you have to pay to play.

Tried it 3 times and the food is very bland.  Not many vegetarian  options.  Also a bit pricey for the portions. I ordered the shrimp pad thai which was decent but the shrimp were not cooked. Another time I ordered the panang with medium spice, they gave me mild. And the third time I ordered the tofu amazing entree and it was bland and left a film in my mouth. The spring rolls look good and the pad thai was good but not for the price.

I've tried most of the famous cheesesteaks in Philly. This one is good, but not the best one I've tried. I got the cheesesteak with peppers and onions and provolone cheese. I like that it wasnt very greasy and it was a good quality of meat. However, it wasnt the most flavorful cheesesteak i've ever had.
Its definitely good- just not the best.

Thai food lovers rejoice!  Finally, a place where you can get SPICY delicious thai food right
here in Deptford NJ.   Going in, I tempered expectations because i have been burned before in this area.  Not here!  This place is legit...   I ordered a green thai curry -xtra thai hot. It was fantastic.  They serve it in a qt. container, so there is plenty of delicious curry broth to slurp. Nose was running and my eyes were watering, that's always a good sign.  So all in all it was a great experience.  Owners were very friendly too.       BUT WAIT there is more.   My
buddy from work brought in his leftovers after I told him about the place.     The dish was called Pad Kratiem and it was awesome!  It takes a lot for me to review a place. This place is worth it.

Great chips and salsa, tons of lunch combos, super fast (though not particularly friendly) service. It's a good go-to Mexican joint.

Map puts it on the wrong side of 70S though, the restaurant is located on the south side of 70S next to Kroger.
Wood fire pizza done right. Great crust, great toppings, and great sandwiches. This place does a great job without much fuss. They've also got some great local craft beer. Highly recommended.

I finally had the opportunity to visit Evangeline's bistro. I had a great experience with some minor hiccups along the way. I decided to pop in on a Saturday afternoon around 4 PM so after the lunch rush but before the dinner hour. I have been wanting to visit Evangeline's ever since they opened up in the central west end area and today was the day. I was greeted by a smiling server name Jennifer Who asked me if I wanted to drink and I decided to stick with ice water so that I could enjoyed the food experience versus an alcoholic beverage. I want to something light that I wouldn't have a lot of leftovers with and the Evangeline's menu was a little expensive for my taste especially with their sandwiches mostly being around $16. Their entrées sounded delicious however the idea of spending $25 for an entrée just wasn't appealing for me on the Saturday. I do understand why they have the prices that they do considering they offer a lot of live jazz band music on Fridays and Saturdays as well as Sunday brunch. So for the cost of the entrée you're also getting entertainment that you wouldn't get anywhere else so I made a mental note to come back either on Friday or Saturday eveningOr to experience their Sunday jazz brunch. I decided on the occasional shrimp Po boy with a side of dirty rice and I added a second side of hashbrowns with creole mustard.

This was at the suggestion of my waitress Jennifer so I decided to take her advice and go with the Cajun shrimp Po boy. When it arrives I was not disappointed it looked very good and the portion of dirty rice was to my satisfaction. The hush puppies were crisp on the outside and moist on the inside and the side order came with three with the side of the mustard. The first thing I noticed was the lack of shrimp on The shrimp Po boy. I saw more lettuce and tomato as well as the jalapeño mustard more than the actual shrimp. For a sandwich that cost as much as an entrée in a lot of places I was at least expecting a hearty dose of shrimp. I literally could count the shrimp and I believe there were maybe 6 to 8 shrimp on the sandwich. That sounds like a lot but when you look at the pictures the bread, lettuce, and tomato all swallowed up those poor little shrimp. The dirty rice was delicious full of meat and vegetables sautéed to perfection it really had a good taste to me and I wish I would've just ordered the dirty rice. The one thing I will warn you if you are someone that doesn't like a lot of oil the dirty rice was quite oily and there was quite a bit of oil at the bottom of the ramekin that it was served in. I did not go for desert the desert was at a price point that I was not willing to pay and once again I think for dinner and entertainment it would have been great but just to pop in for a quick late lunch I had already spent $20 on a sandwich with 2 sides. 

My one gripe about the service is the fact that my server did not refill my water glass not once during my meal. I am not a big drinker however I do like to have ice water when I'm thirsty. So for me to drink a whole glass of ice water and have an empty glass that really means the server was not on her table touches in refilling the water glass in an appropriate amount of time.

Despite the couple of challenges, I will still go back to experience the restaurant on an evening where they have live music or visit there Sunday jazz brunch on Sunday. For food and entertainment I think the price point is sufficient. For a night of entertainment with a spouse or significant other I think it has a great ambience and the service was consistent. The menu has a lot of New Orleans style Cajun and Creole food that is a refreshing change in the St. Louis area.

Stay away from this restaurant. 

I ordered a togo food from this place and they gave me what appears to be dog food.

It was horrible,  I ordered a sweet sour chicken and it tasted old and soggy. My second order was the Schezuan beef, it looked like mangled meat , " like dog food". It smelled awful.


So, please stay away from this place. 

I spent almost $40 dollar and it was a waste.

When, I called the establishment to make a complaint. They hang up on me. 

So, for your own sake and health, do not attempt to go to this place.
Great service- really great salad...grilled asparagus and fresh mozzarella!
This place has an exceptional selection of delicious food. I had the falafel and the tabbouleh plate. I would definitely recommend this place for Mediterranean food in Tucson. Thumps up!

So, there's not a whole lot to say about Finn McCool's other than it's "ok" in most aspects.  It's a great location, doesn't get overly crowded, has a lot of tvs for sports watching, and the draft list is decent.  My biggest complaint is the draft pours.  They were consistently 2oz short on every beer, which drives me crazy at $6-7 a draft.

Stopped in for lunch with a friend and enjoyed a nice lunch in their outdoor seating. After hearing they were named "No. 2 Best New Restaurant" by Bon Appetite, I had high expectations on what I was about to eat. For the most part, the food was delicious. 

I ordered their "best" grilled cheese and aside from the potato bread (fresh made in house) being a tad on the thick side, it was one fantastic grilled cheese sandwich. I also ordered their chilled tomato soup to go along with my grilled cheese and it was OK - I think if they held back a little on the fresh scallions they sprinkled on top it would have been better...the taste of scallions definitely overpowered the sweetness of the tomatoes. My friend ordered their pastrami sandwich on rye. I didn't care for the bread too much, but that was some of the best pastrami I've ever tasted (if you don't mind a little fat on your meat). She also ordered a side of the beet and feta salad which was good. And finally,  we also ordered their bread board to try some of their famous bread, served with a small portion of cultured butter no less. Sadly though, I wasn't a huge fan of their bread. I don't know if it was just a bad batch that day but the bottom crust of most of them were a tad over charred or dare I say "burnt"?? 

Aside from the bread, everything was good. The service was very friendly (a tad slow), and the place is quite small. They had a delicious looking pastry display but sadly we didn't have room to order anything else. I would like to go back and try their dinner one day and perhaps give their bread another go...

I really really wanted to love this place, given that thedailymeal recently rated it the best brew house in the country and it's practically in my back yard (actually Town Hall Coffee, rated #33 is even closer to me). The location is on a residential street corner in a gentrified neighborhood where the cars are parked and packed like sardines and it's almost impossible to find a parking space. (Sure it's a neighborhood coffee shop that you're probably supposed to walk to, but no one will ever find it if they don't live in the neighborhood, so you have to drive or bike there). Once I found a spot 3 blocks away, I expected a line out the door since it was a Saturday morning. But no, I walked right up to the counter and ordered a latte. 

The interesting thing about artisanal coffee houses is that most drinks come in only one size. No tall, grande, venti here. And hardly any syrup flavors, either. So I just ordered a latte and bought my son a pastry.

I'm not sure what I was expecting, but it wasn't the absolutely best latte I've ever had. It was a very good latte, but it just didn't wow me. 

The decor, however, is really nice. I love the meetinghouse-meets-industrial feel, and I like that if you brought your pooch with you, you could sit outside at the tables. 

I'm not sure I'll go back here, given how difficult it is to find a space (I don't live in the city) and how good-but-not-great the latte was.

This place is a hidden gem. Found it on yelp and my mouth was watering just reading the menu. Small place with two tables and bar top. Friendly owner and staff, and fast service. 

Everything we ordered was delicious. Had the Cuban cheese toast, Mo's Huevos with ham,  breakfast wrap, original Cuban, and sweet potato fries. There were NO leftovers.

The coffee speciality creations are fun and yummy. Tried the Sugar Daddy, Moo Moo, and Peanut Butter Cup (with ice-cream). My hubbie is a coffee snob and loved all three drinks that he tried. 

I want go come back to try the beignets since I didn't have room to try this the last two times. May have to stop by on my way to the airport tomorrow! 

*Note - hours are not accurate on Yelp. It closes at 3pm, not 4pm today. Owner said he's updated Yelp but it hasn't changed.

In life you sometimes run across a place that just can't be beat. Now there are several people that will tell you that wings are amazing here or there and they are simply amazing and no one can beat them. I have news for the people that tell you that.......They are wrong! 

I have been going to Richie's wings since he was in Hendersonville and has since moved to White House but fellers, it's worth the drive! Richie makes all his all own sauces and he cooks everything fresh. His wing sauces range from BBQ and regular up to outragiously hot. I have had almost everything on the menu and so far I haven't had anything that is bad.

If you ever decide you to make trip then let me give you some advice on things that you have to try.....

The coleslaw, it is truly the best I have ever had.

The cheesesticks, ask for the "special sauce" you will thank me for this.

The corndog, the batter than man uses is made out of goodness. I don;t know how he does it but the thing is so good I have to get one everytime I go.

So stop listening to everyone who jumps on the bandwagon of the best wings are within 5 miles of downtown, pack you a pillow and lunch and make the drive out to White House and give this place a chance. I know it sounds like White house is so far out there that it's not at the end of the world but you can see it from there. The reality is that its about 40 minutes from downtown to Richie's and it will be well worth the drive.

 Just go in and tell Jen and Richie that Bull sent you and they will take good care of you. Trust me, you will be glad you listened to me!!!

A collector's dream and thrifter's delight. Bathing suits, hats, repurposed jewelry, clean and used shoes- including boots! I will revisit this place as long as they are here. And they have an Etsy site!

We were given our first taste of this corn delight by the owner and it was quite appetizing. The place is quaint and the service is very friendly.
I think the presentation of the food was also good.
I would come back and bring more guests .

I recently attended two Philadelphia events  1) The Philadelphia Film Festival and  2) A Taste Of Philly..On both occasions I encountered that dreaded disease that is infecting Center City: Hipster Rude.You'll know it when you see it. People of a certain age who think their shit is ice cream and everyone should be running for a spoon. The film festival this year for the most part was decent .I have nothing but praise for the volunteers. BUT the people who ran the event need customer sensitivity training and manners.You know who you are.Please learn to acknowledge those who may want to write a check to finance your new project on Samson street.2) Taste of   Philly  not as many vendors this year. as last year. I suspect because the current economy. That I can understand. Again rude guests who could not wait in line to get their fill for $25.00. This is first  time in three years  I've  encountered annoyed vendors,and rude servers.Next year I'll write a check for 25.00 to the charity and stay home.
Stopped in for a breakfast sandwich and coffee on drive back to Philadelphia. Better then most fast food breakfast. Clean, nice spot on the road. Coffee was great.

The ramen was al dente, the pork tender, and the curry broth flavorful. Everything about the ramen was solid, but not extraordinary. The eggplant bun was not good- it tasted and smelled like overused frying oil and it was bland. The service was great- they were friendly and attentive. They even gave us free spicy paste!

Not the ordinary 'mexican' hole in the wall restaurant.  This place is nice, the menu has many options and the food tastes really good!  
I had the shrimp tacos and my husband had the crunchy mahi tacos. Both were so delicious!  Crispy chips and fresh salsa.

This is hands down the best Italian restaurant in New Orleans - but it's also my favorite Italian restaurant anywhere in the country...and I've lived in New York City for the past five years and travel regularly to other U.S. food-mecca cities like Chicago, Seattle, Austin, and San Francisco. 

Everything you could possibly order here will be fantastic. You should know it's going to be good as soon as you get your fresh, hot bread...and things just get better and better from there. 

The shrimp scampi and crab claws are both decadent and delicious. The house pasta duo - pasta ascuitta and fettucini alfredo - are made with fresh, homemade pasta and are topped with the richest and tastiest of sauces. The Veal and Fish Payton are incredible, as is their ridiculously tender Pecan-Smoked Filet Mignon, served with an unexpectedly delicious roasted peach.  I am also completely obsessed with their crab cannelloni and have begged to have it shipped to me on dry ice.  Honestly, I could just go straight through the menu and tell you how awesome it all is - I really have tried it all - but you should go there and check it out for yourself. 

The owner, Mr. Joe, is an incredibly warm and amazing person. When someone as awesome as him is turning out such terrific food, how could you eat anywhere else???
I've been here once and thought the restaurant was nice. Food was pretty good as well. Tried their sushi.

Cheap drinks and good service. Outdoor patio is nice. Gave it 3 stars because it was pretty dirty outside. It's a typical place with all wood interior. Kinda dark and old school. One pool table. The food menu had some great selections. Prime rib was ordered and it looked delicious. Steak fingers looked yummy too.

I could be wrong here, but Indian food seems like a lot of stews. And $15 for stew is fine so long as it has a lot of big chunks of good meat.

I stopped by for take out. The service was very friendly. I ordered Lamb rogin josh and chicken tika masala, saag, and daal (sp), yes all for me, I know, I'm a pig. It tasted good, but I found it a bit expensive for stew which didn't have the aforementioned big meat. And I'm not talking about the chicken, chicken is cheap, there was a bit more chicken. I'm talking lamb. I wanted big lamb. Didn't happen.

I'll go here again but I've had better. 

Note it's byob so bring something. 

See you all there.

Brad

Portland Brew gets all of its stars because of the building itself.  The coffee can be easily beat, but the gorgeous neighborhood location right on Eastland cannot.  

The building itself has a great open, polished warehouse look.  There's a lofted second story of seating that is quiet and away from the main traffic at the register.  It's a great place to come and work.  As I sit here now there are about 6 other people doing the same.  Each table has its own outlet and the wireless is free.

The music is a another nice feature.  They pipe in old blues and jazz at an unobtrusive volume level.  Although as I'm writing this the music just cut out...hmmm.

Excellent Vietnamese food. 
For the price you can't beat it. 
The restaurant is nice, not overly done or fancy, but it's all about eating good authentic Vietnamese food.
I love the Pho, broken rice and everything I've ordered has been great.

Amazing calzone. If you are a fan of Long Island quality pizza delights, then this calzone will do the trick. Can't say anything about the pizza because I did not try it, but the calzone was definitely the best I've had in the Philadelphia area.

Just a word to management though, clean that bathroom! I know the bathroom shouldn't indicate anything about the food, but it may indicate something about the cleanliness of the kitchen. The bathroom was an eyesore.

Wow....

Just saw the Grand Ole Opry here and it was incredible. Front row balcony was terrific seating. Such a historic venue. As other yelpers have said - definitely see a show here if you have the opportunity. It's so worth it.

Horrible. Well, at least the server was nice, and the ambiance was nice. For comfort food, it was not even very tasty, the food took forever, and honestly, I was very disappointed in the fried chicken (Crown's is better), the fried fish, and the okra and tomatoes. I'll will not be going back.

For a Friday night with a Philly's game the place was constantly busy but the service was pretty quick. The food was great. The hoagie was almost too much to eat. The onion rings were great but too much food. Only complaint would be not enough seating. That's what you get for being successful. Highly recommend any of the Tony Luke's.

Very impressed with the staff and service, much friendlier than the other locations. One employee handed me a lid and straw for my drink and a different employee opened the door noticing my hands was full. The manager is doing an awesome job teaching young employees customer service. Portions was generous and tasted great. Glad to see good business in my neighborhood. Will be going back often.

Had decided from the brunch menu...until the server came & told us the specials. Immediate switch.
~Peanut Butter & Nutella French Toast (no side, just a couple of orange slices, butter, & syrup)
~The Trio: Single Crab Cake Benedict, short stack Lemon Poppyseed Pancakes, side of fruit
~Pecan Pie

Tea selection was a bit sparse, but they had my Earl Grey. Only add-in options for coffee & tea, however, were whole milk and half & half. 

Nice patio atmosphere, has the feel of a french sidewalk cafe. Fun, hand painted tables, and I love the potted plants, which brighten the whole corner AND give an element of privacy for diners. If the day is sunny, though, make sure to grab one of the tables with an umbrella. Otherwise, you'll roast. 

Service was not very personable or welcoming. No matter, I didn't come here to make friends - I came here for the food and she got it to me fresh out of the kitchen.

This is an update to my last review which was a long while ago. Not sure what happened, but the service was average and the sushi was not good at all. The cuts were way too thick on the salmon nigiri. It made everything we had with salmon taste awful! The seared tuna tasted like propane or whatever they use to sear it. It was a super disappointing visit. Not sure we'll be back after this. It was that bad! The only saving grace was the ice cream, which is top notch. Too bad. This place used to be one of our favorites. Now we will avoid it for sure.

i just joined the 12th street gym...it's not my neighborhood gym but it is my gayborhood gym...spin class, yoga and cardio...this gym warms the cockles of my heart...the staff is friendly and helpful...you can actually find a quiet place to work out without feeling that your every move is being hyper scruntized...this is not to say that there isn't the occasional distracting bit of eye candy to cause you to miss a step or two on the treadmill... not that this has ever happened to me but well..um...what i am trying to say is that this gym is a keeper...

Looks like this a place whose decor you either love or hate, judging by previous Yelpers' reviews!
Well this Yelper was a fan of the decor.  I found it to be eclectic & cozy & a good match for the yummilicious dishes being served up.

I really liked everything about Farmicia to be honest.  The service was friendly & efficient, the food fabulous & the drinks amazing.
Everything was fresh, nicely presented & full of wonderful flavor.  I was particularly impressed with my boyfriend's pork chop & sweet mashed potatoes - two things I really don't much care for but thought were deliciously prepared at Farmicia.
I can't wait to make a return trip!

& I'm definitely down for trying brunch here one day - hopefully sooner rather than later!

Pretty good tacos, for sure. I had a steak w/poached egg taco and shrimp taco, and both were pretty tasty. However, what some other reviews here state are true: the wait is pretty long. I think I waited 20-25 minutes. Since Boca just moved to 4th Ave too, there were some flies floating about and the fans were blowing to keep the temp down, but I think they're still trying to figure some stuff out on that front. Overall, the food was good, but maybe they need a little time to get used to their new space.

What a fantastic place to have in the neighborhood! The beers are quality - get a bottle of the cask aged, if you can, or take home a growler for later. They have complimentary nibbles, or you can bring food of your own; they have delivery menus too. You can eat in the game room or at the tables. The session IPA is one of the best I've had.

I'm giving it five stars this time because the outside seating was amazing and pretty funny their was a cross fit next door but man their burgers taste amazing as hell wow and I love their sweet potato fries and prices are not bad definally.my favorite burger place with buds in indiana

What a unique experience here... The menu and the decor! So inventive and original! Who doesn't love a place with fuchsia uplighting, gymp covered chairs (yes like the kind you used to make things out of in camp), tons of Mexican wrestler masks, and a eating in car?  

We went around 8 pm on a Friday with no reservations and didn't even wait 5 minutes. We were seated and presented with a bowl of spicy chilli peanuts with cilantro... So yummy! We started with margaritas of course (I had a virgin pineapple because I'm preggers for only $3 and my husband had a honeydew which was $13. They were delish and only served on the rocks, no frozen ones here). 

I wasn't too hungry which was great because this is a small plates place. I had a fabulous soup, possibly one of the best soups I've ever had. It was sugared pumpkin and was offered with lump crab and roasted crushed walnuts on top! It was amazing!! Different and I would never think to put those ingredients together, but it really worked! Then I had the Mexican city style quesadilla filled with mushrooms and pure yumminess! Don't think big cheese quesadilla this was small and more like a tostada, but really enough food and really tasty. They do have some great vegetarian options!! My second choice would have been the grilled cactus, black bean, crispy quinoa and salsa tacos. 

My husband had a pot of refried beans and the skirt steak tacos which came 3 to a plate and were smaller, but he still wound up taking one home. 

Compared to those around us, we barely ate! The plates just kept coming for everyone! The salads, flatbreads and veggie nachos looked great too! Everything looked so interesting! Everything on the dessert menu looked good too! We were tempted by the flan with caramel, gala apples, toasted hazelnut with roasted apple sorbet, but we went with the classic churros to keep it traditional. They were so perfect soft, hot, and sugary! They came with two dipping sauces and were so moist I kept checking to see if there was cream inside. Yum! 

The waiters were very much in a rush and the hostesses weren't super friendly, but the food made up for it and the music was real good! 

Street parking was fabulously easy! Tons of spots, tons!  

It was a very mixed crowd... Older couples, college kids, even families, but mostly groups of young professionals. 

We intend on going back and will even bring our two year old to sit and eat in car which looked so fun! 

A really great time was had! We surely recommend it!

Went on a Sunday brunch for the 1st time.

Great decor . Great presentation with the food and drinks .

Plus they had a band playing smooth music whiles we ate .

I was torn between 3 stars and 4, the reason is that it takes FOREVER to get anything done, but it's cheap and they usually do a great job. You seriously can't beat the price, but you pay for it with your time. I got the heartbreaker special (Keratin treatment, color, cut and a bag of products) girl, it took 4.5 hours! Sheesh, BUT she did a fabulous job. I was actually really impressed with this girl and the past 2 girls I've used. I'd say don't hesitate if you have the time. Oh and one star down because that bag of products? Blonde Ambition. Um?...I'm like the opposite. Oh well, it'll make a good gift for some blonde person I know.

My husband and I have been going here for about 4 years. We have found them to be trustworthy and we are always happy with the work and the price. When we had our son- we made sure to have our car checked out here to make sure it was safe for keeping a newborn (first time- new parents). I have called around trying to find a deal on any work we need and I have found the best deal and the best service is always at United Tire of Willow Grove! We especially appreciate John, who is always there when we call, and always friendly. I would recommend this place to anyone who needs any kind of work done on their car.

I usually have a decent experience here.  The valet service is always friendly and professional.  The front desk staff was welcoming.  The service advisor was very friendly.  When the list of repairs would have kept me away from the office for too long, I asked for a loaner and was provided one at Toyota's expense.  The shuttle driver was the loveliest person to be in a car with.  The service was completed later that day around 6PM and I arranged to drop off the loaner car to Toyota the next morning around 7:30AM.  

Later at work around 9AM or so, I was reviewing my bill again, I questioned a labor charge that was over $600.00 for a part that was less than $250.00.  The last page of the bill had the number to call for the Part & Service Director, John Fletcher.  I called and left a voicemail asking him to return a call to me and I left my work number.  I worked until 8PM. No return call that day.  

I came into work today and called for the Parts & Service Director again.  I got voicemail again.  I dialed the dealership again and asked for the Parts & Service Director and they put me through to him saying he just arrived.  When he picked up the phone and asked who I was I indicated that I had left him a voicemail yesterday.  He responded that he called my office and mobile phones.  I was immediately incensed by his dishonesty.  I received no return calls at either number. In these days of technology,  a phone call trail is so easy to trace I wonder why anyone would bother to be dishonest about that.  I questioned him about the charge and he went on and on about how they test performing a service 3 times before coming up with the standard labor charge.  Then he insinuated that because I have an older car it takes extra time to perform service.  Am I being punished for having a Toyota that is running well since 2009? When I suggested that it is a misleading practice to give a flat rate for a repair but not indicate the cost breakdowns for parts and labor before the service is authorized, it became clear to me that he wasn't going to do anything to have me come away with a good experience.  I was very clear with him that I intended to make my experience public to assist others in avoiding what happened to me, as is my right.  He then accuses me of using a public post as a threat and holding that same threat over his head.  I really lost it at that point and dropped an "F" bomb which he used as an excuse to to end the call abruptly.

The General Manager Kim Gallia later called me.  She apologized for the experience and gave a partial refund.  I appreciated how respectful she was and how open she was to hearing my concerns and suggestions. She turned a negative into a positive.  Hope to be able to give a better rating next time.

Only been here once and that was a month after they opened. NOT a great experience which is why I have not been back.  Hopefully they have changed since then. Wanted so much to like this place going in since it is new and close to my home but was let down. I will give them high marks for the decor and the Pucks soda kiosk.  Also my wife's salmon salad was good. I have been to nearly every pizza joint in a four county area so I have seen the great, the good, and the bad.  My son and I shared a pepperoni pizza, simple right? Nope. This was the most overpriced, overcooked, under toppinged, untasty piece of garbage I have ever eaten.  I can say that it was similar in consistency and flavor to the crappy frozen Totinos I ate in college.  No offense to Totinos.  Yes, that bad folks.  So I brought my complaint to the order taker at the front. She seemed unconcerned but said she would send the manager out. When the manager strolled over finally and asked how the pizza was and I told him in detail the issue, he neither acknowledged my complaint nor apologized. All he could muster up was "I dont think that is the case. All of our pizzas are made fresh and people like them." Ok  so you make fresh CRAP then.  Then he walked away. No "we'll refund your money", no "can we make you something else?", nada. Worst customer service ever and I have eaten in 47 states and 15 countries. Needless to say, we wont ever be going back. Too many other and better choices nearby.  PS Tony Saccos is coal fired and tastes better (see their review I posted).

Near perfectly executed food and the presentations are really beautiful.  It is a bit pricey, but the lunch deal is pretty good.  I went twice in two weeks b/c I just had a need to go back.  I took a friend who has celiacs (can't have any gluten) and it was no problem.  Our server was totally knowledgeable about the ingredients in all the dishes.  The plantains were perfect, the tomato and avocado salad were fresh and flavorful (hard to find good tomatoes in the winter, but they succeeded) and the quesadillas were also excellent (although the sauce was much too sweet).  Oh and the $10 guac was expensive, but oh my god was it good.  It's one of my favorite spots now and I'll gladly take the bus way out of my neighborhood to get there.

My husband requested carry out because a friend had brought him some earlier in the week. I ordered the chili étouffée for him and a " surprise me" for myself. I wish I had asked what it was bc it was awesome! Both were. Very friendly staff, very affordable, great value for portion size. I need to come back for the pie!

Bought a living social deal for a swedish massage and signature facial. The spa appears to be in an old house. The massage and facial were done on the third floor; floors were squeaky could hear everyone walking down the hall. The massage was decent. Good foot massage. The facial on the other hand seemed like a really long face wash. Def have had better facials.

Tried Woody's at an event at the Fairgrounds and was pretty shocked, particularly given previous positive reviews.  I spring for some fish and shrimp tacos.  The fish was a disaster - dry, mealy and generally unpleasant and did not taste like redfish.  It was under-seasoned and the slaw served on top could not prevent the whole thing feeling very dry on the corn tortilla it was served with.  It was chopped very finely, unlike some of the pictures on here - which may indicate this was an unpleasant one off. Shrimp was slightly better experience but the corn tortilla still made the whole thing feel unpleasantly dry.  I would work on improving quality of fish and consider alternate sauce or tortilla options to make the whole thing a little more palatable.

My husband & I went to the Asian Banana Leaf for the first time & we loved it!  The menu selection is fantastic.  What to order???  So much choice.

We ordered the smaller sized bowls of Wonton Soup & the Coconut Milk Soup with Chicken.  As you can see from the pics, the portions were huge!  And absolutely delish.  This was accompanied by a Spring Rolls appie.   For our main meals, we ordered the Pork & Prawn Cucumber Salad & the Pad Thai.

Honestly, everything was so, so good.  No complaints at all.  The service was excellent (however, at that time, it was virtually empty...)

The previous complaints abut the music must have been rectified because I believe there was music playing in the background, but at a very low volume.

We were so impressed with this find & we can't wait to go back to sample other choices on the very impressive menu.

I was lured by the good reviews on here and the amazing price. I was here a long time too, about two hours in total, but now that I know that I'll set aside that time to go. Definitely well worth the price and time. My nails look great. I ALWAYS mess up my nails under the dryer and they were so patient and nice to me about it. I wished that they had some music or the TV on, I'm sure I could have asked. But I'll definitely be back here again. It's so close to me!

Great food and great service! Our waitress Sahara was amazing and so nice! She always had a smile on her face! Thank you so much Sahara for your wonderful service! Also the manager Ali came over to the table to see how we were doing and gave us a free coupon for a free appetizer since it was our first visit, wow! How sweet was that?? We live in Fernandina Beach FL and came to visit family and our family had already visited Pinchers and loved it and recommended us going, Im so glad they picked this restaurant, the food and service was amazing!

We had a lovely meal at La Petite Grocery.  Our server was knowledgable and attentive.  The cocktail list was inventive and the drinks well balanced.  The pineapple, which I generally do not like, worked well in the Great Conflagration.  The Fried Gulf Oysters had a crisp exterior and moist interior.  The endive added pleasant bitterness and crunch.  The braised beef short rib was, however, over glazed and as a result a little dry.   The lemon pistachio cake was most and the lemon, pistachios, almonds, honey, and lavender combined beautifully.  I would highly recommend trying La Petite Grocery.
I had fish tacos and my husband a bacon azul both entrees were very good.  Service was excellent for NOLA.  Drinks were good but a little pricey for a taco joint.  Definitely would eat here again.

I will never come back here.  The food was ok, but the waitress was condescending and the 'manager' was even worse.  After our meal, I finished my glass of wine with a mouthful of sediment.  I understand wine has sediment, but this was, literally, a mouthful.  When I pointed this out to the waitress, she said that's normal with wine, she sees it all the time.  I was simply looking for an apology, which she never gave.  She told us in an annoyed voice she'd send her manager.

The manager apologized after I told her that was all I wanted, but then said "Our pub is more casual, perhaps you'd be more comfortable there".  I'm sorry, I didn't realize sediment = fancy.  She offered a gift certificate, which we turned down, since we never want to return.  

Not a good way to treat your customers.

I came as a tourist. So take this review as you will, but .......

Totally Authentic. 

I came here a number of times during my stay in NOLA. If the music wasn't good, it was great. And they always had plenty of Abita.

When I was there, Uncle Babtiste from the Treme Brass Band was one of maybe 12 other people in the crowd. And the band talked him up on stage where they did an impromptu version of Shake, Rattle & Roll as he buzzed, hummed, and sang the notes and pantomimed a trombone with his cane... The crowd went crazy, and I was in awe. Admittedly, I only knew who he was after I recognized him on an episode of Treme and asked my dad. 

Overall, I had a great time in that whole section of Frenchman Street. Praline Connection, Snug Harbor, and a number of other clubs, bars, parks and restaurants over there kept me pretty entertained and enchanted with the city.

Have been going here for years, love it! I stick to simpler items- chicken with vegetables, wontons, soup.. all delicious. The food is not overly greasy with thick sauce like some restaurants. Tastes light and flavorful.

I'm not a huge sweets person but oh my gosh this place was amazing! This stuff was so friendly and when you walked in and they were happy to answer any and all questions you had!!- they're macaran gift boxes are adorable and the s'mores oh my gosh out of this world and to get a free scoop sorbet! How can you go wrong and the fudge oh my gosh I was practically done before I even got back to my hotel. This is a definite must stop for your trip I can't tell you how much I truly enjoyed this place!

Disappointing, needs improvement, horrible toppings, however the staff is friendly and provides good service. I got the Bratwurst with bacon onions tomatoes and cheese. It was terrible for $9 and the cheese fries even worse. The cheese they use is dry and rubbery. The toppings are tiny diced up onions tomatoes and bacon bits. The fries are just awful. If you're visiting from out of town just skip the place all together. One star for the service because the staff was really nice and another star for a great location.

The sweet pancakes are good but the seafood eggs Benny's are below average. Cheap ingredients and reheated potatoes. The salad remembered better days. I'm sorry but there's no excuse to serve salad leaves that are not fresh.

1. Warm free water - otherwise you have to buy a bottle.  No bathroom??
2. The sushi chef didn't change his gloves throughout my stay there - he probably made about 7-8 different rolls in that time.
3. I saw a giant tub of peeled cucumbers sitting on the floor under the sink in the kitchen (eww?)
4. Warm fish, completely average rolls.

I had the Rachel.  Quite simply one of the best (if not the best) Reuben/pastrami sandwiches I've ever had.  The combination of hot pastrami, swiss cheese, sauerkraut and russian dressing on marble rye made for an amazing sandwich.  I also almost turned down the pickle on the side because I haven't  been too impressed with the ones I usually get with sandwiches.  That would have been a mistake.  The brine does not overpower the cucumbers with vinegar and salt.  More please.

We decided to stay here one night for this year's Rib Cook Off.  Now, I understand that this is their busiest time of the year, but that is definitely no excuse to lack customer service skills.  Our service from the time we checked in at 3:30 on Saturday, to find our room was not ready, to service at the bell desk when I was declined a rolling cart for our bags, to waiter/waitress service at the multiple lounges and restaurants in the hotel, to rudeness by the staff in the arcade, was overall unacceptable.   For the price we paid for this "OK" hotel, I expect better customer service.  Most, not all, staff were either rude or rushed.   The rooms were "ok" and the resort itself was pretty nice.  But because of the customer service we received, I will not stay here again.

I recently attended a beautiful wedding at this venue (congrats, Sarah P!), and not only did the bf and I have an excellent time, but we were blown away by how beautiful and versatile this space is!  While it's a little difficult to find (tucked away in the Sylvan park neighborhood and behind the Nashville ballet...) and parking is somewhat limited (valet was available for this event though which made it perfect!), it's definitely worth it when you get there.

Green glass gives the front a modern look.  When you enter the venue, you ascend a red carpeted circular staircase to the top floor, where we were greeted with a cocktail hour set up near the windows.  When it was time for dinner, a wall was removed and we were able to move into the rest of the space which had been decorated with twinkle lights and table settings.  Noah Liff provided a perfect backdrop for a great evening!
I loved this hotel. Beautiful rooms and pool area! Helpful staff. Great location!! Right by Bourbon St. Would love to stay here again.

I had to stop by here this morning to get my blood drawn for some prenatal tests and I couldn't have been more pleased. I had Lourdes as my phlebotomist and she made me feel at ease and was very gentle. She was very thorough in telling me what she was doing and what tests were what. I was SO nervous that it was going to hurt and she was great. Barely left a mark. Thank you, Lourdes

Great coffee, cyclist friendly, relaxing vibe. Makes espresso drinks, drip, aero press. Prices are slightly below average (2.25 for med. drip, 3.50 for latte). 
Limited food options, just a few pastries. Also offers smoothies 
I'll definitely come again next time I ride to Mt. Lemmon from town.

I realize that there's a lot of deliciousness on this menu, but I have a go-to order that's pretty much perfection. And you don't mess with perfection. 

Chips & guac to start. Short rib torta for the main event. 

The guac has just the right ratio of ingredients to leave the avocado super creamy, the onion not punching you in the mouth, and just enough bite. 

The short rib torta...yum...I eat red meat about 3 times a year and I 0% regret that this is one of them. You don't even need the little salsa cup that it comes with. 

The only downsides: super loud and pretty much always crowded except for weekday lunchtimes.

Very competent compassionate vets and staff and their prices are reasonable. Absolutely nothing bad to say - our dog is older and has had some serious health issues the doctors have been thorough with her treatments and explanations to us

The hand brewed coffee was new for me and the true flavor of the coffee comes out with no need for cream, sugar or anything.  So many distinct flavors come out of the coffee when it is brewed by hand.  The pastries are simply the best.  I like the gougere, almond bear claw and the quiche which is available every day.  You need to Comet Coffee.
I love this fast delicious family run Italian place.   I like the pizza and pastas.  The side orders are large and filling if you want a smaller portion.
Never knew this was here. Glad we stopped in. Very friendly people that work here, wish we had more time to sit and relax.

We were there on a Tuesday, and there seemed to be a few regulars around at least.  Our waitress was really nice and friendly.  I ordered the eggs benedict and my boyfriend ordered the hungry man special.  The eggs benedict was really good, lots of Hollandaise sauce (probably an excessive amount for most people) which made it rich and inviting.  Probably one of the better ones I've had.  The only issue you have with that is that if you don't eat fast enough your english muffins will be soaked in the hollandaise (honestly not a bad thing).  My boyfriend seemed to like the hungry man special.  Also, the food had come quickly even though the waitress stopped by to say that one of the egg yolks was broken for the over easy so it would be a while.  That was fine, it didn't take much longer and we appreciated the attention to detail!  This is in the old Bo's Wok building if anyone is curious on the location.  It was very clean and not loud when we were there but it was a weekday lunch.

Sometimes I see these highly rated places based on hundreds of reviews and wonder what's the point of my 2¢.  But I love coffee so I have to share my standard of excellence.  CREMA is the standard.  What's up with all you other coffee houses?  Catch up.  Actually there are a couple of coffee houses that should be noted for at least not sucking.
There are easy self serve kiosks at this location. I highly recommend it. I received an upgrade, which was really nice because it had Sirius radio. The downside was that I had to pay more in gas.

its a pleasure to work with these guys- easy to book times, always show up on time, clean work and very knowledgeable in all areas. I have since used them at work to do jobs for us as well as at home.

Terrible; awful!  The service was slow and we had to ask the waitress multiple times for things like extra napkins.  It was obvious she did not want to be at work that day. The French Dip was rubbery and could not be chewed.  Poor service and poor food...I won't be going back.
I've gone here for 4 years. Always a great experience. Make sure you get a rewards card. After so many visits you get one visit free.

Wow! Awesome food. Nice atmosphere. Laid back and casual. The udon noodle soups is fenom. Lots of protein in it and not too salty. The sushi is rolled tight and taste fresh. Great place to come. We are visiting from Florida and lucked out here. You won't go wrong if your in the mood for sushi Thai.

Best in class! 
This was a great discovery as far as fast food Asian takeout goes --this tops them all. 
The fact that the menu is very between Chinese Vietnamese and Thai gives you a great option. 
I cannot believe how busy they are with takeout and sit down orders. And with all of that activity the kitchen is hopping. The food comes out delicious on time and at a great price. 
I'll be back!
This is a winner

Great meal. We got 4 appetizers. The pozole verde was fantastic. The Brussels sprouts and New York bites were amazing. As always, fantastic po de creme.
Plus, wiki sticks for the kids.  Very reasonable and great value

This place is a new Asian restaurant at the site of the old Fujiyama's. I am glad to see they have many different types of Asian food: Thai, Japanese, and Chinese. I have tried the green curry Thai chicken bowl, it was good, but the real star here is the sushi. They take their time and it was prepared expertly. Presentation was top notch. Freshness excellent. I will continue to explore their menu further as there are so many things to try. Check out the Thai iced tea, if you've never had it before, it's something else!

My boyfriend and I ate at the Big Skye Cafe last night.  We sat outside, and it turned out to be beautiful & cool summer night.  I can't accurately describe the noise level of the place partly because we sat outside, and partly because of the two Missouri American Water trucks digging up the street right in front of the patio. But even that didn't put too much of a damper on the ambiance.

To start, we had the Chanterelle Mishroom Bruschetta at the recommendation of our server and it was soooooooo good. It was one long piece of baguette topped with mushrooms, parmesan, tomatoes, and a butter sauce.  The sauce was so yummy I wished there was an entree featuring it.

As an entree I had the Grilled Yellowfin Tuna also at the recommendation of the server.  It was done in an "asian" style with mushroom sesame linguine. The linguine definitely had a little bit of a kick. The tuna was done perfectly, and it was very good, but it absolutely was out of its league compared to....

...the Big Sky Seafood Cioppino! HOLY MOSES! The Cioppino was unbelievably good.  If you like seafood, I would definitely recommend this dish. Perfect. 

Lastly, I had the Grande Tito martini, and I wished I hadn't the vodka itself was really clean and smooth, but the blue cheese olives were kind of gross. They tasted almost medicinal, not good.

Overall, I will definitely be back!
This was once a pristine 5-star hotel that is now starting to show wear and tear.  It is a bit pricey ($169/night) for what is now a very standard hotel with great service.  Meh.

French Press has a cool atmosphere and a nice location. However, the seating is very limited. There is room for more chairs and tables but for some reason it is left empty.

The pastries are quite good, but their coffee is extremely acidic. It is so acidic that sometimes it tastes sour! I don't know whether sour coffee is a new trend now, but I don't enjoy it at all.

Good restaurant and fun place. The bartender took long making our drinks but they were worth it. Our waiter seemed annoyed that we weren't interested jn the tasting menu and wasn't so great at hiding it. Food was good and reasonably priced.

This place has always been hit or miss.  The food is good.........if you can get it.  Service ranges from fine to horrible.  Last night I went here to celebrate my birthday with my family.
