I called at 8:05 to find out when they closed.  I was told 8:30 for dinner and 9:00 for takeout.  After we hung up I wanted to clarify that they seated until 8:30, because we did not want to be an inconvenience for a server wanting to leave. So I called back.  The same woman that answered the first time confirmed that, yes, they SEAT until 8:30. Normally we would not go if they were closing, but since they stay open for takeout until 9:00, and I confirmed TWICE at 8:05 that they were still seating for another 25 minutes, we thought coming would be OK. 

We arrived between 8:15 and 8:20 and were sent away.  Kitchen is closed.  She stated that they stop seating at 8:30.  I let the hostess know that I just called and spoke to her to confirm the time and she looked at the clock.  Saw it was not yet 8:20 and checked with the kitchen who said no to seating us. Because it was a Monday, it's location being close to home, but in the opposite direction of other restaurants open on Mondays, and the time of night, our options were limited by the time wasted going there.  We ended up at Olive Garden for my birthday dinner.  We won't be back, because of this and other bad experiences we have had with this place, (there are many, but we kept hoping it would get better so we could enjoy the food).  It's a shame, because the food is good when you do have the rare opportunity to get it without mistakes and delays.

I was in a weird spot with my graduate degree and wanted a part-time job without committing long term to a company. This was a viable option. The application process was a little lengthy. It made sense to me on one level - you need to test people's typing skills if they are going to be typing. On the other hand - I am getting my doctorate....it should be obvious I can type! I got a couple jobs right away. One job was recurring, which was nice. I eventually found my own separate employment (it came up suddenly). Everyone at Philly Temps was nice and professional. They were good about getting my paychecks out quickly. For someone in my situation, it worked out nicely. I would have continued to work with them had I not found my own employment. One big con - there should be a mobile or online way to track hours. Everything was done via paper. It became a little annoying when I had to drop the sheets off at the office in person. It was usually on my way home, so not a huge deal. It might be more troublesome for folks who don't live downtown.

Broth was bland :( I was really looking forward to flavorful broth but was disappointed. The noodles were great though. Not enough toppings offered and no extra spices/sauces to make it spicer. I've had better. Good price and quick service though. Glad I gave it a try.
This place was good. A nice fast casual restaurant for Greek food.

I normally drive out of my way to come here if & when I'm in the mood for McDonald's. Inside is sleek - modern & clean. Drive thru is quick & accurate! I haven't yet to have any problems with this location. I do enjoy their FREE wifi & friendly staff. Breakfast is good & lunch is OK! 4 stars because it's just "McDonald's" (come on now) so if you're wondering if this McDonald's is clean - fast & accurate?  It is.

Excellent. Fair prices and fantastic fields. Lots of bunkers and most of the fields are shaded. I've been playing here for 15 years and they are constantly improving the facilities. Scenarios are extremely fun and some of the best refereed games I have ever played.

Man!!! If one of these were in my area I'd probably be there all the time! When walking it we happened to hit lunch hour! No worries it was quick, was able to get a table! The atmosphere was so welcoming and friendly! There food was fresh and so yummy, I went for a refill of my awesome tea and heard management talking to there employees they were so friendly! It's a great place

Look, I have been an avid Chipotle fan for years. I've stuck with them through all of their health scares and such, but I can't excuse what has happened the last few times I've visited this location. The line is always slow moving usually because of the to go orders taped on the wall. If you're going to offer online orders you have to get your staff up to par and also bump up the number of bodies you have working. 
Each time I've come in lately there has been no attention given to the dining area. Every table is filthy. Tonight I watched three tables have to be wiped off by customers with napkins before they could sit down. 
The employees are letting the steam wells run dry and it's filling the place with that terrible order us food service types know too well. 
Also, tonight they're out of tea for the evening they said and one of the soda machine spickets has been broken for 3 weeks. 
I hate complaining but this really needs to be looked into. Most people here tonight don't look enthused anymore after they realize the experience wasn't what they were hoping for.

My family loves St.Pete Bagel. The bagels are as close as we can get to New York. Also love the gourmet donuts. Be sure to stop for a bagel on your way to the beach. You may want to call in your order though - the lines can get lengthy on morning weekends.

Oh.......baby!  Now this is the place to get a burger.  East Nashville's oldest bar, yes it's a dive, I'm not sure why it took so long to go in there. This bar/resaurant has been through a war and it survived, thankfully!  First off the beer is cheap, please don't change your prices!  $1.75 PBR's and Bud, unheard of!  This made me happy when I only had $6.00 to my name.  The beer comes in ball jars that are frosted.  Yep, they know how to serve a beer!

We ordered two cheeseburgers.  This isn't the kind of place you quick order and eat.  A 1/2 pound burger takes time.  Don't rush genius!  It literally sizzled for 30 minutes and then out came this ball of meat with american cheese on top.  I got the usual fixings; lettuce, tomato, little bit of onions and pickles.  One bite and you are sold. It's juicy, cooked to a medium perfection.  The juices slip out onto the plate.  Not grease, juices. It's also seasoned well. We got the fries too.  They were perfect with the burger.  

Solid, solid burger, it must be tried by all burger lovers.  Oh and Tuesday nights they have a deal on beer, I know, doesn't seem possible but it's true.

Great food.  As you can read in the other reviews, but what makes this review different is service.  Amanda, the General Manager knows how to take care of you and she is amazing.  We were there for dinner on a Thursday and had heard that their Deep Dish Pizza is great, being from Chicago, I had to try it.  

We got the pizza and it was good, other than the fact that the bottom crust was burnt.  And I mean BURNT.  I don't send anything back in a restaurant unless it is burned or non cooked, that seems very fair to me.  So after a bit of hard thought, when our server asked how the pizza was, I had to be honest.  She offered to bring us anything else, to which we kindly turned down.  After a short time, Amanda, the General Manager stopped by, after hearing about the pizza and INSISTED that she help us out while telling us that the burned pizza was already taken care of (paid for).  So, having fell in love with their chef's choice of 3 cheeses, I just told her that anything would be great because I know that it would be good.

Sure enough, a Margherita pizza came to our table, and it was AMAZING!  Get this as an appetizer, entree, dessert, doesn't matter, it is seriously delicious... 

So after all of this, we left happy and willing (obviously) to proclaim that Garces Trading Company is one of the best, if not the, restaurants in Philadelphia.  


P.S.  Having a state run wine / liquor store, WITH AN ACTUAL SOMMELIER!, inside the restaurant is the greatest thing that the PLCB could do other than abolishing itself.

Not a pleasant experience! Ordered House Special Mei and Curry Chicken, asked for extra spicy on both dishes and they were not spicy at all. Lacked favor and very bland! Ordered large fried rice that was suppose to have onions, peas, and carrots and it was just yellow rice(see pic). Ordered 2 pork egg rolls/2 veggie egg roll and were given 4 vegetable spring rolls.

The food is good and they are friendly, but it is a little pricey. I wanted to buy a refill for their honey green tea and the cashier said they don't have refills, but what I meant was that I wanted to buy another. I then told her just give me another and handed her my card, but she said they have a minimum and that she couldn't take my card... I just spent over over ten bucks so it was weird. 

Update: I'm regularly here and they are very consistent. Make sure to get a stamping card if you plan on coming back.

I have been to many Brazilian steakhouses, including in Rio, but never to a Fogo de Chao.  I will never return to another one.  The salad bar was paltry -- very few selections.  The cheese puff/breads were deflated and hard.  But the worst of all was that our sides did not arrive until our bill was presented to us.  No apologies, nothing, just "here are your sides; guess someone forgot."  A couple of cuts of meat were terrific; others were not.  It's not a great selection.

Does anyone know if this place is permanently closed for good?? This was my favorite bar ever! They had pool and really awesome BBQ they'd smoke up on the weekends. The staff was always friendly but I always came for the extensive beer menu. They always had St. Bernardus (the bestttt Belgium beer) on tap and I can seriously not find it anywhere now. My heart is broken!

Always quality. The Brazilian iced coffee is amazing, topped off with a little bit of chocolate. The coffee is never weak or burnt. They also have an incredible selection of greeting cards and small gifts. In addition they have a wonderful selection of sorbet. 

And excellent quiche!

The food was good but customer service is not worth going back. This was my first time trying this place. I walk in and NO ONE even acknowledge me at the entrance. I waited for over 5 mins before walking to the counter where two male employees were and already saw me waiting to be seated. Then they asked how can they help me when I walked over. Mind you there was a waitress walking around wiping tables yet, no acknowledgement of me waiting to be seated. So anyway, I asked where can I order food and they ask me dining or to go and I said to go. They pointed to the bar to place an order to go. When I go to the counter I asked were they about to close;  trying to understand their reason for not serving me or acknowledging my presence. She told me they close at 10 or 11, either way it wasn't even 8pm so the fact is they're just terrible people that don't like to serve certain people.

We wandered into this place after being told at Remeloude  that the kitchen was backed up and the wait would be at least 45 minutes and that we had to stay there.....yeah .....okay.  At Le Bayou we were seated right away.  our waitress Adrianne was very nice.  I ordered the shrimp and grits this dish consisted of a bed of fresh spinach, a good amount of shrimp and in the center a stack of fried green tomatoes with grits layered between them.  OMG this was bliss in a bowl!  I love this dish and try it most times I see it this is the best, the sauce makes it SUPER!
Husband had the Bayou sampler which had gumbo,red beans an rice and étouffée all of which were stellar.  The food and service were great! I may go back tonight:-)

We went here at my two sons request, and I'm not saying no to virtual reality games.  It took me a few minutes to adjust to the situation, but once I did, I wanted to stay another hour. My family talked about it the rest of the night. We are looking forward to more time because it was amazing , and want to go back asap..

We wanted to make a pit stop for food on the way back home and found this place through Yelp. Thank goodness we did too, because this little hole in the wall was delicious! The cashier was very friendly and helpful navigating their menu of several specials. 

The prices were surprisingly low for the decently large portions, and the food was fantastic. My boyfriend got the special guac and bacon cheeseburger and I ordered the brisket-sirloin cheeseburger with bacon. Both were fantastic, but the garlic fries were ridiculously tasty. The food came out within minutes of us sitting down, which was awesome.

This is a good place to stop for a fast and relatively cheap lunch! A lot of flavor, a good amount of food, and the staff were awesome. If you're looking for a quick lunch while you're going down the 101, Home Plate is perfect for it.

Hella vegan friendly if you're looking for that, cool neighborhood 

Moist, flavorful falafel that knocks your average street vendor out of the park, so you can't go wrong with either a falafel with pita or a falafel salad. 

The real kicker is probably their vegan shakes, dubbed "Tehina shakes" (Michael Solomonov's recipe/brainchild). We tried their Turkish Coffee + Coconut shakes and both were outstanding! Tehina is made with soy + almond milk + tahini so the flavor is slightly nuttier than your typical dairy shake, but they do not disappoint. 

Not from Philly but I could see this being a great lunch stop. Seating is sparse though.
Being from wine country (Santa Barbara, Ca} I stopped here and loved their wine selection!  Melville is a fav.  They even carry Young's Chocolate Stout!

Second time we've been to this location for lunch and both times we were left standing up front waiting to be seated for a while and they were not busy at all. We finally got seated and no one came to even take our drink order. After 15 mins of just sitting there with no one even acknowledging us, we got up and left. We went to Glory Days across the street and were not only immediately greeted at the door, but seated and with a drink in our hand and food order in, within the same time frame that we sat around waiting at this place. We will probably never go back.

Food was decent, but the place was empty.  The horchata was watered down. The wet chicken burrito was good but overpriced.  It was over 40 bucks to feed 2 adults and 2 small children.  Only go there again if I am really missing Mexican food.

Night market. 

My wife and I are avid food truck fans.  So when the city puts on a Night Market we meet up don't even change out of our work clothes. We get there early and find great parking. To end our night of enjoying great weather and food we decided on tacos. Smokin had the longest line so how could we go wrong. After waiting 20min it's time to order that's when things go wrong. After about 20 minutes passed my wife goes up and ask for our order guys yells agin I didn't call it yet. Five minutes past I go up he says I called you but someone took it. At this we are heated he assures us our order is going to the front of the line. Another five minuets go by still nothing we demand our money back he's hands it over with such and attitude. He was so nasty towards us, hadn't cared that we've been waiting over 45 minutes. This butthole didn't even have enough decency to apologize. I will be going night markets again..... Never to this truck!!

Great menu, taste & ambiance. Less than a month open and a crazy-busy Friday nite in KoP, so a bit behind. And a wee bit pricey for us. Definitely a cool place. Killer desserts, BTW. We hope to return. Just need to save our sheckles.

Hmmm, today for some reason they had NO drinks available. None. Okay, I'll go to the station, just give me my food. So, I get to the window and the guy says my order is most definitely not here. Really, it's not? Weird. Again, he said it wasn't there. We began pulling off, no longer to his window and he yells "OH HERE IT GO!!!!!!" Whaaaaaaaaaaaat?? No way. Shove that order, man! Also, no Red Box. What can you really expect from people making, maybe, $350 every two weeks?

Had lunch here with my daughter and best friend after visiting a nearby spa. Had the Monsieur and the ham was amazing. The drinks were a bit pricey but overall great flavor and value for the money, and nice atmosphere.

My friend and I were in town for a music festival when we happened to get lost in the wrong part of town. We knew we had reached a safer area when the houses started becoming slightly more decorated and we saw this place! We bookmarked it for later and came back. (The branding and whole farm-to-table thing really got us)

When we returned that night we felt slightly underdressed as we'd just gotten out of a music festival, but our waitress made us feel right at home. She took care of us immediately and made excellent suggestions.

We ordered the oak grilled flat iron steak and the burger (both were excellent)- however, my friend asked for her steak medium-well. After she received the steak, she felt bad telling the server that it was undercooked as she was extremely accommodating. The server came all the way from across the restaurant and asked my friend "is that steak too red for you? let me grab you a new one." and returned with a perfectly cooked steak.

THAT'S service. 

Will definitely come back here again, if I ever happen to be in Tampa.

And they have $3 PBR'S!

The disclaimer here is that I only ate a piece of pie here last night.

But the vibe was so welcoming, the service so friendly, the mood so upbeat, the pie so affordable and the music (The Get Reels - http://www.reverbnation.com/thegetreels) so fun that I had a fantastic time.

I did not expect to hear a bagpipe rendition of Rocky Top, but I'm certainly happy that I did.

I'll be back to try one of the sandwiches that others have raved about or just to chillax in a happy place.

I came on a Saturday night at 7PM, and Farmicia wasn't too packed at all, although it became more populated around 8PM. We started off with an assortment of freshly baked breads - my personal favorite was the pumpernickel, and they also offered rosemary olive and multigrain breads.

The food was great. We started out with the french lentil salad, which had a very generous helping of goat cheese, as well as an interesting mix of lentils, red bell peppers and carrots. The crunchiness of the vegetables complemented the savory yet creamy goat cheese. Then, we ordered the Mega veggies and grains, which was A LOT. It had a delightful combination of the lentil mix, mushroom and tofu, sauteed green veggies, carmelized sweet potato, Cannelli beans, beetroot salad, and also fresh hummus. This definitely was a large portion for one person.

The St. Pete's fish was pan-fried, overall a tender two fillets. The roasted potatoes were also well done. Farmicia is BYO, which is definitely an added bonus! I had a great (more intimate ambiance) experience, and would definitely come again.

Great stop for lunch. We had sandwiches and Mac n cheese. Visiting Tucson from NYC and have to add that the bread competes with my local bakery - a very famous one that bakes for their own chain of top rated restaurants. The turkey was fresh pulled, not the typical food service stuff. The salads at the next tables looked good too. My only comment was that mine had too much mayo, but I didn't specify otherwise (and I should have). 

Will add this to our places to revisit on our annual trip out here

Fried pickles were good but came out with our dinner. Older crowd was there watching golf on a Sunday evening about 5pm. Lots
Of things on the menu. The Catfish Basket was good. Kids meatloaf was good and the bacon cheese burger was also good. I got the Club sandwich, dry but still good. VERY pricey for what it is. The fries are a shoe string style. I like the more thicker ones. Kids welcome but next time (if there will be one) it will be just the husband and I. $3.25 for draft bud light. $4.25 for the "special" drafts.  4 in our party dropped $80. Averages out $20 per person but we had a child with us. Service wasn't the greatest but I think it was just our waitress. Other's I seen did a good job. Over all a good place for family or date night. Couldn't get a
Good pic the place was dark! Bathroom extremely small.
Hall to bathroom tight squeeze.

Great brunch. Outstanding Bloody Mary. Lump crabmeat and apple salad with light dressing was delicious.  The place was packed.  All food was very good and service excellent.

Actually had a business meeting at the table after eating and we were not rushed out.

Wow, just wow. These people really care about their customers and their needs and the quality of the food. We got there right after a big rush and had a concert to get to.  The owner (!) was concerned that we'd have to wait a long time for our food. She was very up front about the wait time, about 40 minutes, but promised we could get seated right away. Our wait person came over with menus and, because we were kind of in a hurry, took the time to review the menu and took our orders right then. I have some allergies so had to ask questions and she was really nice about it. Pot roast for him and green chili pork stew for me. She was in such a rush she forgot the drink order but they came back a little later and got those from us.  39 minutes later our food came, it was so delicious I am still talking about it. By far the best food we've had so far in Tucson.  And they gave us our lemonades for free because of the wait!  I'd give them 6 stars if I could.

I've only eaten here once but was impressed during our one visit. Spring rolls with peanut sauce were great along with the bubble tea. Though they don't have as many flavors as other places, I will say the green apple and coconut we ordered were both great. I'm not a huge pho guy but the lady says hers were great. I instead had the grilled beef with rice and was very pleased. Prices were quite reasonable and the staff was friendly so this is definitely a place I will be returning to. Looking forward to trying more on the menu!

I cannot say enough good things about The House Painters. They recently painted the interior of my condo and did a fantastic job- they were fast, professional and did everything I asked. Brendan was lovely to deal with- very responsive and got the whole project done in an incredibly timely manner. He even weighed in on paint colors and helped me decide based on his expertise. I felt completely comfortable leaving him and his crew to work and I would recommend this company to anyone needing any painting done.

Queen Donair is the only reason I am ever okay with going back to Edmonton.

One of the very few downsides of living in Vancouver is the lack of a decent donair - when the craving hits, I miss Queen Donair something fierce. I've never encountered a better donair, and I have longing dreams in which a QD opens up in downtown Van. 

Every time I'm in Edmonton, we go to QD. Multiple times. Sometimes in the same day. And now I really want one. Wonder if they'd deliver to the coast?

I have read all the other reviews and have to disagree with the negative ones.  If I only had one rental experience with Payless I would have thought perhaps I was just lucky.  I had such a positive experience my first time that I returned all through my house hunting process to Payless.  They were far less expensive than any other rental.  I had researched beforehand and knew they were off site, however, it was only 10-15 minute shuttle ride.  It is true that the agents tried to push additional insurance and gas but I was not interested and refused...end of story.  the rental car was fine, clean and low mileage.  I was on a tight budget so price was important to me.  
If you are on an expense account by all means go to a national car rental at the airport but otherwise Payless served me well.

The San Antonio Spurs contain elements that are the embodiment of Le Foret - ruthlessly efficient play execution, predictable quality of competitiveness (unless the coach decides to send the 3 best players home before a nationally televised game, of course), and focused attention to details. Le Foret features well-executed dishes that are above reproach, fresh ingredients shown through flavor and textural quality, and accessorizing components that synergistically elevate an entree's experience. However, just as fans have been critical of the Spurs' vanilla, albeit excellent play and lack of Showtime highlights, Le Foret's absence of creativity and innovation in its dishes hamstring its otherwise uncapped potential.

The Angus Beef Tenderloin is abounding in juiciness, with its seared and seasoned crust dutifully preserving the clean taste of the medium-rare depths that is as easily sliced through as a stick of slightly melting butter. The small tumbleweed of spinach and thin sheets of potato are carefully distinct in flavor to provide a medley of flavors for the entree.

Le Foret is exactly as advertised, which is reassuring to some and bland for others.

So I never even made it out of my car to checkin.  I decided to book this because of the awesome price and location based strictly off of the reviews.  However once I drove up and got eyes on the place I realized I had made a terrible mistake.  Unless u and whoever you're staying with has concealed carry licenses and are in fact strapped I wouldn't get out of my car.  Trust me I've stayed in some shady places to try and be cheap and get the "steal/discount".  This place is so ghetto and unsafe I wouldn't stay there if they told me it was free.  Luckily they do have nice staff because after calling the booking.com sales associate, who then called the hotel, they agreed to refund me fully.  Just spend the extra 75$ and stay somewhere close to broadway and fun/safe.  Holiday Inn Express has been awesome and within walking distance down Broadway.
Aloft is a Starwood property. A cheaper W hotel but has a cool concept with a trendy vibe. Paid less than $100 a night.

The food was straight-up sad. Bland, low quality ingredients, inauthentic and way overpriced. Chipoltle is better. Please do yourself a favor and go to Oasis down the street, or cross the bridge and get some south philly tacos. I'm giving 2 stars instead of 1 because the server was alright.

seated at 7:00, left by 9:30. 20 minutes just to take order. Another hour till the meals were on the table. Watched a larger party seated 20 minutes later order, get and finish their food before ours was served...and served cold! Server blamed cook. No manager came to table. Gave us three slices of pie for 8 adults. We watched our server drink a beer while our glasses remained empty.
Great oysters, excellent service, and good poboys.  Expect to wait during the lunch and dinner rush.  Only complaint, too much bread and not enough shrimp on poboys.

JT Auto is my go to for any auto service needs. I have referred multiple friends and family here and all have been extremely satisfied. Customer service-great, car service-quick turnaround and zero issues.

I don't know where all these awful reviews are coming from. I have personally been to this spot on multiple occasions. To be honest the first time wasn't perfect but it was by no means not a good sandwich. 

Since then I have been back several times and the sandwich has gotten better every time! Like every new business adjustments need to be made and it looks like this owner did just that. 

The owner is super friendly and will make your sandwich exactly to your liking if you have a special request! I got a pepperoni grilled cheese with the buffalo style cheese and it was prime time. Definitely recommend this place!

Healthy, fast food that tastes great. Everything is fresh and not processed. The staff is always friendly and welcoming. If you want fast food but don't want a processed burger or chicken strip, try CBW. The bowls are my favorite and always leave me satisfied for several hours but never with that bloated feeling that you get from a McDs or Chik--fil-a.

I go to several locations and the experience is consistent.
Finely brewed coffee, great baristas, cool interior, and very friendly. I love this place.
Fast and very good experience! Finding a place to get a decent haircut is a challenge, but Jessica did a great job! This will now be my regular location when I need a cut or trim.
We have eaten here twice now and both times I had the blacked grouper tacos as they were so perfectly cooked tasty and light. Not greasy at all and service excellent highly recommended

There's nothing wrong with the staff. It's all about the set up. The location is great but the parking lot and drive through are horrible. It makes me never want to come here because of it. I can't imaginewhat morning rush is like. Again, the staff is quick and friendly, but this place NEEDS 1 star based on the set up alone.

Got my hair done by Haley, she did a really awesome job!!! I'm from la and normally only go to one person but if Haley was in la I'd make the switch! She's super friendly which made the whole experience  more enjoyable!

Ok. Seriously, the thing that absolutely sticks out here, is their duck. Honestly, I've only dined in here once, but I've taken out a whole duck a multitude of times. Potluck? Party? bring a duck, it'll spice up the environment and people will be super surprised. 
You can even ask for the bones too if you want and use it for a stew or something, but yeah. This place is really good. (especially the duck) nuff said

Opening night of football is kind of a big deal. You would think the management here would staff appropriately. Cheerleaders failed to service the people who are willing spend their hard earned money. Will not return.

New owners have upgraded everything from the ice cream to the decor. Great for a dessert, or rent the place out for an event. Michelle and Tawnie really helped make our recent birthday party a big success.

My review is not directed at any one Publix because I truly don't know which Publix was utilized. I used Publix delivery service for the first and last time yesterday. I've been a loyal customer of Publix for more then 30 years and have come to associate them with quality. So I was pressed for time on the day of my family's 4th of July party and thought delivery service would be a great option. Publix uses Instacart for its deliveries. Among the 29 items I ordered 7 were BOGOs and I ordered the advertised BOGOs. Only 3 of my BOGOs were delivered the other 4 items were single items. I had incorporated the BOGOs into my party menu. Who orders 17 burgers and one pack of burger buns? When I reported the omissions I was told this was my fault for not indicating quantity 2. Well I didn't order the 3 items I did receive BOGOs on with duplicate quantities either and yet I still managed to get the BOGOs so I reject the blame the victim dodge there.  Instacart refused to bring the duplicates and refused to discount the price.  This meant I had to hit a store after all which increased my costs and wasted my time. Buyer beware. i will never use this service again

This place is average in terms of cleanliness & the condition of the machines. We went on a Sun. afternoon & there were plenty of machines available. We are used to laundries at campgrounds, which are usually nicer & cheaper.

I can't believe it has taken me so long to review Pizza Plaza. This is my all-time favorite pizza parlor. Not only do they have an incredible variety of top-knotch slices (chicken taco, cheesesteak pizza and the buffalo chicken are a few of my favorites there), but they also make a series of excellent sandwiches, wraps and other foods. 

Their chicken parmesan wrap is the best I've had (other than my family's homemade ones), and the crispy chicken honey mustard wrap might be my favorite food in general. Alongside the wraps comes a hardy serving of delicious steak fries. Although, if you order a seperate side of fries they're a different style - a little skinnier as opposed to steak fries. Other highlights at Pizza Plaza include their garlic knots and the very cool fountain beverage dispenser that lets you access an endless number of sodas and drinks on a little touch screen. 

Outside of the awesome food, Pizza Plaza also moved/renovated their shop in the last few years, so the establishment is clean and new. The people who own it are avid members of the community, sponsoring local teams and schools and attending a parish right down the road. They also own a bunch of other locations including Warrington Pizza and La Fogata, which is just a few doors down if you're looking for authentic Mexican food. 

I can't say enough good things about Pizza Plaza. As hard as it is for me to break that four-star ceiling, they earn an easy five from me.
This place rocks! Friendly staff and flavors that are anything but basic. I'm very much enjoying my whiskey and praline icecream cone and the bite I stole from my husband's salted caramel cone

I'm kinda surprised by the reviews on Yelp for Embers. This was our first stop for food once we got to NOLA, and I thought it was pretty delicious!

The service was attentive, the drinks were great, and the food was delicious. We snagged a seat on the balcony and it's true the view from here is pretty neat.

I had the catfish, and it was tasty. My only complaint is that on the night we went (and it was a Friday) they seemed to be out of a few menu items, like the ribs for instance. 

It's a nice place to eat, especially if you want a decent sit-down dinner that isn't surrounded by your typical bourbonites.

Oh ya, the Bread pudding... YUM!

I came back again for Saturday brunch and I'm so glad they finally have biscuits and gravy on the menu because that was exactly what I was craving for!! If you're craving some serious southern comfort food, you have to order this. Two sunny side eggs in top of their homemade honey biscuits, with their homemade gravy/sausage sauce heavily drizzled on top. You get their house potatoes on the side too. We ordered a side of maple bacon as well and it was THE PERFECT thing to have after a long week of work. I hope they keep this dish on their menu a long time!!!

Let me start by saying we're pretty laid back.  It took us an hour and a half to get a drink and an appetizer.  We waited 15 minutes for second glass of wine which they finally came back and told us they were out of.  At that point we ask for our bill & left & we'll NEVER return.

PJ's is definitely one of those restaurants that's either dead inside or completely busy 
Make sure to call in before you go and ask if there's a wait
If there's a game going on, you're probably gonna have to wait a good 15-30 mins to get a seat
But no matter what, there food is almost always on point and there service just the same
There fries with cheese (I think they're called the PJ's fries? But don't quote me) and their burgers.
So juicy and scrumptious- makes me hungry just thinking about it!
All of their app's are good (appetizer's) especially their mozzarella sticks :) 
All in all, a great place to eat and watch a good game!

best......barbque.....EVER!!!!  i live in los angeles and anyone who is familiar with LA knows about Phillips Barbque and Woody's Barbque.  The Joint puts them to SHAME!!!!!  

i had the sampler plate: brisket, ribs, and pulled pork.  *mouth watering*

the place itself was tiny and down-home'ish.  the one thing i didn't like about it was that in order to get your drink, you have to get your ice from this huge ice maker bin...and everyone uses the scooper to get their ice.  too many hands in that thing for my liking, but it's a fair trade off for the fantastic food.  next time you're in nola, go there.

Can I give ZERO stars? Great way to run a business...

I am totally PISSED OFF and happy at the same time. If that's possible?

I have been planning a 3-day cleanse for a month. I purchased a ridiculously cheap Groupon for a 3-day juice cleanse from TN Juice Bar back in late July. I placed my order 72 hours in advance (48 was required) and received an email confirmation with time/date/place to pick up my order in Hendersonville today (45 minutes from my home). I arrived on time at 1pm today and the location was closed. They closed at 11am. I waited 20 minutes as I searched their website and the internet and could not find a contact #. Hmmm!

After inquiring with the massage therapist next door, she said, "I'm not a gossip, but I have heard rumors they got in over their head with the Groupon deal". She gave me directions to a second location about 2-3 miles away where the owner is a personal trainer. Their logo was on the door. Closed! Locked up tight!

I immediately detoured to my favorite juice bar (The Urban Juicer) in Nashville who provided me with 15 cold-pressed juices & 3 cashew milks + 3 elixirs + an insulated bag + a gallon of refillable alkaline water to make my cleanse happen. They usually require 48 hours notice but their "cold-pressed team" was in-house and still working.

I came home and chatted live with a Groupon customer service rep who immediately gave me a credit after I explained what happened. It hit my account while I was still chatting with him.

DO NOT do business with unreliable vendors! Super cheap deal should have been my first clue! The bad reviews and no phone contact info came after the fact. I wanted to call and confirm my order but couldn't find any contact information on their website or the internet.


Steer clear of TN Juice Bar!

I'm new to Philly and was very overdue for a haircut. As many of the Hush reviews say, Yelp led me to a very good place. I had a fantastic experience! The girl who washed my hair gave me a spa-worthy scalp massage and was very careful not to get any water in my ears. It felt like true pampering. That alone would've made me write this review. :)
My hair was cut by Pam, who was very laid back and nice. We chatted about the city, and she gave me some great restaurant recommendations (nice as I'm a newbie). More importantly, she did EXACTLY what I wanted with my hair with minimal input from me.
I trusted my hair to the same person for over five years, until I moved. This was definitely a seamless transition for me going to Hush. I loved Pam and would definitely go back to her!
Another stylist made himself available to me on a whim to give me a consult on what I should do about my hair color. Everyone is so nice and knowledgeable about their craft at Hush. It was a treat to go there!

Finally made it out to this place for brunch and was really pleased with it! Really good, Mexican-inspired brunch options, all for under $10 (which given how out of hand brunch options and prices can get, I really appreciate that in a restaurant). The service was very friendly, although in such a small space, it was really noticeable when they all started chatting with each other. I got the vegetarian enchiladas and my boyfriend got the breakfast cemita, which were both quite good. While waiting, our waitress brought us chips and salsa, which was nice since I usually arrive to brunch with ravenous hunger and want to start eating as soon as possible. With two coffees and juices the total was less than $25, which by brunch standards I think is great. I definitely want to come back and try more off their brunch menu, and maybe even their lunch and dinner stuff sometime.

Rooster has great gluten free and vegan options. This is the sirloin and goat cheese crepe (with arugula, caramelized onions, and tomato jam) on the gf/vegan crepe. Only 4 stars because I got a coffee cocktail and one of the ingredients separated and so it was chunky and not pleasant to drink. There is free parking behind the S. Grand location and behind the bank. Only brunch menu on Sat/Sun.

Get's two stars because at least the food was good. 
we have been here a few times now, and nothing change then all the  times the service was bad.I was hopping things would change well maybe not now i guess.

What can I say? Hooters used to be an exciting place for a guy's to go. Back then the women could actually be described as exotic and seductive.

 
It was the Playboy Club for the working class. No more. The girls working there have that over-worked and underpaid Wal-mart attitude and in some weird way Hooters thinks people should pay $15 for fried left-overs of a chicken and a couple of draft beers.

Furthermore servers are forced to handle credit card orders, tip out the bartenders and cooks, and who knows what other BS. So your generous tip gets ground down to a pittance.

Hooters  remember that the clientèle you are attracting tonight will be ordering 49 cent burgers and happy meals tomorrow. My suggestion: turn down the lights, turn down the thermostat to about 70, and let women do what they do best. Compete for dollars from horny men. 

Well at lease the last part was a joke but seriously you guy's need to make a change soon....
I can't get enough of HIS & HERS for happy hour! Great service. Great specials. There is something for everyone and... they are building a roof deck! :))
Food was good, a little too over seasoned. The server was extremely awkward and came off rude to us. Don't think I would be coming back. But they do have a huge beer list, that was pretty cool.

Think about the size of your living room. Cut it in half. Now turn off the lights. Put a record on and light a couple candles and you've got Bar One Fourteen. This spot is supposed to be a "listening room" and I liked that the darkness let me focus more on the vinyl record spinning at the bar. The tunes gradually shifted from soul and jazzy blues to groovy hip hop as the night went on, and I appreciated what the darkness and music did for the environment. The intimate and elusive space reminded me of some of the hidden bars I've visited in NYC. The wine and cocktails are fantastic, and the "Fancy AF" burger just might be the best burger I've ever had. The meat is cooked to perfection and melts in your mouth. You've got to try this burger; it alone is worth the call for a reservation. I also tried the chips & dip (good) wedge salad (good), popovers (really good), and chocolate mousse dessert (really good). If you're looking for a unique dining/drinks experience OR one of the best burgers in Indy, look no further!
Great place. Really creative rolls but not overcomplicated. I recommend the bibou and vetri rolls!

I have never had a bad experience at this Rita's in the 10+ years I've been coming here. My only potential complaint is around a common lack of stock in certain flavors, but could also be cause I am most often here late night. Staff is always amazing, well-trained, and customer focused.

Just had my first experience at Central Pet! Took my Golden Retriever in for grooming and she looks amazing. I checked out the facility while I was there and I can't wait to bring my dog back for daycare and boarding. A must see!

It was Memorial Day weekend. The place was the Oval. I finally found the Tot Cart without a ginormous Nightmarket type line.

It took me no time to decide on the G-Parm Tots. Garlic and Parm cheese on tator tots...yes, please!

The tots were ready within a few minutes and came out fairly hot.

They were good but nothing amazing.  Unfortunately, they just didn't live up to all the hype.

The portion was decent for $6 although if you think about a bag of tots from the supermarket it's kind of a lot.

I would have loved to have a dash of hot sauce or something on top to help the Parm and garlic stick to the tots better.

I wouldn't seek out the Tot Cart or wait in a long line, but I can definitely see myself going back for more.
Love the "baked to order" cookies!  They come out hot and are delicious!  I like that you can get coffee and chill, sit at the bar and have a drink, or dine and listen to great music.

I'm a girl and I just got a haircut by a guy named Ansol. He took his time to cut my hair. I've been to many hair salons and I don't trust many places in the US. I only get my hair cut in Korea but I can trust this guy. He's very skilled. He cut my hair exactly the way I wanted. I changed my mind so many times during the cut but every time he cut the way I asked him to and he never complained. He's also really good at cutting bangs. Totally recommend this place!!

This is my favorite Christmas shopping store. I don't think it is only for goths and dragon slayers. I have bought stuff for my grandmother, little sister, co-workers, husband and notone of them even looked like it came from the same store. I do beleive they have something for just about everyone and it's all pretty unique.. You will not find stuff like this in the mall kids. I say you should try it, just save some goos stuff for me, Christmas is coming :)
This place is delicious!  It's just a little pricey for the small portions they give but otherwise a solid choice for eating out.

Don't know if it was the Living Social voucher (which is discounted, not free) or whether we caught them on a bad day but our experience at Ms Tootsies was a mass of misunderstanding and disappointment.  

The two good things were the mini corn muffins w/ strawberry butter and the Grown Folks Iced Tea.  Now for the rest...

We arrived at 6pm and they already ran out of the turkey slider appetizer and smothered pork chops (which my boyfriend was looking forward to) so we ordered the crab/mac and cheese balls, chicken and waffle sliders and their "award winning, top rated on Food Network"  (as per our waitress) fried chicken.  

After 45 minutes the manager came by to ask how we were doing and we informed her that the appetizers hadn't arrived.  She apologized, said the crab/mac and cheese balls weren't ready yet due to "a misunderstanding" and offered to pack it up and give it to us on the house.  15 minutes later, the waitress brought out both appetizers... no mention of what the manager had said earlier.  The appetizers were bland but we were hungry since we skipped lunch in anticipation of a great meal.  Not 5 minutes later, before we were even halfway done, the entrees came out so we asked the waitress to pack what was left of the appetizers.  The fried chicken (I had the leg and thigh, he had the breast and wing) was over done and dry.  The sides were nothing spectacular, except for the greens which my boyfriend said had a nice "kick".  

The waitress must have noticed our disappointment because she said dessert was on her.  She went down the list of desserts, beginning with sweet potato pie.  When we said we wanted the pie, she said "we're out of pie".  Huh?  Why mention it if you're out of it?!  We told her, thanks, but we'd pass on dessert so what does she do?  She brings out 2 slices of cake, in take out containers and drops them in the bag with our appetizers.  Oh, and we were charged for the crab/mac and cheese balls, contrary to what the manager said.  At that point we just wanted to get out of there so we paid the bill and left.  

Never again, even if Ms Tootsies offers FREE vouchers.

This is the best Reno-area theater but the prices are so high it's hard to enjoy yourself. Or at least I have a problem. I can't think of the last time I went to a full-price movie. And the ticket prices for matinees have gotten high, too. 
I guess that's why God invented Netflix and "Redbox.

Went here for the all day Happy Hour which is on Mondays and Tuesdays. Half price sushi! $2-$4.50 ish. The food is great and the happy hour is a crazy good deal. Service is kinda slow though, especially during lunch/dinner hours.

I am in love with this place. So few places in Tucson have any class or modern flair and this place does. First off they make everything from scratch and use local ingredients when possible. The drink menu was over the top, fresh, and innovative, try the blueberry basil mojito. The menu was perfect, but I don't like a huge menu. The garlic bread was great. the salads were yummy and the pizza was awesome, I love the crust. We had great service and the happy hour looks like one of the better ones in this town. Fresh homemade good food!

Gave two cause food was pretty decent, but that's about it we got sat and table in like middle of everyone and when we asked for window next we carried napkins and menus and the. Waiter wasn't that friendly very short with us. As we where leaving three girl at desk not One saying have a good night. Like damn felt like that for eating now get out.

I stayed here for a 2 day convention.
The hotel room was fine and our front desk clerk, Lincoln, was a doll.

We also got 2 free bottles of water in our room so the next day we asked for 2 more - not realizing they charge for them $2 a bottle.  (I can easily drink 6-8 bottles a day.)

Not the end of the world but I would have liked to have known.

Also the catering service for our group was just AWFUL.
"Cod" fish with mango salsa was so fishy and old tasting and many of the pre-sliced cakes on display were dry and old.

Not a wonderful hotel but not bad to stay over for a night.  (Loaded with families going to Sesame Place).
Just avoid having any catered events here.

I would not waste my money. My son-in-law was one of the top three students in the computer arts school. They were full of promises in helping him locate a job once he graduated. He had exactly one interview through them and it was for data entry - not even in his field. After graduation - forget it - could not reach them - would not return phone calls - in other words - their assiatance is helping you find a job is virtually non-existent. He also found that the skills they teach are in many cases outdated. Graphic Arts and computer modeling changes quickly and what they taught was passe in the market place by the time he got out of school. If you want to throw tens of thousands of dollars away - go to a casino - your odds are probably better there than walking out of the Art Institute with a legitimate job in your field of study.

Enjoyed a nice dinner on a warm Saturday night at a table on the sidewalk. A number of great menu options we were torn about. We settled on the asparago pizza (without meat) and octopus. We were pleased with both, but especially the octopus which can be difficult to prepare. For dessert we shared a budino which was to die for. We felt the total price for our meal and drinks were very reasonable and good size portions.

This place is awesome, smallish, but great atmosphere, food is great for bar type food.
Fish spread, burgers, smoked beef and pork on site, what can I say? 
Tons of beers available, including local brews, which I like.
Their "angry peppers" are very hot, lightly breaded, filled with some sort of secret cheese concoction, and believe it or not, they're still crisp like a fresh pepper. Just awesome.
They have a grilled cheese sandwich on the side of menu reserved for kids. Ask them to add jalepenos, and hot relish. OMG. 
That's what is in picture. If your nearby, try this sometimes hard to find gem.

It is very difficult to find a trustworthy mechanic and auto place these days. You don't need to know someone or have someone "hook you up" here. The owner (Jeff) is always working the front desk which is a rarity these days. What you hear from him is what you get. He is fair and gives everybody the best prices around. Great workmanship is a given. Seriously try them out.

If you're looking for a unique dining experience, you've found it with The Refinery. If you're a picky eater, this might not be the place for you.

I don't even know how to begin my description of The Refinery. It is odd! The restaurant is located in a renovated house, and the seating is limited (make sure to book a reservation, or else you might be out of luck). The service is friendly, and the menu is always unique! The Refinery changes their menu weekly, so there is always something new and exciting to test out. I LOVE that they source local products as much as possible, and appreciate that they use ingredients that we aren't always used to seeing on menus (fiddlehead ferns, anyone? Lamb's brain?).

I tend to fall in love with the small plate offerings on the menu in comparison to the main courses. Green beans with house made ricotta cheese? Yes please! I will note that they always have a burger on their menu (the ingredients change), and it is KILLER. My husband was practically licking his plate the time he ordered the burger topped with brie and fig jam. Whoa.

If you live in the Tampa area, you have to try out this restaurant (and if you're visiting nearby from out of town, head on it as well)!

This is one of the best veterinary hospitals I've ever taken my animals to, and my new go-to place in Nashville.  I had to take in my 10 year old tabby cat because she was having a skin flare-up where she broke out in a scabby rash.  :(  Justin the vet-tech was very sweet and figured out she had fleas, and the rashes were an allergic reaction to the flea bites, something that is pretty common in cats.  Dr. Lawrence is amazing and hilarious, and gave my kitty a couple shots to take care of the itching and rashes.  I also got some serious flea medication for my fur-baby.  The total cost was around $200, but most of it was the flea meds.  The actual visit itself was only around $40, which is completely reasonable.

Do be prepared for them to push the "wellness plan," which is a pretty pricy health package for pets who are already healthy.  I only have to take my cats once a year for check-ups since they are in perfect health, but the plan would probably be beneficial to animals who have a lot of issues.

The cooking class at the New Orleans School of Cooking was something of a last minute choice. We had a flight back to CA at 3pm on Saturday and on Friday evening we called and reserved two spots for the 10am class the next day. So simple. 

We strolled over to the school, just a couple blocks of Bourbon St., and made our way into a small room of tables with a kitchen/stage in the front. 

For the next two and a half hours, we got cooking instructions for gumbo, jambalaya, pralines, and bread pudding. What I liked best was the history of the food and local culture. How the spices typical of New Orleans cooking found their way there over years of immigration. Really cool. 

And the food was super tasty. With the exception of the pralines, we were welcome to have seconds. Nice! Complimentary beers and sodas topped it off perfectly. Might have been the best 27 bucks I spent during my trip.

After the class, we all headed out into the gift shop/lobby and although I didn't buy anything, I saw that there were plenty of great gifts for cooks/ foodies. Lots of spice kits and utensils as well as the tourist standards of beignet mix and chickory coffee. 

I'd definitely recommend a visit if you're a foodie and/or a history geek.

I have been going there for over 30 years!  Yes you heard me right!  Since I was a kid.
 It has suffered since the change of the original owners who were wonderful people!

 Younger generation taking over, higher prices, food I find tastes different and service is bad.  Last time I had their kimchi I was so disappointed.  However tried some other new dishes and they were nice. There are more Korean restaurants around that are giving Bul Go Gi House some serious run for their money.

Sorry - no longer the best of St. Louis. We still go because it's close and it's good pizza, but it's only the third best pizza on my list. 

1. Feraro's
2. Louie's Deep Dish
3. Racanelli's

Still a good place to stop by for a slice.

Found this spot my last night in Philly.  Stopped in for happy hour, and ended up staying for 5 hours.  Beers great (Maudite on tap!), Drinks outstanding (Adam makes a mean Manhattan), Charcuterie awesome (LACON!).  We had eaten dinner already, but if we didn't, I would have been here, not doubt.  The menu looks awesome.  I guess I'll be back in Philly soon just to come back here.

The good: 1. The menu is and has been succinct. The staples are there, it exhibits creativity, but still manages to fit on one side of one sheet of paper. 2. The food is actually good. 3. The beer selection is varied and there's always something new for me to try. 4. When the weather's nice, the outdoor seating is pretty pleasant. 5. The staff is always friendly.

The questionable: 1. Try to find the price of the beer written down somewhere. This inevitably leads to a surprise bill. 2. The narrow first floor can be a challenge when trying to find a table.

The verdict: 1. Tonight, we arrived to find the second floor open - it is open and airy and the custom chairs, tables, and fixtures and very well designed and executed. 2. New items on the menu keep things fresh and yummy. 3. Dollar off draft bitters, can't beat that. Still no prices anywhere though.

We've got a number of good options for beer/food down in South Philly, but Sidecar never disappoints. We're going to add this back to the rotation.

What a fantastic (albeit spendy) hotel.  

I've stayed at some nice places over my years but this place did not cease to amaze me.  fantastic service, food, cocktails, rooms and view.  

The only downside is that it is so far outside of santa barbara and the taxis are 80 ish dollars.

I'll happily return.
Great food, music, and beer!!  Just a great place to come relax and people watch!  Love this place! Ps Jessica is a great waitress!
Friendly staff and fantastic breakfast. It's not fancy but perfect for a nice casual breakfast and they serve lunch all day too!

Wandered in here one night on vacation intrigued by the colorful goodies in the display windows. While the macaroons looked amazing, their price was a bit high for my taste. However, I tried a sample of King Cake and was hooked. Cinnamon infused brioche with a cream cheese swirl, covered in a sweet glaze and Mardi Gras colored sprinkles. Decided to buy one for the family back home. So delicious!
Local Gem! Great place, great people, great food. We always have a wonderful experience here. No complaints at all.

Omg.. This place, It's like heaven and hell combined lol.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND COMING HERE IF YOU DON'T HAVE A PAIR OF BALLS.

But yah, I loved this place. Our waiter was the booomb, such a great guy, personal and funny, but very professional at the same time.  The food was good. My mom though, being the type of picky person she is didn't like it very much, but she said it was okay lol. I got the porkchops which were great, cut just the right size, with 2 over-easy eggs and some sysco hashbrowns. (I can tell c; ) 

But yah, if you like a restaurant that is full of character and talkative locals, this is the place to come!

Great pizza. Top 3 in the whole Tampa area in my opinion. Definitely way beyond anything in south county. 

Update... They changed their pepperoni. Still great but the mini pepperoni made it different!

This location has the best mushroom version of Imo's pizza, period.  If you are a mushroom lover, this is the location for you.  Most Imo's dice their mushrooms and sprinkle them on, as if they were parsley - or something.  This location actually fills the pizza with large slices of mushroom, sized appropriately as a topping, not like other Imo's who sprinkle mushroom on as if it were an embellishment. 
 I had a pizza from  another area Imo's last week and I bet there was one mushroom (chopped fine) on the whole thing.  So disappointing.  I'm NEVER disappointed with my Mushroom pizzas from this Clayton location, though.

Great little neighborhood spot.After a few nights of expensive,heavy meals we wanted something lighter and more of a neighborhood vibe.Walked through Marigny neighborhood Sunday afternoon and were lured in by the $4.00 Bloody Mary-yum! Bartender (Justin??) makes a killer mix,and was very friendly.We asked to see a menu for dinnner and decided to come back-he took care of making a reservation for us.
Dinner that night was terrific-the fried oysters and the onion rings were so light and not greasy! Also did a pasta dish with Penne and crawfish tails-so much I had to take a box home-perfect for breakfast the next day.
A great place  and good value!

I always order the steak fajitas and share with a friend. The grilled onions, bell peppers and avocado along with the salsa are delicious. For $15.00 this is the best deal for two people at this place. The other items for one person are too much for what you get and lack flavor. The chicken taqutos are good too.

Three stars seems kinda stingy, right? Well. Hold on, cuz this is about balance.

As we were leaving, my girl-friend Teeter asked to buy one of their hats with the trademark "I'm a Javaholic!" slogan in cool, icy-capped font (like the slurpee font). 

Well, the cashier made us feel about 2 inches small, saying they didn't have any.

That is F'd up. Like Teeter, I'm a recovering Javaholic, who used to be addicted to Javahol. I wanted to wear a t-shirt as an encouraging nod to other javaholics, but apparently this isn't something the Gold Standard thinks is an important issue.

Also, the back room looks like a ski-lodge, which is cool unless you're trying to film a sci-fi movie in it (again... 3 stars)
Awesome beer good food solid spot, everything's brand new. Big tvs and a projector, awesome place to hang and watch the game

Had a great visit here! The service was great, the restaurant is very clean and the food was delicious. Avoid the long waits and chaos at Los Agaves and go to Los Arroyos!! We both had chicken enchiladas and they were off the hook!
Great pizza. If I lived in Northern Liberties I would probably eat here every day.

It's an excellent place for some breakfast food.

It's located a bit away from the city, however it does have parking.  The parking can be a bit tight though, and there is usually a bunch of people here, so you may have to tap into your creative genes to get a spot.  

The food here is excellent, and the prices are decent.  The people seem friendly, and there is a decent seating area.  It's not a high glamour place, so it's not going to wow you, but they have a ton of options, and very customize able. 

I usually order online (a great feature, which wins a star in my heart) and just pick it up.  However, they seem to get those delayed, and sometimes don't get the order, so if you order online, make sure you call ahead to see if they got the order.  I don't think too many people do it, so they rarely check I believe.  

The bagels are excellent, and the cream cheese is pretty good.  A good amount of choice for bagels and cream cheese.  I'm not a culinary expert when it comes to telling you if it was made fresh or a year ago in some warehouse, but it tasted very good to me.   

They have a pizza on a bagel option, which most likely isn't very healthy, but something I can definitely eat, enjoy, and then omit on the fitness pal account.  Essentially some cheese, and toppings on a bagel.   

The veggie wrap is excellent, I've gotten the hummus and veggie one and it's a wonderful wrap.  The best thing about it is the customize able aspect of it, so you can choose from a bunch of stuff, rather than the standard affair at cafe's where you have to all but choose from what they serve.  

I haven't tried out their drinks, but some of them do seem appealing.  The staff is friendly for sure.  

Just be warned that this place gets very busy in the morning, so you may have to set apart some time to get your food.
best friend chicken ive ever had. light crispy flufly not thicks tender meat falls off bone. sides go good with chicken. waiter was friendly. smiles
Always great service and good, quality pizza for the price. This local business has been around for years and I have never had a bad experience. Fresh pizza at a good price with a big smile.

Pretty good beer selection, great friendly staff. Food was also good, only drawback is the dining space is mostly upstairs, so it feels somewhat disconnected from the activity downstairs. All in all, definitely recommended, if I'm in town again I will absolutely come back!

I have been to this IHOP many times, server does not ask about needs (coffee, drinks) food severed was cold. Very poor for this location.

Also I witnessed a kitchen worker using the bath room and NOT washing his hands as he left. I pray that this is not the new standard for this location.

Saturday night, my boyfriend and I went hunting for a savory dinner within walking distance. La Viola - packed on both sides of the street. Monk's - 45 minute wait. Ernesto's - well, I'd been there before and it was a little pricier than what we would have liked. After a lot of Yelping on our iPhones and a little sample of the latest Tastykake Butterscotch Krimpets water ice sloshing around in our bellies, we found Giorgio on Pine.

The owner must have asked us how we were doing three or four times before we ordered. When our appetizer appeared, we were floored. Their Mussels and Clams are excellent, drenched in a rich, flavorful cream sauce. A little salty, but good nonetheless. Per our waitress' suggestion, we left only shells and a thin film of sauce for the kitchen to clean after devouring most of it with some of Giorgio's complimentary bread.

Instead of ordering one entree, I ordered two sides of pasta - the Fettucine and the Gnocchi. They are essentially just half-sized portions of a regular entree, and at half the price as well. Though, I personally consider a side of their pasta to be quite enough for a normal serving size. However, for a first visit, this was a wonderful opportunity to avoid making difficult decisions and try all the pasta I wanted! The Fettucine happened to be one of the specials of the day -- juicy, succulent shrimp and homemade fettucine, tossed with a bit of chopped tomatoes and mushrooms in a delectable white wine garlic sauce. Definitely getting that again!

I usually get Gnocchi at most Italian restaurants because I love mushy things. However, Gnocchi is usually hit or miss, as sometimes, places like Olive Garden can really screw it up with a cheesy cream sauce that is over the top. Giorgio, on the other hand, presented some perfectly mushy potato dumplings nicely balanced with beef ragout. Though it was not spectacular, it was better than most of the Gnocchi I have been foolish enough to try. It's also nice to know that the "side of pasta" serving of Gnocchi was just enough for me to get my fix - so it was well worth my money in my opinion.

We didn't try dessert because we were so stuffed, but we do plan on visiting again with our parents! Aside from the food, the service is what truly distinguishes this place from any other Italian BYO.

After passing this place by for the first year of its existence, my friends and I decided to see what Mr. Giorgio had going on and I'm glad we finally made it. One thing that sets any dining experience apart from the next is a friendly staff. After all, my friends are the sort that like to take over restaurants and turn them into their own private dining room, a tendency I'm sure fellow patrons appreciate. Anyway, Giorgio's allows you to do just that. They even have a separate room that could accommodate 20 or so people.

My one friend and I ordered the shellfish spaghetti while the other pal went with the gnocchi. Overall, the seafood tasted incredibly fresh and the pasta, perfectly al dente. It's a BYOB, but unlike most others you can pay with a credit card here. Perfect service from our adorable waitress and post-dinner chit chat with Mr. Giorgio himself. This will definitely become a neighborhood go-to.

This was a really awesome experience and was a great way to cap off our New Orleans adventure. We did the tour on a freezing cold saturday morning at 930. We expected it to warm up but it never did, it only got colder, which was the only bad part of the tour. 

Our tour guide Derrick was incredibly knowledgable and friendly, informing all of us from a New Orleanian's perspective about the issues the Ninth Ward has faced, the issues it's still facing as well as it's hopes for the future. It was a really positive tour, focusing more on the brighter and unique features of the city rather than a whole bunch of depressing information about Hurricane Katrina. 

We stopped off at Cajun Joes for a po-boy about half way through the tour, which was  really big and reasonably priced. The other major stop was Ronald Lewis' House of Dance and Feathers, a museum dedicated to the culture of New Orleans societies and clubs, with emphasis on the Louisiana Indians. The museum had a large array of photographs and incredibly complex and colourful costumes worn by Ronald in various parades over the years. He also has a book for sale that he wrote, that delves deeper into the many complexities and variations in this particular culture unique to New Orleans.

Derrick even took us to his local bar afterward for a quick beer, which we found you were allowed to cycle and drink at the same time! Overall an awesome tour, highly recommended and definitely worth the money.

This is my third time here. I am addicted to the food, flavors. I can't get the taste out of my head, it's like you have to eat the food several times a week. Raj is the owner, I think he does the cooking and serving the customers.
Today is really busy, so worth the wait.

Best brunch place in the Bella Vista area by far and that includes Sabrina's, which is always good but not worth the standard hour plus wait in my opinion. 

Can't go wrong with anything in the menu here but the specials are what make this place stand out. I typically don't even look at the menu and order of the brunch specials when I go.

One of the most underrated establishments in the city. Their fish and sweet potato curry tacos are intoxicating. Their tortillas are perfectly cooked and their cheese dip will satisfy even the major cheese dip eaters. I always get a lit and take it home (because I have extra y'all), so I get to enjoy it twice. The flavor is really good too, not like everyday cheesedip. 

I always sit over at gaslight and have a Cadillac margarita (or in my case a Buick Margarita because I enjoy a rail tequila sometimes). Really great meal (really two meals) for two people under $25 is a STEAL. Great for groups too because it's usually not packed and the bartenders are really nice and make great consistent drinks. Really really like this place and am a regular patron because the food and service speak for themselves.

In the brief time since I've moved to Philadelphia, I've been trying to get to know the cheesesteak more and more. I grew up going to Pat's whenever I would venture into the city, but now that I live here (and have enjoyed hundreds of steaks from The King) I am trying to broaden my horizons a bit.

Was Steve's something I should've passed over? It seems like the consensus among longtime locals is mixed. Well, anyway, as a new resident, here are my thoughts (for what they're worth): 

It's a cheesesteak. If it's not at least somewhat tasty and appealing when drunk, there's a SERIOUS problem.

Thankfully Steve's doesn't have that problem. The steaks here are very much edible. But they are nothing special in my opinion. The roll was slightly stale, plus they used sliced steak instead of chopped, so the sandwich ends up being a little flatter than other places. 

If I was drunk, popping into Steve's would be a no-brainer. But for a casual, satisfying, quick lunch or dinner.....I give it a pass.

Onward to my next cheesesteak!

This place has great coffee and kava and kratom. The space is very modern and versatile, so you can work or study there during the day, or unwind and relax at night. The employees are all very pleasant and knowledgeable. This addition to Largo is a welcome breath of fresh air. I highly recommend that anyone check it out.

Wanted to compare this to the DC location.
 Nicely designed. The food was good as i was hoping it would be. The service was slower than I liked. Ordered a specialty tea and after waiting awhile asked the waitress how much longer before we received it. She then told us they were out of the tea. So if we didn't ask we would have just been waiting. Used utensils were cleared away and again waited awhile for a new set. We actually had to ask for a set. Too many little mistakes more of a nuisance dining here actually. I don't feel I should have to constantly ask or remind the staff to bring me what was ordered or what they removed from my table

Asshole Central.

Goto the USPS near your work..not here. If you work here, go wherever you live..not here.

Epitome of smug, slow, angry fuckos... too important to be waiting on you. The opposite of courteous, helpful and "customer-oriented". 

Sure, its a post office "What do you expect"? Well, I expect guys behind the window to speak. Also, when asked a question, it'd be ok if they answer. Ya know, do your job in a speed faster than a glacier melting. Else, quit and work at Wendy's. 

Save yourself a headache, stay away.

Great place. Quarter Notes, very solid cover band.  Male vocals pretty good. Female lead is amazing and makes it worth the visit when they play.  Drinks about same as most of The St. 

If the shot girls come up, say "no"forcefully so that others hear you and turn your back to them.  You will get raped otherwise.  Owner needs to tone these parasites down.  Nothing short of criminal. Classy joint otherwise.

I understand history and all but I don't think this place is very good. The raw oysters and the bread get stars but the famous bbQ shrimp was mealy (over cooked) and not v flavorful. My salad was limp and some pieces had turned. The last star is for the asparagus which were well cooked. Save your money and go to one of the 45000 other restaurants that are amaze in New Orleans.

Service was good, food was mediocre at best, and atmosphere was a bit awkward.  We ordered soup to share, and they were unfortunately unable to make our first two choices due to not having the ingredients, but they did make accomodations by substituting a couple ingredients. The shrimp wontons were also "just okay" for my tastebuds, compared to other restaurants in Indy.  While I don't believe I'll try it again, I'd recommend giving it a shot for your own tastebuds.

I enjoyed this restaurant immensely. I saw a tv show that featured their coconut cake. And the food in general but I take coconut cake very seriously. We enjoyed every minute while there. Our server, Asha, was lovely and knew the menu items quite well. Our every need was seen to and the service was impeccable.  We had the ribeye for two and it was delicious. The cake was ridiculously good. If you come to Nashville, you should eat here.

So very yummy!! I ordered the salmon and then the baby spinach salad for lunch, and both were amazing, a flavorful taste explosion! The setting is stylish, fun and casual, and the service was also excellent. I brought home the Shepherds Pie for my son and I to share for dinner (which I have never had before), and it is a cheesy, meaty, potato-y, DECADENT treat- and comfort food. I Love this new find and am excited to return when there's live music in the evening.

I had the best experience getting my first Brazilian ever with Erica! She was so kind and relaxing. I'm not going to lie it was waaaay out of my comfort zone but she made it such an enjoyable experience that I already booked my next appointment! The salon she's at is so cute and cozy too! But she's so polite, professional and personable which is hard to find sometimes. But you will not regret going to her!

I enjoyed my visit and haircut and eyebrow wax today at Encore.  It was a nice, clean and stylish salon.  And the cut is great- just what I wanted for summer.  I appreciated Rick's coloring and styiing insights that he gave while he did his work. I will be back!

Wow. Where should i start? This was by far our worst experience while visiting New Orleans. We've been to some great places, but this...wasn't that. We stumbled upon this place after seeing that Dragos was closed for the evening. Just to give you the rundown...the waitress didn't offer bread that should come complimentary with the charbroiled oysters. When we asked about it, she stated that, yes it came with the meals "but lot of people waste the bread so...." Excuse me?? So does that mean you just don't offer it?  I cant help but wonder what criteria ones party must meet to be offered the complementary bread :|  I'm thinking the waitress was extremely absent minded, new, or a combination of the two.  She forgot to bring out the steak entree for one of us and a dessert for another.  Please keep in mind that our orders were TINY and it really wasn't much to remember outside of the steak and dessert besides a couple of cocktails and the aforementioned oysters.  When the Manager came over to check on us after one of us asked her to take back the Gumbo which was extremely salty, I asked him about the status of the steak. He disappeared and that's when our server came back asking how it was to be cooked since she had forgotten to put the order in.  At this point we cancel the steak because too much time has passed.  Since our bill was only $35 you would think the Manager would have come back over or comped us after forgetting the main entree and dessert, but he retreated to the back of the restaurant and didn't come back out.  I wouldn't waste my time or money here.

Casino is so gross. Their is no ventilation at all, it is hot and very smokey inside. This place was very depressing to be in. Will never go back again. Not as I remembered as a kid. The cashiers are very rude and not very attentive. Thought I would check out Gilly's bar in the casino on a theme night. Their was 3 people in the whole bar... Never again!!!

I just left this location. I must say the customer service was amazing! I went in with a issue that no where else could help me with, and they did! Thank you  Gonzalo, Teresa, and Nate for you top notch advice, and help!

Best place ever to get your hair done ! It feels like home , such a cute little shop ! Where everyone is your best friend or your family ! Most times people come early or stay after just so we can finish talking or have some dessert drinking some coffee or tea , ok well enough about the clients ! Let's get down to the real lady at hand !!! LINDA ! Linda knows everything , and if for some reason she doesn't and you want it you better bet your bottom dollar she will find it out and master it ! You can't go wrong here ! Trust me ! I started going here 4 years ago ! Kerri

Somehow, we got a bent axle on our travel trailer and completely ruined one of the four tires. I only found it because that tire happened to get a nail in it and went flat. I called numerous RV and auto shops in and around Carson City where we live and nobody could work on this problem. 

I found Sunshine Service on the web. They DO work on axle problems, and even though it's a 40 mile drive to get to them, we had no choice if we wanted to fix our trailer. We made an appointment, and dropped our trailer off at 8am. 

About four hours later we got a call, informing us that our trailer was done. They straightened the axle and completely aligned all four wheels to specs. We got a print-out showing the before and after caster and camber, and toe in and toe out readings on each wheel. Impressive! Everything was explained to us in language that we understood. We drove out feeling relieved that our trailer had been fixed, and we got the service we hoped for.

Now the icing on the cake. I have NEVER been to an auto repair facility that was this clean. The waiting room was immaculate. You could sit there in a wedding gown and not get any dirt on it! The bathrooms were also spit shined. Everything in the establishment where a customer would find themselves is spotlessly clean.
