Now, you probably think I come here once or twice a week and post up for a few hours, but that's not the case. I get my Chinese take out fix about once a month like everyone else, but the hospitality here is wonderful. My order is that obnoxious one that everyone hates to take "Cashew chicken, no cashews please!" but they are pleasant and thoughtful every time I come in. The one and only time a mistake happened, they corrected it quickly. I'm so glad I live nearby and If ever I move out of their delivery area, I will still come back to this business whenever possible.

OMG! This place is so cool. This has to be the most comfortable coffee shop I've ever been in. It feels like you're hanging out in someone's well-decorated living room. In fact, that really must have been what this place was originally. 

We only got some ice cream, but it was delicious! A must-stop when you're in the area.

I love this place.  I think they will be a great addition to the Rendon Inn.  I recently went there on my way to the airport, for chicken friend steak...  Kinda like a last meal on my way to the NW.  

Really really wonderful.  the Mashers, and beans?  good old skool southern yummy goodness.

Of course, I had to have some guacamole, and some chips, because I'm addicted to them, and it had been a while.

beer selection good, and I'm not really a beer drinker, but had a few, since we were on vacation.  It was the perfect meal, and right amount of everything to send me on my way.

I look forward to more meals at this place.  Thank you Craig and Kimmee...  again, you bring the goods!
Great hand crafted ice cream in hand made waffle cone about $5 I had chocolate friend had strawberry. It's around back of Apple bagels

We were here on a Sat.night in line deep with about ten in front or us as we got closer we saw it posted only FIVE flavors,and you don't serve yourself,customer service is really good....let me put how much I want in my bowl,let me mix and match my topping the way I want to,plus it was hot and all the tables were taken,we look at each other and all the saw was ass and elbows.

I found the breakfasts overpriced and haphazardly prepared the service less than average the place a bit disheveled. The outside is dominated by table hogs passing judgement with about as much worth as my two cents here.

Before you go here don't , also you should Google them and find out about this co. as a whole. They will overcharge you and offer you fake discount card. Apparently they charge you and then subtract that amount and call it a discount, then if you try to use again they then tell you it's a one time discount. Then they tell you they have to order and tell you they will call when comes in but guess what they don't. Plus there's more but don't want to rant to much, so unless you like to be screwed without even being kissed find somewhere else.

Farmer's Cabinet is elaborately decorated and I think it sets an unrealistic expectation.  Upon entry I was prepared to be taken back to a simpler time, but in that nostalgic "I wish things never changed" sort of way.  I found myself questioning these notions throughout the meal and I just think I was let down, despite a perfectly fine meal.

To me, the food is just woefully uninspired based upon the period it is trying to reference.  Now, I want to say this before getting too into it: I went for lunch at Restaurant Week, so it may not be a completely fair review in that regard.

My veal short ribs did not cut very well.  I love fatty meats, but the fat attached was not gelatinized at all and so it didn't want to cut cleanly.  This is not unforgivable, but let's take a step back; I'm at a place that looks like a saloon or general store from the mid-1800s gold rush. You want to believe that a place like this is going to be a leader when it comes to wild game, food preservation technique, and rustic fare.

This is probably me expecting too much.  The drinks were good, though, again, nothing transportive.  I've heard extensive things about their charcuterie, but my girlfriend does not enjoy cured meats very much, so I passed.  Her burger was also good, though unremarkable.

I really wished this place was something unique and special. The walls are begging for it.  But it's just a pretty decent place for food and drink.  In a city with several hundred places to check out, nothing about Farmer's Cabinet makes me want to travel back to this simpler time to be let down again.

Wonderful food, would not be able to say enough about it. I've eaten there several times and it's all top of the line. I live right here in the neighborhood and will continue to go there at the drop of a hat. Nice patio out back and nice entertainment.  Love living so close. . . Score.

UPDATE: 10/30/16 Returned today for another try. Called ahead at 10:30 and told we should be seated around 11:15 but actually seated closer to noon.  They should use the Disney approach. Better food and service this time. But still seemed chaotic for some employees. Our waiter, Rashad was excellent!!! Upped my rating by one star. Thanks to Ms. McCarthy at Corporate for the complimentary entrees and stellar follow up. The willingness and eagerness to improve and satisfy are obvious and exemplary.

Never a long wait time and they always get my somewhat complicated order correctly! I even like getting coffee and just sitting in there. The atmosphere is comfortable and not too loud, plus it smells amazing with the bakery and coffee scents. They put in a drive-thru too. I like that when I am in a hurry, I can order & pay online then just run by and pick it up. Convenient. Pleasant staff always.

The best corner store for the best prices. Have all the nuts and other little treats you could need in nice size bags. I don't think there's a better place to get nuts at such reasonable prices anywhere else in the city.

This place has the best customer service of any restaurant downtown. I've had nothing but a great experience every time I've gone. Plus, their food is amazing. I'm addicted to their bowls! I can usually get two or three meals out of one of them and it's very affordable. My coworkers and I have now added GRILLiT to our weekly rotation.

I liked the vibe of this restaurant. Love the music selection and the decor. I ordered the spicy chicken sandwich with the potato salad. Unfortunately although the chicken tasted delicious... I have to say that the sandwich fell apart super fast and got super soggy fast with all the toppings. My potato salad was also very watery... I am not sure if it was an off day for the cooks...but I wasn't very pleased with what I got. Perhaps just the chicken alone would have been good like if I ordered the chicken wings alone and not in a sandwich? I had asked the waitress after I ordered and she brought the food over if there was milk or dairy and she said they use buttermilk and there was dairy in the potato salad. So since it was my fault for not asking before I sucked it up and ate it (I would deal with my lactose intolerance afterwards). The waitress was not friendly about it and took my plate away saying they could give me something else other then the potato salad and would charge me an extra dollar. However she came back with the same potato salad. I wasn't very impressed with the service. I think I will try this place but just the chicken next time but this place didn't live up to the vibe and ratings I have been hearing. So it's a 2.5 rounded up to a 3 out of 5 this time for me. Maybe next time... maybe...

Sushi was amazing however the takeout is taking forever. Waited about 20 minutes after the time time they said I should come... Still waiting for my food.... 40 minutes later...  Get it together people. How long does it take to roll up some fish.

Really cool and surprisingly large restaurant in an unsuspecting location. My buddy and I started with 2 iced coffees which were great but ridiculously sweet as they come with sweetened condensed milk (good for the tastebuds, bad for the waistline).  We shared an appetizer of the pork meatballs and then each had a vermicelli bowl. I went with the chicken and a spring roll, he has the steak and spring roll bowl. Now looking back I feel like a big fatty...thats a lot of food. Next time I go back I'll try the pho, I just never think that's going to be enough food. Ambiance was nice, waiters attentive, maybe a little too attentive actually. There's a parking lot behind the restaurat as well. Check it out!
Delish and great service! You will not be disappointed! I went during their soft opening when it was EXTREMELY busy and the wait staff was so friendly and helpful! Truly a great dining experience,

T.G.F.Y - What???? How about "Thank God for Yelp." How do people order sushi without pictures? Pictures make it so much easier with ordering when you can just point. Plus, I love colors. If I could eat all the prettiest brightest sushi on the menu, that would be great!!!!

Had some great sushi today at Sushi Alive. It's been like 3 years since I've been here. It's not like I didn't like it last time. I just don't always have a sushi buddy, & now I have a few.

Shannon & I ordered two rolls from the Happy Hour menu: The Mexican and the Gator. Both were good. The Gator had a spicy kick for us, but was still good. We also picked the Hawaii 5-0 which I liked a lot because of the mango. Loved all three of them. Our waitress also helped us too. She was super sweet and efficient.

We also ordered drinks: a plum wine & a raspberry saketini. I liked mine better because it was sweeter.

Happy Hour is everyday from 5-7 pm Monday through Friday. They also have $1 & $2 nigiri & sashimi respectively. There's a wait because it's that good, but if you are flexible, and can sit at the bar, let them know. There's deals at 8pm too for drinks, and lunch specials too.

I really liked it here, and there are other appetizers, entrees, soups, salads, etc. I'm already wanting more.

Before I start, I would like to add that I created a yelp account specifically to write a review about Mt. Rose. I have never been so disappointed up here in my life. I have been snowboarding at Rose for at least 10 years. I have been a season pass holder for 3 of them. I was very excited (despite the lack of snow) to renew my season pass for this year. I tried to do so online, but couldn't because I had to prove my age to get the pass. The pass I was trying to get was for ages 18-24 for $449. One day I had planned on going I couldn't because I got really sick, so my boyfriend went. He tried buying me a pass but they wouldn't let him because I wasn't there, however, he was assured that the prices would not rise by the next time we came (today). When arriving today, I went to buy my pass. I am a full time college student working two jobs, and had saved up the $449 to pay for the pass. I asked for the pass, and was told the price went up $100 on the 1st. I explained my situation, and that it didn't say anywhere online that the prices would be rising, and the manager simply said "sorry, nothing I can do". How this resort can justify raising the prices when there has been zero snow is beyond me. I bought a day pass, which is also a rip off, and enjoyed the slushy mountains for a few hours. Needless to say, I don't think I will be returning. Mt. Rose, a stingier place than Disneyland.

Andrea rules all. she has the best eye for makeup, waxing, et al. and she has a wonderful personality. She is the only person who comes near my eyebrows and I get compliments on the waxing all the time. AND she always finds a way to squeeze me in when I call.
I had my wedding everything done here and have had my makeup done here for other weddings as well.
Paul is the greatest for formal hair.
I don't think they are reopening anytime soon.  Made my last trip for nothing over there this morning.  They had good bagels, too bad.

So we are in Franklin this evening and decided to grab some dinner.  Opened Yelp and looked to see if there was anything new worth trying.  We were not disappointed!  Great atmosphere, cool music, wonderful service, and the food was outstanding.  Some of the best pork tenderloin I have ever had and the scallops were as fresh as we get at the beach.  Make it a stop on your food tour of Franklin, you will be glad you did.

Nice having a good Chinese restaurant near our home. Had the hot and sour soup and it was good! The food was good and the portions large. Reminds me of restaurants back east where the family works at the restaurant and take pride in what they do. Will be a regular place to eat for me and my family.

I go here regularly for happy hour - no where in the area can touch the food menu!!! So many choices at amazing prices. Great place to meet family, friends, or really for any occasion. The atmosphere is always lively and I love the industrial feel. If someone in your group likes beer this is the place to go. I have never had anything negative to say about the food, drinks, or service. I will continue going here and I hope they keep their fantastic happy hour specials!

A transplant from NYC Chinatown so I had high hopes for Nom Wah. However I was not that impressed by the food here.

First of all, the shrimp dim sum here is very salty, which I presume is to balance the milder sauces. But I think the shrimp is too heavily salted... I like the quality of the shrimp used in the dim sum - succulent and fresh... But definitely too salty! The wrapper of the shrimp in rice wrapper (虾长) is the redeeming factor.

Highlights of my dim sum dishes include: tofu skin wrappers (鲜竹卷), snow pea shrimp dumplings (雪菜饺子), and eggplant. The tofu skin wrappers (鲜竹卷) are a classic go-to of my family, and these were done quite well. The skin had a lovely texture and the sauce was mild but flavorful. The snow pea dumplings had really fresh and generous snow pea veggies as well.

Dishes I was disappointed in: taro and pork dumpling... (I bit into a piece of bone in this one and the pork flavor was weird...)

Another dish I was disappointed in was the sticky rice in bamboo wrapper (糯米鸡). Usually this is my favorite dim sum dish, and I think Nom Wah's chef has his heart in the right place. The meat stuffings were quality and tasted fresh and the rice is delicious... But the rice was also UNDERCOOKED, and my friend found a piece of plastic in her meat... It's unfortunate because I really wanted to like this dish. I just think more attention needs to be paid in the process of making this.

Overall, a mixed batch of authentic dim sum flavors. I loved the quiet ambiance here and the teas. Did not appreciate needing to pay for the tea though...

Excellent BBQ  (pork and beef brisket) served no frills cafeteria style. Jumbo sandwich with a side was plenty filling. I really like the multiple choices of sauce that are kept warm at the condiment bar. It was too hard to choose so I created my own mixture of the three I liked best!

I can't imagine anyone giving this less than 5 stars.  We LOVE this place - except in the bar area it is extremely difficult to hear.

Service is nearly always excellent, and the food couldn't be better.  I actually had a tough fillet mignon once, and did mention that to the waiter.  Not only did they give me a new one, but they removed the steak from my bill.  I guess they like repeat customers!

Never disappointing - always delicious - speedy but not rushed - polite servers.

Now - if the servers only would STOP saying "How are WE doing"!

First time here   . Wow for the price , the portion of food is unbearably small.  I would suggest that for anyone consider going here , make sure that you look at the menu first before going.  For 9.5 dollars you get a size of dish that is worthy of 3 dollars at most. Be aware!

I went here for the first time today after many recommendations to go. I have to say, it was surprisingly fast. I had my food within 5-10 minutes of ordering. The pizza was hot. While I'm not sure of the exact size of the pizza, I'm guessing it was 10-14 inches. It definitely was enough that I had leftovers. My pizza had toppings and came to $7.95. Well worth it. 

They had to go boxes located conveniently next to the soda fountain. There was also parmesan, oregano, and pepper flakes available. 

The inside was clean looking with lots of natural light. The music was blaring but eh what you gonna do. I'd come back here again for sure. BONUS: they accept diamond dollars.

Awesome food, great ambiance and beautiful deck. Excellent service and even our dog got a bowl of water, met a couple furry friends and enjoyed it. We had pasta and a pizza and both entrees were tasty and perfectly prepared (love wood fire baked pizza). Deserts we had were tiramasu and a blackberry bread pudding which were delicious. Great date or family place and we're definitely going back.

Brought a Groupon to try something new and I picked a winner!  Started out with the Falafel which was very tasty.  I then had the Lamb Gyro which was delicious and my friend had the Chicken Shawarma which she said was good.  We also tried the Grape Leaves which were not our cup of tea.  The overall price was right and the staff was very friendly!  After leaving we walked around the corner to Fro Yo to end our evening with something sweet.

This was a really exceptional experience! My parents took me out to celebrate a new job and we were not disappointed.

First off, the restaurant was nice. What you expect from a seafood place I'd say. We ended up in private dining, which was pretty cool. It was Sunday which meant they had 50% off wine bottles. It may be worth going back just to try out some of the wines for much cheaper than you'd find them otherwise.

We ended up with a collection of food when all was said and done. The calamari and crab cake apps were excellent. I didn't care for the lobster bisque soup, but others seemed to enjoy it. The true star was the fish. We had several varieties, and all of them were outstanding. For my part, I had seared tuna, cooked rare with just a bit of salt and pepper to season and it was fantastic. The side of roasted potatoes and asparagus were ok, but certainly didn't take away from the meal.

All in all, good service and good food (with some excellent fish) made for a good experience. I did not see the final bill but judging from the menu prices, this is definitely a special occassion restarant. Would definitely make a return trip!

The massive unique selection of cactus and the helpful friendly staff make this place a gem of Tucson.  The people who work here are truly wonderful and the most knowledgeable we've ever come across at any plant nursery.

The ambience was great. The portion sizes were good. The server was fantastic. The food was a tad on the bland side (I had the pappardelle, the wife had the salmon carbonara) but not bad by any means. We'll try it again for sure. Highly recommend.
This place has delicious vegetarian options and a great cup of coffee in a very cool, historic building. Love the cafe and the neighborhood!

Really good pizza and I love the fact that they have vegan cheese. Customer service was fast and friendly. But I hate how much waste they have there. No washable cups all disposable Cups, straws, cutlery. ( even if you're eating in the restaurant ) Very wasteful -hard to support a restaurant like that.

I visited Nashville recently with the wife and  we decided to check out M. Restaurant & Bar for dinner before a Nashville Predators game.

We started off the meal with the Fried Green Tomatoes w/ pimento cheese and they were awesome.  Aside from the pimento cheese what made the dish stand out was that the tomatoes were cut very thick and the breading was perfectly balanced and not overwhelming.

I ordered the Three Little Pigs.  Once you throw pork cheeks, pork belly and pork tenderloin into one entree you grab my attention.  And this did not disappoint.  Both the pork cheeks and pork belly portions were generous, tender and extremely delicious.  The brussels sprout kimchi that came with the pork belly is not for the faint of heart.  It is pretty hot, and thankfully I don't mind spicy foods one bit.  The apple stir fry and candid apple gastrique that accompany the dish are also perfect compliments.

The wife ordered the shrimp and grits and they did not disappoint.  If I had one criticism it was that they could have gone a little lighter on the creole cream sauce.  But overall it was a solid shrimp and grits dish.  And of course I stole a few bites from her with the andouille sausage, because one cannot have too many different variations of pork at dinner. 

So we definitely enjoyed the food and would recommend this place to others.

Hotels.com thinks it is a 3.5 star.  Knights Inn would be an upgrade.  Check in-king size room we reserved was not ready, we accepted 2 doubles instead (no biggie and check in was long) Lobby was nice.  The rest was a house of horrors.  The carpet on the hall floor was old and worn. The doors were all beaten down and falling apart.  The previous poster must have taken a pic. of the best door.  They were really bad. The tub had old loose tile, dirty grout, a make shift patch job, and the curtain rod was rusted.  There was no hot water and tub was dirty. The beds did not have blankets.  The hotel uses sheets instead of blankets.  There was a hole on the cabinet.  The television, sink vanity, and bathroom floor tile were new.  I assume this was one of their "renovated" rooms.  Early in the evening I could hear a couple yelling obscenities at each other and it sounded violent.  The next morning on my way to breakfast, I walked by a man passed out on the floor in the hall(not the same room as the quarreling couple). The only redeeming quality of this hotel is the downtown shuttle.  The shuttle is great!
The brownie was delicious. The food was mediocre. Our waitress was super cool. Yeet. They don't have burritos, which is a really sad. Really really sad. Jk this place bomb
Some of the best fries I've ever had and the cheesesteak fries from last years cheesesteak festival was absolutely amazing.

We have come to Puckett's Boathouse so many times and would normally rate our experience and food a 4 out of 5 stars however this evening was a huge disappointment.  We were looking forward to a nice evening with prompt service like we are used to.  We ordered the dozen combination oysters and crab claws. (The crab claws our my favorite).  We waited awhile and the server came back to ask for our entree order. We ordered the coconut shrimp w/ sweet potato fries and my husband ordered the Prime Rib.   Time passed and we saw other tables that ordered apps after us get their food. Finally our oysters came out, but no crab claws.  Waiting for our crab claws our entrees came out.  We told the server we understand these things happen but we don't need/want the crab claws anymore since they were supposed to be our appetizer, not an entree.  She understood and told the kitchen to not send them out. She came back and told us they would take the claws off our check. (All is okay at this point. We travel and eat out frequently so we understand this happens sometimes) but what occurred over the next 15 min was a huge disappointed from our server, the kitchen and the manager on duty.  
The server came back to our table telling us that her manager insisted they still give us the crab claws. We told her that was a nice gesture but we really were almost done with dinner and it wasn't necessary, but the server said they insisted so we said okay.  Waiting, waiting, waiting.... We have finished our dinner... Saw tons of apps come out of the kitchen (our table was by the kitchen door) but not ours.   We have our server bring us the ticket and paid for our dinner and still... No crab claws... We asked our server for boxes (for our leftovers) our server brought us the boxes, we packed up our food.... Still no crab claws. Our server continues to apologize and goes back and forth from being in the kitchen, peering out the door to see if we were still there. You can hear her talking to the kitchen staff.....still no crab claws.   Finally with our dinner completed, paid for and boxed up. We stay there for a little more time and still.. No crab claws,and now annoyed, we left.  Here are some issues I have now that I left 
1. All through our meal the manager never came to our table.  I would have expected the MOD to at least come by the table once to apologize or at least ask how our meal was. 
2. Communication is key with a successful restaurant.  The server, while apologizing,  told us they took our crab claws to another table. In my mind, okay that happens, but wouldn't the kitchen communicate to expedite a new order for us? 
3. When we told our server the crab claws were not necessary and she insisted. If they insisted, maybe we should have actually received them? Maybe the manager should have made sure this was taken care of properly. 

Disappointed and not really sure we will be back.  Tons of other great options in the Franklin/Cool Springs area.

Great service and friendly staff. Clean and courteous. Owners should be commended for revitalizing a real eyesore on broad street in Lansdale. They've set a high standard. Hopefully they can maintain it.

We had a SUPERB lunch today! Shrimp and grits were so tasty...lots of flavor and shrimp! The seafood lasagna was amazing as well. Loved the Motown music today. Service was quick,friendly and we felt very welcome. The decor is fun..lots of NOLA items.
This is our favorite place for crawfish tails! We could only find them in Alabama when we went on vacation but these tails top the Alabama ones and save us a lot of travel expense;)
Treat yourself to this great place. Bet you'll go back;)

This is the best sushi you will find in Santa Barbara. They have the freshest selection of fish and do not use frozen/preserved fish. This is obvious from their menu and their selection of sushi. They are interested in quality and if a fish is not available from the harbor they will not have it in stock. The menu is a bit pricey but well worth it for the quality and the service. In reality the rolls are only two or three more dollars than if you went to any other sushi restaurant. I would recommend this restaurant to all my friends.  

Get the Umami roll.

I came here tonight by accident and decided to sit down and watch the sunset and have a few drinks. This place is an absolute gem and the best happy accident that I have stumbled upon as a beach bar since moving to the Tampa area. 

The view here is just stunning. There is ample outdoor seating and a bar area to enjoy the outdoors, the view of the ocean unobstructed and just a lovely atmosphere. I was able to walk up and just grab one of the last tables that gave me a up close ocean front view to enjoy the slow sunset this evening. 

The drink menu was just wonderful. This place has hands down bar none, one of the best bloody marys that I have ever had. Every drink we ordered off the menu was delicious and just as aesthetically pleasing. We also tried the black bird drink, the bali blossom drink and the cilantro ginger cooler. Some of the best and most unique cocktails we've tried in a long time at an establishment. 

To gnosh, we started with the fish dip (divine, also served with pita chips which was a huge plus), the jerk chicken with fingerling potatoes and the beef short rib sandwich.The food was just as enjoyable and delectable as the drinks.

The customer service was wonderful. We had the most consistent, attentive, professional and kind service that I've experienced in a long time. Their professionalism, kindness, quick service and overall demeanor was the thing that made this evening so memorable and enjoyable.

The atmosphere, ocean front view, cocktails, food and customer service was just all around perfection. I recommend anyone come here and spend the evening here. I will absolutely be coming back in the future again and again.
Out on a snowy day, it nice we can stop at Starbucks for a chi tea latte and at Carlo's Bakery for one of their awesome peanut butter cup cakes. Happy day

This is my new favorite Indian restaurant in Nashville! The service was amazing and the food was to die for. I drink (water) like a fish (seriously, it's weird), so I told our server whose name was Nitin, to leave the water pitcher since I have most restaurants do that. He responded, "No, I'll take care of you, don't worry!" And he kept his word and was so nice the whole entire time! He was so nice and funny and made the dining experience wonderful. Definitely recommend if you're looking for INCREDIBLE Indian food. They will take care of you and serve fantastic, fresh food.

We went to this place for a bday event, it was the 6 of us. it is very small loud place, we had to yell to each other otherwise you cannot hear each other when it is full house. 

We had the same experience like others, we were being served "distilled water", which we did not want, and he tried to refill the glasses with the second bottle, we told him that we actually wanted to have tap water, not the sparking water. he said sorry and put away the half of the second bottle. He never refill the tap ice water again, we were all so thirsty after the meals. we were charged for $10, I believe it is $5/bottle. but we did not get to finish our second bottle! if you still want to go after these reviews, you need to tell them that you want tap water. 

We all felt very pressured and did not enjoy it as much. We loved the meals that we ordered, some of the portions are way too small. 

I will never return to this place ever again. i love their food, but it is not worth it. This place will never last with the way they scam their customers.

First time here, and happy I stopped in. The ambiance is upbeat and happy, and the staff are very friendly and inviting. The building itself is quite unique as I'm told it was once an old cigar factory and of course that adds to the charm. I decided to continue my quest as a native Californian to try as many Cuban Sandwiches as are geographically possible while staying in the Tampa Bay Area.  Habana Cafe does not disappoint, in fact the black beans and rice that come the be 1/2 sandwich combo was fantastic. As for the Cuban, it easily ranks in the top I have had.  Looking forward to coming back and trying more things on the menu!
Great place with a great staff. I could eat anywhere but these guys and gals are too notch and the apps and desserts are more like high end restaurants than a franchise.

The BF and I came here last night using a gift card from Rue La La.  I didn't do too much research ahead of time except that I knew that Paloma is BYO and that you can bring your own tequila for Margaritas.  I expected it to be kind of fun, hip, younger, etc.., but instead I felt like I was eating dinner at an older relative's house.  On the whole, the food is very good, but there was nothing that truly made me want to return for a second visit.

First, I'll agree with the other reviewer here who mentioned that the decor needs a serious upgrade: it's dated and stodgy.  The service was also a bit slow in the beginning (at least to take our order), but after that, the food came out at the perfect pace: not too fast, and not too slow either.  To start, we split the crab ceviche and the mushroom flan.  The former was our favorite of the two: you actually get a decent amount of jumbo lump crab meat on top of thick tomato and avocado slices.  The mushroom flan was interesting, but wasn't really something we would want to eat again.

For dinner, I ordered the filet mignon while he ordered the duck.  I thought my filet was actually pretty good and cooked really well, especially with the red wine reduction and mushrooms.  Plus, the sides were pretty tasty (very buttery mashed potatoes, crispy potato slices, and sauteed spinach).  The duck, on the other hand, while aided by the addition of smoky bacon, didn't really stand up as well.  The BF lamented how the duck could have been more tender.

Finally, the desserts were terrific.  I had the kaluha cheesecake which was served with a mexican dark chocolate crust (excellent, especially since the crust contained hints of cinnamon that elevated the cake to a whole new level).  As for the trio of sorbets and gelatos, I wasn't as impressed.  Much to the BF's disappointment, I couldn't get into the concept of a spicy sorbet (the strawberry-habanero sorbet, to be exact), and found the heat to be too overpowering for dessert.

So while the food was actually really good, my main problems are with the concept, decor, and pricing.  It's a little too expensive for food that's just good and nothing that is going to want me coming back for more.  Aside from the cheesecake (which is apparently made in house), you could easily get any of the other dishes at any other restaurant in Philly, and probably at the same if not better quality.  Also, I don't understand why the restaurant advertises itself as "haute mexican".  It's really more of a European fusion concept, and aside from some nods to Mexican/Latin American cuisine (ceviche, horchata ice cream, blue corn gelato), there is little evidence that you're actually at a Mexican restaurant.  And finally, if not for the gift card, this definitely would have been much more of a splurge than a simple dinner out.  Overall, good food, but the atmosphere, menu, and concept need to be improved to match the quality of the cuisine.

Don't waste your time! We tried calling twice this morning and were on hold for 10 minutes each time before they hung up on us. Went to this location and the parking lot was full. Only two bankers working and 35 people waiting. I'm talking about the line was wrapped around and around inside and then people were having to wait outside in the 10 degree temperature. No sign in sheet and it was chaos. We left. And may just leave Wells Fargo in general. If you plan on using the drive through services be prepared to wait behind 5 people too (if you can even get in the parking lot).

Staff and management was not aware of food content for allergies and food sensitivities. When questioned on dairy and gluten content they were indignant when questioned and not concerned about the effect on me the customer.

We had a reservation at 5:30 and called them to save the seats when we were stuck in the middle of high way because of the extreme weather composed of pouring rain and thunderstorm. They said sure no problem they could definitely reserve the seats while when we arrived they told us the seats were taken and we need to wait in line. What's the point to reserve the seats then? 50min's driving in the thunderstorm paid off as a starving night-- anyone has other recommendation around this neighborhood? Considering alternative options now since the waiting queue they put us in looks like infinite

My family and I were not impressed with the food.  With only 3 other tables of guests I figured the quality of the food was going to be lacking as an empty restaurant is a sure sign of a restaurant in decline and I was correct.  I got the sausage and chicken in a red bell pepper sauce.  It was very bland and the chicken was gross, leather like in texture.  I expected to get food poisoning but thankfully I didn't.  The rest of our dishes were less than mediocre.  There are a number of quality Italian restaurants in Indianapolis, this is not one of them.

They start out quoting .33 per image, but by the time you pay outrageous shipping both ways, it's more like $1 a piece. Customer service is singularly unhelpful. Beware! It's a "bait and switch" business practice....Won't be using them again. Wish I had checked the reviews first.
The actual location could use a little sprucing up, but the pretzels are delicious and always popular when taken to get-togethers.

$4/lb crawfish boil
+$1.29 corn (2 corn)
+$1.29 potato (6 pieces)
The corn and potato are legitimately just boiled. There's no flavor to them, so toss it in that bag well, although the crawfish really wasn't juicy the way I'm used to the cajun boils being done in California. But for the price (market price of crawfish in CA at the time was 14.99 according to  my friend that works at Boiling Crab), I'm satisfied. Plenty of guests were coming in and ordering 5lbs of crawfish at a time. 

$4.95 small gumbo
My bro said this place's gumbo was to DIE for, so we worked it into our driving route. It was definitely buttery and savoury, but I don't think I've had enough gumbo to say. 

Service
=====
Five stars for service!!! The guy was just so laid-back, calm, and down-to-earth, I was like he would be a great personality for a country music star, haha.

We returned for our second visit here.  This place is still amazing.  The food is absolutely delicious.  My wife ordered the fish and chips again.  The fish was lightly breaded and her piece was huge.  I couldn't resist again ordering the fisherman's feast.  The fish was sweet and delicious, the scallops sweet and tender and the shrimp were large and tasty. The menu prices are reasonable for the food you receive.  This is a must stop if you like seafood and you're in the area.

All time fave spot! So many good things going on. I love the sushirrito, also the jack fruit sandwich. Can't leave without the vegan frozen yogurt! They have Mother Kombucha on tap too. This place is so delicious and refreshing, really one of my top lunch spots in st. Pete.

I don't think I have ever given only two stars to a restaurant on Yelp. Unfortunately I made a mistake in not checking the dates of people's posts that this place was so awesome. Won't do that again. Pretty much all the reviews are 1 and 2 years old and not only are items that people Rave about no longer on the menu but what is still on the menu is questionable. I was greeted walking in with the sight of the waitress eating. Even after she saw me she took another bite before addressing me. During my meal, which took forever even though I was the only one there, I witnessed the chef eating behind the counter right where he was making the food. I got the salmon omelette with toasted bagel and cream cheese. I asked for my home fries well done with onions as I always do. The bagel could not have been considered toasted, the cream cheese schmear was on The Omelette not the bagel, there was a minimal amount of salmon in the omelette and the potatoes were far from well done and had about four small pieces of onions. The waitress was very sweet but checked on me once during the meal and never again. I had to holler out for her and still it was the chef that heard me and told her to come over to my table. Also, placr could use a good cleaning and watch put fpr the extension cords everywhere. Sorely disappointed and will not be back.

We frequent Santa Barbara often from Orange County and always try to grab a meal somewhere new. I was so grateful to have found this place for lunch on our last day in Santa Barbara last weekend. We wandered in after reading the menu and had such an amazing lunch- met by even better service. Our server was Tim, and he was WONDERFUL! So polite and helpful! It's easy to forget to write a kind review when someone is amazing so I had to grab a business card to remember to post how lovely he was and be sure to come back in the future. 
By the way the food was excellent as well! (Amazing lunch special! Farm-fresh foods and great wine list!) 
Will definitely try and be back soon! Thanks for the great service!

Great place to eat in the ballpark.  I have had the pit beef and turkey both slathered with the tangy house BBQ sauce.  If you are looking to skip the cheesesteak lines and try something new this is a good alternative.

THIS IS NOT AN AUTHENTIC DELI.  GO ELSEWHERE
This is the first time in my life where I threw out the leftovers that I had brought home; I hate to waste food and will eat most anything.  However, this food was so unappealing that I threw it out.  

1) I tried the matzoh ball soup and it was flavourless; there was no taste of chicken in the broth nor in the matzoh ball (which means it was prepared in plain boiling water).  
2) The Knish was not authentic; the pastry was wrong and the filling was potato which was too creamy and didn't really taste like potato.  
3) The Reuben was disgusting.  The sauerkraut wasn't drained, resulting in a soggy sandwich.  What passed for pastrami was bland and if it was from a brisket, it was sliced on the wrong angle and paper thin.  There was lots of what they called pastrami, but that doesn't compensate for the poor quality.  
3) The fries were cold and smelt as if the oil needed changing in the fryer.  The server brought out a fresh "hot" portion, which I could tell from the consistency had been re-heated in the microwave (to give me "hot" fries".  Like the first portion, the fries smelt of rancid fryer oil. 

Again, this is the first time in my 57 years that I have ever thrown out leftover food from a restaurant.  However, this food was so terrible, I could not even consider eating the leftovers.

I contacted Fast Signs for a Van Wrap price they welcomed me and a designer contacted me. Then I waited for one month never heard from them again. So to me  that is not good customer service. So save your time they do not care about small business.

As a very loyal patron of the uptown Slice for years I cannot begin to tell you how bad of an experience I had today ordering from the St Charles location now that the uptown location is closed.  Yes the gluten free pizza is still very good but to put up with the extremely long wait times (yes I ordered on line) and to be ignored while sitting at the bar for long periods of time and then being dis'ed by the manager when I requested and talked to him.  My advise for long time uptown fans is to stay uptown and not bother with the bad attitudes of the people you will encounter at the downtown location.  Good luck to the owner.

Nick

It would really be nice if the service was better. ..

Warning, hold your bladder if you are a male.  And is there some need for a cigarette advertising sign on the front door?  Happy meal and a carton for the kiddies??? (Yes, it is attached to a gas station, but come on!)

My family came here to celebrate my daughters bday. It was nice some of us got the all you can eat sushi and some ordered off the menu. The sushi is pretty solid and comes out fast. I love that you can get fried rice as a side, salads m, edamame ice cream etc w your sushi meal. 

Love the lazy Susan on the tables. Also the decor is very cool. 

Service was top notch. The guy was on top of things for our party of 15. The all you can eat sushi is $22.95 pp but you can eat till you are full.

My trainer in LA helped find this gym for me when I am in town for work.  He wanted a gym that was similar to his style of training.  Double Edge was just that.  I dropped in for 2 classes on my most recent work trip and I enjoyed both.  They were the right kind of tough, Kris was a great coach for Ladies Night too.  I will be back when in town.

The hotel is very reasonably priced. The rooms are comfortable and clean and quiet.. The staff is friendly, especially Ryan at the front desk. Even when it was very busy, he quickly handled everyone's needs in a timely manner and was polite, friendly and accommodating to everyone. I really appreciate when staff in any establishment are personable with their guests. And he seemed to go the extra mile to be professionally and handsomely dressed, which really stood out. He appears to have a good work ethic and cares about presenting well for the company. A hotel is a hotel is a hotel, but it's the people that make the experience a good one. I can honestly say he made my experience enjoyable.

Go to the deli and get one of there fresh made sandwiches! Boars Head meat and cheese all the fixings! $7-8 feeds two people and you can even get s chilled bottle of wine closer to the butcher part of the store! If you are hungry, sick of paying for food in a restaurant, give it a try! Grab a sandwich and sit on the beach. Cheers

Nice little place.  Casual with a nice basic ambiance.  The service was good not great, the food was tasty and fresh, and the wines by the glass were fine.  We had the lobster tail app, the trout, the cioppino, and apple pie with ice cream for dessert.  All of the items were very good,  the lobster tail was small and a little over priced but that's kind of what you expect.  The ice cream and pie were a nice surprise.  Would go back but there are so many great places in Santa Barbara that we may try some of those other places next time.

I used to adore Red Robins but I have recently found this location sadly lacking. My in laws live 2 minutes away from this particular location. The first time we ever came the food was wonderful but the place was crowded as all heck. The 2nd time it was crowded and Service was horrible.  The 3rd time and the 4th (today)  was slow, half empty, and horribly run. These 2 times they had several tables empty but dirty. Today 10 places dirty, one of which could have sat all of us. 2 tables could have been cleaned and placed right next to each other for us. Last time I don't remember how many were dirty but there were several. And we had a party of 7. We were told a wait of 25 minutes for a table and waited while staff chatted with each other. The hostess repeatedly flipped her hair and did nothing else. No one was busing any of the tables for 10 minutes. Then when I made a comment the hostess tried to clean a table or two while we waited. The side door was a hit for everyone working there but the tables were not. 

It took them 15 minutes to get us seated and 10 minutes to attempt to clean it when on a slow day/time. That is unacceptableable. From a customer service stand point this is horrid for business.

I have been visiting Pickles Plus regularly since we moved to Florida over 20 years ago. I hear a lot of people say, "oh, it's like a Lucky Dill." No, Lucky Dill is like a Pickles Plus that's not doing it right. If you're a fan of Lucky Dill I would urge you to go to Pickles Plus and se what a real NY style deli can provide. 

I've had so many things over the years, some of the greats are the tuna melt on rye or just tuna salad, matzo ball soup, egg salad sandwich, fries, Italian hoagie, hot pastrami on rye, oh and the pickles!!! On my most recent visit I tried a special called the turkey frisco melt that was also amazing. 

The tuna sandwich holds a special place in my heart as it was my Gram's favorite sandwich and we would share it almost weekly but it's also amazing. The rye bread is so good and the tuna salad is just the way I like it, make it a melt and it's even better!!! 

The matzo ball soup is the best I've had in Pinellas county. There's not much to it, it's simply delicious. 

The egg salad sandwich on white has been my new obsession. Again, their bread is just out of this world - fresh baked goodness. The reason I love the egg salad is it's as good as mom made it. No weird additions like relish or mustard. Simply eggs, mayo, salt and pepper like it should be. 

The turkey frisco melt was thin sliced Boars Head turkey breast, Swiss cheese, crispy bacon, and honey mustard on grilled rye. It was warm and melty yet crispy all at once. I'm glad I tried this new item!!

I love that Pickles stays true to their name, their pickles are amazing. If I could have one type of pickle for the rest of my life it would be a Pickles Plus pickle! Give Pickles a shot, you won't be disappointed.

This is the best hotel i have ever stayed at. First of all, 20 million dollar renovations were just put in place this year. The place is brand new inside. Also; the price is lower than the surrounding hotels such as hyatt or sandpearl. We have coast view on the 8th floor. If you do take coast view make sure its room 855 or above or 815 and below (if youre on the 8th floor). The rooms in between that are somewhere in a corner with like half a view. The only thing i would improve is that i would put a vent in the bathroom because we had 4 people in our room and whenever someone used the bathroom the whole room knew it. Another thing is that there was a weird smell in the bathroom kinda like a sewer smell. I didnt feel like mentioning it because it wasnt a big deal but overall the room was very updated. What a great, renovated, affordable, and right on the beach hotel.

Best all around BBQ I've ever had. Chicken is phenomenal, ribs are perfect with a smoke red/pink rim around them, just how ribs they should be. Mac&Cheese is a must. Apple crisp cole saw is on point. Savory backed beans are what I've always dreamed about. Craft beer is well balanced. Beef brisket is "meh", but the beef brisket sandwiches are very good!!

EAT HERE
On line check in was nice. Went into an exam room in less than 15 minutes.  Great care, never left alone more than a couple minutes at a time. All the test ran efficiently.

Around 1 pm on a Saturday, Mom and I were looking to grab lunch and quick. She suggested this place as we both have not been here. 

Maybe 5 tables sat. 3 servers. Not busy. Huge menu selection. Our server came over, wasn't very engaging. Took our order. The steak fries came out first..but the other server had them and delivered to the table in front of us. I saw. That chick said she didn't order them so the server took them back. They waited a minute and then my server took them over to me. I was too hungry to care at this point.

Then the main meal comes out. Mom got a turkey cobb salad with bleu cheese. I ordered the Cuban Pork panini. Server came over with a salad and a wrap. Really?? Twice now you've delivered wrong food/ wrong table. The servers were looking bored and still nothing came out smoothly.

And to be honest, I should have taken whatever that wrap was because the Cuban Pork was gross. Grayish looking pork that you couldn't bite through!! My mom looked at me and asked how it was and I just shook my head No. I was happy I got a side of fries because even the chips that came with the sando were stale.

 Would I come back, nope.

An astoundingly good, creative, artistic place for any city.  Standard as well as vegan options.  The pricing is quite reasonable too.

Absolutely delicious cuisine which seems inspired by Moroccan, Israeli, etc.  I especially recommend the kefta meatballs (vegan) and the stuffed acorn squash.

A very clean decor reminiscent of Europe or Asia. With lots of pillows in the booths.

Following the strong Yelp recommendations, I ordered the Bobbie. I liked the bread, turkey, and cranberry sauce, but found the stuffing the be too mushy in consistency. I did get a bite of the Cole Turkey, which I liked a bit more.

What a wonderful surprise!! Ate here many years ago and it was dark and just blah.  Had heard it had changed...a LOT so when out-of-town friends wanted to meet, I suggested Darfon's.  It was FABULOUS!  We had a reservation and our table was ready. Our waitperson, Jill, was attentive but didn't hover. The food was OUTSTANDING!  We had the homemade cheese sticks and the homemade hummus plate for appetizers.  The cheese sticks were big and fried perfectly.  Jill had recommended the hummus and she was RIGHT! The hummus was amazing and the plate included pita points, marinated red peppers, mini feta cheese balls, sliced cucumber, and olives.  The men ordered Steak Oscar and it was cooked perfectly to each of their preferences. One ordered the Baby Back Ribs and loved them--a sweet but tangy sauce.  I had the BBQ Salmon and it melted in my mouth! One thing I noticed was that the clientele was older...since I am too, it was really "comfortable."  If there is one thing that was a turn-off for me, it was that it was loud...it was hard to carry on a conversation with our friends.  But if you want great service and fantastic food, go there!
Great little lunch getaway, large portions, great Sausage and a super attentive bartender.

Blech. I am never going anywhere my co-workers go for lunch again. I haven't been here in at least 15 years and there is a reason for that. It's not good. Things have not changed. Salsa in squeeze ketchup bottles, American-Mexican food, and the National Anthem at full blast on the hour.  First off, let me say the service was good. Our server was fast, no nonsense, and accurate while this place was packed. I spent $12 (included tip) and this is the run down. A water and the Tres Amigos lunch special which included a hard shell taco, an enchilada, and soft taco. The hard taco: ground beef. lettuce, tomato, shredded cheese. The enchilada and soft shell taco were identical. One was a flour tortilla and the other a corn tortilla. One was covered in queso while the other in chili sauce. Both rolled up ground beef. On the side was about a 1/2 cup of sour cream. I paid $12 for a serving of rolled up ground beef swimming in a variety of sauces. I felt yucky, cheap, and dirty when we left. When people suggest eating here I will decline.
Great find!!  Love this place! Great wine list! Also enjoyed Range the following day for lunch!
My favorite Mediterranean restaurant! Food is always fresh, hot & nicely seasoned! My fav is the beef shawarma! Love the hummus, too. Creamy & just right!

At a three-star hotel in old city, there are certain standards that are expected by default. All of those but one were provided: internet.  Oh, they have free wireless.  But it is so dumbfoundingly slow that it precludes useage.  Do not stay here if you plan on using a laptop, even for a bit.  I'm writing this very review from my phone because the yelp page on my lappy hasn't loaded after -- in all seriousness -- twenty minutes.  If not for this glaring flaw, the wyndham would be a perfectly lovely place to stay.  But until their wireless speed improves, I won't be coming back.

Ordered off the special 4 course menu. Waitress didn't understand the system so we lost out on part of the menu. Had to call manager and he took 20% off. Steak was TOUGH! Sorry not going back. ....why run a steak house with bad meat?

What a great experience!  Danny the owner and exec chef will make this a memorable night.   Some of the food was mediocre, but there were some amazing highlights as well.  The crab cake was amazing.  The pineapple- haberno sauce was amazing.   You can't come here without getting the Caesar salad is a must.  The highlight of the evening was getting the cafe diablo after dinner.  I am so happy we found this gem!

I called John originally to help fix a screen on my older macbook pro.  He went through the different options with me including buying a new computer as this one was old and may not be worth the repair investment.   I ended up going with his advice and buying a new computer.  I really appreciated his knowledge and honesty, even when it meant not providing himself with business! I then called him back to see how I could get the data from my old computer on to my new one.   He explained how I could do that myself and even offered to lend me the firewire cable if I didn't have one!    I really appreciated all the time he took to talk to me about different options on both occasions, and I will definitely be calling him back if I need anymore computer help.   He is very helpful and honest.  I highly recommend him!

Got up and left. Took 15 minutes for server to show up and he brought an attitude... after the host had already mocked us. Guess a group of women worries the staff at restaurants in an area where bach parties are the norm. We were happy to take or business across the street to The Pub where the service and food was fantastic.

The best time we had on bourbon st.
Great music and personality.
Steam boat Willie made our night.
i ordered pasta alfredo with shrimp but the portions are way too small and not filling:/ left the restaurant pretty hungry. the server was very nice

Lovely breakfast spot!

A constant line the whole time, it is clear this place is a local favorite. The menu offers a wide variety of options, ranging from salads, to pastries, to more traditional pancake/egg dishes. The orange juice was the freshest it could possibly be!

I thought the portions were small, and the quality was not quite 5 star, but is certainly worth checking out, maybe on a weekday when the lines are shorter. Very friendly staff, and quick service.
Very convenient airport. Easy to get around and not too big where it takes forever to get out.

I usually love red robin. Tonight was horrible. I want in and was told 15 minutes wait time it ended up being 25 minutes. Then was in a corner table and waitress took my order gave me a drink and then saw her 2 times. Food came out and I didn't even have silverware.  Had to beg her to pay them. The service was horrible.
Great food with decent prices. (Except drinks are kinda expensive). Have been to continental at least a dozen times and have never been disappointed. Gotta try the swinging baskets at least once!

I have been using University Physicians for the last 18 years. And until the last 6 months I have been very happy with them. But that was when I was going to one of their offices on the North side of Tucson. When I changed insurances I had to change practices and ended up at the Alvernon location. 

If you are just going in for acute treatment or wellness checkup's then this is probably a good place to go. However, if you are going for treatment of a chronic illness then you may want to consider your alternatives. Because this is a "learning facility" you have staff rotating in and out on a constant basis and you really never see the same person twice. 

A recent experience I had with their office left me completely baffled and stuck with a very large Urgent Care bill. I called in for a sick appointment. I was told that nothing was available on the regular schedule but that a triage nurse would call me back. No problem there. They did call back and after reviewing my symptoms they affirmed that they did not have any appointments available. I stated that I needed to be seen that day. It was recommended that I go to urgent care (which my insurance requires that I get a referral from my doctor prior to going). I expressed that I would be doing that. 

A month and 10 days later, I got a bill for several hundred dollars because my insurance showed that there was never a referral for urgent care. I called my doctor's office and explained the situation. I was told that they have no way to fix errors like this but that they would be glad to put in a current referral for me to go to urgent care. WHAT??!! I have no use for a current referral. I want the mistake taken care of. I didn't make it. Why am I the one who has to run around and fix it? And why, at a "learning facility" would you not have a computer system that allows you to fix mistakes?? 

I went in to talk to them face to face and it was reiterated that they have no way to fix a mistake like that, even though their call log shows that I was supposed to be referred to Urgent Care. The lady at the office was kind enough to print out the call log for me and attach information for how to reach that nurse directly. Hopefully she won't rotate out before my insurance company reviews the appeal I sent in. 

I understand that people make mistakes. It is the complete lack of trying to fix the mistake that I find appalling. Not once did anyone offer to write a letter on my behalf or to call my insurance company and explain their error. Even my bank would do that if they made an error that effected my account. And given the service standards of most banks, that is saying something.

Found the BEST Italian restaurant. I loved the crab stuffed mushrooms and the Pollo Valdostana (rolled chicken breast stuffed with arugula, sun dried tomato and fontina cheese in mushroom sauce) was amazing. The staff worked together to cover all the tables ANC I never had to think about having my drink re-filled. Fantastic food, great service and a nice ambiance means I'll be back the next time I'm in town.

Where do I begin with Babylon Cafe?

From the homemade hummus with fresh bread to the grilled salmon with vegetables, this was most likely the best meal I had in New Orleans. DEFINITELY the best hummus I've ever had. Service was A+ and the waitress was really helpful with my indecisive self trying to decide what to eat. Lots of options here (which is always a plus). The place is walking distance from Tulane.

I miss NOLA a lot, partially because I miss the food at this awesome Mediterranean restaurant!

Los Nopales may not be the best Mexican restaurant I've been to but they are the best for what they do!  Strongly recommend the "crisps."   Uniquely their own!  They have all the expected offerings also.   Locally owned and ran which is important to me to support local small business owners.  Their chips and salsa, free with every meal are yummy.   Servings are large so come hungry or be prepared to take some home.  Service is excellent and the place is always clean and friendly.  Prices are fair to inexpensive.  They offer beer/wine.  Looking for a casual dining experience - Los Nopales is an excellent choice!

Second time here, first time was great, second time was phenomenal!
Our waiter, Mike, a 15 + year veteran absolutely made our night. His suggestions to our were questions were spot on. The table side Caesar and Steak Diane were expertly prepared and tasted amazing. The cooking tips were very cool. Mike is a true professional gem. The food, wine and service were some of the best we have ever experienced. I look forward to another excetional meal here and will be sure Mike is here to wow us.us. Aged and regular rib eye steaks are Both the Bonn too !
Cheers !
The best sushi and Thai food, awesome staff and Diana rocks! We eat here several times a month. So lucky to have such great quality food so close to our home.

Five stars are elusive for the picky sort like myself, but the flavors here have lingered in my thoughts long after my visit. The aesthetically pleasing stinky buns are a fine vehicle from plate to mouth for diverse and tasty fillings. The shrimp ones conjure memories of The Point's (former location) bang bang shrimp recipe, now perfected with a further reaching complexity of delightful flavors that aren't constantly fighting for supremacy on the palate. The pork belly filling has such a rich, notable taste. I tried the coconut curry chicken wings whose name doesn't even begin to speak for itself and must be had again, but the Truffle Tots win my heart for being one of my favorite dishes in Tampa when I can afford something on the fried side. I adored Erica our server, and she really made my night so much so that we invited her to sit with us, as we had a spirited discussion regarding the direction of food concepts in Tampa (what a bunch of nerds, I know) for the rest of our meal. I've wrestled internally with the service vs. taste issue in Tampa, and it's really simple with this place: You can slap me in the face and insult my mother for more of those tots, but I'm so glad you won't have to. See you really soon Erica and Singh!
Absolutely loooooove this place!! We go for breakfast, lunch or dinner, even just dessert!!! Everything on their menu is delish!!!

My wife and I were spending my birthday in New Orleans and looking for a unique breakfast experience. We searched YELP reviews and agreed "Toast" appeared to be what we were looking for. Since parking in and around our French Quarter hotel is difficult, we decided to use Uber for a ride to the other side of NOLA, and arrived at what our driver stated was a hole-in-the-wall - but he said don't worry, some of our best restaurants are holes in the wall.

As we entered the very small diner, we had a choice of two empty tables or seats at the bar- we opted for the latter. Sitting at the bar gave us an opportunity to talk to the kids running the place, and as a result of that conversation my wife ordered both a sweet and savory crepe, while I went for the well reviewed french toast and side of bacon.

My wife seemed to truly enjoy her crepes - her only negative comment was how large they were and the fact she regretted she could not come close to finishing them. My french toast was prepared with delicious bread coated with egg, cinnamon, and powdered sugar - with their maple syrup and my side of bacon I had a taste in my mouth I can't describe other than heavenly. And the aforementioned bacon, oh that bacon. This had to be some of the best thick tasty bacon I have ever had. If you come here for no other reason, try a side of bacon!

We were there on Taco Tuesday, and I was hoping I would have room for at least 1 bacon. egg, and cheese breakfast taco, but it was not to be - I couldn't even finish the food I ordered. 

I don't want mislead anyone - the food portions are not overly huge - my wife and I are older and can't eat as much as we used to - if we could, we would have ordered that dang taco!

Coupons:

http://couponclipper.com/loc/KINGBUFFETPLYMOUTHMEETING

Had lunch here today! Delicious! My husband had the bayona salad as his starter, I had grilled shrimp with a black bean cake. Husbands entree....the to die for. .shrimp and grits! Not feeling hungry,  I had a salad with goat cheese and strawberries! Highly recommend Bayona!

Nice Local Lower Bucks Co spot. Good craft beers bottled and tap. Nice music after 9pm. Sweet bartender Scott keeping it all together Clean inviting atmosphere. This place is relatively new and they need to get a bigger following. No kitchen yet but they say that's coming. In the mean time you can order out from local pizza places and such. So nice to have something like this that is nonsmoking and close to home. Move over Hulmeville, there's a new Dog and Bull in town!!!l  Give it it a try

I am very disappointed with this Walgreens. 1 month ago I picked up my rx's. Didn't realize they had given me someone else's medication. Of which is similar to one I take in size and color. So for a few days assuming it was my meds took them till the one morning I looked at the bottle. Made this aware to the pharmacy manager and store manager. For my inconvienence and thankfully no health issues developed the store manager said they would compensate me with a gift card. And it would be available with my next r.x pick up. Well went to pick up my meds for this month.... no mention of the gift card... just like nothing happened....very disappointed with customer service. Didn't make a big issue to Yelp or corporate. But now.....a bit peeved for the inconsiderate brushoff....

Okay! This place isn't new but it IS my new obsession!

Tacos with amazing and interesting ingredients! I always go with the "Triple Play" 3 tacos of your choice for $9!!!

My favorites are: 
The Ban Mai! Tender Pork, pickled veggies and a hoisin sauce. 

The Gangam Style! Short Rib, pickled veggies and a spicy creamy sauce. 

Carne Asada! Marinated Beef, cabbage, queso and guacamole. 

Carnitas! Shredded pork, cabbage slaw, queso and guacamole. 

Also for fish lovers there is a Poke taco with a wasabi sauce, fish tacos, shrimp tacos and a rice ball, that looks like a baseball with spicy tuna inside!

The baseball theme is because they are located by the batting cages on Milpas. 

This place is legit! So tasty and so reasonably priced! I rate it a "Home Run"!!!

We were told about the Junction while at breakfast. We stopped by today. We are visiting New Orleans from California for Jazz Fest. The staff was so very friendly to start with. The food was delicious. I had a pickled Cobb salad. It had a beautiful pink pickled egg on the side of the plate and the vinaigrette dressing was so good on it. My husband built a burger with the add-ons he wanted that he could not finish. And a selection of beers that is so inviting.  Try it when you visit NOLA

The sushi surprised the hell outta me. I did not expect this place to have sushi, much less be very good sushi. We had the Spider Roll, and a vegetable roll, both very good. Our waitress Brooke was great and very attentive. Also good draft beer selections, which seems hard to find a lot of places in downtown Nashville. The rooftop bar  is also great for the night life, good music, good vibes and a beautiful view.

Looking for a spot near Forest Park following a round of golf on Saturday, Llywelyns fit nicely.

As it was amazing outside, our group was looking for a patio to enjoy the weather, watch some college football and have a bite to eat.

The beer garden out back was really nice.  We sat down right away and were greated quickly by our server.  Once we had our drinks we all dived into the menu.  The group shared a couple of orders of the dragon wings and the Welsh potato chips.  The wings had a nice kick to them and the chips were brought out hot.  Both were really tasty and a nice way to begin the evening.

For dinner I went with the Llywelyns chicken sandwich.  I enjoyed the onions and the sauce but the chicken was pretty standard.  However, the combination of the three made for a pretty good sandwich.

All in all, it was a good time on a great patio.  I would go back again if I was in the CWE looking for an easy bite to eat.

Fun place. We went for Mother's Day and everyone enjoyed themselves. My kids in particular enjoyed the baby octopus. (Try it and watch it cook. You'll understand) There was a good selection of meats and the staff did a good job of explaining the process and making recommendations. What I really like about this style of dining is that you are forced to go slow and savor what is in front of you. There is no pressure to rush, and I left feeling full but not stuffed. I am very impressed with all of the IJJI restaurants and they have effectively applied their business model to the world of Korean BBQ. It's definitely worth a try--even for those who might be afraid of asian cuisine. Make sure you try the octopus!

Pinky's has awesome coffee and an even better breakfast, probably the best in South Tampa. The downside is there is almost always a wait. 

The egg sandwich is out of this world. At first, I couldn't figure out why myself and so many others are obsessed with it, and now I believe it's on account of the ridiculous amount of cheese they use. I have tried many other things on the menu, but always come back to the sandwich. 

The jalapeno cheese grits are also the bomb. 

I love the self-serve coffee where you get to pick out your own kitschy mug and then fill it with your preferred roast, they always have a great variety so I typically try them all. The servers are always friendly, too.

The place is a nice place in a small shopping center.  This was my second time there.  They have a very large menu, ranging from sushi to Thai, to Hibachi, etc.  I ordered the Green Panang Curry with #3 spicy, with chicken.  The food came out hot and nicely presented, the curry in a bowl, and the rice on the plate beside the bowl.  There was quite a bit of chicken with a nice mix of veggies.  Personal preference only, but the 3 spicy seemed a bit light on the spice.  I will probably do a 5, next time.  I could certainly go hotter, but I don't want to pay for it, later.  The service was inconsistent with the drink refills, which is somewhat common in a smaller restaurant, depending on what else is going on in the place.  They do have a feature that allows you to get a $5 credit with every 10 meals, or something like that, as I just discovered.  I expect I will be back, from time to time.

Attended a wedding (of all things) in this facility.  Wow!  The ceremony itself took place in the library upstairs, which was an imposing scene, but was beautiful.  Reception was held in the marbled main entrance.  
We were able to then tour the museum itself while dinner was squared away upstairs.    I'm sure it is just as interesting without the couple of glasses of wine already in my system, but I would return just to see the exhibits.  
Dinner and dancing were held upstairs.
What an amazing venue for a special event -- excellent!

Hands down best thai food in the area, definitely some of the best in the city. You cant beat the prices, the people, and the BYOB. They have always been welcoming and very friendly, and the atmosphere is great.

The Deli counter is awful! I can never get my meat cut right.  Its always either too thin to pull apart or too thick to make a sandwich.  i asked for low sodium cheese which I got at the other one on township, but wynnewoods just gave me american . They seemed to not know what I was talking about when I said LOW SODIUM

Made a reservation over 4 weeks ago.  Was told to be on time since it will be crowded.   Arrived 20 mins before reservation.  Not seated until 25 minutes after reservation.  Walk ins were being seated before people with a reservation.  And to make things even worse, you have to walk through everyone waiting to be seated with your food.  Also, there should be more serving utensils for the buffet. People should not be using their hands to get dessert. Table service was good.   Management is a disgrace.  Taking more reservations than you can handle is simply greedy.  In the long run, you lose customers like me.

Oh Stephen Starr, you have redeemed yourself after so many lackadaisical outings to the overly motiffed and plastic-loving Pod. A spontaneous decision on a Thursday night found us in front of the well-established Continental Midtown. Despite the semi-dramatic decor, the food was actually pretty damn good.  

Here are the dishes we quickly devoured:

Mushroom flatbread: I'm not sure why I've been having this obsession with mushrooms and cheese lately. I'm hoping my incessant talking of mushrooms and cheese will get you to go and try this amazing combination pronto.

BBQ Chicken Quesadilla: it was topped with a very decadent ranch sauce. yum.

Cheesesteak Springrolls:  Its basically a cheesesteak fried. is it absolutely fattening? duh. but is it worth it? totally. 

Of course we ordered not one but two desserts. sigh. 

Blondie Bombshell:

Cinnamon Sugar Pretzels with Caramel Sauce and Guinness Ice Cream (dessert special of the night)

the desserts were pretty standard and although they are pretty inexpensive, its because the portions are also smaller. Save the 5 bucks and go get a nice cup of gelato from Capogiro
Tom was great and the price was right.  They did a great job removing some old furniture from my parents home.  Would recommend for sure!!!!

Wonderful place to eat and enjoy friends.  I enjoy eating my friends.  Dogs welcome. Good beer.  You can check in, but you can never leave.  It does take a while to get your check, so plan ahead and have a beer whilst you wait.  Not a place for those in a hurry.  My fave neighborhood hangout on a pretty night---and the front porch heaters are nice and toasty in the winter.  Great pesto, smoked chicken is a delight, fresh fish ceviche for a cleaner feel, or do what I do----order a garden melt with smoked chicken and leave the beer selection up to the waiter---who usually knows what unlisted treasures await;)

I have mixed feelings about this store. I love the store itself and their collections, but somehow I always feel as if I don't belong here... And it's usually because of sales associates who give me weird looks. The shoe dept is the worst! 

Today I had another shopping experience I have mixed feelings about. I came here to buy a gift for our niece. I knew what I wanted and was going to buy this small gift here and a bigger gift elsewhere. 

The sales associate of the kids dept was friendly and helpful in finding me the book I was looking for. When I was ready to pay and I gave her my debit card, she looked at it and asked for my ID. I informed her it was my husband's debit card. She then refused the debit card because it wasn't mine. I didn't say anything about it, because I felt somewhat uncomfortable and didn't expect this at all. Neither have I experienced this before, especially not when I'm spending only $13! 

The fact that I wasn't able to give her my own debit card made me feel even more uncomfortable. Thankfully I had some cash on me (a rare thing), so I was able to pay for the gift anyway. 

Like another reviewer said, I will only come here for things I can't get anywhere else. Maybe next time I'll even shop online...
Killer pancakes & lovely small-town ambiance. Perfect little brunch place for this small town Kentucky girl in town on business :)
These are fine cleaners. Service is quick and cheap. People, things happen to your stuff sometimes.

Tonight my Husband surprised me with one of my favorite dishes,  Spaghetti Carbonara. We ordered take out on the way home.  Fabulous doesn't do it justice.  Not only was the  Carbonara wonderful,  it came with a Salad and hot bread.  The staff was very professional and it was ready when promised.  Highly recommended this restaurant.

This branch is probably one of the best branches in town. They have helped me with fees a few times. All of the employees are awesome. If only WF Would do away with the exorbitant fees and be a little more lenient with the credit cards in regards to people who have less than Stellar credit. Don't know why it put 3 stars instead of 5 like I put.

We went as a family last night.  The staff was so friendly and quick to help and serve.  We had a miriad of items and they were all completely gone by the time we left.  My 5 year old loves their queso and my 14 year old loves the challenge of the hot sauce bar.  My 11 yo daughter who is highly picky loved her quesadilla with steak.  I love that they let me put steak on the kid quesadilla.  She wouldn't finish the adult size one.  They handled all of our special requests with ease.  We initially sat outside because it is so nice and peaceful, but it proved to be too cold.  The staff helped us move.  The girl held the door and all of our dinners at the same time.  I said, "I should hold the door for you!  You have all that food!" She said, "oh no, I am sure you take care of everyone all the time.  My turn to take care of you!" So sweet.  

The value is great.  Special days like Taco Tuesday makes the value even greater.  We will be back often.  I do think we get asked for refills a bit too much.  But, in a world where so many businesses have forgotten how to provide customer service I would rather have a little too much service than not enough.

My husband and I just had breakfast at this new restaurant and we really loved it. The service was absolutely great and the food was excellent. I have the waffle sliders which were really good and something different. My husband had the Floridian omelette which he really enjoyed as well. They were doing a fundraiser so the bill was free, which I think is so nice of the owners. Everything is brand-new!
I absolutely love this hotel stayed here a a week ago and cant wait to go back service was excellent

The food itself is good but it's pricey. They have really good happy hour drink specials however. It gets a little hot inside-- I wished they would pump the AC a little higher. The service is great-- the hostess and our server were very friendly and accommodating. I remember going to the Gyu-Kaku in NYC a lot during my college years and I don't remember if the prices were just as high but I remember the food was super delicious then. The location is good considering there's tons of parking even on a Friday night unlike midtown or Rittenhouse. 

Although I feel like going to AYCE Korean BBQ is a better deal, I would probably go back to Gyu Kaku again for a random date night.
