Welcome to your own mini vacación to Havana, Cuba. This restaurant and the one on Broad Ripple are the only Indy options for Cuban, and both are good. This one differs from BR in that it is a formal sit-down restaurant with sandwiches, appetizers, and a large entree menu + deserts. 

When you walk in, there's soft lighting and vibrant music (usually salsa). There's six 4-person tables and four 6-person tables, plus a bar with some seating (great if you are doing take-out). 

I'd recommend coming here for lunch, because the lunch specials (3 each day) are about $9.99 and include some of their best dishes like arroz imperial (chicken and rice, so juicy) or ropa vieja (shredded beef with rice). The lunch specials rotate. 

Their entrees are reasonably priced, and there are lots of options (unless you're vegetarian or vegan, sorry). The ropa vieja is, I think, on the more expensive end at $13.99 (but totally worth it!) but other dishes are $10.99 or $11.99. Whatever I e tried, I've liked. They take a lot of care with their food - FYI which means it can take a while to be prepared, so understand if you're on a time rush (but not always! Today at dinner I got mine in 15 min!)

The appetizers are WOO good. The marinated beef in the beef empanadas makes this one of the BEST beef empanadas (if not the best) in the city. The papa rellena is very good, also (and VERY hard to find in Indy). Both are $3 or $3.50, which is a great deal. 

The fried plantains are cooked PERFECTLY and are beautiful. 

Service is great, and it's always this one woman (owner?) and an older woman. 

Parking is right in front of the restaurant!

I want to cry just thinking this place is located all the way in Tampa.

  I love how small these are!  You can taste many different flavors because they are so small.  They also look beautiful.  What an art they makea

  There was a line when we went but it went by quickly and we placed our six donut order.  I wanted 16 but my sister didn't think itwas a good idea... my favorite was definitely the Samoas, the donut was so soft and sweet. All the donut were sooo good!

  For six donuts, I paid under $5. You can also customize your item donut. They were not greasy at all or overly sweet. The staff were super polite and knowledgeable.

   I can't wait to find myself in Tampa again.  I will definitely make a detour if I have to to get some of these delicious donuts

Just like the first reviewer I was lied to twice on the phone and the driver showed up over 4 hours late. My car broke down and was using roadside assistance. I totally believe they lied to get the job. They knew they couldn't pick up my car in an hour.

This is an awesome, intimate and sophisticated steakhouse. Our waiter "Walter" was an amazing addition to an elegant dinner with optimal presentation and overall personal need to make sure our experience was enjoyable. Every request was countered with inviting smile. It was his pleasure to make sure we were served. From what I hear and see the steak was prepared to perfection and seemingly the beast steak they've had in a long time. I chose the chicken parm which was delectable. We'll return again!

The actual facilities here are fine. The pool is beautiful during the summer. 

This month, I had to cancel my credit card and get a new one. I forgot to update my PSC account with the new card. Instead of calling me once and leaving a message, PSC called from an 800 number 4-5 times a day for two weeks without ever leaving a voicemail. Finally, after two weeks of calls, I got a message asking me to call back and update my card. I thought I was being harassed by telemarketers. Who just calls 4-5 times a day and hangs up if they actually need to get a hold of you? This is a ridiculous communication method. I've been with the NYSC system and their bad business practices since I lived in Washington and am sick of dealing with them - will be canceling my membership and going elsewhere.

If there was such a thing as 100 stars, these guys would get it. Nicest, most understanding and flexible I've ever met. Cameron got me set up for a 24 hr rental on a 2018 Scout. Brand new and NICEE. The Gorgeous green monster. The weather wasn't the best as we had thought, but it great nonetheless. I'll be renting again very soon! THANK YOU!!

While waiting to be seated, several tables leaving or picking up to-go orders were commenting that it was their 3rd, 4th or 5th day in a row!!! I understand why...the food was absolutely outstanding! Had the seared tuna salad,buccaneer roll and spicy tuna roll. Everything was fresh with unique flavors that made it extra delicious. The tuna salad had half an avocado sliced in it along with a generous portion of tuna. If anything, it almost needed more greens/lettuce because the portion was so generous. The owner was circulating and checking in with customers the entire time we were there. I am rating 5 stars because the food was truly phenomenal. The only negative was our waitress. She kept us waiting,made several mistakes and never once apologized. When I asked her, for the fourth time, for lemon for my water she informed me that she would have to cut the lemons because they didn't have a full bar. How about, "I'm sorry I have to cut them and I haven't had a minute?" We had tried to order sparkling water, but they were out and she was defensive versus apologetic. When she only brought one of the salads instead of two, "oh most people split them,but I'll get you another if you want." Not a biggie, just irritating and it certainly won't stop me from returning for the outstanding food.

Really disappointed in my burger here. 

The place is, ONCE AGAIN, one of those, "hey hepcats! Bring your best girl down to the malt shop and be the bees knees with all the other daddy-os....Elvis!" type joints. When you open a burger joint, do they like give you a tax break or something if you make it a 50's themed sock hop? Jesus Christ. I'm so sick of eating burgers in a tacky diner with pictures of 57 Coupe Devilles on the walls. Ugh.

ANYWAY, the food was just as annoying as the cliched decor. Our server was a sweet little girl; and I do mean little girl, as it definitely appeared to be her first day at her first job. She was INSANELY nervous, and forgot almost every request we made of her. One of those requests was to please cook my (pregnant) wifes burger to well done. Now listen, I GET IT. You ask for a well done burger, you deserve what you get. I get mad if my burger is even slightly over medium, but this wasn't a personal choice; we HAD to get well done. That said, "well done" here means, grilled to hell and back, then put back on the grill and REgrilled to a second well done. Holy hell what a hockey puck! You could've used the patty to crack walnuts. It was ABYSMAL. And please believe that shit ain't cheap either. Our two burgers and fries with a shake was in the neighborhood of $40. 

Cheeburger Cheeburger was pretty much the only game in town while we were there for a Cirque Du Soliel show, so I doubt I'd ever be back here, but if I ever was, theres NO way I'm stopping here for a bite. They don't spell Cheeseburger correctly, and they sure as hell don't make one any better.

Shake was ok though.

Decided to try it out with my family as it was new and we love a great burger. Unfortunately we were severely disappointed. I had originally deleted this app off my phone because I rarely use it anymore. I reinstalled it specifically for this review because I felt obligated. The pictures of the burgers and reviews were excellent. The atmosphere was even as expected for a bar/burger house. That's where it went south. The burgers were all bread. The bread was good, it should be about the burger. Pretty sure they weren't hand made. I ordered the pizza burger. Pepperoni, sauce, cheese, burger, bread. My first clue it was going to be bad was when it came out well done when I asked for it medium. Next I noticed how much bread there was. A huge bun for a small burger. Then I took a bite and I asked my wife why the pepperoni was stringy. I finally realized it was because when they sliced their pepperoni they forgot to remove the plastic it was packaged in. Horrible. I immediately called the waitress over and showed her and asked her to take it back. I lost my appetite immediately. My wife got an original burger and asked for hers medium as well. Hers was well done. She said it tasted like a frozen burger. The owner did come over and apologize and said he would have to better train the kitchen staff. No kidding? It never should have happened. We will never be back.

Took my wife here for her birthday. Reminded her of the pubs back home in England so she really enjoyed the ambiance from the moment we walked in. Not too crowded but not empty by any means. Having the hostess smile and welcome us was definitely a plus that most restaurants overlook. I had the Beer Batter Venison sausage and my wife had the Braised Lamb Shanks. Both were absolutely heavenly. The venison sausage was literally melt in your mouth delicious and the lamb shanks were fall off the bone good. We simply could not say enough good thing about our entrees. Perfectly portioned and seasoned just right. Service was also a plus. Our server was very courteous and very helpful when it came to choosing the perfect entree. 

We definitely plan on coming back. I would love to bring my dad there for his birthday, as well. Loved it!!

The bakery here is very delicious!  I love coming in and getting cookies for the office every Tuesday morning.  Nothing beats a macaroon in the morning!  Recently I decided to dine in there to see what the café is like.  The service was all right and the food was great as always.  I will be returning to La Bonne Bouchee very soon and very often.  I recommend this bakery for anyone's catering needs, or if you just want a cookie on a bad day!
Great customer service. Very dog friendly and accommodating. The food was amazing. I would definitely come back with my 2 dogs.

You would think that with all the money that Costco makes they would avoid selling us foods from China, the most poluted country in the the world, but think again.  Costco carries a lot of china made food products.  Do not subject your families and children to dangerous foods from china full of chenicals,  pestcides,  cancer causing agents and grown in poluted water.  Read the lable if it states country of origin as china, return it , don`t buy it.  I always thought Costco was better than the rest, but greed for that extra dollar is their bottom line.  Costco do the right thing and dump china food products and protect your customers...

Carcassonne + Beer Flights = Good times.

Needs a matchmaking app to find a quick PUG with strangers.

I was very disappointed in this store today. Normally Ace is amazing. But today there were no staff in the Service Area. I waited for 5 minutes, then went to ask a clerk to call someone back there for me. 10 minutes later, still no one showed up. At least a half dozen staff walked by, but they seemed more interested in going on break than responding when I said "Excuse me...."  So I left and took my business to Lowe's.

For an afternoon snack, we happened upon Sweet Charlie's! I was thrilled to see rolled ice cream since I've never had it. I was completely willing to take some Lactaid and chance an upset stomach. Then as we began to order the staff asked if we wanted milk, yogurt, or the vegan option. What?? Dairy Free?? Yes!!

I ordered the dairy-free s'mores rolled ice cream with an extra torched marshmallow! The ice cream was pretty good but I will admit it was very sweet.
Best sidecar in blue bell! Great atmosphere, chill place. My bartender Laura was amazing :)

So pleased to receive a recommendation for this gem here in New Orleans. Our first time here, we were looking for a special dining experience. From the moment we crossed into the courtyard we knew we would not be disappointed. I recommend the sweetbread which is one of their specialties. Really enjoyed our evening!

Decided to try another Mexican food place near South Meadows, as I have been going to Super Taquiria on Double Diamond for far too long. I want to see what their competitors on this side of town had to offer. 

It wasnt busy, no one in line so ordered from the beautiful cashier. I ordered 3 tamales(pork) and 2 carne asada tacos to go. With a large ice tea. The tea was actually good, and its a crap shoot everytime you order tea, because sometimes its spoiled and not fresh and that sucks. This tea was fresh. 

I got my order in a bag and off i went back to work. Their were like 4 tables with messes on them (11:30a on a Friday), and that should have been cleaned up i think, looked messy. 

Got back to work, and viewed my feast. There were 2 tamales and 3 tacos, exactly the opposite numbers on the items i ordered. The tamales were ok, more spicy than these types of places make but they were ok still. The tacos were pretty standard too, nothing to scream about. I did enjoy the salsa, it was delicious! 

I guess ill stick with Super Taquiria up the street. They havent been beat yet, and their tamales are superior.
Very nice place. Good food all they are missing a cold beer. Highly recommended. Crab cakes!!

Ah, Fox & Hound. Once upon a time, I came here once a month for WWE PPVs, accumulating all sorts of goofy memories. Then, a few years back, I came for a Steelers playoff game and the place was packed. So we came for a regular season game on Sunday. The menu hasn't changed. But almost everything else has.

Let's start with the service. It was terrible to the point that it put my "always give ~20%" rule to the test (I did, but it was tempting not to). My group was consistently ordering drinks + food, and yet there were stretches of 20-30 minutes when we didn't so much as see our server. And the place wasn't crowded in the slightest. Our server could barely be bothered to say anything when she did come around, and would just kind of stare back at us after we placed an order. Lastly, at the end, she told us she couldn't split our check among the 3 of us. Great.

I've had many a Black Forest Sandwich there - which I do enjoy - but the pretzel bun was cold, with the rest of the sandwich being lukewarm, at best. My brother said that his burger tasted like a frozen Boca burger. He ordered it at the same time as a beer... and they brought the burger out first. How does that happen? Oh, and despite the fact that there were only 1 or 2 football games on, we couldn't get the 76ers game on a SINGLE TV when we asked. In Center City Philadelphia.

That being said, I do like the environment for watching football games, which is why I probably will come back for a playoff game, at some point. And, despite my not being a big drinker whatsoever, I actually enjoyed the array of alcoholic beverages... That being said, there's not a mention of non-alcoholic ones to be found on the menu. Can a man get a soda!?

In closing, if you're as sports obsessed as I am, this place serves its purpose. But it really wouldn't kill them to work on the actual RESTAURANT part of it. Cause if you're just looking for a meal, there are INFINITELY better options.
Pies are great. Customer service lacking. They don't keep pies out on display for odd reason. Overpriced for a slice. $5.75. I'm a fan.

My mobile order was even being made 5 min after it was placed. I had to wait in line and remind them I had a mobile order. The staff was playing and loud. Others had to inquire about their mobile orders, as well.

This was the ultimate in "Just Okay" for me. We stopped in because the place we wanted to go to up the street was way too busy and we didn't want to wait. So we got in here and got a table thinking we wouldn't wait. But we waited anyway.

I ordered the  Shrimp Scampi Pizza which tasted both burnt and bleh. Admittedly I may have been imagining it would taste like a Shrimp Scampi Pizza I've had from ANOTHER establishment, but it didn't.  I can forgive that part, but the burnt part I just couldn't get past. 

I doubt I'd ever come back, and I couldn't really recommend it to anyone.

I visit New Hope Pennsylvania every month or two and it's great to see the town redeveloped the market. All the new restaurants in the food court are pretty good for the most part, prices are reasonable and the place is kept spotless. 

This is a great place to stop with a variety of healthy foods, indoor and outdoor seating and fast service. I would recommend stopping by.

#132 to review and so thrilled to have gone here.
After a grueling day on the golf course, came here with a co-worker for delicious beer, a wonderful glass of Kim Crawford Sauv Blanc and a spicy Bayou margarita and...seriously incredible food.

Screw the carbs that i've been trying to avoid. 

Why i love this place:
-Their Champignon (thank goodness i can use my high school French) flatbread is the best I've had anywhere. I know I ate 3/4 of the very generous sized flatbread. Also ordered the Creole Shrimp flatbread. How do they do it?

-House made tapenade- for olive lovers everywhere and their crispy homemade crackers...

-Industrial layout yet very welcoming and spacious. Great upstairs with a full bar as well - the balcony view reminds me of New Orleans..with a drink in hand of course. 

-Kat, our server, really knows the menu, which served us well. 

Lot of enthusiasm from the bartender and our server. The owner was on hand as well; our server Kat said he is there all the time - which is truly impressive.

love this place

I love the tips & dip powder I got at Royal! They really took their time and you could tell the goal was perfection :). I spent a lot of time looking at photos of dip manicures in Indy and I really feel this is the best! They had a huge color selection and they were kind and careful. Thank you so much!

Love the service & bagels here. A little too much if you know what I mean. . . 
My husband almost always gets the Ranchero wrap. I enjoy all the varieties including the chocolate chip. They have just about any type of soft drink, juice or coffee you could want. 
I never liked cream cheese until I had their garlic & herb kind. Now I'm addicted. 
The ladies that work here in the morning work miracles when it's crowded. And they're super pleasant.

Huge, well kept multi dealer mall with something for everyone. This place has great help that are friendly. The prices range from very low to what I would consider fair for the high quality items (so the rating is hard to set).  We didn't get there until 5pm which only gave us an hour to shop and I don't think I saw one third of it. It's on my list for one of the better antique malls and will revist it every time we are in town.

I'm a sucker for a grilled cheese sandwich so my husband knew he would be able to lure me to the farmer's market with the lure of melted dairy between two pieces of bread. Toss in an avocado and you have a happy girl. 

The Gambler with avocado, tomato & basil mayo caught my eye. That with a Mango Pineapple Lemonade to sip on the warm day was a nice early lunch to tide us over until it was time to head out to the Yelp's Around Tampa Bay party. The sandwich was loaded with cheese and it was hard not to get it all over me when eating. And the tomato soup dipping sauce was an added bonus. 

I will definitely be seeking these guys out on future visits to Cigar City.

This review is for an IN-PERSON SERVICE. About 2.5 weeks ago I had my makeup done for the Zulu Mardi Gras Ball. I was very pleased with the turn out. Tia is the truth! I requested a natural look and it came out well. Full face done all the way to the hairline. Minor blemishes smoothed over perfectly. The lip stain did not come off all night after eating and drinking several times after said makeup appointment.

I have officially found heaven on earth. Most bakeries these days consist of cakes, cupcakes and cookies..but not Moreno! They have everything! I felt like a kid in a candy store. They have donuts, brownies, pies, tarts, cakes, cupcakes, pies, bonbons, you name it! Everything I tried gets an A+. Next time I will have to have lunch there (I was a little distracted by all the sweets). I will definitely go back!

I tried the cod again, based in part on the decent feed of sole that I had here awhile back.  This time around, it was much, much better.  It's still pricey, but that's to be expected being this far from the sea.  Recommended.

A decent stay and nice rooftop, which was the highlight though the staff (a young lady) sitting on a stool the night of my arrival could use some customer service training as her greeting seems to have had more of an investigatory tone (as though my family and I were Trespassers not guests)! 

Walls are quite thin and I was awakened every morning before 7am by loud guests next door. Also have never stayed in a hotel at these rates with no iron, ironing board and without ample storage space in a room with double beds. Parking was a bit high too (25.00 across the street for Self parking and 39.00 for Valet).

Like a finely crafted cocktail , I prefer my food be interesting as well as delicious . Food has been around forever...so to find something visually appealing, bold, delightful and innovative is quite a treat.  

Each dish was beautifully presented. The wait staff was pleasant and efficient. Many tables have an interesting view of the chefs at work in the kitchen. The atmosphere in the kitchen seemed very happy.  I much prefer to think my meal is being lovingly prepared, as apposed to "Hell's Kitchen"! 

There is a small patio area out front to allow for alfresco dining, which would be very relaxing in this charming neighborhood. The valet service provided is complimentary, and in this area an enormous plus.

All of the fare was memorable...but none quite as spectacular as the dessert. Panna Cotta with cucumber and rhubarb ice. The Panna Cotta was silky and creamy, the cucumber ice was bright, and fresh, while the rhubarb was tart. The ice itself was soft but with the surprising crunch of lemon lime "Pop Rocks," that snap in your mouth...now that was a true taste sensation.  A dish that will live in infamy in my mind, and rank a spot on my "Top 100 Best Things I Ever Put in My Mouth"!  
Join me , and find your own Niche and excite your tastebuds!

We traveled from Boca Raton about 4 hrs to this venue to see one of our favorite bands Donna the Buffalo for New Years Eve.  We weren't expecting much from the venue and were pleasantly surprised!  This outdoor venue had excellent food from the raw oysters to the crawfish and mac.  There were about 400 very friendly people there with plenty of seating and dancing area for all.  The sound quality was fantastic and the owners were present and making sure the crowd was enjoying themselves.  They even treated everyone to a delicious breakfast after midnight!  What a great experience and well worth the drive-the funny thing is there were people who flew in from VA, IL and places much further away than us.  They knew - now we know and we'll be back

My SO and I came here for an impromptu date night a couple weeks ago.  I live well within walking distance and we've been wanting to try out Lebanon's for a while now.  We were so happy we finally did!

We got small plates of hummus, kibby, spinach filo, and safeiheh.  The hummus tasted pretty fresh and had wonderful lemony flavor, as well as a nice smooth texture.  The kibby, a fried ball of cracked wheat, ground beef, onions, and pine nuts, was excellent.  The flavors were great; it kind of reminded me of a boudin ball, but with Mediterranean flavors.  Any reminder of boudin is A+ in my book!
The spinach filo was pretty simple - filo stuffed with feta, spinach, and ricotta.  My SO is not a feta fan, so I got to enjoy most of this myself.  It was cheesy, spinachy, flakey goodness...  The safeiheh is a mini pizza - ground lamb and beef, tomatoes, and spices on a pita bread.  It was my favorite dish all night!  The lamb and beef were seasoned perfectly and there was plenty on the pita.  The kibby, filo, and pizza were also served with Tzatziki sauce, which was pretty damn good too.  Not too yogurty, or cucumbery, but just right.  

We got the Combination Kabob for our main dish.  It came with chicken, lamb, and beef, as well as onions and peppers.  It was served with a small salad and (MORE!) hummus.  Again, everything was seasoned quite well, and we ended up making pita sandwiches with all the ingredients on the plate.

The whole meal cost about $30-35 and I had enough leftover for dinner the next day.  It was an excellent deal for excellent food.  I hope we return soon!

This is the must spot to visit in Willingboro. Came here today with orders from North Jersey. And firgit to use my telp discount. 
Each steak and one chicken was all that an more. If you have not been there. Please check them out. You will not regret i

I feel they need to make covered caps mandatory for all staff specially the person making your sandwich.

The guy who made mine had a bad case of dandruff and didn't want any grated cheese on my sandwich as a topping of my choice.

What can you a say. The chicken sandwich is flat out delicious. Line has been wrapped around the restaurant for days. I heard on the radio the other locations are out of the new sandwich. We stopped by and they promised my son they would save him a sandwich if he came back tomorrow, they did. Great job to all the staff at the location. I know it's been crazy for days.

HIGHLY RECOMMMENDED!!!
From the start Leen and the guys at the shop have been top notch. Their over all concern was for my safety in the vehicle.  They took such good care me and my vehicle. 
Leen walked me through every step of the process,  contacted my insurance company,  and handled it all.  I received pictures everyday of the progress they made via email, so I knew exactly what was going on. Even with the extra fixes they found after they gave me the estimate; they stuck to their estimate. Amazing! 
My car looks wonderful!  I am so happy with the work they did. I would take my car back to them in a heart beat!

Went here on a drive across country. We had called ahead and asked about safe parking as we were hauling stuff. They had promised good parking. When we came they could not accommodate us. 

The hotel was under reconstruction. The room were dated and the places was noisy and dusty. There are lots of great hotels in New Orleans, this is not one of them.

It's a bar. With bar food. You come to drink, get driggitty drunk, play pinball and some video games if you want. And munch on some finger food. 

If you're expecting something outta this world, hop in a UFO. Or lower your expectations.

I will say the Spanish fries were tasty. Two BIG stars, baby!

"Burger Medium Rare. Service Well Done."

File South Philly Bar and Grill under: good burgers. Actually, luscious burgers. 

Mine came *perfectly* medium rare as requested, handsome in mozzarella and absolutely excellent bacon: real, not smoked flavor; thick-cut; well cooked, yet miraculously not burnt. (See photo.)

The accompanying long-hot was a scorcher: at your own risk. (See photo.)

Caramelized onions under the patty were a miracle in burger architecture: they didn't sog out the bun and the patty remained well in place. (I'm looking at you, Adsum.) Waffle fries were fine: far superior to coated or Brand X matchstick, but kinda lightweight and throwaway. 

Only negative was the bun itself, which was a tad stale. But the burger itself was so standout, f!ck the damn bun.

Coke tasted excellent and clean, unsullied by the other mixers that pass through the lines. (I'm looking at you, Royal.) They didn't even balk at my princess request to add lemon. Yay!

Server was A+. 

Tip: go on an off night, when there's no game on. It'll be you, your scrumptious burger, and a bit of earnest Top 40 to carry you through.

As a local (I wasn't born here but raised in the area since I was 3) I have heard several stories of Antoine's.  The stories of snobbery, how the menu use to be in all French and if you could't read it, it was your problem, and of course all of the history.

Antoine's had intimidated me.  I didn't think I was refined enough to dine there.  I felt as if though I needed practice at other restaurants in order to be worthy of dining here.  Antoine's was on my short list of must eat restaurants for years and until this Saturday I still wasn't sure if I was up to their standards.  After dining there, I don't think they are up to mine.  

There is no longer the snootiness that once existed.  The waiters are personable, friendly, helpful and make the experience enjoyable.  My waiter was somewhat aloof but nothing too bad.  He would just give me my lady friend's food and vice versa and read us the lunch menu instead of dinner for the Coolinary.  

We started off with the Oysters 2-2-2; Rockefeller, Bienville and Thermador.  They invented the Rockefeller and will remind you of that throughout your meal.  They even give you a card telling you what # order you are of the dish as a keepsake.(It's not very accurate as they have probably sold twice as many according to the waiter)  The oysters were pretty solid with the Bienville being really good!  The Bienville are baked in a white wine sauce, onions, and peppers.  Delsih.

After that we did the Coolinary menu.  I had the Shrimp Au-gratin to start.  The portion is quiet small but being as it was a pre-fixed 3 course menu, it's understandable.  The cheesy shrimp flavor was really good and au-gratiny.( I made up a word)  My entree was the French Pork chop.  The description has it as a '10 oz. French-style pork chop with apple port sauce and served with Brabant potatoes'.  If there was a sauce on mine, there wasn't much of one.  French style must mean bone in but in this case could have meant over cooked.  I love a thick cut prok chop and have gotten them at several places in the city and this was my 1st time getting one that I'd call mediocre.  It was like when I 1st started grilling and was afraid of undercooking them.  It was borderline burnt.  The Brabant potatoes are a fancy way of saying home fries.  The desert was Peche' Melba.  This was candied peaches, ice cream and rasberry sauce on top of a crushed almond cake.  Simple but delish.  The girlfriend got the drum fish dish that was suppose to be in a rich cream and white wine sauce but was quite bland.


Being as the Coolinary menu is 3 courses for 35.00, I didn't feel cheated but if I had paid normal menu prices for the same dishes, I would have.  Antoine's lives on it's history.  They talk it up as they should as the oldest restaurant in America but while their history dates back 174 years their prices are 74 years in the future.  Entrees start in the high 20's and go upwards of 50.00.  All sides are a-la carte and are about 7-9 dollars each.  Appetizers are in the 15.00 range.  I say this not to seem like a cheap ass but to say that their food isn't good enough to charge those kind of prices.  The atmosphere is great, the history even better, the oysters were solid and the sazerac was spot on.  However when I'm dropping the 175.00 for a meal for 2, I want to be WOW'd.  I was not.

Stop looking for a DJ and hire Hecktik! DJ Hecktik (Josh) kept our wedding going from beginning to end. We love music and wanted to dance all night long. His website made it easy to incorporate the songs we did and didn't want to have playing on the dance floor. He took the time to meet with us ahead of time to understand the vibe we were going for and made sure to incorporate all of these aspects into our big day. His crew was professional, timely and made for a great event. Our dance floor was full the entire night! People kept saying our wedding had the best music and kept dancing until we were forced to leave.
This place is a great hidden treasure. This is a locals place with absolutely awesome food and craft beer.

If you want the best Thai food in the greater Tampa area you have to come.  I was so stoked when they moved to the Riverview area.  Now just down the road.  The food! Where do I begin!  My consistent go to is the Drunken Noodles.  When the flavor of that first bite hits my mouth it's impossible to restrain the shitty grin that takes over my face.  BAM!  Pad Thai! BAM! Crab Fried Rice! BAM!  You get the point.  Service is awesome.  JJ and her crew always look after me like a friend that's come over to hang out.  Only bad thing I can say is that they're closed on Mondays and Tuesdays.  Booooo!

Very Disappointed. I ordered food to go on Christmas Eve and my husband and I decided to dine in for Valentines Day today. Let me say first, Yes it is always expected for businesses to be busier than normal on certain occasions. Both experiences on Christmas Eve and today were horrible. One person waiting and bussing tables. Same person also working on to go orders. Food took forever and there was a young girl who was also helping with to go orders and a little girl, maybe 2; both coughing like crazy. Perhaps have extra help when business will be a lot busier than normal.

First experience was amazing, food was great, service and staff was quick and friendly. Staff greeted us upon entry and held the door for us. We ordered the "trio chip" appetizer which was great. For my entree I had Chicken tacos which were rich in flavor and came out promptly. The ambiance and vibe is spectacular (as seen in pictures) and its a cool place to grab a quick lunch or hangout and have a few beers from the selection of the 12 Florida micro breweries available. Management greeted our table to assure everything was going great, which it was, and was very nice and helpful with any questions we had about the menu. 6/5 for Taco YOLO, I will definitely be back.

Come here several times a week. Good falafel, good shwarma, reasonable prices. 
Quick, casual, and delicious. 
And the man who works most days is super nice!

Very good food, but I get poor consistency and service which has made me stop having lunch there. There churros are spot on amazing, not to soggy or hard and crunch, perfectly made. Burritos are a different story, I love myself a Good burrito and my first experience with them was promising. But every time I came back one thing was off, either the tortilla was burnt, or too much cheese. I would have to literally pull out half of the cheese with my hands because they just put it in a blob in the middle, it wasn't even spread out evenly. I eventually asked them to put half of what cheese the normally put in and most the time they didn't even do that. They also don't salt there French fries, which are great, but sucks when I have to stop by a store to pick up salt for them. I even asked them if hey had any and they said no. 

It's just make my stomach queasy trying to even pull up anymore, since they can't get anything right, there Drive through manners are poor, or better said they lack communication with me, with greeting, knowing when to pull up and even if. He even heard your order correctly.

Sad to see a good lunch spot go downhill over poor execution

Had the French toast special in Tuesday. Then I decided to sit down and eat it, so glad I did. It was hot and warm and when I spooned some strawberry jam on there...Baaam! Awesome-sauce! 
But it wasn't over. I got that Dutch Apple goodness with cream and went beyond heaven. Can I just melt here?

Perfectly fine, but from all the hype I expected something a bit nicer. Very nice lobby area. Comfortable bed and suite. No overhead lighting in the bathroom which made for a dim showering experience. Overall we were not terribly impressed.

Came back here on my 4th trip to NOLA this morning, and this one woman staff working was rude and snarky with our party of 3. We asked if they had fried chicken but, was told it's only served on, Thursday. Ok, fine today, was Monday. They didn't have fried chicken this particular day, which was what my daughter wanted, and was told that they were also done serving breakfast for the day, too. So, we turned around to leave and find somewhere else to eat with food we wanted. Apparently, the woman working behind the counter began to yell at us to watch out for a man coming in while we were leaving. I had no clue what she was talking about because there was no man coming in at all. I personally, didn't hear any of this conversation but, my sister heard the woman complain to the other customers that we had ignored what she said. She was mad because we hadn't ordered anything, left, and didn't open a door for a man to walk into the restaurant first. However, where we come from, ladies go first, and men usually open doors for women, anyway. Sorry, but all that attitude she was giving us just doesn't cut it with me. The first time I visited this restaurant with my husband lat year, we had an excellent, friendly server who I didn't see. Unfortunately, not this time. And because of this rude woman and that incident, I won't ever be returning. Get over yourself, lady. There's better restaurants in the area who value their customers and who are friendly.

I've pass by this deli place so many times and was always curious. This is one of those place you're happy you tried it.

Personally the food was alright, nothing's special about the sandwiches except for the price, I mean 15 bucks for a Reuben sandwich!? 

Ha! So we oredered Reuben sandwich and a chicken shawarma plate and a side of fries. I ordered my Reuben with macaroni salad on the side but came out with potato salad instead, no big deal.

The sandwich was not worth 15 bucks and for that I gave it a 2 star; will not be going back :(

Service was SO bad! Waited 25 minutes for drinks and 40 minutes for our  appetizer. Entrees missing food and asked for condiments and they never arrived. I am a huge fan of Chili's, but I will never return to this one.
Love all of the topping options MOD has to offer. The hot honey is super delicious. The crust is perfect. Super excited to see that they had hard cider and not just beer.

A new gem on Davis Island! Fantastic menu of delicious, original, and fresh dishes. Every thing we ordered for our lunch was great, I had the quesadilla, peruvian potatoes, salad and bacon, all of which were skillfully made, fresh and looked fantastic.  The space has a very cool vibe, with brick walls, rustic decor and an assortment of local artwork which I particularly love, as there is a movement of restaurants and bars featuring local art to fill their walls.  They have great desserts, sauces and homemade pickles that are popular compliments to take home meals as well.  Always love the Davis Island vibe, and to have a high quality, nice feeling restaurant, with friendly staff will give me a reason to visit more often.

I had been going to Dr. Stratford-Jones for several years and was generally satisfied with the service. He's a nice, competent guy, and his hygienists were always gentle, thorough and caring. Then, a couple of years ago, after finishing my six-month cleaning, I was told by his front desk person that I had a fairly hefty co-pay that I was responsible for, and that payment was due on the spot. No one in his office ever bothered to tell me that that they were no longer accepting my insurance. I continued to make co-pays, not realizing Stratford-Jones was no longer in my network. More recently, he hired a new crop of hygienists. After years of having no cavities, I suddenly, allegedly, had four, for which I would be expected to pay something like $800 to fill. I was suspicious and scheduled an appointment with another Santa Barbara dentist. This dentist examined the most recent x-rays Stratford-Jones ' office had taken, thoroughly examined my teeth, and pronounced that I needed no fillings. My adult daughter had a similar experience with Stratford-Jones. She has never had a single cavity and recently was told she needed several fillings. The hygienist showed her x-rays purporting to show the cavities. When my daughter remarked that the x-rays appeared to have been taken in 2014, she was given some sketchy explanation to the effect that she was only being shown the dated x-rays to provide historical context. Stratford-Jones of late has been advertising cosmetic procedures like veneers. He makes his patients fill out a questionnaire that asks if they're happy with their smiles. I don't know if he's having financial troubles or what, but it was all enough to make me change dentists.

Absolutely, the worst service I have ever seen. 2 missed appointments from them for a service call for repair. 3 hours behind appointment time and no one cares. I called CSR and she tells me tech is 6 miles out, tech then calls me and says thats incorrect hes 40 mins away at the minimum.

We just went there tonight for Valentine's Day.  The food was exceptional.  The service from Michelle was exceptional.  The music is good for a romantic flare, I was just saying that on internet they asked what song reminded me of the beach.  And I replied Under the Boardwalk.  And not one minute later he was playing it.  It is for an older crowd.  People were slow dancing which Bob doesn't do but definitely a good time.  I recommend it highly.

I brought my siblings in to experience a phenomenal burger and the bomb cajun fries... and was a little disappointed. Our order got pretty messed up. Cajun fries were not made cajun, when I went back and asked to have them remade he just handed me seasoning to put on top instead of re-tossing the fries. I also needed to go back up to repeat our shake order to the same gentleman three times. I remained understanding, but the restaurant was not busy. Burgers, however, were made well and we loved them. We also received extra shakes after we got ours... It seems that the location may need time to find their flow with teamwork. I'll come back in awhile and try again!

I love this Salon's decor, a lot of natural lighting, spacious and has a cool vibe.

I was greeted by a very warm hearted individual and I was impressed by the work ethic.  Sweeping, empty the trash, organizing shelves all the while answering the phone, product sales and checking people out.  Very good employee. 

My Stylist Monique was knowledgeably a Pro. She took time to discuss my hair and style. Not rushed what's so ever. I love my color and cut and the shampoo was a bonus with the scalp massage. 

I would recommend Monique at Tribe Salon.

I have been a patient here for more than 10 years. Dr Billela and his staff are amazing!!! They have truely saved my life on several occassions. Their bedside manner is beyond any kindness i have ever expierienced. I would highly reccomend if you want a doctor that truely cares for you and your well being. Contact Dr Billela for an appointment. You will never regret it!!!
owner is great and supporting a black owned business is also great! def stop in here if u can!

A solid dining experience that I hope to repeat in the near future... My visit to The Office possessed every element that I look for in dining out. The place is clean, with a rich interior, yet the atmosphere is casual and homey. From the moment we stepped in the door we were immediately greeted, seated and watered by very kind staff. They offer two variations of salmon, which we ordered along with a basket of fries and a Stella and water cooler cocktail. 
The food was delicious. I could have licked the plate as the dining room had cleared out, however I don't want to set a dangerous precedent. All in all I really enjoyed my meal and I hope to be back soon!
A must if you're dining in the Greenwood area! Bar selection is nice and the pork chop was the best I've ever had!

I've been coming to Sonia's since high school. Almost 10 years now! She's an amazing and sweet lady, always smiling and very welcoming. I've trusted her and her staff with my eyebrows and I don't go anywhere else. I recommend Sonia's to anyone!
Everything at Craft Street was awesome tonight. Our server Tyler recommended our drinks, appetizers and Entrees and they were all spot on. Will definitely be back
Mother s ruin the service es good is the best sandwich I recomendable the mother s i love the vest I come with my son and great food

Wow, what a great place! Friendly, great service and Jill, our waitress was amazing! This was during covid.. and all staff had masks on and followed all the protocols. 
Jill was really great, visited with us, gave us some choices to hit in the surrounding area and was super duper nice!!!
It was so good that we went back again one more time before heading back home. Delicious food, good service and laid back atmosphere. If I come back to NOLA again, I'd stop here, definitely.

Standard tap is just a great Northern Liberties go-to. Fantastic beer and drink list (though my friend was very disappointed that they don't have red bull) and great food. They don't have the largest menu in the world but if you're looking for a spot on burger and a great beer, or some fun appetizers make your way here. 
Its more of a quite, sit down and chat bar, but the atmosphere is great - super warm and welcoming! 
The prices are pretty reasonable and service is almost always great! 
Honestly if Standard Tap were a person it would be that great, dependable friend that you can call all the time, and hang out with every night with out getting bored.

I broke my foot in 2015 and haven't been to a cycling class since.  While I'm not as good at it as I used to be, I've absolutely loved going the past 2 weeks and can't wait to keep going.  I really enjoy Susie's classes.  Her energy is contagious and I feel like I'm pushing myself harder.   The facilities are so clean, unlike the big gyms in town that offer spin classes.  The employees clean all of the equipment and set everything up in between classes, which is also really nice.   The first class is $8 and then you can get 3 for $30.  Individual classes are $16, which I think is a really good price for the workout that you get.  If you don't have your own SPDs, you can get a pair at the front desk and I think they'll also order you a pair as well if you want to purchase them.  Having used regular tennis shoes before, you definitely want to get a pair of your own if you're going to get into cycling classes.  You're feet will thank you.  They have a no-show policy where you have to let them know 4 hours in advance if you're not going to make it to class, which I think is awesome.  If you don't let them know, you get charged a fee.  A lot of their classes fill up quick but you can be added to the waitlist so if someone cancels, you can move into their slot.  I'm so happy that I found (R)evolve!

A great nonprofit that gives tours of the many different kinds of cats in their care. The tours are informative about the biology and behavior of the cats, but they also don't shy away from telling the sad side of their stories. A great place to visit for an animal lover and a great cause to support.

I've been to ORH twice. The first time I came was years ago for a Digable Planets concert. I hated it. There were a TON of local acts and the main performers didn't come on until about 11pm and I was hot, it was obnoxiously loud, and I was tired. So my sister and I left during the main act's third song. I vowed to never come back to Old Rock House again (as if this experience was the venue's fault).

I broke my boycott Saturday night to see the incredible Tank and Bangas.  The venue is a decent space with upstairs seating, a bar, and a large downstairs main floor. I have never been upstairs to see what the views are like up there or to see how much seating is up there so I can't judge that. The venue isn't bad, however the microphones weren't turned up as loudly as they should have been for the show, so the lead singer and background singer's voices were drowned out by the band the entire show! The performers asked to have the mics turned up several times during the show, and they were never really raised up. That was unfortunate. Outside of that, the sound quality in the space (of the band basically) were good, but still, it did take away from the entire experience.

Another good point is that this venue has its own parking lots: one nicer one that's not so big and a large not-as-good gravel lot, but still FREE PARKING!

I would come back here again, but I will admit that this is far from my favorite concert venue in STL.

Easily some of the best food and drinks I had in Nashville! Service was very fast and the waitress was friendly although I could tell she wasn't having a good day.

I've had similar lavender infused vodka drinks like the lemon drop I ordered, but this one was perfect. The second cocktail was a bit more difficult for me to manage but still good, I don't remember what it was.

I loved my goat cheese platter. The cheese had chopped almonds on top and honey throughout, it tasted heavenly on everything. The mac and cheese was pretty good too, although I don't usually care for the overly cooked/softened noodles.

If I do return to Nashville, I'm coming back here.

Horrible restaurant. Food is terrible.  It's not a clean place.  The lack of customer service is almost as bad as their food.  The Customers that frequent this place are sketchy, shady, rude and no respect for the neighborhood.  They park up and down the streets, and hang out at their cars playing loud music and toss Applebee's food, cups, napkins and trash in our yard and on the streets where they sit. I am very tired of this restaurant with no regard for the CWE, along with the people that frequent it.  I suggest anyone looking for a quiet, nice, respectful, decent restaurant, to go over one street where you have Wildflowers, Taste, Brasserie, Little Saigon etc.

This place advertises about their Happy Hours and other encouraging marketing to beef up liquor consumption and yet when their customers get over served and leave their car behind they tow them that night. This happened to my girlfriend who was being responsible and not driving!!  But she goes to get her car at 9am and it was towed overnight. 
It's crazy that PJ's encourages their customers to drink and drive. CRAZY!  The Corp. Office should at least allow cars their for 24hrs. Cause the day is gonna come when someone does drink and drive from one of their establishments and when they get dragged into court they will reconsider those signs and maybe change them so that their responsible customers have time to retrieve their car in the morning.
Fast and excellent service! I was driving by and decided to take my car there due to a small air leak from one of my tires. They checked me in and repaired my tire in less than 30 minutes.

Let me start by saying it would give them 5-stars had it not been for a single bad experience. I found all but one person there to be very friendly, informative, efficient, organized and pleasant. However, that one experience and the followup exchange with the general manager of the resort simply leaves me with one star overall experience.

My family went there on a light and uncrowded day. We were two adults and two children as well as a 1-1/2 year old infant. Both my wife and I purchased full day lift tickets and rental. With the infant, we did take turns staying with the baby in the lodge while the other skied. 

In the morning, one of staff members told my wife about mother's lounge upstairs to take the baby to. It is in a corner with a curtain and a couch. It also has small area where I suppose walking infants are able to wonder around. Again, it was not crowded and there were no other mothers or children all day that day.

In the early afternoon while my wife was outside, I was sitting on a bench near mother's lounge. Baby was playing on the carpet in the mother's area. I recognize the optics of a father in mother's area may make some people uneasy so I choose to stay outside and just keep an eye on the baby. There were no mothers or other small children nearby. There were hardly any other patrons nearby. Suddenly, a staffer showed up from around the corner and snapped "This area is not for this, can I have you move your stuff". I was not interested in a confrontation so I picked up the baby, his jacket and blanket and took him out of mothers area and brought him to the bench where I was sitting. She then proceeded to 'disinfect' the area and drew the curtain to keep me and him out. She had a combat like focus on her mission to kick us out and she could hardly see the small infant walking around the area and almost ran him over. Again, I was not even in the area. Only the baby and his jacket and blanket was there.

Later, when my wife was sitting there and I was skiing, that Gestapo woman showed up again and asked her to move out of the area as well!!!!!

The sign outside the mother area say - Mother's lounge. Do not disturb when curtain is drawn. 

For the life of me I cannot figure where I or my wife did something out of the line to prompt this type of insensitive, callous and outrageous treatment. I'd also like to think that it is just the attitude of this one employee that was the problem and our ethnicity had no bearing on it. 

Here is icing on the cake...

I left a comment in the feedback box. I later received an email from the general manager simply asking for additional feedback. I replied with quite a few details. Again, saying everything else was 5-star except this inexplicable episode. 

As of the time of this writing, about two weeks after the incident I have not received any other reply. Not so much as an explanation of what their policy about that area is and where we misinterpreted. 

My two cents:

By all means go there to ski. It will be pleasant. Just don't do cross the path of the Gestapo woman who wonders around enforcing whatever she thinks the policies are. If you do, you will not find a sympathetic ear anywhere. Not even the GM!
They gave my grandmother an infection by cutting her with a nail file she was in pane DO NOT GO HERE a waist of money
Had a great visit. Manager was awesome and stopped by our table to make fun of our team... all in good fun lol. Great place and great food

If you are comfortable overpaying for pretty good sushi, come here.  I have had sushi all over the west coast, east coast, and this was THE most expensive place I have ever been.

Average roll price is $17 and the quality was just good.  For that price it had better be one of the best rolls I have ever had...not the case.

Atmosphere was fine, though when eating Japanese, I want to feel the Japanese vibe  and not listen to 90s Rock hits and country music.  

Won't come here again, the only reason I give this 2 stars is because it was clean, and I don't have food poisoning.

Wow...we came here a year ago and service and food was amazing..I wish I could say the same today. We brought friends and family to come try this amazing place but they failed us. We ordered the boiled platter 3lbs crawfish,shrimp,corn,potatoes, and sausage and it all was served cold. After asking to have it reheated the individual took it to back to reheat it pot and brought it back semi hot. My family asked the lady at counter if they could fix it and she said "Well it's the end of season and we can guarantee the crawfish to be hot "temperature " and you only paid $3.50 a lb. She refused to refund or apologize for serving the food cold. I was hoping for a better experience like we had last time. We will not be back.
Drinks were good but food was alright. Would I go here again? Yes maybe for drinks but probably not for food. I got a burger and my wife got fish tacos. Both were alright.

They take cards! They take cards! It's a Chinatown miracle!
Honestly though even if they didn't I would probably still be here as they have an excellent selection and reasonable prices. Make sure to ask for less sugar, unless you enjoy that 'most likely to get diabetes' feeling. 
Also note it is usually pretty crowded in here. Not a problem for me as I take mine to go, but if you are looking for a place to hang out seating is slim.

Favorite new spot in South County. Excellent service and atmosphere. The food is awesome. We ordered the lobster Rangoon, wings (my wife's favorite) and the Timmy's pizza (my favorite). All amazing and a great beer selection. Would highly recommend.

I've been with PEDU for about a year now and have enjoyed my experience so far. The class environment is very welcoming for all. The programming is challenging but if you put in the work you'll get results! Plus, Rachel is a rockstar coach who cares about everyone's progress!

Stopped in for a quick bite. Red Beans and Rice. Not a tough dish. Sat at the bar. Bartender comes over after 25 mins and says "Computer in Kitchen went down they have to hand write everything."  This is Red Beans and Rice. Everything is made way ahead of time.  Another 15 mins go by and I get a Luke warm bowl of beans, half slice sausage and a melon baller scoop of rice. What a joke. No apology, bartender thought it was funny. Screw the tourist, there is another one behind him. Bourbon St is fun, but don't come here to eat.

Amazing food! The bacon wrapped scallops are to die for! The staff is very friendly and the atmosphere is casual yet elegant enough to enjoy a romantic dinner or even bring out of town guests to try unique pizzas. The pizza is the best I ever had! Definitely a must try!

Tried it out for the first time since I've been craving Chinese so much and I can't believe I've never been before it's so close and convenient from my house & the food was yummy! I ordered the spicy mandarin chicken with fried rice not spicy really but so delicious  I ate it so fast I forgot the picture! Prices are decent too not spendy at all and it's very good portions!!  I went with my dad,brother, hubby & 3 yr old and they all enjoyed their dinners also! There's only one gal and we went right at the rush but she handled everyone so well. Be prepared to wait a little bit but we'll worth it! It will be my go to now!

Food was amazing. Nina our server was excellent! She spent time teaching our son how to crack his king crab and opened my lobster tail too.  Thanks so much, we will definitely be back on our next trip!  Highly recommend to others too!!!  Thanks Nina!

I wasn't looking forward to another upscale grocer in this area, but this one blows the others out of the water. Place is immaculate and selection is amazing. Was approached by someone in the beer area, requested if they had a certain beer, he said no but he knows it is available to order and he said he will order it next time...will see if that happens. 

Yes it is expensive, but they do have some good specials and the service is amazing.

Please make sure to tell your staff to wear their masks properly though, especially in the meat department handling fresh food where I saw a worker with a mask not covering his nose. Also, a lot of personal conversations between coworkers that probably shouldn't be had in front of customers...particularly by the entrance manning the line.

Authentic Brazilian buffet! This is by far the best Sunday brunch buffet I've had in the United States! Fresh salads, meats, fish and vegetation dishes, cheeses, chocolate and desserts! Brazilian bbq! The staff is super attentive. I'll be back....many times. Sunday there is also a buffet that focuses on Brazilian bbq where the waiters walk with slabs of meat- they will cut you a fresh piece at your table.

This is one of the few sushi places in the area that is open for lunch or snack time before dinner. Not sure why... But it makes for a convenient stop when a snack is needed.

This time I tried the dynamite roll. Yellow tail and tuna with kimchi. It's really not that spicy. Not at all. But they are generous with the amount of fish that is in the roll. It pleasantly was surprising. And it tasted good too!! Of course I also had to order the mango sticky rice... And yes it was a little different than others I've tried... But it was still very good. Also they give you a generous amount of mango!! Much appreciated! I love mango. It was sprinkled was a lot of sesame seeds... So be aware.

The service was very good and friendly. So very nice!! If I'm in the area again I'll be sure to stop by.

I used to donate to Goodwill regularly. Recently, they moved from Baring at Sparks to their current location. When I went to the new location I learned:

They only take small items.
They will not take furniture, stereos, or other hard items.
Their new storefront was completely stuffed full.
They were recently "bought" and are now managed from California.

Anyone will take knick knacks, doo dada, and gew gaws. Anyone will take clothing. I was bringing in stuff literally worth thousands of dollars and they said they could not take it.  So what use is a charity if they can't take stuff that's really worth something?

To the credit of the staff, they were apologetic about it. In fact they were probably thinking the same thing I was, only because they worked there they couldn't say anything.

I used to think Goodwill was the best because they took anything. Their old store was huge and they took TONS of stuff I brought in, much of it worth thousands.  Now someone else is going to get it.

This was so lame this year.  First of all, if you are going to sneak in vodka, which I didn't actually attempt this year, they go through your purse, so get the bra flasks or have your partner just put a flask in their pockets, or put it in your pockets.   The checking of the purse thing is so stupid when there are 101 ways to sneak in something.  You will want to sneak in booze rather than pay a ton of money for nasty drink choices, I think I could get red or white wine or Southern Comfort mixed drinks, I would rather die, I actually opted not to drink.  

Now this leads me to the dumbest thing ever, the placement of the portapottys-  I hate these things so much and its a chore to even piss in one for me, and of course they were 3 blocks away and this is after I found one close by and some snobby artist woman told me these were for artists only and was guarding it with her life.  I have never been so pissed off in my life.  Who was the genius who thought this awesome new layout for the bathrooms was a good one?  Probably the same person who thought Southern Comfort based drinks only was a good one to offer the public. Ridiculous.

Food was fine, nothing stood out but the ceviche from Milagro.   Will skip next year!

Good food but horrible customer service. They put queso in my bag after I told the cashier I did not want chips or queso. I was charged for it and there was no apologies. Manager was extremely rude. My son was there to witness and call him out on his rudeness. Only reason I'm giving it two stars is because the food was somewhat decent. Otherwise, this location don't deserve any. And chipotle should not have people like that working there.
Forget using your rewards because if you don't do it on your own before you order, they don't ask you or allow you to do it after.

Stopped by ChopHouse Grille on Friday night for appetizers and drinks. 
Pros: Beautiful atmosphere. They've really done a nice job with the interior. Outdoor bar with fire pit. Modern and elegant, but not stuffy.
Service: We sat at the indoor bar. Our bartender, Tim, was great. Attentive and made nice recommendations. The GM stopped by during our meal and asked us if everything was okay. The staff work together as a team and food came out of the kitchen very quickly on a busy Friday night. 
Cocktails/drinks: Creative and delicious. Thyme lemonade ($11) was tart and earthy/herbal. Irish mocha cold brew ($9) was like having a chocolate martini but only better. I like how they use their cold brew coffee in cocktails. They have good local beers on tap. 
Cons: This place is expensive! Drink prices are reasonable, but value for food is not. 
Food: Found the food to just only be okay. The kona filet tips ($17) were decent, but only a few pieces of meat and mostly the dish was made up of mushrooms. The crispy Brussels sprouts ($13) again were okay, chili sauce was pretty good, but not worth the price. Buffalo shrimp ($16) was your standard fare, nice with chunky blue cheese - but the shrimp seemed like they were sitting around for awhile because they were somewhat cold and soggy. 5 shrimp, standard size, for $16. Whipped ricotta ($12) was a nice option for dessert - because the ChopHouse does not offer a "real" dessert menu. Just dessert "shooters" for $3. This is always a good idea if you want to just have a small sweet treat after dinner - but ChopHouse would not be a good place to stop by if you were looking for dessert and and a cocktail. 
The place is new so certainly they are still working on their operations. ChopHouse is owned by the fine folks at The Pour House and PJ Whelihan's, so they are good restauranteurs and will figure it out. The food coming out of the kitchen looked really good and maybe we just ordered wrong. Go check out the place for yourself and if the weather is good sit at the outdoor bar area.

I wish I could give this 0 stars.My husband and I ate there the other night. We went there because in a mailer it said if you bring in the page, you would get one free meal when you bought another. When we got there they asked if we were there because of the coupon and when we said yes, she informed us that the add said with a reservation only. That info was written in such small print that you needed a magnifying glass to see it. To me it was a bait and switch tactic. We decided to go in to eat anyway. We had been there in the past and it was an OK place. Well, the other night it was horrible. I ordered salmon pinwheels that was stuffed with crab and spinach and my husband ordered pasta with shrimp and crab in a alfredo sauce. The person that waited on us turned out to be the owner. From the time he brought the salad, over 45 min passed and he never came back to the table. I had to ask another server to get him. I asked where our food was and he went to check. He told me the chef didn't like how the pinwheels came out so he was redoing them and had not communicated that to him. It then took about another 20 minutes before we got out food. The salmon pinwheels were horrible. the salmon was tough on the outside and hard to cut. The crab stuffing tasted like paste with some green specks in it. I couldn't taste crab or spinach. The inside part of the salmon was tasteless as well. I told the owner that it was terrible and he asked if I would like a salmon filet instead. When that was brought out, the menu said it was salmon with bourbon sauce. the salmon I got looked like a Mrs. Paul's frozen salmon filet complete with fake grill marks. There was no sauce at all but there was a lump of slimy crab on top of it. The salmon was dry and there was Cajun spices on it. It also had a strong fishy odor. After eating less than half, I decided that it tasted like old fish and left a bad taste in my mouth. My husbands pasta came out with a few fried shrimp that were a funny color and rubbery. The pasta was dry and the bottom of the bowl had melted butter, a ton of garlic, and clumps of parmesan cheese. It was one of the worst meals I've ever had in a restaurant. I wrote all of this on the owner's facebook page and he tried to defend himself and said all his fish was fresh (not) and the filet I got was the same fish that the pinwheels were made from which I know was not true, because the pinwheel salmon was light pink like atlantic salmon while the filet was dark orange like coho salmon. He even sent the check to use by another waitress. Basically whatever it says on the menu is not what you are going to get. Every time in the past that we were there the place has been almost empty. I don't know how this place is still open.It will be a long time before I ever go there again.

The moment I walked into Famous Tate I was greeted by a friendly salesperson Peter. He spent a good hour helping me put together the perfect package for my new kitchen. Not only were the prices great but they had rebates too. Peter explains all the rebates and even followed up with phone calls. When I did have a question and was in the store another person took time to help me as well. Finally one of the rebates sent an email with a question and when I went in and asked not only did Peter help but the manager Kim sat with me till the problem was resolved. Again the problem was with the rebate company. I will definitely go back to this store!!! Thanks to all at Famous Tate for making this large purchase less painful. Joanne G

Oh this custard is too good....you must come try it. Simple. Few real food ingredients. Rich. Perfect. The cookies are also delicious but we definitely come for the custard....if you need cookies for a party though this is a great option!! Will be back frequently!

Second review a year and 9 days later...
This place has gone to shit! 
No veggies except 2 pieces of broccoli and a crap ton of I think... cabbage. Asked for extra sauce Bc it was super dry last year. I was given TWO big sauces containers with a drop was than what comes in the TINY sauce container. WHY?! Smh i ordered THREE LARGE TERIYAKI bowls smh... really 2?? Now we all are stuck w dry teriyaki bowls. Smh 
This is the last time I will come here. It's gotten so crappy!! The owner really needs to talk with his staff and cool team.

We arrived at this facility on Saturday to attend a family affair. The above rating is for the following reasons.

Positive

The check in staff was courteous and efficient.
Our room was clean.
Their is a Starbucks in the lobby.

Negative

The room was quite dated.
During the night I was awakened by the toilet flushing in the room above us.
We waited at least 10 minutes before the valet appeared.
The food is beyond awful.
The cocktail food was cold and presented without garnish.
The dinner buffet food was cold at all stations.
The breakfast in the restaurant had stale sweet rolls and cold pancakes, eggs and soggy bacon.

We are happy we won't need to stay at this facility again.

I'm unable to eat dairy. Your page states you have ice cream and frozen yogurt, we are not from the area and was only staying over night. The cost of fuel and our time was wasted! You really should update your page so no one else leaves your establishment with a bad taste in their mouth!
This place is not open not sure if its certain days but they ned to change the schedule on times and don't bother calling the phone is out of service. Its closed as far as I'm concerned..

My friend and I decided we wanted steak for dinner. I live down the street and have heard great things since moving here about this place. We both opted for the Hawaiian Steak and it didn't disappoint! We shared the Caesar salad that has kale instead of Romain and has corn too. It was delicious as well! The key lime pie for dessert was also rather tasty! I recommend this place if you're looking for a nice steak dinner in a nice atmosphere!

There are a few iconic places in every city that you just kind of have to visit, and in the Nashville area Loveless Cafe is one of them.  This place went "viral" before the internet, convincing people to head out to a former motel in the middle of nowhere to indulge in biscuits and jam.

I will admit that I don't like to wait in lines, so I've been avoiding Loveless as a result.  I've heard sometimes the wait is up to two hours, and they don't take reservations for small parties.  But when my friend Lindsey and I were texting at like 7am about breakfast, we figured we could go super early and beat the church rush on a Sunday morning.  We were right; we barely had to wait, and you get to wander around their little stores while you do.  It's like an original Cracker Barrel in that regard.

The biscuits were AWESOME.  I loved them!  I tried all the jams they brought with them too.  For my breakfast, I went basic with scrambled eggs and crispy bacon, plus a small side of their hash brown casserole.  That cheesy goodness was so rich and heavy, I didn't even finish half of it!  I ate very well and enjoyed it a lot.

I'm not sure if I will be back to Loveless, unless a visitor or friend wants to go... it's about 20-25 minutes from where I live, and nothing else is nearby.  I liken it to eating at Lady & Sons in Savannah; it's a haven for tourists after so many appearances on Food Network and the like.  But it was definitely worth checking off my Nashville "bucket list"!

I'd they are in business, they were not when I walked a half mile to go here during their advertised business hours. 

Based on the appearance outside, it looks shut down.

Sorry, this review should have been put up Long ago!
I first had my Yamaha 150 2 stroke serviced here a year ago and, frankly, it ran better than when we first got the boat!!! Stunning! I think I'll only buy Yamaha since their service is so great. The service dept is Seriously punctual, thorough and they produce Great results. 
Keep it up and I'll never go elsewhere!

Outback Steakhouse in Cherry Hill was a total train wreck tonite (11/23). Not sure whether they were short staffed or what but getting seated even with the "call ahead" which is normally around 20-30 minutes was 45 minute wait tonite. The food took forever to come out and even drinks were slow. Just a suggestion:  if you know you are short staffed or everything is slow, tell your patrons. This way expectations are tempered.

So this was super fun! I'm not a huge prison fan or anything, but I highly recommend this as one of your stops if you visit Philly. Just the fact that the prison looks like a castle on the outside and the layout is in a spoke design is visually appealing. On top of that, this was also where Al Capone stayed!

Every entry comes with a self guided audio. If you do the audio tour only, it is 35 minutes. But if you want to do this place justice, give yourself at least 2 hours. I stayed for 2 hours and I was still not able to do the whole thing!

Tickets at the door is $16. But if you purchase online, you save $2. Since I'm money thrifty, I did a quick search for promo code and was able to get the ticket down to just $9 each. 

It's easily accessible using public transit. (That's how I got there!)

You definitely don't want to miss this attraction!
Very well put together pawn shop. Prices are very reasonable and the staff is super friendly. And the work that helped me (drew) was super helpful.

Great and fast service . Food was excellent and the prices were amazing . I ordered the spilt decision , it was DELISH ! I also ordered their new dish , fresh strawberry croissant filled with cream cheese , it was to die for . The coffee was great , my kids ordered the sliver five . They were 5 regular sized pancakes unlike New York which has the smaller size . The prices were so cheap , loved everything about ihop

I had Old Pueblo out for a regular clea out of our septic system. Manuel was efficient and knowledgeable and the price was fair. They recommended what I should do to keep the system running smoothly in the future. I would highly recommend.

Came here for the first time today.  Clam Chowder was very good and so were the conch fritters.  The salad was wilted and some brown lettuce (more iceberg) than any thing else.  It was hot like it literally had just been sitting in the hot kitchen for a while.  I ordered the combo platter with clam strips and coconut shrimp with a side of coleslaw.  The clam strips were good and the coleslaw was good as well.  The Coconut shrimp was regular boxed shrimp no coconut what so ever.  Waitress tasted it herself and took it back to the kitchen.  She was polite and apologetic and offered to bring me something else but I declined and did eat the clam strips.  They didn't take the "coconut shrimp" off my bill but I didn't say anything else just paid the bill and left and since the owner (and chef) who was there didn't even bother to come out and address this I won't be back.  Unfortunately not a good experience.

This is too funny a story not to share. My husband made a reservation for our first wedding anniversary. He noted, "If there is a table by the window, we would appreciate it." The day before the reservation, we received the confirmation call. We confirmed. The day of, we received a second confirmation call. We again confirmed. The manager said, "By the way, we have the table by the window for you. Happy Anniversary!"

Fast forward four hours. We walk in to another couple sitting in the window seat. We asked about our window seat and were told that Niche takes requests for special seating but cannot make guarantees. Odd given that Niche had called us proactively to let us know we had it hours before. But, oh well. What happened next was amazing. The manager brought over champagne to apologize, but instead of simply saying sorry and wishing us a Happy Anniversary, she proceeded to say, "Our most regular customers came in and asked for the table. You understand... you can't really say no to customers who have been here 317 times." 

As we sat there letting it sink in, we became increasingly incredulous:

1. Niche knew it was our anniversary.

2. They clearly gave away our table on purpose. 

3. They then tell us explicitly we aren't valued customers!

4. And by implication, of the two couples, we were clearly the only ones with reservations.

Since they didn't care about us being there, we took our anniversary din elsewhere. And it was fab.

PS. Interesting to note that I am the Duchess of Brasserie by Niche on Yelp (where we eat at least 3 times a month)...so I guess we actually were very much regulars at one of their establishments.

Cool-looking space. Food was great. I had chicken and cornmeal pancakes. The friendly owner chatted with me for quite a while about his experience opening the restaurant. Good people. The menu is very limited- a handful of items, presumably because they are so new.

I love this place. It's got a big back room with comfy booth seating. The food is creative and comforting, nice presentation, excellent service, cool soundtrack that's kept at a nice low volume, super reasonable prices. I keep coming back.

Neighborhood feel, with regulars coming in and out. Lots of good banter. The food was solid. Bottomless coffee that was drinkable. Good roasted potatoes. Fried egg cooked the way your mother intended (even when your mother couldn't cook). The decor could use some serious freshening up. But it's a rock solid breakfast alternative.

We had Jerrys Kitchen cater a corporate event last month in our NJ office and it went off without a hitch. Food was AMAZING, service was professional and communication was on point. 
Would definitely use their catering services again and can highly recommend to all in the tri state area.

I love goose the market. They have great selection of meats, cheese, and condiments. Go downstairs to find an awesome selection of beer and wine. 

This past week i had the pleasure to sample the meat and cheese platter with a tasty Australian sparkling beer. All the meat and cheese selections were unique things I've never tried and most were locally made.  There are also wonderful sandwiches and gelato. I find something new and fun to try every time I stop by this Indy gem.

This place is a JOKE!!!!! 
Do yourself a favor and go Elsewhere. ANYWHERE ELSE!

They are unprofessional, Inept and rude!!!!


I commissioned a custom cushion.
