My bride had a slice with sausage, and each of the men had a slice of pepperoni. The pizza is amazing: great sauce with just enough cheese. The dough is super thin and cooked perfectly, and the flavor and texture are very traditional. It's tough to nail the flavor of New York pizza pie, but these guys take a good run at it.

So why the 3 stars?  We ordered 3 slices and some garlic cheese bread. The bread was decent, but came out after the slices and I'm a little picky about making multiple trips to the counter for my order. It would have been nice to have everything come out at once. Again, if you've ever read on of my reviews, you know I am a stickler about customer service and even though it is understandable they might be grumpy due to the heat; I'm scoring the store and not the individuals so they get dinged for not providing a comfortable work place as well.

I say get your pie to go but be prepared to wait knowing it will be worth it when you grab a slice. 3 out of 5 is not that bad, you have to almost kill somebody to get a lower score.  

We'll go back when the temperature outside drops a little.
This is the best steakhouse I visited .Great food.Great personal.Nice atmosphere.Higly recommend this restaurant.Will come back again.

Worth traveling from very far. Having this in our town is such a treat. The quality of their bakery and bagels are up to par with top bakeries in NY. When I lived in the area full time I stopped in at least 3 times a week! This place is what I look forward to most when visiting the area.

I took a friend here this past weekend. I go to tasting menus every chance I get, but, for my friend, it was her first tasting menu.
This night there were 12 courses and we chose the drink pairing that was mostly wine.
There are several comments on the food already posted.  All I will say here is that my friend and I agree with the people who thought the food was excellent.
The evening began with the seating and the basic questions about what drinks we wanted and if we had any allergies.  The two chefs fixed our food in front of us.  Then we got our drink pairing and description (excellent pairings).  Next, we got our food followed by a description of the course.  Everyone was polite and patient as we asked our questions.  
This is definitely a meal worthwhile and, hopefully, I will get a chance to return.

Went here for lunch and came back at night because I loved it so much. Then we came back again for drinks BECAUSE IT IS JUST SO SOLID. We met the bartender that created the cocktails menu the first night, and let me tell you- they make their own peach purée! Now I'm all for the drinks with like 8 ingredients including egg whites or cynar or whatever, but these drinks are solid without all that fuzz. 
I got the burger with all the fixins and couldn't have been happier. I know some other reviews say some bogus about "bland food" but if you know savory food you'll be sure to appreciate this stuff. My roommate got the chicken burger-type dish and that was "the juiciest chicken ever". And my burger was SO GOOD. 
Please give this place your business because it is literally my new favorite bar on MorganFord.


Update: Was literally JUST TOLD that the wings are "amazing"- by my friend that LOVES WINGS! So get those

Three Pickles... You're fine. You're doing good. You're not special though, besides your hours, those are special. Not too many businesses get away with being open for such a short amount of time, but I get it, being tucked into a business park. 

Work brought me into the area, lunch brought me into Three Pickles. The staff was the crown jewel of the place. They were funny and energetic, joking with each other, genuinely smiling, and keeping up with a decent lunch rush. I had a veggie sub, really disappointed in the bread. It's basically as exciting as Subway's white bread. 

I didn't get a pickle, which I now regret after reading all the rave reviews about them. :-(

The toppings on the sub were generous, not Mother Theresa generous but definitely more than Subway's Scrooge portions. (Sorry for comparing you guys with Subway, but as a Sandwich shop you gotta feel where I'm coming from.)

I hope to come back here honestly, even if it's only to try a home made pickle.

This place either need new management or it need to be shut down..

The staffs here are just a bunch of lazy underpaid  employees with nasty attitudes and terrible costumer service.

Disorganized and basically trashed with random clothes everywhere.
 
I've been in there a few times, only for  "active wear" clothes, and every time I ask for help to locate a certain 
Style/size the employee would just point his/her finger from across the store and say "check over there" or "let me see" and disappear for awhile and don't come back.
We waited for 30 minutes to get a wedge burger.  It wasn't that busy, maybe 50% capacity.  Ordered without cheese,  it came with cheese.  Didn't want to wait another 30 minutes so we left.

My boyfriend and I went to Bliss for our anniversary.  I was hesitant because I normally don't like expensive restaurants or fancy food, and the "casually elegant" dress code threw me off.  

The dining room was relatively small and plainly decorated.  We were seated along the wall.  My seat faced the windows, which were all open to allow in the breeze (which was nice), but the street lights were very bright, so it was difficult to look across the table.  If there had been a shade to pull down even just a few inches, it would have been wonderful.  

The food was incredible.  We ordered the short rib ravioli for our appetizer.  The beef was so tender, and the pasta was delicious.  Then we each ordered the filet mignon with mascarpone hash brown, sauteed brussel sprouts, and black bean puree.  The filet was cooked to perfection.  For dessert we had the creme brulee, which was probably somewhere in the top 5 best creme brulees I've ever had. 

As for drinks, I had the strongest long island iced tea of my life.  It made me physically recoil at first.  I also had a chocolate martini with dessert, which was to die for. 

I'd definitely recommend Bliss to anyone looking to celebrate a special occasion, but I think the prices are a bit high for a normal night out.
Highly recommend it, the food was amazing. I love the beef noodle and summer roll a lot .

Do you want personal attention?  Please go to the bar at Clear Sky.  Personal, good time, bartenders like, Nick S,Get to know you, feed to your wants and cater to your needs .  Great conversation with locals at the bar, refreshing drinks, abundant food options to choose from, sweet eats and memories!

I enjoy hanging out with friends watching Sunday Night Football at BWW, not because it's a great place, but because I have good friends.  There are some things about BWW that really bug me.  Back in 2004 my friends and I started going to BWW in Rivergate every Sunday Night for NFL football from pre-season to playoffs.  A few years later this location was closed and the Hendersonville one was opened.  Since that time they've declined in several ways.  First, they increase their prices multiple times throughout the year, and they are overpriced on almost everything they sell.  Second, they got rid of Coca Cola products and I hate Pepsi.  I refuse to pay $3 for a Pepsi.  Third, their appetizer prices are too high and some just downright outrageous.  How can they charge $8 for a side of onion rings????  Fourth, they advertise themselves as a great place to watch sports yet most times we go they are playing the juke box and don't have the sound on for games.  On Sunday Nights we have to request them to turn on the NFL game and turn off the juke box. Sunday Night Football is usually the most watched NFL game of the week yet whenever we ask for them to turn it on the server asks, "What game is it?"  We show up at 7:00 pm and we often see on the TVs shows like The Simpsons, and rugby games.  That's fine as long as you're also showing the major things such as Sunday Night Football.  Rarely does the game get turned on in time for the kickoff.  We most always miss the first few minutes and even when it is turned on, a lot of times the sound is not on.  

There was one time several years ago a very large group of us went in May to watch hockey and basketball playoff games.  Half of us were watching the Blackhawks playoff game and the other half was there to watch the Cavalier's playoff game.  About an hour into our time there the lights came down and EVERY screen was switched to the same channel for a UFC fight.  I asked the manager to put the two TVs by our table back to the games we were watching but he refused saying "We paid $600 for this pay-per-view and we're not changing it".  I complained saying we came here to watch the playoff games and were still eating our meals.  If BWW planned on forcing everyone to watch UFC they should have posted signs on the door at least an hour ahead of time because we would have left and gone somewhere else.  We definitely wouldn't have ordered food.  He didn't care, but thankfully the GM overheard my conversation and came up to me later agreeing to give us our two TVs.  

One more thing.  For years and years BWW didn't allow paying a tip from your BWW gift card.  No problem, just leave cash on the table.  Well a few years ago my son was using his BWW gift card my wife and I gave him at Christmas.  He used his card for his food and I left a cash tip.  The next Sunday Night when we were there my son was told he didn't have enough on the card for the full amount of his order.  He still had his receipt from the week before showing he did in fact have enough.  The manager was called over and looked into it.  He went back to the computer to look up the previous week's transaction.  He came back and said the order the week before had a $4 tip added.  I explained that was wrong and asked how it could be if tips weren't even allowed on gift cards.  He said that policy was recently changed and I told him the server from the previous week then stole from my son because we left cash on the table and didn't put it on the card.  The manager didn't care and said there wasn't anything he could do.  I pressed the issue because I was mad someone stole from my son like that. He agreed to knock $2 off my son's bill - WHAT A JOKE. Since then I haven't bought another gift card from there.  Our group only now comes for regular season games.  We stopped coming for pre-season and we usually skip playoff games.  It's just not the sports place they claim to be.  Now that there are other options for watching sports my friends and I are seriously considering making a change for future NFL seasons.

There's a great selection of hard to find Korean groceries here and the food is amazing. It's seriously like being let into your Korean friend's house for dinner. There's homemade quality but amazing taste. Come here and try it!

For starters you forgot one of my burritos. Second you gave me the wrong drink. Third my three tacos have basically nothing on them! They were so thin, I will post a picture. 
Seriously GET IT TOGETHER! Change up management! This is the worst tacobell I've been to in the entire United States!  I will post a picture of the taco you served me.

Palomino is an outstanding place to eat, with interesting and pleasing decor and food that will make your mouth very happy that you went there.

While this is not St. Elmo's, or a Shula's, the steak is still outstanding.

Dress nicely, and be prepared to spend $50 per person before drinks, but definitely bring your appetite as the food is outstanding.

I am visiting from another state and took my son, daughter in law and 4 month old out. We picked this place because of the good reviews. The staff was very helpful and courteous.  Unfortunately, the food was barely warm and not worth the money. I will say the beet salad was very good, but the mac and cheese was not cooked and the oysters could not be found in the breading...literally no oyster. The fondue cheese was hot but the veggies(brussel sprouts were raw) etc were barely warm.
If you want a REAL cheesesteak, this is your place. I went to college in philly...this is the real deal.  I like the the "pizza steak wit" (whiz of course)! Enjoy!!

We went for the first time for lunch today and were bowled over at how good it is.  IMO, the best we've had in Reno.  We went because while shopping recently at Asian Market, the young man said they'd opened this restaurant.  We asked if they had a "special" menu and they do.  Not the same-old, same-old for which we were grateful.  We got bean curd with pork belly and spicy fried duck tongue.  Both were terrific.  The pork belly was melt in your mouth tender and plenty of it.  The duck tongues were tiny, little things, much smaller than the only other time we'd had them in the San Gabriel Valley at dim sum.  We just chewed on them til there was a little bone to get rid of.  LOADS of dried red peppers to navigate around.  We intend to work our way through the special menu and some of the other dishes, including the jook.  This is an attractive, modern looking place with plenty of light.  I can't find a single thing to criticize about it.  Welcome to them.

My experience here was very mediocre, but my girlfriend who had Manuel as her nail tech got an awesome pedicure. He really cared about what he was doing. My lady did just enough to say she put all the product on me she's supposed to and then painted my toes. Long story short... ask for Manuel.
Quit impressed for american style restaurant. Everything we had was amazing from the chip and verde salsa to the pork tamale  and pastor/chorizo tacos. Will absolutely be coming back.

My wife, daughter and I stopped in today. We were looking for somewhere that wasn't a greasy diner. Found this place. It was really nice. The people were friendly, the food was very good. The ladies had smoothies and chocolate croissants. I has espresso and an egg, cheese bacon bagel. Everything was delicious. We will definitely go there again.
The food was amazing!!! It's a hidden gem but I will definitely be back! Best bbq I've had in awhile!!

Hands down, the absolute best place in the area to get your nails done. Carol is the most amazing manicurist I have ever had. My cousin and I both love her. She is really detail oriented, asks every step of the way if everything is okay, and never fails to impress. Seriously, the first time I ever went, she did a pinterest design for that looked identical to the picture. She's awesome.

The prices are also ridiculously affordable. It is so much cheaper than I am used to in Center City and, unlike in the city, I never feel rushed. I am also a really awkwardly quiet person and for me to say I feel comfortable here (which I do), says a lot about the salon as a whole.

Went to Bacio last night with the family, its  a cute little spot in mount airey that we drove past the other day.. We arrived and it looked promising. We started with baked gnocchi which wasn't baked rather a pasta plate with Cream sauce and spinach and the capresae salad which lacked balsamic vinegar a key part to a capresae salad... But don't worry the lack of balsamic was covered with salt..  
They messed up my moms salad twice an ten the chief sent over a plate of something that no one not even the servers knew what it was.. The chef ended up telling us it was stuffed peppers (which were okay) and a zucchini corn cake which was nasty.. 
The dinners were surprisingly good I got pesto which was way to creamy for pesto but I mixed it with tomato sauce which made it good, and the ravioli was delicious.. The portion size is HUGE though I swear we brought a freezer home with us... 
The service is another story.. It took 45 minutes to get our appetizer and after that another hour till our dinner.. My brother ended up being late to the party he was going to... We decided that would be our only trip to Bacio due to the bad bread and bad service..

I bought 2 Groupons to use at Famous Dave's and wanted to use one of them.  We were greeted at the door by a woman that was obviously mentally disabled.  She opened the door and we walked in.  There was not a hostess at the hostess stand nor did we see anyone near by.  We walked into the bar area and sat ourselves at a table.  A few minutes later a young woman walks up and plops 2 menus down and says "just so you know for next time, you don't seat yourself in the bar area only if you're sitting at the bar".  I told her there was no one at the front when we walked in.  She said "I saw you, I was getting there as fast as I could".  No, darlin', we looked in the dining room and saw not a soul.   Couldn't believe her rudeness.  Bartender comes over to take our drink order and I asked to see the manager.  She shows up and I explained to her what her hostess said to me.  Manager apologized and compared the girls behavior to her 15 year old daughter making a joke about it.  A few minutes later she returned with a basket of deep fried onion slivers in an attempt to  make up for her rude hostess.  We ordered our lunch which took a long time to arrive.  The manager came by and asked how we were doing. I asked her if she talked to the hostess and she said that the girl said, "I didn't mean it that way" and blew it off. The manager told us that she was a really nice person and once again compared her to her 15 year old daughter.  Our food finally arrived and it was all room temperature!  Manager came by again and we told her our food was cold.  She said, "I need to go back there and yell at people, I guess".  In the meantime, I was trying to pull up the Groupon on my cell phone with no coverage in that particular building.  I went outside to the parking lot trying to get reception.  On my way out, there was no one at the hostess stand.  I had to come and go 4 times trying to get reception.  All 4 times, there was no one at the hostess stand.  One time, I did see the manager and the hostess sitting in the take out area laughing and talking.  This brings me back to the rude hostess that chewed us out for seating ourselves.  Finally, we got the Groupon number and got the hell out of there.  That was such a miserable experience!  You have a lazy hostess with an attitude and a manager trying to be their best friend.  I will be cancelling my second Groupon for Famous Dave's because we won't be going back!

Cafe Patachou has been my favorite breakfast cafe for the last 4 years. I am always looking for new places to try and Patachou still always comes out on top. I favorite meal is the Broken Yolk Sandwich. So simple, yet so delicious. If you have a sweet tooth, the waffle is also a must! I have been to 4 different locations and they all have great service and great food. The atmosphere is perfect for a weekend brunch with friends or family.

Came across this gem purely by accident and decided to check it out. Great decision.
The interior is modern functional and what a French bistro should look like.
We worked our way through the menu, slowly but surely. we started of with Sparkling Mineral water, the Parisian cocktail and the baguette with butter. That alone was delicious... I think I could have eaten a whole loaf of this bread.
Then we indulged in the onion soup, I mean how could you not go for it, since this is a French place. The soup was delicately flavored, the croutons crunchy and buttery. It was a bit more dry than the inon soups you can generally find in this country and also not drowned in gobs of melted cheese, more like a hint of quite flavorful cheese. 
We tried both the meat and the cheese plate and were amazed by both.
I went on to try the crepes with sugar and butter while my friend enjoyed the duck medalions. We were impressed by both dishes.
We topped off the evening with the chocolate ganache cake, which was seved still warm out the oven and filled with ganache which spilled out once the cake was pierced. We also had the chocolate mouse with fresh berries and Chantilly cream... OMG... served in a glass container with lid... so rich, so chocolatey, so decadent one simply has to lick the dish to get every last trace of this....
I am not French, but I am from Europe and I deem the food served here quite authentic and a definite 'must try' for all...

I wanted to add, that while their menu seems rather limited, it does have choices for all tastes and budgets available. 
And our waitress Camille was a gem, friendly and attentive.
Have eaten here numerous times. Aside from being very reasonably priced for sushi, the fish is ALWAYS fresh and delicious. In my opinion, good sushi had to be consistently fresh. Love this place
Great place with affordable sushi. Gotta love a BYOB & the staff is quick to open and chill your beverage. Always ask for a free beer. They want you to!

This was an amazing dining experience. We were celebrating a birthday. All of my friends got different entrees, so we got to try a few things. I personally had the "chicken kabob with yogurt." Seriously amazing. Rich, but delicious flavor. 
I tried the zucchini pancakes, too, which were so good! Perfect sear. 
We had the combo appetizer: several spreads for pita bread. I love restaurant pita bread! I cannot find an equivalent in grocery stores here...
We also had three desserts: the kunnefe (I think thats what it was called); the baklava; and the chocolate pistachio cake. My favorite was the chocolate cake-but I guess the kunnefe is supposed to be the best. It is goat cheese with kind of a breading on it. My friend Kait, who doesn't love desserts, actually really liked it. 
Our server was amazing. Very kind and funny and fit well with our group. 
We noticed a table getting what looked like shots, so of course we asked what shots they were doing; it was tea. :)
BTW, there is a free tea with yelp check-in. 

Very fun place, yet excellent food. We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves.

Love this place! Love their crépes. Always have super friendly service. I always order the Heavenly Chocolate Delight. And it is both heavenly and delightful! All other crépes don't stand par to these.

Valentines day dinner with my wife.  Great ambiance on a great little Main St.. The arugula salad was fantastic, except for the prosciutto wasn't great.  The buffalo shrimp appetizer was awesome.  My lobster ravioli and the sauce was spectacular.
Best place in town! I won't go anywhere else! Quality work. Friendly staff. You won't be disappointed!

Olive Garden of Greek Food!  Food Factory and impersonal. Second generation Greek myself  - so unfortunate experience - truly was excited to eat at Estia for the first time. . New to Philadelphia and had high hopes..not returning!  If you want a Chili's or Olive Garden franchise like experience - eat at Estia. Sad.
One of our favorite spots at Indian Rock Beach. We come at least twice each trip here, I have the snapper, it was wonderful, my wife have the 6 oz. Filet,  so tender you could cut it with spoon.

Wow, terrific PIZZA and great Italian dinners. My wife and I have been here several times since they opened. The pizza is one of the best in this Palm Harbor area, the crust is the KEY to a great pizza, leftovers reheat easy and the topping are fresh. My wife had baked stuffed shells and saidd they were great. I had a stromboli one day for lunch and couldn't beleave all the cheese filling, it was baked to perfection. The salad greens are fresh and not wilted, if you like a Greek salad this is one of the best. Great food, great and friendly service and moderate priced. Nice family restaurant.

The food was actually pretty good considering it was my first time ever. However, the chicken was so hot that I couldn't enjoy it. I was pretty sure I had mild, but I think it was a mixed up order. I want to try them again soon to see what else they may have, but I'm such a chicken wing person I was hoping to really enjoy this.

Food was great. Right on bourbon street and an agreeable contrast to the madness outside. Our waiter, brad (i think) was cheery and accommodating. Got the free appetizer with yelp and all went smoothly. Skewered shrimp, Charbroiled oysters, alligator po boy, and a Cajun spiced bowl of steamed mussels with andouille sausage. All reasonably priced. Highly recommended if you're a seafood fan.

Great place for brunch.
Strong bellinis and a lot of diversity on the menu... I do wish they had crepes on the menu. I mean, it's New Orleans! 


Enjoy,

Isaac.

5 stars considering the intel I got on this dive: It's the oldest public house in Philadelphia, which means this is where Ben Franklin used to drink. I could only wish they had a regular who dresses up period costume

... or something to mask the smell. What's with me and alleyway entrances? I guarantee the smell was not from the alley; it emanated from within. CRAZY that we still went inside the dark, yet lively place for a Friday night. Good thing a sign was lit indicating the second floor bar was open. There should be a Monopoly card that reads, 'Go directly upstairs, and collect your sense of smell'. A sense that is worth far more than $200. 

A few TV screens broadcasted NCAA games and a pro NBA match-up. Villanova has been on fire this year! Music was of the vintage college variety: Dave Matthews, Journey ... even Michael Jackson. I've never seen people start dancing to 'Man in the Mirror'. My friends have always found it an introspective song. Still I prefer that title to 'Ben & Me'.  

Though the actual bar was crowded, a friendly guy on the end made space for us to order: Jameson on the rocks in honor of the record number of Irish bars I've seen in one city. Does the count rival Boston? Only one way to find out; another trip! Not sure what Manoj ordered, but he said it was a house specialty like a Guinness knockoff. 

We weren't here long since Mitchell called and we went to meet up. This was a fun place aside from the first smell. BTW I was told this place has karaoke 3x a week; that's quite frequent programming unless you own a system at home! I really like the old timey neon sign

I've loved their pizza and wings since they were at their old location. And you can order online with the Slice app! 

Great food and service.

We got to the venue at 10:30. Being out-of-towners, we didn't know what time the band would start and finish. So, we walked in the front door and the doorman asked if we had tickets, which we didn't. He said that'll be$20. 

We really wanted to see The Steeldrivers, but were hesitant to spend $20 each if the show was half way over. The doorman (Nelly) insisted that they had just started their first set, so we decided to go on in. 

By the time we got a drink and found a table, the band finished and the place was cleared out! 10:50. The waitress agreed that it was ridiculous that we had just been coaxed into paying $20 for the tail end of the show and that we should go see Nelly to express our concern. 

When I mentioned it to him, he just laughed and said, "well, they didn't take a break." I said, "you told us they had just started." He shrugged. We left unhappy.

Nelly is a liar.
We thought it was yummy!!  My daughter got grilled chicken with chips & cheese dip - soo good!! We will definitely go back!  Only wish they took Amex.

I wanted to try this restaurant because I consider myself to be an adventurous eater, and really love trying out new places. Unfortunately, Maypop didn't really pan out for me. The actual restaurant is beautiful, and the service was excellent, but the reason we came to the restaurant, the food, was underwhelming. My boyfriend and I came for Coolinary Week, which allowed you an appetizer, entree and dessert for $36 a person. Probably the only meal we both truly enjoyed was the salad, which was very good. After that, everything was either bland or just not tasty. Overall, I'm glad we tried it, but we won't be back.

I was introduced to Dulce because I accompanied one of my friend's to her cake tasting for her wedding.  The owner, Juanita, is a fabulous hard working lady.  Even though she was clearly extremely busy she had no problems sitting down with us, giving us several options, even letting us taste things that were not on the cake tasting menu.  Unlike many places she was actually making suggestions that could help the bride and her family SAVE money instead of encouraging her to pay for things she didn't need.  That's before I tried the first sample.  I'm addicted to her cupcakes.  I've gone back several times and no matter the time of day the service is always great and the cupcakes are always awesome.  I'm getting married soon and I already know she'll be doing the cake.

I have eaten there 4 times now because my coworkers keep wanting to go back. 2 times I couldn't eat it because it was nothing but salt. The third time it was just ok and the 4th time 5 hours after I ate it I felt like I had food poisoning. I will never go back.

The burgers and fries are always fresh and delicious, but you'll have to wait for them. Even if you're the only customer in the restaurant, you will wait a questionable amount of time. This location is grossly over-staffed which leads to staff boredom which leads to unprofessional behavior. One of the times I was waiting for my food, two of the staff were loudly complaining about another customer calling him/her "a disgusting person." The owner is lucky they are the only Five Guys close by. Expect truly terrible service.

This place was sooo good--foodwise. I'll definitely go back there to eat. They had the best fajitas that I've had in a restaurant (and I'm from Texas!). The steak fajitas were cooked medium rare and so flavorful and delicious. The chapulini (grasshopper) tacos were really good, though they got spicy towards the end (I'd asked the waited if they were spicy, he said no, but I thought so). The corn was also phenominal, and my  friend loved her enchiladas. 

The service was just okay, though, because they were busy and looked short staffed. It took about 10 minutes before we got our drink orders and about 10 more to get them, but they were busy, so it was understandable.  We had the happy hour skinny margaritas which may have been a mistake because they tasted really watered down.  I think usually those are just made with more juice instead of sugar, but these didn't taste much like margaritas. But they were cheap, and so was the food, so I'll definitely be back.

Well the food is "alright" being a mexican i give it a solid 4 out of 10 i was disappointed to hear that they only have one kind of salsa. That should of been enough to run out the door. Like what?????But i give it the benefit of the doubt. Sad to hear that they are the same owners as mission taco that place is amazing! Just go to mission taco and avoid disappointment. Simple!
Love this place!  Food is always fresh, elegantly presented and the service is impeccable!  Oh and the price is just right 50% off sushi everyday!!

This place has the worst customer service. They continually talk among themselves as you are standing there waiting for them to take your order. They give you dirty looks while you're watching them. This was the worst Lee's hoagie location. I will never return ... wouldn't recommend. 
Jenkintown location is the best!!!
Tai Lake is one the gems in Chinatown. You can't beat the freshness of the seafood and the authenticity of the cuisine.

Last night was my first time having dinner here. It was for my little sister's birthday and let me tell you this place is amazing. We had a group of 14 with a reservation and were seated passed our reservation time but we were just waiting for the table to free up. The staff were very pleasant and very accommodating. 

On to the cuisine, the fish of the night was yellowtail tuna so I definitely had to try the yellowfish tuna crudo appetizer. An appetizer good for two to share, the tuna looked fresh and was accompanied with slices of bread and diced mushrooms and a bed of yummy sauce. All together this dish tasted heavenly. 

For the main dish I ordered the grilled hanger steak and fries and my sister ordered the duck breast with Parmesan crusted cauliflower and spinach. The meat was cooked to our liking which was medium. There was a definite balance of flavors, not too salty at all.  

The service was excellent and very accommodating. My sisters boyfriend had brought a cake from outside vendor and they were open to storing it for us. And when it came time for the birthday song they came out with candles. They also cut the cake and served it for us. Awesome crew last night! Definitely will eat here again. Oh almost forgot we had the Pimm's spritz cocktail which was also delicious.

This place used to be good. 5-6 years since it opened it has the feel of a neglected dump on the downhill slide toward extinction. Which it well deserves. It has devolved into the 2nd rate student-level food-to-drink-with joint like The Italian Pie that preceded it in this location. It's filthy (not just dirty), in dire need of a facelift, new menu and new staff. Our family had the worst service we've ever had at any restaurant in New Orleans. Waited over an hour for pizza (think about that), the order came out wrong, and at different times. The final person's order arrived after everyone else at the table had finished eating. A complaint to the manager was greeted by a dumb stare and a barely mumbled apology. Reginelli's is only a couple of blocks away with the same food done better in a clean, friendly, and efficient environment.

I went to NOTO for the first time, I wanted to check it out since I've heard so many "great" things about it. Long story short, it was wack as hell, the dj played way too much house music and not as much hip hop. I went in there tipsy af expecting a good time, but that house music sobered me up real quick. There was also a security guard next to the stage that was a douche, giving people nasty looks all night, like do your job and stop checking out other girls asses. You know it's wack if the dance floor isn't even 50% full, sorry NOTO, you disappointed me. I don't want to say this, but Rumor is a better club, even though it's so played out.

My family was very excited to have our Easter dinner at the William Penn Inn but were extremely disappointed. Each person was charged over $50 for a mid level hotel buffet style dinner only to find tasteless everything including old mini deserts.  The space was packed in and the noise level uncomfortable.

But the real problem was the service - obviously they, the owners/management, had booked big time so the wait staff they had to hire were untrained and very unprofessional temps who preferred to talk in small groups and ignore our attempts to get their attention to the point where we had to walk across the large room to order drinks from the service bar and remove our own dirty plates.

Really disappointed.

My mom and I went to Kane`s over the weekend. My mom wanted to look around at couches. She has major back problems and the current couch she has is no longer comfortable. We went in with no intention of buying anything. However, the sales guy Josh was extremely amazing. Not once did he pressure us, nor did he act like a sales guy. He was just there answering our questions, Sat down with us, made us feel so comfortable that my mom decided to get the couch that day. If anyone it's looking for furniture I would in a heart beat send then to Josh. Great job!!

LOVE IT! LOVE IT! LOVE IT! That really is all I need to say about SLAM. This is one of those fine jewels of the city that makes St. Louis great. The Art Museum features multiple levels of traditional and modern art including sculptures, tribal masks, impressionist paintings including Monet, contemporary art, classic artwork , and more! And it's all FREE!!!!! Well, outside of the featured exhibition but even that's free on Fridays so you can't beat it! SLAM Underground is also a newer initiative that provides a party at the Museum on the last Friday of the month. There's live music, DJs, an art DIY project, and cash bar which serves as a great opportunity to meet with friends for a cool ladies night, or a nice date, or a fun family night. PLUS IT'S FREE!!!!! This museum is a treasure and anyone who lives in this city and chooses not to visit it should really be ashamed of themselves. You don't know what you're missing!
Food was really good, service on the other hand was horrible.The atmosphere is awesome but I probably won't be back...and yeah the service was that bad.
Happy hour made for a happy tummy. The sizzling rice soup and Hawaii roll were excellent.
Clean, hearty food with excellent veg options and delicious meat dishes. Their injira is excellent; fluffy and moist, perfectly spongy.

The sandwich is tasty, but it's just too much filling for the bread their use. My sandwich completely fell apart when I first picked it up - because of the moisture from the filling, the bread gets soggy and breaks
 I ended up taking home the meat that fell off the bread, but I'd rather have it in my sandwich. Maybe they could use a different bread. It's a good sandwich, though.

We stopped here for lunch.  Our waitress Suzie was very polite attentive and friendly.  I had the grouper sandwich and he had the fish tacos.  We both enjoyed our meals very much.  My husband for the coleslaw as a side.  It had mandarin oranges.  He said it was delicious.

I went for lunch with my husband and son. We were looking forward to trying it based on their reviews. Disappointed to say the least! My food was oily and flavorless. Yuck! My husband and son ordered the sesame chicken. It was more like sweet and sour chicken with sesame seeds on top. My son took two bites and was done and he eats just about anything. Two stars based on the fried rice tasting better than our chicken. We won't be going back. Big bummer since we made a drive from the NW side of town. So not worth it!
Weak beer selection, too many yuppies and hipsters, and awful service (very pretentious). The usually have good crowds, decent margaritas, and really good empanadas.

This place is one of my favorites!  I just had Vietnamese in L.A. at 2 places highly regarded and neither were as tasty as this place!  I especially love their Bahn Mi prk sandwich, their #49, 50 & 51 (Rice vermacelli dishes), their Filet Mignon Curry and Golden crispy noodles, smoothies/slushies are awesome too!

What can I possibly say that may add or subtract from the hundreds of other previous reviews? 
Lines...oh the lines...snag a seat if you see one ASAP regardless of how many people you have with you...you can share the space...1 seat was plenty for the 4 of us. 
Food...be prepared to order when you sit....the roast pork with broccoli rabe and provolone is the tourist choice. It was ok...bread did tend to get a little soggy but the ingredients were enough to make up for it. Roast Beef was mezz-mezz...
Service...don't expect conversation or suggestions...they are all business. 
Overall...so/so experience...all hype, worth a try and move on. ..you're better off going to Tony Lukes for their Roasted Pork sandwich...to die for...seriously.

In a word "FUN" !!

What's not to love in 45 mph karts and 14 laps around a 1/4 mile track & it's all INDOORS.
You can race and just have fun or actually focus and try for your best lap times. 
A details print out of your performance is offered after every race.

It's pretty safe and the staff is really helpful and friendly.

 Best of all, is the League nights... usually the first Tue of the month. Some pretty skilled drivers show up and is a good place to see how you stack up.

THE MOST DISAPPOINTING FOOD/SERVICE/STAFF EVER. 

We ordered dinner from this place at 10 PM. The minimum price order was so high we had to order food we didn't want. Then they called us 20 minutes later to tell us that the food we DID want wasn't even available. After this call we waited 1.9 hours for our food. After giving them a 20 percent tip for delivery they didn't even have the decency to walk up to our dorm and instead made us walk 5 minutes in the rain to get the food. As if that wasn't enough the man told us that it wasn't his fault because we ordered so late (MORE THAN 2 HOURS BEFORE THE RESTAURANT CLOSED) and that he was sorry he couldn't deliver because IT WAS RAINING. OH REALLY? YOU'RE GOING TO SIT IN YOUR CAR AND WAIT FOR US? 

Then after grabbing the food and walking back in the pouring rain to start eating our food. THE FOOD WAS COLD AND STALE. The naan was left over from God knows how long ago and stale and cold and flat. Additionally, there was a blonde hair in our salad. None of us have blonde hair.

WE'RE NEVER ORDERING FROM THIS PLACE AGAIN. GET YOUR ACT TOGETHER SABIR. ORDER FROM SOMEWHERE ELSE.

Meh. I have had much better food and service in my life. Everything was just ok. For a place that seemingly caters to those with an expanded palate, I was unimpressed with the seasonings on everything I tried. CAVEAT: this place is super tiny and not suited for groups(there were 7 of us) and while being crowded is always a good thing in the restaurant business, there is no where to wait inside so be prepared to stand on a street corner for an hour plus.

I came here for the first time tonight with my boyfriend and his family who was visiting from out of the country. We had been looking for something different to do and since we happened to receive a promo card in the mail for $1 tickets, we figured we couldn't go wrong with a show at the improv. We arrived and picked up our tickets about 45 minutes before showtime. The seating process was organized and the host brought us right to the table. The server was efficient and friendly right from the get go. We liked the first two opening acts and then the main act Jimmy Shubert came on. All were very funny and had everyone in the room laughing non stop. Of course as is the case with most stand up comedy shows, it was definitely a bit crude and profane, so not for those who are easily offended! Definitely many hilarious moments overall. Although others have commented on the food, I cannot review it at this time since we didn't eat on this visit, but may do so next time. 

Being my first true comedy show experience, I had a great time especially for the value of what we got. The only thing holding back from 5 stars is the uncomfortable chairs. There were 5 of us squished into a table for 4. We would have had no room for plates if we got food. Everyone agreed that the chairs were not ideal for a 2 hour show. They could use some more comfortable seating for sure. Overall, a great time was had by all. I'll be back again

There are certain places you shouldn't go when you are used to fresh ingredients. I learned this is one of them. The sauce was clearly from a can and the dough tasted like biscuit dough.  The employees were nice

I bought $4300 worth of furniture on 5/26/17 biggest mistake of my life!We were promised the bedroom furniture on 6/12 so removed our bedroom set it never got here until 6/15 we had no bed for all those days.
Called Vallery in Bensalem on Monday got Amber who was rude and said the manager would call us well Vallery did not. I called on 6/14 again the manager never called back, I went to the store on 6/14 no manager working no call. I got a call four days later and Vallery was rude and blamed everything on us and called us liars. Had to call her boss nothing done.
Part of our furniture came on 6/19 and they broke the front door. Called to report it told they would call me back! Yep no call I had to call them. Talked to Chris Donnelly wanted me to fix it myself I said no.
He told me not to expect anything fixed quickly. Called the store and the warehouse to find my furniture. It is either on a truck somewhere or floating around the ocean who knows were. They gave me a new ETA of sometime in July.
NEVER NEVER BUY FURNITURE FROM THEM.
To top it off the second set of delivery guys did not even know how to put the love seat together.Help!
Review about: A Bedroom Set And Living Room Se

Sonoran dogs! This is the place to go to in Arizona. A huge place. It's pretty clean as well. I came here near closing with my friends before our drive back to California. They had a pretty good menu with typical Mexican meats to choose from. The thing to get here is the Sonoran dog. Its a hot dog filled with guac, beans, tomatoes, mayo , mustard, inside a sweet bun. It's a funny shaped bun but it tastes real good. The food is inexpensive and they also have a big salsa bar. 

The Sonoran dog is like a hot dog on crack. It's really good with a lot going on. This is a must order for hot dog fans.

Carne asada tacos - It was a decent taco. I've had better but it did it's job nonetheless.

Horchata - A bit watered down here. 

Recommendation: Sonoran dog

My first visit here was for Abby's Farewell, and I will return for the true Latitude experience.  I got enough of a tease to know it will be amazing. 
It may sound weird, but I judge a Mexican restaurant by its Margaritas, chips and salsa and queso.  If they can pull those three things off,  you've got me hooked. 
The staff was extremely friendly and made us feel as if we were attending a private party in someone's home. 
I'm sure I'll raise my stars after I experience a full meal.
I love the school that they teach all hands on skills. The instructors are very professional with plenty of experiences and skills.

Ok I am just going to say it.  Baja style Mexican food is totally under-represented in St. Louis!!   Fuzzy's does help fill that gap with their wide variety of Baja style tacos including the tempura fish, grilled fish, tempura shrimp, and chicken fajita with their special sauce. I usually order a side of chips & salsa because I CANNOT live without chips & salsa with my Mexican food and their salsa IS tasty.  The tacos are very small so surprisingly you will need to order more than what you might typically order at a Mexican restaurant.   Their burritos are also amazing according to my husband who said "this is the best burrito I have ever had"!! Next time I come in I plan to try the Torta style sandwiches which is another of my favorite Baja style dishes.  
While I am not a beer drinker they have a broad selection of beers on tap if you enjoy having a beer with your tacos.  They also have a variety of margaritas and who doesn't love a good margarita with your Mexican food from time to time huh? One more thing to love:  they have these plastic cups that you can bring back with you that are refillable..... they say "Oh Queso Lets Do This!" Ingenious!!

This is St. Louis Italian which typically means you either like it or your don't. No it's not the same as "real" Italian but if you grew up here this is what you grew up eating and it's delicious.  Chicken with white wine sauce and white pasta plus a salad with provel and more bread than you should eat? Great every time.

Best Bar North of Lehigh Ave.

Seriously, best bar in Northeast Philly.  Great craft beer and amazing bar food.  Good clientele, no beer snob douche bartenders.  Excellent all around.

The few times I've gone to this occasion it's what one would expect. Good food and pretty good service. However, they ALWAYS forget to put something in my bag, on my food, or how I asked something to be prepared. Now, the manager ALWAYS makes it right, makes me whole, makes me happy and apologizes and is AWSOME. Yet, the staff need to do better with the basic foundation of customer service, which is listen to the customer and give them what they've paid for...

Penzey's is the only store I've been to where I can honestly say that I want to and could easily use every last product they sell.

Amazing selection, excellent prices, good quality product, cute store, endless opportunities to craft your own gift boxes, and an unobtrusive yet helpful staff. 

What's there not to love?

Was really looking forward to taking the family to the Christmas Village but was extremely disappointed today.  Over the past 20 years, I've been to real German Christmas Villages in Karlsruhe and Coburg, Germany.  Other than the mini log cabin style vendor shacks, this Philadelphia event does not resemble an authentic Christmas Village at all.

The actual percentage of Christmas related vendors was maybe 10-15% and the rest was cheap jewelry, arts & crafts, hippie style clothing and other non-holiday related vendors.  Was dumbfounded by this fact - why?  It is supposed to be a Christmas/Holiday event not just another local arts & crafts street fair.

Was especially disappointed in the lack of authenticity of the food vendors.  They were selling thick American style bratwurst (should be thin and long) on extra thick buns ( instead of thinner German buns).  "Belgian" fries were just regular American foodservice fries instead of authentic thin, long & crispy Belgian fries.  Pretzels were regular local Philly style pretzels not German style pretzels.

The layout of this Village is a nightmare for people  with strollers or disabled folks.  Garbage cans were overflowing, 30-40 homeless people constantly milled through the crowd during our two hour visit panhandling for change.  A huge pile of reeking garbage bags were blocking traffic on one of the main sidewalk paths.

As an event coordinator myself - here is my advice: They should boot the non-holiday vendors, get authentic German food vendors, hire 10-15 security guards to keep the panhandlers-scam artists-pickpockets from entering the Square, triple the quantity of maintenance staff and install ramps to assist young families and handicapped individuals.

My new life in Saint Charles started here, at Towneplace Suites. I may have shipped all of my possessions and flown into town, but this is where I spent my first night in my new city. So, how was it?

Eh. A lot of the amenities, like the pool, were closed for winter. The "suite" was your typical hotel room but with a kitchentte for extended stays. I was only staying the night since the delivery van arrived in the morning, so I didn't really have a use for the kitchen area.

What I did use was the TV and the Internet. Let's start with the Internet. It was either run by too few access points for all the guests staying there or ones that were woefully underpowered for the hotel's needs. I could barely connect and when I could it was painfully slow, worse than 3G on my phone. The TV was an large, old CRT with a busted up cable box attached to it. I got some basic cable channels but most were distorted on one side of the screen or had a weird ghostly image of a bat across the top. 

The price was really cheap and having a kitchen area would be nice for an extended stay, but when you skip on the cost you get what you pay for. I don't think I'll be staying here again unless I have to, but I've been at places so much worse.

I've been coming here for years and loving the haircuts.  Recently the 4 main guys all disappeared (Freddy, Jose, dude with glasses who drinks water and lifts).  Anyway - does anyone know where they are at now??  In need of a good haircut.  Thanks

This was our stop after our 111 mile bike ride from DTLA.We were seated promptly as the group had made reservations. Drinks and food were served in a timely manner. I had a little incident,not service effecting and the owner went over and beyond to correct my incident
I highly recommend this store if you're looking for something that you won't find everywhere else. Salespeople have always been very helpful. Fabulous inventory. Very nice management.
Dumpier than the other Primo's I've visited and my bread seemed to be a day old,

Service was excellent. Make sure you ask for Brittany when you dine. He was spectacular. Meal was fantastic, for the price.  If you are looking for something quick and easy you'll find it here.  Oh and brush up on your Forest Gump trivia you'll be asked.
You can't go wrong with this place! Friendly smiles, clean environment and affordable.

Iberian Rooster's menu has a rather unusual theme.  It does not feature food from a country or an area, but rather themed around Portugal and its ex-colonies and trading ports from around the world, so you have traditional Portuguese dishes like caldo verde and duck rice, but also Indian curry, Macanese minchi, Mozambique burger, Brazilian braised ox tongue, and tempura. What an interesting menu! 

We started with caldo verde, which is delicious and a lot heartier than any version of this soup we've ever tried, with large chunks of the sausage, potato and greens.

The duck rice is totally plate-licking, no-morsel-leave-behind delicious, but the red wine and chocolate braised boar is not as exciting as it sounds. The meat was rather dry (maybe it's just because it's boar and not pork) though the polenta was good.

Price is somewhat high for the small portion, but service is great and the eclectic menu definitely deserve a try.

This place know how to cook crispy chicken, incredibly delicious, simple menu 
- white rice
- crispy juicy friend chicken
- tasty and delicious curry 

You wont regret it
Zero stars. Terrible in about every way. Pit bosses to food options to customer service  I would rather sit at home, warm up a frozen meal and flip a quarter.
Tried to get some pants altered.  No such luck unless you want to wait 10 days. Good luck trying to talk to the manager- too busy you have wait.

Good, not great.
Better pizzas closer to home.
Owner is friendly & anxious to please.
Hamburgers are a safe bet here.
Willing to give the Peddler another opportunity to show their "stuff ".

Updating my review  of yesterday cause we're still at the Fess Parker (last night thank good news).   Let me preface my review with the fact that I am a very easy going and patient mother.  So today, we went to the pool at 4:00ish.  The kids played for about an hour and then wanted a treat and we were ready for a cocktail.  NO POOL SERVICE after 5:00.  Now, it's summer and the pool is packed.  But no pool service.  Now we thought we would get some water for the room.  The sundry store is closed as employee is taking their 30 minute break.  While waiting, 5 people came for sundries.  We all inquired at front desk for possibility someone else could assist and were told it was owned and operated by an outside vendor.  If I could, I would not even give this a one star review.  We came here for a a good time - too much work to stay here!

Stood at entrance with 3 other parties of 2 - 4 people for 15 minutes without anyone acknowledging our presence. There were PLENTY of open tables. 

However, if being ignored is your fetish, this is absolutely the place to go. 

Also, here's my obligatory "I wish I could give 0 stars" comment. 

Made an account just to tell people this particular Steak n Shake is a joke. I usually let things go, but this place is just awful.

Incredible.

One of the gems of Reno. Few places really make their food from scratch. Here you can get excellently crafted tuna or chicken salad sandwiches with wonderful pastries and gellato. 

I've had a marzipan crusted cake here more than once and have to say if you would like to make your significant other happy, bringing home a cake here is sure to work. 

And yes, the owner is actually Austrian!

This has got to be some of the best Mexican food I've ever had. The chips...to die for. Margaritas not bad either.  The manager Ever has got his staff together.  Definitely coming back next trip to Santa Barbara!

My husband and I are vegan and when I had plans for my sister and her husband who are meat eaters to visit, we weren't sure where to take them to dinner that was close by. I called Chambers 19 Bistro and was floored by their desire and excitement to make us happy. They said that their chef, Jason, loves challenges and enjoys making vegetarian/vegan dishes.  Not only did they say yes they will accommodate us, but went way beyond any other restaurant in my experience.  Jason started thinking up dishes and after creating one of them, sent me a picture of it on my cell phone a couple of days before the reservation.  It was mouth watering gorgeous.  My guests, my husband and I were so thrilled with our experience there. And, the dish Jason made for us was fabulous.  Since then my husband and I have been back a couple of times - whenever we have guests who are not vegan and each time they outdo themselves.  Their food is delicious - their staff so friendly that you instantly feel comfortable and like you just made a friend and their atmosphere is comfortable, casual, warm and charming.
The tacos are amazing. The seasoning is different then other places I have been, however, it is really good! Definitely will be going back!

Finally a store under my name! HEHEHE!!

Just kidding!

Love trying all the sauces , sweet and savory jams, salsas, rubs, hot sauce and even some spicy snacks. They provide chips to try all their lovely items.  Great flavors and combination of spices , its a great place to familiarize yourself with what HOT SAUCE you really really like. Be careful though, some of them are really HOT. Great service and affordable.

One customer even asked, have you ever had to call the ambulance ???

Last week was my first time in New Orleans, and a group of friends and I thought a ghost tour would be fun. You all exceeded our expectations! Dartania was a wonderful guide. She was knowledgeable, entertaining and made sure we had a great time. Thank you for a lovely experience in the French Quarter! I would highly recommend this company.

July 16,2011. The wait staff staff for one is not very attentive to you're needs,HIRE some more servers. Seen 2 very large groups come in and leave ,for the lack of more tables.BBQ,is just plain BAD!!! No taste,No seasoning.the only thing worth having are the shrimp poppers and having 20 for a meal is not a good idea.Kitchen was behind the entire night 2 hrs for you're dinner to be brought. expand it,but as the reviews go, this wont be here long.

Simply put: This place  S U C K S !  

How much does it suck you may be wondering... Well let me put it even more simply for you: I could cook better food out of a dumpster than what was served to us for lunch.

Upon arrival, we were seated immediately by the friendly hostess. After 10 minutes of waiting, our waitress finally shows up to take our drink order. She must have been in a "rush" (due to the 3, possibly 4 tables that were seated in the entire restaurant) and attempted to scurry away before even taking our appetizer order. Seemed like a shame (insert obvious sarcasm here) to inconvenience her, but both of us were under the impression taking care of customers was part of her job description. But the poor service unfortunately did not end there: finding her throughout the meal was virtually impossible. You'd think that she were afraid to check on us because she herself knew how terrible the food is.

Appetizer: Calamari
Taste: None
Sauce: Pesto (? Why.. who knows, but it doesn't go with squid that's for sure).

It would seem as though the chef's find it necessary to mask the squid and drench the small pieces in batter composed of flour and cornmeal. And they left lot of fried batter clumps were left on the plate, too. I should have known better than to trust the waitresses "they're really good" recommendation about them. Silly me. Needless to say, it was a fried mess of nasty.

Main meals: Chicken Caesar Salad and Field house Burger
Tastes: Extremely unpleasing
Sauces: The waitress didn't even bring ketchup to the table for the burger

The salad tasted as if it had a dressing comprised of watered down mayo and vinegar. I for one thought that Caesar Salad was an idiot-proof dish to make, but  I guess I was very wrong. The croutons were chopped toasted foccacia and it tasted like rosemary was sprinkled all over the dish. Rosemary, watered down mayo and vinegar do not make a palate pleasing dish by any stretch of the imagination. The Field house Burger my boyfriend ordered was barely touched as he said verbatim "This is the worst burger I have ever had." Realizing that waiting for our server to eventually make her way to us was like waiting for water to freeze in the desert, we had the hostess replace his meal with an appetizer he's had there before and actually enjoyed.

All in all, I regret giving even a cent to this disgrace of an establishment. I left feeling embarrassed since I was taking my boyfriend out to lunch when he was having a bad day. I will never, ever go here again and will make sure that people know what to expect if they do.

While I lived there I loved it.  Now that I'm away, I have mixed opinions.

I LOVED the layout of our actual apartment!  The price was REALLY stellar, even for back on the day when I lived there.  Management was always nice and respectful, even when delivering undesirable news or enforcing building rules.  They were flexible with move in/out scheduling.  The security people at the door learned your face very quickly and were nearly always amendable to your and your guests' needs.  

Maintainence came quickly to fix issues and properly prioritized tasks.  There was a mini laundry room on our floor!  The elevators worked consistently.  I had a STUNNING view from my bedroom window of the Art Museum and the Schuylkill Expressway.  They eventually included DSL with the cost of rent!  There was a decent restaurant and adequately stocked grocery store in the basement.  They even had a shuttle which regularly drove you from the front door of your building to midtown.

But now that I'm away I realize that the building really didn't always feel safe.  There were often helicoptor lights shinning into my window.  This may have been due to living by the Art Museum.  But it may also be because there were brambles right behind my building.  

The stairwells and basement weren't the cleanest.  Parking in the public lot was impossible.  I'd often drive around for over an hour before finding a spot.  And I once had my company-issued vehicle broken into while parked in said public lot.

I'm not sure whether or not I would consider Park Towne as an option if I were to move back to Philly...but I've definitely had worse housing experiences in my life.

Staff is very  friendly and professional! We were seen for our appointment right on time too! We were given a thorough explanation of what could happen to fix our dog's broken tooth. We will will def be coming back again!

My husband and I love coming to the Edge! You can't beat the price for bistro seating in a recliner where you can get food and drinks delivered during the movie! We buy them ahead of time online and since it's assigned seating there's no worry about getting there early for a "good" seat. They have a great selection of beers, one of the best sandwiches is the Mississippi flyer and the fries are seasoned so yummy!
Authentic Vietnamese cuisine. Very good and they offer different dishes if you want to try something new. Clean and friendly service. I'm from philly and I make the trip because it's worth it!!

I'm booked for 5 days to stay in this hotel and so far I've been very disappointed. My first day went well, but my second and third day have been frustrating. My room was not cleaned until I have to request for it. I keep calling the house keeping and no answer. I called the front desk and was told that they will advise the supervisor of the housekeeping about the issue. I came back to the room, and it's still not cleaned. Same process was done, called housekeeping, no answer again. I called the front desk, they remembered that I called about the issue and was advised that a manager on duty will give me a call but didn't receive a call back. Most likely I will not return to this hotel.

I waited for over 25 years to be able to afford an LV bag.  I finally made the plunge last November on my 54th birthday.  The Sales Associate was a lovely young woman who took time with me while I made my decision. My sister mentioned it was my birthday and my SA offered me a glass of champagne.  I love my bag and the long wait was worth it.  If I am ever in the position to do it again, I will make sure that I go to this store.

This is a nice hole in the wall kinda bar. Inside it is a showcase of who else, Lincoln. The furniture is old, but very unique. In the summertime there is a patio area out back with plenty of seating to make for a nice night with friends drinking!

Tonight I placed a to go order for chicken fingers and upon biting into them realized they were completely raw on the inside. They were not close to being cooked. Upon driving all the way back to the restaurant I was greeted by two individuals (one being the cook) who seemed to care less about the incident. I asked if the grease could have not been hot enough (knowing items in grease are normally cooked by time) and I was told the batter could be too thick. I was offered my money back but a re-cook was not offered.

My wife and I anxiously awaited the opening of this store, but, unfortunately, we have been disappointed with the lack of value. The produce and meat are fresh and of quality; however, the purchasing done for the goods on the shelves was done without consideration to basic goods - The least costly loaf of white bread is currently four dollars. While the store is conveniently located right on Butler in Ambler Borough, all-in-all it doesn't make sense to do the majority of your grocery shopping here. I sincerely hope they make it, but would strongly suggest more diversity in price, especially in the basic items that everyone needs.

I like this place and truly wish I could like it more as whole, but I've been there two consecutive times and the bartender/waitresses are such dicks that I can't get past it. It used to be better than it is now.

I know you're a Belgian tavern, cool. And I know you reeeeally know your beers. Awesome. But that's not an excuse to be condescending to me, especially when I'm answering your question. If you ask me what kind of beer I generally like, and I say I like lagers, raising your nose and snarkily letting me know that you are a Belgian pub and don't really have lagers is ridiculous. I expected you to give me a recommendation based on my preference, not to ask me my preference and scoff at it. This happened two separate times with two separate people. 

Mussels are good but everything else is way overpriced, including the beers. $8-$9 for many beers that I've found elsewhere for less. Two entrees and two beers will run you a $70 tab, which is a bit too much for your average pub.

This place never has wax. Over the last several months, I have washed my car here at least 6 times at different stalls, and every single time there is no wax. Because there is no wax, the car never looks very clean after it dries, plus you waste time spraying what you think is wax but is actually just water. And this of course means you pay more for absolutely nothing.

Delicious sushi that can be delivered to Fountain Square! Yes! Jeff the manager was so friendly and I'm a sucker for great customer service. Also the sushi was fresh. I made my own roll: spicy salmon, spicy tuna, jalapeños, avocado, cucumber and sesame seeds. The boss sauce was awesome. Thanks Sushi boss!

I did a wonderful thing this weekend by going to Freret St. Po'boy and Donut shop to check it out. I picked up a dozen doughnuts for my parade companions and a few extra sweet things for my own house. The building is at the end of the Freret St. businesses in a bright blue building that you can't miss. You may miss the sign, but that building is pretty easy to spot. The inside itself is pretty small but once you walk in that wonderful smell of fried dough hits you and you are a goner. While standing in line my mouth began to water. The line moves pretty quickly, the staff is definitely on task, yet friendly, on a busy Saturday morning. I saw that they had a budget breakfast which seemed to have all the good components of a Southern breakfast (Read: Eggs and many varieties of pork). But I was there for something much grander: I asked for a dozen mixed, a honey bun and an apple fritter. The prices are great for the quality! I was out of there for less than 10 bucks and grinning from ear to ear. The honey bun - to die for! It was light and fluffy and not overly sweet. The apple fritter was yummy as well and packed with apples. I will be back to try a po'boy soon but I know I'll be taking some dessert home with me. If you're not eating beignets in NOLA, you'd better be eating these.

Hands down best meal we had in Nashville in Gulch area. Everyone loved their entrees ranging from salmon, yellow snapper, pork chop, and halibut. Lobster mashed potatoes and clam chowder so so delicious!!! Chic contemporary ambiance and super nice server.  Large parties fit comfortably in booths too.

One of my favorite hangout spots in Philly!  Been coming here since 2 years ago. 

Some nights it can get very crowded, but we never had trouble finding a table.  There is no hostess, so seat yourself.  A bouncer is at the door, so have your ID ready. 

My usual is the Turkey Reuben. Good selection of beers. Love the cheap prices.
This location, along with any of the other locations, provides great service, affordable prices and food in a family friendly settling.

My first impression of Bluefin Poke is that you'd miss the little place if you didn't know it was there, sandwiched in between a well regarded Italian restaurant and a gourmet pizza shop. Its downtown location means parking is at a premium, and you may need to feed a meter if doing a weekday lunch visit. Counter service was friendly and fast, and they didn't mind the woman who brought in a slice of pizza for her small kid to enjoy during his mom's raw fish feast.

Bowls come in two sizes, a regular bowl with 4 scoops of protein ($11) or the large bowl with 6 scoops ($14). An extra scoop of protein can be added for an additional $2. Having chosen a size you next select a base of sushi rice, brown rice, mixed greens, wonton chip, or a half and half mix. I had wanted greens and chips in my large bowl, but they were all out of the crispy bits. I stuck with the greens, while my adult children went with mixes of rice and/or greens.

Next you decide on proteins with any combination of ahi tuna, spicy tuna, salmon, yellowtail, shrimp, or scallop. My choice of a scoop each seemed pretty obvious, being I'd get to try everything offered. Dressing was next for my fish salad, with dollops of spicy ponzu, wasabi aioli, and fried garlic soy sauce. I could have also added sesame sauce, unagi sauce, sriracha hot sauce, or spicy aioli, but felt that three sauces was already pushing the threshold of flavor overload. My son showed no such restraint and got the lot. All that I tasted were good, with the wasabi and fried garlic being extra tasty.

Perhaps the best thing about building your own poke bowl is choosing what to top it with, and you can ask for as much as the bowl will hold. Bluefin's list offers a fair amount of variety, with green, white, or fried onion; tomato, edamame, tobiko, jalapeno, cucumber, pickled ginger, furikake, nori, panko, and both crab meat and seaweed salads. Avocado is 50 cents extra for about a quarter of a large Haas, cubed fresh for your bowl. Again, I didn't want to go overboard, so in addition to that nicely ripe avocado I chose green and fried onion, tobiko, cucumber, furikake, nori, and a big scoop of crab. The fried onion was particularly good, adding a nice bit of crunch.

I got a taste of each rice and was pleasantly surprised by both flavor and texture. The brown rice was about as non-chewy as possible, and the sushi rice had a nice hint of vinegar; both were served just slightly warm at the bottom of the bowl. My fresh greens tasted great, though I did miss the wonton for contrast. The ahi, salmon, and yellowtail were cubed a bit larger than other poke I've tried, but still sufficiently bite-sized and very fresh. The shrimp was done sushi style--butterflied with edible tail on--and the spicy tuna was chopped and mixed with seasonings. The scallop chunks were exceptionally good, lacking the squishy, snotty texture so often encountered with those in AYCE sushi. Soft, yes, but surprisingly enjoyable.

My group of poke fans enjoyed a healthy, delicious meal that filled 'em up without breaking the bank. My toddler grandson really enjoyed it, stating the best part to be the flying fish roe "bubbles". I'm ordering bubbles from now on.

Been here a bunch of times but have never rated it on Yelp. By far my fav sports bar in the area. Service is always average to good. They gave us new fries when first ones came out cold. The wings are definitely the best in the area. Must get the Shake n Bake wings. Prices are just average. The only negatives here is it's so popular, you have to go on a night where the Lightning aren't playing or any other big sporting events to actually have a peaceful meal.

I'm so torn  on how to review this , bc the vendors were all nice . I volunteered at a beer booth in the festival but also had down time to participate in the food n activities . So workers working the diff booths were nice but idk I feel like some things weren't clear like the exit situation I had asked a worker if their was an exit down on an end n they said yes but it was so far bc 2 exits before were shuttle exits which I wasn't even aware they had bc I. Came In the volunteer entrance ! So I just find those woman working those exits were rude it's like Idk what I'm doing it's confusing just tell me where to go !! But they did have signs but idk I guess I wasn't looking but I did notice on the 2nd exit I was like better not go their I don't have a ticket . And that was another thing at the first exit she was like where's ur gray ticket so I showed my ticket to get in the thing she should of said where's ur shuttle ticket it's gray or something about shuttle me and another person were so confused and then I made it to a reg exit and then they had ppl who were suppose to be directing us but all they were screaming was about the damn shuttles how about say shuttles this way exit for others this direction so I think someone was like maaam hello are u on a shuttle I was like no she's like u gotta go this way I was like ok. Then omg after exiting the park it was like a 3rd world country ppl selling water out of coolers I was so embarrassed to call this my city like go home they were hustling I just wanted to say no go home ur aggravating . But besides the food was good it was on the high side but it's a festival but it was all hot and tasty which some festival food isn't and is still high so , but it was also hot ass hell

My husband and I have been looking for a tasty BBQ joint in Reno and we've finally found it! We've tried the pulled pork burrito, chicken breast dinner and half slab ribs and all have been delicious. Sides are also very good. There's a great vibe and the staff is great. We'll be back again soon!

I've always been pretty fond of Bravo! in the past, but the past couple times I've been I was less than charmed. My server was excellent, on the ball with the foccacia and seasoned dipping oil, all around pleasant, but the food was sub-par from what I remember.

I've always been a big fan of the bruschetta with mushrooms and boursin in the past, but it seems they changed their recipe a bit since I last had it, the bread tougher and there seemed to be a little lemon zing in it I hadn't noticed before. But, it still got the job done in my belly. 

The main disappointment was the plate of Penne Med I split with my wife. If I were to guess the ingredient list for the dish, it would go: salt, salted pasta, salted butter (menu said olive oil, but it definitely tasted more like butter), less than 2% of spinach, sun-dried tomatoes, pine nuts, and feta. We were both gulping down water afterwards. 

Like I said, I've enjoyed Bravo! in the past. I think the pasta Woozie is a pretty safe dish, and their pizzas are solid. But, someone in the kitchen just seems a little heavy handed with the salt well when it comes to entrees.

I will preface with: this should be a 4.5 star, really - for dinner.

The first time I had the pork chop. FANTASTIC first choice. It had great flavor, definitely was the star of the plate. The squash adorning the plate was really just for that, but were very buttery & fulfilled that pesky veggie requirement ;) I ate the whole thing, would have made my mom proud.

I suggest getting one or two side dishes to accompany your food. The portions are enough for two people. The sweet potatoes are a favorite of mine.

I've had all the desserts... um, at least twice. Same wonderful freshness as the food.

So, now it's a goal to try everything on their menu. I've been through about half the dinner menu. I still need to go for brunch and more lunches. Since the food is from local ranches/farms, it's incredibly fresh. 

On to the atmosphere, etc: you definitely feel like you're not in downtown Reno; it's a little close-quarters, like in SF, but if you get a booth, it's just fine; it's loud because of the tall ceilings & minimal baffle; GREAT paintings of the pig & rooster to talk about. The wait staff isn't constantly in your face, though, sometimes they let you sit just a touch too long. Food & good company makes up for it!

One time (out of the 7 or so times we were there), the young chef was our waitress - yet, I was unaware of this fact until I saw her photo in a local magazine. She described her Grilled Chicken as "lovely" - she's right, sincerely, it is.

PLUS POINTS: no corkage, bring a great wine to pair with their great food, share a taste with your server. Kitchen is open until at least 11pm, at some times, midnight. Late eaters (like me) will love this.

Wifi down for three days with no clue when it will be back up.  Left a bitter taste as i just stopped to relax, catch up on emails/work and enjoy..    didnt happen-3 three days down????  And after i got my latte they told me well there Is another Starbucks just a block up the road that has Wi-Fi you can go there

Absolutely wonderful pasta!!!. delcious sauces and a plethora of choices putting aside the fact that everything is take home it is well worth it the only food I haven't liked so far was their pesto. Food aside the staff is knowledgeable and perfectly willing to help you pick out a meal you can even watch the owner hand making pasta while discussing every piece of pasta there

I've been to Elcy's many times over the years.  It was great when it first opened.  Then with some changes it slipped.  I'm happy to say Elcy's is back!  The atmosphere is warm and welcoming.  Servers couldn't be more helpful and attentive.  They have done a great job transforming this once drab space into a vibrant respite for travelers and locals alike.  The food on my most recent visit was delicious.  They took a basic turkey sandwich put it on multigrain bread added avocado and sprouts and suddenly it's a hit.  The roast beef with cheese and vegetables on sourdough served warm was delicious.  The ice tea/lemonade is always a favorite.  All food is made to order, despite this our lunch came quickly.  I'll definitely be back.

I just moved to Tampa and after trying a few different places for manicures, I found my place. The place itself is beautiful and there is a bar when you walk in. I went during the afternoon so it wasn't too busy and I was taken right away. They had a great selection of colors and they were very professional.
