After our group entered I had to stop.... is there something on my face? Toilet paper on my shoe? Do we smell? Just shy of a record scratching, everyone seemed to stop and glare at us. We were in the wrong place, this was the cool kids lunch spot and not just any dive bar. Thank goodness I know all the snaps and dance moves from West Side Story in case we need to rumble. We went out to the very nice, and empty, patio. We enjoyed our bucket of well priced beers and were on our way. I don't see myself returning anytime soon though. Not quite the warm and fuzzy sort of place I choose to booze in.

Came here for dinner with 3 hard to please people.
Not big beer lovers/drinkers, but the IPA I ordered was nice, and well priced.
The big bonus was the food.  The people I was with (remember, hard to please) were skeptical when they were looking at the menu.  We all took a little leap of faith and ordered.  All of us (ALL!) were really happy.  The appetizers, fried pickles and Chef Eric's wings, were fantastic.  One of our group said he the idea of fried pickles was repulsive.  Once they arrived (very quickly) and he saw how we were devouring them, he joined in.  He loved them, and totally ate the most.  The wings were spicy and tangy, really enjoyable, and a different flavor than anything I've tasted.  
The fish and chips entree was fantastic.  It was well cooked and seasoned perfectly.  Two of us had burgers.  Good quality meat and cooked to order.  One us us just got the mac and cheese appetizer as an entree.  Smooth and creamy and surprisingly topped with crushed up goldfish - really worked well.
The service was perfect!  I mentioned our group was hard to please - we all agreed that 25% wouldn't be a big enough tip.
I was really happy to see this place in the neighborhood.  It was a big improvement over the run down shell that stood in its place for so many years.  Loved it and will be back!
PS:  I really loved the mason jar light fixtures.

I GOT SICK!!!  In plant city. Everything tasted good, but I got sick after eating here last night. Had to pull over on way home and throw up entire meal. Never had problem here before. 

Went back to talk to manager in the morning, after last nights meal. Some older blonde lady manager said no one else reported problems. She said viruses are going around. I said I was fine beforehand and I am fine the next day. I asked for my money back. SHE REFUSED!!!  I said I would come back if you refund my money for last night. She said NO!!  I told her I will never be back. 

Wow.  I can't believe she treated me like that!  She lost my family's business and doesn't care.  The place  made me sick and they didn't care.  They got their money from me. Oh well, there's millions of restaurant choices. I don't need this place, for sure.

I reported the incident to the government agency that takes food borne illness complaints. The Florida number is 850-487-1395. They will have to deal with them now.  I'm done with this place.
Just stumbled upon this place!  Great coffee! Cute stand!  Independently owned!  Will be back for sure!!

My favorite bar in town! I always get the Ken Tiki Kentucky and the Pimm's No. 1212, they taste delicious. Really cool Great Gatsby ambience at night, when the lights are dimmed. The only con I can think of is the lack of seating space at night, but it's only an issue because this place is so great. 10/10

Tried this place a couple weeks ago and I have gone back many times. Me and my girlfriend love Chinese food so we tried a lot of different ones and this is the best one. We keep coming back. The only reason it gets four stars is because the delivery is a little slow

Came here for lunch on a rainy Saturday afternoon and basically I must echo Matthew S - too expensive! $50 for a lunch that is not even filling and is served on paper plates is pretty darn ridiculous. The cold and wet day made me want some warm chowder, theirs is thick and chunky, but needs a bit of salt. My husband and I each had our own bowl. I had the fishwich with grilled yellowtail. It's served on an overly grilled buttered sesame seed bun. Because the sandwich is so saucy, they need the bread to be pretty hard. The sauce - tabasco vinaigrette and tartar sauce is pretty tasty and the fish was tender. My husband enjoyed the 3 tacos sampler and savored each one as much as he could.

Overall friendly service (walk up order and they bring the food to you) and food was tasty, but damn for $50 you could throw in some fries?!!

I wasn't able to get a photo of the meal because I was trying to take care of my baby while eating...please note the bathrooms while new, clean, and spacious, do not have a baby changing table :(

My favorite local spot for Gyro's and Greek salad. They have other varieties as well that's sure to hit the spot! Staff are friendly and the prices are reasonable. However the place during lunch could get packed. Good luck getting seats. Other than that you will not be disappointed.

This place is awesome! I showed up one Friday night after getting married at the SB courthouse with 20 people. They reserved adequate space for everyone and prepared specialty punches for toasting. We ordered other drinks and all were delicious. After a few drinks we were all ready to party!
Brandon, Misty, Jonathan and Eric were very welcoming and really know their stuff. Quick to take drink orders and fast making them. Their knowledge of booze history and how they mix together with fresh local produce make incredible drinks is second to none! We recommend this place to everyone we will be back every time we are in Santa Barbara!

Plenty of bar space and good beers on tap for the most part. I've only come here after work for a happy hour but every time I have the food has been so-so. Not good, not bad but just forgettable. The service has always been very good though. I've never had a bad bartender or server. If you are planning on having a drink or two you are good but I would have dinner elsewhere.
Stellar, chill atmosphere, with big, bright windows and extremely friendly staff. Cold brew was delish, and the canine visitor made the visit top-notch! I'll be back!

So good!! Whenever you need a Korean bbq fix this place is definitely one of the best options. I have never been disappointed. The restaurant itself is a little bit older and the decor seems outdated but that almost adds to the charm of the restaurant. The food is always fresh and very well done.

Here is how ill put it...this place is a kick ass blues joint!  I did not eat here because it didnt give me the foodie vibe, but the set up of the place....pure awesome.  The bands here the night we went are out of this world talented.  There are only a few venues in a few cities where you can get his kind of talent in a groovie place like this, while still keeping it classy feeling and this place is one of them.

Hotel: so the low review is for the hotel. I chose this hotel based on the reviews here on yelp. It looked like a fantastic place. Upon arrival the place looks nice. I chose the the bungalow rooms towards the rear of the hotel. They appeared to have much charm. Check in was uneventfull. Once I got into the room I noticed the fireplace was not working. I called the front desk and was informed they were turned off for the summer. I was disappointed but did not cause a fuss. Later that evening I found food belonging to a past guest (cheese) in the fridge. Live spider was found on the bed when I pulled back the sheets to go to bed. 

As for the restraunt all I can say is it was amazing. Service was impecable, food was fantastic. Jerry our waiter was attentive to every detail.

So of it is food your looking for I highly recommend it. If it's lodging you might have better luck with one of the newer rooms.

Worst massage of my life. It was supposed to be  a deep tissue massage and Iiterally could not feel it. I left there feelinf zero relief and maximum stress and anger for throwing my money away. I felt like because I used a Groupon that maybe he just didn't even try but had he put in even a little effort, I would have become a lifelong customer. Maybe if you are arthritic and in your 80's or 90's you would like his "barely there" approach.  Otherwise, don't waste your time or money.

Hole in the wall place with excellent food! We all had the shrimp and grits, and it was delicious. Large portion size. Salad and shrimp bisque were elegant and tasteful. Service was great. Free parking. Wish the lewd woman with bottom hanging out wasn't the advertising logo. Wouldn't come here with older children because of that.

I really enjoyed my initial experience here, but was disappointed with the follow up service for a chipped nail. I tried dip nails for the first time after telling the technician working on me the reason I was getting my nails done. She told me the dip would last just as long if not longer than the gel, so I decided to try it out. It was a great experience and I was happy with the service. The next day, I noticed one of my nails had chipped. It was a really small chip, but I was worried the rest of the paint was lifting off my nail, so I called them and they said to come in and they'd fix it. When I came in, they hadn't remembered that I'd called, and then proceeded to re-file my nail to make the chip less noticeable. When I expressed my concern about the other nails possibly chipping, the technician helping me that day simply said, "It won't chip." Well, the next night, three more of them chipped while I was packing for a business trip. Perhaps I should've stuck with gel, or maybe the application of the dip wasn't as good as it could've been, perhaps my nails are to blame, but I had high hopes and was told great things only to be disappointed days later. If these had lasted at least a week, I would've been happy, but this all happened within four days. As I'm leaving for a trip today, I can't get them fixed, and their guarantee is only for 24 hours, so I doubt they'd let me fix them for free at this point.

This place is great! It is clean, professional, and reasonably priced. I am always happy with the results. They recently moved and although I did like the convenience of the former location better, the current location isn't too bad.

Awesome awesome! 
We only wished we lived closer!

We are frequent visitors of the city of Reno, and this time we thought it'd be nice to beat the heat and watch a movie. We chose this theater because it happened to be the closest to us. 

We walked in with no real expectations, but boy, we were blown away.

Tickets.
We were in a pretty long line for tickets, when I saw that they had an automated self service ticket kiosk. It was really easy to use and super quick. You can even purchase tickets for different days.

Assigned Seating.
When we were buying tickets, we didn't realize that you can choose your seats. This is an awesome feature! I love how you can go out to lunch/dinner and not have to worry about making it to the movie early for good seats. 

Theater.
Amazing. We were not expecting a theater with such awesome seats. Totally made the 'assigned seating' thing make more sense. We were bummed out that we had to sit up in the front, but the seats are like lazy boys. They go ALL the way back. If you had blanket, you could fall asleep in those chairs, easily. Each chair also has a little table, which is awesome for holding your super large popcorn, or eating you yummy nachos.

We will DEFINITELY be back here to watch a movie again! :)

Oh, did I mention they serve alcohol? ;)

I ate here with a friend for lunch. It was a beautiful day, so we sat outside. I was surprised to have a server come to our table and wait on us (which differs from the service at their other location where you order at the register, and then they bring the food to you). Our waitress was very friendly, and knowledgable about the menu, which changes daily! The service was nice, but I felt that it took a while for us to get our food, even though they weren't that busy.

I tried the savory crepe, which was filled with sausage, spinach, caramelized onions, and brie. It was delicious and came with a small side salad! It was crispy on the outside, probably because it was heated again after being filled to make the cheese melt. My friend and I felt that was interesting since we had never seen a crepe served like that.

Inside, they also have a small display with some pastries and baked goods for sale. I didn't try anything this visit, but I can attest that the croissants are out of this world; I especially like the savory ham and cheese pretzel croissant. They brush it with lye to give it a nice "pretzely" crust.

Overall, delicious food and pastries and friendly service. I've heard their coffee's great, too, but I'm not a coffee-drinker!

Whether you enjoy Buffalo wings, sandwiches, salads, or burgers, Buffalo Wild Wings Grill & Bar has that and much more to offer. The restaurant has certain things it specializes in, for example, the various amounts of sauces for those who prefer a milder one versus a spicy hot sauce. The atmosphere aspect is unique and comfortable because of the various amounts of TVs and tables for dining. Buffalo Wild Wings Grill & Bar provides some of the most amusing waiters and waitresses in the area. It provides the best service possible for their customers. 
 I have dined twice at the restaurant and both of those times I was provided with the best customer service. When my friends and I entered the restaurant the greeter was nice and respectful she gave us an accurate time of when our table would be ready. Some restaurants provide an inaccurate time so the customers can stay and wait for a lengthy time. At Buffalo Wild Wings Grill & Bar, there is a waiting area that is to the side of the restaurant so customers can comfortably wait until their table is ready. Our table was ready in about ten minutes, which is a fast time compared to other restaurant like BJ's. The employees wear jerseys and it sets them apart in a more personal and unique way. Jerseys seem better than the typical black and white dress code other restaurants follow. The waiter that we had was entertaining and made me laugh. Not only do the waiters show respect but they are enjoyable by providing humor when they check up on tables. Some restaurants are so busy they forget about their customers. In the aspect of their servers and greeters, Buffalo Wild Wings Grill & Bar did an outstanding job. I was pleased with their customer service. They also excelled in how tasty the food was, it was fulfilling and delicious. 
 The food is variable because although the restaurant is called Buffalo Wild Wings Grill & Bar they do not just sell Buffalo wings. There are burgers, salads, desserts, appetizers, kids' menus, and the drinks vary from lemonade to beer. This is a good quality to have because when eating at a restaurant they should apply variety in case some customers do not like certain foods. The restaurant is really known for the diversity in their sauces. Some of the sauces are Medium, Spicy Garlic, Honey BBQ, Wild, and Blazin. When we visited the restaurant I got the chicken tenders with ranch because I am not a fan of hot sauce. My plate was well cooked and it came with fries and four chicken tenders. For my drink I chose to get the Strawberry-Mango Lemonade, it was tasty.  The price is neither too cheap nor too pricy it fit the budget perfectly. My food and drink was a total of about $13.00.
 Buffalo Wild Wings Grill & Bar is mostly known for having big game nights. One example is the Super Bowl that is coming up they will be having the game played on the big screens so people can enjoy their food while watching the game. They not only play football, but baseball, hockey, rhythmic jujitsu, MMA, and basketball. At Buffalo Wild Wings Grill & Bar they also have game boards that people can use and play while waiting for their food or entertain themselves when they are done. 
The restaurant is spacious and decorative because there are numerous amounts of tables and the color of the restaurant brightens the atmosphere. The colors are black and yellow, and it suites the restaurant perfectly. I have gone when it is lunch time and dinner time. When I ate lunch the light was bright and relaxing, and when I went there at night, with a group of friends, the lighting was dimmer, it fits the mood. It is neither too noisy nor too quite that people can hear your conversations. When I dined there someone had a birthday party and the servers sang to them while also bringing them a cake. They danced and sang along, it was enjoyable. It seems like they care about their customers. 
 What makes Buffalo Wild Wings Grill & Bar great is their food, atmosphere, price, and customer service. They know how to hire the correct team to portray a well taught customer service skill so they can be respectful and entertaining to their customers. This was shown with my personal experience the two times I ate there. Not only is the restaurant spacious but equipped with big screen TVs for the customers to watch various amounts of games or just to sit down and relax an enjoyable meal. The food is delicious because their Buffalo wings and sauce are one of a kind. This also applies to the rest of their food, because of the variety they have to offer. As a customer I left the restaurant with a satisfied meal and delighted entertainment by the waiter. I would go back and recommend friends to stop by and try their delicious food and excellent service. Whether people enjoy Buffalo wings, burgers, a comfortable atmosphere, or excellent customer service, Buffalo Wild Wings & Grill has that plus much more to offer.

Food and service was great. Steak was cooked perfectly and the red velvet cake was delicious. We loved the dinner so much we went the next day for the brunch and it was even better. It's weird to say but the steak wasn't better than the burger and thats not to say the steak wasn't great. It was just one hell of a burger. The manager came up and introduced himself to us and continually checked in on us. Had a great time...and Philip (manager) comped us a T shirt as we were leaving. I would highly recommend

i LOVE TJ's. i live in Texas where there aren't any so anytime I'm in a town where there is one, I have to make a stop there.

made some new discoveries in the dried fruit aisle on this particular visit - dried bartlett pears and triple threat (mango, cranberries, and blueberries. i would've stocked up if i had known how good these were! ;(

Went with a friend for dinner on Monday night to check out Sumo Sumo.  Let me start out by saying read other people's reviews and they are definitely right on a few things - their parking lot is pretty weird, the outside of the restaurant has a nice brown patch of dirt to greet you and some of their maki sushi pieces are unusually large.  But those weren't that big of a deal breaker.  The inside is very modern, clean and has a very calm/relaxing atmosphere.

But back to the food.  We split everything (to try more stuff out duh) - started with the seared black pepper salmon tataki ($14) which was very nice.  Came with a ponzu sauce and was cooked perfectly.  Then for sushi, we ordered the dragon roll ($13), volcano roll ($14) and Joe's special roll ($15).  The maki's were all very good but as other people have said, some of the rolls are cut into ENORMOUS portions.  One roll could easily be cut into two pieces.  Not sure why they don't do that as the last two maki orders have 6 pieces each but could easily be 8 or more.  Plus it would be more manageable to eat.  

We also ordered a small maki - spicy tuna tempura maki ($6.75).  Came in 6 pieces and was different than everything else as it was warm.  Decent but I would pass on this one.  For dessert, we split a deep fried tempura green tea/chocolate/vanilla ice cream ($6 or 7).  So total of the bill was around $70+ which is a bit more on the expensive side but we had lots to eat and even had a mini box of leftovers for the next day.

If your in the Sherwood Park hood, it's worth checking out especially if you can go during the "Happy Hour" specials (3-6pm) where they have a bunch of dishes, all for $5.
Great staff, Dr Mary knows her ish, affordable as well
Please see my review from the other location... this one has more seating (esp. in the summer when you can sit outside) and the wait is generally nonexistent but otherwise theyre about the same!

Their brunch is amazing!!! I've also been here for a pre-bachelorette party dinner and they went above and beyond to take care of us. They have a beautiful venue space for private parties with fantastic service. The pretzel bites are so delicious!
Well this flavorful establishment is my husbands job so un-biasly I'll say the rustic decor compliments the wonderful smells of oysters, shrimp and fish..

Went on a Tuesday night with my children without knowing that it was Kids Night.  What a wonderful surprise.  My children loved the magician and Nerdy the balloon twister.  Nerdy may be the best balloon twister ... ever.  Our pizza was great, the Bavarian pretzels even better and kids eat free on Tuesdays.  A great night!

Let me begin by saying that I enjoyed my meal at Germantown Cafe. I went in with high expectations that, unfortunately, weren't met. If I had to break my star rating down into categories, I'd say that service was a four, atmosphere a five, and food/drink a two and a half. As I weight the quality of food and drink the highest, I'd have to say that this experience was more of a 3.5; unfortunately Yelp doesn't allow partial stars.

My wife and I arrived twenty minutes early for our reservation, which was completely unnecessary on a Monday night, even during Restaurant Week.  We were seated immediately. We took a moment to appreciate the wonderful view of downtown and the great attention to detail in the restaurant's decor and design. Shortly after we were seated, our server greeted us, informed us of the night's selection of pasta and soup, and then took our drink, appetizer, salad, and entree orders all at once. My preference would have been to wait a little longer, just for pacing, but as we HAD been looking at the menu online for nearly a week, we knew what we wanted. Other than the slight rush to order, my only other service complaint is that our knives weren't replaced between the appetizer and bread service; my wife and I spread butter on their delicious bread with the backs of our spoons. 

My cocktail, A Monkey Named Roy, was a concoction of Monkey Shoulder Scotch, Amaro Segesta, Rothman and Winter Apricot Liqueur, and an orange twist. It had a couple of issues. I was expecting a little more of the blood orange bitterness from the Segesta, unfortunately it wasn't there. Even with the pith-heavy orange twist, the drink was cloyingly sweet; with the natural sweetness of Speyside Scotch whiskies, there should have been either more Segesta or a dash or two of bitters (maybe Bittermen's Meyer Lemon or Regan's No. 6). I ordered a glass of Anciano Tempranillo with my entree, but the bottle was past its prime. It wasn't a particularly great beverage experience; even the coffee I ordered with dessert was a little too subtle and light-bodied for my taste. 

Our food was somewhat of a disappointment as well. The pork belly tater tots, which were really more of a shredded pork belly croquette, were nearly black when served. I believe they were fried in bacon fat, which has a smoke point of 370 F. The color, flavor, and speed at which the dish came out, led me to believe that they were cooked at about that temperature or perhaps a tad higher. Crank that fryer back down a little and they'll be a more appetizing golden brown color. The richness of the pork belly hid most of the burnt flavor, so we enjoyed them anyways. My wife's hanger steak was a perfect medium rare, and the butternut squash mashed potatoes and asparagus served alongside were excellent. My duck breast was, unfortunately, another disappointment. The breast was cooked to a nice medium, but I don't think it was seared at a high-enough temperature; the  fat layer and the skin were chewy and rubbery instead of the usual crispy skin covering a layer of fat that's almost creamy in texture. Thankfully, the plums, carrots, and risotto served alongside were excellent. Desserts were Apple and Key Lime pies. The apple needed a touch more spice, but the Key Lime was the best I've had in Nashville.

In short, I enjoyed my visit to Germantown Cafe. I'll likely not order the duck again, but I'll definitely come back to try some of their other dishes. Also, I'll probably stick to bottles of wine when it comes to beverage service.
Came in for breakfast, fast service and great prices. There was a wait but the lines moves fast.  Wait staff was friendly and attentive.  Will be back for sure.

This place is steps from the beach and way better bar then the bar that's ultra busy right on the beach. The staff is AMAZING, Smiley and super accommodating. Beer selection is SUPER and ASK for the Chicken Tacos (they're not on the menu) your taste buds will be having Tantilizing FUN! Shane our waited and  bartender was pretty chill!

Tzatikis now takes a back seat after eating here. 

This place is perfect for foodies with no frills needed. Look the inside is basic... it could be any restaurant outside of the plastic white columns.

But THE FOOD .. also THE PRICE. I got the Soluvaki Platter. Includes rice, salad, four pieces of pita bread and pork soluvaki, peppers, onions. Holy Moley it's a lot of food for under $10. The oil vinaigrette on the salad was super good. Best way to tackle this platter is to mix it all together. And don't forget the tzatiki sauce. I think next time I'd forgo the rice and do all salad with the meat. Rice was forgettable but with all the flavors going on, not a big deal.

If you're looking for a super quick, no frills, cheap yet delicious lunch - this is it!

We passed this cafe several times during our vacation and decided to try it out for breakfast on our departure and it was a great way to finish a great vacation. Biscuits and gravy are my go to at any breakfast joint and there biscuits and gravy were so good. Definitely will return on our next trip to Santa Barbara.
Best Mexican in the city!  The original Guacamole is a staple!  I come here at least twice a month and this place never disappoints!
Small hole in the wall place that you might miss but they make one mean gyro. If you in the Soulard area give them a try.

Great summer night place to eat. This place has unique food that's great. Foods feel very authentic and fresh. I like that the bone in jerk chicken comes with rice n beans, veggie slaw, and fried plantains. The rum bread pudding was amazing, super dense definitely something you could share with friends. Bummed every time I have came in they have been sold out of the Coco Bread. Just have to keep trying. Nice selection of Jamaican bottled drinks and canned beer.

Food is unappealing, greasy, and the delivery is often slow.  I've had to call them several times to inquire where my order was after the delivery guy failed to show up during the estimated delivery window.  On average a third of my orders were 15-20 minutes late, and at least once it was over an hour late because they had to redo the order and did not inform me of this until the end of the expected delivery window.

Overall, I think this place is best suited for an upscale lunch. Its not really nice enough for a date night or evening out, but its not exactly casual either. I've been quite a few times and the service is never impressive. The waiters don't seem to have much personality. I like to interact with my servers and have a good time but the staff here isnt very responsive. The wait is never long, but its certainly never quick. 

The food is yummy and satisfying, but its not something that has me worshiping the chef. Typically I order seafood here and it tastes fresh but the flavoring is never anything too creative. I do have to recommend the cookie dessert. It comes hot in a mini skillet with ice cream on top-AMAZING. Its big enough to share too, so don't order a whole one for yourself unless you don't want to get out of your chair when youre done (which is okay sometimes).

Overall, this isn't a place I ever choose, but it's great for business lunches because it has something for everyone.

I met a former co-worker at The Shack for lunch.  This was the first time I had been here since the ill-fated attempt for one of St Louis' restaurant legends to try to jump on the barbecue bandwagon with Salted Pig.  I know The Shack is part of a local hospitality group and by the time a restaurant owner is successful enough to be part their own hospitality group, I usually avoid them.  But this was convenient for my lunch partner and I wanted to try it.

You can order breakfast here at lunch time and they really do a lot of breakfast business.  I may or may not try that, since I am pretty dedicated to Mexican breakfast in small and real Mexican places.  I skeptically noted a lot of Mexican and Southwestern influence in the breakfast menu.  For this lunch however, we both ordered from the burger menu.  My friend had the bacon and egg burger which I must say, looked great.  I kept mine to the Cease and Desist, which is just a cheeseburger with lettuce and tomato (I skipped the onion).  I had slaw on the side.

This was a good burger.  The server asked if medium well was OK.  We both agreed.  I did that since I thought Ms T would eat the half I took home if it was not pink.  It was cooked properly and was not dried out.  These are good quality burgers, and since they are probably  1/2 pound, they are not going to be the smashed kind with grill crust.  There was no hint of char-broil, so are probably done on a flat top.  I have had a lot of burgers like this in the last month.  All good, none really remarkable, but certainly worth getting.  They all need grill crust or char broil and all need some salt and pepper.  My slaw was just OK, the usual bland stuff, it needed the Cholula that I added.  

The Shack is a busy place and there appeared to be a wait when we left at 12:30.  I am thinking this is very popular with the Sunday breakfast/brunch crowd.
Great food and great service! To me, Maritsas is a step up from a typical diner. I've never had a bad meal and there is plenty of parking behind the building.
Hire some more staff! Your wait staff is completely overwhelmed! This is the 3rd time we have been here that this has happened! Totally unacceptable and unnecessary for the business y'all do! Melanie

Great service! Everyone was friendly. All the employees were helpful and helped each other. Food was delicious. The Telky was amazing! Omelette was great. Coffee was good and in a great sized mug that didn't need to keep being refilled. Service was quick and the value of what you pay for was excellent. Highly recommended!!

Food: 2
Decor: 2
Service: 4

We dropped by here after lunch to check it out. After browsing the windows, I asked one girl for the most popular item and got the chocolate drop. 

Unfortunately, it was pretty disappointing. The chocolate was a bit melted onto the wrapping paper, and neither the pastry nor chocolate tasted very good. At least it was only 90 cents.

Great - free - way to ride on Mississippi.  Took the ferry as the sun was beginning to set behind the buildings in the business district...gorgeous views, and a perfect break from the hours of walking we had done that afternoon.  Round trip is about 30 minutes if you don't disembark.
Overpriced but good food.  The fresh brewed root beer and cream soda are worth going for!

The ribs here are flat out the best thing you could ever eat.
i went with someone who doesn't like BBQ and they completely changed their opinion on BBQ.
Don't ever be discouraged by the lines, it is well, well worth the wait.
I love the fact that they show you to your seat so you don't have to worry about finding one.
Just an amazing BBQ experience. 
Thanks for putting ST Louis on the map.

The service was quick but very rude. Pizza was cheap ($7.62 for 2 slices of pepperoni and sausage and a coke). Pizza tasted pretty good it was just the a-hole guy at the service counter complaining about how much he hates his job that lost it for me. 

The inside is nice though.

This place is probably one of the better restaurants in this part of town. I've gone here 4 different times over a span of 4 months, so I've experienced a lot of different types of rotating dishes. Because they are constantly changing their menu, it's hard to say what's good to order. Their meat entree specials are mainly pork or fish from what I've seen, their pizzas also vary, and even the small dishes rotate. 

Their pizza crust is good. They also make gluten-free pizza dough for $2 extra, which is a plus for those who love Italian and have gluten-free needs. My gluten-free friend said that she was almost scared because it tasted so much like regular crust. Unfortunately, each time I've ordered their pizza, their sauce changes (once it was sweet, which I was not at all a fan of) so it's hard to review anything about the pizza besides the crust. The toppings are fairly unique, with a few standard toppings (margherita, salumi, etc). They once had a beef cheek with fig pizza that was good, but it was a bit sweet for what I'd like my pizza to taste like. 

Their lasagna is awesome. It tastes like something I would have in Italy. It comes with a fried egg on top, and while this is very faux pas for some people, I thought the egg complemented the lasagna very well. Regardless, you could get it without the egg, but I'd argue it doesn't taste nearly as good.

As for the specials, some of the specials sound very good (on some days, they roast an entire pork as a special), and the others aren't as good. I've tried their pork shoulder (it was a bit tough), as well as a white fish they had (it was bland). I have learned to stay away from the specials unless it sounds absolutely amazing.

On to the small plates. Their bruschetta seems to rotate every one or two months. The one I fell in love with was their goat cheese and fig bruschetta. If it's ever back on the menu, it is by far one of the better things on their menu. You can't really go wrong with their meat and cheese plate, Tuscan fries, mussels, or calamari (in that order of quality). These are fairly large appetizers, so you'll want to share.

I've only had their panna cotta for dessert. This also rotates. The ones I've tried are raspberry and mint. The raspberry one is very, very, very good. I'm not usually a fan of panna cotta, so this is saying a lot. However, we went back recently where they changed it to a mint panna cotta. Unfortunately, I did not like it one bit. After one bite, I felt like I had mouthwashed. Not the best feeling for dessert, in my opinion. But if you like mint, this would be a pretty good choice, since the quality is still there.

Since I've only come on weekdays, it's always been fairly empty and quiet. Their wine selection is good, the entire restaurant is decorated very well and gives a very comfortable feel, and I'd say that for the most part, their food is really good. I'd pick this over any other Italian chain any day.

this is our usual morning go to.  they are friendly, fast, and always get your order correctly.  bagels are fresh and they are really great about substitutions.  They know us by name and always greet us with a smile.  and their coffee is awesome!

my go to is the asiago cheese bagel and sausage, egg, and cheese.  that thing can carry me all day and I usually don't need anything until dinner.  my boyfriend is a huge fan of their bagel and lox and schmear. and his son loves the  hashbrown bagel with egg and cheese.  so there are options for everyone!
By far the best drunken noodles, masaman curry and chicken Tom Kha soup in Metairie and even New Orleans!

The food was pretty good, I love the cheesy-crab mixture, taste great and wish every Chinese buffet had it. Waitress was great, even made me laugh by saying "U-like?" at the end of our dinner. Food was warm but I didn't care for the stuff they fried for you. Desserts not so hot either. Over good purchase though.

The food was delicious, the service was great, and I'll definitely frequent this place often. Not only was our server attentive and extremely friendly, but I called to make sure they were open (It being New Years Day) and It had went to voicemail... moments later they called me back apologizing that they missed my call.

Excellent experience from beginning to end! The food was fantastic (well worth the money) and the staff couldn't be friendlier! If you go, I suggest the Chilean sea bass and the wasabi mashed potatoes!

The food was outstanding, I got tuna as an appetizer and for my entree I had the filet and lobster tail and the food was delicious.  However, you will paying top dollar at this restaurant and should expect high quality service, and that's not what we got.  When we first got there, our server didn't come to the table for the first 15 minutes.  When we ordered our drinks, our server came back with one of our drinks and said the other one spilled so they were making the other one, so this took about 25-30 minutes to get our first drinks.  Our server hardly checked on us and it also took a long time just to get our servers attention to get our check.
The service is friendly and quick! I was in out for an oil change in less than 20 minutes.

Just went for the first time and loved the selection. Everything seemed fresh and each employee kindly greeted us and quickly helped the line that formed behind us. Try the chocolate frosted custard filled donut, that was my favorite. Even the regular glazed donuts look amazing.

Decent prices, friendly staff, good donuts, five stars.

It was one of the highlights of our trip. We only had drinks but if they take as much care with their food as they do with their cocktails... why would you go anywhere else. We were in town for 2 1/2 days and went back for drinks twice. Favorites: Cable Car and Bramble... and Richard, our bartender on our first trip. Can't wait to go back!!

Worst experience ever! Found a Groupon deal and decided to call before purchasing deal.  Spoke to a rep and she explained that the deal was for a generic background with no customized  design... I decided to just book it with her through the phone.. Premium package she said included an extra hour(total of four hours) with unlimited prints, gold shimmering backround, customize design, a scrapbook with all prints and a digital disk with all of the pictures. She said someone would get in contact with me about a week before my event to go over designs. It was two days before my party that I had to reach out to them. I called and a rep gave me an email to get in contact with someone. I got an email back stating that the attendant will arrive 30 mins. I had the reservation from 7:30pm to 11:30pm. I was busy hosting and got a phone call from john around 7:55 pm stating he is on his way and was running late.  I then told him I reserved it from 7:30pm and he was already late. He didn't arrive until almost 8:30pm!  He arrived and set up. Didn't save any picture in the beginning for the scrap book. I had to ask/remind him to print an extra copy for it.. I didn't even receive a digital copy of the pictures. Thanks for ruin my 30th party. I don't even know where to start to contact this company with the poor service they provided or if they even care. I wasted that much money for nothing

Scott is amazing. Truly the best wine tour I have ever been on. We were picked up in a Tesla SUV and visited four exclusive vineyards- small, local, and up and coming. We learned about Santa Barbara and the various regions in the area. We met two of the winemakers and learned how they got into the business of winemaking. Scott's passion, knowledge and connections within the Santa Barbara wine community truly lend itself to an amazing experience. I would absolutely do it again!
only the best spray tan in nashville...seriously no one can touch her! great and easy to get to location!

The concept that Chef Garces has created for this Philadelphia standard is very much appreciated and needed. The service, drinks and food were all excellent. GRG not only paid quiet homage to the Philadelphia institution but expanded and created a historical record of well executed cocktails on the menu. It was wonderful to see such cocktails as the Last Word invented at the Detroit Athletic Club and the Pegu invented at a British Officers Club in what was then Burma. A very nice selection of food items in various portion sizes. Well done!
Great service and nice hot food. Sushi is the best in town. Always busy. Definitely a place to go for a good meal.

Fine SB elegant dining. Great service historic room. Our 4 dishes were all delicious and richly flavored to point of being almost too much. Classic room with amazing ceiling n fireplace. Limited menu and high prices are only things keeping it from 5 stars.

This was an overall good pick. The restaurant seemed like a popular tourist choice which can make for long waits but this didn't take away from getting good service. All the staff was friendly and helpful. The food was very good but lacked any signature flavor. The Fried Green Tomatoes were my personal favorite. The Redneck  burrito was yummy but the pulled pork over powered the baked beans and Cole slaw in the wrap. The fried chicken was tender and golden. There is a great selection of local beer and spirits on the menu. They do have an in-house BBQ sauce but that was not so special.

Only Spanish speaking employees. Worst LA Salsa in Arizona. Mixed up two orders. Asked for money back. Never will come back. Victor needs to hire English speaking employees to avoid mixups. Horrible!!

This is a small museum but entertaining nonetheless.  I think very young children would enjoy it the most. The short movie they show in their special theater was a lot of fun. The butterfly garden was beautiful.

After a customer of mine recommended SK Noodle, I decided I should give it a try. We went in on a Sunday afternoon and there was a family of 5 and 2 other couples in the restaurant. One of them was placing an order to go so we grabbed a menu and sat down at a table close by. We were greeted by a nice woman and we told her that we were getting it to go as well and that we needed a few minutes. It seems that their menu had a little bit of everything, but we both decided to get our old Pho standby to compare what we have had in the past. I had also heard that their fried rice was amazing and I had yet to find anything in Reno that deserves that title. 
They had a newspaper article on the wall that said, 'you won't run out of meat before you run out of noodles". My boyfriend always asks for extra meat, so he was very interested to see if that was true!

It took about 15 minutes to get our food and we rushed home to try it. Sure enough, there was a ton of meat in the meal. The meat was perfectly seasoned, the egg rolls had great flavor and crunch, and the shrimp was cooked perfectly. Then, the moment I had been waiting for, the fried rice! I opened the box and it sure looked good. Then I dug in and it was AMAZING! I was so excited I almost cried. It had wonderful flavor and texture and I wanted to eat the whole container myself right then. (The left overs are equally AMAZING right now!) The dishes we got more than stuffed us full.

I never would have found this place on my own and I am so thankful to my customer for telling me about them. I would still be in a fruitless search for fried rice! I am looking forward to going back and I already have a list of friends and family members that I am planning on taking there.

Went here a few times with a small group of friends. Being all women, we went and had a great time. Coffee was nice and simple. Tea was hot and fresh. Hookah was also nice. No one bothered us and the employees were very nice

I've been to the brewLab twice and tasted four of their beers.  Of course everyone's taste is different, but I found two beers that I really, really enjoyed.  One is an IPA with green tea, and the other is a stout (I think) with Ethiopian coffee.  Knock your socks off flavor.  Other beers I tried were ok, too, wouldn't turn them down on a warm day. Note: this place is small, in an industrial park-type setting, and can be very noisy.  But I'll be going back.  Note the days and hours open; they are limited.

Excellent corndogs (and other stuff). I admit, I hadn't had a corndog in YEARS, and was pleasantly surprised by how light (ie, not heavy and greasy) the batter was, and impressed by the variety of 'dog' and toppings I could choose from.
 
I also shared the cheeseburger fries, which were OUTSTANDING. Looking forward to going back to try poutine and other items on the menu.
Had the falafel platter, it was super tasty, it came with lots of food and was a great deal at only $7! I'll be back again soon.
My first visit today and will surely be back.  The goat cheese pasta is absolutely the best.  Very large menu sure to please any taste.

FAVORITE wine bar in St. Louis. Everyone is so friendly and fun!! They are also very knowledgeable of the wines! The menu changes seasonally and is full of interesting and delicious dishes. I honestly have not had one bad meal (or glass of wine) here!! They have a great wine club and various events each month (including participating in fundraising for charities). The patio is awesome.....in fall and spring they have outdoor heaters. Live music sometimes as well. It is located in a cute part of Webster Groves and is a lively atmosphere. Perfect for any occasions. Their lunch is also great!! This is mine and my friends' favorite hot spots go to place since it opened!!

Being from the west coast originally, I am very used to classic bubble tea. Went hoping for the same, authentic taste and was sadly disappointed. The place had an odd smell, like cigarettes and perfume, we didn't stay after we received our teas. Also, don't forget to say you want boba, or you'll just get milk tea. The taro boba tea was basically milk, tinged the slightest shade of what might be purple with boba. There's room for improvement here, still looking for authentic boba in Nashville!

Very nice place for an airport...iPad ordering was a little different.  Didn't take anytime to figure it out.  It was kind of nice, especially if you are in a hurry.  No waiting, order, eat and go.  Cheesesteaks and fries were very good.  Staff friendly and attentive.

Local Harvest is a few blocks from my home and office, so I usually end up eating here once a week, which unlike some of my other faves, I don't end up feeling guilty about.  

I'm quite fond of their Mediterranean salad which has Azeefa, which is a locally made beluga lentil spread, in it--so much more interesting than your standard hummus.  Now usually I'm not so interested in a ham or turkey sandwich, but both are really really good.  And I can never turn down one of Chef Clara's fresh soups, particularly the Borscht.  The fresh local ingredients certainly make the food taste that much better.  

And don't pass up brunch!  My friend and I ate here New Year's Day both couldn't resist the "Bacon 6 Ways."  That's right--bacon biscuits, bacon chive butter, quiche lorraine, black eyed peas with bacon, root veggies with bacon, and bacon wrapped dates--YUM!

I went here on 12/22/14 to take my Fiance out for a light dinner as a capstone for a lovely outing.

I have been here three or four (Fairly certain it is four) times now and it seems like the restaurant is slowly improving. But more on that later, first the most important part.

The food here is pleasing I would say. It isn't mind-blowing but it's better than simply "good". The menu does seem a bit hit or miss with the choices and while they are what I would call standard it at least hits a wide enough array of targets you should be able to find -something- to eat. If you're used to the eclectic selections of Midtown you might perhaps be less ecstatic. 

None the less I have never had bad food from here nor has anyone I have brought here, I've never had to return an order due to mistakes or any such things. The portions are fairly priced for what you pay although I do think they could stand to be less skimpy on the fries and perhaps not charge $3 for a soup du jour added to an Entree but instead offer it as a substitute. I've tried their chowder and it was very good if a bit small. But I digress, a casino exists to make money no? I will say the French Dip I tried on my last visit was stellar! 

Edit: As a side note, I do like their presentation of the food! It is not simply flopped on but tastefully arranged.

The atmosphere here is more or less pleasing. I love the pop art and the furniture is incredibly comfy. The place is well lit but not harshly so, nor is the music too obtrusive. The seating is however very open, not the place for intimate gatherings or if you hate being looked at while eating. On a related note, the windows from the main hall allow passerby to look in so for other strange folks like us mind that you will be gawked at by some of the less tactful passerby.

The wait staff can be hit or miss as well, but I suspect that has a lot less to do with them as individuals and more to do with management. The staff themselves have always been kind and exceedingly polite. They always seem understaffed, I've overheard workers not having a chance to take a break (Which I should remind you all is illegal), and I've definitely seen management breathing down their necks on the restaurant floor itself!

Let's talk about that for a moment, as this was a major annoyance for me when this place first opened. While I understand the GSR wants a certain level of quality control, I really despise having some guy in a fancy suit standing around scrutinizing everything. The staff, the patrons, the food, everything. I do not find a mildly disgruntled looking manager to be pleasant atmosphere for my dinner. Not to mention this behavior noticeably makes the staff nervous and service suffers for it as a result. Back then I'd have given this 3 stars for this impression I got, but it seems like they're hanging around less now than they used to be. I'm sure they have their reasons that are perfectly valid, but as a repeat patron I have found it distracting and bothersome and I wager others have too.

But I digress. My only other nitpick is that I once found a dirty utensil at my table. Lately the service in general has been much better and I'm definitely going to be coming back again.

Stayed here recently during a conference.  Staff were great.  Rooms were spacious but dated.  Scraped my leg on the 2x4 sticking out from underneath the bed. Looked like it was used to brace the frame.  

Convenient to downtown venues and restaurants like other downtown hotels.  The entrance is a bit unconventional.  There is no entrance facing the street, and yo to go up an escalator to get to the front desk or take the elevator by the restaurants on the corner.

Managers happy hour in the afternoon and breakfast were great.
Neat place with a lot of old books. Building is a bit beat up but it's quiet and no one bothers you. Great place to spend a few hours browsing for old books.
Large variety of bagels and spreads. Crowded in the morning but usually only a 5 minute wait

Love this place.  In 2009 I traveled from coast to coast searching for the best cupcakes out there, and they were right in my own backyard.  Well, a short 13 mile from home.  Which I occasionally do, buy a cupcake, then take a taxi home.  Totally worth it.  Even my husband, notorious for claiming not to like desserts and then eating half of mine, would do serious crime for a sweet potato cupcake. Just the right amount of icing to cake ratio:  1 to 3.

My Favorites:  Wedding Cake and Red Velvet.

I just had the most amazing blowout by Linda! All I have to say is WOW! She was so friendly and left my hair with lots of volume and I couldn't be happier. I will definitely be back when I come to New Orleans!

The sashimi is very fresh and delicious, but their rolls could use improvement. The beef they used was the cheap cut, but the price reflect on it. I randomly yelp this place coming from the zoo. Saw it had such great rating that I must try. It's not too hype up to what is it.

This looked like it was going to be a real find!  Looks can be deceiving.  From the completely uncaring staff to the over priced drinks this place had problems from the start.  It's very dark so the filthy interior wasn't obvious at first.  What was obvious was the broken stools and ripped seats.  The band was great so we tried to stay but the waitress lost interest in checking on us and the bartender wasn't behind the bar.  We decided to just go but first my husband needed to use the facilities.  Biggest mistake of the night!  toilets overflowing with actual feces and no one doing anything about it.  GROSS

I love Forno.

I come here once a week for the half off pizza slices. They are excellent! Everything on the menu is reasonably priced and looks delicious, although I have only tried the pizza and the gelato.

The unlimited bread for free is really a plus.

The staff is super friendly and helpful.

My personal favorite is the gelato. I have never tasted anything like it! It is sooooooooo good! The price is a little steep (4.00 for a small), but is well worth it!

The on-going specials are great. Overall, this place is the BEST in the area for pizza!

I am looking forward to trying more menu items. This place is HIGHLY recommendable!!!

GO!

Ps. They serve draft/ bottle beer and wine too!

Hello, my name is Brian and I recently discovered your downtown location and was excited to do business with you seeing that you are a short distance from my residence.  I had called in advance to dropping off a few items to see if you would sew on a button that had fallen off my slacks that I was having cleaned.  When I returned to pick up my belongings, I had noticed that the button had not been sewed back on even though there had been a tag attached to the pocket.  It was not a big deal at all, the young lady who had helped me apologized and took them back to correct the problem and asked me to come back in a few days and the button would be fixed... cool.  That is until I picked them up, not checking the button before I left, just to get home and realize the button was still only fastened down by a safety pin. I then returned for a third time now, making my 4th trip to the cleaners (including the initial drop off), to fix the problem yet again... I was very disappointed in the service I received and thought that the I should have received at minimum the pants free or discounted.  I payed full price and wasn't offered any kind of discount for the inconvience. I by no means am looking for a handout, but do believe that something should have been done other than hearing "I'm Sorry".  Well I'm sorry to I will no longer be doing business with you in the future... best wishes. Brian

Amanda has been caring for my hair since 2004! I can take her any number of photos and walk out feeling amazing with fabulous hair. The new salon is beautiful, open, and Melanie Joye LMT has her massage studio in a private area in the back. I love Paul Mitchell products & their commitment to no animal testing, & you'll see all the stylists have photos of their animals at their stations. Cognito also chooses a cause of the month and donates to that charity. Great salon, wonderful people, and some good coffee - what's not to love?

For the longest time I wanted to try Crumbs. Everyone has raved about them. Today I was excited to finally get there. The store is exceptionally clean, bright and the cupcakes look amazing in the case. The variety of flavors makes it almost impossible to choose one. The friendly, helpful sales girl recommended any one with the lemon cake, since that was the cake she loved. I bought a Coconut Lemon. The icing was so  laden with grains of sugar, even me, a self proclaimed "sugar addict" couldn't take the sweetness or texture. And I guess people who loves these never had a Mom who baked cupcakes and cakes for them from scratch.

I hate this place. Every time I go here it's some different ridiculous issue. The bouncers are awful and will throw you out for any random illogical excuse. The first time I came my friend tripped on their rug because it was crumpled up and they threw her out and confiscated her real PA id and called the police. The next time I came it was dead inside, there was only a few customers and the bartenders had a bad attitude and didn't want to provide service. Lastly, on Wednesday for the special I was dancing with my friends and the bouncers dragged us out violently and called the police and we got cited. I will never be coming back here or giving them another cent of my money and I suggest that you don't either.

I'm not really sure how or why it has taken me this long to check out the new Tin Palace but this place is awesome! I love love love what they have done with the place, it looks great! As far as Earls go (typically I try to avoid them) I have to say I enjoyed my time here. Our server was pleasant and quick with our food. I have no complaints as far as food goes, everything was delightful and good sized appetizer portions. While Earls isn't my go to restaurant I have to say there are a few dished that are my favorite and no matter the time of day Earls can offer you something. They have lunch, mid-afternoon snacks, delightful dinners and items that pair well with wine on a romantic evening out. This is my favorite Earls I've ever been to and it's right downtown! Can't wait to check out their patio this summer!!

A friend and I recently visited this course on a Saturday. We travelled from about an hour away because I saw so many great reviews about white clay creek country club and for the most part the course lived up to our expectations, except for one very strange occurrence that we didn't expect at all. On hole 16 the tee box backs up to the train tracks. As we were about to tee off kids walking along the train tracks, that we didn't know we're there started throwing rocks at us and yelling in our back swings. When we finished our round and I told the gentleman at the pro shop about our encounter and he informed us that this is a semi regular occurrence and not only does it happen on 16 but also on another hole where the kids climb a tower and throw rocks at golfers. I must admit I was pretty taken back that the course doesn't take more action than just calling CSX security. Until the course can take care of this we will not be returning and I suggest to all golfers interested in playing this course to bring this up when scheduling a tee time. At the end of the day it is a serious safety concern to all golfers.

Love.  Can I go back again today?  

Joseph was our incredible and knowledgeable server.  He brought us several wine samples, because we couldn't decide. He made some very thorough recommendations and helped us pick a bottle.  We started with the smoke Caesar salad, and added the bacon, which was unreal.  These ain't no bacon bits.  A huge piece of bacon came served on a separate plate and it was like butter.  So good!  Oh, and the bread?!  Yes.

For my entree I chose to go with the bison ribeye and it was spectacular. Cooked absolutely perfectly.  My husbands fortune with his steak wasn't quite as good, but in the end he was thoroughly pleased.  He Initially ordered the Kobe ribeye and he had to send it back because it wasn't cooked enough.  When they brought it out the second time it was completely well done and chard... Very disappointing for a $90 piece of meat.  Joseph offered to bring him something else and he chose the bison ribeye as well, because mine was so delicious.  Of course, the manager came by to apologize, which was appreciated.  For my side I chose the lobster mac & cheese which turned out to be freaking amazing.  My husband ordered the mixed vegetables which I thought would be kind of boring... I was wrong.  It was also delicious!

Because we were celebrating our anniversary our server offered to complimentary glass of sparkling wine as well as a dessert. We couldn't decide on a dessert so we chose two: chocolate cake and carrot cake.  Both were great.  The chocolate cake wasn't life changing (which is what I was hoping for) but it was very good.  

In the end the Kobe dish was taken off the check and the bison he ordered in it's place was comped, which was certainly appreciated.  Definitely loved the experience and will absolutely be back.

Anyone bad mouthing CB doesn't know what they are talking about. Yeah it can get a bit crowded, parking can be be a hassle at times, and the old retirees can be a real drag while on the road... All that aside, it's still one of my favorite Beaches. 

Sunsets at the pier offers games, music, dancing, at times even magic shows. Then you have the Sunset cinemas showing family friendly films at sundown, just bring a chair, blanket and your favorite snack. 

Clearwater Beach is the place to be, great ambiance, plenty of sports bars, and beautiful sunsets.

Great pretzels, and awesome service! The pretzels had recently come out of the oven, and smelled so good walking by, we had to stop and buy a few. We're glad we did! The person serving us was very pleasant, efficient, and made us feel welcome. We will definitely be back!

Love this place. Fresh food with no set menu is a fun experience. My wife and I had our rehearsal dinner here in 2012. We had the whole place to ourselves which was very intimate for our family and friends. Since then we have eaten at Italian Cucina several times and loved it every meal. I often recommend this restaurant when friends and coworkers ask.

This is a review of the service since I wasn't actually allowed to come in. I came to lambertville wanting a coffee and something light to eat at the lambertville station so I park in their parking lot and as I start walking to what I thought as the entrance since I saw the door as I was driving in, the manager comes out of the side door which is actually the entrance and starts harassing me on what my business is. So I said I'm coming into the restaurant and he then says well this is the entrance so what can I help you with? I said I just wanted a coffee and something light to eat...is that okay? And he says well we're not open yet but there's a coffee place down the street you can walk to (mind you they opened in thirty minutes so I'm sorry I didn't know that not being there before). So I said should I move my car? And he goes no you can leave it there for now if you'd like. Um.....I literally felt harassed. Is this how you treat potential customers? A million questions before they even walk in? I went ahead and moved my car so he wouldn't have a cow but seriously,  I don't know if I'll be back that was horrendous service and I didn't even make it inside. And guess what, I'm a manager of a restaurant too. Shame on you.

A tale of two dinners.

  We ate here night 1 in Nashville and our server was amazing. The food was terrific as were our drinks.

  We ate here again night 4 which was a Friday night, an ironically we ended up with the same server. We waited a good ten minutes for our drinks from the bar, but ironically our appetizers and entrees all arrived at the same time.. Turned dinner into a race.. Made it less enjoyable for sure.

I've visited BellaBrava three times and been please all 3 times. I also think I've ordered the chicken bbq flatbread all thee times (I fear change) so I can't comment on 90% of the menu. The staff is very friendly and attentive and I enjoy the atmosphere, especially if it's a nice day and you can be seated outside.

Drink options vary from house sangria to your full bar. The red wine sangria was ok, though I admit that I'm not a huge sangria fan. Happy hour specials allow for many more options at a reasonable price, especially when dining on Beach Drive.

Appetizers and salads are great and I recommend the bruschetta. I almost ate so much that I wasn't hungry when my main entree came out. Luckily, I got my second wind for gorging, and had no problem enjoying my chicken bbq flatbread. The lady ordered the italian sausage flatbread, which also was quite tasty. Maybe one day, I will stray from my sole selection...

I wanted to LOOOOOOVE Jackalope - a Nashville brewery whose CEO is a woman? How cool is that? However, a few things kept me from loving it! 

The good:

1. Lots of beers. This is not one of those small local breweries with six beers (although I haven't notice that much in Nashville - it was definitely a possibility in Texas, my home state).

2. GAMES. What's more fun than beer and games?

3. Often a food truck outside. 

The not so good:

1. While I appreciate creativity in brewing, a few of Jackalope's summer seasonals were creative, but not good. Peaches and cream? Sounds interesting. Tastes...not so interesting. After trying a few of the creative selections, I stuck with their basics, which were much better. 

2. The tap room is SMALL. We stalked people in the room until a group got up to leave and grabbed their table faster than anything I've ever done. Something that can kill an experience at a brewery? Holding your flight with no where to sit! 

3. Parking. They have a "lot" - about 8-10 spaces, which, let's be honest, could be taken by two groups of patrons. There's supposedly street parking. But, realistically, you're paying to park. (Or Uber.)

4. Line for bathrooms. In the tap room, they only have one men's and one women's restroom.  There are more bathrooms with a sign that says "for tours only" or something like that. I'm pretty sure women use that one too, because one stall really isn't enough! 

All in all, I had a good time at Jackalope! But a few more tables and bathrooms would go a long way!

Good food, good price. Spooppp good chocolate cake is a must try worth it for $6.50. Reserved booking is a must since it's a Saturday UFC fight night so it was full house. Tailgate party platter very worth it for 3-5 people

Kingfish was amazinggggg. Shout out to our waitress Angelina for the great food recommendations and being fun.

We had bottomless mimosas, and I got the Bloody Mary which was nice.

As entrees, we got the Shrimp and Grits, which were nice and creamy, great cajun flavor. The French toast was pillow soft. 

Highlights: Their Jumbalaya is to die for. It was like comfort food.

Being that it was the first week and they are still working out their kinks, service was ok...the food on the other hand needs a lot of work.  To start the portions are VERY small.  We ordered the fries in mushroom sauce which was very good, however there were like only a skimpy handful of fries.  The table also got an order of the calamari and the pork belly, both portions being a joke for the price!  Finally, for dinner I got the lamb gyro which was terrible!  The meat was dry and crumbling apart, there was hardly any sauce, the only redeeming quality was the pita bread...I will not be visiting Barrel House again anytime soon, which is a shame being that it is right across the street from me.

Great place! Very clean and their tanning beds got me super dark! Love the blonde behind the counter she is very knowledge and nice! I found this place on groupon and wasn't sure how long I should tan for or much about it since In the past I went to a place in Tampa and I burned a few years back but I wasnt uncomfy to ask which is nice for a change .. I will be back

The Longue Vue House and Gardens is a spectacular place to take yourself and visitors. There are plenty of beautiful gardens to walk through, fabulous architecture, great old trees, and don't forget to take the time for the tour of the house itself! Gorgeous.

I basically evaluate a visit to a restaurant on 4 categories:
Service  5 stars
Food:     3 stars,  only because I can make everything 
Price:     4 stars
Atmosphere 5

Now these categories may change slightly but yiu could fit almost anything into these categories.  I grew up in this type of food in the south so I have had some fantastic and innovative dishes.   The food here was really good but it didn't blow me away.  Show me a country dish that yiu don't get too much in the country and then I will upgrade the score.  However, just over 4 stars is not bad at all.

Cozy venue for a spirits distillery and I'm happy to watch their success since opening. They probably now need a longer bar or 2 bars to keep up with the guests i think. The drinks are really good and fancy. The bartenders are friendly and helpful with navigating the menu and your preferences. The menu changes seasonally and decently priced at about $8-$10/drink. There's only 2 restrooms and sometimes it's a little uncomfortable to wait when the need hits. The Fletcher Place/Fountain Square area is fun to explore, especially during the warmer seasons. Whenever we're in the area, we find ourselves stopping at Hotel Tango.

Best pizza in north Tucson, and top 3 in all of Tucson. Greasy and fresh great toppings. I've also dined in and had several dishes. Always satisfied, as always with Italian, servings are generous and service is great. Ambiance is a little crammed.

I love the size of the mall. They have every store it seems.  A lot are factory outlet stores so the prices are cheaper. My favorite is G by guess.  It has some very cool restaurants. They are chains but the aquarium and the rain forest look really cool.  There is plenty to do. There is a Dave and busters and a movie theater.  The only issue is that it always seems busy and sometimes parking is not easy.
Easily the best pizza in the area. I have lived in NPR for 6 years and this is my go-to pizza place. I grew up on LI outside NYC so I know pizza.

After hitting debris on the freeway interrupting my Lyft shift on St Patrick's day, and dealing with the at-fault parties insurance for weeks, these guys hung on to my car for a month and kept it safe. They were so comforting the entire time and kept re-assuring me everything would work out. 

This- coming from a gal who usually does her own Maintinence work on her car. I.E. Filter cleaning, fluid exchange, changing motor or break parts. These guys even saved me a couple hundred bucks! I am so very grateful for the time and consideration they took while I was out of work. 
Thank you and thank you and thank you again guys!

Harrah's is my casino of choice in St. Louis.  There's always plenty of parking, and depending on what day and time you go, there's empty machines and tables, depending on your gambling preference.  I'm a slot machine girl myself, and Harrah's definitely delivers on those.  There seem to be new ones every time I go.  I rarely win, but for me, it's about the atmosphere and the thrill of it, not the outcome.  They offer free coffee, tea, and non-alcoholic beverages, though the mixed drinks and the beers are obscenely cheap.
Ariana did a great job with my pedicure. I'll return, and maybe for a haircut as well.
Fast service. The wings and garlic knots are the best in Tampa. The have done in or takeout. Always had a great time here.
Big slice, authentic Italian pizza, very delicious. Will be back! A must stop when in Santa Barbara!

Everyone's comparing the newShake Shack to 500degrees or Five Guys. 
The reason why I love Shake Shack is because you can tell that the meat they use is def not cheapo meat. You can actually tell by the first bite that the meat they use is way better quality than other fast food places. 

I think it basically comes down to this, if you are in the mood for a greasy gourmet-ish burger go to 500 degress. If you want a greasy burger with unlimited toppings and lots and lots of fries on the side, get Five Guys. If you are in the mood for a burger but don't want anything too greasy and still wanna feel less guilty after eating a burger (and want beer on the side), get Shake Shack. I like all 3 places and this is how I would decide which burger to grab quickly. 

Shake Shack's fries are alright. There's nothing special about the fries/cheese fries. The vanilla shake was good but normal too. However, the vanilla custard was reallly good. I'm not a vanilla fan and never get vanilla icecream. But this custard was pretty amazing and I would def get it on my own next time.
Great customer service in the paint department. Really nice guy helped us find exactly what we were looking for!
Museums are great and this one is nice.  I just wish it would open a little earlier.

Anna is awesome.  I first discovered Body Sanctuary in 2005.  She gave me my very first Brazilian and I've been hooked ever since.  

Her day spa is so cute, cozy and quaint.  It's decorated beautifully and is very relaxing.  Anna does more than waxing, she teaches you about skin care.  

She is very friendly and tries her best to accommodate your schedule.  Her prices are comparable and I'm sure she'll take care of you and all if your spa needs.

One of my favorite places to go.  Food is great especially the bang bang shrimp and the bread.   Martinis are a must as a cocktail there.    The menu is very diverse and great for seafood lovers and non seafood lovers.   My fiancée does not like seafood and usually gets the steak or the pork chop.  There are many great entrees on the menu.   Great place to go to eat or for happy hour.
This place is romantic, fun, and relaxing all at once! The food is excellent! The staff friendly and the wine is wonderful!

Ok, so I finally tried out Rebaud's but on a Saturday afternoon when the selections were not at their peak. I will return but the chocolate croissant was really good. Next time, I will hit this place in the am! Merci!

This is a pretty typical shopping mall, but I like it. They have a good selection of stores, plenty of parking and there are convenient food places nearby. My "musts" in this strip mall are Bath and Body Works and Sally's. I think that this complex is a nice addition to the area and they seem to have a store that appeals to everyone.

This theater has really gone downhill.  The movie theater itself stank.  In spite of complaining twice during the film, the air conditioning did not come on once making for a stuffy, smelly, uncomfortable experience. 

In addition, none of the urinals were working in the men's room - yet another sign of mismanagement and neglect.  I'd think twice before paying movie/concession prices at this place until they get their act together!

We could not get into the Bluebird Cafe...Happily we enjoyed this place. We went to a songwriter night mid-week. So did not expect to see STARS.  Getting in was smooth with prior paid. Show started on time. We saw American Idol performer Craig Lloyd Boyd...great voice and top entertainer. About four other songwriter/artists. Can't remember the food... but that it was better then we expected! We were there for the music.  We were staying downtown so this was a walk away.

Two days in Tampa: spring training and beach excursions. Press box was the first local place we tried. Best wings and sports atmosphere. Servers are fast and drinks cold. Great place to watch a game and scream.

I am very familiar with the PJ's brand. 

We popped in for dinner on a Friday, received a vibrating disc, and an estimated 25 minute wait at 7:30 for a party of 3.  Luckily we were buzzed in less than 10 minuets later. 

The server was good, quick drink order and delivery. We ordered two buffalo chicken salads and a buffalo chicken wrap. 

Both salads had sandy lettuce, not washed enough or at all.   Made the greens kind of gross. 

The sauce I ordered was disappointing. My fault, not theirs. Kickin Korean is ketchup sweet with minimal heat, I expected spicier.   The chic bites are similar to a pizza place, heavily breaded and fried (some parts crunchy) and dipped in sauce. 

The wrap was fine. It was likely the wrong sauce. Mild was ordered, but the wrap was the spiciest dish at the table, maybe that is where the Kickin Korean sauce was???  

Overall, pretty basic pub grub with nice staff.
I love this place.  If you want to sit down and enjoy shared dishes the experience is very warm.  The food is delicious and I highly recommend their wonton soup!

An Asian buffet is a lot like pizza or sex in that, even when it's not that great, it's really not THAT bad.  So we'll apply that here.

The bad: first off, the NAME.  This might be one of the worst-named businesses ever, and this comes from someone who has been to the Meet Rack.  I could forgive an ill-conceived name if the food made up for it.  It doesn't.  What do you expect from a buffet, I guess?  This ain't Vegas.  The food was just okay.  I think I enjoyed the sushi and the garlic shrimp the most.  The shrimp had a nice kick and texture to it.  Everything else kind of tasted the same: like salt.  

You can build your own hibachi, which I should have taken advantage of, but once I figured that out I was already 2 plates in to the purgatory of Gluttony, and in no shape for a 3rd plate.  The place seemed clean enough.  Service was prompt and very courteous.  Also, at around $7 for lunch, the price is right.

I probably wouldn't go back anytime soon, because I don't particularly enjoy stuffing myself (I say 'probably' because my boyfriend does enjoy stuffing himself, so we might be back).  Personally, I think the next time I want Asian food, I'll just head over to Guilin Chinese or Miss Saigon for some pho.  

But I guess if you're REALLY HUNGRY and low on cash, this is worth considering.
Coin Op. best mat near me. Clean. Always a staff member present. Always room and available washers/dryers

I went with a friend for lunch on a Thursday afternoon, and this place was empty. Not a good sign, I thought. The decor was very chic. Our waitress was nice. We ordered oysters (my first time) and I got their special of the day, mahi mahi served on spinach with apple slices, bleu cheese, and a balsamic dressing. EXCELLENT! I'll definitely be back, the fish was cooked to perfection. I thought the prices were reasonable, as well.

The Old US Mint is part of the Louisiana State Museum. This museum was definitely worth seeing, if you are in the area. We liked it, it was both enjoyable and educational.  There was displays of all kinds of coin stampers and old weights/scales and counters. Really cool old fashioned tools, amazing how they used some of these tools that by looking at them I couldn't seem to figure out. Lots of displays and information. Upstairs there's a Jazz preservation area, where you can see lots of photos and listen to some of the music and voices of some of the greats.  On the first floor there is an old water fountain where you can see it has been there since the times of race separation, interesting. Well if you are ever in the area stop by and visit.

Pretty neat spot that is what you'd picture for a typical Irish or English bar.  I haven't tried the food yet.  Tried the Harry Potter shot - its a gimmick..  sticky and no alcohol in it.  But its fun to watch them make it.  :)

Otherwise, neat little bar.
Great craft cocktails by Justin! The shrimp Gaufre is ah-mazing! The collard greens are delicious. Great vibe, old time jazz in the background. Highly recommend this spot!
