The food was average at best. The chicken on my chopped salad ( which wasn't really chopped) tasted like the pre packed junk that's already cooked. The salad had more croutons than anything. My husbands Oyster basket  was mostly limp fries.

I love the Buddakan in NYC because of the cold udon noodles. I think this Buddakan has more vegetarian options but what I ordered seems too bland for what it was. I got some kind of dragon tofu. I thought it would be spicy but wasn't. Also think it was too oily and fried. I am sure people love it but it wasn't for me personally! I think this place is too hyped

Hubby wanted a burger and I wanted something different.  The Duke has a large menu with all kinds of different choices for everyone.  The fried mac n cheese bites were amazing! I enjoyed the buffalo tots and my husband loved the Duke burger.

I have terrible gas but I'm going to not let that affect my review of this wonderful new brunch spot hanging out at a great corner for people watching. All kinds I guess. Listen, we sat outside because truth be told it was pretty loud inside and I'm not much of a people person. Of course a four-top sits next to us minutes later when all I wanted was peace and quiet. My lady friend ordered the Veggie Benedict Special and I have to say I had a bite and I liked it. But not as much as my fine choice, The Clucker. Get this thing, I tell you what. The Clucker is your ideal brunch choice, even if you didn't realize it till right now. Our waitress was a bit much though. Sweet girl, but Jesus! Anyway, you owe it to yourself to give this joint a whirl. And if you don't like it post a review saying you didn't like it. That's all I got.

I thought this place would never open! So far it has been worth the wait. I have been here three times in the last two weeks. I think I am smitten. I can't wait for them to get the breakfast and lunch menu together and their times permanent. 
SInce I'm sure that they are reading the early reviews I want to suggest trying to open on Mondays since Common Grounds is also closed on Mondays. Maybe catch some of their coffee sale overflow.
Anywho, the place is gorgeous and the staff was really polite and helpful.I tried the blueberry muffin and it was honestly on of the best blueberry muffins that i have ever had (not that I'm an expert). The cappuccino was really good. I went back because I want to try their whole menu. The next time I went it was specifically for the Amore Latte. It was as amazing as it sounds. The orange peel and cinnamon were not overpowering, but worked amazingly well with the vanilla latte. That will be the drink I compare the rest of their menu with! The final thing that I have had from there was the London Fog. It's a strong earl grey tea with frothed milk and vanilla. They are not too common here so i was excited to try it from here. It was as good as you can imagine. If you are a tea person, you will love it.
I will definitely come back and support them as they grow and figure out their lunch menu.
Had an amazing stay at this beautiful hotel. Room was adorable and the location is great. Food, especially breakfast was amazing. Will be back. Overall amazing service.

This is the 2nd time i've given this place a chance because the food is actually pretty good, but the experience is sadly just not worth it. Its fine dining without the fine. 

Our recent visit clocked in at 3 hours for a round of drinks and dinner. It wasn't a busy night, but somehow drinks took a good 30mins to arrive, but it was nice out so we still went for it and ordered dinner. MISTAKE. As the night got colder the server turned on another table's heat lamp, but didn't offer to turn ours on- so we sat in the cold, without a drink or food for another 30 mins until I decided to climb the table and turn on the heat lamp myself (servers watched on). After about another 30 the server came by to take another drink order and a mild apology for the wait. It took another 30 for a full apology. Finally our food arrive 2.5 hours into the ordeal. Mine was a cold plate so I was absolutely floored at the wait. 

Note to management. 1. It felt like there was absolutely no management happening 2. If people do have the courtesy to sit in the cold for 2.5 hours maybe offer a drink or a fee app or something. I'm disappointed to cross this spot off of my list, but 2 strikes and you are out.
Owner Todd Syx Scammer! Beware Took $500 deposit for marble counter last July and never received it after a year. Had done the same to others!!!!!

This was such a cute and inviting place to stop off at, for something sweet. I had the La Diva and my boyfriend chose one of the newer chocolate flavored cakes. It hit the spot! 

Sooo delicious! And not only that, but the workers were welcoming and informative about their pastries. 

Highly recommend

I was visiting from out of town and was shocked at how cheap Baja cafe was! The food was great for an even better price. My only problem is the service was pretty slow. Our waiter was very sweet but it just took a little too long to get our food. Still definitely a great place!!

I've eaten Sushi all over the World and the quality here would be difficult to surpass. Absolutely the most amazing variety of rolls anywhere. Our server was knowledgeable, professional and an excellent guide.

Favorite restaurant in Philly. Antonella was our server and guided through our choices. She was spot on and knows her food. We will also request her to be our server when e come back. I had the skirt steak cooked to perfection,my wife had the salmon which was delicious. Sangria was awesome. Mushroom empanadas, Papás Españolas a la provenzal (fried potatoes with garlic.)and for dessert the crepes with dulce de Leche. Next time we are in Philly we will be back here.

Wonderfully thought out and notably affordable happy hour menu.  Try the Philly Dilly pizza!  Bartender was very helpful and engaging.  Decent beer specials, $4 wines and and delicious $5 lemon  martini  Try it!

Great experience buying a car from Carsense in Chester Springs. Our salesman Jeff Reifsnyder went out of his way to make sure we got the car we wanted and got a fair trade value for our trade-in. Their fair pricing and customer service before and after the sale can't be beat and that has been a consistent experience for us in purchasing here vs other dealerships.

It was burger night at Caleb's!

Well at first I was disappointed because I don't eat meat but then I saw the burger night menu...and there it was. The Faro and black bean burger! Had it with blue cheese and it was as good as- no better than a meat burger. Caleb crushed it!
Also had the goat cheese, arugula salad and an order of fries. Great dinner, great crowd. 
And remember it's BYOB! ENJOY

Ok, this place has a pretty good vibe. Right on the water.
Food is better than I remember. Although it's deep fried, in moderation, the shrimp and onion rings are hot and crunchy. Mahi sandwich is a bit too salty for me. Chicken sandwich was alright too. Not screamin good.
  Waitstaff was great as we got there after sunset. The crowd starts thinning after sunset. Full bar!!
The food was acceptional, got the chicken Rhodes! Also great atmosphere. Service from Alex was very attentive and nice! Will be back soon :)

Let me start by saying I have always been prettified of the dentist. I haven't been in a while. My very first experience here with Dr. Shusterman & Olivia was amazing! They both made me feel like I was a new patient @ every single visit. My case was a very complicated case not once did either of them complain. The entire staff is friendly and welcoming. I would recommend this dentist @ a 5 star rating!!
My wedding cake was amazing! Not only was it gorgeous, it tasted good! Everyone has said it was the best wedding cake they have had.

By far the best beignets I have ever had. I prefer these since they are lighter than Cafe du monde, which are more dense and doughy. The praline filling was delicious. Sweet Buttery goodness with a hint of salt. I regret not getting any pralines to take home with me.

Went to Santa Barbara again when everything was starting to reopen to get away all of our regular to go places were super packed maybe because they're closer to the water so I did a Yelp search and found this place open for dining.It was a little weird to go order at the counter for such expensive stuff the drinks are pretty pricey and not that great I got a guava margarita they didn't even salt the rim it was $15 and it was like whatever the food itself was OK better than most Americanized Mexican places but the salad dressing they put on all their salads taste like a mango smoothie and not in a good way.I think out of all the things we order the best thing were the size of the shrimp but they were not spicy at all like they were supposed to be. I leave two stars for the taste of the food but I cannot say anything about the service since there was none you basically order your food sit down with a number they drop it off and never come back.

The main hospital is fine, the people couldn't of been nicer when my husband was admitted. But the ER is very scary depending on who was on. One visit they were wonderful answered all my questions and efficiently stitched up my husband. Last visit I sat not knowing anything for an entire hour in the waiting room till I threatened to get loud and obnoxious. My husband has dementia didn't know where he was so I'm sure he was very confused, upset and in pain so to shackle him and not have someone with him was beyond cruel.
Excellent reasons why I prefer Paoli Hospital

This is a great new place on Clearwater Beach!  The owners are very nice.  We are locals who love to grab a slice and salad on the go.  The salads are super fresh and you get a nice big portion.  The mozzarella is delicious- reminds us of NJ/NY.  We recommend you try this awesome takeout ASAP!

S & W kitchens and our designer,  Yina Brown, are awesome!!!!  Our kitchen has far exceeded our expectations!!  Everyone was friendly and professional and their work was extraordinary.   Totally recommend S & W Kitchens and Yina Brown!!

Do not believe their shipping times.  Don't bother sending emails or calling.  They truly
don't seem to care.  I strongly suspect when they get an order they just turn around and
order it from a 3rd party.  Also do not pay upfront for a "pre-order."  Soundstage has in 
the past advertised pre-orders that they have no idea when the record is going to be 
released.  If all you care about is price and sturdy packaging they're fine.  But be prepared
to wait, and wait, and wait some more.
I had a great experience! Helen was very gentle with my nails and did the design exactly how I asked, I would definitely go again.

Shame I have to post 1 star!! Don't trust this manager Aamer Ahmed. Aamer Ahmed told me the total fee with taxes took my card (Amex Gold which covers my insurance, plus my own insurance) and swiped my card. I then found out that Aamer Ahmed had charged me for both the top insurance and the second tier. His name is Aamer Ahmed. Their customer service told me that I signed and there's nothing they can do about the liar Aamer Ahmed. What an utter CU#T Aamer Ahmed is. Plus the car had used tissues and a vape pen left inside!! Aamer.ahmed@hertz.com I'd love to bump into him again! Come say hi Aamer Ahmed.  He has my number. Call me Aamer Ahmed.

What a fantastic experience, start to finish. Our server was friendly, knowledgeable, and attentive. She answered every question about the menu, as our party had specific dietary needs. She made excellent suggestions, and was so patient with us. The cocktails and food were the best I've had in a long time. Everything was perfectly cooked, seasoned, and portioned, and exactly the quality you'd expect from a St. Elmo's restaurant. I can't wait to go back.

Friends of ours booked a destination wedding at this resort. There was a miscommunication in booking the rooms, and by the time we called to book our room, the resort was full the night before the wedding (Friday), but had open rooms available for the night of the wedding (Saturday). Our fault for being late in booking. However, we asked if we could stay Saturday night, but were told that there was a two-night minimum. They were unwilling to make any exception, even though (a) we wanted to stay two nights but they didn't have the availability, and (b) the entire wedding group would be at the hotel Saturday night. They advised us to call back three days before the event to see if there were any cancellations for Friday night, since they have a 72-hour cancellation policy, which we did. We then spoke to one customer service rep who said that given the circumstances, few days left until the wedding, and since the couple had a wedding block at the hotel, they could likely lift the two-night minimum stay requirement for us, and put us in touch with the main office to do so. However, the individual we spoke with from the main office refused to allow us to book for Saturday night. Instead, she said that the two-night stay requirement would likely be lifted the next morning, and to try to book then. Unfortunately, the other hotel at which we were staying required us to cancel by that day, so waiting 12 hours for the hotel to lift the two-night minimum would mean either not staying at the Sirata with the rest of the wedding, or paying for two hotels for Saturday night. We told the woman this, and basically begged her to reserve the room for us given that the two-night minimum stay requirement was being lifted in half a day, but she basically said, "too bad." I'd say if you are thinking about booking a group event at this hotel, perhaps think twice about the way they will treat your guests. They'd rather have empty rooms than make a 12-hour exception to accommodate your guests (and so that your guests can stay to celebrate your day/night with you).

This is a very solid Poke place.  The service is always friendly and portions are good.  There are many options available for toppings and fish.  Don't forget your punch card because you get a free bowl after 9 purchases I believe.

The place was recommended to me because I was looking for a taste of Spain and it didn't disappoint. I got the Griddled Sourdough with Boquerones and Green Olive  and the Beef Shank and Potato Bombas with Aioli and Pickled Chilies tapas and broth were incredible! I don't remember which wine I had, the bartender let me taste 3 different reds but what I got was really nice. I will definitely go back.

This scum is finally being brought down for sexually harassing his tenants. I had to live with this loser constantly coming into my apartment without my consent and making inappropriate comments. It was terrible. https://www.nola.com/crime/index.ssf/2018/08/new_orleans_landlord_harassmen.html?utm_campaign=noladotcom_sf&utm_medium=social&utm_source=facebook

This is a fine dining restaurant. Had gone as a group on a Saturday evening. The menu is quite curated and most of it looks delicious. Everyone in our group liked the orders. The plus point is that it's by the Delaware river which makes it scenic locale. It tends to get very crowded on weekends. The service is also nice. They also have an area called wine cellar which has a good ambience.

This is the worst food experience ever in Santa Barbara..I gave them a second chance ant i sincerely regret it. This time I ordered sirloin and eggs and it looked5 like dog food no eggs visible and the sirloin must've been shredded something! The tea steeped 10 + minutes still water. The girl took away a plate pretry much as it was served less a bite or two. I feel so disappointed. Who enjoys wasting money and food...first experience was just as bad with a different selection. At least I know...btw the pastries sit overnight in the case possibly. It made my stomach cramp immediately. Lovely people though. Very friendly.

This was the easiest repair I ever had done. I dropped my car off, all of my paperwork was ready to include getting the rental. The job was done quickly, and thoroughly, and the professionalism of all of the staff members was so refreshing. I was so happy that I also got a lifetime guarantee on the repair. I would recommend caliber collision to anyone needing car repairs.

I had trouble installing a SSD, so I took it to MicroCenter to see if they could figure out what I couldn't.
"$80" they said. I said that was fine, and they opened up my case and looked inside. "Uh, we can't install this, it doesn't have enough cables." I said "I know" because that's why I couldn't do it myself. They then said they could switch out the SSD for the HD, but that's a simple matter of swapping two cables. I said I would do it, if that's all they could do. Then they swapped the two cables and said "that'll be $80."
I didn't fight them on it, because I did ask them to install the SSD. But they knew I could do it myself, and they ignored that fact and charged me $80 for less than a minute of work.
Don't trust these snakes; learn to do it yourself on YouTube tutorials.

I have not had a meal this bad in a long time....fries were old and reheated.. salad was shedded lettuce like in taco salad and the chicken strips over cooked in stale grease...when complained was told by cashier that she didn't cook it and offered no refund or another meal...

Happened to be in that area and stopped in for a laugh to see if anything had changed. Nope. Same blah gear as every other store varying in condition from playable to useful only as a door stop. Same musty smell.  And dust. Lots of dust. Same craptacular types of staff from manager to floor people (racist, misogynist, unnecessarily vulgar, completely self absorbed. Though no different than any other Sam Ash. Looking at you New York) No greeting of any kind, complete indifference in helping me or any one of the whopping 3 other people try an instrument. Actually no effort whatsoever to interact with customers. Too busy playing on their phones. 5 minutes in and out. Barring a few specifics this place is pretty much a garbage heap on par with the rest of them. I wouldn't even steal from here. That's how much this place and people suck. I'm amazed this place, let alone the chain are still in business.

Isaiah was our server and he provides excellent service. He knew the menu very well, was funny, friendly and attentive (but not overly).  The food was delicious- I honestly felt I was eating the same food that I ate at Shaya (duh) but the vibe in the restaurant was different: just plain old good vibes. The cocktail menu was cool and they serve their sparkling EXTRA COLD. All and all a fab experience!

It pains me to write this review about what used to be my favorite casino to go gambling.  I have been a loyal customer of Eldorado for 20 years or so. I go there from San Jose 4-5 times a year, gamble on tables, spend a few "budgeted" thousands of dollars every visit.  I have not been there since March 2020 due to Covid concerns. After being vaccinated, I just visited on May 12 and 13. I have nothing bad to say about my hotel stay, check in process, folks at Eldorado, it was good as it always is especially since I know most of the people that have been there a while.  This review is specifically about the Casino. I guess during the last year Caesars management have taken over the casino.  Very few tables were open (I counted 4 out of 50 or so tables were open on day shift, a few more opened on night shift. No Pai gow, No ultimate Texas Holdem, No 3 card Poker, No let it ride, no roulette.  a few BJ tables and a Baccarat table (on day shift). On top of that, most tables had a $25 minimum!! in Reno??   Ceasars must think Reno is equal to Vegas or Monte Carlo. This has driven most local customers away as well. I would see them all the time previously, I saw none this time.  I am hoping this was just due to some remaining Covid restrictions.  I will give Eldorado one more try in July after all restrictions are lifted. If is stays the same with the number of tables and high minimums, I will take my business to GSR or Peppermill. That will be a sad day for me.

I got a bad apple here. Let me start with the good- the drinks and food were exquisite. Order the pork sliders! However, I was just so colossally disappointed in the service here. I waited for a really long time to order my cider,, which could not be ordered from a table. You have to go to the bar. The bartender was watching Mulan on television and wouldn't turn around to take my drink order. I had to find another way to order. I came with a large group of people from my office, and we ordered lots of individual plates and food, so our service was probably complicated. Three or four times the folks who were running the food out to us tried to remove plates that still had food on them! The place was not packed, so I wasn't certain why everything felt like such a fire drill to clear the tables. I also thought it was very frustrating that we had to order food from the bar. When I asked about a substitution for a different side item, the bartender was very snide and said no. No explanation, no courteousness, just very stern and very rude. Demeaning. Here's my thing with all of these new places in Nashville. I know that there's a service industry desert. It's tough to get great people to show up and work with all of the new establishments opening in Nashville. But if the service is terrible, there are just so many places to choose from and explore... now because of the explosion of new places, I have less patience than ever with inconsiderate service. If you want to come and hang out and play board games and have some lovely cider and nice snacks AND don't care so much about servers who are rude, this is your jam! Because Nashville is having a moment, I will try to give grace. But I will most likely never return. I hope you hear that there can be tweaked service improvements! Treat your customers with respect, and people will come back. The ten of us said we would not. The food here is wonderful, just try harder to step up the service part. Otherwise, there are other apples to choose from in our fair city.

Horrible horrible . I couldn't believe the negative reviews I thought people just love to complain. Went there today and I picked number one which includes cleaning the inside of the car and outside. I go pick up my care and it was a mess from inside and when I told the manager I was advised I picked the cheapest plan so pretty much 21.99 don't clean the car good. I need to pick option 4 which it ll coast 45.99 to clean good inside the car. What a joke . The little girl that runs the cashier is the owners daughter. She's a total mess and told me well that's what u get for a cheap plan. 21.99 I expect my care to be spot less from inside . Then she said pay the difference to plan 4 and we ll clean it good from inside. What a jokeeeeeeeeeeeeee

I had pretty high expectations for dinner at this restaurant and was let down a bit . The food was ok, there were two memorable dishes but everything else was average and definitely overpriced. 

We asked our server to course out our dishes, we wanted to take our time eating and not rush through each dish. Although our server obliged with our request, I  think he was a bit preoccupied and distracted with some personal guests he had at the restaurant at the same time we were there and there was definitely longer waits than necessary between dishes. 

We had some fresh raw oysters, the yellowfin tuna and artichoke appetizers, the grilled Florida fish and wagyu culotte entrees. The most memorable dish was by far the artichoke app, it was amazing. The flavor profiles were on point and the mix of savory and sweet was a winner. Everything else was ok, some dishes like the tuna app were bland, but everything was  way overpriced. Even though we had more food than we needed, we decided to try the ricotta donuts which were amazing. There was something about fried cheese balls that felt extremely indulgent yet we ate them all up.

Hold on to your wallet
Ok so im a doctor myself and also a trauma doc. My dog was vomiting after giving her people food. Im thinking IV fluids, exam and antiemetic. They recommended X-rays and complete blood work in addition.
Estimate was over 900 dollars. We do major surgery on humans for less. Take off the X-rays and bloodwork because it probably would all be negative except for a chronic situation . I wound up paying 300 dollars which I thought was reasonable especially on a weekend.

I enjoy a staycation on occasion to check out the hotels in our lovely city. This is exactly what I did when a group of sorority sisters arrived for a visit. They wanted me to be a guest too and not a hostess. I liked the idea so I checked all of us into the Epicurean.
 
This Marriott property resides on Howard Avenue in the trendy SoHo area of South Tampa. The location is perfect and so much is within walking distance. The upscale hotel has many amenities that you will not find at most hotels. There is a wine shop, they host cooking classes in another room, they have a dessert shop, spa, pool, gym and a roof top lounge with awesome views. Pool parties during the summer for locals and guests alike. The restaurant, Elevage, is nice and offers a great happy hour.  I would suggest you checking out Bern's Steakhouse across the street,  if you have never been.  People say the hotel is rather loud at night and many find it hard to sleep if you are a light sleeper. Although a light sleeper, this girl had no problem after a night out with the old crew. The hotel is also a stones throw from Bayshore Blvd. which holds the title of the longest unbroken sidewalk in the world. A great way to get in some exercise, sun and views of the bay.  

The staff is welcoming, professional and accommodating.  Glad we stayed here. A real treat. I would not hesitate to return.

Anna did everything perfectly to sell our house near the price point we wanted and send us to our next chapter of our life. She is extremely knowledgeable for anything in the St. Louis market and I cannot recommend her more.

This is the worst example of a McDonald's I've ever been to every time I order here or something is wrong or missing from my order the staff is very rude and they pretend like they're closed when they're supposed to be 24 hours when really they're not even open after dark most times because they say that they're closed even though their hours on Google and everywhere else say that they're open 24 hours. My most recent interaction with them I ordered about $30 worth of food for my whole family and I only got drinks and fries they didn't give me any of the sandwiches to go with the meals and when I came back they accuse me of lying and told me that they know they put the food in the bag yet they didn't

Stopped here to get some bottles of local bourbon/Rye we could not get at home.  Selection was solid and we were able to find some unique items.  Only issue was one of the items we bought as a gift , which the store labeled as TN made, was actually distilled in IN, only bottled in TN.  Would not have been a big deal if it were not a gift.  A bit misleading but all in all a solid stop.

What I love about Jill's place is it just feels so darn local. The food is solid; the service is genuine and the atmosphere is fun. When we were there, Jill was enjoying dinner with a friend while keeping an eye on the place. 
All main entrees come with house made split pea soup, salad, bread and potato choice. I did not know think that I like split pea soup but it was delicious. I had the lamb and it was cooked just right. My husband had the dry rubbed ribs and enjoyed them. Our friend had the arugula and steak with chimichurra salad. It was quite a good size and everything was really fresh.
If you do not eat meat, this may not be the best choice for you. I think there was one vegetarian option and a couple of fresh fish choices.
Next time, I want to try the fried chicken.
Jill's family has run the local butcher shop for years so they know their meat.

In town with my daughter and her girlfriend, the gentleman behind the bar was the most warm receptive young man bartending in a long time. 
The welcome and constant attention we were given has made us a loyal fan of bourbon pub.
More bars should have a Wes making all their guests comfortable and welcome ...
Love, Love the Food, nice quiet place to eat with friends and family. Definitely will go back.

My boyfriend and I walked in on a rainy Saturday night ready to dig in to some pizza goodness! 

Our hostess was very welcoming and seated us right away. On top of that we had a very attentive and pleasant waiter. It was not a busy night so we got all the attention! My boyfriend and I wanted a 12" pizza but wanted different choices. We asked our waiter if we could do half and half on the order and was told it was no problem! 

We dived into our half BBQ Chicken and half Supreme Leader pizza as soon as it hit the table with the smell of freshly oven baked pizza engulfing our senses.

I have been a little under the weather and a very thoughtful friend dropped off a care package, including 3 of these beauties ! One peanut and jelly, one apple, and one turtle! I am not a pie person, I am not a sweets person,  I would defiantly rather have another serving of something savory, or cheese! 
But oh my Gawd!!!!!!! These little things are perfection!!'nnnn so damn good! I can not say enough nice things abt. Them. The crust, light, flaky, and dare I say full of butter, each filling completely different but perfect. The creamy ones so smooth, the crumbles so crunchy and each flavor distinct.
I'm going to become a good customer and they will definitely become a treat on my gift giving list !

Always a great experience! Known for their burgers but everything is worth a try! I am here with family and friends on a regular basis and I have never been disappointed! By far the most reliable option for delicious food, exemplary service, and a relaxing atmosphere!

ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE! Placed an order for pizza and mozz sticks and after 50 minutes of waiting, received a call saying they don't deliver to my address. And on top of that, even if they did deliver "it would be an hour and a half wait." Please place your orders elsewhere

I was surprised that location had been open 10 years. I was looking for something new and was heartened by all the good reviews on yelp. 

The atmosphere was more casual than expected and unusual with a plethora of wine from floor to ceiling with TV sports screens interspersed. It felt more like a sports/wine tasting bar combo or upscale lunch place than a special occasion for Saturday night out. It seemed to have a lot of regular patrons and ranged from families with younger children to dating couples. it was appreciated That the noise factor level was medium, especially for patrons with hearing aids. 

It felt more like newly trained wait staff that hadn't worked out all the kinks yet. There were a few challenges in making a reservation because the person answering the phone did not have good command of English. I was accompanied by a person that had owned an Italian restaurant all of his life and was celebrating his 95th birthday. I wanted to know if there was an early bird menu as he doesn't eat as much and if they had anything for a Birthday like even a candle. No on both. 

When he ordered hot tea he was delivered a cup of hot water and two teabags and was never offered any more hot water the rest of the evening. We had to ask for sugar, and then a spoon and napkin on the next pass. He was looking forward to the rack of lamb and I took the waiter's advice for the Churrasco de Entraña, Med Rare. About 10 minutes later we hear there is no lamb. It was only 5 PM so you'd think that the chef would have apprised the waiters of what wasn't available on the menu. 

My partner ordered the Milanesa  Napolitana with the ham cheese and sauce on the side. It was way over deep-fried. The edible interior was tasty but the rest was not pleasing. The glass of wine recommended was delicious and much better than the Comp glass when checking in on Yelp. My beef was juicy and seasoned tastily but mostly not chewable, Our accommodating and enthusiastic waiter, Dominic, had said it would be so tender, even more than a filet mignon, that I wouldn't even need a knife to cut it. That set a high expectation. It was an ample portion with a large and small piece. I shared the smaller piece with my partner who was barely able to chew it so had to dispose of the bite attempts on his plate. While a tad on the salty side, it balanced out the under seasoning on the side of mixed slivered vegetables that were mostly carrots and negligible on string beans or squash. My partner's side was the yucca fries which were new to both of us (very unlike the garlic boiled yucca Cuban fare) and were fried perfectly served with a side sauce that resembled a refined ketchup/mayo with seasoning. My side salad was fresh and green. 

Our waiter offered to Take my meat back and cook it longer but it is not my experience that meat would get more tender if cooked longer so I declined and exercised my jaw instead And took the rest to go to cut up into tiny pieces for a tasty cold salad the next day. 

Our waiter did his best to make amends and offered the birthday boy a dessert. He highly recommended and was proud of a unique dessert made by them which consisted of a cake and some pineapple bits, cream and crumbles of meringue on top. Thankfully my birthday guest was happy with the dessert. 

I wanted this to be a very special meal and evening and hoped that the experience would have been memorable for the right reasons. Unfortunately people pulled up next to us as we were getting into our car, excited about finding this new discovery. They asked us what was great. I couldn't answer truthfully and ruin their evening. I just hope our experience was a fluke.

Looking for a 50s style  diner? Eggs, pancakes, burgers, pot roast, fries, Turkey and dressing and vegetable  soup?

Ginhams is an old fashion diner, just what Dennys tries to copy. This is a long time  St. Charles favorite that improved a few years ago when it went smoke free. 

We always get the same thing. Open-face Turkey, dressing, mashed potatoes on a couple of pieces of white bread  is perfect comfort food. 

Great service,  pleasant surroundings, clean bathroom is all part of the deal. 

We stopped coming here when smoking was allowed. Today with more smoke free restaurants in St. Charles,  there are more favorites to rediscover again!

I lived here for a year about 2 years ago. I agree with most of the other residents: no parking (my car was hit and the response was "so sorry), way too expensive, laundry never works an is expensive as well. the BUGS are disgusting. Literally crawling on my ceiling just waiting to drop on my head while I was sleeping. You can't control either the heat or air. There is no security, you could walk in there at any time and no one would stop you. The leasing staff is either rude or just annoyed that you have a problem with something.

On the good side: great location, awesome pool, and a mini gym. Unfortunately, you have to work off hours(nights as I do) to enjoy any of this because it's too crowded.

Do not move here.

I got a Groupon to Check this place out. I was quite impressed. I came with my sister we did the two hour wine tasting tour. We were educated on how to taste smell and drink wine with proper wine pairings. Even though I am vegetarian, they catered to us as well. We also ate at their restaurant. We recommend the Mac and cheese bites. They are very friendly and have live music performances. Come check it out friends!

Worse experience ever. I scheduled for an eye exam with Dr. Deepa Chandrasekaran for 11/7/2017. She did not see me at all and instead it's a new graduate intern there who did eye exam on me. Then I received a bill of $441 (my responsibility after adjustment). I called my vision insurance and complained, then saw the bill dropped to $91(still my responsibility) and the weird thing they did not charge on my vision insurance at all, they used my medical insurance instead. I again called vision insurance, and they tried many times to reach Vanderbilt eye institute only to no avail. I called too and still can't reach anyone. Their phone system was designed so you can't left message nor your phone number. SHIT! I called patient relations, they give only the operator number finally got the real number supposed for patient relations and left message but nobody responded. BE CAREFUL when you want to try with them.

My second time to this place, we love it! A few clues to help you out:
-No reservations, but they do the yelp reserve ahead seating thing through the app, we still had to wait 10 min after we did that, so know it's not a reservation
-Parties bigger that 4 get sat a a bigger table and have one big pot in front of them with the choice of two soups within that bowl with a metal divider in the bowl separating the two.
-The server will explain how everything works, ask questions if you've got them, they're so helpful
-Don't put a lot of weight on the type of meat you choose. One wagyu brisket for the table is enough (The broth is more important over the long term)
-After you order they bring each customer a bowl for dipping with a little sauce in each bowl, they set a tray of "stuff to add" to your dipping sauce. You only get this tray for a few minutes, so feel free to try each one and put a little extra garlic or BBQ sauce on your plate to add to your broth once that arrives.
-Go easy on you the spice in your soup, you can always add more later or add it to your dipping sauce to your liking
-If you want alcohol get teh Soju, it's $15 and is 19.5% rice based alcohol kind of like saki, but much smoother and milder, very pleasant, its served in shot glass, but you should sip it
-The stuff on the conveyor belt is tempting, but you may get a bigger portion from the server, however, if it's happy hour it's buy one get one on the conveyor belt, get the best deal for you 
-The greens and mushrooms are great to add, order the combo platters if you don't know what you like
-If you like fish the fish/shrimp/lobster rolls add a lot of flavor to your soup
-Free refills of your broth, but the refill is the house original (the top broth on the menu)
-The spicy broth is very spicy
-Ask to taste everyone's soup at the end, everyone makes a different creation
-They ask you for an honest review and if you check in feel free to use the check in offer (a free dish off the conveyor belt)
-Budget $25-35 per person

I've been to a bunch of hot pots and this is the only one which has a full depth of flavors. Delicious, eager to help staff, fun for everyone.

Visited here on 10/04/20 was not very busy. Appetizers arrived on time it was decent but our burgers on the other hand took forever. 2 tables that sat after us got their food before we did. Server realized we were not thrilled said she doesn't know whats going on in the kitchen and would talk to her manager. But no manager bothered to come visit our table. But luckily our server took it into her own hands & discounted our check & bought us desert but don't see how manager does not come speak with us. Then the follow day my wife & i were sick for majority if the day. So you can say we will never return to this establishment ever!

This was the second time I've been here for lunch, primarily to enjoy a fine juicy and thick all-beef Chicago Dog dressed with a tomato slice, Emerald Relish, White Onions, pickle, and sport peppers on a soft Poppyseed Bun.  I then added some squirts of available Heinz Yellow Mustard along the length of the bun myself.  

But this time a side of Criss Cut Fries was so spicy as to be fiery.  And Diane's Chicken Nuggets were mostly good, but there were a few tough ones in the batch.

This time XXX-1/2 stars overall!

I've been a patient in the Tucson area for going on 5 years now. Since I live on the far north side this is the furthest dispensary from my house so I do not frequent this location. I have had a few bad experiences in the past but I visited today and got their 5g shatter deal for $75. The selection was decent, quality is a1. Bud tender was friendly, asked her recommendation and I followed it and she was spot on. Highly recommend checking them out if your in the area. They have improved greatly in my opinion. Last time I was there they charged more on your weight for concentrates against your allotment but upon calling them today after seeing their email special on shatter ounces they now charge accordingly per the weight of the smokeable product. Dope!
The Original hand grenades!!! Sweet/Sour tasting Daiquiri!!! A New Orleans must!!! Liquor!!!

I brought a watch in to see about getting the crystal replaced.  The lady working there said that she could take the watch, then send it to their repair center for an estimate.   I didn't want to do that, so I said 'thanks, but no thanks' and started to leave.  Then she said that on average, new crystals are around $30 - $50 some dollars.  So, in effect, I kind of got my quote, which I guess is 3 star "a-ok."

I didn't have them replace the crystal, so I can't speak to that end of their service.

My husband and I went for Easter brunch and were excited about going as we had frequented this restaurant several years ago and really liked it. We were so disappointed to find out it is no longer the upscale restaurant we thought it was. Our table was in a very drab side room right near the kitchen where the staff had to be going in and out of constantly. To get to the food we had to walk through the foyer which was full of people waiting for tables and we had to push our way through . The food was very mediocre ; nothing like you would expect from a $36 a head brunch. We could have gone to a diner for better service and the same quality of food at half the price or less. Much of the food was not hot;slightly warm at best and the displays were half empty and many unappetizing. The dessert selection was especially poor. Even the coffee was almost cold and undrinkable. We left as soon as we could and went to a nearby coffee shop for a decent cup of coffee. We will never visit here again.
Liars.......I drove 80 miles to see a used car that they said was perfect..........other than needing $3-$5000 in body work, it was perfect....Bastards.  ....don't trust PAT or Mario

OMG. So flippen delicious!!! True NY pizza, greasy, cheesy goodness, amazing crust, fresh ingredients, quick delivery. Oh! Did I mention they gave us complimentary garlic, cheese, red pepper and some kind of yummy Italian seasoning? Would give 10 stars if I could.

best place iver ever eaten sushi next to margate city nj!!!

the shrimp and king crab are outta control!!!

La Scala's Pronto has take out that goes beyond take out. I've ordered from here a few times now and quality is the first word that comes to mind. So they might be a little more expensive than the other area pizza joints but it is totally worth it. 

My most recent order included an eggplant parm sandwich, a small arugula pizza and a meatball parm sandwich. The eggplant sandwich was mine and the arugula pizza was split with my husband. As we ordered take out, we were able to go back and forth between our sandwiches and pizza. Both were so incredibly enjoyable. The eggplant was fresh and had a nice seasoning to it. It was perfectly cooked too- not too mushy but not raw. It came on a fresh, large sesame seed roll. The pizza included arugula, prosciutto, mozzarella, garlic, olive oil and aged balsamic vinegar. They call it a gourmet pizza and that it was! Every bite was more enjoyable than the last. So my husband thinks a large would be overall kill, but I was longing for more after it was gone. 

While the price inhibits La Scala's from being the go-to take out place, it tops the list of special occasion takeout pizza.

My wife is the food snob and the one who likes posting about everything she eats but I felt compelled to post after having one of the best filets ever. 
Even with all the great foods in Nee Orleans, I love a good filet over fish every time. Their filet comes with a coffee topping but since I don't like coffee, I ordered it without. I usually like a baked potato with my steak, but they only had sweet potato. 
When the steak arrived the first bite was amazing. It was so tender, you could have cut it with your fork. I look forward to having it again, so if you like a great filet, go to Red Fish!

Marina was an excellent server and it was her 1st day! Great personality and just a kind and caring person. Food was excellent and met the owner who really cares for his guests.    Thank you and we will be back soon!  Stuart and Cookie

Had a beautiful evening celebrating our first Valentine's Day with fantastic lobster tacos, queso fundido and yummy mojitos. I must confess we're so happy Cholita's survived this really tough Covid year!  We  love the awesome festive brunch for kicking it with friends but also the evenings for a romantic dinner and drinks. Jessie, the manager, always makes sure we have a great time. We love the hospitality and the food ...well what can you say about sooo many delicious things on the menu except scrumptious!  Go to the brunch, but be warned...you'll be hooked. Jessie we need that lobster taco in our lives on the regular!!
Music stopped playing about half way through our visit. Tried to order food, were unable for some reason, despite what the workers said.

I've had the displeasure of renting from this place now on two occasions. The first time I was several years ago and I had forgotten until I pulled into the place. I pulled into the parking lot and found a guy trying to back out across the entire parking lot. Little did I know that they intentionally block the other drive way with a truck. Jesse came out and started yelling at me as if I should know that they block 50% of their business access. Never again.

This was my second time at August, the first time I went there the young lady I was dating was a vegan, so I wanted to impress her and get the vegetable tasting menu, I didnt have very high expectations because I am usually very meatcentric...HOWEVER I DID NOT MISS MEAT AT ALL! To say I was impressed would be a understatement.

This time around I basically had the would menu with wine parings, now here is the truly special part, a vegetable dish was STILL my favorite thing on the menu, it was a simple cauliflower soup but it was like a explosion of cauliflower, it was like the Mercedes-Benz of Cauliflower or something, its like they grew it in the garden of Enden and only watered it with spring sun showers and the tears of angels! Oh and the Executive Chef Ross Dover came out to our table and shaved fresh truffles on it, which really took it a whole new level.

The Ravigote salad was a pure delight and it literally made me smile out loud, that dish is the perfect seafood dish and it would be a crime against humanity if it ever came off of the menu!

I had no idea that I liked Rabbit until I tasted the Cavatelli dish, so much flavor in the sauce and the Cavatelli itself had a wonderful texture and is a wonderful vehicle for the dish as a whole.

I have had turtle soup 3 times at 3 amazing places, first at commanders palace then at the Palace Cafe and lastly at August, if you think I am exaggerating when I say that I could eat that turtle soup every single day of my life you obviously do not know me and more importantly you sure as heck have not tasted that soup!

I have been to a LOT of the so called best restaurant in the city and no one is quite on par with this place as far as the sophisticated and modern cooking techniques, amazing execution of the dishes along with smart and attentive service. 

The desserts this time around were also on par with the savory dishes and one of my favorite bites of the night was Chef Patricia Mortons Lava Cake Souffle thingamajiggy, whatever its called it was freaking DELICIOUS!

I thought the food at CoreLife tasted good, but I would not say that the price was right for what you got.

The scoop for their meats is TINY. I got a double-scoop of steak on my black & blue salad, and it was about the same amount you find at other comparable places.

I guess they have cool in-house drinks, but I was already dishing out something like $13+ for a quick-service salad, so I skipped that.

If I return, next visit I'll likely go for a grain bowl or soup bowl instead.

A good place with a good vibe.  I would say it is a good neighborhood place; not a destination to make a trip.  Staff was friendly.  A steady stream of people in and out on a Sunday morning.  Inside seating seemed right for the size as well as covered outside seating along the front walk.  Took about 15 minutes to get two gourmet coffees and an order of the avocado toast.  $17 for that is a little too much to make this a regular stop, but I will get coffee here if I happen to be in that area.

When planning for our "staycation" for our anniversary in St. Petersburg, I did a lot of research before choosing the Ponce de Leon Hotel. I read many reviews before choosing it, so I thought I knew what we were getting into. Turns out, we were surprisingly pleased that it was better than we expected. 

The location was perfect for us since it was within walking distance of so many things - the Salvador Dali Museum, the St. Petersburg Pier, the Mahaffey Theater, Al Lang Stadium, the marina and yacht club, and many, many parks. The hotel has a deal with a parking garage around the corner. You can acquire a pass from them to park on the 4th floor for a discounted price. Or you can choose to park on the street. It's a dollar an hour until 8 pm to 9 am, then it's free. 

The check in went smoothly. The lobby is charming and the elevator is right behind the staircase. It only fits about four people and the door to the rooms opens on the opposite wall! Our room was a bit larger since it was a corner room. We had two sets of windows, with only a street and a building view but we weren't here for that. (Obviously when this was the very first skyscraper in town, they had fabulous views!) There are Art Deco touches still remaining all around, and it's fun to find them. The wooden floors are wonderful.

We had a queen bed that was very comfortable. (Sadly, the pillows were flat and lackluster, consider bringing your own.) The closet in the room was removed and a kitchenette placed inside. It was good quality, with a tiny stovetop, sink, microwave and fridge. Excellent set-up if one was to stay for a few days. The coffee pot was the only thing we used. If one needed a closet, there was an armoire in the room, more fitting to the era. The bathroom was very small, but that did not bother us. It was very clean and had a modern toilet. Was everything in the room brand new? No, but it was spotlessly clean. The only other thing besides the flat pillows that was very obviously worn was the vinyl headboard that had age cracks and flakes.

Our room was facing west and right when we were about to leave for dinner, we realized that the sun came right into the room, blinding us. Luckily, the blinds and the curtains were excellent quality, practically blackout shades, and cut out the light almost 100%. The restaurant that was located next to the hotel closed, but the hotel has a small tapas bar next to the lobby front door. Using Yelp, one can find many restaurants and bars within walking distance as well.

We slept well and check out was just as smooth as check in. Everyone we encountered was pleasant. There was a large bottle of hand sanitizer on the counter for everyone to use and all the employees wore face masks.

We came here because this is a hotel that was built in 1922. We didn't want to stay in a cookie cutter hotel that you can stay in "anywhere America." We wanted to spend the night in a piece of history that was unique and sadly disappearing from our landscape. Seriously, where else will you find something like this? The Ponce de Leon Hotel is charming and sweet and we enjoyed our night. As we had breakfast the next day, we wished we had planned a second night here. If you are looking for something out of the ordinary, please consider this charming little place and give it a chance.

We ordered a rug back in January to be delivered with an eta of 6 weeks. Fast forward 6 weeks and no word from this store and I had to call to get an update to be told it would arrive in April or May.  Fast forward a another month and I call for an update to be told someone would look in to it more and return my call as anticipated delivery was now May 29. No call returned. 
This Monday I discussed going direct to Ashley Furniture to get the rug and ask for a refund. It's 4 days later and Ashley Furniture has delivered my rug to McCall free shipping. Notified the store to get a refund and inform them that I had hoped to use them for additional needs for a new build but have since changed my mind since I can go direct and get items faster. I understand that covid has really done a damper to delivery of items but a bit of customer service would have gone a long way.

Laid out over three floors there is a food court, and pretty much every name brand you find across American malls. We never found it crowded at all. Honestly, I wonder how some of these stores stay in business as most were dead empty. 

At least there is a Cafe DuMonde in here which makes it convenient to grab some beignets and cafe au lait to bring to your hotel room and enjoy while getting ready in the morning.

Also, try and avoid the annoying salespeople trying to lure you in as you pass their kiosks in the middle of the halls. They pretty much attack anyone who walks by.

Atmosphere usually good,  sports usually on TVs, upkeep and cleanliness was good.  However, on the contrary, one male bartender was so vile and tortuous he deserved something like a punch in the mouth; in a different environment, what he was doing is called 'intentional infliction of mental suffering'. We got bacon flatbread pizza and truffles potatoes as an appetizer. Both were fantastic. For my main course I got the stl bbq pork steak. It was pretty good, but nothing crazy. It did come with a jalapeño corn biscuit which was amazing. There is plenty of parking available since they have that massive garage right there which is free to park in.

It could be the hangover talking, but Im pretty sure this is the best brunch i've ever had. The wine was amazing. We all loved the fennel bacon, but the chorizo sandwich was probably my favorite. The bread on that thing was incredible

It was late, I was hungry and One Pound Cheese steaks was just around the corner from Fish Town.
I was a little sketchy about going here knowing that it wasn't the classiest part of town, but it was the closest so we went.
I ordered the one foot pepper cheese steak with green peppers, pickles onions, and ketchup. Being an out of towner, it was a rather awkward experience ordering, the lady gave me lots of funny looks but that comes with the territory I guess. But lets get back to the cheese steak. When we got it back to the house and unwrapped it was one of the most beautiful things I've ever seen. The bread was so soft, the cheese was so cheesey the pickles added a little crunch, the onions and peppers added the perfect amount of flavor. There is a Starbucks on Mandalay (main street through), though they do not accept mobile orders. Our favorite spots to eat are Frenchy's Rockaway and Clear Sky Cafe (which has the best breakfast around).

I can't speak for there food as we only stopped in for bubble tea.... but the bubble tea is delicious! I bought the coffee milk tea and the honey dew milk tea ... both of them are great!
I will check back after we eat with a food review.

Great Zoo! I think it be five stars once they complete all their renovations. The zoo had quite a lot of exhibits closed so I could see a lot of people were frustrated with the price tag to get it. However, there was still plenty to do and kept my godchildren happy and content and gave their parents plenty of rest! We did the turtle experience and it was perfect-well worth the 15 bucks. Would definitely go again and do the experiences such as the penguins or the rhino feeding.

The food is top notch. 10/10 !

My husband and I, both long time wearers of eyeglasses and multi year clients of the Eagle location, toodled into the Meridian store for the first time last Saturday morning right after they opened (8a to Noon Saturdays) to see if there were eyeglass styles for him he liked better than the two pair on the 'finals list' at the Eagle location before he made his purchase there.  Friendly staff greeted us and let us look about as we told them the reason for our visit but were readily available when my hubby had a question.

INVENTORY:  Good variety of frames here for men and women, although for our shopping profiles maybe more at the Eagle store in the brands we purchase.  If you're looking for children's frames, there seemed to be a really great variety and assortment here.  Frame prices across price points here from those marked "special value" (or something like that) to designer brands.  

COVID19 SAFETY PRACTICES:  Here as in the Eagle location, all staff and customers must wear masks.  After you have handled a frame off the display you leave it on one of the stations and the staff cleans it before it is put back on display.  (This process is a little better organized at the Eagle store where they have a "deposit basket" for the handled frames and an auto-clave looking piece of equipment below it that the staff puts he frames in to clean them.)  New construction, high ceilings, good venilation, a comfortable place to shop.

THE PRACTICAL MATTER:  When one is going to invest several hundred dollars between frames and lenses in spectacles, one needs to be able to see oneself without mask.  One of the reasons we went in early when there were no other customers in the store was to be able to stand at one of the far back mirrors so that my hubby could lower his mask to assess how a frame looked on him, something we would not do were there others in proximity. 

LOO:  Is in the lobby.

ACCESSIBILITY:  From parking lot in and throughout this seems among one of he few truly ADA compliant facilities in Meridian, including having perhaps the only correct for parking scope and placement in the area.  Level in the door, ample clear floor spaces, seating for fittings is at standard height tables.  Lobby loo accessible too.

GOOD DEAL PS:  Once a year they have a "back to school" special that applies to all customers not just students.  It is buy two pair and get 50% off the price of the second.  My hubby took advantage of that great deal which expires today (August 31).
Enjoyed the patio, the staff, the scene, and scenery here. The Brussels were a little sweet and greasy but they comped the order in light of this.

I'm originally from south philly and so far this is the only place in jersey that I have been to that the crust reminds me of Philly.  

The staff is nice.  This is going to be my go to place for pizza when I don't wanna pay the bridge toll.  I haven't tried any sandwiches yet but they get four stars from me for their pizza and the yummy crust.  

I look forward to trying more of their menu items in the future.  Give them a try.

I have had nothing but negative experiences with this Micro Center. Their prices are WAY too high. Their customer service is abrupt and condescending, which I've experienced twice from two different employees. They seem to think everyone knows (or should know) as much about tech as they do and when you don't, they get judgmental and I've actually had someone laugh at me. 

Really don't bother with this store.

There used to be an amazing sandwich shop in Tampa called Olde World Cheese Shop - they were my go-to for quality, delicious sandwiches. But when they closed their doors after 30yrs, I was in a real pickle in trying to find an alternative...thanks to the power of Yelp, I stumbled across Sulphur Springs Sandwich Shop, and decided to give it a try - and suffice it to say, I think I've finally found a worthy replacement!!

The shop itself is very small and unassuming, but clean and comfortable. The staff were friendly enough and efficient. But the star of my visit was the Florida Ave Rueben sandwich...I don't know where to even begin! The thick, soft slices of rye...the INSANELY juicy and flavorful corned beef that practically melts in your mouth...the briny housemade red cabbage kraut...melty cheese and creamy thousand island...I mean, it is flavor-and-texture perfection!

If you like a goos sandwich, I HIGHLY recommend checking them out - I will definitely be back, and am now making it a goal to work through their entire menu.

Egor promised same day service; called to let me know he was on his way and arrived during the timeframe he quoted that morning.  He diagnosed the problem,lubricated the freezer door and as it did not need repair left without charging me for the service call.  He was knowledgeable, polite and gracious.  I would definitely call them again.

Vegans, vegetarians, and people with allergies BEWARE! I ordered the "Vegan Hulk Roll" along with friends who ordered other items. The restaurant put my vegan roll along with a friend's shrimp roll, mixed together! When I called and spoke with the MANAGER, she took zero responsibility. Her response was that it is the restaurant's "policy" to mix different menu items together (apparently however they like) and she felt this was justified because "not everyone who orders the vegan roll is a vegan." Yes, the manager actually said this to me. Totally unacceptable.

Just had one of their contractors arrested for breaking into my house. When I've called the building manager with issues and about the break in he said it wasn't his problem and not to call him again. He then hung up on me. It's been 6 months and they still haven't fixed or even acknowledged my issues. STAY AWAY!
Awesome coffee shop in every respect. Great coffee, great food, free WiFi, friendly staff. Try the avocado toast.

The pizza was amazing and so was the Caesar salad. Our waitress, I think It was Maggie, was so kind and explained everything for us first timers. We will be back. In fact, I'm already craving the Bubba. Thank you!

It took 25 minutes to get a soup to go. They were so slow "working" it was painful to watch. Will never return to this location. Also the guy charge wore his mask on his Chin and was totally unprofessional. When I got my soup they had the wrong "sides" and I didn't have the patience to wait for them to switch it out. AWFUL.

Billie is the best hair stylist in Reno! She knows exactly how to make my hair look amazing. Not only is she a wonderful stylist, but she's an awesome person. Very friendly, nice, professional and goes above and beyond to make sure her customers are happy. I might even ask her for hair extensions next time as I've always wanted to try them!
Hands down best calamari ever. They are very busy so be prepared to wait, but so worth it.

I'm upgrading my review. The dick that used to work in the kitchen is gone. The people in the kitchen are very friendly. The food is good. The bartenders are all friendly. It's a great, friendly, dog friendly neighborhood bar.

Friendly people, tasty sandwich, but not up to California standards. Man said be careful of the jalapenos, but I didn't even taste any.  The meat was partially gristly, and it could have been filled up more too, especially since the bread was on the small side.

Seth is an amazing lawyer and individual.  Very professional and knowledgeable.  Brought my case to resolution and with results we wanted.  If you want the best representation possible and get the most value for your dollar, you can't go wrong with this firm.  He was always available and responsive to any calls or inquires I had about the case. He is a person you can feel you can trust with your situation which is an amazing quality to find in a lawyer.  I tried every other firm and had horrible experiences, and I am so glad I found his firm.  I highly recommend Seth!  He is amazing.

Had dinner with friends there last night. Staff was friendly and attentive and my Tamarind margarita was good but I ordered the shrimp fajitas and was really disappointed. Bland, no lime or lemon, no spice or char. Veggies  and shrimp almost seemed boiled. The rice was good.... beans just ok. The corn tortillas are very good. Guacamole was bland, as well as the salsa. My friends liked their dinners.. Guess I ordered the wrong thing but good fajitas should be easy to make.

I'm going against the grain of all the rave reviews from here, OpenTable, and Google, but my meal today was just...not good. I can't justify a higher rating while I'm still sitting here regurgitating it. Maybe they were having an off day, but I'm in so much pain right now that I'm unlikely to consider a return any time in the near future.

The Olive is located in the same restaurant space as Nina's and Val's Seafood before it. Like Val's, they didn't renovate the interior, so it was like stepping back in time (gosh I still miss Nina's). The vineyard themed decor works since it's an Italian restaurant. It is still a BYOB. They serve Pepsi products.

When we walked in, I informed them I had a reservation, but no one else was there midday so they seated us without notating my name to check in via OpenTable.

I hadn't eaten yet all day so I was ravenous. I ordered the fried mozzarella, a small Caesar salad, and a cheesesteak sandwich - added mayo to that.

The salad came out first in a bowl too small for it. The lettuce didn't include any romaine hearts - it was just the outer, less desirable part. The dressing was average.

The mozzarella sticks were clearly of the frozen variety and not special at all.

But the cheesesteak? Yikes. As I picked it up, I noticed it was dripping grease. I was so hungry I ate half of it, but looking back I really should've just sent it back when I noticed how soggy the roll was to start. Plus I figured they'd blame it on the mayo -- which was not the culprit. The beef just was not drained. There was a pool of grease on the plate.

The fries were pretty good, however, and my mom enjoyed her meal -- the chicken Caesar wrap (though she was surprised by the lack of cheese in it).

When the server asked about boxes, I said just one and pointed at my mom's plate. She still brought two, so I picked up the latter half of my steak and said it was way too soggy to box up. She didn't reply; just took the second box back.

I then asked about my OpenTable points, since I hadn't (and still haven't) received a confirm. She replied she didn't know anything about OpenTable, but she was sure it checked me in. Oof.

We were the only guests there, and I just expected better. I'm hoping the restaurant can use this review as constructive criticism, as I've been suffering for the past several hours. Tums and peppermint tea did not help.

TLDR, tips for management:
- Serve better lettuce parts.
- Drain grease from food.
- Confirm OpenTable points.

I only wish there was a zero star rating.  Not only didd they put the wrong oil filter on our van, but after it wouldn't build oil pressure they advised my wife to drive it anyway.  They said that happened all the time.  After she called our normal mechanic who told her to absolutely NOT drive it, they finally discovered the wrong filter was used.  They were kind enough to point out that they wouldn't even charge her.  
In addition to the oil filter, they also told my wife that the anti-freeze only tested to +5 degrees and they recommended not driving it off of the lot until it was flushed and replaced.  Funny but when I tested it at home, it tested to -20.  
If it were me, I'd find a more reputable business than this place.

This place truly reminded me of Pittsburgh. It's a great mom and pop type Italian restaurant with great service and parking!

This restaurant is located in what I believe is referred to as the Hill area. It was really easy to find and not far from our downtown spot. When we arrived, the server greeted us immediately and led us to our table. I love that they are taking care to provide distance between patrons. Our waiter soon arrived with water and shared the lunch specials for the day. I ordered the fettuccine alfredo with shrimp. The shrimp was cooked just right and the mushrooms in the dish were well seasoned with garlic. I loved that they didn't just throw them in as I've had at some other places. They also brought out fresh italian bread with the delicious toasted sesame seeds and some real butter. Omg carb overload heaven!!!! My dining partner ordered the spaghetti and said it was good too. She's a sweet sauce kinda girl and while she said it wasn't sweet, she loved the flavors. Everyone working there seemed really friendly and helpful and their menu options made me want to come back again to try more in the future.  If you come thru, check them out!

Anyone in here in STL should definitely stop by here! After reviewing multiple massage places I was skeptical about this place at first because I was gonna opt for massage envy since it is a chain and at least I can rely on knowing its good. However I was very surprise with how well Troy was with the deep tissue massage! Normally massage places like Massage Envy starts their one hour from the time you walk into the room and leave so perhaps 10-15 min isn't really for massages. However, Troy is definitely fair and sets his one hour for the full one hour massage! He is specific is asking where you want massages targeted but he also does a good job in balancing out to the rest of your body to have that balance all throughout your body! The deep tissue was really good I felt so relax and didn't even realized I had parts of me that were sore and I didn't even know it!

Just want to give best buy a shoutout for how well their social distancing curbside pickup system works! Order online, tell them when you're there and they bring it to the car. All through an automated email system. Super easy and convenient! Also the workers are so nice and helpful even waving when you drive up and leave. Great job best buy! I appreciate you!

Pizza and Mexican...why not?

When I got home yesterday from running a few errands, I saw another "pizza menu" wedged in my railing.  Great, more paper wasted...so I thought.

To my surprise, it was Rosario's (like you didn't know where this was going).  

I am always settling for pizza because my wife is the pickiest eater EVER.  Now we have the perfect compromise since I am a Mexican food junkie.

Last night I tried their Chicken Nachos, Pastor Tacos, and pizza (for the wifey) and all three were great.  The pizza sauce reminded me of Lorenzo's on South St, which is a good thing.  The Mexican food was out of this world and my order I structuring were followed to a "T."

Well, the tree was not really wasted, my wife and I now have a great "compromised" delivery spot, and Rosario's has a new customer.  It is a win-win-win.

The only negative is why didn't I get this menu sooner?!?!?!
This new Thai spot is absolutely delicious and FRESH. Nothing is soaked in oil, fresh vegetables, delicious noodles. I loveeee Thai food and am extremely picky. This is the spot.

If I could give them 0 stars I would. If you need continuous supplies, do not use these people. They don't answer the phone. They don't return calls and they are very lax with follow ups. Average time to sit on hold is 18 minutes then whoever answers the call can't help. Then they have to return you call which they do at odd hours. DO NOT USE THEM UNLESS YOU ARE INTO WASTING TONS OF YOUR PERSONAL TIME.

I Called Roto Rooter because my toilets and sinks etc. backed up, and they were able to get here faster than another plumber I called who was cheaper in an estimate.  When they arrived, they gave me a $451 quote to snake out our pipe line.  I said no, he asked how much the other guy was, I told him $198, so he said how about $250 and we will give a free camera check (which does cost a lot, so I went for it).  Well, he couldn't get though on one side, so he went to the other side of the house and snaked out where the septic tank was.  But when lifting the septic tank lid off, he dropped it in the septic tank, which cost $125 to replace.  He then paid for that by reducing the price, but said that no warranty because of the reduction.  The lines apparently were clean, everything drained.  2 days later, back to clog.  I called them back, a new guy came out and told me $517 to take out toilet and snake again, as it was the only way now.  I said no, called the other guys mentioned earlier, they came, went on the roof, snaked it through the vent as should have been done originally, cost me $185, all is fine.   Roto Rooter cost me actually $250 for not doing it right, all they had to do was go on the roof and do it right.  Do not call them for plumbing.  It is a joke.  Call a professional.   I gave 1 star for the plumber and supervisor for being very nice.

I would have given this place 5 stars, but I left with a very bast taste or should I say feeling. I had a reservation for 6 for 5 of us. We got seated right away and the food was excellent, especially the humous scharwama! Anyhow, we ordered drinks (wine), appetizers, full meals, desert and coffee! Dinner was over $130 and at 745, the hostess came to tell us, "I just wanted to let you know that in 10 minutes there is another reservation for this table!" I was literally IN SHOCK! I have been a hostess, a waitress and a patron at many restaurants and NEVER ONCE did someone ask me to leave! WE had only been there less than 2 hours! THAT WAS PLAIN RUDE! WE did not get up right at that moment, we did finish our conversation ,but I DID NOT want to stay there after that! SERIOUSLY, AM I WRONG FOR FEELING LIKE THAT WAS INAPPROPRIATE? Plus, there was  three tables open and no one was standing around and waiting. I LOVED The food and the atmosphere, but I am not sure I would return!

This is the absolute worst building I have ever lived in! The walls are paper thin, the management doesn't care about any problems you might have, the floors and countertops are not sealed and every thing you put on them shows a stain. Don't both taking the elevator as it takes at least 5 minutes to catch one. You better hope the neighbor next door doesn't smoke, as you can hear and smell everything! Do yourself a favor and rent anywhere else than this shitty place! This place sucks.

Fu*k yes! We just relocated to the Tampa area from Texas, and in true Texan fashion, we LOVE our tacos from Texas! I was so worried I wouldn't find a taco place to call our own... we first tried a place that we drive 30 mins away to get to because it looked more authentic AND they had barbacoa, and we were so disappointed in the overall taste. This place is less than 10 mins away from us, AND THEY NAILED IT! So delicious. The only downfall is they do not have barbacoa, but it seems like that's a bit more challenging to find here. The first place we tried missed the mark with barbacoa, but this place seems like if they tried it, they'd nail it!

I strongly recommend CertaPro-Reno.  
These guys made my 28 year old house look brand new. There attention to detail when pressure washing, scraping, caulking, masking, paint spraying, back rolling the paint, final touch-up and cleaning my property when done was at a level all construction contractors should aspire to.  
Four to five workers at a time, took only two days to paint my two story, 2,220 sq.ft. home.  
Shout out to Cosme Ortega the Production Manager and his hard working crew.
Lives up to it's rep.  The brisket was really good.  The Mac and cheese was excellent.

Okay... first off, I am writting this as quickly as possible because I have seemingly launched myself into a damn food coma...  As I said on my check-in... I have NEVER been let down by a RTP location... This falls directly in that catagory.... One word... Fantastic.... 

The delivery was a full 40 minutes ahead of projection... The delivery driver was a joy.. courteous, happy and well... Sierra Hotel.  

After reading the reviews... I will now formally poo poo all marks below 4-Stars.... 

I felt like a skinny crust slightly well done on a Ulti-Meat Pie... Gooooood Lord... Just because I was hungry from the 7-hour drive into Reno today... (see, I drive and don't eat much IOT make good time)   Any hew, I was hungry but didn't over do it... Med Pie, and some Garlic Parm Twists... 

Again... Good Lord... Best think I now have in  my mind is the fact that the left overs are in my fridge and will be consumed in part for BFAST and likely dinner tomorrow.. Yup... That damn good.... The only reason they won't be lunch is that I will not be at my hotel at that time... LOL.

Folks, bottom line... Damn good chow... would definately order from this location again... Way to go RTP... You have NEVER Let me down... 

Thank you..

We had our baby at SAMC on 4/4/17. This was our third baby, and my other 2 kids were born at different hospitals in different States. Given the latter I can not only rate my experience, but also compare it to former ones. I am also a physician and can definitely recognize good care that follows latest guidelines.
Our doctor was Anita Schnapp. 
Admission was easy and quick, and the delivery room was large, quiet and clean. Everybody was welcoming and supportive. My wife's delivery took several hours, but the doc and nurses continued to be very supportive. The nurses and techs were simply amazing. Every single one of them was working very hard to make our stay a good one. "Above and beyond" is an understatement. Our delivery took several hours, but they continued to monitor the baby and did not push us into have a C-section. Dr. Schnapp and the nurses just continued to give us excellent care with a smile for hours.
After delivery we were moved to a regular room on the maternal floor. The room was a bit small, which is probably the only negative thing I have to say. The nurses on that side was equally amazing, and the baby care was world-class. Post-delivery care and education provided (breast feeding, wound and baby care) is unmatched. 
Sorry for the long review, but I thought the details would help you understand why we liked the hospital

I enjoy coming here, with the yummy pastries, fresh tea, nice beverages, etc.  I haven't tried most of the sit down meals but when I did sit down to order with a friend, the service was slow and the waitstaff forgot about us.  

The cafe has a good concept of healthier food options, but the prices are too expensive.  I paid over $4.50 for a large hot tea, and that is too steep, pun intended.  I think for that price, I'll stick with my Starbucks tea for about $3, and at other cafes, I am never given a hard time about double cupping or a beverage sleeve, like I often am here.  For $4.50, I would appreciate more friendly service.  

Again, I really do like the idea of this cafe, it seems nice and cute, and I would like to go there, relax, read a book, but I hardly ever feel that it's inviting or warm.  

I feel that yesterday a situation left me upset.  I knew what I wanted to order, and I kept waiting to order, the people ahead of me couldn't decide and kept thinking about what they wanted.
